10.title: One of the greatest superhero films
10.content:
When "Batman" was made in 1989, the hype was massive. The movie promised a return to the dark Batman of Bob Kane's comics, while still keeping the joking essence of the camp 60's TV series. What followed was an action film that surpassed all expectations. The direction by Tim Burton (of "Bettlejuice" fame) turned out to be a great choice by production company Warnar Bros, Micheal Keaton showed that he could do drama with his witty Batman, Jack Nicholson gave a flamboyant performance of the villain he was born to play, and Danny Elfman made what is arguably his most memorable movie score. It was lively and grand, and was awarded with an Ocsar for pulling it off.

The one's that followed couldn't keep up the same vibrancy. "Returns" was too violent and perverted for its intended audience, "Forever" is a mix of a thousand production problems, and "Batman and Robin" should be wiped from the face of the Earth.

Yet this Batman, now headed by "Memento" director Christopher Nolan, sees a new beginning for Batman, portrayed by Christian Bale. This Batman is a lot like the one in the animated series or the graphic novels, yet you should not get me wrong, this is not a film for children under the age of twelve.

We see Batman (or Bruce Wayne rather) starting out with training in the Himalayas. We see in a series of well-placed flashbacks exactly what makes Batman. Everything, from his father's calming words after being pummeled by bats in an abandoned well, to the psychological training given by Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson yet again reprising the "mentor" role) brings out what drives Wayne to dress up as a big bat.

In the second act we meet present-day Gotham. Unlike the shining Gotham that you see in the flashbacks, this Gotham is dirty, polluted, corrupt, and coming apart at the hinges. It's a Gotham that looks like a mixture of South American slums and Modern-Day Chicago (where it was ironically filmed on-location). More specifically, it's a Gotham that needs saving from mysterious forces.

It's Wayne's drive to use his fears against other that is the major theme featured in the film. As he builds his array of weapons and equipment, partially thanks to Lucios Fox (Morgan Freeman), we finally make sense of everything that goes along in the world of Batman. Most of his weapons, his suit, his tank-like Batmobile and his cape (to much amazement) are throw aways from unsuitable war products. As Fox says, commenting on the prototype suit, "No matter how good this is, the Government doesn't believe a human life is worth $300 000 each." All these weapons and gadgets are painted black and come together to form a pure system for batman to hide in darkness, capture, the get away, all without being noticed.

When the battles begin, we see the dark invisible nature of Batman at its finest. The camera moves in coordination with drug-smuggling thugs, seeing flashes of movement behind them. When Batman finally appears he moves swiftly, gracefully yet violently to rid them and them disappears again. It's one of the greater techniques that this "Batman" has over the other films, yet is overused to a point where fight sequences seem muddled and unknowing.

This Batman keeps a consistent feel to itself, and is one of the most truthful comic book adaptations. Bale's performance as the Dark Knight is among the greatest film portrayals of a superhero,where he gets the hero, playboy and especially the psychopath parts of Batman all on target. I wouldn't be surprised if he gets an Oscar nomination for best actor, in the same vein that Jonny Depp got a nomination for his portrayal of Jack Sparrow in "Pirates of the Caribbean." Liam Neeson (If your confused, I'll just say that a great twist to the story explains it all), Tom Wilkinson (as a mafia kingpin) and Cillian Murphy (as an ecstatic Scarecrow) all do great villains. Micheal Caine gives depth to the role of Alfred, making him a father figure, as well as offering some great humor to lighten the mood. Morgan Freeman has the same effect as Head of the Applied Sciences division of Wayne Enterprises.

The only disappointment was Katie Holmes. She's given the lines to be a great addition to the cast, yet doesn't work with them. Sometimes she even gives off a sly smile at the end of what should be a truly dramatic scene, something only viable if your working with the Monty Python crew. She couldn't support Batman with dramatic effect like Kim Basigner in the original, couldn't take control like Michelle Pfeifer in "Returns," and couldn't be the only person making an effort like Nicole Kidman in "Forever." The only Bat-lover she's really beating in the acting stakes is Elle Macpherson, and anyone can tell you that isn't much of an achievement.

I've always believed in the saying, "If special effects happen all the time, they're not really that special." It's a mistake made by most comic-book films, yet Batman doesn't fall into that gap of modern cinema. Instead, in what is probably the best art direction of a superhero film since the 1989 original, special effects blend into the environment, supporting what is already a realistic view of Batman while giving it the edge only CGI can give it.

Aside from one plot gap (every comic book film has to defy nature somehow), this is probably the most realistic and dramatic superhero film there has been. Easily installing itself with the greats like Superman, the original Batman and the X-men series, the only plausible reason Oscar voters would disregard this great piece of cinema is because its an action film that's apart of a franchise.

10.title: Best Batman Movie Yet
10.content: For some reason, this movie doesn't get the recognition it deserves. I will never understand why the other Nolan Batman movies tend to be so revered. Yes, Heath Ledger made a phenomenal Joker. But, IMO, that movie dragged on way too long. And I found the final installment to be just a bit too over the top for my tastes. I think the one word that comes to mind when I watch this movie is: Believable. Most superhero movies require you to suspend belief. This one does not. You truly see the journey Bruce Wayne goes through to transform into Batman. The car chases are realistic and electrifying. You won't find any over the top CGI happening here because those cars are speeding and crashing. The Tumbler is also the best Batmobile. Ever! All of Bruce's toys that he creates are, again, completely believable. The score is fantastic. Every actor nails their role. I loved Katie Holmes and wished she'd been in the entire series. Christian Bale is the best Batman, with Ben Affleck a close second. The movie also holds up on repeat viewings. Batman Begins may be the best superhero origin story ever done on the big screen and ranks as one of the best superhero movies.

Christopher Nolan crafts such intelligent, immersive narratives that I really gravitate toward. He gives weight and substance to bruce's trauma and fear, really giving us an insight into Batmans inception. I've never seen such clear and powerful insight given to this popular hero. I love how the first half of the film was character building, and even when Bruce puts on the mask, he is a stumbling, a not-yet-complete version of the superhero. Absolutely amazing depiction by Nolan, 10/10. His pacing, story flow and careful attention to character is unbeatable. There was so many conversations and moments that just felt perfect and gave me goosebumps all over. "It's not who i am underneath, but what I do that defines me." 10.title: My First 10/10 Nolan Film
10.content:
Having a Christopher Nolan binge right now. I've seen his short film entries. Was captivated by his first feature-film, Following. Had a good time watching his psychological-thriller, Memento and not to mention, his remake of the 1997 Norwegian film, Insomnia. It's been a great ride so far.

It's been 18 years since Batman Begins was released and I was able to see it just now, it's honestly embarassing. This movie by Nolan is astounding and truly not to be missed. It's my first 10/10 Christopher Nolan movie.

Gotham City is stunningly dark and atmospheric. It is so graphic that you can smell it's stinky, crime-ridden alleys.

The pacing, for me, is flawless. It does not drag nor lacks spotlight on interesting parts. Nolan took the time for Bruce Wayne to develop as Batman and it's worthwhile to watch. Before you get to the fun and action, you get to experience first Bruce Wayne's fear and grief.

Some of the scenes effectively evoked emotions that will linger for a good moment, thanks to Nolan and Goyer's satisfyingly good writing on the dialogues.

Batman Begins does not only entertain the viewer but it also opens them up to important moral issues which are faced by the characters within the film. You will leave the cinema not only amused by it, but you are also left pondering.

10.title: Great Bat Film...No...THE DEFINITIVE Bat Film! :)
10.content:
*** This comment may contain spoilers ***

POSSIBLE SPOILERS (though not really) ARE SPRINKLED throughout, although none are about the plot. :)

Unlike both of Schumacher's horrendous entries, we...Yep, Crap-maker. I'm pointing my steely Bat-gaze directly at you, you...(Readers & true fans: insert your own colorful, neon green, creative nicknames here, with my blessing!)

Erm...excuse me, I just needed to get that pile of mush off my thankfully non-nippled-Batsuited chest. :)

Well, anyway, unlike ALL those bat films that have gone on before it, we have a bona-fide winner: 'Begins' is COMPLETELY, HANDS DOWN superb! :)

When I first walked into the theater 2 days ago, i was apprehensive to say the least. Aside from Newsies & Empire of the Sun, I'd never really seen Christian Bale, the actor, before. (sad but true.) But, dude, he totally socks it to all the other bat-mans out there. he looks the part AND acts the part of BOTH his alter-egos like they're BOTH a second skin, like he REALLY is BOTH of them.

I emphasize BOTH b/c every bat-dude before has only got it, at most, half right. Keaton got bats right, kilmer got Wayne right (SORTA anyway), & clooney...got neither quite right, although he came a bit closer to a tabletop balance between the two sides of Bruce than either of his 2 predecessors.

But, Bale, Bale's something else entirely. and that's a good thing...a very very very good thing. :) he's what batman should have been back in '89: a fully functional, fully complex hero, with an actual direction, a guy with flaws, a guy with nuance. And WITHOUT that god-damned bat-nippled, nut sack/thong, anatomically correct Batsuit, thank you very much!!!

The supporting cast was superb. Perfect compliments to bale who add to the story rather than distract!!! (a folly the previous villains always seem to fall for time and again) This time though, not even THAT happens. Gary Oldman (better known to me as Sirius Black from Harry Potter 3 & the bad guy from the great "The 5th Element") was very cool & understated as Gordon, adding some actual weight & levity to his words rather than just adding it to his middle like pat hingle.

freeman, always a treat, was a nice addition & added some needed color (though not flamboyantly!Schumacher gay-neon) to the proceedings.

And Cillian Murphy & Liam Neeson are super in their parts too, esp. Cillian who is what a pretty-boy psycho should REALLY act/sound/talk/be like...not like the deplorable, witless Keanu performance from The Watcher. So, do NOT let the looks fool you. 'cuz he was MAJORLY creepy. :)

Last but not least, Michael Caine...three words. ALFRED HAS ARRIVED Finally, we have a 3-dimensional character, not just a droll, boring, old manservant who sews codpieces into batman/robin suits for a living.

(Yep, STILL looking' at you Schumacher. HIS Alfred to kilmer's Wayne: "I took the liberty, sir." The liberty of what? Sewing thongs & codpieces into your now supposedly anatomically correct masters's uniforms???) Oh well. THAT was the writer's fault, NOT Michael Gough's, who was pretty great for what he was given...

But Caine just adds and adds and adds to a great performance & the chemistry between he, bale, & freeman is felt & felt very well by this loyal Batfan! :) Nolan is BEYOND great as a director who has both style, grace, & story-telling know-how WITHOUT sacrificing any of the characters...no small feat to wink at.

CONGRATS TO EVERY SINGLE ONE OF YOU, PLUS TO THE ONES I DIDN'T MENTION, FOR A JOB MOST MASTERFULLY WELL-DONE!!!! :)

Go see this NOW!!!

As Gordon says, "I gotta get me one of those!" & unlike robin or batman in the previous films, he actually, GENUINELY MEANS IT.

And so do I!

If you see nothing else this summer, see this!

you will be blown away!

here's to the 2 other films (& all the returning cast & crew) this one will hopefully be spawning within the next 4 or 5 years. :)

Welcome back, Batman!!!! We have missed you!!! :)

Sharma, a loyal viewer & reader of batman for nearly 21 years...

10.title: A Grand And Terrific Piece of Movie-Making
10.content:
When I went to see Batman Begins in the summer of 2005, I was extremely excited. The film looked dark and complex, which were two things that I hadn't seen from this franchise before (the only Batman films I had seen before this were Batman Forever and Batman & Robin). I also expected it to be exciting, both in terms of its action sequences and its visuals. I am extremely glad to say that all of my expectations were tremendously rewarded.

Batman Begins is not only the best film in the franchise so far (fingers crossed for The Dark Knight), but it is also one of those indispensable comic book movies which takes the realism of its subject matter into deep consideration, and emerges even more compelling and intriguing as a result.

After witnessing the death of his parents, Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) began a determined quest to understand the criminal mind. Whilst on this journey, Wayne encounters Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson), who in turn leads him to Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe), who is the leader of the League of Shadows, a group which combats evil. Bruce receives training and knowledge within this group. When he has been trained, he splits with the League and returns home to Gotham City. Adopting the persona of Batman, Bruce takes on crime boss Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson) and corrupt psychiatrist Jonathan Crane AKA Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy). However, another danger lurks in the shadows, waiting for the right moment to strike...

The direction by Christopher Nolan is probably one of the key reasons for the film's success. Taking Batman out of his safety zone full of fantastical locations and ghoulish villains and placing him in the real world was an extremely courageous decision on behalf of Nolan, and it was this decision which gives Begins the necessary edge and complexity to stand out in a crowd.

Nolan also crafts a enriching and clever story, and fills it with smart ideas. There isn't even a trace of camp in this Batman, which makes the events which unfold all the more believable. Nolan also makes sure that the darkness doesn't fully engulf the viewer, crafting well-timed and paced action sequences and moments of clever humour. However, his best decision in this film, by far, is the casting.

First and foremost is Christian Bale, who delivers a mesmerising portrayal of the titular hero. Bale grips and moves the audience with more conviction and maturity than any of the previous Batman to grace the silver screen. He also oozes realistic emotions and humour. We believe him when he is engaged in furious combat with his adversaries, we can believe him when he is having discussions with those close to him and most importantly, we can believe that he would fly through the streets of Gotham City, pounding bad guys with unprecedented fury. This is because Bale perfectly shows Wayne's emotions to the audience, whilst avoiding going over-the-top. He is easily the best Batman, and isn't likely to find any competition in the foreseeable future.

There is also impressive villainy on display here. As Ra's Al Ghul, Ken Watanabe doesn't have much screen-time or many lines, but he is still effectively threatening and, as his excellent debut sword fight proves, extremely deadly. Tom Wilkinson sinks his teeth into the meaty role of Carmine Falcone, providing hardened menace in a restaurant scene with Bruce, as well as several of his other scenes. Cillian Murphy is brilliantly cold and chilling in the role of Dr. Crane, and the scenes in which he tortures people with both a deadly hallucinogenic and a frightening scarecrow mask are genuinely disturbing. None of these actors go over the top in order to have themselves remembered as the best nemesis, which is stupendously refreshing for a Batman film.

Liam Neeson, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman also deliver wonderful performances. Neeson adds another great performance to his CV as Henri Ducard, brilliantly delving into his character and producing a truly original portrayal of what could have been a rather ordinary character. Caine delivers a perfect rapport with Bale as Wayne's butler Alfred, also showing great complexity when needed. Oldman shows marvellous restraint in his performance as good cop Jim Gordon, whilst Freeman is brilliantly sly and humorous in the role of Lucius Fox. The only flaw is that Katie Holme's love interest feels underdeveloped, and never exhibits the spark which should be exhibited by Batman's love interest.

Begin's script also takes its job seriously. The screenplay needs to delve beneath the skin of the character of Batman, to find out what drives him to fight crime. It does this terrifically, providing a direct view into Bruce Wayne's world and thoroughly convincing the audience that he is doing the right thing. It also stays true to the rest of the production and remains realistic, providing believable confrontations between the characters.

James Newton Howard and Hans Zimmer both contribute to the film's exceptional score. Both composers apply their different styles to the score. The end result is moving, exciting and tense, and never distracts from the main events occurring on screen.

Batman Begins is visually exceptional. All of the locations in the film are terrifically designed and brought to life, with great details added in each location. Mixed with some superb cinematography, the visual look of the movie couldn't be better.

The action sequences are excellent. With at least two excellently choreographed and suspenseful sword fights, and the terrific highlight of a heart-pumping car chase ranging from the roads to the rooftops of Gotham, each action sequence is expertly thought-out, intense and involving. Also, they never get repetitive, such as the action sequences in Batman & Robin.

Overall, this is a terrific movie. I highly recommend this to anyone who hasn't already witnessed its grand scale and its terrific execution, and wait with baited breath for The Dark Knight.

10.title: Making up for past disappointments
10.content:
When I heard they were making a new Batman, I was initially a bit..well...less than enthusiastic. However, as the release date approached, and more was revealed, hope grew in my heart. I am happy to say I was not disappointed - from the casting to the action sequences, from some splendid performances to a plot that was actually more than fluff, Batman Begins was an excellent movie, incredibly well done, and I can only hope it erases the memories of that nightmare known as Batman & Robin. One can only hope and pray that Christopher Nolan and David Goyer get the opportunity to expand on this new view of Batman with future films.

Christian Bale also deserves credit for finally, finally managing to portray both the tortured psyche of Bruce Wayne, and the charming playboy he presented to the world. So many before have managed to get either one or the other right, but seldom both.

Best Batman movie. Period.

10.title: One of the greatest movies I have ever seen in my entire life!
10.content: Let's see...first Batman movie: 1989, the director is Tim Burton. Michael Keaton is Batman, and Jack Nicholson is the Joker. Great action, funny lines, dark Gotham City, great music and theme song from Danny Elfman, everything a Batman fan would hope for. I really liked it! Now we go a bit forward to 1992: "Batman Returns". Same director, same Batman, Danny DeVito is the Penguin, and Michelle Pfeiffer is Catwoman. It was good, but not as good as the previous one. We fast forward again to 1995: "Batman Forever". The director is Joel Schumacher, Batman's Val Kilmer, Tommy Lee Jones is Two-Face, JIm Carrey's the Riddler, and Chris O'Donnel is Robin. Now, all these years I can't understand what the HELL Warner Bros. found on this director! I mean, the movie was like there was no darkness, it was like you were watching a cartoon! But anyway, it's still watchable. 1997: Batman's worst year EVER!!!! With "Batman&Robin", I lost my faith in Batman movies! You cannot cast George Clooney as Batman, and what's worst, YOU GIVE HIM A BATSUIT WITH NIPPLES! Are you guys kidding' me?? Arnold Scwarzenegger as Mr.Freeze?? Holy Mother of Jesus! Crappy dialogues, no darkness at all. Joel Scumacher, you're an idiot! And then we wait for 8 years. we hear whispers about a new Batman movie, a reboot. We wait, and in 2005 it finally hits the big screen. The title is "Batman Begins". I walk in without having seen a trailer, just knowing the plot, who the director is, and who Batman is. I walk out of the theatre and I'm like "Holy cow! This was AMAZING! Where do they come up with this stuff??". This film is a great apology from Warner Bros. after the ridiculous "Batman&Robin"! The film takes us back to the origin of Batman, when Bruce Wayne, age 8 sees his parents get killed right in front of his eyes. Ever since, he swears that he will fight crime at any cost, making the criminals understand that the city doesn't belong to them.Years later, Wayne travels to the far side of the world to study the criminal mind. He ends up in Korea, where he is trained by a man called Henri Ducard, who is a follower of a mysterious person called Ra's Al Ghoul. When he gets back to Gotham, he realises that he can't fight the bad guys as Bruce Wayne, but as a symbol: BATMAN Christopher Nolan does a great job as a director, and he gives us a visually stunning film, with incredible music by Hans Zimmer & James Newton Howard, outstanding performances bu Christian Bale (Batman/Bruce Wayne), Michael Cane (Alfred Pennyworth), Liam Neeson (Henri Ducard), Gary Oldman (Gordon), Cillian Murphy (Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow), and Tom Wilkinson (Carmine Falcone), and a great script. WARNING: HUGE SPOILER AHEAD The last scene where Batman flips the card and sees that it's a joker card, it just gives me me the chills every time I see it! END OF SPOILER I recommend this movie to all superhero fans, you're gonna have a great time if you haven't seen it. I'm so looking forward to comparing this movie with "The Dark Knight"! Only 6 days to go, and we'll see who's best!

10.title: Batman Begins is Christopher Nolan at his best, creating a spectacular film but also a superb origin story - My Ultimate Review
10.content:
Batman Begins tells the origin story of Bruce Wayne from the death of his parents to his journey to become Batman and his fight to stop Ra's al Ghul and the Scarecrow from plunging Gotham City into chaos. Christopher Nolan's trilogy is the main reason why I fell in love with Batman and the large mythology surrounding him. It's Christopher Nolan at his finest, creating a film that everyone can like, superhero fan or not. But why is that the case? Well it's more of a crime thriller than a superhero film, that's why. If you're a Batman fan, you'll really like this film and if not then you'll find something to your liking. Both the critics and the people agree on that this is a great superhero film and my opinion, one of the best Origin stories told in superhero film.

Christian Bale portrays Bruce Wayne and Batman, doing both the physical part as Batman and the dramatic part of Bruce Wayne, giving each his all and ultimately giving us one of the best live action portrayals of the Dark Knight. There is so many things Bale does right and I love his take on the iconic Caped Crusader, but there are people who have some criticism towards him and that's completely fine. He isn't really perfect in the role, but Christopher Nolan's vision for the character and world he built, Bale's take on the character is perfect for Nolan's The Dark Knight Trilogy. The great and memorable performances doesn't stop with Bale, he's joined by talented actors like: Michael Caine as Alfred Pennyworth, Liam Neeson as Henri Ducard / Ra's al Ghul, Gary Oldman as James Gordon, Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes, Cillian Murphy as Dr. Jonathan Crane / Scarecrow, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Tom Wilkinson as Carmine "The Roman" Falcone and Rutger Hauer as William Earle. There's so many iconic characters and performances in this film, but I'll narrow it down to Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Cillian Murphy and Gary Oldman, their performances are an amazing part of the movie and a reason alone to watch the film. They capture the comic book versions of the characters and successfully brings a quality and fantastic performance to the film.

"Why do we fall, Bruce? So we can learn to pick ourselves up." It is known that this trilogy has many famous quotes, it's mostly because of the superb writing from Christopher Nolan and David S. Goyer, combined they created a screenplay and story so smart and just overall great. Giving us a more realistic and grounded Gotham and story. One major theme in the film is fear, which supports the story of Bruce Wayne becoming a hero. Director Christopher Nolan stated that the idea behind the film was "a person who would confront his innermost fear and then attempt to become it". Allusions to fear are seen throughout, from Bruce's conquering of his demons, to becoming Batman, to the Scarecrow and his deadly fear toxin. Thus making Dr. Jonathan Crane the perfect villain for Batman Begins, but he's not the only villain nor is fear the only themes. Corruption plays a huge role in the film and regarding the story, is about the corruption inside the police department and the crime family led by Carmine Falcone. Carmine "The Roman" Falcone along with Ra's al Ghul is the other two villains in the film. What's interesting is how Christopher Nolan succeeds with making a superb film with three villains in the run time of 2 hours and 20 minutes, every villain and character are as well thought out and well written, he needs praise for that and of making a film of that length never feeling boring. The pacing and editing is perfect.

Batman Begins is full of beautifully crafted and just terrific set pieces, done by how they kept everything grounded with practical effects instead of relying on CGI. Some sequences that just show how great looking film it is, is for an example Bruce Wayne fighting his way out of the HQ of League of Assassins. There's plenty of sequences and scenes that were created with the upmost care and brilliance in mind. Wally Pfister and Christopher Nolan is to thank for the stunning set pieces, the cinematographer and director. Wally Pfister actually got nominated for an Oscar for his work in this film, an award worthy of winning. With The Dark Knight Trilogy, things were to be as grounded and realistic as possible which I thank Christopher Nolan for. Every gadget, vehicle and item Batman use in this film exists in the real world or could exist.

Experiencing this trilogy for the first time in 4K, starting with Batman Begins. I just have to say it's brilliant and the right way to watch the film. The HDR is perfect and truly captures the cinematic picture Nolan wanted for these releases, making it the closest to a theatrical viewing. The soundtrack is superb, the music and everything are truly phenomenal. Hans Zimmer worked with James Newton Howard in creating the unique and powerful musical score, a truly mesmerizing one. It's still a mind blowing experience to watch after all these times, and a film I'll continue to rewatch. If not for the beautiful cinematography and direction, it's the acting and characterization, but also its action sequences. There's so much to enjoy whilst also setting up the sequel, the writing is spectacular.

10.title: To this day, this remains as one of my all-time favorite Batman films. How does it hold up today?
10.content: "Batman Begins" (2005), I've always been a huge fan of the superheroes in DC comics, especially Superman and Batman. So, when this movie was first announced, I was stoked to see it. However, I feel that I must confess something to you. I didn't really care for this film so much when I first saw it. Hey, I was 12 years old and pushing 13 at the time. Maybe because it was a bit too complex for my young brain? However, after it came out on DVD, I decided to give it another chance and I'm glad I did. I paid much more attention, and I got more into the story. Then, from there, it just got better and better with every viewing! Now, I simply can't get enough of this movie, it gets better with age! "Batman Begins" has even found a spot on my top ten all-time favorite superhero films list! It has a perfect story, perfect acting, perfect sets/locations, perfect special effects, and also a perfect soundtrack to tie it together. The plot is, Bruce Wayne undergoes training from his mentor, then soon goes back to the corrupted Gotham City to eventually become his alter-ego, Batman. This was an interesting concept, we got to see Batman's origin story, which has never really been shown on the big screen. Another thing, they gave this storyline much more realism and grittiness, which really helps it to stand out. The two "Batman" films with Michael Keaton are dark and gritty, granted. Which is a good thing on their part and I like those two movies just fine. However, those two films lack what "Batman Begins" does, and that's character development, which is crucial for any movie. That being said, showing the origin story for Bruce Wayne/Batman gives us much more appreciation for the character which yields a stronger story. Along with great character development, "Batman Begins" has an exciting and intriguing plot that will keep you invested and excited all the way through. I won't go into any details about the story itself. But, I guarantee that it'll be a storyline you'll never forget. At 140 minutes, it goes by in the blink of an eye! On a final note, Batman's suit in this film is a big improvement over the one in the comic books. Now, hear me out on this, all right? Yes, the Batman suit with the spandex and it's symbol are iconic. But, the one used in this movie actually looks like a bat and makes the superhero name Batman more superficial within the context of the story. Plus, it's an awesome suit, and the symbol/logo is cool. The unique design really helps it to standout above the other Batman suits! Normally, I'm against when they change superhero suits to meet film standards. That being said, this is one of the rare times when they got it 100% right. As far as the acting goes, it's just as strong as the plot itself. The casting is some of the best I've seen in any superhero movie. The on-screen chemistry between the cast is nothing short of impeccable. A lot of actors have played the role of Bruce Wayne/Batman, but Christian Bale is head and shoulders above the rest. To say the least, he was born to play this character! All of the other actors and actresses cast do a phenomenal job as well. Michael Caine is the best Alfred, Liam Neeson is brilliant as the villainous Ra's al Ghul, Gary Oldman is outstanding as James Gordon, Katie Holmes is great as Rachel Dawes, Morgan Freeman is exceptional as Lucius Fox, etc. The only nitpick I think I need to point out with the casting, is that maybe Katie Holmes was a bit too young looking for the role. Granted, she nailed her performance, but she looks like a teenager! Nothing wrong with that, but it can get kind of distracting at times. Overall, the whole entire cast do a sublime job with their respectable characters! All of the sets/locations are beautiful, and give the film a stunning atmosphere. Gotham City for example, was filmed in multiple cities; London, New York and Chicago. Yet, with all those cities combined it all looked like one single location. At the end of the day, it stayed consistent and that's all that matters. As far as the special effects go, they are all perfect and still hold up to this day. Which is not surprising, being that this movie came out in 2005! Finally, the soundtrack composed by Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard is exceptional and the film score sets the perfect tone for the movie. Hans Zimmer is one of my top ten all-time favorite film score composers, and his work in "The Dark Knight" trilogy is some of his best. James Newton Howard does great with movie soundtracks as well, but Hans Zimmer is in a whole different league. "Batman Begins" is a phenomenal superhero movie. As far as superhero origin stories go, this film is one of the best in that category. On top of that, this movie is the first one to get Batman right. Prior "Batman" films have come close, but this one, along with the rest of the trilogy does Batman and all of the other characters in it justice, and then some! I'm giving this film 5 out of 5 stars on my scale, which equates to 10 out of 10 IMDB stars. Do I really have to say go check out this movie? I think that's pretty obvious with my review. I'm still surprised that I didn't really get into it the first time I saw it. But, when I saw it on DVD, I loved it. That being said, all films, good or bad, deserve a second chance. If you're a huge fan of Batman, or any of the DC comics, you owe it to yourself to see this movie. I promise that you'll love it. If you don't, then be on the look out for Batman!

10.title: excellent thriller
10.content: Finally someone has got it right.The beginning of batman from the perspective of the original DC comic with a few added twists to render this film the best of all the Batman Genre.All the artists are fantastic and this film should go down well with all Batman enthusiasts as it is in my opinion an in depth portrayal of the beginning of the Black Crusader and his commitment to combat all evil.Having been an avid reader of the Batman series in the past,the film tries very hard to explain Father/son bond which unfortunately could not be realized due to the sudden killing of both his parents.It would now be interesting to know how the next Batman film will begin.Could it be with a joker?Who knows!

10.title: Batman's triumphant return
10.content:
Batman begins made a memorable return on screen last summer, because of its strong psychological aspect focused on the Dark Knight's origin. It is very faithful to the famous graphic novel Batman: year One, and that's why it was so popular and exciting, 8 years after the disastrous Batman & Robin, who almost killed the franchise for good. In general, it's a very good movie, although not as good as the 1st Batman, which I like most of all movies of my favorite hero.

Christian Bale was done for Batman's role, and all well-known actors (Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson, etc.) did a great job too. I'm awaiting impatiently its sequel, cause I was very enthralled with Batman begins.

If you like Batman as die-hard fans do, you won't hate it, cause it's more closer to the comic book than ever comparing to Batman & Robin.

Steve Baillargeon

10.title: Great Movie!
10.content: This is one of the best in the franchise if not THE best. No more silly Batman but down to Earth serious. Christian Bale does great.. especially as Batman. He looks great in the mask. Not sure why they changed him to Ben Affleck for the Batman vs Superman. I don't like the next movie as much though.. more dark.. Bane especially. But you gotta take the good with the bad. Love this movie & love that it showed his beginnings better than any other movie or production.

10.title: Batman Begins is THE Batman movie
10.content:
The opening display of the DC comics logo followed by the bats swarming the screen was a great opening. The first half of the film was perfect for introducing the audience to what makes Batman such a unique comic book character and what drives him to do what he does. The sequences with his father were touching and well acted. It established the family legacy which Batman fulfills.The scene where he enters the Batcave for the first time was awesome. The lone man amongst the thousands of swarming bats was a great spectacle,I guess Alfred has rabies shots in the medicine cabinet.

The training sequences with flashbacks to his childhood and youth were perfect. Great mix of story and action leading to a climactic battle with the faux Ra's Al Ghul.

I thought that the Lucius Fox character would suck based on the commercials but the charming Morgan Freeman won me over along with the development of the character just like the comic. BTW, did everyone catch the remarks between Alfred and Lucius while Bruce was recovering from his first contact with Scarecrow. " Good seeing you, Alfred" "You too, Lucius" In pre-Crisis Batman mythos, both Alfred and Lucius fought together with the French Resistance during WWII where Alfred fathered a daughter with the resistance fighter known as Mademoiselle Marie. In other words, they have known each other for a very very long time. I wonder if they will build on this relationship in future films.

Who doesn't love Rutger Hauer? His cocky CEO character was perfect but of course we all knew how it would end. But it was a nice little side story to show Bruce's ability in the business world. Along with the spoiled billionaire displays, Nolan gave us a great picture of Bruce Wayne, the man, albeit as Rachel notes at the end, his true mask is when he is not wearing the cowl.

The inclusion of Arkham Asylum was a great way of introducing the rogue's gallery of Batman and the casting of Cillian Murphy as Dr. Crane was genius. He looked perfect in his suit, slender and lanky, just like the book. And having the inmates escape was a great device which has been used many times over the past decades to create chaos for Batman. Perfect setup for sequels. Liam Neeson was his usual excellent self portraying Ducard with an initial slight reservation then thundering back as he slowly reveals his true abilities. That was a wonderful little twist which was kept quiet. And he ain't dead, they League of Shadows( actually the League of Assassins in the comics) will recover his body and give him a dip in the Lazarus pit. Remember his monologue about how the League has been there for hundreds of years to destroy civilizations at their apex? He has been around for a very long time.

After hearing the complaints regarding Katie Holmes, I didn't mind her character. The thinking for this film is that one man can't clean up the city unless he has help, an honest DA and an honest cop. Of course, we all know who the next DA will be. Gary Oldman was another perfect casting as a young Lieutenant James Gordon. He looked perfect in reacting to the whole situation like any normal person would when first seeing a guy in a batsuit. The inclusion of Flass was a nice touch but unfortunately he looked like Harvey Bullock. Go check out the trade paperback Batman: Year One to see how Gordon gives it to Flass and Commissioner Loeb, much better than the movie scene. Did everyone see the Batgirl cameo in the highchair? Aww, she was so cute. Batman actually saves her in the Year One comic book.

Speaking of Year One, the scene where the Batman is talking to Gordon about how to rescue Rachel was inspired by the comic book. He uses the sonic frequency to call the bats, and he actually fights the SWAT team and goes out of his way to ensure that he doesn't kill the cops and even saves a cat (awww!) while battling them in a dilapidated burning building. The Batmobile is a monster. I thought it looked dumb in pictures but that think kicks ass! I also wonder if we caught a preview of a young Tim Drake during the film. Who knows which Robin they will bring in the future, if at all.

Overall I would say this is the definitive Batman on film. The atmosphere, settings and casting were perfect. Although there were some tweaks with the mythos, it paid tribute to the comic books with many shots like Batman standing on the building ledges and his dropping from the sky with the cape spread open. I read interviews with Bale where he said he wanted to honour the character and not be campy. Both he and Nolan deserve credit for preserving the legacy of the Batman character for the next generation to enjoy on film. Bob Kane can rest easy as the Bat is in good hands at present.

With Spiderman 2, Sin City and now Batman Begins, is it possible that Hollywood is finally realizing that staying true to the comic books produces the most entertaining movies instead of a director or writer giving their interpretation of characters? If they wanted their interpretation to be seen, go write or draw the comic book. Most comic books, despite being ridiculed by many ,have crossed pop culture from the page to every other medium out there. Even people who have never read a comic book have heard of Superman, Batman, Spiderman, etc. so why not stay true to what put them on radar, the comic books. Go see this film, you will enjoy it.

10.title: Dark, brooding, expensive, and excellent
10.content:
First off, I'll say that I saw Michael Keaton and George Clooney as Batman, and I remember the TV show. In reading some of the reviews posted here, I realize that I missed a lot of Batman over the years. Apparently this franchise went way wrong (uh, did it start with the Clooney version?), and people were nervous about seeing this one.

All I know about the Batman cartoon is that his parents were killed leaving the movies after having seen "The Mark of Zorro." Not a Warner Brothers movie, so you can forget that.

This film purports to tell the story of how Bruce Wayne became Batman. I'm not sure how much it sticks to the cartoon Batman, but it's terrific just the same. Bruce (Christian Bale) struggles with his anger and bitterness over the death of his parents. He becomes involved with the League of Shadows, a group with a very extreme mission, where he learns a lot of survival techniques. Wayne finally settles on trying to do some good for the broken down, crime-ridden, mob-infested Gotham -especially when he learns that the League of Shadows plans to annihilate it.

No expense was spared either for the cast or the effects, and there are some amazing ones. The casting is inspired: the handsome Bale is a perfect Bruce/Batman, who manages to hold his emotions inside; Michael Caine as Alfred the Butler - fabulous casting, and one really sees the bond beween Alfred and Bruce; the brilliant Tom Wilkinson as the evil Carmine Falcone; Liam Neeson as an instructor in the League of Shadows; Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, who works for Wayne's company, which is in danger of being stolen from Bruce. The only off-note for me was the casting of Katie Holmes as an assistant district attorney. She came off like a high school student. Age-wise, as a childhood friend of Wayne's, she's in the right age range, but Holmes seems much younger than her years.

This is a dark, brooding film that combines the effects with human drama. Really a great film.

10.title: Batman Begins: Warner Brothers's Redemption
10.content: I have to tell ya, the 50's almost spelled doom for Batman in the comics. As crime stories were replaced with outlandish sci-fi stories. The same happened with Batman in the movies, after Tim Burton turned Batman into nothing more complex then the Punisher and an equally lazy back story for the same character, the Joker was the star of the movie, while Bruce Wayne remained emotionless and stiff and Batman basically operated in a Gotham City that is so bizarre you fail to connect with it(or Batman) on any level. It got worst with Batman Returns where they had penguins and clowns attacking Gotham City, The Penguim reduced to a sewer rat, rather then the sophisticated Mob boss we know in the comics, C-grade romance between Batman and the new villainess Catwoman(but played exceptionally by Michelle Pfeifer) and bizarre sexual innuendo. It got worse when Joel Schumacher turned Batman into a funny guy, turned Gotham City from bizarre to outlandishly cartoony, introduced Bat-nipples and Bat credit cards. After I saw this movie, the first thing that popped into my mind was: Wow! Then I asked: Is this the same company who released Catwoman a couple of months ago? On the stop, I can say this was the best superhero movie of 2005, the best Batman movie and one of the best, if not the best superhero movie of all times. Ignoring the previous continuity of the original Batman films, Chris Nolan and David Goyer decided to re-invent Batman by going back and for the first time recreating the origin story of Batman. The movie tells the tale of one young boy named Bruce Wayne who's afraid of bats, he witnesses the murder of his parents by a small time thug named Joe Chill(just like in the comics), the movie narrates his coming of age and how he decided to become the violent creature of the night Batman. The first of half of the film, is broken down in flashbacks that connect with the overall storyline. In the start of the movie, Bruce is a nameless vagabond who finds himself locked up in a Tibetan prison and out of focus, after getting involved in another prison fight, he gets sent to a private cell, where he is greeted by a man who seems to know his identity, a stranger known as Ducard who works for an underground vigilante group called the League of Shadows who offers Bruce training to become what he's looking for: to be more then just a man. Through the first half of the film we are guided through stages of Bruce's early life. The latter half has Bruce Wayne returning to Gotham to fight the crime and corruption of the city he wishes so much to defend and becoming the Batman, while teaming up with some idealists. The movie delivers as a well-balanced action movie with drama that doesn't feel as awkward as say, Spiderman 2. Bruce Wayne in the movie is someone you care about and his morals and his selflessness goes deeper then your average superhero. Played by Christian Bale(now nobody has an excuse not to know this guy), he channels Bruce's 3 personas with ease and you wonder if he was actually born to play this part. Michael Caine plays Bruce's butler and father figure, Alfred with competence, provides some clever sarcastic humor and connect well with he hero. Gary Oldman plays a different type of character, this time around a good guy, not only does he fit the part, he looks exactly like Jim Gordon. Katie Holmes is competent, but her role is rather disposable but thankfully her romantic involvement with the main character doesn't derail the movie. Morgan Freeman delivers as Wayne's supplier of bad gadgets. Villains in Batman Begins are no longer colorful and competing for most humorous performance and screen time, Cillian Murphy plays an impressive and creepy Scarecrow, who breaths intelligence and cunning without falling into the typical villain stereotype, he's a sick person and filled with corruption, but he has real goals. The same could be said for Ra's Al Ghul who's identity I won't reveal, a terrorist who tries to make a valid point for his actions(possibly better portrayed then most terrorists in action movies). Batman himself as probably scarier then the villains, as nothing seems to stop him and he attacks his opponents viciously but with caution. For a character who has no super-powers, tricking your opponents into thinking you're some superhuman demonic creature is one amazing feat and the movie pulls this off quite well. Other actors like Rugter Hauer and Tom Wilkison are also competent. The movie makes for good storytelling and character that feel true to life and camp free. And they finally made Gotham City into something you can believe in, a city that looks pretty on the outside but on the inside it's rotten to the core, there's poverty, desperation,degradation, slums, corrupt city officials and corrupt police officers: all the elements for a crime movie(which is vital for the Batman comics). The soundtrack is another high point in the film, deep, strong and moving. You can almost visualize the action just by hearing the songs. I'll be waiting for the sequel for sure, as Batman is once again up there among the ranks of Spiderman and the X-men.

10.title: The Batman legend reinvented
10.content:
Christopher Nolan is definitely one of today's most creative filmmakers, and one that has brought what is often considered "art-house" to the general eye, uniting all audiences effectively.

And whilst The Dark Knight is often considered perhaps his best film, Batman Begins, the first installment, is almost as good and an incredible film on its own.

The tone is mature, realistic and feels very close. It is more of a crime drama than a typical superhero story, and the inclusion of acclaimed dramatic actors such as Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine adds to it all. All of the cast overall do an incredible job.

Overall, an incredible masterpiece with lots of breathtaking cinematography, cutting and editing, great action and beautiful messages.

Definitely a film every lover of film should watch, whether you are into action or superhero movies or not!

10.title: La mejor película del mundo
10.content:
Finally, after the previous 2 outings of the caped crusader, the Batman franchise is back on track. Having been a big comic collector over the years and a long time fan of the Dark Knight, I was especially disappointed by 'Forever' and 'Batman and Robin'. To me, these film lost the essence of what drives Bruce Wayne to do what he does and turned Batman into more of a pop star than misunderstood hero.

Thankfully though, Nolan has gone back to the roots of the character, portraying a confused and angry Bruce Wayne, who ultimately rises to become Gotham's greatest champion. Don't expect to see loads of shots of Batman in this film though. It is the story of Wayne and focuses mainly on his years of training and preparation for becoming Batman. You are almost teased throughout the first half of the movie, waiting to see the excellent Christian Bale in the costume, as it keeps holding back to keep you in anticipation. When Batman does finally turn up on screen, it is well worth the wait. In my opinion, Bale was born for this role and for the first time when watching a Batman film, I enjoyed the scenes of Wayne being Wayne as much as Wayne being Batma.

10.title: Batman Begins - Nolan style !!!!!!!
10.content:
Absolute crackerjack version of Batman.

Nolan reboots the series and electrifies it by eliminating all of the superhero fantasy superpower elements and grounds the franchise deep into the basics of a thrilling, gripping pulse-pounding crime-fighting vigilante movie that while it pushes physics remains firmly grounded in the causal laws of the natural world.

A fantastic cast, solid script, terrifically moody dark cinematography, and awesome BGM that aids without intruding makes this not just the best Batman movie but arguably the best superhero movie and in many ways much beter than his own Batman parts 2 and 3 - although the consensus is part 2 (Dark Knight) is the best, but in my opinion this one as the origin story with all of the background and motivations that go into transforming Bruce Wayne into Batman, absolutely takes the cake especially the first hour which is beyond gripping.

The fact that the script and story and the packaging is so tight with absolutely no fluff, boast or bombast, puts this firmly in the Top 3 of Nolan's all time greatest movies - Oppie included !!!!

10.title: This movie is a perfect start to the perfect Dark Knight trilogy!
10.content:
Batman has always been my favourite "superhero", eventhough he does not have any superpowers, which is also why he is so damn cool. He is not born with superpowers or anything, he just had a very tragic childhood with his parents getting killed in front of him, which is the main reason why he decides to become the protector of Gotham. No superpowers, just his wits, combat training and gadgets! Everything in this movie is perfection. The whole Dark Knight trilogy is PERFECTION and it is one of my favourite trilogies of all time.

The cast is near perfect. Everyone fit their role perfectly, except Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. She just looks way too young, like she is 16 years old. Sorry Katie, but that is just my opinion.

The story is so good. It is so interesting to see Bruce Wayne's training and what he went through before he became Batman. The fights are amazing. The Batsuit is so cool. It is also nice to see when he comes up with the ideas for everything when it comes to the gadgets, batcave, etc.

The chemistry and the jokes between Bruce and Alfred, and also between Bruce and Fox is so funny to watch.

The villains are so good as well. The only thing I would have wanted to be slightly different is Ra's al Ghul. He did not feel that super powerful as I would have wanted.

This movie is a perfect start to the perfect Dark Knight trilogy!

10.title: What's there to compare? uhmm... nothing?
10.content:
Anyone who goes into this movie with any sort of expectations should stop. Before you go see this movie, wipe the slate clean. Don't even consider the original three(I don't count the last one. Sucked way too bad.) as any point of reference. Because, frankly, you'll be confused.

This movie was unbelievable. Action was awesome, but not too much. It was much deeper with the emotion than ever before, especially with you know who about you know what at the you know where. (watch it and I'm pretty sure you'll know what I'm talking about.) The darkness portrayed in this movie was unlike anything I'd ever seen in a movie before. Tim Burton couldn't have gotten this close.

The actors were awesome. Christian Bale, who many people didn't think would do a good job, surpassed Michael Keaton and Val Kilmer. He captured both Bruce Wayne and Batman better than anyone. Morgan Freeman is awesome. "small role" you might think, but sure is important. Then Michael Caine as Alfred. Beautiful. Gary Oldman played the best Jim Gordon I've ever seen. He looked and acted like Gordon should. Liam Neeson's played his part beautifully. But I better stop. If I continue on, I'll have to hit the spoiler button, and I don't want to ruin the movie for anyone.

Bottom line, go see it yourself. 10 out of 10, and I'm really picky.

10.title: Batman is back, bigger and better than ever!!
10.content:
Ever since the abomination of Batman and Robin, it was rapidly decreasing its fans and movie-goers. But Batman is back from the grave after 8 years of disappointment. Thanks to Christopher Nolan, the series was revived.

It stars Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, Cillian Murphy, Morgan Freeman, etc.

In tone with the early "Batman: Year One" style comics. As a boy a young Bruce Wayne watched in horror as his millionaire parents were slain in front of his eyes, a trauma which led him to become obsessed with revenge but his chance is cruelly taken away from him by fate. After disappearing to the East where he seeks counsel with the dangerous but honorable ninja cult leader known as Ra's Al-Ghul, he returns to his now decaying Gotham City overrun by organized crime and dangerous individuals manipulating the system whilst the company he inherited is slowly being pulled out from under him. The discovery of a cave under his mansion, and a prototype armored suit leads him to take on a new persona, one which will strike fear into the hearts of men who do wrong - he becomes, Batman. In the new guise, and with the help of rising cop Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman), Batman sets out to take down the various nefarious schemes in motion by individuals such as mafia don Falcone, the twisted doctor/drug dealer Jonathan 'The Scarecrow' Crane (Cillian Murphy), and a mysterious third party that is quite familiar with Wayne and waiting to strike when the time is right.

But this movie right here was BETTER than Batman and Robin (due to the fact that the movie was very campy, cheesy, and weird).

So far, Christopher Nolan has made two very successful films to the series, so that adds up to one of the best superhero films ever.

Batman Begins gets 10 stars.

10.title: We need a classic superhero
10.content:
After hearing about The Dark Knight coming out and not seeing the movie that came before that, or at least remembering seeing it, I had to see this. And I must say, the 2005 summer movie is better than a lot of the 2008 summer movies. And I think The Dark Knight will be as great at this. If not, better (or sadly worse).

We needed a classic superhero like Spiderman. Not really much powers, but can be as strong as Superman, The Hulk, and Iron Man put together. This is why people loved this movie and why I loved it. And with such actors as Christian Bale and Michael Caine that beat the actor Michael Keaton of the 1989 Batman, who wouldn't love this movie? I especially love the length of it, so I wouldn't have to be bored that there was only an hour, but there's two.

Gotham city needs Batman as drug dealers rage around the town, and the man that helped Batman or Bruce Wayne become who he was also wants to destroy Gotham city, who do you have left to call? Well, that's where Batman comes in. Rich and powerful Bruce Wayne, owner of Wayne Industries (I think that's what it's called) is Gotham's most famous person, and secretly Gotham's superhero.

You will enjoy this movie as much as I did. And don't bother seeing the Dark Knight without seeing this.

10.title: One of the Best Movies Ever
10.content:
Everything is great about the film: the action, the acting, the directing, the cinematography, the music...THE MUSIC! The original score is so amazing that it practically makes the movie. Without it, the movie wouldn't be half as good. It really drives the movie, especially the action. During short, tie-in scenes the music may consist of only deep, dark drum beats, but those drum-beats are so amazing that it makes the scene even better.

The sound effects are also fantastic, and they really do a good job in the action scenes. The action scenes...they are amazing.

Now here's the part where I analyze the acting: Christian Bale is the best batman, Michael Caine is amazing, so is Oldman, so is Neeson, Holmes is pretty good, and Cillian Murphy is the best! The movie, although long at 2 and a half hours, moves VERY quickly. It also feels like they kept in the best scenes, although i'm not sure if any scenes were deleted. It's so amazing.

The editing is also very good, and all the scenes are put in the most amazing order.

This is the best batman movie and one of the best of all time. Be sure not to miss out on it!

10.title: i loved it!!!
10.content:
i really liked it and i wish to see it again. i was a lot scarier then i thought but i was still the best!!! i liked how it was really dark and scary but all the same it was still heroic with brief comic reliefs! i also liked how they put his father in to a character. in the comics he was never really there just told about.

i also liked how they played up on how a normal man can live in the shadows and just provoke fear by just being around.

in all reality this movie is not your average superman-ish story, it is dark and the villin, Scarcrow. is super, duper, freaky

p.s.- i thought that when batman was that demon dude and when he talked he like spit sludge, cool!

10.title: Its not who I am underneath but what i DO that defines me
10.content:
Batman Begins Does what Both Burtons and Schumachers Failed on Tim Burton Delivered a dark Batman But there was no Motivation or belief to the character, I have to admit I enjoyed batman Forever it had great potential But the Villains were too comical and not bad enough and what a mess the whole Claw island thing turned out to be. Batman And Robin was Just The Campy 60s show set in Modern day.

But Nolan Finally Pulled it off His Story wasn't set around the Villain But Batman Himself and his Journey From Bruce Wayne Billionaire Playboy to the Dark Night It explained everything from How he learned the skills that makes batman to why and where he gets his Suit, It even Shows you why he wears a cape

Bale is the Perfect Batman/Bruce Wayne You can Feel his Pain and understand his Motivation for ridding Gotham of Corruption and Crime. I wasn't the Biggest Fan of Michael Cains performance He was a likable Alfred But His accent was Too cockney, Katie Holmes is great here too as Bruce's childhood best friend(she is so sexy)Liam Neeson is one of my favourite Actors of all time and pulled of a great job as Ducard Morgan freeman is top notch too one of the most underrated actors in this Film is Cillian Murphy he is an excellent scarecrow hes always edgy but at the same time calm

When I heard Gary Oldman was James Gordon I was surprised and couldn't see it working as all I could see was Dracula and Sirius Black but I was pleasantly surprised with how he was as Sgt Gordon

Final Words Mr Nolan Please Make us a Sequel

10.title: With so much potential for failure, Batman Begins is amazing
10.content: For any fan of comic books, action movies, interesting stories, or a half naked Christian Bale, this movie is incredible. I went in with high expectations and wasn't disappointed. Val Kilmer and George Clooney don't do the Dark Knight justice in comparison. Beautifully written and executed, It seems unlikely another comic book film will come to surpass this one in the near future. The special effects were completely invisible and the car and gadgets were true to comic book genius. I highly recommend you go see it. The newest of villains supplies the audience with some scary scenes so I would suggest leaving the kids home for this one.

10.title: Perfect
10.content: Best movie I've seen so far in 2005. Christopher Nolan is a can't miss with me. I loved Memento, liked the Pacino/Robin Williams movie set in Alaska, and now this. I had it on the in-flight movie for 3 round trips (10 hours or more flight) and found myself enjoying it every time. I actually watched it 3 times the first trip. Anyway, first great point is the atmosphere. Gritty and substantial, but beautiful at the same time (I don't know how to express this well). Anyway like all great directors he grabs your attention and sucks you into the story. Very few old tired gimmicks or waste with this guy. Next the actors/actress. Perfect picks it seems to me. Very aesthetically pleasing choices in Christian Bale and Katie Holmes, and the acting talent is high too. Christian Bale, is this guy good looking with hard and soft edges or what? 10.title: Perfect Bale
10.content:
Wow. I have just seen not only a phenomenal "comic book movie," but a truly dark spectacle of a movie. This movie works on so many levels. The cast, the script, direction, effects, they are all excellent! Now, I must warn you, I have been obsessed with batman for a long, long time. I remember watching the Batman TV show with Adam west. I even have most of the old batman shows from the 40's. But with this move, I believe the series has hit its peak.

First of All, Christian Bale is a man-god. He is the best thing about the movie. He is perfect for Batman and Bruce Wayne. I thought he conveyed the Fanaticism of Bruce Wayne perfectly. His acting was top notch and as long as he stays Batman, I have great hope for the series.

Next up we have the rest of the cast and my, what a great ensemble this is. Morgan Freeman is great as fox but still seems only like a filler character. Gary Oldman is incredible as Gordon, perfect casting right there. Rutger Haur, Tom Wilkenson, hell, even Katie Holmes in her small role was great. Cillian Murphy was creepy as hell, even without the Scarecrows mask. I hope Nolan and Goyer decide to include him in future outings of the series.

Nolan's direction and creativity shine through. I found the cinematography to be dark, much like insomnia. His added touches were ever present in the film, especially with the overall atmosphere.

Now for the movie itself. everything works here. I spent most of the night reading the script when I got home from the show. It really does the film justice. The cast, even with the huge A-list names they have, no one really shines more than they should in their roles. Everyone serves their purpose well.

The only beefs I have with this movie are subtle things such as Christian bale changing his voice as Batman, but when he yelled at the crooked cop that was redeemed. Truly Frightening. Some scenes also look as if they were cut short and it does seem as if some of the better dialogue was cut out, especially in the parts with Liam Neeson.

Overall, (I know you may have heard it before) Batman Begins marks a true return of the character. The movie is dark, scary(yes scary) and beautiful. My hat is off to everyone involved with the film especially Bale and Nolan. I can't wait for the sequel as this has been one of the best cinematic experiences of my life.

***10 out of 10***

10.title: A new meaning to the words cape fear.
10.content:
It took sixty-five long years since first appearing in DC Comics, but Batman finally received cinematic justice in the summer of 2005. In truth, Hollywood had taken an interest in the Caped Crusader after Bob Kane's creation made its debut in Detective Comics #27. But what emerged didn't come from a major studio with a budget similar to that of GONE WITH THE WIND. Rather, these were serialized matinee cheapies from Tinseltown's poverty row, and the production values looked shoddy even back then. Batman fared much better on the radio, where listeners could fill in the visuals with their own imaginations.

In the comic books, Batman would undergo a makeover every decade or so, introducing Robin as a sidekick in 1940 before later adding Batwoman, Batgirl, and Bat-mite {remember him?} as supporting characters. In 1966 the campy "so bad it's good" series starring Adam West premiered on television and reignited interest in the Dark Knight, especially among baby boomers. Although Tim Burton's late Eighties take had a darker tone than the television show, a certain campiness remained {the villains still overacted!}. As for Joel Schumacher, he nearly ruined the franchise after taking over for Burton on BATMAN FOREVER and BATMAN AND ROBIN, the latter of which George Clooney continues to apologize for.

Shortly after the start of a new millennium someone over at Warner Bros {which still owned the rights} thought it might be a novel idea to resurrect the Caped Crusader again....except this time turn back the clock to explore his superhero origins. In Burton's BATMAN, the director only paid lip service to the metamorphosis via a flashback sequence showing a prepubescent Bruce Wayne witnessing his parents' murders. It never really delved into his psyche not did explain how he got his Batsuit, Batmobile, Batcave, and utility belt with various crime fighting gadgets. {After all, having the funds to purchase all that is one thing; acquiring them surreptitiously is another matter altogether.} Neither Burton nor Schumacher were to be involved in the reboot, so the big question over at Warners was: who could call the shots now?

Christopher Nolan had made a positive impression on me with his one-two punch of MEMENTO and INSOMNIA. As far back as 2002 it was clear that Nolan had the filmmaking vision to go far in the industry. So when I read that he was going to direct the newest Batman movie, my initial reaction was somewhere along the lines of "Oh, no. He's selling himself out to Hollywood already!". Boy....was I ever wrong about that!!!! Instead, Nolan turned out to be the franchise's savior, for not only did he agree to direct, but he also co-wrote the screenplay. Nolan described the previous installments as more focused on style than substance, and he was convinced both could be achieved through his reimagining.

In BATMAN BEGINS, Nolan continues to go back and forth in time by employing the nonlinear narrative hallmark of his previous films. For the sake of chronology my synopsis will start with a young Bruce and his first encounter with chiroptophobia. He's playing on the sprawling family estate with childhood friend Rachel Dawes when the wooden planks on which he is standing give way, sending him falling below deep into a cavern populated by....yup, bats! Also living with him and his parents at Wayne Manor is loyal butler Alfred Pennyworth (Michael Caine), and Rachel's housekeeper mother.

It never really states what decade(s) BATMAN BEGINS is set in, but Gotham City is gripped by an economic depression similar to that of the 1930's. Rampant poverty brings about desperation, and because of that desperation Gotham has evolved into a crime ridden cesspool that culminates in the murders of Thomas and Martha Wayne. Ironically, it's their legacy and the philanthropy of Wayne Enterprises that's kept Gotham's financial heartbeat on life support. Now that Bruce's parents are gone, the Wayne foundation is in the hands of the board of directors until the lad becomes an adult.

Meanwhile, the city has gone to hell in a hand basket. The stench of organized crime is represented by Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson), the Al Capone of Gotham City. Brazenly wielding his power like Scarface, Falcone has most of the police and judges on his payroll. One of the few policemen that can't be bought at any price is Sergeant Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman), who watches on in disgust as fellow officers {including his partner} accept bribes from Falcone to look the other way. Like many honest officers, Gordon is intimidated by the blue wall of silence that turns its nose down on the Serpicos of the G. P. D. {Besides, as he tells his colleague, "Who is there to rat to?}

When we're introduced to a grown-up Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale), he's languishing in a Chinese prison camp. Since dropping out of Princeton, Bruce has been trotted the globe, living on a self-imposed hand-to-mouth existence while trying to better understand the criminal mentality. It's in jail that he meets Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson), the man who will become a mentor to the lost boy-man. Ducard has the clout to arrange for Bruce's immediate release, and urges him to enlist in the League of Shadows, a secret Illuminati-type society that for centuries has been dedicated to wiping out corruption.

The current leader of the League Of Shadows is Ra's al Ghul (Ken Watanabe), who rules from a Himalayan mountaintop temple. When Bruce arrives there with the blue poppy requested by Ducard, he is immediately indoctrinated as his teacher instills in him all of the necessary mental and physical requirements. Where the student and instructor differ, however, is their interpretation of justice. Ducard has the Old Testament, eye-for-an-eye brand of justice while Bruce, despite his tragedies, still believes in the New Testament concept of trial of jury of peers. Their differences come to a head that eventuates in the death of Ra's al Ghul and the destruction of the fortress.

When Bruce returns to Gotham after a seven year absence {he'd been declared dead for legal reasons}, Alfred has tended to the family estate while Rachel (Katie Holmes) is now an assistant district attorney. Wayne Enterprises's board of directors have voted to take the company public, leaving Bruce as a minority shareholder. Meanwhile, lawlessness in Gotham has only gotten worse! By this time, Bruce has conceived the idea of a secret alter ego to strike terror into the hearts of Gotham City's criminal underbelly. And what better symbol to do that with than his own fear? Bats!!

The cave Bruce fell into as a boy will serve as the perfect hideaway, but he will still need the special tools to perform his job as Batman. And in the Applied Sciences division of Wayne Enterprises is the ideal man to assist him. Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman) will be to Bruce Wayne what Q was to James Bond: the gadget genius who provides him with the equipment {original designed for the military}. There's a Kevlar bodysuit, an unusual cape, and the armored vehicle on steroids that will become his Batmobile. {Don't we all wish we had something like that during rush hour?} 😆

BATMAN BEGINS is easily the finest treatment of the Caped Crusader to land on either the big or small screen {that is, until superceded by THE DARK KNIGHT}. Nolan and leading actor Bale can take the lion's share of credit for the great leap forward insofar as quality is concerned. It's a stylish meditation on the contrast between retribution and justice, and Nolan handles Bruce Wayne's journey with intelligence and grace. He even throws in a little historical context too, with Alfred commenting that part of the Batcave was used by Bruce's ancestors as an Underground Railway to escort runaway slaves to freedom. Nolan also tosses in bits about the London fire of 1666, the Black Plague, and the sacking of Constantinople.

Portraying Batman/Bruce Wayne, Bale dominates in what could be considered a dual role despite being the same person. And what a supporting cast Nolan assembled to back Bale up!! BATMAN BEGINS would be the first of seven collaborations between Nolan and Caine, including two sequels, making the veteran British actor a lucky charm for the director. Oldman, Freeman, Neeson, Watanabe, and Cillian Murphy {here playing the Scarecrow} would also reunite with Nolan on subsequent projects.

The previous Batman films placed too much emphasis on elaborate set decoration and art direction. Nolan wanted his Gotham City to resemble a typical metropolitan centre, such as New York or Chicago, and often used real buildings to film interior and exterior sets. Working in tandem with production designer Nathan Crowley, the Gotham of BATMAN BEGINS looks spectacular without being ostentatious, and Crowley did similar wonders with Iceland subbing nicely for the Himalayas. Nolan's frequent cinematographer Wally Pfister is another asset; his photography gives the nighttime scenes something that was missing from the preceding pictures: the look of film noir.

BATMAN BEGINS was the booster vaccination the franchise needed after the Schumacher debacles. For loyal fans of the Caped Crusader, this was the Batman movie they'd been waiting their whole lives to see. However, it should be noted that membership with the DC/Marvel Comics universe isn't necessary for any given person to enjoy BATMAN BEGINS. Thanks to Nolan's vision, it can be appreciated by virtually every demographic. 🔚

10.title: The definitive Batman movie
10.content:
An awe-inspiringly, intricately worked superhero movie. Like the instances throughout it that explain how Batman is inspired into picking his equipment (the spiked gauntlets, fire-proof cape), everything about the movie assembles into an enthralling whole. With an almost perfect cast, ample production values, seamless cinematography and music, and script that never lets up, no movie in the genre betters it. In fact it raises the bar for all superhero movies, keeping the tone gritty and real, yet doing every bit of justice to the characters.

Christian Bale is Batman, covering every nuance of the character; the journeying, the reactions. He conveys the most cerebral Batman yet, expressing the characters strengths and what sets him apart from other superheroes. Much better than the darkly humorous Keaton and the plain bored Kilmer.

Michael Caine forms a pillar for the storyline and helps draw out the background of Bruce Wayne. Caine simply is Alfred, leaving no doubt that anyone could have played the role better. Morgan Freeman's role is almost ethereal in it's presence which makes it very fitting for his commanding gravitas.

Katie Holmes has been decried as being a bad pick for her character but considering the limited scope in terms of the story, she didn't do a bad job. Maggie Gyllenhaal is taking over the character in the sequel, but it can be argued that it is mostly due to the politics behind the movie-making.

Cillian Murphy impresses in his role as the seriously flawed genius. He earnestly conveys what makes the character tick.

The guy playing Carmine Falcone is the most major let-down. But at least he shouldn't be in the sequel.

Gary Oldman isn't given much to do, but he does none of it wrong and we can all look forward to his expanded role in the future instalments.

One gripe is that the movie has a bit too much of a glossed over look to its visuals, this can be attributed to the high contrast lighting in the night and dark sequences which naturally there are many. But it helps to give the movie a more engaging polish and is a small niggle at the cost of realism.
