10.title: Batman Begins...as does a new legend...
10.content:
Going into the cinema I had no idea if this was a prequel to the original films or the start of a franchise. I was delighted to realise that it was not a dismal attempt at a prequel to the awful original Batman films, but rather a fantastic creation of its own.

This film captures everything required to become a classic of its time. First, it hits the roots behind the legend 'Batman' as it explores Bruce Wayne's life after the death of his parents, following his journey to becoming the Caped Crusader. By doing so, the audience are sucked into the emotions behind Bruce's life and feel the rare highs and many lows that he goes through and are able to relate well to the character...a necessity for the start of such a series. Second, the film also helps create a very colourful and detailed creation of Gotham City, and its current state from Bruce's childhood to the time of Batman. This is achieved by a very realistic picture of Gotham being portrayed as we see very graphic images of the wealthy and poor areas of the city, similar to that of a real life place. In addition, the train service running through 'Wayne Enterprise' appears new and clean when Bruce's parents are alive, but when Bruce returns from his time away the train and other areas are covered with vandalism, thus portraying a realistic image of a city that is bleeding due to corruption. Finally, the characters of the film help make it what it is...a legend. Bruce's allies, his butler, his old friend and potential love interest and his colleagues relate well to Bruce and to the overall story of 'Batman Begins'. Also, the other characters, particularly Bruce's enemies are not the well known, typical villains that you expect from a Batman movie, but rather they are a good way to centre all the focus on the growth of Batman, with entertaining villains nevertheless for Batman to defeat.

As a result, 'Batman Begins' has all the ingredients of a classic. With an excellent script and fantastic direction grouped with these factors, this film is a classic of its time and is worthy of numerous sequels of the same theme. This film has a unique edge as it is dark and is as realistic as a marvel comic can be, as it related more to the person Bruce and all his emotions as Batman, than to the stereotypical, vintage Batman character. Therefore, 'Batman Begins' barely has a criticism to its name and rightly so, as it is one of the best films ever to grace the entertainment world and it must be said that a legend has begun...roll on the sequel!

10.title: Even heroes have to conquer fears to become super heroes. this movie raises the bar for 'comic-to-film' adaptations...
10.content:
WOW!! Simply WOW. That's a one word answer to how the film is. The USP of this film is that it does not portray the batman as an outright super hero – whacking criminals with super power but shows a vulnerable Bruce Wayne who has to be shaped into a combat machine to be a super hero. This makes the film 'connect' instantly to its audience.

The story explains the origins of the character of Bruce Wayne and starts with Bruce (Christian Bale), as a gypsy traveling the world starting fights with petty criminals to shadow over his guilt over the death of his parents. He is greeted by the mysterious Henri Ducard who along with a legendary warrior Ra's Al Ghul, teach him to turn fear against those who prey on the fearful. Bruce takes him up on his offer and learns to become a warrior of justice only to rebuff the laws of the monastery blindly and return to Gotham city to save it from 'dying' in the hands of the mob. Things are worse than ever in Gotham...Carmine Falcone, a mobster, owns most of the city's officials, and as he runs drugs and gambling. He begins with his Bat-Suit, weaponry, and bat- mobile. His trusted aides for the 'mission' are his trusty Butler, Alfred (Michael Caine), the head of science divisions at Wayne Enterprises, Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman), the only decent Cop left in Gotham, Gordon (Gary Oldman), and his old flame, now the assistant D.A. Rachel Dawes (Katie Holmes – she disappointed with mediocre acting though). But his test lies when he meets his ultimate nemesis – Ducard who wants to destroy gotham in order to save the savaged livelihood of many.

The film is not about firepower (though it has excellent fight sequences) but about 'mind over body' type tactical warfare blended with a comic book persona that batman is. It's not about the heroics of a hero but the struggle to become great and the insecurity which induces one to strive. A hero has to grow as a 'person' first and then as a 'super-hero'. The fights are great, the gadgets all there, the plot is thorough and exciting, and Gotham looks great. Batman really is frightening & menacing (and lethal!) The film wins hearts as it is not conventional, corny, over-digitalized comic book –to-celluloid adaptation; but a well orchestrated drama – crime feature film.

Whether you're or aren't a fan of Christopher Nolan or Batman fanatic, you'll enjoy every single second of the movie. Batman finally begins from here.... (Only to be overshadowed by the legend – the joker in the dark knight —phew!! what an anti climax to the 'hero' stuff – a birth of a super hero in 'batman begins' who fights his way to be one – to the birth of a super anti-hero in 'the dark knight' – I thought batman was good but joker even better!! )

9 out of 10 definitely. Comic-book films grow up with this one... the franchise fell earlier only to rise in 2005 and again in 2008

10.title: Awesome Comic adaptation

Batman Begins is obviously the most innovator film in Batman's saga. Innovator in the sense of the plot and the comic adaptation. No more Schumacher's unfunny jokes, no more childish characters, no more stupid lines. Here is the start of a new era in comic-based films. This one made my day - and night. Watching late in the evening and finishing it around 1am seemed to be a good idea AFTER doing so. Why? This is a dark movie where bird chirping outside would be a bit - off. Too bad I missed it in the theater, as this clearly is a theater-kind-of-movie.

The F/X are as expected state of the art, but the little surprise in this one is the drama and the excellent performances by a range of well known and fine actors. I have to say I like the style of Morgan Freeman - and even though not in a main role, he plays his part superbly also in this movie.

In this movie, Nolan brings us back to the beginning and retells the story of Batman. And he tells the story right, he tells the story so fans of the original Batman recognizes him. Oh, BOY, do I look forward to the next one...

10.title: Batman is here to stay!
10.content:
O what a tragic tale it is of the Batman film series! Batman was at its peak in the late 80s and early 90s with Tim Burton's dizzying incarnations of the Dark Knight. Two films that inhabited the darkest recesses of the character in ways I never thought could be possible. In 1995 it all came crashing down when Burton was dismissed and that most terrible of filmmakers took the directors chair, Joel Schumacher.

And the decline in quality was shocking. His two outings stripped Batman of all his shadowy mystery and intrigue, and replaced it with camp theatrics, empty-headed plots and snazzy visuals with nothing underneath. It seemed Schumacher had managed to do what Batman's enemies never could. He had killed the Dark Knight.

For eight years it seemed Batman was buried in a grave even he couldn't claw his way out of. But all that changed with Christopher Nolan. Nolan emerged on the film circuit with the astonishing Memento, a beautifully crafted murder mystery that scaled impressive heights by telling the story in reverse. Memento established Nolan as one of the most promising filmmakers today.

When it circulated he was directing a new Batman film, Batman Begins, that took the whole story back to its roots, it made me wonder if even a director of Nolan's talents could salvage Batman. And the answer is...yes, absolutely!

Batman Begins is a film that really flies high. Nolan gets right inside the dark psychology of the character, and turned out one of the most intelligent and thought-provoking superhero films ever made.

This is a film that takes Batman back to his beginnings. We learn everything about him. How he became obsessed with bats. His parents' murder when he was a child. Watching him grow consumed by vengeance. Travelling the world searching for answers. And finding his true calling.

Batman Begins is a film of two distinct halves. The first half details everything about Batman's origins and its this part of the film where Christopher Nolan seems the most at home. The part where the orphaned Bruce Wayne has to find his direction in life. So it was important that they find the right actor who can embody tightly controlled anger and channel it into the persona of Batman. And Christian Bale is that actor.

Bale has always been an actor worthy of notice. After I saw The Machinist, a part that required him to lose half his body weight I was convinced he is an actor with an almost obsessive desire to embody a role. And its this quality that makes him perfectly suited as Bruce Wayne/Batman.

Its a good solid hour before we even see Bale in the cape and cowl. This allows enough time to explore Bruce Wayne's struggle with his dark half. Never has Batman's origins been told in such detail. Something not even Tim Burton's Batman films can attest to.

There are wonderful scenes in this part of the film with the conflicted Bale and his teacher, Henri Ducard (an excellent Liam Neeson), a member of the League of Shadows. An organisation that wants to harness Bruce's need for justice (or revenge). Neeson gets to play a bit of an Obi-Wan Kenobi, and gets a lot of rich dialogue to spout:

"A vigilante is just a man lost in the scramble for his own gratification."

The first half of Batman Begins is beautifully constructed. Each part of his origin falls into place a piece at a time. Bruce wants to kill his parents murderer, and is beaten to it by somebody else, robbing him of his revenge. And I particularly loved the way Bruce comes to embody the symbol of the Bat. In an ingenious twist, bats are what he fears most, but Ducard teaches him to embrace his fear and use it against those who prey on the fearful.

When Bruce returns to Gotham City, now the origins are out the way, the story really takes off. And the way Bruce rediscovers himself as the Batman is very satisfying. There are scenes right out of a comic book, like when Bruce discovers the Batcave beneath Wayne Manor, and is enveloped in a swarm of bats and just stands there.

When Bale becomes the Batman, he seems for all the world a truly unearthly creature. Nolan makes sure he cuts a striking figure against the Gotham skyline. And Bale's piercing eyes and voice ensure this is one Batman you won't forget.

Also worthy of mention is the really exceptional cast Nolan has put together. Just look who we have here! Aside from Bale and Neeson, we have Michael Caine who makes a wonderful Alfred. Gary Oldman's a revelation as a young Commissioner Gordon. The always excellent Morgan Freeman as Bruce's weapons designer. And even Rutger Hauer and Tom Wilkinson are here too.

Cillian Murphy is a fine young actor but I think he was a little too young to be playing the part of a criminal psychologist, and one of the film's villains, the Scarecrow. But nonetheless he's totally professional, and infuses his performance with his trademark intensity.

Really the only black mark on BB is Katie Holmes, who's a thoroughly unconvincing assistant DA. She only gives one of her insipid performances, and she's just shoehorned in as the token love interest.

Fans of Tim Burton's Batman sagas may be disappointed this Gotham City has none of the dark psychological atmospherics he brought to the table. It could be any city in the world. And I was disappointed the Batmobile is a tank instead of its usual streamlined self. But remember, they're still sorting things out, and hopefully the Batmobile will metamorphose into its true form as time (and sequels) go by.

Overall though, Batman Begins is a triumph. It's a wonderfully told story. Brilliantly directed, acted and wondrous to behold. Batman is back, and he's better than ever!

10.title: Best origins film ever
10.content:
Since his first dramatic appearance in Detective Comics in 1939, Batman has grown to become a pop-culture icon. From movie serials in the 40's, to a classic campy TV show in the 60's, to a solid animated series in the 90's, fans have thrilled to the super heroics of this unique character. However, as a film franchise, he has brought results that were somewhat less than impressive creatively. While the Tim Burton directed films, BATMAN and BATMAN RETURNS were stylish and dark, they also suffered from plot holes you could drive a Batmobile through. Then Joel Schumacher introduced a Day-Glo sensibility to the Dark Knight in BATMAN FOREVER, before drowning the character in ludicrous costumes (a Bat suit with nipples???), pun-filled foes, and whiney sidekicks in the lousy BATMAN & ROBIN. By then, Batman as cinematic property had become a laughingstock. Fortunately, indie film director Christopher Nolan reinvigorates the franchise in glorious form in BATMAN BEGINS, a reboot of the Batman legend that, for the first time, puts the focus squarely on our hero and not on the over-the-top villains of past films. Nolan also bases the film in a strong semblance of reality that allows the audience to not only accept the possibility of the winged vigilante, but embrace it as well.

Most fans already know the story of how wealthy Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) loses his parents when they are slain during an attempted robbery, but the movie also tells how he chose the bat as his symbol, as well as the steps needed to become the avenger of the night that he turns into. Disillusioned and frustrated by Gotham City's corrupt judicial system, the young Wayne goes abroad to study the criminal mind. Later, while locked in an Asian prison, Wayne is recruited by the enigmatic Ducard (Liam Neeson), who offers him a path in which to focus his anger and hone his skills. Wayne eventually joins his new mentor as a recruit in the mysterious League of Shadows, headed by the sinister Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Wantanabe). Eventually, Wayne realizes that he cannot follow the League's extreme methods of dispensing justice and returns to Gotham to forge his own way. It soon turns out that Wayne's return is just in time as Gotham falls prey to a fear epidemic engineered by the twisted Dr. Jonathan Crane AKA "the Scarecrow" (Cillian Murphy) and a familiar figure from Wayne's past.

From the top on down, this film is blessed with a solid cast that adds wonderfully to Nolan's vision. As the title hero, Christian Bale blows all other Batman portrayers out of the water with his intense and scary take of the role. This is a Batman that you not only fear, but can relate to as well. In fact, he turns in the definitive performance. Michael Caine adds warmth and humor as Wayne's trusty butler, Alfred. Liam Neeson does a great variation of his usual mentor roles as Ducard, a man with his own surprising secret. As an assistant DA and Wayne's childhood friend, Katie Holmes does a nice job with what is basically a thankless role. Cillian Murphy makes for a perfectly creepy Scarecrow, while Morgan Freeman is solid as usual as the man who provides Batman's wondrous car and gadgets. Gary Oldman is wonderfully cast against type as Jim Gordon, one of Gotham's few honest cops. The scene in which he drives the tank-like Batmobile is a sheer delight.

The screenplay by Nolan and David Goyer (who wrote the BLADE films) is awash with characterization and motivation...something that you don't see in many comic book films as a rule. In fact, you get so engrossed by the proceedings that you almost forget that you are watching a "superhero" film in the first place. The special effects are used to enhance the story and not overpower it, while the set design pictures a Gotham that is a unique cross of Chicago, New York and Hong Kong. If there is a flaw, it lies in some of the fight sequences. Done in close-ups and quick cuts, they can get frustrating for those who want to see more of Batman's fighting style. However, this is very minor since the story never ceases to grasp your attention.

In the end, Nolan and his superb cast and crew succeed in achieving what was once thought impossible: the resurrection of a film franchise that, if not dead, was at least on life support. As a result, Batman is once again flying high and BATMAN BEGINS is a film that I wholeheartedly recommend.

10.title: A Dark, Powerful Origin Done Right
10.content:
Batman Begins is a masterclass in how to reboot a hero. Christopher Nolan didn't just tell a Batman story-he redefined what a superhero origin could be. The film dives deep into Bruce Wayne's psyche, balancing emotional weight with gritty action and world-building that feels grounded yet mythic.

Christian Bale brings intensity and complexity to the role, supported by a strong cast-Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, and Cillian Murphy all deliver. The villains don't just fill time; they serve the story and its themes, adding layers of fear, justice, and identity.

The tone is dark without being grim, the visuals are rich and immersive, and Hans Zimmer's score ties it all together with emotional punch. Every element feels purposeful-from the League of Shadows to the streets of Gotham-and the action scenes have real weight and tension.

This isn't just a good superhero movie-it's an excellent film, period. It laid the foundation for one of the greatest trilogies in cinema and still holds up incredibly well. Rewatch-worthy, iconic, and deeply satisfying.

10.title: Filmgasm
10.content:
I hope my title doesn't offend anyone, but I have to say that that term just about encompasses the feelings one will have after watching this film. I cant imagine anyone having anything horrible to say about this, the latest incarnation of the Batman Story. Fans of the comics as well and comers to the Dark Knight alike can enjoy the tale told here.

A wonderful adaptation of the origin story of one of the most well known superheroes, Batman Begins simply has it all. Excellent acting, amazing cast, tremendous writing, and insightful directing. There is no aspect of this film that will leave you unsatisfied. My only wish after watching th is film is that it were a TV serial instead, that way I could tune into it every week. Nolan and Bale got it right.

There's enough action to keep the burliest of men interested, and enough passion and intrigue to get the girlfriend hooked (Pardon the sexiest stereotypes). There are no lags in the film as the story flows from moment to moment with great ease.

If pressed to find criticisms, I would say Cillian Murphy as Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow was not given enough to work with. I would have liked to have seen him more involved and not a secondary status character as he was used.

I eagerly await all the sequels they intend on making, and hope this train doesn't stop.

10.title: The first "Batman" movie that does NOT suck !
10.content:
I am officially IMPRESSED by "Batman Begins". It exceeded by many, many, many orders of magnitude all of my expectations (meaning, they were very low). I had no idea I could be so enthusiastic about a (recent) movie.

Where do I begin ? Well, the subject: Batman. The only well-known character worthy of the name "superhero" that isn't "super" at all, which says a lot. You might even say this movie isn't a "prequel", but a whole new restart of the entire franchise, and I hope that WHEN (not if) they decide to make the next one, they'll maintain same style.

The actors ? Most of the main characters were almost perfectly casted. Christian Bale (Equilibrium) as Bruce Wayne was just the right mix between muscle and looks, and even if he does seem pretty stiff at times, he fits the character perfectly. Michael Caine as Alfed (the butler), Morgan Freeman as Fox (call him the "tech guy") Liam Neeson as Ducard (the "inspiration" figure)... they all fit the roles they played like a glove, I couldn't even imagine who else would have been better instead. Gary Oldman as Gordon was slightly disappointing, but only because he had way too little screen time. Katie Holmes as "the girl" was so-so, I would have expected a less cute-and-cuddly-looking actress casted for that part, but she also played her role quite well.

The plot ? Ah, the weak spot of all comic-book adaptations. Now, THAT one was the biggest surprise of all, and a very pleasant one indeed. There is NO major bullshit in there. Almost everything makes perfect sense. Only in a very few short scenes you start to go "now, wait, that can't really happen, now can it?", but those moments are quickly dismissed by the ensuing action or plot development. There's quite a bit of "deviation" in the story from what you might come to know from the established franchise, but all of them are for the better (and more "believable").

There's so much more to say, but I don't want to spoil the fun. GO SEE THE MOVIE IF YOU HAVEN'T ALREADY.

10.title: Batman Begins (2005)
10.content: This movie is an impeccable start to the Batman/The Dark Knight Trilogy and does a nearly perfect setting up Batman, Bruce Wayne, Gotham, and the rest of the main characters in Gotham. The plot, settings, theme, dialogue, characters, character scenes, character development, actor performances, deaths, soundtrack, cinematography, choreography, visuals, CGI, practical effects, plot twists, opening scene, and ending are all impeccable. Christian Bale is nearly perfect as the leading role of Bruce Wayne / Batman. Michael Caine as Alfred, Liam Neeson as Ducard, Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes, and Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon are all nearly perfect in their starring roles. Cillian Murphy as Dr. Jonathan Crane, Tom Wilkinson as Carmine Falcone, Rutger Hauer as Earle, Linus Roache as Thomas Wayne, Mark Boone Junior as Flass, Ken Watanabe as Ra's Al Ghul, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Larry Holden as Finch, Gerald Murphy as Judge Faden, Colin McFarlane as Loeb, Sara Stewart as Martha Wayne, Gus Lewis as Bruce Eayne - Age 8, Richard Brake as Joe Chill, and Rade Sherbedgia as Homeless Man are all impeccable to incredible in their starring and supporting roles. This movie does an impeccable job developing Batman, Bruce Wayne, Gotham City, and the chemistry between all the characters. I love all the villians and all the chemistry between all the characters like Christian Bale and Michael Caine, Christian Bale and Katie Holmes, Christian Bale and Gary Oldman, Katie Holmes and Cillian Murphy, and Christian Bale and Morgan Freemen. The ending of this movie is impeccable and the Action Epic, Epic, Superhero, Tragedy, Action, Crime, Drama, and Thriller Aspects are all done nearly perfectly. I absolutely recommend you watch this movie if you like Batman Films, Christopher Nolan Films, or if you like Action Epics, Epics, Superhero Films, Tragedy Films, Action Films, Crime Films, Drama Films, or Thrillers. I rate this movie a 9.8 out of 10.

10.title: Best Batman Movie, Best Comicbook Movie, Great Film
10.content:
Christopher Nolan has created a universe for Batman that is beyond our wildest expectations. We get to see Bruce Wayne, from the hurt child at his parent's murder, over a young man consumed by rage and guilt, transform into the heroic identity of the Batman. Christian Bale performs amazingly as Wayne, giving us a deep glance into the character's dark soul. He is equally outstanding as the man in the cape and cowl, bringing menace to every word and importance to every look. Michael Keaton will always be my childhood's Batman, but Bale has brought the Bat back into my adult life.

The other actors shine as well. This is bar none the best ensemble cast for a superhero movie and even one of the best casts I've seen in a LONG time. From the endearing and witty Michael Caine (Alfred), to the always splendid Morgan Freeman (Lucius Fox), the lovely Katie Holmes (Rachel Dawes) and the utterly classy Liam Neeson (Ducard), Bruce's allies and mentors are indeed a delight to watch. Even more so are the villains, exploring all different shades of evil in Gotham, with Ken Watanabe (Ra's Al Ghul), Tom Wilkinson (Falcone), Rutger Hauer (Earle) and the outstanding Cillian Murphy (Jonathan Crane / Scarecrow) all giving deliciously nuanced performances.

Christopher Nolan and his cinematographer Wally Pfister really brought to the film what they promised: an epic scope, beautiful shots reminiscent of "Laurence of Arabia" and "Blade Runner" and a return to the traditional, but by no means bland or uninspired, action adventure story. It has amazing dramatic flow, good dialogue, fantastic characters and an intelligent, layered plot.

A great movie, the very best its genre has to offer and a cinematic treat to any film fan.

Each Character had his own life and troubles and acts so. -Catches the Batman Mood, but goes even beyond.It is more Realistic but not too much (The Dark Knight). -The Music and the Epicness is unrivaled by other Comic Adaptions. -Just watch it.

It is said that they tried to imitate the Blade Runner Atmosphere, but i think this Movie did it even better.

10.title: The greatest film
10.content:
I have been waiting for this film for years, I remember the excitement I experienced 2 years ago when they announced the casting of my favourite actor (and my top choice for the Dark Knight) Christian Bale as the Batman. 2 years later I was watching him giving an Oscar worthy performance as the intimidating, scary and tough S.O.B the Batman. Christian Bale owned in this film and we finally we got a Batman film where Batman was the main focus of the film and not the villain. Bale's performance was better than Keaton's (whom I loved as Batman) and even better than what many consider the definitive Batman Kevin Conroy (as did I until now) The dull performance of Val Kilmer and George Clooney playing himself in a batsuit don't even count as Batmen in my book. I also don't think i'll compare Adam West (he played a camp Batman and was good for the time but now that performance and show are seriously outdated).

This film makes Tim Burton's Batman look like Power Rangers on steroids and makes you realise how bad the sets and style were of those films. I loved the pacing of the film, how everything had an explanation and the performances by all actors involved in this film. This in my opinion is without a doubt the definitive Batman film and the greatest film ever made. Well done Chris Nolan you nailed it.

10.title: Amazing... The best movie you'll see this summer
10.content: Batman is back and better than ever in this newest film. Director Christopher Nolan does a fine job of capturing the darkness of Gotham, and he offers a disturbing insight into the effects of fear on a person. Bruce Wayne begins in an Asian prison, where he is rescued by the league of shadows. Here he learns to confront his fear and returns to Gotham to clean up the corruption that now rules the city. The acting is great, with standout performances by Christian Bale and Liam Neeson in particular. The story is very fluid, and it is easy to follow. I can't wait for the sequel to happen, whenever it does. If you only see one movie this summer, make this the one.

10.title: The Dark Night is born
10.content:
I am very proud to say that this film was very closely related to Frank Miller's (writer of the Sin City comics) 1997 graphic novel, "Batman: Year One". The story of a fearful, angry, grief-stricken Bruce who is still, after 18 years of the event, trying to cope with the murder of his parents. In the book, Bruce has returned to his hometown after being away for 12 years (in the movie this time is shortened to 7), during which he trained to become a vigilante. Wayne's first attempt at crime fighting ends in disaster, but leads him ultimately to adopt the bat motif so as to inspire fear in criminals. So for all who have experienced the movie, you can see the similarities in both. I was talking with a friend about successful movies made from books, and we came to the agreement that the closer the book is written into the script, the more efficient the movie will be. Specially with a fanatic audience. Nolan was very intelligent in knowing that.

One thing I did notice was missing from the movie were some scruples on Gordon's side. According to the comic books, Gordon as a cop is trained in hand to hand combat and although he is a bit rusty, he's still better than most. He doesn't so much at all fight in this movie; he doesn't do much more than cower. But hey, he's about the only cop who isn't corrupt, right? Good for him. And Gary Oldman's acting was great, to say they least...it just seems so hard for me to say anything bad about this film.

I spoke with some people about what they didn't like about the film...and the arguments were these: 1. Too many cheesy one liners; and 2. Fight scenes were hard to follow. Although these are good reasons why not to like the film, my answer to them are 1. The one liners were there to pump up the comic book lingo and motif; and 2. As you can recall, the fight scenes with Ra's Al Ghul (KEN WATANABE) were easy to follow, but when he became the Dark Nigh, they were a little less clear. My assumption is that Nolan's technique was to create a relationship between the villain and the audience based on fear and confusion. Batman's purpose was to mimic the shadows, and it is never an easy task to follow a shadow.

I have to say, I was a bit worried on the outcome of this film. We can all remember the tragedy that was 1997's Batman and Robin. That film is arguably the worst of all Batman movies, but in reality...there is no argument. Batman and Robin was a terrible movie, and I was not ready see the fate of batman fall into that sad category.

When talk of this new movie came about...roughly three years ago, crazy batman fans such as myself have anticipated the growth of this project with much fear. It all sounds really good, but somehow, they're going to mess it up, right? Christopher Nolan was a great choice for directing this movie. Memento was a wonderful film and one of my favorites. In Batman Begins, the casting was picked very well. The acting is superb. The stylistic choices are very successful for this movie. Gotham city has never been depicted in a truer light. The villains, although still menacing, are more common than the fantastical versions that have come before, and thats because of the solid fact that batman created his villains. This is very well put towards the end of the movie, during a conversation between Jim Gordon and "the" Batman. Overall, I recommend this movie to anyone, everyone, and their mother.

Thanks to Chris Nolan, Batman finally Begins from here....

10.title: One of best superhero origin story
10.content: This definitely made me love with the character batman.

10.title: Dark, thrilling, and exciting
10.content: This movie was absolutely dark, thrilling, and exciting. Christian Bale who played Batman was terrific and all of these great actors Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, and Morgan Freeman. The movie was shot in Chicago such as Wayne Tower which is the Board of Trade building, and the tumbler chase scene at the lower Wacker Drive. Also, the special effects of the monorail down La Salle Street looks great. This movie is one of my best films.

10.title: One of the BEST movies EVER MADE!!!
10.content: Usually I don't give a 10 out of 10 rating, or a good review for that matter. But this film deserves a just praise. This film has convinced me that a movie doesn't have to be depressing, violent, or R-rated to be good. Before I saw this I had a strange tendency to develop obsessions over films like Sin City which is also based off a comic book, but contains graphic and disturbing violent content. This film on the other hand relies on it's creativeness, and style to make an impact. Batman Begins does something that few other films do. Some thing that is contained with in the very title. This title is almost like a statement; "Batman Begins." Implying the promise of sequels to come, which as it turns out they are keeping their promise, and the sequel isn't called some none imaginative title like "Batman 2", or "Batman Returns" in fact the sequel doesn't even contain the word 'batman' in the title, it evolves just like any good series should and is called simply THE DARK KNIGHT. They really milked this one for everything that it was worth. When they are designing the bat-suit they don't simply come up with the idea for it in mere seconds (like in Star Wars episode 3 where they just toss it on Vader in mere scene cuts, or DareDevil where they don't even explain how he got all those gadgets) no they show that the characters actual had some difficulty in designing the suit, and at one point Batman can be seen trotting around in a prototype version showing that the characters didn't always have things figured out. It gives them a more realistic quality. Like when Alfred inquires as to why Bruce is making his throwing stars in the shape in the shape of bats to which Bruce explains; "Bats scare me I just want my enemies to share my fear." There is even given a reason for why Bruce created his persona of Batman. He states; "As a man I can be weakened I can be corrupted, but as a *symbol*... as a *symbol* I can be strong I can be irrefutable." It's so great to see a version that does the character justice. I don't usually have moments where I am rooting for the characters but this was a rare time when I was. We don't need to see Batman kill people just seeing him flying around with that special cape lets us feel his power. I believe this has the potential to be the greatest movie series since Star Wars, and with their dedication to staying true to the comic books, not just in the portrayal of events but in tone, I excitedly look forward to the next great sequel.

10.title: Incredible film that brings the Dark Knight back to his roots.
10.content: He finally makes sense. For more than 10 years any one walking in off the streets would be totally baffled by the thought of a man dressing up as a bat. Why a bat? Isn't that sort of random? This film explains it. This film makes plausible the fantastic. Christian Bale not only looks the part of the playboy, but he is fantastic as Batman as well. Michael Caine is a fantastic Alfred, playing it as stern but loving. Liam Neeson shows once again that he is extraordinary at playing the mentor. Cillian Murphy is fantastic as the creepy Scarecrow. Morgan Freeman plays the "Q" type character, supplying Bruce with all his tools. This Batman film does what even recent comics doesn't: Makes it real and still fun. In closing, I loved this movie and everyone who enjoys good stories should see it.

10.title: Not a typical superhero film
10.content: This film has 2 subjects I enjoy: Psychology and Philosophy. The Psychological aspect is fear. This is shown in the throughout the film that Bruce got to overcome the fear to save himself and Gotham. The Philosophy aspect is mainly what principle Bruce has and decision he made based on it. Both aspect is a good build up from the start till the end and now I know why people love Batman.

10.title: Batter than ever!
10.content: This movie is really good. It has really intense action scenes and a great story. Everything is great in this movie but there were somethings that I didn't like. One was that in the Batman Comics Joker is the man that killed Batman's parents and then they show him get shot after the trial. Another thing at the end Scarecrow gets hit by a tazer and runs away, so you never exactly know if he is dead. One last thing is, if anyone noticed, Batman sounded a lot like Keanu Reeves. I highly recommend that you see this movie it is probably the best Batman movie yet. After you see this you should watch the first Batman movie because it ties right into it.

10.title: The best big screen Batman.
10.content:
It is hard to judge this version of Batman compared to its previous (few) movies; that is, the absurdity of those interpretations of the Dark Knight were just about ridiculous enough to make any comparisons rather insulting to this fresh vision of the most popular comic book character of the 20th century. This isn't the nippled costume wearer who drools over Poison Ivy and offers his Bat-credit card to buy her gifts. This is... far from that.

Batman Begins takes us, as the title suggests, to the roots. A boy's world is shattered by two bullets that take his parents away forever, and he might as well have died there with them; his demons scream in his ears ever since as he grows first into a bitter and angry young man, and then into an obsessive wanderer with vague ambitious of restoring justice and protecting the innocent from those who would pray upon them - somehow.

We watch Bruce Wayne's fall and rise in his most fascinating portrayal by Christian Bale; his work is excellent, maintaining the brooding, dark moods that rage within the character and maintaining a bitter sense of humor none of those who played the same role before - perhaps with the exception of Michael Keaton - managed to even come close to.

The greatest strength of the film is not even the excellent supporting cast that seems to be having genuine fun with the whole ride; Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, they all carry the movie just far enough to justify Caped Crusader not even be _seen_ until halfway through the movie, without taking anything away from its value - and, indeed, it only lends strength to his first appearance, making the gadgets in that utility belt actually have meaning after we witness the costumeless Wayne almost fall to his death in his first attempt at rooftop jumping.

Perhaps a sore point of the movie could be considered to be the presence of Katie Holmes; she's cute and everything, but I can't help but notice the undertones of teen soap opera in every line she speaks, and truly lacks the intensity required for a supposed idealist trying to make a difference in the most corrupt city in the world; Gotham City.

10.title: The Best Movie of the Year.
10.content:
Last night I attended a midnight showing of this movie and it blew me away. Christopher Nolan deserves a bow for the best Batman-heck, best MOVIE of the year. While I always enjoy comic book and action films there have a lot of dull flops( Hulk, Electra...)these past years. But Batman Begins makes the whole genre so much more fresh, original and exciting. I judge comic book films by their ability to entertain with action and special effects, not great plots, characters or dialog; I leave that type of criticism for dramas and war epics and whatnot. Yet Batman Begins deserves a lot more praise and recognition for what it is- superior movie-making.

Christian Bale gives a great performance as Bruce Wayne/Batman. As does also supporting cast Liam Neeson, Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine and even Katie Holmes. The movie takes place before the original Batman movies and tells how and why Bruce Wayne becomes Batman. From the reason why he dressed himself in a bat costume, the Batmobile, the Bate Cave all is explained. The action and fighting is incredible, realistic and gritty; the movie is fast-paced and engrossing and will leave you absolutely stunned. 10/10

10.title: The definitive Batman is born !
10.content: Christopher Nolan has created the best Batman film ever, with a plot that makes the masked hero's evolution into a champion of justice believable. A superlative Christian Bale, perfect for expressiveness and interpretative ability, flanked by a cast of the highest quality which sees Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Leam Neeson and Gary Oldman in the key roles. Vivid settings, Gotham almost palpable in its dark reality sees its favorite son evolve from the condition of privileged to that of a symbol of justice. Simply the best superhero film ever produced, surpassed perhaps only by its sequel, The Dark Knight.

10.title: Batman really returns
10.content:
I was quite impressed with this Batman. At first, i was not even going to consider watching it on the cinemas, but i started to unveil the list of actors. Cristian Bale?? The main actor of the superb movie equilibrium and the Machinist, started to surprise me and than i decided to go and watch the movie.

I was really impressed. This is actually the image from Batman i have from the B.D books i used to read when i was younger.

This movie , has achieved a super-hero image, so close to the designed on the 90's Comics, that X-man, and the fantastic four are light -years away from this amazing movie.

A must see. I already did it 2times.....

10.title: Not just the best batman movie, but the best movie that you can ever watch!
10.content:
This movie is the most underrated movies among all others, and this is mainly due to its brilliant sequel TDK which people liked due to Heath's immortal Joker acting. But for me there is no movie better than Batman Begins.

It is the only movie which brilliantly explains the journey of a common man from just a nobody, to a superhuman, a symbol feared by criminals. We've all seen previous batman movies and sort of assumed batman or any other superhuman character with the special abilities from the go. This movie portrays Bruce Wayne character in detail, his struggles, fear and the desire, the reason he became batman. It is all very very engaging.

The storyline is one of best from Christopher Nolan with so many odds stacked against batman which he has to confront to save Gotham. It's one movie in which you remain on the edge all the time. On top of that the acting and especially dialogues are one of the best you can have in any movie.

This is one batman movie which moves you and encourage you to have that level of dedication for our community that Bruce Wayne had. A must watch.

10.title: The Movie The Dark Knight Finally Deserves.
10.content: Finally The Dark Knight has hit cinema as he should have, forget Batman Forever and Batman and Robin the whole Dark Knight Image and Vision is not mean't for kids. The whole Batman/Dark Knight character deals with issues such as Revenge,Murder,Crime,Insanity and Despair these things are not to be put in a kids film. Batman and Batman Returns were both Great Films but they will be separate from Batman Begins (Different Origins and Darker Vision)the others were plain overplayed kids crap that are not worth watching.I would compare this movie with Brandon Lee's The Crow as both have got the Bleak Comic Book Vision Perfectly and the Title Characters are incredible. The Crow is another amazing film that tackles the serious issues as above. Bale is Awesome in the title role capturing the calmness and despair of Bruce Wayne and switching to the Sheer Aggression/Rage and Darkness of Batman and the other actors Oldman,Caine,Hauer,etc play the characters perfectly but this is definitely Bale's Movie. The setting is perfect,capturing a time 5-10yrs from now and with present day issues(crime,poverty,etc).The Sets and Visuals are Fantastic and the Images on Screen are Mindblowing.The score is also spot on and it gives a feeling of emotion to key scenes. Let's just hope that the Dark Knight Films get Darker and More Brutal and that they keep hold of the actors (Bale,Oldman,etc)and go back to it's origins because the Future of the Dark Knight does not exist in camp,overplayed kids films, let's just hope the movie moguls understand this! it's more than just bums on seats. There are tons of films out there but very few with real substance, but this has it and in bucket loads.

10.title: The legend ends here
10.content:
I will always love the fiction character Batman. I saw the first one, at Cinema when I was twelve. The one starring, M.Keaton. After that, No Batman movie that followed was good at all. It went downhill very fast. Until this one came. The dark atmospheric mystery, like in the first one will not appear in Batman Begins. But its all the rest, that is so well formed from scratch to; -Im Batman. The first time I saw it, I didn't really went childish and wanted to be the Batman. Its to mature and smart for that, a movie that needs full focus from you. And If you let it, You might love it.

Some might have issues with movies with pieces of different time sessions, like this one will offer. But It, just makes the movie even better. Best Movie yet. I do rank movies I like very much to 10. But if 11 was available , this Movie would have been the only one at that score even today.

No More Remakes/Reboots pls of Batman, The legend begins, and end here

10.title: Batman's return to the big screen is a hit!
10.content:
Warner Bros. released four previous live-action Batman films. Those films are not related to Batman Begins. What the title of this film indicates is that this is the beginning of a new series. After the fiasco that was 1997's Batman & Robin we could have declared that series dead. Here, director Christopher Nolan and screenwriter David Goyer attempt to bring a more faithful adaptation of the comic book. There have been so many incarnations of Batman in the comic books that I really don't know what that's supposed to mean.

What makes Batman Begins such a great film is that it allows the audience a better chance of getting to know the character of Batman/Bruce Wayne. The film explores Wayne's back story to every single detail. After you're done watching this film you could probably call yourself an expert in Batman's genesis.

However, the film has its flaws. The Scarecrow for instance is an example. I understand the character's purpose in this film, but like Dr. Doom in the Fantastic Four movie of this year, he doesn't really do anything special.

RATING: 4 (****) out of (****)

Features amazing performances by Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Liam Neeson. Bale is physically the best Batman to appear on the big screen to date. Performance-wise I do not know if he is technically yet the best. Let's see how he does in the sequel.

10.title: Shockingly Great!!
10.content:
I first became aware of this movie back in January. After the other 4 movies, I had zero interest in seeing "Batman Begins." But then the positive word-of-mouth and the good/great reviews began mounting. Also, who could resist the cast?! I saw it a few days after it was released.

This movie both blindsided and shocked me with its greatness!! Nothing prepared me for it. It is THE movie of the Summer. The one I've TRULY been waiting for (I thought it was "Revenge of the Sith.").

This is the movie that should've come out in 1989. The Batman movie that fans deserved, but didn't get. (For those of you old enough - remember those long lines back then? How they either wrapped around the theater or were several city blocks long? I do.)

Where to start? There is so much to love about this movie. The following are my comments thinking back on the movie I just saw:

1. It's apparent that a lot of thought, heart and hard work went into every frame.

2. The material was respected and taken seriously. It's a comic-book movie by adults, FOR adults (and unlike "Hulk," it succeeds!).

3. There aren't really any silly one-liners or "Rocky Horror"/crowd-pleasing/sell-out moments (where the audience cheers/claps, etc.). No pop-psychology crap ("Spider-Man" movies).

4. The dialogue and scenes are consistent with the characters and within reason.

5. The spectacular, exciting scenes taking place on a highway, the other a train.

6. I loved the dynamic score during a scene involving Bruce Wayne and his progress within the League of Shadows (you'll know the scene).

7. Killer cast. Christian Bale and Cillian Murphy were both superb and unforgettable.

8. Smaller, quieter moments involving simple, common words. In one of the movie's best scenes, Gordon thanks Batman and his words have WEIGHT. Batman's response has equal weight. And, as far as I'm concerned, the movie earned my emotional reaction to that scene.

9. It's just damn thrilling and exciting seeing Bruce Wayne's transformation into Batman. This is half of the movie's running time right here, and I'm thankful for that. We get to know, understand and like Bruce Wayne/Batman.

This movie is for anyone who loves great cinema. You don't have to be a comic book fan! (I'm not.) Just see it!! It is by far the best Batman movie ever made AND the best comic-book adaptation since "Superman II." (I'm thinking about seeing it again as I type this!)

10.title: fanboys gather here please
10.content:
batman fanboys finally has a movie to be victoriously shoved to other comic book fans' faces and glee in victory. this is saying a lot, i'm a x-men fan since a child and i found this movie the best comic book adaptation and the best movie this year, so far.

you read that right people, nothing touches batman begins. before i tell you how awesome batman begins is, i would like to do something a lot of batman fans have been dying to do to the people who are in self-denial: to the people who thinks star wars crapisode 3 is better than this, go bury yourself alive. it'd be nice if you can take george lucas with you too.

back to the movie. christopher nolan, incorrectly labelled as a director no one knows, shows just how a comic book movie is still able to keep up with high-quality movies that deserve Oscar nominations. he showed us a comic book movie that doesn't try too hard to be a comic book. Needless to mention he pulled it off beautifully. Beautiful directing, beautiful settings and beautiful imagery.

The actors are solid too. Christian Bale does the perfect bruce wayne. Of course some might say keaton's voice as batman was better than bale's but if you look at the bigger picture, who cares about batman's voice? As long as he doesn't sound like hello kitty on helium or have stupid cheesy lines, I'm fine. Alfred was done really well, the choices they've made for the main villains and supporting characters were brilliant too. Ken Watanabe, Liam Neeson and Cillian Murphy did their job superbly. And yea, you star wars fanboys, ep3 was made up of the cheesiest dialogues ever and some of the worst acting this new millennium has seen.

enough crapisode 3 bashing.

this has got to be the most realistic comic book-based movie so far. although some things are still a bit impossible to be pulled off in real life, there's enough science behind it to convince you that it's possible.

beautiful, beautiful movie. this might be the only movie that makes "fanboy-ism" a reasonable thing to do. this is a superb movie.

it's amazing how that guy who did blade trinity can come up with this fantastic script. the combination for this movie is perfect.

only problem would have been the action scenes, it's hard to see who's punching who sometimes.

however this seemingly big flaw is overshadowed by the countless excellent things that makes up this movie that it turns into a very minor problem.

you'll enjoy this movie.

10.title: Batman on an epic scale
10.content:
This is the most incredible Batman movie I have ever seen, when you consider both the Keaton/Kilmer/Clooney series and the Bale series. I think I like this film just a hair better than The Dark Knight. There is perfection in how the filmmakers tell the story of Batman's origins. I'm not speaking of faithfulness to the comics, because I don't bother reading the comics. I'm speaking of pure film-making quality, cinematography, acting, music, and directing. The pace of storytelling was perfect; there was a lot of story to tell in this film but they did not overload it. There were no slow parts, and no cramming of stuff into a short period of time like they had in Spider-Man 3. The placement and usage of flashbacks was done well too. I like how half of the film was devoted to Batman's training, and the other half devoted to his first major campaign against crime in Gotham City. It took me a couple viewings to completely understand all that was going on but I liked how they tied the League of Shadows to his training and then to being his ultimate enemy later in the film. Ra's al Guhl was awesomely played by Liam Neeson. The teamwork between him and Scarecrow, very well done. And of course there's the musical score, provided to us by the musical genius of Hans Zimmer. Although the soundtrack for The Dark Knight is superior, it largely contains the same music and is very, very good. The music really set the mood and the power of the film quite well. I also highly approve of the choices of Michael Caine to play Alfred, and Morgan Freeman is amazing in almost any movie he does. Any movie gets extra points just for having Morgan Freeman in it. While the Tim Burton films were enjoyable, I like that this movie was more realistic without over the top camp or art deco. It looked like real life, not fantasy. Not over-stylized like the Joel Schumaker ones. Simply perfect. I can't even find anybody in the film that needs a punch in the face!

The filmmakers have set the bar really, really high for the new Batman series with Batman begins. Miraculously, equaled their success with their release of The Dark Knight. Because of these two films, the 3rd Batman movie has two tough acts to follow. Let us hope the series is not ruined.

See my profile to understand my rating philosophy.

10.title: Batmans back! And you better believe it!
10.content:
When i first heard of a new batman film i was a bit cautious due to the complete muck ups like batman forever and batman and robin.

But Finally Batman Begins has been out and is spectacular let me take you through it.

The plot is that Bruce Wayne has his parents killed when he was young. Distraught by this all his life he travels the world to understand the criminal mind. He joins an old group known as the leauge of shadows but leaves them and returns to gotham city to fight injustice as Batman.

Good points: The cast was an amazing choice. Christian bale as batman was a great choice and the always great Michael Caine as his butler Alfred. Cillian Murphey Plays his first villain scarecrow and he plays his role with great flare.

The amount of darkness. And i don't mean like how dark it was at night. I mean that it was a dark film. Batman always needed to be dark and even Tim Burton didn't get it right when you compare the two.

Batmobile has an amazing new look. While the first batmobile looked good the new batmobile looks astounding. The whole design of it is a stroke of genius and it's car chase was amazing.

Bad point: You would have noticed i put bad point rather than bad points because there is only one bad thing about this film and that is one person. KATIE HOLMES. her acting is more wooden than a walk in a forest. But this doesn't ruin this gem of a movie.

10.title: Fear is the key
10.content:
I liked the movie. It is by far one of the best super-hero movies I have seen for a long time.

Fear is the key. Why are we afraid? As a kid, we are afraid of the dark. As a teen, we are afraid of being turned down for a date. As a man, we are afraid of LIFE. A man is afraid of losing his job. A man is afraid of losing his family. A man is afraid of his own shadow.

Life is all about conquering that fear. The great men are those who have braved the world, vanquished their fear, made fear their friend, their weapon.

'Batman Begins' is about conquering that fear. Bruce Wayne is the man within all of us. He is the mask behind which we all hide to protect ourselves. Batman is the Bruce Wayne who has conquered his fear. And that is why he is the ideal superhero. Batman is the man we all try to become, but can't because we are afraid. Rachel says in the end,"Perhaps I will come back Bruce, when Batman is needed no more". That's the ideal state -- when Bruce Wayne does not need Batman for his protection anymore.

10.title: The Batman film we have always wanted.
10.content: Batman Begins gets it right on every level. The story behind why Bruce becomes Batman. We get to know how he was trained. We get to see the transformation of Bruce to Batman in the most realistic way. This movie delivers exactly what you want from a superhero film. Not a lot of CGI, so the film feels more real. Everytime I watch this film I forget I am watching a superhero film. This movie is amazing and the beginning of one of the best trilogies ever made. Nolan did a excellent job and this is just the first of three masterpieces of his Batman trilogy.

10.title: ...It's been a long wait, but it was worth it...
10.content:
Just seen it, walked out of the cinema jazzed - just like I felt after seeing the Lord of the Rings movies. For a long time I was worried that LoTR was the pinnacle of movie making and I would never get the same buzz from a film again - Batman Begins gave me back my faith in films as an entertainment - and I will see it again.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that Batman Begins is a perfect film, neither am I saying that it is better than the LoTR trilogy - they are epics and stand head and shoulders above anything I have seen. But for what seems like an age everything I've seen at the cinema since Return of the King has been a bit mediocre in comparison. I've seen some pretty good films in this time (and some rotten ones too!) But none of them has given me the same buzz... until now.

I rode the hype back in '89 when Tim Burton's Batman was released. I started reading comics for the first time in my life (at the tender age of 18) and was immediately hooked on Legends of the Dark Knight, and to this day consider The Dark Knight Returns and Batman: Year One, two of the best books I have ever read, the fact that they are 'comics' shouldn't diminish the story, rather it is an enhancement - If you've never read a comic, or consider them childish or poor excuses for fiction (and lets face it, some of them do indeed fit this description), I implore you to pick up a copy of The Dark Knight Returns - it'll change your mind and open your eyes. So, after having a revelation and discovering (comparatively late) the delights of comics on the back of the movie hype, when I finally saw it I was sorely disappointed. It's not a bad movie, but it contains fundamental flaws in the mythos of the character and was too much like a cartoon for my taste. 'Returns' was more promising, but Tim Burton lost my respect when the 'penguin army' made an appearance. Too 1960's for my taste. I had high hopes for Joel Schumacher, Flatliners was a pretty good film, but he took all the things I hated about the Burton Batman and accentuated them - I hate 'Forever' and '& Robin' was farcical and by this time almost sacrilege to someone who had become an ardent fan of the comics.

I am grateful to WB and Tim Burton for bringing the character to my attention and giving me another passion in life, but at the same time I felt they had screwed up big time and denied the world the chance to see Batman for what he is. Whatever the reason, I have been waiting since 1989 for a big screen treatment that does the character some justice and Batman Begins is exactly what I have been waiting for. Thank you for giving me what I have been crying out for. A Batman that is a lot truer to the source material than the TV show and one that I will see again and buy when the opportunity arrives.

'Begins' takes elements of the graphic novel 'Batman: Year One' (written by Frank Miller, of Sin City fame), adds in Ras Al Ghul (one of writer Denny O'Neil's greatest creations) and classic baddie the Scarecrow, sets them in a believable Gotham City and then presents Batman for what he is - a traumatised little boy, forced to watch his parents' murder and set on a path that will consume him. A brilliant detective, a gifted combateer, a resourceful opponent, a frightening winged beast and above all a man on the edge of sanity, driven beyond comprehension by the need to avenge his parents deaths. Batman is full of pathos and walks a razor's edge that separates him from those he fights, he is scary as hell, mysterious, brilliant and totally driven - this is the Batman I crave, and it is the reason he is still around after so many years. Thank you for restoring my faith in movies and giving back a large helping of credibility to Batman.

There are some problems with the film, some of the plot lines are a little bit too fantastical for my liking (not enough realism), Ras Al Ghul is one of Batman's most deadly foes (and will return, like Lazarus ;-) ), but he isn't scary enough in the film and is supposed to be of middle eastern origin. Liam Neeson does a very good job, but was a little miss cast in my opinion. But these are pretty minor.

The pros far outweigh the cons. Gary Oldman is excellent as Jim Gordon, the bat signal (not the searchlight, the other bat signal) is straight out of Year One and is superb, the acting is generally first rate, as are the effects and also the plot which builds and builds and builds. The fight scenes are superbly done considering the material - Batman 'strikes fear into the hearts of criminals' and therefore is mysterious, sudden and devastating. Fights are glimpsed, Batman is an unstoppable, malevolent force rather than a balletic kung fu / matrix style show for the camera. The movie is well paced, setting all the right foundations and then building through set pieces to the finale, the character development is well set out and superbly performed, Christian Bale in particular does very well, especially when you see the A class talent he is acting against. Chris Nolan does a first rate job telling the tale, setting the scene and throwing more than enough thrills and spills to the audience.

To you movie goers out there. Go and see it, it's a great evening's entertainment.

To the movie makers. More of the same please.

10.title: An almost perfect origin story!
10.content: There have been many Batman movies before, but this is the first to actually tell his origin! Previous movies have only mentioned it, or had a short flashback about it. This one takes it's time and is as much of a Bruce Wayne movie as a Batman movie! It also shows how life is in Gotham before Batman, and what motivates Bruce to do what he does. Every aspect of the story gets it's fair share of time, and it never feels rushed or dragging. The cast is very good, which is expected since most are well established actors. 10.title: "Batman Begins"- A stirring and gripping retelling of the Batman legend.
10.content:
Director Christopher Nolan ushers in his now mythical "Dark Knight Trilogy" with this stirring and gripping rebirth of the Batman legend. 2005's "Batman Begins" is very much a revelation, showing us a keen new vision and a darkly gritty reboot of a story that spans back for decades. In many ways the most psychologically complex and realistically grounded version of the character to ever grace the screen, here we finally get a good sense of the iconic Bruce Wayne as a startlingly true-to-life human being, resulting in a compelling and often fulfilling movie experience.

In a fractured and somewhat non-linear narrative, we learn of Bruce Wayne's (Christian Bale) tragic past, losing his parents to a criminal years ago. Spurred on by his torment and feelings of guilt, he eventually begins training in Ninjitsu at the hands of mentor Ducard (Liam Neeson) under the cruel master Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe) and his "League of Shadows"- an organization that seeks to destroy the corrupt at any cost. However, Bruce realizes that the League is far too dangerous a force, and he is forced to betray them, eventually using his newfound skills to become the vigilante known as "the Batman"... An alter-ego he uses to protect the citizens of Gotham from criminals and psychopaths, included the devious Dr. Crane (Cillian Murphy) and mob-boss Falcone. (Tom Wilkinson) However, new revelations about the dark forces at play in Gotham may very well force Bruce to confront a figment from his past in order to save the city...

The great success of the film is its finely crafted storyline that seeks to give a great deal of respect to the characters and the concept in a way previous adaptations had struggled with. Nolan's work in this film in trying to create a far more real-world take on the character is a bold choice, and has since been repeated in other properties to increasingly mixed results. However, it perfectly compliments the dual character of Bruce Wayne/Batman and allows for a far greater scope of emotional and psychological development. The film in many ways is a character-study first and a grand action spectacle second, with Nolan and star Bale far more interested in those small moments of development and establishment that let us know what makes Bruce tick and Batman brood than the ka-pow, whizz-bang fisticuffs and nifty gadgets. Not to say that the film is lacking in that department in any way, however, as Nolan injects finely tuned and carefully planned action set-pieces at just the right moments in the narrative to help them really drive him the struggles and turmoils that Bruce faces as his heroic alter-ego.

Directorially, the film is quite the wonder to behold. With his previous work, Nolan had already proved himself to be a fabulous visual storyteller, but here he really starts to shine. He establishes a pitch-black tone up front that is perfectly complimented by his ideal use of guerrilla-style hand-held camera-work and fast-cutting. While this has become a crutch for many a modern filmmaker, Nolan wisely only uses it in service of the style and tone he has established and he's perhaps one of the very few modern directors to really have a grip on this particular aesthetic style. I also highly admired his good choice to add consistent, subtle moments of levity and humor to the film, as so to not make it too overwhelming as many other modern "gritty" films become.

The performances are uniformly marvelous. Bale makes for an outstanding lead, giving Bruce just the right amount of pathos while still always maintaining a likable sense of wit. Neeson makes for a wonderdrous and complex mentor-of-sorts to Wayne and emerges as one of the stand- outs of the film. Michael Caine takes over the role of the trusted butler Alfred with a giddy sense of class and humor, in a piece of casting that I can only call "perfect." Gary Oldman is a revelation as the young Jim Gordon, who quickly becomes an ally of Bruce in his war on crime. The rouges gallery consisting of Watanabe, Murphy and Wilkinson are just wonderfully devious villainous presences, and are all characters you'll just adore hating. Honestly, the only sore thumb here is Katie Holmes in a rather miscast role as Bruce's lifelong friend Rachel who has become an Assistant District Attorney. She just looks so comically young and childlike for me to take her at all seriously. Still, she has enough of a chemistry with Bale than I can forgive this.

In the end, "Batman Begins" is very much the perfect modern re- interpretation of the Dark Knight Saga. It's wonderfully developed characters and expert psychological analysis of a man pushed to fighting back against the criminal and the corrupt make it a wildly fulfilling and compelling watch. And it's wise use of moody atmosphere and grounded action set-pieces will also thrill that child inside all of us who wants to see the hero and the villain duke it out. In many ways, it's an ideal reconciliation of the fantastical and the realistic, and it's one of the finest comic-book to film adaptations ever released.

And for that reason, it easily earns a perfect 10 out of 10.

10.title: Simply superb!
10.content:
Finally a film which lives up the hype, and more. If George Clooney killed Batman, Christian Bale has well and truly brought him back to life, with a vengeance. Batman Begins is as about as far removed from the Joel Schumacher-inspired disaster that was Batman and Robin as is possible to be. Where Schumacher seemed to just throw a full palette of colour at the film, Christopher Nolan has returned to Batman's roots, and has brought back the original, and definitive Dark Knight. He is once again the heroic anti-hero, and not the cut-from-the-template typical clean-cut hero that Schumacher turned him in to. Spiderman/Peter Parker he ain't. The new Batman is a much darker creature, not solely driven by the inane desire to do good. Instead he is revealed to be a much more complicated individual, angry, grief-stricken.and driven by desire to wreak vengeance on the criminal underworld of Gotham City that took his parents from him.

The film reflects this new, less clean-cut, almost more sinister Batman. The tone is one of a delicious darkness, with precious little sunlight allowed in. Taking it's source material from the Batman: Year One comics, the campness of the 1960s Adam West series is well and truly gone. And no Robin in sight! The plot is an unusual one though, as rather than having just one nemesis to battle, he faces many different foes throughout the film, highlighting the desolate, God-forsaken nature of Gotham, and the size of Batman's task to restore justice to the city - and mirroring the task of director Nolan to resurrect the Batman franchise!

However, this darkness is more than compensated for by the sheer star power present in the film. Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, Linus Roache, Tom Wilkinson, Rutger Hauer, Katie Holmes, and Ken Watanabe all provide superb stellar support. Caine in particular clearly revels in the role of Alfred, Bruce Wayne's butler and mentor. Oldman, playing completely against type, is the world-weary but honest sergeant Gordon (obviously destined to become Commissioner Gordon) and, for a man so often a brilliantly effective bad guy, is surprisingly believable as a nice guy.

The star of the piece though, is of course Christian Bale. The ultimate method actor who famously slimmed down to a walking skeleton for the Machinist, after bulking up for American Psycho, has regained his former muscular frame to be Bruce Wayne. He brings a new intensity to the role which really captures the full essence of being Batman, something even Michael Keaton did not fully manage.

The film has everything required to be a top film. Adrenaline-pumping action, a wide array of gadgets, an exhilarating car chase and a fight against evil (as well as the obligatory romance). But the important core of the story is one of a man's struggle with himself, the fight to find a purpose for his life amidst his inner conflict, and overcome his own demons of grief and anger. At the film's heart is a real human story, and all the action and gadgets serves to amplify rather than obscure or pad out the film.

Most probably the best Batman yet, the way is set for Bale to don the cape once more in a sequel to the prequel, and for once it will be a sequel welcomed with open arms. The only question remains at the end is whether or not this film (or films) will tie in with Tim Burton's original Batman, or if it will plough its own, new path. The intriguing ending leaves both options open.

10.title: Mesmerizing
10.content: I am neither a comic book fan nor a super hero fan and I am generally not a connoisseur of action movies but my husband is and I knew he would want to see this movie so we went to a midnight showing. This was a great movie! Christian Bale is excellent as the caped crusader, having the ability to show the torment and determination of this human super hero. Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, Rutger Hauer and Liam Neeson were great. I know little of Katie Holmes and I was a bit surprised at the mention that she discovers who he is but it ties in with the idea that they cannot have a romance between them. The imagery is stunning and the reality of this hero's potential is fascinating. The explanations of the origin of the suit, vehicle and "gadgets" make the story more interesting. The evolution of the boy who loses his parents to a man who truly wants to help people is inspiring. I rarely see movies in the theatre these days but I would go see this one again. I can't wait for the sequel.

10.title: The First Comic Book Movie Masterpiece
10.content:
In a time where comic book movies were complete jokes, in comes Christopher Nolan to create the first comic book movie masterpiece. Batman Begins is the definitive Batman origin story. This has some of the best exposition ever put to film with how they build up Batman.

Christian Bale's performance, I feel, gets too much backlash. Yeah, he has a gravelly voice (especially in the sequels), but I feel like people didn't get it. Don't get me wrong, I'll joke about it any day, but it makes sense as to why he has that voice. With Michael Keaton, he still sounded like Michael Keaton when he was Batman. Even the legendary Kevin Conroy (with his Batman from the Arkham games being my favorite Batman EVER) still sounds like Kevin Conroy when he was Batman. When Christian Bale plays Batman, he does something that no Batman before him did: make his voice unrecognizable. Think about it, he does not sound like Christian Bale when he's playing Batman, he sounds like someone else. If Batman's goal is to make his voice unrecognizable, then he fully succeeded.

In the end, I love this movie. It might be my least favorite of the trilogy, but Batman Begins still gets a 10/10.

10.title: Amazing film
10.content: This story gave the true essence of Batman. I try not to have expectations when attending films, but even if I had had expectations they would have and were met with this film. The attention to detail, keeping the dark undertones, the character development all created the ultimate Batman experience. Chritian Bale did an excellent job, this coming from a huge Michael Keaton fan. I cannot wait for a sequel to this series of Batman stories if they continue with the same director and caliber of actors that graced Batman Begins--Liam Neeson, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine. The only character/actor I felt fell short was the character played by Katie Holms.

10.title: The definitive batman movie!
10.content:
I am not a huge Batman fan, although I did enjoy the first 3 movies and when I was younger I was a regular viewer of the animated series. However, I didn't believe that any of the movies had accurately captured what Batman is all about. The first movie was almost all Jack Nicholson, the second just didn't have a whole lot of action, and Batman Forever had far too much comedy in my opinion. Batman and Robin, well, I don't think I need to say anything about that movie.

I was really excited to see Batman Begins, because it looked like they had finally made a more gritty and less outrageous Batman movie. Let's just say that after seeing it, it definitely exceeded my highest expectations. Even if you aren't a big Batman fan, this is just a great movie in general. It has enough action, the right amount of comedy, some excellent drama, and I must admit a few parts made me jump.

Christian Bale blows all the other actors who portrayed Batman away, even Keaton. Bale IS Batman. He is the first guy to really be good at portraying both sides of Batman, meaning the Dark Knight and Bruce Wayne. The rest of the cast is definitely top-notch, everyone seemed to fit their part perfectly. Liam Neeson was the perfect choice for his role as Ducard, and like Bale as Batman, I can't picture anyone else in the role. It also featured strong performances by Katie Holmes, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Cilian Murphy as the Scarecrow.

This movie bring all the elements of Batman together. It has his rough and difficult past, it is the best at explaining how he became Batman. It also has a very outrageous plot, as every Batman movie should. It is definitely more realistic and intense then the previous Batman films, but it still fits in some welcome comic relief. This is BY FAR the best Batman film to date, the only problem is....how will they ever top this?

10.title: Film that grows on you
10.content: I did not like this film much the first time I saw it -- for the odd reason that I was still holding on to the Burton flicks and thought Nolan's work would be a prequel. However the film stuck with me after viewing in a way few movies these days do, and as no previous Batman film has ever done. The more I view this film the more in it I see, and it made me want to go back into the comics and delve further into the Dark Knight's history to further my cinematic enjoyment. Subsequently seeing the film deepened my appreciation of the comics -- an ideal outcome of seeing a superhero movie. "Batman Begins" made me love comic books again. Besides "Sin City", "American Splendor", "Spiderman 2", and "Ghost World" this is bar none the best comic book film since Donner's "Superman" and it excites me to the possibilities of this genre. It makes you remember you can sit down to these things over and over and revisit these characters and situations like old friends, distant memories. "The Dark Knight" cannot come with fast enough to suit me.

10.title: Freudian Vission of Batman
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins is a Freudian interpretation of the classic comic book hero, drawing extensively from the oedipal theories of psycho-sexual development and intentionally creating the Bruce Wayne / Batman figure in an almost exact accordance with Freud's perspectives of the unconscious.

Christian Bale's creation of Batman is the product of a hectic world, where there aren't simply two faces of the one man, but three. According to Freud the human psyche is the product of three divisions; The Super-ego, Ego, and the Id. Bruce first appears to us as an eight year old boy, who is undergoing the dissolution of the oedipal complex, he is coming to terms with hid father's prominence. David S. Goya symbolizes Bruce's awareness and reverence of the father in the phallic symbol of the Wayne Public Transportation system, "Did you build this train dad?" Goya is forming the basis of Bruce Wayne's Super-ego; he is showing the internalization of the father figure and the particular morality that governs him, notions like charity and nobility. As soon as we have the Super-Ego established the film continues the progression of the stages of psycho-sexual development to show how Bruce's Id is born. The young child is exposed to the emotional trauma caused by being witness to his parent's murder; Joe Chill replaces the role of Jack Napier in the Wayne's death, diminishing the Jungian concept of duality, which had previously been maintained in film. This setups up the vicious challenge to Thomas Wayne's cultural belief system, and creates an Id that desires brutal vengeance. This Id is nurtured by figures like Henri Ducard, Bruce's mentor in the martial arts, who preaches of the ruthless pursuit of criminals. The Ego is how Bruce balances these two opposing forces, how he satisfies the Id's obsessive compulsion for justice, whilst honoring the Super-ego's memory of his father, and then establishing a compromise for his own Ego. The climax of the film sees the destruction of the Wayne Public Transportation system, symbolizing the end of Thomas Wayne's prominence and the birth of Batman / Bruce Wayne's own identity.
