10.title: Great movie!
10.content:
Keeping this short and simple: Movie was fantastic. Started off slightly slow but was needed to show Bruce's training and how he became Batman. Another thing that I thought was a plus was that they didn't make it "another one of those love stories" as many "action" movies do.

Overall: Plot was detailed enough but not boring, action was amazing, special effects were astonishing, cast was outstanding. Bale did great as Batman which when I first heard about the movie some years back I was reluctant to think it would turn out good. 10.title: It Begins Right!
10.content: Batman Begins (2005): Dir: Christopher Nolan / Cast: Christian Bale, Katie Holmes, Liam Neeson, Cillian Murphy, Gary Oldman: First Batman film in eight years and easily the best. It is a detailed telling of Bruce Wayne's fear of bats and the death of his parents. Story opens with his release from prison and the training he undergoes to preserve justice. Central plot regards a toxic substance released in the water supply in the city of Gotham City. Assuming the identity of Batman he captures a mob boss and discovers that an even greater foe by the name of Scarecrow is behind the madness. Easily the best screenplay in the series thanks to Christopher Nolan as director. He previously made Memento and Insomnia but this ranks among his greatest work. Christian Bale is fantastic as the caped crusader who struggles with revenge and justice. Fine supporting work by Katie Holmes as an attorney whom he knew since childhood. What is interesting is that she is instrumental in defeating one of the major villains. Cillian Murphy plays the Scarecrow, an effective terror of nightmares and brainwash. Liam Neeson delivers a knock out performance in perhaps the most surprising role of the film because he is not as typecast as it may seem. Gary Oldman plays Commissioner Gordon who ends up in an alliance with Batman. Excellent film about facing fear and becoming one with it. Score: 10 / 10

10.title: Best Batman Yet
10.content:
This movie was easily the best Batman movie ever.

There are so many reasons why this is the only Batman movie to see, if you haven't seen any. Gone are the Tim Burton, "Look at my sets, I'm so clever and weird!" types of things that held back the first two. Gone, too, are Joel Schumacher's "Bat Nipples" and cornball humor. The technology used has an air of believability and we finally get the answer to Joker's question about "where he gets those wonderful toys."

The storyline is easy to follow and the villains actually make sense in a way that "Ah-nuld" never did. The acting included some very good performances, and Lt. Gordon was interesting in a way that never showed in other Batman movies.

If you have any interest in seeing how Bruce Wayne becomes Batman, go see this movie. If you just want to see a good dramatic movie with some great action scenes in it... still go see this movie.

10.title: Terifically entertaining
10.content: Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins is the comic book film masterpiece about the life and times of Bruce Wayne/Batman (played by Christian Bale.), not only that it was the only batman film to get the origin correct. The performances, costumes, story, photography, thrills, and especially the directorship by Nolan for this film is what made the whole thing great. Nolan uses a great cast besides Bale of which includes Tom Wilkinson, Katie Holmes, Cilian Murphy, and Gary Oldman. Nolan and his cinematographer Wally Pfister make a great team together of which they made a few other greats such as The Dark Knight, The Dark Knight Rises, and his mind bending masterpiece Inception.

10.title: The Best Batman Ever Made
10.content: This film, to me, is better than the other two. I haven't directly seen the two, but I had seen parts of the second movie, and it felt very violent and mature. This movie however, is one of the best movies I have ever seen, let alone a Batman Movie. I saw it several months ago, and I have made it a top favorite movie in my eyes. The story is about Bruce Wayne, who's father and mother were murdered before his eyes. Years later, he wanted to kill his parents' murderer, but someone else did. The next 7 years, Bruce Wayne, comes upon the League of Shadows, where a man named Ducard, teaches him a powerful way to combat justice. When he returns, Gotham City is now a corrupt city, where police are cowards, gangsters are controlling, and crime is everywhere. Soon, he gains help from Lucius Fox, who gives him his armor, his Tumbler (the Batmobile), and ultimately all his gadgets. With his support of his butler Alfred, and police officer named Gordon, Bruce Wayne becomes his worst fear, into the ultimate superhero Batman, and save the now corrupt Gotham City. Christian Bale's performance of Batman is probably the best, I have ever seen out of the character himself. He is more realistic than the other interpretations of the character, and is able to pull off such a complex character. Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, and Liam Neeson, also give awesome roles. You will love this film.

10.title: Hell Yes!
10.content:
Just like Burton's Batmans, a great ensemble cast led this film to triumph. Nothing can be said that wasn't said previously in these comments. It seems to be unanimous, it was a complete and ultimate success. Bale is phenomenal, as usual, and Freeman, Oldman, and Neeson give great performances with no one showboating and stealing the spotlight. Very descriptive take on the forming of our caped crusader, with all your questions answered and then some.

Katie Holmes sucks.....sorry. She is the only thing the movie could have done without. But then we would have a movie without breasts, and even though it worked in Master and Commander,....Batman movies need breasts.

Great movie, take the kids,...just don't sniff any psychotropic hallucinogens before you go. Although, dropping a hit of acid would probably be cool in some parts.

10.title: A fresh new take on the Caped Crusader
10.content: At long last after many years of waiting the fans finally got the Batman movie they were waiting for. A Batman movie that puts the hero in the spotlight, not his enemies, putting more emphasis on his growth and internal struggles than the heroics. Forget about the Biff! Pow! Campiness of the 60's series or the tongue-in-cheek darkness of the Tim Burton movies, this one gets it right with the origins and more. We see our hero go through many painful stages before finally becoming Gotham's protector. As much as I loved Tim Burton's first take on Batman, this one expands upon it even more, and you get great actors to back it up like Michael Caine, Katie Holmes, Liam Neeson, Morgan Freeman, and Gary Oldman in their roles and they play it straight not hamming it up here. Christian Bale is a strong contender for the role of the Caped Crusader bringing both torment and duty to his role. Throughout his character has to make difficult choices between vengeance and justice. The question is can he put everything together and save Gotham from a deadly menace? That remains for you to see.

10.title: The Batman movie we had been waiting for
10.content:
In 1989 Tim Burton changed the idea of the comic book movie with Batman. His twisted take on the Caped Crusader showed audiences that Batman could be much more than the camp version seen during Adam West's tenure. After two films, Joel Schumacher took the reins and subsequently plunged Batman back into a neon soaked, pun filled disaster, effectively killing off the character.

Enter Christopher Nolan, who decided to take Batman and place him in a world which was much more familiar to us. The strength of Batman Begins lies in it's gritty realism. Nolan crafts an immediately believable world in which we see how and why Bruce Wayne decided to become the Dark Knight, wrapping it in a story which takes on weighty themes such as fear, justice and grief.

The movie is effectively split into two parts, with the first half dealing with Bruce's transformation into Batman. After spending much of his time fighting petty criminals, Bruce encounters Ra's Al Ghul; the unforgiving leader of the mercenary group: The League Of Shadows. After training with the league, Bruce realises that he doesn't have it in him to act as judge, jury and executioner and decides to return to Gotham to clean up the streets. It's a fantastic origin story which explains, in great detail, how Bruce manages to pull off the incredible feats as Batman.

The second half is a little more generic, as Bruce realises he has to stop an evil psychologist, known as the Scarecrow, from destroying all of Gotham. Even though it sticks more rigidly to an established formula, it is still rollicking good fun, with Cillian Murphy offering a suitably creepy performance as Scarecrow and some breathtaking action sequences; the best being a chase between the Batmobile and the cops of Gotham. Despite it not reaching the heights of The Dark Knight, Batman Begins is the perfect starting point for anyone not familiar with the character, and the final scene is a perfect example of how to set up a sequel.

A dark and gritty take on the Caped Crusader; Batman Begins is one of the best comic book movies ever made. Nolan has not only re-invented the character but also raised the bar considerably for every other superhero movie out there. A triumph.

10.title: Comic book to the Big Screen
10.content: 'Batman Begins" at last penetrates to the dark and troubled depths of the Batman legend, creating a superhero who, if not plausible, is at least persuasive as a man driven to dress like a bat and become a vigilante. Batman Begins kicked off Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy, which has gone on to become an integral part of the world's conception of not only Batman but also superhero movies in general. Christopher Nolan's First Batman film really shows that very smart and unique directors like Nolan can make a superhero trilogy and its watched over and over, and everyone loves. When Wayne refuses to kill someone as a membership requirement, Ducard becomes his enemy; the reclusive millionaire returns to Gotham City determined to fight evil, without realizing quite how much trouble he is in. Gotham crime details and the counsel of the faithful servant Alfred (Michael Caine) delay the actual appearance of Batman until the second act of the movie. Lt. James Gordon (Gary Oldman), apparently Gotham City's only honest cop, are faced with a local crime syndicate led by Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson). The movie has been directed by Christopher Nolan, still only 35, whose "Memento" (2000) took Sundance by storm and was followed by "Insomnia" (2002), a police procedural with Al Pacino. What Warner Bros. Saw in those pictures that inspired them to think of Nolan is hard to say, but the studio guessed correctly, and after an eight-year hiatus, the Batman franchise has finally found its way. The movie works dramatically in addition to being an entertainment. There's something to it. Nolan casted the characters very well, and Christian Bale was the right way to go to play Batman, and in my opinion, he's the best Batman yet.

10.title: And so it begins.
10.content:
Greetings all, This may come as a moderately biased review, but to be honest, it is my favourite film of all time so I have very little criticisms. I apologise for what follows.

Firstly I say what a pleasure it is to see Nolan's non-linear timescales playing a major role in this feature, and to great effect might I add. Drawing reference from the past to seamlessly flesh out a rich back story while progressing the present time line works in sublime fashion here.

The much darker tone is conveyed wonderfully with connotations of inner-turmoil and unresolved issues from Christain Bale. And while the comedy is kept to a minimum, it remains accessible to nearly all ages.

A simple, fairly stereotypical plot backdrops the character development, but it is done in such a manner that when the crescendo looms it is a believable, satisfying climax.

I must applaud the casting, as Bale is a chameleon, from the clean-cut Bruce Wayne to the juxtaposition of a brooding, animalistic Batman. Liam Neeeson plays the villain with such class and ruthless resolve that the often intertwining ideologies driving these two main characters converge and diverge in true manner. Which, all the while, gives rise to a setting that becomes something akin to reality, one of the most defining characteristics of this film.

Hans Zimmer, as ever, writes and unforgettable score that marries both dark and light, calm and frantic, and leaves massive inspiration for future filmmakers.

Great set design, costume design and locations are the icing on the cake here, as all layers come together, producing what I consider to be a masterpiece.

To it's detriment, perhaps, the film is rather lengthy and may not hold the attention of every viewer for the full length.

It has been so long since the days of Michael Keaton or Val Kilmer as Batman, on might have wondered if any director would be able to do better what was done then. Happily I can say that in many ways this films surpasses all expectations, and I hold it in the highest regard.

This is my benchmark for films of any genre now, and I sincerely doubt it will be beaten in every aspect.

10.title: Loved it !

Katie Homes,Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson and Michael Caine played the most other favourite characters of mine! Nice story line! After a series of unsuccessful projects Nolan and David S. Goyer began to work on the film in early 2003 and aimed for a darker and more realistic tone, with humanity and realism being the basis of the film. I always want to see they together as soul mate ! But you know, that never happens for the super hero, remember the superman and his girlfriend ?

10.content: This movie makes the old batman movies seem as campy as the TV show of the 60s. I went to see this movie just because it was raining and did not have much else going on. I was not expecting it to be as good as it was, I was just blown away by the depth of the characters and the story. I like the way that most of the items in the movie were plausible and there were explanations to each the items that he used. They did not just show up without being explained. Also, I like that he is human, in respect to the fact that he does get hurt and that he was vulnerable to some of the things in the movie. I thought that it was great movie and I look forward to the next one. I hope that they do not pick another Joker movie for the next one, would love to see a different villain.

10.title: Finally!!
10.content:
I have been waiting so long for a Batman film that would live up to the cartoons I loved as a child. The previous Batman films were far from that quality - to put it mildly! But now it is finally here - Batman Begins! I must say that I frowned when I saw that they had chosen Christian Bale to be Batman. In my world Christian Bale was Patrick Bateman from American Psycho. But did he prove me wrong! He is the perfect Batman! The entire crew is perfect! Michael Caine is perfect as the butler Alfred with his witty remarks. The script is brilliant. I don't know much about the comic version of Batman, but this is just the way Batman (and his story) should be if you ask me.

The only thing I have a slightly negative comment on is Batman's voice. Why does he have to sound so strange?? But since he does not talk much, it is okay - one gets used to it. I have seen it at the cinema twice now and the voice does not bother me any longer.

10.title: A movie that truly represents the Caped Crusader
10.content:
As a lifetime fan of the Batman, I have to say that this is the greatest Batman movie ever made. I am one of the biggest Tim Burton fans and this movie blows Burton's films (which were spectacular) completely out of the water.

This movie not only raises the bar for Batman movies, it raises expectations for ALL comic based movies. The Marvel films pale in comparison to this film.

There is some grumbling in the "Batman" community that the film wasn't dark enough. However, I have read 70% or more of the Batman catalog and this is the ONLY movie that has perfected Batman. Some people have expected a Batman that slaughters villains and is non-stop action. This film mixes the correct amount of wit, ability, and vengeance. Remember, Batman started as a detective. So many times, people expect Batman to show up and knock someone around and then fly away. Burton's Batman was more of a smash and grab guy and that was great... but this movie is presents a great story with a great Batman. This movie can be enjoyed by any true Batman fan as well as any movie fan. This movie has so much depth that almost anyone could enjoy the movie.

The Batman is not a killer, but the movie is somewhat dark and is not suitable for younger children. However, if a child is mature and can handle some violence and understands the Batman story (and can determine fiction and reality) then the movie would be great. This movie reaches across all demographics and satisfies everyone. In fact, the people that complain about this movie are those people that are never satisfied. They probably loved Citizen Kane... and don't even try to tell me that's a classic. Anyone who's sat through that borefest knows it's garbage.

10.title: This movie got everything right
10.content: Christopher Nolan just knocked this one out of the park. This is the superhero film we have been waiting for since 1978. Great story, awesome acting, no over-the-top cgi effects, and no villains that seem more suited for the Broadway stage. Christian Bale is a great choice as Batman and his supporting cast is brilliant. The Gotham created for this film looked original and you don't feel like you are on some Hollywood lot. The fight scenes were realistic and impressive. Instead of a choreographed dance like sequence, the fight scenes are all business, just like the ones from the Bourne Identity/Supremacy films. Batman makes the outfit, it does not make him. The film does not take too much time concentrating on his specialized tools. You don't feel like scenes are set-up just to show off these tools. They are merely a means for one man to do the job of many. You don't wanna miss this one and we should all hope that Nolan hopes to match this masterpiece sometime soon with a sequel.

10.title: Creation of a Legend
10.content:
Though this is very likely forever going to be overshadowed by its epic sequel, The Dark Knight, Batman Begins is nevertheless a masterpiece in itself. It is the film which rescued the Batman franchise from the campiness and superficiality that had all but destroyed it after Joel Schumacher's dismal Batman and Robin and redefined and reinterpreted this iconic character for a new generation, by telling a story which had thus far seldom been coherently and completely told outside of the comics canon: the origin of the Batman. While at its core, the story is a simple and tragic tale of a young boy, forever scarred emotionally by the brutal murder of his parents, who is motivated to fight a relentless war against injustice in order to rid a city of the evil which claimed his parents life; there are greater dimensions to the story which Christopher Nolan has done a superb job of representing on the silver screen in a most compelling manner.

The primary appeal of the story lies in its psychological depth. Unlike previous superhero outings which relied primarily on plot and action, Nolan has chosen to centre both of these around the psychological development of the protagonist, Bruce Wayne (played to perfection by Christian Bale). This movie is as much about Bruce's emotional and spiritual journey from a traumatized young orphan, to an aggressive young man disillusioned with the justice system, to the aimless wanderer seeking a means to fight injustice and haunted by his childhood demons and finally to a determined and focused man who has mastered his skills and fears and is prepared to begin his war against injustice; as much as it is about the story of how Bruce puts on the cape and cowl. It is under the tutelage of Ducard (Liam Nelson) that Bruce Wayne learns to conquer his own fear and by doing so manipulate the fears in others. Returning to Gotham and resuming his public life as a billionaire playboy and socialite, Wayne secretly goes about his task of constructing an alternate identity, a symbol that shall forever remain incorruptible and indestructible and shall strike terror into the hearts of the criminal underworld. Before long, with assistance and moral support from his faithful butler and confidant Alfred Pennyworth (Michael Caine), Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman) an old friend of his father's and a skilled scientist and engineer and Sergeant James Gordon (Gary Oldman), one of the few untainted officers of the Gotham City police force, Bruce unleashes upon the city's corrupt underbelly his alter ego: Batman, and succeeds in single-handedly bringing down its biggest crime lord. But soon, Gotham's mysterious new vigilante finds himself facing his first great challenge-of saving the city from an enemy who has also learnt to manipulate the fears in others, through more insidious means...

Bale's performance as both Bruce Wayne and Batman is par excellence. Bale portrays Batman as being not merely a man in a suit, but rather a force of nature unto himself, completely distinct from albeit wielded by Bruce Wayne. Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman play their parts well enough and Katie Holmes does a fair job as Bruce's childhood friend and love interest Rachel Dawes. Liam Nelson's character is a far more sympathetic villain than previous 'Batman baddies' in the films, being, like Bruce, a man committed to fighting injustice, albeit in more extreme ways. His actions act as a counterpoint to Batman's strict moral code of refraining from lethal action.

With an excellent musical score and eye-popping (albeit moderately realistic) action, Batman Begins is undoubtedly a fait accompli which can never be underestimated no matter how successful any sequels it has spawned are or will bee...

10.title: The Way It should have been
10.content:
This is how the modern Batman film should have been directed. It is dark, dirty and dangerous. This is the real Dark Knight. Having read the comics and coming to admire the story 'The Dark Knight Returns', the Batman is not some campy show in the 70s, nor was it the film directed by Tim Burton. Okay. Tim Burton approached somewhat the style of the Dark Knight, but it was still not as dark as it could be.

Christian Bale is amazing in this, he has the right physique and he has the fighting skills on film (see Equilibrium). The supporting actors of Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Liam Neeson and Cillian Murphy are perfect.

Gotham City is dark and a scary place, just ripe for a winged crusader to save it from the criminals lurking around.

The story itself is quite 'meaty' and setups the story quite nicely. It also ends by leading the audience to a possible sequel. If the sequel can outdo this excellent first attempt, then I am already salivating.

10.title: Yes

10.title: The beginning of a new era
10.content:
After the failure of Batman and Robin Warner Brothers took a gamble with art house film director Christopher Nolan to revive the franchise to stellar results.

Batman Begins strays away from the cheesiness of other comic book movies as it takes a more realistic approach to the Batman mythology showing Bruce Wayne's journey as he fights against the corruption and decadence of Gotham City after the death of his parents.

Great performances all around from Christain Bale as Bruce Wayne/Batman, Michael Caine as Alfred, Morgan Freeman as Luscious Fox, Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon as well as excellent villain performances from Liam Neeson as Ras al Ghual and Cillian Murphy as Johnathan Crane/Scarecrow.

Christopher Nolan's direction is pitch perfect with great cinematography, combination of practical effects and CGI, and Hans Zimmer's amazing score.

Batman Begins is a great beginning to an excellent franchise as well as a new era for comic book cinema.

10.title: Perfect movie

What a great, great movie.

I've personally built myself up so much for this movie over the past year that I was afraid it was going to let me down. I entered the cinema with a feeling deep down that maybe, just maybe this movie wasn't going to be quite as good as I had dreamed it would be...

10.title: Exhilarating (no spoilers)
10.content:
As its name implies, this movie goes back to the beginning to tell how Bruce Wayne became Batman (and that's all I'll say about the plot). But this is no prequel to Tim Burton's 1989 movie with Michael Keaton. Christopher Nolan (director) and David Goyer (writer) have completely ignored the four Batman movies made in the late 80's and 90's and started fresh, and I, for one, am thrilled. While I liked Burton's two movies, they were really nothing more than an exercise in Gothic costume and set design. Don't get me wrong; I like that just fine. But while watching them, you never forgot you were watching a "comic book" movie. The final two movies, directed by Joel Schumacher, were just travesties, no matter how you slice it. He kept the Gothic look but channeled the campy 60's TV show for the action. Ugh. Batman Begins is firmly set in the "real world," even if Gotham does look like every Midwesterner's nightmare of what a Big City is like, and this adds a much-needed intangible that decreases the amount of disbelief that must be suspended.

I was pleasantly surprised by Christian Bale's performance. He will be inevitably compared to the three actors that portrayed the character in the 90's (Keaton, Kilmer, and Clooney). This movie should put any comparisons to rest. The closest comparison is Keaton, who was able to convey Batman's borderline psychosis. Unlike Keaton (and Kilmer and Clooney), however, Bale has the physicality to make you believe that when Batman kicks bad guy butt, he's really doing it. As Bruce Wayne, Bale is a much more believable playboy than any of the three previous actors.

Another nice surprise was Liam Neeson playing such a physical role, as Wayne's mentor in the martial arts. Neeson has the size to play intimidating characters, but this is the first time since Rob Roy that I've seen him look so, well, menacing.

My only "complaint" with Batman Begins is that it took two great character actors who are renowned for playing psychopaths, Gary Oldman and Rutger Hauer, and put them in very straight roles. Oldman plays James Gordon (pre-commissioner days) as the lone good cop. He plays it very well -- he is a great actor, after all -- but I kept expecting him to just go ballistic and start shooting. Alas, it was not to be. Nor was it fated for Hauer, who plays an ambitious CEO, to poke somebody's eyes out while saying, "I want more life." *sigh*

These minor glitches aside, BB was an excellent movie. The storytelling is crisp and clear, with enough "inside" stuff for comic geeks like me to enjoy and feel smug about but it didn't leave the casual movie goer out in the cold. I'm sure if I tried hard enough I could find snafus and inconsistencies, but I don't really want to be a nitpicker. While I was sitting in the theater, the movie totally absorbed me and I lost all track of time. The last movie to do that was Kill Bill Vol. 2. Highly recommended.

One quick comment on the rating: the movie is PG-13 for a good reason. It is very intense with a few scary scenes -- nothing gratuitous, but if you're easily disturbed by frightening images (or have children that are) please take this into consideration.

10.title: Goodbye Burton and Schumacher, Hellooo Nolan and Goyer!
10.content: I'm not one for going into an in-depth critique on something, so my review will try to appeal to those looking for a quick review, This movie was quite amazing, I'll admit some of the fight scenes were a little too up close so you really couldn't see much, but that was forgivable, the writer and director did a great job of grounding this movie into reality, the cast was superb, the actors all are talented without being MTV hyped such as Halle Berry in last summer's flop Catwoman. I recommend it to anyone, fan or not, and hope you enjoy it if you take my advice.

10.title: "Batman Begins" is technically the first in the Batman series.
10.content: This movie is really awesome. Out of all the Batman movies, this one is the best in my book, and I have seen them all. Christian Bale is such a talented actor, and he brings such a powerful, dark, tortured presence to Batman. I hope Christian Bale does more prequels in the Batman series, he s so good. There are such great actors in this movie.

10.title: The circle is complete
10.content:
Now those who brought us the saga of mystery dedicated to practicing "true" justice, give an audience to know why a guy goes around in custom of bat, doing beyond police power to combat criminal deeds.

This story takes the comic of DC into, what would happen if someone was trying to make just action out of correcting all criminal deeds, tied into a city of corruption.

We also get to see how the many factors evolved from Wayne Enterprises device prototypes, the military aspect never saw fit to soldier use. This helps allowing the audience to know Thomas Wayne, Bruce's father, was no idiot. He would be comparable to the genius of Tesla, for those who know, in standing on the shoulders on giants.

Morgan Freedom did wonderfully in character, showing the traits of "crazy Joe Clark" from that truth based story of cleaning up a corrupted school of 20 years making. It was fun seeing Rutger Hauer's character drop like executive lead as Freeman's character makes his come back to the executive board he had already been.

I salute the script for a super well deserved done in story line that actually made sense. Touche'

10.title: You still haven't given up on me? NEVER
10.content:
The first of an extraordinary trilogy.

In front of us we have the best Batman, the best Bruce Wayne, the best Jim Gordon and the best Alfred compared to any other Batman movie.

Incredible performance by all the actors and film directed to perfection.

Sir Christopher Nolan really saved this franchise, and inspired a lot of others Batman movies.

10.title: Not just a great comic book movie, a GREAT MOVIE
10.content:
I read one review of "Batman Begins" that essentially summarizes my feelings for this movie: "It's like 'The Godfather' with batarangs." So many people make the mistake of thinking that this is just another dumb, cliché comic book-summer movie for the kids, but it's really not. This is the first big blockbuster movie for director Christopher Nolan, and, instead of selling out like most action film directors and going for the easy thrills, he sticks to his sophisticated, intriguing, thought-provoking indie film style of directing, and trust me, it works. This is the best Batman movie I've ever seen, the best comic book movie I've ever seen, and one of the best movies in general that I've ever seen.

There were so many things that annoyed me about the previous Batman movies, especially that crap-fest "Batman and Robin." The villains were focused on more than Batman, the movies were too stylized (Burton) or too campy (Schumacher), and they didn't really tell you anything about the process Bruce Wayne goes through to become Batman. You can ask someone who just watched any of the first four Batman movies why exactly does Batman fight crime, and all they might be able to answer with is "because his parents died." That's just the tip of the iceberg; there is so much depth and intrigue to this character that hasn't been shown in a movie yet. Until "Batman Begins."

The first half of the movie doesn't even mention Batman. Instead, we get to see Bruce Wayne transform from an innocent youngster into a misguided, hate-filled teenager into a dedicated man with a purpose in his life. The second half of the movie? Action. Entertaining fight scenes, amazing visuals, witty dialog, interesting plot twists, and a Batmobile car chase that, despite the fact that a car is jumping from rooftop to rooftop, appears absolutely realistic. Plus, one of the greatest scenes of all time in which a seriously angry Batman interrogates a crooked cop; and by the way, that's really Christian Bale talking, it's not any fancy post-production audio tricks.

There are some complaints about the movie, especially with the fight scenes. The shots are kept very tight so that you can't really see exactly what's happening, but, in a way, that's why they're so cool. That's how Batman is: fast and mysterious, and never really allowing the men he's fighting to see what he's doing until they find themselves lying on the ground with a broken arm. Also, there are some complaints that the movie has too many villains, or that they don't receive enough screen time. However, try to remember that the title of the movie is "Batman Begins," not "Villains Do Stuff That Batman Has to Stop." The villains are present for as long as they need to be, without stealing any of Batman's thunder; this movie is more so a character study of Bruce Wayne than a typical action movie where we need to see villains killing someone every ten minutes to remain entertained.

This review may seem a bit long, but I dare you to go see this movie and not spend this much time talking about it. Between the great acting, brilliant interactions among characters, amazing scenes, and endless sequel predictions (the last 5 minutes are just plain awesome), this movie will definitely have you talking for quite some time. If you like action movies, if you like horror movies, or even if you like indie movies, go see this movie. It's great.

10.title: Fantastic
10.content: I loved this movie. It gave a whole new respectable and heroic look to Batman. This movie is in an entirely different class than any other movie or show done about batman. The story is well written and believable. It's exciting and fun. Christian Bale is attractive and very manly and fits the part better than any predecessor. He represents a man who despite inner fear and weakness chose to make of himself something better and use his new found power to fight injustice and save an entire city. One thing that stands out is that "Batman Begins" is clean cut without any trashy language or sex to muck up its image. It's O.K. to show the whole family (a little too violent for little ones, though). This one passes all of the tests.

10.title: Surprise, surprise! Big action films can have character, too!
10.content:
Thank you Christopher Nolan & David Goyer!! Thank you for proving that you can make a big-budget action picture that also has the elements of quality film-making, namely plot, character & writing.

These filmmakers have managed to do what we all considered was impossible. It is possible to have character development amongst ninja fighting. It is possible to have great dialogue amongst high-tech gadgetry. It is possible to have solid acting performances amongst green-screen CGI. It is possible to have an interesting plot line amongst explosions and carnage.

All the Jerry Bruckheimers and Roland Emmerichs of the world should take careful note of Batman Begins and learn how to do this genre right.

Quite possibly the best comic book adaption ever seen on the big screen. 10 out of 10.

Barky

10.title: This film ROCKS!!!
10.content: OK people.. i know the trailer might make some of you out there doubt that this film could actually be 'the one' to pull the Batman franchise from the steaming pile of... cheese that it has become. i mean, how can Batman doesn't drive a friggin' tank and the suit looks like overkill and katie holmes isn't helping things with her teeny-bopper looks etc.. right? well shut up and listen: this move ROCKS for one simple reason: it is BELIEVABLE. there is character development, the acting is great, there is absolutely NO CHEESE, and it's DARK! instead of focusing on Batman, Batman, Villain, Batman... to the point where the audience is like "who's Batman this time? Clooney,.. no wait, Kilmer?" -- the movie focuses on Bruce Wayne and his badass back-story. the story has a lot to say, and it says it over 2 1/2 hrs. of pure well-paced action. special effects aren't abused either fyi. let's put it this way, i'm looking forward to going to see this movie a 2nd time - and i haven't done that in over 10 yrs! see it. you won't be sorry.

10.title: The movie that brought into life the superhero I have adored since I was a kid
10.content:
I have been a superhero fan when I was a kid. As I grew up there are those I have already outgrown. But Batman is one that I have never forgotten and for some time I don't know why until I watched Batman Begins.

The movie focused on the origin of Batman, on how little Bruce Wayne lost his parents, on how he developed grudge on the injustice in Gotham, on how he searched for inner strength and eventually becoming Batman. Then and only then did I realize why as an adult I still like this superhero. Batman is not a super strong hero. He is not a character with supernatural powers. He is much like us, humans, with limited physical abilities. Only, there is more to Batman than just being human. He has a very strong will power. He can tolerate pain, find strength in even the darkest hours, and find the courage to fight injustice, even if it means sacrificing his own interest for the welfare of his people. Batman relates to any one of us who can do the same. One does not necessarily have to be as physically and mentally strong as Bruce Wayne/Batman before he can effect a change in his society. By being strong with one's stand on justice, one can call himself a superhero.

That is what this movie is all about. Inasmuch as it is a superhero movie, its impact and influence is on how one does for his society and fights for justice. And fighting for justice does not happen overnight. Just like Bruce Wayne, one needs to find inner strength and courage first, discover one's weakness and fears and turn them into weapon before becoming the Batman who is ready and strong enough to effect change.

The stellar cast was amazing. They did a perfect job. The cinematography, sound, and special effects were undeniably excellent, and Christopher Nolan did an amazing job in bringing life to a superhero that I have always looked up to since I was a kid.

10.title: Don't listen to the naysayers and watch this film
10.content: If you are a true Batman fan you will enjoy this film immensely. This film comes as close to the comics as it ever has. I know a lot of people say that it was Joker who killed Batman's parents but sorry to burst your bubble because that is NOT true. In the comic books, it was a thug named Joe Chill who killed his parents, NOT Joker. It was the first Batman film that got this aspect completely wrong yet people took it as fact. For people who are not Batman fans, I will say this: go in with reasonable expectations. It is not a perfect film but it is still very good. 95% of the time disappointment in a film is caused by having unreasonably high expectations and that is why I don't agree with reading reviews before watching a film. Watch the film and judge it for yourself before reading what other people think about it. Cheers to Christopher Nolan for bringing us the most accurate depiction of Bruce Wayne yet.

10.title: Batman Begins Review
10.content:
Batman Begins Review The most recent Batman movie line has been a huge hit in theaters upon the release of each of the three movies. All of the movies received at least an 85% score from critics on rottentomatoes.com and at least a 90% audience score. Therefore, before I even get into my own personal opinion, let it be known that almost everyone, even the critics thoroughly enjoyed the most recent batman movies. In fact, I believe that these movies have been some of the best of the 21st century thus far. The intense special effects, the brilliantly cool aspect, the absence of any non-fitting actors, and the connectivity between the advanced story plots are among just a few of the reasons why I believe these movies are seriously awesome. When analyzing your favorite movie, is there a better place to start other than the action packed machine that started it all? I think not, therefore; I believe Batman Begins is one of the best movies of this century because of the brilliant moral theory behind Batman himself, the incredible action scenes, and the fulfilled recipe of a perfect hero movie; all making such an enjoyable experience for most anyone who decides to view this film.

Batman is the only character who can be cunning, heroic, and selfless at the same time while also not even being a true hero at all. To me, he is the epitome of moral excellence. His selflessness is almost overwhelming. Many other comic book characters or heroes do the right thing and stand as admirable, valiant figures. Batman, however, goes above and beyond this. Batman protects his identity with the utmost care so that his loved ones remained protected. Many others do this, but Batman completely throws himself under the bus to protect all others. When Raz al Guhl shows up at Bruce's mansion in the middle of his birthday party, he pretends to be a drunken fool, kicking out all of his acquaintances and calling them "two faced, fake phonies." Bruce doesn't care that his face is going to be in the paper, shunning him for disgracing his legacy. Bruce only wishes to protect the good from evil, purely and simply at whatever cost. He also pretends to be a drunken, foolish billionaire at a hotel with two supermodels. His life as a playboy masks the potential of being accused of being the Batman. The two-sided life of Batman is also brilliantly articulated through Christian Bale's acting.

It's near impossible to deny how awesome the action scenes are throughout this movie. When Batman makes his escape from the cops in his tank-like Tumbler Batmobile, It's just undeniably cool. When he's jumping from rooftop to rooftop in the escape, the atmosphere is near perfect along with the dramatic music to make for an awe-inspiring experience. Another great scene is when Batman is in the shipping yard, one-by-one taking out Falcone's goons through the most terrifying means imaginable. He swoops down from nowhere to get a few of the goons, then, he lands in the middle of a circle containing about 15 of them, taking them all on in hand-to-hand combat without breaking a sweat and avoiding all bullets. Following, he comes through the roof of Falcone's car, pulls Falcone through the windshield and ties him up to a spotlight that uses Falcone's body to display the shape of a bat in the sky. For lack of a better term, could there be a more badass first scene to open the door to Batman's crime fighting ways? I seriously doubt it; well done Christopher Nolan.

The plot of Batman Begins follows the traditional sequence of an epic story while also throwing in plenty of exciting twists and turns. Batman has to overcome his need for vengeance in order to become something greater. This classic struggle between hero and self is a common element of many great stories. Also, Ras al Ghul is the villain whose goal is to wipe out the modern decadence of Gotham City. There can't be a good ballad portraying a hero without his beloved villain, right? And of course, Batman wins in the end with an exciting hint towards the next great sequel. The traditional formula is present with a twist that makes it so brilliant and exciting. Batman is the hero, but at the same time, he's not a hero. The cops pursue him consistently. Batman always takes the course of action leading to the greatest possible overall outcome for everyone except himself. Another twist is seen in Ras al Guhl. He is the villain, but truthfully, he only seeks to destroy Gotham because of how awfully corrupt it is. Batman believes there are enough good people in Gotham to overcome how its corruptness; there's a thin line separating good from evil. These twists make Batman Begins so insightful and unique.

Therefore, Batman Begins is one of the best movies of this century, entertaining most anyone who watches it due to the brilliant moral theory behind Batman, the incredible action scenes, and the fulfilled recipe of a perfect hero movie. It's hard to deny the feedback of a movie when the critics and audience agree, and in this case, I agree with them both 100%.

10.title: Dark, gritty, and absolutely perfect.
10.content:
I very much enjoyed the first two batman movies with Michael Keaton but the last two movies were utter garbage. I very much enjoyed this batman more than even the first two. I loved the story written by Blade's David Goyer and I thought the casting was perfect. Chris Nolan did a most excellent job and captured batman better than any other comic character has been in a movie yet, yes even better than Spiderman.

Everything about this movie was done so as to revitalize the batman we have come to love and I being a huge DC comic fan absolutely loved this movie. I can honestly say that I can think of no way that this movie could have been better and I left the theater with a great feeling.

10.title: Black magic
10.content: I'm biased, as I am a big fan of Christian Bale's, but I think he may be in the running for an award for his performance in "Batman Begins". Backed by a star-studded cast, he takes the role of Bruce Wayne and makes it his own. This is a truly brilliant film, giving (for once) full depth and character development. Bruce Wayne comes across as a modern-day Lord Blakeney (The Scarlet Pimpernel). For once there are no poncy and moronic characters; the villains are chilling and believable. The film has an uplifting, almost spiritual feel to it that makes it a joy to watch and to think about afterwards. I don't often hope for sequels, but in this case, I'm really hoping that they make one. Darn, I'm so impressed with this film that I may just go back to the cinema tonight and pay to watch it again (I saw it last night).

10.title: Batman (The Legend Begins)
10.content:
And so begins The Legend of Christopher Nolan's and Christian Bale's Batman. From plucking a flower from a garden, to bringing it up to a fortress on a mountain top, to being trained by Duccard in Ra's Al Gul's palace. Bruce Wayne is suiting up toward his Destiny, from a billionaire orphan in a mansion, to a martial artist ninja, to becoming The Legend which is Batman. But first before he become's that Legend. He realizes that the group of vigilantes that are training under Ra's Al Gul are no more, than criminals seeking to destroy everything, rather good and evil and the best way to stop this injustice? Simply burn down the fortress itself and stop Ra's Al Gul in his track.

After destroying the fortress and completing the mission. Bruce Wayne sets off a road, to becoming Legend. He suits up as Batman and fights crime, while facing off against villains such as the scarecrow, which is played really well from Murphy! And included a bravo, best performance of this film is played by Liam Neeson playing Duccard!

The film itself sets it's sight vocally on Bruce Wayne though, adapting a wonderful storytelling plot of the origins of Bruce Wayne's training in becoming The Bat of Legend. The film does not allow the villains to overshadow the main character, rather this film is beautifully intertwined and allows Bruce Wayne/Batman to setting in with the audience for an adventurous ride!

Batman Begins from visual, sound, music, acting, the cast, everything, Christopher Nolan made a Masterpiece with Batman Begins.

The film that started The Dark Knight trilogy, in becoming one of the greatest trilogies ever made!

10.title: Best....Batman....EVER!!!
10.content:
I have seen the other batman movies, but this one...WOW! There's something about this movie that stands out from all the other comic book films. The other four Batman movies made the villains look so off the wall. Meanwhile, Batman Begins makes the villains look more political, than anything else. The villains in the other Batman movies had their own hide-out, and their men wore uniforms most of the time. Don't you think out of all that, the government would step in and put a stop to all this? In Batman Begins, the villains try not to make themselves noticeable. They might be involved with the political issues, that way the government wouldn't think anything of it. I'm assuming that because of it, the government won't suspect anything. THAT, I believe is the work of a true villain.

This new Batman is a lot tougher and meaner, than the other batman's, and you gotta love that! Plus, you have to wonder how in the world Bruce Wayne got all this equipment, without someone finding out. Surely, he couldn't have made all this stuff on his own, such as the batmobile (Which, let me say, is a MONSTER of a car). There had to be someone to have helped him out, and fortunately there was (And you probably already know who).

I could go on about what makes Batman Begins the best comic book film ever made, but I know you wouldn't want to read all that. So I will leave you with this: Watch this movie! I can assure you that this will not look like a comic book movie, but rather a man in a costume whose out to bring justice into his city.

You won't be disappointed.

10.title: one of the top movies for the summer
10.content: This is hands down the best Batman movie I have seen. It really gives the audience (whether you read the comics or not) an understanding of Bruce Wayne developed his nocturnal alter-ego. I don't mean to disagree with the YEAHINDIE's review, but I myself thought that the action scenes were great. Its a dark movie with a dark character. I expect the action to be set the way it was, it all goes along with the Batman persona. This movie left me wanting for more, and I hope that we don't have to live through another change in Waynes. Christian Bale did an excellent job, but I do agree with YEAHINDIE in the fact that Katie Holme's did look a little too young for her role. The ending of the movie gives you a hint that there may be more to come, and I know that I"m hoping there will be.

10.title: The film that Defibrillated the Batman genre!!
10.content: At first you get drawn in and then you begin to wonder and then you say WOW and then you feel a bit silly and then you say WOW again and then you begin to realise that you have a brain and then you begin to think and feel beyond the initial need for a dopamine rush toward the realisation that you want to leave the cinema having experienced a life changing experience. This is what Nolan did with this movie. Batman was reborn. You then seek to tell your friends about your experience and you are searching for new expressions as WOW just don't cut the mustard. However it's Okay as the rest became a new history anyway which was credibly incredible!

10.title: Batman Begins...to leave Joel Schumacher's mess in the dust.
10.content: For those of you who haven't seen this movie, I bet you're all wondering, is everyone raving about this movie just because it is a good Batman film, or just because its not a Joel Schumacher Batman film. Well I'm raving because it is neither, it is not done by Joel Schumacher (good) and it is not a good Batman film...it is the BEST Batman film EVER! This takes what was great about Tim Burton's films (and believe, a lot about them was great) and makes it even better! This is what Batman should be, epic. Even though he has no powers, Chris Nolan at the end of the day that Batman is a superhero. And superheroes need to save cities, rescue people and be very cool. But at the same time this is distinctly Batman, moody, dark and unforgiving, the fight scenes are very masterfully done, done from the villain's perspective instead of Batman's, making it believable that Batman is a figure of fear. The music is up to the standard of the 1989 version, contributing to the slow burning pace of Batman movies. All in all this is a very good movie, everything about gels together really well, one small niggle however with Scarecrow. He may be scary if you're drugged but otherwise he's just an idiot with a grain sack on his head but that is the only microscopic dent in this movies Batsuit.

10.title: Batman Begins is excellent
10.content:
The Batmnan movie we have all been waiting for. Perfect cast Perfect direction I cannot wait for a sequel. I read the DarkKnight Returns comics in the 80's and this movie has come very close to the comic's dark qualities and gritty story line. I recommend this movie to the non Batman viewer as well and the Veteran comic book fan My wife expected the TV comedic version but was impressed wit the quality of the acting the action and the surprises. From Michael Caine to Liam Neesom the acting was superb. I have been reading Batman for over 40 years now and have seen the older movies. The Michael Keaton ones were wonderful but the later ones with the modified "nipple" suits were boring and hyped. Too many "celebrities" and not enough "actors". I am pleased to see a balance of good acting and good storyline which doesn't insult one's intelligence.

One question "Where can I get one of those?" LOL

10.title: Awesome
10.content: This movie was excellent in showing the raw events that shaped the Batman into what he became out of the scared Bruce Wayne. We see many renditions of the Batman in television shows, etc. but there is always one similarity, that the Batman is someone, something, to be respected. This movie allowed for most Batman fans to finally understand what motivates Bruces' alter ego, rather than seeing an athletic and intelligent man fighting justice. Bruce Waynes' mysterious nature often portrays a persona of greatness that is only rivaled by his actual ability to exert such greatness.So here I want to say, Batman is the best!

10.title: Best 'Comic Book Hero' Film ever
10.content: undoubtedly the best comic book hero flick ever. What separates the character of Batman from other superheroes is that he is Real. He does not have any supernatural powers. This film realizes that. The film is believable and real. I thought the film was fantastic. Atlast.. a batman film, where batman actually plays the lead.. and not second fiddle to some colorful, lunatic villain. The huge star cast of this film.. the use of established actors in small.. supportive and pivotal roles really enhanced this masterpiece. The best part was that.. batman did not have 'nipples' on his costume this time.. good riddance!! I would recommend this film strongly.

10.title: Not just another Batman movie
10.content: My initial reaction was probably the same as most of the general public's, "Just another Batman movie." What could've ended up being a horrid movie wrapped in pretty visuals to cover lame plot or acting turned out to be much more. The plot was fairly simple but never boring. It chronicles how Bruce Wayne grows up to become the Dark Knight to rid the streets of Gothem of it's worst criminals and seek vengeance for his parents murder. Christian Bale portrayed Bruce Wayne in a convincing way that was both believable and stylish. If you're looking for another movie focusing on Bruce Wayne the billionaire playboy, don't see this movie. However if you want a film about the vigilante crusader Batman, you've made an excellent choice. Stunning sound editing, heart-pounding action, and fear inducing special effects compliment rather than cover up the acting of the cast. Michael Caine portrayed Alfred the butler in a way that I haven't previously seen offering fatherly advice and some comic relief in a calm but very unique way. Liam Neison and Cillian Murphey deliver performances so good it was quite often frightening. Overall it was a gorgeous film blending action, drama, and a healthy dose of suspense mixed with fun bits of horror elements. Although you don't actually see the Dark Knight in costume until about an hour through it is by far the best Batman and possibly best super hero film ever made.

10.title: Batman Begins with a bang!!!
10.content: Batman Begins with a bang!!! Exceeded all of my expectations and showed that superhero movies can be dark and interesting again. The trio of Christian Bale, Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman is an excellent foundation to keep this saga continuing for hopefully many many movies. Having dark, sadistic villains is more entertaining than the MTV pop villains like in Batman Forever and Batman and Robin. Gotham also looked more realistic than the previous movies. It was also nice to see a movie that wasn't flooded with special effects. I don't think they could've cast a better Batman than Christian Bale. He is perfect for both Batman and Bruce Wayne. Scarecrow exceeded my expectations and was definitely better than advertised.

10.title: Superb updating with slight retro back story elements
10.content: I saw this in a multiplex audience and everyone gasped and cheered at the peaks of thrills and visual effects. The "history of Batman" is treated with respect and suffers none of the indignities of the 60s TV series. I was stymied a bit as to how the modern-day elements fitted with the "classic" setups of the Wayne family helping society overcome the "Depression" (1929- late 1930s); I guess the director/writer assumed we would make a "jump over the logical paradoxes" with him and the Ninja-fighting styles. Quite a super choice to offer this Director such a mega-budget when story is his predominant strength. I would recommend that parents leave the under-13 crowd at home and talk to the young teens about some disturbing imagery, like the attacking crowds who've been "poisoned" and the ethics of capital punishment. Well worth the trouble to get to a theater - - don't wait for it on the small screen! See it this June or July!

10.title: Fans can finally rejoice!
10.content:
With Batman Begins we get a film that is truly for the fans. I do not know if the general public will react to it as strongly at the 1989 picture. But, if you are a fan of the comic books then this is the film for you! It is a film that explores Bruce Wayne and how he became the Dark Knight. Something the past four films mostly failed to do. My predication is that fans will LOVE it and audiences will gain a new understanding of the character. I congratulate everyone involved on this picture. They did a GREAT job!

4 stars! So far the best picture of the year!

I do, however, have one nitpick. The fight scenes were a little disappointing. There was no master shot, so you can barely see what's going on. The fight scenes pretty much contained close-ups of the actors. I don't know why director Christopher Nolan decided to do that.

10.title: Brilliant, Mr Nolan n Mr Goyer take a bow
10.content:
The most awaited movie of the year,the most brilliant cast assembled together for the past few years, the strong word from the principles.so does the movie live up to all the hype? Yes it does.it lives up to all the expectations and definitely kicks ass.best movie of the year so far.script is the king here.brilliant cast and great characterization.Its a groundbreaking movie for its genre and shows the path for the directors who r making superhero movies.Mr singer,Mr Mendes u will have a hard time bettering batman begins.

Christian bale is the best batman yet.though he could still improve when he is wearing the bat suit,his portrayal of Bruce Wayne is perfect.Cillian Murphy as the scarecrow is excellent.Michael Caine, Morgan freeman,Liam Neeson r all perfect for their parts.Katie Holmes is good too.

But the script here is the real king.don't know how much they have deviated from the comics, but all the liberties they have probably taken have made this a perfect movie.this movie shows how and why Bruce Wayne became batman.from a young boy who loses his parents to a mean crime fighter.

warner bros, quickly green-light the sequels, we r waiting for more flicks of this quality.

10.title: A great film on many levels.
10.content:
Rarley anymore can I be pleasantly surprised when I leave a theater, but lets cut to the chase I came out very happy with Batman Begins. During a lot of my childhood I watched Burtons versions, as well the horrible last two Batman movies. But I remembered I never liked them, not even Burtons, they seemed to flaky, Burton's Batman seemed like a circus, and the others were just plain horrible.

But finally out of no where WB decides to re-start Batman give him a clean slate, and boy, did they start off on the right foot. Batman Begins is an excellent movie from start to finish. The story engrosses you and it focuses mainly on Bruce Wayne's inner struggle, how he becomes fear to destroy it. The acting was well done and the directing was superb.

Now some complained about the fighting scenes, I thought they were great, when you are in a REAL fight not everything is choreographed and smooth, it is very rough and gritty that is what Nolan brought to Batman I think.

I felt that Zimmer and Howards score was better then Elfman's. Though Elfman is a superb composer his theme fit a more "circus Batman" the new theme *Sounds like bat wings flapping* is just creepy, and it's kinda like Jaws theme where it gets closer and closer. It represents Bruce Wayne's anger throbbing, getting stronger.

The only nit pick I had about it was that it seemed almost that they had too much condensed into 141 minutes, minus the 9 minutes of end credits you have a two hour and 12 minute movie. But I feel that they should of stayed on some scenes a little longer, but hey maybe we will see an extended Batman Begins some day.

But hands down this is one of the best films this year, actually one of the best in many years it is now in my list of favorites. Batman Begins is excellent.

10.title: Couldn't have been better!
10.content:
I remember loving the original Batman with Michael Keaton back in the late 80's and it's still a very good movie, but that series truly went downhill under Schoemacher's direction, but this was such a pleasant surprise. I remember seeing the previews for this months ago and thinking well that looks a bit different, but I was really in for a surprise.

Instead of the puns, jokes, and ridiculously ludicrous dialogue/jokes between main characters during combat in the previous Batman franchise (the latter two movies especially), this movie was serious. Oh sure there's a comedic comment here and there, but when things were serious, they were serious, and that's the way it should be in any movie if you want the movie taken seriously and want people to watch it again and again. I've already been to see it twice.

Batman is much darker in this version. It follows the DC Comics, and is so much more believable. Everything is well explained in terms of the storyline and why Bruce Wayne does what, and how.

The acting is also superb on all counts. I felt Scarecrow could've been a little more realistic, but overall EXTREMELY well done and the actor did such a good job being creepy and strange like Dr. Crane should be.

So that's my two cents. I really hope a sequel is made, and I really hope they do not deviate from the type of stage they've set here with the darkness and seriousness. Christian Bale did such an awesome job! Congratulations to those of you who produced this movie if you get the opportunity to read this!

10.title: The Legend Lives On
10.content:
I've always wanted to know the roots of the caped crusader, this film was my answer. Christopher Nolan's directing is superb, delivering a full on 2 hour death grip that would not allow me to get up from my chair. Every actor/actress performed brilliantly in their roles, and since this is a live action film based on the popular comics, it's good to see a storyline sticking to its origins rather then embracing an "entertainment only" viewing experience that has nothing to do with the plot.

Christian Bale surprised me - he actually is a good Bruce Wayne/Batman; Michael Caine - aced at playing Alfred; Liam Neeson - so intense, his on screen appearance alone is beastly; Katie Holmes - a catalyst of innocence (sexy, in a weird way) Gary Oldman - i'm amazed how this guy can transform himself into other people (such as Dracula) Cillian Murphy - definitely has talent for being a villain which was later shown once more in Red Eye (i recommend anyone to see that) and..well....i could go on and on, great film. Hans Zimmer brought a composition that will go down in soundtrack history as a classic. The subtle black comedy gave the movie that little extra glow.

Batman Begins is a biographical journey into how fear and anger (when channelled correctly) can make a man legendary 8/10

10.title: well made movie
10.content: Even after 10 years this movie came out, I still watch it to this day! Batman Begins explores the origins of Bruce Wayne aka Batman. From the death of his parents right in front of him, to him taking down his mentor Ra's Al Ghul. This movie makes you feel almost as if you're in the Dark Knights shoes. I was highly anticipating a great remake for the Batman Franchise and Christopher Nolan and Christian Bale did not disappoint. With the other characters that made this movie, Michael Caine as Alfred. Liam Neeson as Ra's Al Ghul was perfect! Cillian Murphy was amazing as Batman's first true challenge in saving Gotham City. Buy this movie its highly recommended.

10.title: BEST OF THE TRILOGY
10.content: I know it is an unpopular opinion but I really think that Batman Begins is the of the dark knight trilogy.

10.title: Oh wow
10.content:
They got a bit wild with all of the Batman movies. There'd be a villain, villain tries to do something bad, Batman stops villain. It was the same thing over and over again. The only thing different was the villain, and possibly adding Robin or some girl or something. That's when I started to get sick of Batman movies. Oh, I still liked the whole villain and Batman saving the day stuff, it just was kinda predictable.

So, naturally, before I went to see this movie, I was expecting to see something that I've seen before. Was I ever wrong. It was thrilling, dark, and the characters were extremely well developed. I also liked the special effects, and it was funny during some parts of the movie.

This movie was awesome. I can't wait for future Batman movies.

10.title: Best Batman yet...
10.content:
When I first went to see this movie I knew it was gonna be a hit. I mean, it totally explains everything while starting the whole series over (that's the cue for a sequel, especially after you see the joker card at the end).

At first you may think that it's getting off kinda slow, but that's just the brilliant way the director Christopher Nolan sets up the plot. After that the whole thing gets really good with plenty of action, but not too much to set off the movie.

There are some great new gadgets, some clearing up why batman doesn't end up in a bloodbath every time he goes to work, if you know what I mean. The new car was also a sensation with the overly cool stealth mode! Unlike the old Batman series I'm hoping that Christian Bale (who by the way did a superb job portraying Batman) will stay the original batman, instead of there being a new batman for every movie.

What made this Batman so great was that it was dark for once, instead of being candy-coated like the old movies. They had too much humor in them, but this one portrayed what being Batman was all about. Great job Nolan! You've set the bar for further sequels!!!

10.title: the first truly adult comic book adaptation!!!
10.content: i just watch batman begins here in brazil and i was rewarded by a film that transcended in 3 important aspects of any film: cast: the casting was not just about household names to insure some "credibility" but honest performances and the chemistry among them screenplay: nolan and goyer had freedom to developed a more relevant aspect of the hero and put into a more realistic context. directing:nolan's dark and raw approach on the movie couldn't be better. but really impressive is the freedom that the studio gave for this project.specially the initiative to make an adult oriented movie,that for sure will sacrifice a more substantial box office gross. maybe this film will encourage others to developed more comic books into the screen for older audiences. Christian bale and michael cane gave true heartfelt performances.another important aspect of this film is the concern to bring a comic book hero into our reality,and making so it seems even more fantastic and exciting,breaking up that monotony of digital effects and "action packed" in exchange of a more introspective and interesting experience

10.title: Awesome Batman
10.content: Saw this film yesterday. All i can say is Awesome. What a great story and all the actors were great. Christian Bale is going to take this Batman to exciting places. The new Batmobile is totally different.Nothing like you have seen before. This film is much more a thinking persons film. Not all the crazy makeup and colors of previous films. We see how Bruce Wayne came to get all the great gadgets and the great Batmobile. Katie Holmes was not the girl i would have picked for this movie but she did an OK job. Cant wait for the next installment. Micheal Caine was the best Alfred. ANd Morgan FReeman brought a quiet intensity to his role. Gary Oldman is always good. Just an all around well made film.

10.title: Realistic Batman Film
10.content:
Title: Batman Begins (2005) Director: Chris Nolan Cast: Christian Bale, Cyllian Murphy, Katie Holmes, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Rutger Hauer Review: Um, I think we should be thanking Joel Schumacher in a strange sort of way. Now, before you start hurling your baterangs at me for saying that let me explain. As we all know, Joel Schumachers disastrous run on the Batman franchise nearly annihilated any possibilities of future Batman films making it to the silver screen. His films where campy, cartoonish and didn't take themselves seriously. Dumb story lines, too many characters, bat nipples, reverse photography, neon colors, you name it Schumacher did it. And with one final blow know as Batman & Robin the series ended its ones fruitful and artistic run that Tim Burton helped shape with his first two films.

Now I say thank you Mr. Schumacher because if he hadn't made his laughably cartoonish versions of Batman, then maybe we would have never seen a serious Batman film like Batman Begins. Schumachers films pushed the studios to go in a completely different way this time around, the complete opposite of what Schumacher did. Nolan has finally given us what we had never seen before....a realistic Batman movie.

The story centers around Batmans origins. Where he came from, why he became the vigilante known as Batman, and what pushed him there. Once we get past the whole "formation of Batman" phase of the film, the movie kicks into high gear with Batman defending Gotham City against Ras Al Ghul, a villain hell bent on destroying Gotham to see it "reborn" from its ashes. With the help of another goon known as The Scarecrow, he plans on releasing a gas on the city that will make people have nightmares and make the city destroy itself basically.

There's more good points in this film then bad ones so Ill start with the good ones. First off, this movie has depth. Its story is deep and it takes its time to develop Batman as a character. In a great moment in the film we see how he deals with the anger he feels towards the man who murdered his parents something that had been previously ignored in other films. He is not a perfect citizen, he has many flaws and makes many mistakes in this one. After all, this is his first adventure. So Bale as Batman gave the character a depth that had not been there before.

The rest of the cast is excellent. Without a doubt the best cast in any Batman flick EVER! Michael Caine as Alfred was lovable as Bruce Waynes father figure. Morgan Freeman was basically that character in the James Bond films that supplies Bond with all the cool gadgets. Cyllian Murphy was creepy as the Scarecrow, the guy who runs Arkam Asylum, where all the super looneys get locked up in. Having The Scarecrow in the film allowed many cool scenes involving nightmarish images. You wont believe what Batman looks like through the effects of the Scarecrows nightmare inducing gas! The look of the film was very realistic when compared to Burtons gothicky Gotham or Schumachers campy sets...this Gotham feels real and alive. In many instances it felt like the city in Blade Runner and that was because Nolan used that city as an inspiration for this Gotham. Of course its got its few futuristic touches here and there (like that train that goes around the city) but its nothing too far fetched. The Batmobile is awesome! In previous films the Batmobile felt like if it could never really pull a curve or anything, this new Batmobile is a tank that will swerve any way you want it, turn through the narrowest curve and destroying anything in its way! The car chase involving the Batmobile running through the rooftops of Gotham was very very memorable.

And as an added bonus...CGI was only used when necessary! Hurray, it seems like certain directors are finally releasing that CGI is best when kept to a minimum and used only when there's no other way of filming a scene. So Kudos to Nolan for that.

But there's always something that doesn't work. What was it? Well for me anyways, I didn't like how Bale changed his voice when he was Batman, he sounded kind of goofy. Some people in the audience actually giggled when he talked with his raspy voice. And then there's the thing with the story being very similar to that of the first movie. In the first one Joker (Jack Nicholson) wanted to poison the cities water supply so that everyone who drank it or used it would die with a smile on their face, here its the same thing only Ras Al Ghul wants to poison the water supply so that everyone will have nightmares and kill each other. I don't know, I just found the story to be too much like the first one in that respect.

But those are only minor nit picks, because I really thought the movie achieved what it intended to do, which was give us a fresh and realistic look at the Dark Knight. While at the same time making us say "cool!" every five minutes.

Rating: 5 out of 5

10.title: The Way It Should Be.
10.content:
Geez, what on earth took them so long? After the campy Adam West TV series, the Tim Burton Gothic flicks and Joel Schumacher's nippled Dark Knight, the real Batman has finally arrived. In Batman Begins the Caped Crusader finally becomes the brooding hero he was meant to be. It traces back to his origin, as young Bruce Wayne, the only son of his billionaire father, who witnesses his parents die to the hands of a mugger, and swears to uphold justice by 'turning fear against those who prey on the fearful'. However his journey towards becoming a vigilante is not as simple as that. Unlike the original Batman where we're shown pearl beads dancing on the floor that inspired a rich kid to don a suit and fight evil, this Bruce Wayne had a strenuous journey learning the difference between vengeance and upholding justice. He must also confront his fears and decide on his own ideology.

This is probably the first time I've enjoyed seeing Bruce Wayne more than Batman. It was compelling seeing him develop, as he studies the mind of a criminal and, being human, sometimes questions even himself. Fortunately there's his trusty butler Alfred on his side, who instead of just serving him steak, assumes the role of a fatherly figure. There's also the up and rising cop in Jim Gordon, in his early days as a sergeant, posing as Batman's only ally at this point in time.

Chris Nolan does again what he do best; playing with the scene sequence. Although this time he only uses that style for the first half of the film, alternating Wayne's training scenes with his childhood memories, it did nothing except enhancing the whole story-telling process. The heavyweight cast live up to their names. Christian Bale does a great job as Bruce Wayne, excellently portraying his transition from a troubled young man to a profound, philosophical individual. Batman, on the other hand, is a cold and menacing figure who's rough voice(that was heavily under criticism) I felt was appropriate, considering that his priority was disguise and also to scare the living daylights out of criminals. For the rest of the cast, Michael Caine and Gary Oldman looked like they came right out of the comic books, and then there's also Morgan Freeman and Rutger Hauer, making a surprise return to mainstream cinema.

Begins sets a new standard for dark comic book films. If Spider-Man 2 is considered one of the best superhero movies in the 'fun' category, then Batman Begins would undoubtedly be on the other end of the spectrum, the prime example of how a serious comic book adaptation should be.

I'm glad to say that they've finally got it right. For the first time in film history, The Dark Knight is portrayed correctly. The Batman franchise didn't reboot; it has only just begun.

10.title: "Batman Begins" allegorical?
10.content:
Some folks might think that the quasi-religious element present in the movie makes no sense. Or, that the portrayal of a particular character or three, does not jibe with how him/her/them was developed in the comic series. However, to my mind, folks who watch any of the live-action Batman movies should keep in mind:

1) The live-action Batman movies, while BASED on the comics, are not going to BE the comics, word-for-word, action-for-action. Any movie based upon a book or comic series should be taken on its own merit, and not evaluated solely upon its resemblance, or lack thereof to the story in another medium.

2) Religious extremists are affecting world events more than ever before. I view Batman's quasi-religious back story as an oblique allegory to today's world situation. It is interesting that this Batman, while able to find some equilibrium within himself concerning his personal situation, still had to contend with the quasi-religious vigilante group with whom he once trained who are now bent on destroying evil by overstepping their bounds, and forcing the world to THEIR world view, by ANY means necessary, even though it destroyed their moral base.

3) I rather liked the development of the secondary characters. I felt they had enough depth that I got a sense, not only of the evil vs. good conflict, but of the real people that ALL of it affected.

4) I rather like this Batman showing his "darkness" and his "inner conflicts" without being annoying in the angst and melodrama departments. This sort of neo-film noir production can be ruined by that sort of poor interpretation. Additionally, I sensed every bit of the Batman "cool" without THAT becoming a caricature.

5) Liam Neeson I could watch in ANYTHING.
