10.title: An Origin Story that Redefines a Legend
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins is the rare origin story that not only revitalizes a character-it redefines an entire genre. Released in 2005, it marked the rebirth of Batman on screen, abandoning campy aesthetics for a grounded, character-driven narrative that treats its mythos with gravitas and realism. It's a 10/10 film not because it reinvents the wheel, but because it sets the gold standard for how to do it right.

Christian Bale delivers a layered, intense performance as Bruce Wayne, charting his transformation from a grief-stricken orphan to a symbol of fear and justice. Bale's Batman isn't just a costumed hero-he's a man wrestling with anger, identity, and responsibility. We understand his motivations, and more importantly, we believe them.

Nolan surrounds Bale with an exceptional supporting cast: Michael Caine as the loyal and heartfelt Alfred, Morgan Freeman as the brilliant Lucius Fox, Gary Oldman as the earnest and principled Jim Gordon, and Liam Neeson as the morally complex mentor Ra's al Ghul. Every character is treated with care, and every performance adds depth to Gotham's world.

The film's tone is its triumph-rooted in realism, but never afraid to be mythic. Gotham feels like a living, breathing city plagued by systemic decay, and Nolan's decision to focus on fear, corruption, and redemption gives the story weight. The League of Shadows, Scarecrow's hallucinogenic terror, and the collapsing social structure of Gotham create a narrative that's both thrilling and thematically rich.

Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard's score is haunting, pulsing with tension and hope. The action is intimate and raw, emphasizing impact over spectacle. And while the film never loses its blockbuster appeal, it never sacrifices character or theme for the sake of cheap thrills.

Batman Begins isn't just a great superhero movie-it's a great movie, period. It reintroduced Batman as a symbol with psychological complexity and purpose, laying the foundation for a legendary trilogy. It's dark, thoughtful, and emotionally resonant-a cinematic origin story done to near-perfection.

You can throw out distasteful memories of Batgirl, bat suit nipples, Robin, hammy lines, and everything that brought Batman to the ground in the third and fourth movies. There is tremendous respect here for the comic book and graphic novels and for the character of Bruce Wayne. We see his troubled past and how he takes his journey from frightened boy to vigilante.

This is perhaps the most complete and entertaining comic book adaption in cinema history. It has everything for the comic book fan and regular audience member alike. We have villains with purpose. We have heroes who are noble. We have a world that is believable. You will come away from this movie saying "so that's why Gotham City needs Batman." As good as the 1989 version was, it never really addressed these needs. Tim Burton threw us into Batman's world assuming we knew his background. Chris Nolan does not take that assumption in Batman Begins. He makes you believe the world needs Batman, and we are better for having him.

A+

10.title: The best of the best in superhero movies
10.content:
Even though much acclaimed compared to most adaptations, Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins is still much underestimated with regard to its actual worth, depth and greatness.

Like most, I despised the Schumacher Batman movies but was a big fan of Tim Burton's earlier work with the character. I thus had huge reservations about a franchise reset. And after seeing Batman Begins the first time, I was left unconvinced.

But this is one of those rare movies which grew on me after each time I saw it rather than the usual decline. And now that I grasped its philosophical implications and the depth of Bruce Wayne's development, which obviously escaped me the first time, I realize that Batman Begins is much more than a movie, let alone a mere comic book adaptation.

Even though it is loaded with some heavy reflexions about life and justice, there is no lecturing here. Nolan masterfully manages to take us into the deep confines of the nature of law and justice, and uses real, important issues as a springboard to send Bruce Wayne into the Batman character. Where justice is absent because it is in the hands of those who seek to avoid it, Wayne finds that he cannot save Gotham by himself. He has to become more, a symbol around which people will rally and will regain hope. And indeed, don't we all have the feeling that this is what the world needs when the corrupt go free and nothing can seem to help it?

At the same time, Nolan illustrates that justice is a relativistic idea, that one's justice is different than another's. The League of Shadwos is convinced that its actions are driven by a concern for justice, and thus Wayne cannot reason with Raz Al Gul for both of them are reaching for opposite ends of the same principle.

Another important theme carried by the movie is that actions are more important than intentions. Few people on the political, academic or public stage really grasp this, let alone put it into action so powerfully.

Nolan's Gotham and characters are real to the point that Batman Begins is a superhero movie which isn't a superhero movie. It rather is the very believable story of a tormented young adult who, confronted with the ugliness of the real world, finds that he has the tools to help make the good fight, but that in order to fight for justice, he must not follow its accepted rules and will have to hide his identity in order to fulfill his purpose.

With a solid cast, splendid photography and top notch direction, Batman Begins is one of the all time neglected greats. Without question a milestone for mature comic book adaptations, character development, and for political reflexion without any lecturing.

10.title: Batman Is Dead, Long Live Batman!!
10.content:
Finally, the Dark Knight achieves cinematic justice with Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins". After Tim Burton's strange, art-house approach and Joel Schumacher's camp-on-steroids versions, moviegoers are given a Batman feature made with dignity, intelligence and respect.

The title says it all: the film charts Bruce Wayne's growth and transformation into the Caped Crusader. Only this time, much more of the material delves into Bruce's psychology, which grounds the entire film into a reality more akin with the Bourne films than a comic book. Everything about Batman is explained; his weaponry, his tactics, the people around him, everything. Not a moment is wasted in David Goyer's script, his best since "Dark City".

Each character has an important role to play in Bruce/ Batman's life. Unlike the previous four films, Bruce Wayne is center stage for most, if not all, of the proceedings. Christian Bale takes full advantage of this, making his performance the now definitive Bruce Wayne/ Batman of the silver screen. Nolan surrounds Bale with a top-notch supporting cast that's all talent and no ego.

The villains, no longer the focus of what was never their films to begin with, have never been better (at least in a dramatic sense). Their relation to fear and how it functions plays into the very theme of not just "Batman Begins", but Batman himself. Ken Watanabe, Liam Neeson, Cillian Murphy and Tom Wilkinson give it their all. The good guys, played by Michael Caine, Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman and Katie Holmes, are fleshed out enough to create a surrogate family for Bruce Wayne. Performances such as theirs help keep the film grounded in reality.

Gotham City is no longer towering statues and neon-colored city blocks, but an actual American city sprawling in its own decadence. Even the gadgetry and the Batmobile seem plausible, if not insanely expensive. In closing, Nolan has created a film worthy of a hero such as Batman. No longer content with just "comic-book movies", the Dark Knight now has a full-fledged MOVIE to call his own. In fact, as far as adventures go, this is the most dramatically competent I've seen (and that includes Indiana Jones -- honestly, how much do you really know about his character?).

I am amazed by how much time the script took to develop everything, and it tells an honest-to-goodness story, instead of filling in the blanks and insert-action- sequence-here. Bravo to all involved; it's about time a live-action film gave as much respect to Batman as the animated series did. Here's hoping that Batman Continues. (This is not a spoiler, but I would like to put in my vote for Mark Hamill in a certain role for the next film. That is all.)

I loved how the film explores Bruce's tragic past and his training with the League of Shadows. Christian Bale is perfect as the brooding, intense Bruce Wayne/Batman.

Intriguing storyline and realistic situations you can relate to. The themes of fear, redemption, and justice really resonated with me. The action scenes were thrilling and the whole movie had me on the edge of my seat. Overall, Batman Begins is an incredible reboot that sets the stage for The Dark Knight trilogy.

10.title: "...everything begins from here..."
10.content: That was what I thought when the lights of the theater turned on, and I was still on my seat. It was quite difficult to bring my dad to see this movie, because of his 50-year-old-prejudice: "It's a kid's flick". Well, patience finally paid off and we went. It was quite a thrill to see a character as complicated and disturbed as Bruce Wayne in the silver screen; to see a tortured soul in search for an unreachable redemption; all what the real character Batman meant. This movie, really, is the beginning of a legend, of a myth created 60 years ago. Forget all those Burton-Schumacher attempts to approach to the man with the mask. Everything begins with Nolan's. About the cast, though Christian Bale was incredible as the Batman (just see his anger when he puts the cloak and mask), it's Michael Caine's representation of Alfred Pennyworth that caught all my attention. I don't want to bore you with details, but there's just one scene that remained in my mind for quite a while: When Bruce/Batman is under the effects of the Scarecrow's gas and is helped by Alfred. You can see how Bruce struggles with his fears on the limo, meanwhile Alfred drives and cries, unable to help him. That scene, I believe, represents the whole movie: a man fighting with his inner demons and those who are around him can't do nothing but see how he develops a never-ending battle into his auto-destruction. That's what Nolan does with his movie, that's what he captures, the essence of the main character's obsession (and doom). Forget you're dealing with a comic character. Nolan gives a total-realistic vision of a tortured man, who dresses up as a bat to deal with his own struggle: a never-ending battle to his past, and recover all what he thinks he lost when he was eight years old: his innocence.

10.title: The Dark Knight Rises From The Ashes
10.content:
Released eight years after the Batmobile wreck known as Batman And Robin, Batman Begins brings the caped crusader back to his dark roots and would kick off The Dark Knight Trilogy. After his parent's murder, Bruce Wayne travels the world, eventually going to train with the League of Shadows, led by Ra's Al Ghul. However, when he is required to kill a man to prove his worth to lead an army to destroy Gotham City, he sees their true colors, and destroys the monestary. Now, he returns to Gotham, he becomes Batman, using Wayne Enterprises' latest inventions to thwart Carmine Falcone, however, Dr. Jonathan Crane, who has helped Falcone, is in leagues with Al Ghul, and becomes The Scarecrow to help him destroy Gotham.

It is a good movie. Christopher Nolan does a good job bringing Batman back to the dark atmosphere it belongs. Christian Bale does a good job as Bruce Wayne/Batman, with notable actors like Gary Oldman, Liam Neeson, and Morgan Freeman doing good as well. The story is an interesting take on Batman's origin, and the special effects are good. This is a good Batman movie I would recommend to any fan of Batman or anyone into superheroes in general.

10.title: An excellent drama
10.content: I went to see this film without any attachment to the Batman franchise, and having only seen on of the previous 5 (?) installments made in the 1990s. Neither am I a big comic books fan. Batman Begins just seemed like an entertaining way to spend a summer evening, and with a slew of semi-disappointing action movies recently the expectations weren't running too high. However, even if they were, BB would have surpassed them. Finally there's an action movie where there is more to watch then CG special effects. The story is captivating and deep, and the acting is fantastic. While we expect it to be so from the likes of Christian Bale and Liam Neeson, the biggest surprise for me was Cillian Murphy as Scarecrow. Throughout the entire movie the storyline, if not completely realistic, is at the least plausible, and never cartoonish, even in its depiction of villains. In BB you get a great dark multifaceted drama, and the action component is a terrific compliment to it. Even after two-and-a-half hours I did not want the movie to end. I Hope that there are more movies like this one to look forward to from DC comics, and hopefully the same brilliant cast and production team.

10.title: Probably The Best Comic Book Movie EVER!!!
10.content:
Spiderman was good, Spiderman 2 was great, but in my opinion, this is without doubt the best comic book movie I've ever seen. And I know most people won't agree, but I personally enjoyed this a little more than Sin City although that was ace too.

I was a bit sceptical too, cos I didn't really like Memento (directed by Nolan) although its premise was very good. And Bale sometimes seems a bit...I don't know...just the way he does that macho voice all the time in every part.

But it all WORKED in this movie! And how!! The story was gripping, the action was dark and intense and the effects were brilliant. I really loved the way the whole concept of Batman was developed from his symbolism as Wayne's fear to the way his costume came together (the cape and the suit etc.) Bale was ace as Bruce Wayne and every better as Batman, but I think this is because he really treated him as a disturbed character. I think I heard Bale say in an interview "Batman is not Bruce Wayne in a costume. He's Bruce Wayne as a demon." The supporting cast were brilliant (well, actually I didn't like Holmes buy hey!) - Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freedman are legends! Hopefully it's the first of a few and maybe, just maybe, one day the nightmares of Batman and Robin will just be a ghost story you tell grand children!! Excellent movie - 10/10

10.title: Stunning
10.content: Forget everything you know about the other Batman films; Batman Begins is in a class of its own. An amazingly powerful dramatic film that also features eye-popping action sequences, Batman Begins transcends the superhero film clichés to become one of the best films of 2005, and the first Batman film that is truly Oscar-worthy across the board. It would be hard for the incredible cast involved to miss, even with a mediocre director, but Christopher Nolan is brilliant in his treatment of the material, and the resulting film is absolutely sublime. Making the previous two Batman movies seem almost amateur by comparison, Batman Begins is The Caped Crusader finally captured properly on film. Absolutely amazing.

10.title: The Best Batman Movie Ever
10.content: Batman Begins is the best Batman movie ever. Christopher Nolan does a good job directing this film. This movie got nominated for an Oscar for Best Cinematography. Christain Bale does a good job as Bruce Wayne, Katie Holmes does a good job as Rachael, and Michael Caine does a good job as Alfred. This movie has cool technology. I also like the sound. All of the other Batman movies are silly. I like the Batsuit and Batmobile. I also like the cave. I am surprised this did not get nominated for Besr Picture. This movie is a ride to watch. I think Christain Bale is the best Batman. I can not wait to see The Prestige hopefully it will be as good as Batman Begins.

10.title: The way Batman should be!
10.content: Growing up watching the Batman series and movies I have alway held Batman above all other super heroes.However, even though I loved all the Batman movies, I never thought any did Batman justice since Micheal Keaton. But now my hopes were full filled. The story plays out at a fast pace yet it explains it self quit well. The plot has its twists and turns but I found that my mind was always one step ahead. Unlike the recent Batman movies, Batman Begins is set in a more realistic Gotham City and a more reality based society. The comic book look is still there with its long shots of the city but it does not over do it. The Characters are more believable also, Christian Bale does an excellent job, his style suits the Billionaire who is not a money hungry rat, but a Billionaire who wants to do more for the people. I could never understand Bruce Wayen's mind extensively until now. Micheal Caine as Alfred was an excellent choice and I think he was exceptional, but I did miss the original Alfred. Morgan Freeman was his usual best and a lovable character. Liam Neeson was truly mind warping, he defines what an actor should be, I think Hollywood should recognize him more. Katie Holmes was also good but her character and place in the story kept reminding me of Mary Jane from Spiderman. But all the leading women in Superhero movies seem to go along these lines also. I recommend any one who wants to have a rush and leave the movie learning more about how humanity is should go and watch Batman Begins. 10/10!

10.title: Brilliant!
10.content:
Simply Brilliant! This is how Batman should have been portrayed from the start of the whole Batman series...better late than never I guess.

The scenes, especially of Gothan City and the Bat Cave were brilliantly portrayed.

All the characters were superb in this depiction of the "caped crusader"..... Christian Bale was made for his part as Batman.

The bat mobile is another eye-opener for all Batman fans... a beast of a machine

Well done.... if you're a Batman fan, it will be a movie to see over and over again.

Cheers

10.title: Christopher Nolan's Batman Trilogy Begins With A Great Background Check On The Hero's Alter Ego (First Movie In The Dark Knight Trilogy)
10.content:
As to start the Batman franchise back up again, Christopher Nolan delivers the focus of both Bruce Wayne and Batman accurately in this first installment to the absolutely outstanding The Dark Knight Trilogy. Batman Begins is a 2005 Action Superhero film directed by Christopher Nolan. Christopher Nolan has been known to be one of the most influential directors in the film industry today. Even alongside the Dark Knight Trilogy, he directs The Prestige, Inception, Interstellar, and Dunkirk. However, Nolan creates a more eccentric look on Batman with the Dark Knight Trilogy. The first installment involves around Bruce Wayne's life before Batman and as the start of becoming the hero. After his parents were killed in front of him at a young age, he grows up wanting revenge. After setting and leaving the League of Shadows, he goes to become Batman. He decides to strike fear in the hearts of criminals and bring them to justice. More characters involved include his allies Alfred (Michael Caine), Rachel Dawes (Katie Holmes), Sergeant Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman), and Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman). The villains include Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson), The Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy), and Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson).

Not only does the Bat-flick show Batman in action, but it also shows us how and why Bruce Wayne became what he is. What's cool about it is that the Dark Knight Trilogy starts off with the origins of Bruce Wayne/Batman and then it will involve into a much bigger story. I really enjoyed the film! Plus, I am a Batman fan and a DC Comics fan as well! Any fan of Batman or any superhero in general should find this film fascinating! I loved Christopher Nolan's direction and his idea to make the Batman story bigger than what it is. He also shapes the movie to make it focus on more than Batman and also his allies. The acting was also great and I've also decided that Christian Bale is my favorite Batman so far! The cinematography was moving, the musical score is well-known to many viewers (also as it continues on with the rest of the trilogy), and the accuracy for its depiction of Batman was also fantastic! I give credit to Nolan for his direction, the amazing acting (including the portrayal of Batman), the moving cinematography, and for the outstanding well-known musical score provided by Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard. This is a great Batman film and a great start to the Dark Knight Trilogy!

Batman has always been a very complex superhero. He doesn't have powers, but he is considered as one of the most iconic comic book characters of all time! I give Batman Begins a 10/10 for its outstanding depiction of Batman's story, the amazing direction by Nolan, the awesome acting, the moving cinematography, and for the well-known musical score! The Dark Knight Trilogy has started off fantastic with Batman Begins!

It was nominated for 1 Academy Award for Best Cinematography (Wally Pfister).

10.title: Was Blown away and can not wait till the next one comes out
10.content: well what can I say about Batman Begins except you have got to see it for yourself the best way to experience this movie is in the theater with a large Drink And monster popcorn bucket that way you don't miss a moment of the action, well except I Decided against the Popcorn I try to lose a little wait. I went to a showing of the movie at 4:00 P.M. at the Sunnyland Cinemas well I arrived a little after 4 but they were still going through the trailers so I hadn't missed a moment of the movie. the only thing I had know about the movie was from watching the trailers but they do not prepare you for what is coming. I like the way they revealed the past of Bruce Wayne through the flashbacks giving you a little information then going back to the present. The scenes with Bale and Neeson really added to the movie and it was that that got the movie going good. Gary Oldman was well used in the movie, when ever he was in a scene he made it unique because he was in it and he made the role his own giving Gordon more of a role in Bruce's life from the Police station Just after the murder of his parents, till there last scene together at the end of the movie where he sends Him on the trail of the Joker. This is nothing like the last Four Batman Movies this one is darker but that it what makes it good and it has what the others were missing a true Beginning not some continuing saga with out true depth of character, this movie has the exploration of the Character, the Fighting, the cool tricked out (well I do not know what to call it it is not a car or a tank but it is well the Batmobile). Michael Caine beautifully executed the role of Alfred Pennyworth some might say that we should of seen more of him but to them I say This is about Batman and his story the other actors are here to add to the story and to complement the performance Bale. You will not want to miss a minute of the movie in-fact not one second because that is how good the movie is and one more thing as the movie gets close to the end the more twists and turns there are, such as well Maybe I should leave you waiting for more all I can say is that the last portion of the movie will blow you away so take my advice when seeing this movie get yourself a Huge Bucket of Popcorn the Theaters give you and get the largest cup they have because you will not want to miss a second of the movie.oh and one other thing this movie is a must see.

10.title: ....Perfect....
10.content:
When Batman first hit the silver screen, in his own movie named after himself, he was treated as a secondary character because jack Nicholson cost ed the producers a lot of money for screen time. in his second outing, he was placed in a soulless nightmare and didn't seem very heroic. Then his last two movies were so corny and out of whack that we thought we, the viewers, would forever shudder when we hear the name Batman.

Friends, those days are now history.

BATMAN BEGINS ****/**** It's Batman's origin story. Not only does it follow its original material from the comics (which is always the best way to go with these type of movies), it is consistently dazzling with its action, its drama and its incredible cast.

This has got to be one of the greatest ensembles of actors ever to be involved in a film. Christian bale becomes a superstar, Micheal Caine portrays his loyal butler with true grace and soft power, Gary oldman nails the character of Jim Gordon both in vision and in performance, Cillian Murphy also grabs our attention, Liam Neeson portrays the mentor (again) with perfection, Morgan Freeman... what can you say that has not been said already?...... It's just amazing.

The action here, for what it is in its heart and soul, is easily 10X better than CGI festivals like the new Star Wars movies. Most of it is all real, using miniatures and sometimes full scale Batmobile action, stunt men flying etc. etc. It's the kind of action that has you feeling emotions you've never felt for a long... long time.

The characters are all three dimensional. Everyone has motives, backgrounds, and reasons to do what they do. Batman is rightfully the best developed character. Ultimately you have to ask yourself "How in the hell can a man become inspired to fight criminals while dressed as a bat?". As crazy as it sounds, the movie provides very good answers.

Now it is long, but worth every Milli-second. We first get to know Bruce Wayne through multiple flashbacks. Then we move on to his training and some of his early days of crime fighting. We don't see the suit for a good chunk of the film. But rest assured, the majority of the film does have Batman in it.

We get to know everything about him. the explanations of his Wonderful Toys are freakin' awesome! Some of his items, including his cape, are based on actual technology. Personally when I saw publicity shots of the new batmobile I thought it was the most atrocious piece of crap ever to grace a Batman film, and I imagine some of you probably;y feel the same way now. But let me tell you, that car is amazing. It's ugly because it's designed to plow through everything like a tank on speed-steroids. You have to see it in action to truly appreciate it.

Fantastic movie. basically anyone who's been missing that spine tingling feeling you get from perfect action movies should go out and rent this now.

10.title: It is what Batman should have been
10.content: One of the best would recommend this movie for anyone teenager to adult one of the best . Is is what Batman should have been in the beginning everything else is comic this movie hits the mark, being the only hero that is mortal this movie explains all and is a joy to watch and to quote: "I have to get me one of these". I heard they will make a sequel I just hope it is as good and has the edge this one has. Get Tim Burton to direct. He is awesome. Cristian Bale is so good I had my doubts but quickly was converted as soon as the acting started. I have always been a Liam Niesen fan and even as a misguided villain he is good. All in all you should see this film get popcorn and go to bathroom first you don't want to miss a thing.

10.title: Best film I've seen in a long while
10.content:
This is a great film whether you're a Batfan or not - I personally disliked the recent Batman films and just wish I could see some more of that Shark-repellent Batspray. It's probably just not meant to be.

There are some brilliant performances by Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson and Michael Caine, though I'm glad the former two had fairly minor roles since it could have detracted from the story.

The story was very compelling and while I believe there were some continuity issues with the other films, this stands out brilliantly from the others so it doesn't concern me.

There are moments where the film is dark and scary - I'm sure there are guidelines for parents about whether this movie would be suitable for their children, just be sure to read them if you have children who are prone to being frightened. Needless to say there are bats. The special effects were very good (thankfully there wasn't much CGI in the film) but didn't distract the eyes.

Compared to other films I've seen recently it's in a league of it's own - if you're looking for an action film this summer it just has to be Batman Begins.

10.title: The Greatest Reboot of All-Time
10.content:
Nolan couldn't have been a better choice to take the director's seat, and while Bale has a strong resemblance to West, their Batmans are completely different. After eight years of silence, the Batman reemerges with a most appropriate reboot which explains the whole history of how Bruce Wayne became Batman. Nolan makes both Burton and Schumacher look like Ed Wood — most impressive of all is that, while technology has improved tremendously since 1997's flop "Batman & Robin", "Begins" chooses to take little advantage of it. A-list actors are casted as supporting characters, with Michael Cane as Alfred, and a calm Gary Oldman (that's a first!) as Gordon; among others like Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes and Morgan Freeman. Tom Wilkinson, Rutger Hauer, Ken Watanabe and Colin McFarlane are also so wonderful in their minor roles. Cillian Murphy modestly appears as The Scarecrow, which one can say is a bit underused as a well-known villain, but it actually makes it all the more realistic. Perhaps the older series should have considered using major stars as supporting characters, not villains. This film proves that superheroism isn't impossible — you just have to be a billionaire. Nolan's uncle, John Nolan, plays Fredericks.

**** (out of four)

10.title: How all the story began
10.content:
I didn't expect that Christopher Nolan could do a better job than Burton, but that it is. Bale is by far the best Batman ever seen on screen, and I'm very pleased to find out that he has signed for the next episode. The gloomy atmosphere and the dark setting of Gotham mirror the inner conflict of the hero and for the first time is batman himself, rather than his antagonists, the protagonist of the story. I think that this new way to see Batman could be seen as a very new beginning for a series that Schumacher had almost tried to kill. I invite those who have never seen a Batman movie to go and see this one. They won't be disappointed

I'm looking forward to seeing the next episode and I hope not to wait too long. What about Edward Norton as the Joker?

10.title: Best Batman movie to date
10.content:
The Batman movie that stood out the most. Yes, it is better both The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises. Yet unfortunately, it is the arguably the most underrated one.

So where do I start here? Oh yes, the beautiful scenery that caught my attention first. When you see Bruce Wayne traveling to Ra's Al Ghul's palace, you are exposed to incredibly eye-pleasing landscape. You see even more during the sword fight between Wayne and Ducard (Ra's as you will find out in the end). Beautiful sky-blue mountains everywhere. How can you not commend this movie for having this? So Ra's trains Bruce Wayne. And let me tell you, his lines are magnificent and poetic. All his talk about theatricality and deception makes you even more excited for Bruce Wayne to finally don the cowl. In my opinion, his performance was far superior than the not-so-amazing Health Ledger's Joker. Liam Neeson did an excellent job as a ninja master and his lines make his fights with Bruce seem like a masterpiece. Why did we not get this sort of action in the sequels?

After returning to Gotham, Bruce is no longer the angry rich kid. Now he is a different person. However, before he completely goes 'all-out', he must run a test, and I'm referring to his very entertaining visit to Gordon in his ski mask. With Gotham you can tell that it's not a place that you would want to live in. It is pretty much the ultimate dystopia for law. Corruption, drug trafficking and bribing is virtually everywhere. Nolan did a fantastic job portraying more hell-like than the Gotham in TDK or TDKR.

Now for Christian Bale's Batman. Before I watched this movie, I expected to see very little of Batman or see him at the end of the film. But I got more than I expected and we received Batman who occupied the 2nd hour of the movie. Batman here is a BEAST. "The Dark Knight", "The Caped Crusader", "The World's Greatest Detective" apply perfectly to this Batman. This is not the wimp with throat cancer we got from the sequels. Bruce Wayne was trained to be a ninja, and it is reflected how much he learned in his Batman activities. He has got everything you want from a Batman: stealth methods, mind games, fluent martial arts skills, tons of gadgets, intimidating suit, AND a voice that you can understand. Don't believe me? Watch this movie again. This Batman tackled a whole group of ninjas (who should be as, if not more skilled as him). Yet in TDK he couldn't beat Joker, a clown who doesn't know how to fight, and a few of thugs? The Batman got a little rusty, hadn't he? Also, this Batman does not shout/talk as much as TDK's Bats. During the tumbler chase scene, he really did not speak much, except on occasions to calm Rachel down. To add more proof, re-watch the scene where he gets poisoned by the Scarecrow's fear gas. When he breathes in, he starts getting hallucinations, yet he doesn't say A WORD. This is the true "silent guardian" that Gordon was talking about in TDK. This makes me feel that Batman himself is not the primary character here, Bruce Wayne is. However, when Bale dons the cape, he steals every scene he's in, something I did not receive in TDK (aside from the lack of stealth techniques).

Alfred and Lucius Fox's fantastic in this film. Both of their lines are very clever and very humorous at times. If you had a butler like Alfred in real life, he will reassure you that things will work out. "Why do we fall, Master Wayne?"

However, this movie is not one without flaws. Katie Holmes, as much as I think she better than her replacement in the sequel, sounds extremely sarcastic in a lot of her scenes, e.g. when she first meets Batman or when she meets Scarecrow on a horse. Also, some people complain that the fight scenes in BB are terrible due to their 'shaky' feel. I must agree, it can be frustrating sometimes to work out who's hitting who. However, it works effectively with Batman as it makes him look more like a living shadow. Overall, this movie is my 2nd most favorite film I've seen in my life. Batman's performance, Ra's Al Ghul, the amazing cast and the fantastic soundtrack more than convince me that this is superior than the rest of the trilogy. It's entertaining, clever, soul-grasping and most of all, inspiring whereas The Dark Knight is mentally exhausting. If you love Batman and see him be a total badass monster, go watch this movie. If you despise Batman with all your heart and want to see him suffer, please go back to watching your TDK and keep telling yourself how "amazing" the Health Ledger's Joker is. Or you can watch The Dark Knight Rises to see Bats' ass handed to him by Bane.

10.title: They Finally Get It Right!
10.content:
Batman has always been my favorite superhero. So, that being said, I just have to say that Batman Begins finally got it all right.

The story tells us how Bruce Wayne became Batman. After his parents were murdered he traveled halfway across the world and joined a secret ninja society known as The Legion Of Shadows. After he refuses to kill a man in cold blood, he travels back to Gotham city where crime has overrun the streets. There, he becomes Batman and goes up against three villains: Carmine Falcone, The Scarecrow, and Ra's Al Ghul.

Christian Bale plays Bruce Wayne/Batman very well. He makes you believe that he went through all this anguish. Christopher Nolan directs this movie. He is the only director of a Batman movie that understands and respects the story of Batman. He co-wrote the script with David S. Goyer and they have really done justice here.

Batman Begins is the only real Batman movie. It is definitely worth checking out on the big screen however many times you can see it. I can't wait for the sequel and I hope it comes out soon. I also hope that in the sequel, the villain will be the one they hinted at in the final scene.

So, as a true Batman fan, I found this movie to be perfect in every aspect as a Batman movie. The action scenes were very well done and exciting. I was even able to keep track of who was getting their butt whipped during the hand to hand fight scenes. 4 stars out of 4.

10.title: The best comic book film EVER
10.content:
This is without a doubt (in my humble opinion) the best take on a comic book hero ever put on film. An incredible cast, a director with a fresh take on the mythology of the Dark Knight, and a strong and almost-realistic storyline makes this one a definite 10 out of 10.

Christian Bale owns as Bruce Wayne/Batman. I had my doubts about him taking on this role, but they were quickly laid to rest when he first dons the Batsuit. Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine are excellent in their supporting roles, and although screen time is limited for both of them, the both have time to shine. Gary Oldman, well, this is one of his most subdued roles and yet he still does his thing, memorably taking the character of Gordon from secondary character to a pivotal figure in the storyline. And, oh my God, Cillian Murphy....steals the show. Who would've guessed that the guy from 28 Days Later could play such a menacing character? Fantastic performance, and I hope we see more of the Scarecrow in future films.

The direction is tight, giving the movie a darker feel than even Burton's version of the tale. Kudos to Nolan for delivering every fanboy's wet dream. I hope Warner Brothers signed him to a sequel contract, as his directorial style meshes beautifully with Batman lore.

Overall, I can't find anything that I did not like about this movie. It was the best time I've had at the theatre so far this year. 10 out of 10.

10.title: Batman at it's best.
10.content:
So before heading off to see this movie, I was a little hesitant. I have been a Batman movie fan my whole life. Being only 17, the first two were a little violent for me, but I fell in love with the whole idea of the one man vigilante story. I grew up with Batman. I went through my awkward phases, and so did the storyline. There was a noticeable difference with the shift from Tim to Joel, and Michael to Val. There wasn't any continuity other than the key player of Batman. Gotham changed instantaneously, and it became a more airy feature and an audience pleaser, but that was all. I thoroughly enjoyed the last two in the Batman series, but I could never get over the Batman i had first viewed after borrowing one of my big sister's videotapes when i was 5. The villains kept getting funnier and funnier, and the scenes became less meaningful and more action packed, heart racing, and pointless. But then I ventured in to see Batman Begins.

I left that theater happier than ever. This movie was everything and more. It was a return to the darker, more mysterious Batman I first fell in love with. Christian Bale is the perfect man for this role, he has all the appeal. I was hesitant at the idea of a star studded cast, because some of these movies receive more hype than they are worth. Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Tom Wilkinson, and Liam Neeson are all Oscar contenders and some winners. They gave well rounded performances and proved that as actors they can truly dive into their roles and not steal the show. Katie Holmes was good as Rachael Dawes, but her role wasn't as pivotal as I had hoped, but despite that, she managed to hold her own and deliver a good performance. I was so surprised by this movie. The comedy was light, but present none the less.

This Batman was unpredictable, and the unknown villain always makes for more edge of your seat viewing, and this movie did not let me down on that factor. I never took my eyes from the screen. The cinematography was so splendid and the story was so perfect. There wasn't so much focus on Batman, but it was on Bruce Wayne and how he transformed into Batman. That was the winner. This plot was so rich and perfect to the return to roots theme every prequel should take. Batman is supposed to be dark, mysterious, and more thought provoking than the, "saving the world and Gotham from certain destruction theme as two villains team up and giggle and joke the entire time" themes that were so prevalent in the last 3 Batmans. This movie was the best of the bunch, and a return to the original Batman from 1989.

Batman Begins is a great movie, and the best of the pack. It has everything the previous movie had, but delivers them in a more concise and pleasing way without focusing too much on one aspect such as action, mystery, or comedy. It is all of these and more, and I guarantee everyone will if not love, at least enjoy this movie.

10.title: FINALLY, a DC Comic movie that gets it right!
10.content:
I was a comic collector as a child and young adult so I obviously love comic book movies. The Superman movies were okay and the Batman movies were also barely okay. They emphasized the things that made them non-comic book and took away many of the comic book elements. When Marvel started getting great movies with X-Men and Spiderman, I saw that someone finally had learned to do it right. Of course there are some misses (Elektra) but overall, I have come to expect more of Marvel comic book movies than anything from DC (the company which owned Superman, Batman, Justice League, etc.).

This movie really goes back to the comic book roots. Forget the other Batman movies, they have nothing to do with this one. In this Batman, you see how Bruce becomes a hero and why he chose Batman. The portrayal of Gotham and of Thomas Wayne (Bruce's father) help to flesh things out more like the way a comic story would than "character development" in a movie fashion. The league of shadows and the Scarecrow all flow with the story rather than serve as elements inserted as generic villains of the week.

I completely enjoyed this movie and although some elements are different from the comic book, they are true to the spirit of the books and that is what counts (like Spiderman being able to shoot webbing without webshooters was still faithful to the idea of the comic). I hope you will give it a try and support Hollywood making movie actually from comic books rather than just movies with titles or characters from comic books.

10.title: The Best Batman movie of ALL time!
10.content: Nolan's Batman is by far more superior than Tim Burton's mediocre stylized Batman (that seems to lack in character development) - in so many ways possible. Unlike Burton's vision of establishing Batman as a second rate character in his own films which I disliked immensely, Nolan creates layers upon layers of dimension for the Batman character as well as the Bruce Wayne individual that acts as the mask for who he really is. The 'realistic' approach makes the film stand out upon others, with the gritty realism pouring everywhere throughout the film that makes it sometimes take itself a little too seriously. Let's face it, Christian Bale is better than Kilmer, Clooney and possibly Keaton as playing millionaire Bruce Wayne - a man with a haunted and distort soul. Not only does he embody everything I see in Batman and Bruce, he's an amazing actor and adds a great blend of dark, brooding, and richness to the portrayal of a quite sane young man. He has the best of scenes (especially the one's involving Freeman), and he's fairly buff in the role, something the ladies will undoubtedly like. The rest of the cast is top-notch, mostly Oscar winners or nominees or just plain outstanding actors (though Holmes is neither) in some way or another. Caine is butler Alfred, Freeman is inventor Lucius Fox in Wayne Industries, Oldman is good cop Jim Gordon, Neeson is Henri Ducard (well, this turns out to be false) - mentor and father figure to Bruce, Watanabe is actually the decoy as Neeson turns out to be terrorist villain Ra's Al Ghul, and Holmes gets to play the damsel in distress/love interest/childhood friend as D.A. Rachel Dawes; her character isn't in the comic and was only invented for the film, just to let you know. She's not at her best to be honest - with her slightly insipid lines and the fact that she looks awfully young compared to Bale (and her character is older if you can believe that). There's also two performances that took me by complete surprise. First, Cillian Murphy is Dr. Jonathan Crane also known as the Scarecrow, who happens to work in the infamous Arkham Asylum. It's nice to say, his creepy presence on screen gets creepier by his influence of his 'fear gas' - hallucinations from your wildest dreams or nightmares. Then there's Tom Wilkinson as crime boss Falcone who has a lot of people doing his dirty work in Gotham. The accent he puts on is somewhat mafia-like and I like it. Now enough with the cast, let's talk about the fight scenes that are disappointing to some degree. Nolan isn't really good at the fight sequences delivered in this film, but he still has time for major improvement (I'm talking about the sequels - if he's willing to make them). There are extremely choppy, yet not what you'd expect. The editing is all wrong, but I'm willing to look past it (you should too). Overall, the plot is convincing as a Batman flick and Nolan deserves most of the credit as do the people that have worked their butts off creating a masterpiece with depth. Batman has been truly reborn, once again.

10.title: Batman is back!!
10.content:
Must say at first I was a little skeptical about this movie. Would it be a disaster such us the last Shumacher's Batman.

Could not be more wrong. It's a great movie and not just for the Batman's fan. It's seems almost true and possible. The characters are excellent. Nice job!!!! The only flow is trying to connect this movie with the first Burton Batman. The guy who killed Bruces parents in Burton Batman actually becomes Joker when Batman drops him into the acid, while at the end of Batman Begings we learn that Joker already exist and the murderer of Bruces parents is already dead.

Other than this, this movie is worth watching and not only from Batman fans.

10.title: Excellent!
10.content:
I have to say it. This Batman movie is by far my favorite. After the atrocity known as Batman and Robin (now let us never speak of that again), I was hoping- REALLY hoping- for a good batman flick. Man, this did not disappoint. I think what really makes this movie shine is it's cast. Christian Bale IS Bruce Wayne. He is dead on as the dark knight.

I cannot understand how Michael Caine was not cast as Alfred for the other 4 movies. If he was busy with something else, fine, if not what was the excuse? Morgan Freeman is excellent as Lucius, same goes for Tom Wilkinson as Falcone. Cillian Murphy really broke out last summer, and this movie helped significantly. He was great as the creepy scarecrow. Watanabe was great as Ra's Al Ghul. But my favorite performance was Liam Neeson as Ducard. He is the main reason I love this movie so much. I mean seriously, is there a movie where this guy sucks? He is awesome in very movie I've seen him in. I have to agree with Roger Ebert. This really is one of the best movies of 2005.

10.title: Best Superhero Film Ever!
10.content: Gripping from Start to finish. Christian Bale is the perfect choice for Batman (and Bruce Wayne). The action is great, the dialogue is great, big players like Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman are used wisely and effectively. A must see film and probably one of the best I have ever seen - and I have seen a lot of films! It's emotional charge grabs at your chest like a rampaging Gorilla and there is never a second when you are not entertained or swept along with the story as it unfolds. From the tender moments to the high octane action this film hits the spot at all levels and is relentless entertainment form start to finish. WOW!

10.title: Well scripted, filmed and acted, one of the best "superhero" movies.
10.content:
I was surprised that it was this good, i just got back from the movies and damn i expected something good but this is one of the best, if not the best superhero movie i've seen. People always tend to think of superhero movies as not being able to achieve the same blockbuster status as other movies, but all that changed with Spiderman which set the bar higher for other superhero movies and i can say that Nolan has clearly found the best way to show the birth of batman. I mean come on, this batman is nothing like any other batman we've seen. Its not bale wearing a costume, its Batman, Nolan showed us how different Bruce Wayne and Batman are. The split personally shown in a very in your face way. And Bale portrayed that very well, change of voice as batman, change of walking pace and style and the way he shouted to that corrupt cop: "Swear to me" when the guy said "i swear to god" that was powerful, its the way Bob Kane wrote batman at the beginning. That is, not as Bruce Wayne in a costume but as a separate character from Bruce Wayne. The only thing in common is the compassion that he has for people and the hatred for injustice and crime.

The Scarecrow was impressive even with just the mask and not the whole scarecrow costume that we've seen in the comics. And Luscious Fox fits well in the story, as usually(in other movies) its Alfred who designs/works on the gadgets but this makes more sense. Alfred cant do everything. Michael Caine is believable as Alfred Pennyworth, a father figure and a friend for Bruce.

Henry Ducard(Liam Neeson) impressed me in the first scene itself when he beats up Bruce Wayne, he's bad. The training looked cool on screen, with the ninja outfits and armour. In the previous movies we haven't been told how batman has all these skills(in fact they don't show that much fighting skills anyway) but this one shows how, by training Bruce Wayne becomes more than a man.

He doesn't have any superpowers thats what i like about Batman, he doesn't need the powers. The way that he scares the enemies was well thought, in the first scene where we actually see Batman in action, he gives these guys the creeps. And thats what Batman is all about.

Gotham city looks great, the landscapes, buildings, the train and especially the Wayne Building. Now the Batmobile not only looks good, its bulky, bumpy but still sleek looking and its massive, the scenes where the cops are chasing it are awesome, even if its just a vehicle you can get a feel for how it relates to Batman's personality.

10.title: wow
10.content: BATMAN, FROM THE ASHES OF THE JOEL SHUMACHER DEBACLE, HAS BEEN RESURRECTED. Quite frankly Chris Nolan gives Tim Burton a run for his money. Talk about your good interpretation of the origin. Character development was phenomenal. Plot was classic Batman fare. Truly a good beginning. Michael Caine was brilliant as Bruce's heartwarming and caring guardian. I can only hope Gary Oldman sees more screen time in the next two. It looks as though he will. There's a bond between Batman and himself much like the animated series. There will be more of a collaboration between the two I think. Will Katie Holmes make it to the next one or like so many Bond and Batman movies will there be a replacement?

10.title: What a gem!
10.content:
For all fans of Batman 1997 was a desperate and depressing year. Not only was it to be George Clooney donning the bat suit (a woeful choice of casting) but Batamn and Robin was to become one of the most universally hated films ever made. It was a crying shame really, as a fairly decent series (the Burton films were works of pure genius) came to cataclysmic end with such a diabolical piece of s**t.

Thank god, then, for Bataman Begins, which not only re-invents the tale of the dark night but gives the character the moody edge that the Schumacher instalments sorely lacked. Written by Blade scribe, David S. Goyer, this film puts a fresh new spin on things, showing us events leading up to the creation of the Dark Knight.

As the title suggests this is the beginning of the story. We start with Bruce Wayne as a young boy, playing hide and seek. after falling down a well he is confronted by a swarm of bats, that terrify him. We then cut forward 20 years or so to see him in a Korean prison where he is met by a man that calls himself Ducard. He takes Bruce under his wing and teaches him the ways of the Ninja. Once Bruce find out that this group (known as the league of shadows) plans to destroy Gotham, he takes them out. Desiding that he must return to him home town, he gathers all the equipment he can in order to become the fearless vigilante that we all know and love.

This film is essentially a two act film. the first half focuses more on the drama, on the desperation of Bruce Wayne. In fact we don't see him in the Batsuit until an hour in. But once he become the Dark Knight, the drama takes a sidestep for some breathtaking action sequences. There's a car chase around the streets of Gotham, a scene of mass pandemonium around Arkham Asylam and the end monorail set piece that is a non stop ride of hard pumping action.

This film is a fan boy's dream. It has non of the campy god awful one-liners that made Batman and Robin such a failure. This is a much darker Edgy film and works all the better for it. This could be the start of another beautiful franchise. With Marvel stealing the limelight in recent years, it's good to see that D.C. Comics is making a grand return. Lets just hope Superman Returns will b this good.

5/5

10.title: First Step To World Peace
10.content: This was a great first step to world peace. I believe that it could end all wars. Maybe if all this movie was thrown to Iraq instead of bombs, then everyone there would be like "wow, America isn't really so bad at all" and then want to come over to our basements and watch Batman: Begins and listen to Ramones records. Seriously though... I have never seen anything like this in my life. In fact, cancel the 2005 academy awards, I think we have a winner. I propose that we start a fund to have a real Batman. I elect Christian Bale to be the first real batman, if he accepts. Maybe he could help bring along peace. You know, doing what he does best. Maybe now there won't be so many problems in the world. I feel like a changed man after seeing this film. Batman begins to be the best movie ever, and it never stops. BEST... MOVIE... EVER.

10.title: In a word. Excellent
10.content: Why excellent? I've been a superhero buff all my life and I a 42 year-old woman. This movie does the Batman series a huge tribute. It brings a tear to my eye that the first series didn't due Batman the justice that this movie does. I have been a Christian Bale fan ever since I saw "Newies". He plays an excellent Bruce Wayne/Batman. I was a little nervous for such great actor to play such a part. When it's not done well, an actor can get type casted or worse. Now I actually look forward to seeing him playing Batman again. Like Tobey McQuire when a superhero movie is done right, you don't have no fear of losing your career. Top notch stars like Liam Neeson, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Gary Oldman round out this movie. Such great talent for such an excellent movie. I hope the director Christopher Nolan stays on board as well through the series. At this time, I have no idea what they have in the works, but as long as the team stays on I hope to see many more. (RULE OF THUMB - Never let the bad guys out shine the good guy!) This should be as successful a film as the Spiderman series. So go spend the big bucks to make it happen.

10.title: Wayne's World! Arguably the best of the Batman flicks; high quality production and highly entertaining prequel to a lucrative franchise; Nolan hits a homerun
10.content: BATMAN BEGINS (2005) **** Christian Bale, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, Michael Caine, Cillian Murphy, Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman, Tom Wilkinson, Rutger Hauer, Ken Watanabe, Mark Boone Junior, Linus Roache. Excellent prequel 'origin' of The Dark Knight that adds fresh blood to a weakened franchise thanks largely to the unlikely POW! BAM! combo of indie filmmaker Christopher Nolan and Bale (with an intense, brooding yet vulnerable turn and a fine jaw for the infamous cowl to boot!) as billionaire heir Bruce Wayne hellbent for vengeance for the murder of his parents which leads him on a journey of redemption from the brutal Asian prison camp after taking a nowhere-to-go downward spiral attempt at crime where he encounters the mysterious Henri Ducard (a suitable Neeson) and the ninja-training from guru of vigilantism Ra's Al Ghul (an imposing Watanabe) laying the foundation to his inner turmoil exploited into an iconic hero to thwart the evil in Gotham. Watching all the jigsaw puzzle pieces interlock from the beginnings of Wayne's brainy conceit of the Batsuit to the Humvian Batmobile are giddy joys for the inner fanboy of every squandered youth. A sound cast of international bravado (Caine as Alfred, the butler, Wayne's manservant/father figure, adds a dash of subtle observations and common sense; Freeman as Wayne Enterprises' best kept secret displaying the varying degrees of know-how and Bat-phenalia; Oldman as a young (soon-to-be Commissioner) Jim Gordon  apparently the only honest cop on the force has a few nice subtle moments of awe and cunning; silky Murphy as Dr. Jonathan Crane AKA The Scarecrow; Wilkinson as ganglord Carmine Falcone affecting a New Yorkese dialect tuff guy demeanor; Hauer as a reptilian board chairman of Wayne's empire with oily ease); sterling production design by Nathan Crowley envisioning Gotham City as "New York on steroids", the dank cinematography by Wally Pfister, and reimagining of the stealthy costumed Caped Crusader by designer Lindy Hemming combine for a robust display of ingenuity. The wraithlike incarnation of the man into batsuit avenger is a thing of Gothic beauty (echoing the Tim Burton and Frank Miller conceit) expertly designed by screenwriter David S. Goyer (the "Blade" trilogy to name just three successful comic book to screen adaptations) with Nolan flexes the mind, muscle and sardonic humor quintessential to a truly American original hero. Arguably the best of the Batman films and highly entertaining; what more can you ask for when you see a flying Batman soar over the glassy plains of Gotham! ** see this on the IMAX and all I can say is : wow! Five words: a 90 foot Katie Holmes; how can you go wrong!!

10.title: My new favorite movie!
10.content: Batman has always been my favorite superhero, and when the first Batman film was released in 1989 they put a decent stamp and a fair intro of the dark knight to the big screen. But this movie interprets the batman as realistic and as human as possible, and what a job the cast does, their are some big names in this movie and they all play their part in equality, only Bruce Wayne/Batman is hogging screen time which is what I wanted to see unlike the previous Batman films, we're the story was focused on the villains. I've seen all of the Batman films from 89 to 97 and none can compare to the quality and the storyline of this film, especially the last two flops.

10.title: A detailed prequel to the Batman series...
10.content: This was by far one of the most exciting, entertaining and overall best films of the year. Christian Bale's excellent portrayal of Bruce Wayne/Batman is captivating. Outstanding performances done by all, except for K Holmes. (I think the casting director really could have chosen someone better suited to play opposite such a strong character as Batman.) It's hard to get past the Dawson Creek days and take such a cheesy "actress" seriously. (Besides the fact that she talks out of the side of her face) Any and all questions regarding the history of Bruce Wayne/Batman are answered and to trivia buffs, this turned out to be most fulfilling attribute. A never before seen twist on what could be thought of as a campy, can't take too serious, franchise. The screenplay really takes the city of Gotham and gives it a true existence possible in today's world. Storyline is interesting, action packed and keeps your attention. Two thumbs up, Bale is definitely an awesome actor and the best Batman so far!

10.title: The Future is Dark, Batman has truly begun
10.content: This film gave me everything I wanted/expected plus more, but will still leave you thirsty for a sequel. Top quality performances all around makes this my film of the year. This really has launched something truly remarkable in the Batman movie time-line. Hopefully this will show Warner Bros that giving the fans what they want instead of commercialising will still guarantee impressive figures at the box office. Cant wait to see this film again. This re-birth of Batman has set strong foundations for the future of the franchise and I hope the same cast and crew sign on for many more if they are made this way. Go see it, then see it again. Its the first time this year I feel I have got my moneys worth from a cinema.

10.title: The Original Batman Legend
10.content:
What will you want to see when you go for a Batman movie which tells you of how Bruce Wayne becomes the Dark Knight of Gotham? An introduction to his childhood, his deepest fears which become the stimulus for what grows within him, his aimless wanderings around the world, his methodical training, his realization to where he should put himself in this world despite what his training demands him of, his preparations for his new life, the slow and very slow ways of introducing his secret self, teasing glimpses of his style and action, and a prodigious ending where all of what he is, is displayed full, as the colossal BATMAN.

This movie has it all.

Christian Bale is one of my favorite actors since Equilibrium (2002). He has given a very responsible and matured performance. I liked Michael Keaton. I liked Val Kilmer. And Bale? From his post-adolescent age, through the wanderer period and till the end as a superhero, he has shown significant differences in every stage of his acting. He is born for this role.

Bale has given a performance through which the subtleties of his character of a Batman growing from scratches are very carefully depicted. For an instance, even after wearing the hood, his manners and ways of delivering speech are full of emotions. He shouts, swears, worries. But as his personality builds on and on, he becomes more silent, more methodic, more dark and more a Batman.

Liam Neeson is as usual the screen stunner. He is as cool as he was as Qui Gon Jinn (Star Wars - Episode I) and as Godfrey (Kingdom of Heaven). I loved watching him train Bale exhibiting his arrogant confidence. Morgan Freeman comes only in a few scenes but makes his mark. His witty talks and the proud-but-humble way he displays his inventions to Bale are some on the lighter side of the movie. Hats off to Sir Michael Caine as Alfred. No one else would suite better, particularly when he has to say - "Never".

Every character and every scene has been chosen properly. The deliberate minor imperfections in clothing, weaponry and action scenes vividly reminds us that this is a prequel portraying a beginner and not an advanced superhero. The gripping score from Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard constitutes the power drive for those amazing 141 on-screen minutes. Ultimately, the movie has justified its title.

I have never seen Batman so dark and so powerful. This movie is a dream come true for a die-hard fan like me. Extending his black wings the Dark Knight vanishes in flight before we could even realize it. Nolan has teased us to the core but has made sure to leave those awing flashes behind our eyes which tells us of... what Batman means!

10.title: This movie is greater than life!!!!!!!
10.content: "Batman Begins" is a movie that it arises with the mission of recover the franchise, after the horrible "Batman & Robin" of Joel Schumacher. Now, the Warner Studios leaves the project in the hands of Christopher Nolan (director of Memento and Insomnia)and the scrip writer David S. Goyer ,familiriazed with the comic book world. And the only way of regaining the lost prestige of Batman it's trough a picture that it treats the character in a very realistic way, but without losing its roots with the comic book. The movie has a serious treatment and the action that involves a movie of this size it is given in a smart way and always according to the story. There is attention in that the figure of Batman does not came in a spontaneous way, instead, it shows the many sacrifices that Bruce Wayne had to face in order to become the dark knight. Bruce Wayne has the same importance than Batman, and it is show to us how it was those years moved away of Gotham and how a man could transform his live in a quest for justice. The bat mobile,the batman suit, the bat cave, his weapons, are in all moments justified. The suit it is just a military armor whit some adds on. The bat cave it is not was constructed by man, it is just a big cave with a waterfall, that it is the home of the bats that frighten Bruce Wayne. And the same happen with everything else in the movie, where the script respond to the necessities of the story and does not result skillful the way in which are told this actions. During the whole picture we are before the presence of a city that it's look real, but in a certain way it's a hyper reality. As in the comics, certain aspects of the reality are emphasized. In fact, Gotham remember the look of Blade runner, for the way in which mix modernity with decay and darkness. The story is surrounding, because in each moment we wanted to know more about the journey of this hero in order to stop the imminent terrorist action against Gotham.One character that it had been left of side was the commissioner James Gordon, who in this occasion is a police sergeant, one of the few honest in Gotham, someone which in every look shows a feeling of sadness but at the same time of hope that things could be done in good way, in a decent way, that Gotham does not succumb in corruption and crime. He becomes one of the allies of the dark knight, because it intuits that something impressive is needed in order to wake up the people of Gotham. Batman Begins it is the best adaptation of a Superhero to the big screen, because it respects the origin of Batman, developing convincing characters and situations, showing the cape crusader as an threatening and brutal figure, that it relocates it as the hero he always has been, lord of the knight and doom of the criminals.

10.title: WOW! Now that's what I call a movie!!!
10.content: Firstly, let me say I have been a life long Spider-Man fan and love both of the recent movies, but after seeing this, I am finding it hard to decide which I prefer the bat or the spider. I guess it will all depend on my mood as they both have significantly different atmospheres. Of course no movie is perfect, and only 1 movie has ever scored a perfect "10" but this came damn close. Great acting, writing, directing and a realism no other superhero movie could possibly match. Mind you Batman isn't a superhero in the true sense of the word as he doesn't actually have any super powers. The whole origin was superb. His training, his gadgets, his fears and torments, they are all feasibly realistic. And best of all, no cheesy nipples on the costume! I hope for the love of God that we will not be inflicted with a Robin or Batgirl in any of the sequels because that will spoil the mood. In closing, if you haven't seen this movie yet, do it!!!

10.title: A cinematic masterpiece (POSSIBLE SPOILERS)
10.content: After seeing Batman Begins on Friday night, I was just totally gob smacked, sitting there as the credits rolled, I've seen a lot of films, and being an actor myself, I find myself being very critical, analysing and over-analysing films from the acting to production, and so forth; but as I sat there after the film finished, it dawned on me that I had seen for than just a Batman film, more than just THE Batman film, what I had seen in my eyes was truly a cinematic masterpiece, that realised and achieved everything the script by the talented Mr Goyer, and indeed the comics of the last 66 years and set out to tell; Mr Nolan and company, have put together one of the finest most breathtaking films I have seen in a long, long, long, long time. The epic quality of this film, gives this the feel that this is very much a real film and not your typical comic book hero film. There is very much a wealth of emotion within in this film, predominantly fear, but it draws you in to care about the characters, especially Christian Bale's Bruce Wayne, you can at times feel yourself in his shoes. One of the catalyst moments in this film, the murder or Thomas and Martha Wayne, is handled and executed (no pun intended) very well, the camera angles draw you in from both sides of the situation; it isn't drawn out too long before there demise, creating a quick sense of panic and fear, ending quickly with the murder, bang Thomas is shot , within a second or two, Martha is shot, as someone viewing this you're are not given time to react the first shot before hearing the second, which places you in the young Bruce Wayne's shoes; the whole scene is just in your face up close and personal, and through out the film scenes are done in this way, no matter how far away from the screen you way be, this technique draws you in and involves you in every critical moment. The very essence of this film and the examples in cinema, and graphic novelisation it draws from (last time I use the word draws, promise) Blade Runner for example, and the very comics its based on, this film surpasses them all for it's visual quality, indeed the comics could learn a lot from this film. The Spiderman films may have raised the bench mark for these sort of films, but this film has made the bench unreachable, and could easily hold its own up against the the top 50 classic films of all time; it is a real pleasure to see this film in 64th place of the Top 250 films on this website. Full praise is deserved to the actors in this film as well, Bale is Bruce Wayne/Batman, its hard to imagine anyone else in the role, Bale owns it. The same goes for Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Gary Oldman, the roles they play, were made for them; the chemistry between these actors works works extremely well and adds to the attention to detail this film maintains through out. But I'm not going to single out the rest of the cast, as all were exceptional, no matter how big or small their part in this film. The villains of this film, all carried a certain panache, all equally chilling in their individual ways, nothing over the top, just purely sinister and insidious. One thing that annoyed me about reviews of this film is the Katie Holmes bashing and how she lets the film down, can I say to those of you out there who feel this and you know who you are, you are talking rubbish, Katie does a splendid job playing the friend and the D.A. that gets caught in the whirlwind events that take Gotham city, indeed even her performance plays a vital part in the chemistry that links the characters, and makes you care for them. My hats off to the Production staff and Special Effects team, every location of the Batman myth has been faithfully and realistically recreated, the Batsuit, the utility belt and kit, especially the bat mobile, all make realistic sense, considering Batman's mission to reclaim Gotham and considering how dangerous that will be. The Tumbler is an amazing piece of machinery, and shouldn't be changed at all. I love the way every aspect of Batman's suit and gadgets are explained, with out boring us, and with out sounding far fetched, remember the bat mobile really can do most of those stunts. My only recommendation is to go and see this film, see it as many times as you can on the big screen, whether it will earn the credit or respect it so rightfully deserves, this film has earned its right in cinematic history. I have one piece of advice, forget Starwars, and War of the Worlds, these heavily special effects laden films think that CGI is the answer and is the selling point, and ignore good story telling, and lose passionate character acting, both films represent a misguide tired tradition in Hollywood, Batman Begins finally proves that CGI should only be used to enhance a film and not carry it. Don't be made to think these films are better than Batman Begins, they are very different in their own right, but can't hold a candle to good old fashioned story telling, god bless you Mr Nolan, for sticking to your guns, and producing a film the way it should be done, as for you Mr Lucas and Mr Spielberg....shame on you, the public is wising up, Batman Begins has sent the bench mark sky high, just try topping that

10.title: Excellent Movie .. But a Change of Pace
10.content:
Others have beautifully described this elegant film, so i will dispense with trying to copy what has already been done.

My contribution is slightly negative. Even though i gave the movie 10 out of 10, there was one thing that bothered me the whole time. I really feel that this movie should have been given a different title. "Batman Begins" uses the same naming convention as the other Batman series... "Batman Returns .. Batman Forever .. Batman Begins," but this movie is clearly something completely different. The other movie series was Batman in its own movie world. This one is more strongly tied to his comic book roots. I'm not saying that's a bad thing, in fact, i loved it... however, when Bruce's parents were killed, and then the killer shot dead years later, i was left scratching my head. "He's supposed to become the Joker in the 'next' movie," i thought to myself.

I walked into this movie expecting it to be a "prequal" of the existing movie series, not the start of a new one. I feel that difference is very important, and should have been more clearly presented to the public.

That, however, was the only gripe i had. It was beautifully shot, wonderful written, and expertly cast. A true gem.
