10.title: A "real" Batman for the ages
10.content:
I was a young child who was terrified by both of Burton's Batman movies. Gave me nightmares for years, no joke. Only as a teenager, was I able to watch the original and appreciate the show and Gothic darkness that Burton put onto the screen. Joel Schumacher's Batman Forever wasn't too bad, but Batman and Robin ranks up there with one of the worst movies I have ever seen. It was like a train wreck I couldn't turn away from. When I heard that Christopher Nolan (of Memento) was directing a new Batman, I knew that it would be something I had to see.

I was not disappointed. This movie has everything - drama, action, love, hope, and yes, even a few clever wisecracks. The movie is dark, but it seems real. Unlike both previous directors, Nolan has made this movie quite persuasive in its realism. Sure the plot itself is doubtful - a renowned billionaire heir disappears off the face of the earth to train with a secret ninja association in Asia, returning to fight a villain employing a hallucinogenic "fear powder" to render his victims helpless. The characters on-screen, however, are three-dimensional, as complex as any human being alive right now.

Christian Bale is excellent as Bruce Wayne/Batman: a young man bent on reining in his anger for a common good. However, his Batman is not invincible. You question some of his choices and feel his vulnerability in several of his nocturnal outings. He gets HURT in this movie. It is also clear that Batman is the real personality behind the character, and not the rich playboy Bruce Wayne.

I adored Michael Caine as Alfred, the devoted-yet-concerned father figure. He doesn't quite approve of Bruce's career choice, but still helps out whatever way he can. The relationship between Alfred and Bruce was so heartwarming I had tears in my eyes during several scenes.

Katie Holmes surprised me by bringing great strength to assistant DA Rachel Dawes, girlish voice aside. The character has a spine and won't allow anyone to sway her. Same with Lt. James Gordon, played by Gary Oldman. He has his doubts about the new mysterious vigilante, but holds hope that this figure will bring hope to the ravaged city.

It was great to see Liam Neeson really savor his role as a mentor, despite it being the umpteenth time he has played it. A few of his lines would have come out completely cheesy if it were not for his persuasive delivery. (For some reason he couldn't find the same oomph in Phantom Menace, but that's another thing entirely.) In teaching Bruce, he employs tough love, and nothing short of it.

All of the other characters only added to the film. The casting was absolutely perfect, in my opinion.

Despite its 2.5 running time, the movie seems a lot shorter. The only time I looked at my watch was when Batman first appeared: I wanted to see if an hour had really passed by from the movie's start, and it had. I've read some criticisms about the movie's pacing, but it didn't bother me at all. In fact, I thought that the first 20 minutes were too fast, since a lot of things happened in those 20 minutes that changed the characters greatly. I felt as if I had been thrown into the movie in the middle of it.

There have also been some criticisms about the action sequences. The fast-moving camera angles and quick edits confuses the viewer, but in my opinion, Nolan was trying to give us a taste of how Batman worked. His victims do not see him coming at all, and when he attacks, it is a flurry of action. During the big one-on-one fights, I was able to track the characters well enough to see who had the upper hand, which I think was the point. Batman's first night out is wonderfully shot - it is a scene straight out of a horror movie, and I jumped in my seat several times. The bad guys disappear one by one and when the audience finally gets to see Batman in full costume, it is awesome.

The fear sequences are well done, but not too frightening. I had been expecting worse, heh. Or maybe I've just grown up enough to not have that kind of stuff scare me as it did years ago. Despite it not affecting me the same way as Burton's original did, I feel that this is the best Batman movie to date. It's not just a great comic book movie, but one of the best movies I've ever seen.

10.title: Best comic book movie ever
10.content: I tend to dislike comic book movies, but "Batman Begins" is much more than that. It's action packed, but realistic, with characters you feel emotion for. It's dark, mysterious, and moody. The hype, cartoon junk of the last two Batman movies is gone, and in it's place is a movie which is scary, dark, action packed, and fun. A perfect cast combined with a perfect story line combined with perfect direction and production equals the BEST comic book movie I have ever seen. Christian Bale plays both the roles of Bruce Wayne and the dark knight with perfection. He doesn't go without a hinge, and you actually can develop feelings and emotion for Bruce Wayne, the first time I have ever felt that in a Batman movie. Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Katie Holmes, Liam Nisson and the others all do their roles very well also. Go see it today and see what Batman truly should be like.

10.title: The best Batman movie ever made!!!
10.content:
I loved this movie. "Batman Begins" has done something other movies have failed to do in my opinion, it lived up to it's expectations.!!!!!!

Words can't describe how the good the movie was except it was excellent. I knew this movie was going to be good when I saw the cast list: Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, the question mark seemed to be Christian Bale could he pull of the biggest role of his career? The answer to that movie fans is yes!!!

Bale is somewhat underrated, he's appeared in some good movies and some stinkers but this movie interviews he did for "Batman Begins" on Access Hollywood, I knew he could do He was sincere and serious about making a good impression and he did on them some. He underwent some serious training to get into the role and it definitely shows on screen.Bale did an excellent job!!!

Liam Neeson who I praised on "Kingdom of Heaven" likewise comes through with another memorable but short roles as Ducard, the man who takes Bruce Wayne under his wing and makes him a fighting machine.

With Ducard's help, Bruce Wayne (Bale) is able to come into grips about the murders of his parents, something that was eating away at him and destroying him.Through Ducard and Alfred's (Michael Caine) guidance, we see the origins of the Batman starting to come through until his Metamorphis in Gotham City is complete.

Plotwise the movie title says it "Batman Begins" we see the origins of Batman/Bruce Wayne in detail from childhood to adult as he grows from a child coping with the death of his parents to a man possessed by his own destiny to rid the world evil and battle the demons inside him.

Then comes the real challenge for Wayne as he faces the corruption and violence that is overtaking the city. Sure we've seen this in the other Batman movies but what sets this one apart from the other ones, is the acting, the character development, in Bruce Wayne's growth as a man as he struggles within his demons, the psychological battles he plays with himself.

Enter Katie Holmes who plays Rachel Dawes , Waynes love interest and Batman's love interest, a good girl being caught in some bad company. You know Wayne loves her but he is still dealing with issues, becoming the Batman then provides an avenue for Bruce to get closer to Rachel while protecting her at the same time.

Cilliam Murphy as Dr. Jonathan Crane/The Scarecrow, is also excellent, he actually seems like an insignificant foe but once he's alter ego shows on the scree, it's a different story. Ken Watanabe as the other important figure Ra's Al Ghul who aids Wayne's training is good and last but not ;least Morgan Freeman as Luscious Fox who basically gives the first look at the creation that is the Batmobile is excellent.

Director Christopher Nolan not only deserves a pat on the back for his excellent adaptation of the comic book character but a hug from every comic book fan whose been wanting a respectable version of the "Dark Knight" for quite some time.

This movie had heart, it was gritty, it was dramatic, and Batman wasn't a stupid a cartoon cutout like George Clooney's stupid portrayal but he was a man, a real man with real problems and issues, and above you liked it, you really him We sympathized with Bale's portrayal as Wayne, and we cheer as he goes through his whole training until he becomes the Dark Knight and imprints his legacy as the defender of justice and truth.

I can't say anymore about this movie except it's perhaps the best if not the best Batman movie ever made, at the same level if not surpassing the original by Tim Burton.

Go see it now and enjoy!!!

10.title: Not Just a Great Superheor Movie but Just a Great Movie
10.content: Last year around may the batman begins hype started up. I of course always being a fan of batman was excited to get the chance to see batman done right. The cast was perfect, the director was perfect, but i always wondered if the story would be accurate and perfect? Last night my questions were answered when i was privileged to see a free screening of batman begins. Anyone who had any doubts about this movie can now be at ease because this movie has now set a new standard of what a good superhero movie truly means. We have seen spider-man and have seen daredevil but what both of those have in common is there fake and not believable. Don't get me wrong I'm not saying a guy who dresses up like a bat and fights crime is real but in batman begins as you watch you start to realize why he is doing this and why for some reason it makes sense. I was trying to figure out if the acting was just great or was it the story. Well the acting is amazing Christian Bale is batman and thats all i have to say bout that. Michael Cain, Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman and Liam Neeson all give great performances and you can tell they put everything they had into this movie. Cillian Murphy as the Scarecrow was something to see as they tie it all together very nicely, Ken Wantanabe as Ra Ja Gule is very good even though you only see him for a short time. One aspect of the movie that could have been left out but you learn to understand why it is in there is Katie Holms, not to say she didn't do a great job but the character of Rachel Dawes being in the movie can be questioned. But as good as those actors are it was the story that makes this movie, the story was right on and explains every single thing in detail. You will not leave the theater asking yourself questions about the movie but leaving the theater talking about part after part of this movie. In closing this is the batman movie everyone has been waiting for and the superhero movie that will be the new standard on what good is.

10.title: Great Movie
10.content: This is, in my opinion, the best of all the Batman movies. Under Christopher Nolan, director of the dark movie Memento, the franchise enjoys a successful revival. Nolan is sure-handed with is script and direction, and it shows. The performances are top-notch, and Gotham City is very dark and in trouble. The movie begins with Bruce Wayne's(Christian Bale) childhood, from the incident that causes him to fear bats to seeing his parents killed before his eyes by a robber. It also shows his recruitment from a prison by the enigmatic Henri Ducard and subsequent training so that he may join the League of Shadows, a mysterious group bent on justice, led by the ever-scowling Ra's Al Ghul(Ken Watanabe). Bruce returns to Gotham, ready to fight injustice. Gotham is unknowingly gearing up for their first villain, the creepy, extremely frightening Scarecrow, who plans to use the citizens' fear against them. But there is a bigger villain at large, and nothing is as it seems. Bruce also runs into his childhood sweetheart, incorruptible assistant D.A. Rachel Dawes(Katie Holmes). He suits up as Batman to begin the fight to save Gotham. Overall a dark and scary film, but very good with a believable story and excellent performances.

10.title: Best Movie I have ever seen
10.content: Batman has never been this real! I was gripped from the beginning, the Director considered every angle of the character and portrayed him as you would see in the comics, dark, raw almost animalistic. With every aspect of each toy being described with feasible technologies that can well exist, as well as scene's that are written to be as close to reality as possible this movie really brings Batman to life! I was and still am a big fan of the Burton films but Batman Begins is on a whole other level, looking back now, Batman was Keaton in a suite this does not hold true for Bale, his entire character changes in the suite, this made the battle that Bruce has within himself easier to relate to.

10.title: Batman Begins makes its mark as a dark and epic superhero tale
10.content: Be forewarned that I am an avid Batman fan and have been since I was a child. I grew up watching the motion pictures and the highly acclaimed animated series, gradually becoming more or less obsessed with the Dark Knight. Once I was able to read I started collecting the comics and haven't looked back since. I was hardly nine years old when Batman & Robin was released in June of 1997, and I honestly thought I'd never see Batman make the big screen again (after such a campy take). But here I am, age seventeen, and not only did Batman make it to the big screen again, but this time it was for real. Batman Begins satisfied my thirst for an accurate and dark portrayal of the hugely popular comic book icon, easily ranking among the best comic book adaptations ever created. In my opinion, although some might view at as a biased one, Batman Begins is the single best comic book film thus far. What more could you ask for in a film based on comic books? The acting was grand, the story had substance, there was action, explanation, and even some dry humor to lighten up the majorally serious movie. Christian Bale hit the weights for this movie and is the closest physical replica to Batman that I've seen in the movies. (Sorry Keaton, Kilmer, and Clooney). Not only that, but his attitude towards criminals was exactly similar to the Batman we all know and love in the comics: downright scary. He is the exact opposite of your average superhero, he's just not a nice guy. He's filled with guilt, anger, and rage, and he takes it out on his enemies quite nicely. The manner in which he scolded Flass with such ferocity made me want to congratulate Christian Bale. The lighting, the atmosphere, the overall feel of this movie just made me a completely happy camper. My goal is to someday portray Batman in a film, and after seeing Christian Bale's solid performance, I've got my work cut out for me. I'd have to honestly say that the only advantage I have on Bale as far as playing Batman would be that I grew up interested in the character, and have hundreds upon hundreds of Batman comic books under my belt, with various styles and portrayals to mix and match with. Jim Lee's Batman is probably the concept I'm most partial to. Anyway, I'm getting slightly off subject with my radical hopes and dreams of starring as the caped crusader in a future film. All I can say is this: I'm a hardcore Batman fan-boy if there ever was one, and this film not only pleased me, it did something even better than that. This movie left me wanting more...which, with the beautiful seg-way at the ending leading into the sequel, should come along within the next two or three years. Batman Begins is a must see film and in my humble (yet biased) opinion is the best movie of the year so far...Thanks for reading -Ryan

10.title: Batman is back and better than ever! Begins is a whole new Batman!
10.content:
After four films, (since 1989) and years away from the big screen, Batman "Begins" in a whole new way, and it's by far the best adaptation of the caped crusader on film yet.

Batman Begins, written by screenwriter David S. Goyer, and directed by Christopher Nolan, is definitely the best screen version of one of the most popular icons in American history.

After more than half a century of his adventures in print, and on television, we now find out about the beginnings of the caped crusader, where he got his state-of-the-art Batman fighting costume, his utility best, his cool gadgets, his Batmobile, and how the Batcave was conceived. Best of all, Batman Begins allows the audience into the mind of Bruce Wayne and why he became Batman himself in the first place.

For the first time on film, Batman is not upsided by the villains of the piece, but rather Batman/Bruce Wayne himself becomes the most interesting character of the film with some of the coolest gadgets seen in a comic book movie.

Christian Bale does a terrific job of becoming Bruce Wayne and his alter ego Batman, while Liam Neeson, Michael Caine, and Morgan Freeman shine in their supporting roles.

Only Katie Holmes is wasted as Bruce Wayne's supposed love interest, Rachel Dawes, an assistant Gotham District Attorney, and is given nothing much to do in this film.

Cillian Murphy, known to audiences in the film 28 Days Later, does a great job of portraying the frightening Scarecrow.

All I can say is that Batman is back and better than before, bring on the sequels of young Batman and many more to come! After years of Marvel dominance at the cinema, DC comics is finally back on track!

A 10 on a scale of 1-10!

10.title: Nolan did a great job.
10.content:
I'm a long-time Batman fan and I'm pretty hard to please when it comes to treatments of the character. I hated what Burton did with his opportunities, and what followed those was beyond sad. I didn't expect to be impressed by this, even with Nolan in the chair.

I am so glad I was wrong.

This was an astoundingly good job. The performances of each actor was so good that I got lost in their roles. For example, Gary Oldman was not in that movie, Gordon was. Michael Caine? Was he in that movie? And even the media darling of the moment Katie Holmes didn't disappoint. It was tight. The lack of camp and the general minimization of in-jokes was also a plus. What "Batmanisms" there were seemed more aimed at making MORE fun of the previous attempts. The statement I saw was: "THIS IS BATMAN TREATED WITH THE REGARD IT DESERVES" rather than just having a Nolan 'stamp' on it, whatever that might mean. Burton 'Burtonized' Batman. Nolan brought Batman to life. It was as if Nolan finally GOT the character and instead of thinking he was hired to revamp, reinvent or stylize Batman, he just let the character do what it does on the pages of the comics: Kick a lot of ass.

It was a rough and rugged, ninja-strewn rise out of darkness followed by a gritty, dirty Gotham City experience that kept my eyeballs glued to the screen from beginning to end. See it. Love it. See it again.

10.title: Goes way beyond a typical comic book film
10.content: I just saw Batman Begins and I was extremely impressed and pleasantly surprised. I went in there with the assumption that it was going to be another blockbuster comic book adaptation that would be forgotten within a year. This film took the character of Batman and really went deep inside it. It was a very dark side of Batman, which is the way it should have been made by Tim Burton. When they were writing the script they could have easily went with a well known "bad-guy" with super powers and it would have been like I said another blockbuster comic book adaptation. Instead they chose the enemy Scarecrow, who I have vaguely heard of. What was so interesting about Scarecrow (who was very well played by Cillian Murphy) was that his "power" was not something like super strength or he shot laser beams out of his eyes, it was an intangible object, fear. He put people in shock by releasing their fears. That whole concept went so far off-course from your typical superhero movie, I really can't say enough about this film. Christian Bale took the character of Batman and brought it so far away from where Michael Keaton, Val Kilmer, and George Clooney brought it. I strongly recommend Batman Begins and I will be the first to add it to my collection once it comes out on DVD.

10.title: Marvelous Scripting and Film Crafting!
10.content: I highly recommend this marvelously romantic, superbly scripted, super-heroic, sci-fi film!!! Special effects, music, casting, performances, and especially scripting are superb. Good versus bad, ethical delineation, is rarely this good! The film is an ethical struggle epic. I was taken with the clarity of the dialog in conveying the author's views of ideal heroism. Kane's original sense of good versus evil is enhanced and glorified, to become totally thrilling. Performances were skillfully done. Humor was subtle and added to my enjoyment of the film. Character development drew me into this rich drama. Special effects were imaginative and effective in promoting the drama. All in all, this is the kind of entertainment for which I often hunger.

10.title: The Dark Knight Returns..... in Top Form!!!!!!!!
10.content: Well, I was glad when I came out of the theater because I was smiling. This is the definitive Batman movie because It actually explore Batman's Origins and went a lot deeper than other previous films have attempted. This had a much grittier, darker and realistic feel which I thoroughly enjoyed the way the material was handled with great respect and care and to try and make it all realistic??? excellent approach!!!! I thought all the actors were wonderful, Liam Neeson as Ducard/ Raz, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon, Michael Caine as Alfred, and Christian Bale as The Bat. Michael Caines one liners were just hilarious. I thought katie holmes did well in this film, The Tumbler was awesome, and the way Batmans voice sounded when he was in the mask, awesome! Especially when he shouted "Rachel!" that was beautiful. I thought it was a bit sad when they broke up but then again, Batman was destined for a greater Love, which resides in Catwoman. I especially loved it when Bruce told off all the rich phonies! Ha! Awesome! It was just an awesome movie all around and is one of the best Movies of the Year!!!

10.title: Perfect Batman.. True Adaptation
10.content:
Most non Batman fans might not be wild about this film. The film as a stand alone is not what I would call a great film, but as a Batman film it is The "Greatest Batman film".

My opinion is this tops Burton's Batman mainly because it is not cartoon-ish or childish. This is Batman the way Bob Kane envisioned Batman;

A Gritty, introspective man "bat-bent" on fighting injustice.

In Bale, we finally have Bruce Wayne/Batman played perfectly. Thisis not to take away from Keaton, who played Batman the way Burton envisioned Batman. Here Bale portrays him the way Kane envisioned. In one scene, we can see and feel Batmans anger interrogating a thug, with a kind of almost "out of his mind" anger and focus. For me it was like watching the comic book come to life on the big screen.

Quite possibly, this might be the best comic book to screen adaptation ever made.

Gone is Burton's fantasy land. replaced with a real life feel the comics had.

This is the definitive Batman film to date, if one judges a movie on how it is adapted from the comic book.

10.title: Fantastic but Not as good as its Sequel
10.content:
I saw The Dark Knight last week and I was absolutely blown away by its brilliance and everything about it in general. After seeing it, I decided to revisit one of my favorite movies and its predecessor, Batman Begins. I think that The Dark Knight is a candidate for the greatest movie of all time so I didn't think Batman Begins was as good but that doesn't mean it isn't an overall great film that deserves all its recognition and the number 100 spot on the top 250.

Bale is the best Batman. There's no way around that, he simply just is. Everyone else is great and perfect for their roles. They all added so much depth to this film. The effects and storyline are wonderful also.

This is a must for any Batman fan and you should probably check it out before you go and see The Dark Knight.

10.title: This is what the other Batman movies should have been like
10.content: The movie is easily the best that Hollywood has made for the Batman character. Christian Bale is wonderfully supported by a top notch cast and does a wonderful job of showing the character as a possible real world character instead of just a comic book character. Other DC Comic movies should take a lesson and keep in mind for future movie installments. The character has more depth and you get a real good idea of how and why Batman came into existence. The movie also shows the beginnings of all the familiar characters in the series (Police Officer Gordon and Alfred). There is none of the "circus" atmosphere and better action than in any of the previous Batman movies combined. A definite must see!!

10.title: In a nutshell it's good how it begins....!
10.content: Cheers for an nice event! Very wisely done and very illustrative. 3D animation is brilliant! 2D animation is as good! Brilliant! An outcome of achievement and perfection! The whole story begins and continues as dramatic and equally unpredictable. If there is anything that inspires it is the fact that there are a lot of changes of equipment and scenes. There are of course a lot of similarities with the batman movies but as regards the everyday life anomalies and the quick solutions they needed. It is an absolute miracle to have something like that in front of our eyes knowing that it does not exist yet knowing it is not real 100%. It is a brilliant peace of cinema children and I suggest you watch it!

10.title: Didn't really need Holmes
10.content: I loved the movie, well written and easy to comprehend how Bruce Wayne became Batman and why. And the twist of who is real enemy is was very well scripted. I'm not sure why Katie Holmes was in it though, she wasn't totally necessary. Did she add anything to this movie? Not in my opinion. I'd be really surprised if she was in the next one, since she didn't do much in this one. But I gave it a ten, and I'm definitely going to buy it on DVD. Perhaps someone here can explain one issue I had...in the first Michael Keaton movie, Jack Napier kills his parents, but not in this one. Or did I miss something there? It seems that the killer was some no-name thug, which obviously doesn't coincide with the Michael Keaton first, "Batman" movie.

10.title: Wow!
10.content: This is just a throwaway to add to the list, but this film was so much fun and so well done that I just had to add something... Having 2 kids, a wife, a house in the 'burbs, and being the only working one (outside anyway), means missing a lot of films until DVD release...Nevertheless,I was so impressed with the scope and story of this film! In the style of the Spiderman series, Batman Begins starts BEFORE the beginning and chronicles the evolvement of the whole sha-bang, and boy, what an evolvement! Christian Bale, Katie Holmes, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Ilam Neeson, et. all are finely cast, and the direction, story, and appearance of this film are all right on! The care taken in the story to tie so much so neatly together is evident; any small reference at the start of the film could have major implications by the end... It's a wild, complicated plot, but hey, this is based on a comic strip and it ALL works! GREAT Film-making! If you are so bored that you actually read this review, I hope you had or have as much fun watching Batman Begins as I did!

10.title: The ULTIMATE Super hero experience!!!!!!
10.content:
This is truly the best super hero film I have seen since the 1989 Batman! This rocked! I was not bored at all from start to finish! I also have to say that when I watched this film, I felt like I was inside the film with the characters! I have not had that feeling at all this year from any of the films I have seen, besides Cinderella Man and Star Wars.

This is much better than the average comic book film that is usually so stylized, that it becomes stupid like the last two Batman films, directed by Schumacher. This film is basically the start of Bruce Wayne, becoming batman, in a whole new, alternate version.

Yes, his parents were slain before him, and feeling that he must seek justice and vengeance against the evilness of Gotham city, he disappears to China, of where he meets a man (Liam Neeson), who helps fulfill his quest. From here on is the action-packed film that starts an unforgettable tale of good vs. evil. The villains are hateful and dark in this film, the film itself is dark, and there's unpredicted twists and guest appearances of well known actors.

The two and a half hour film flew by for me! There's a lot of up close in your face action, especially the brutal hand-to-hand. I warn fans now, it is much darker and intense than the average Batman flick, but it is also much better!!! Truly, the ULTIMATE super hero experience. 5 out of 5 stars. See it, it is truly worth it!

10.title: Welcome back to the dark, Batman
10.content:
I read the comments of other writers and I won't repeat their common comments. Quite frankly I was breathless at the end of this movie. Finally, Batman returns to what Batman should be. It is a story about a man tormented by helplessness; from losing his parents as a child, to being failed by the justice system and in watching his city fall apart under a corrupt system.

It is not about selling toys to children anymore then great character movies such as "Ray" were. It is about entertaining not marketing merchandise.

I am sure that Bob Kane would be happy with this movie. It brought the dark knight back from the darkness of movie mediocrity. Thank-you so much to the writers, the director and all the cast for their excellent work.

10.title: An Outstanding Batman Origin Story
10.content: Batman Begins is not just an awesome origin story of a superhero we know of to this day, but easily one of Christopher Nolan's greater films. It would stay fateful of Batman's legacy with an engaging origin story, top notch visuals, great editing, memorable characters played by actors that give their incredible performance, awesome action, and a powerful moral about unity of justice. If you're a fan of the director's works or if you're a true Batman fan, this is a must watch. Thanks to how we've gotten films like this, superhero movies have grew stronger many years later. This has given Christopher Nolan a brilliant start at making superhero movies. But believe me, this was only just the beginning.

10.title: batman surprises
10.content:
I thought this movie would not appeal to me much, For I was not much into Batman & Robin, from its serial days. I always felt it was a potentially great concept that failed miserably in its fakeness among amateurish "pow" "wow" comic strip antics of the most basic kinds of sensationalism without substance. Its plots were largely pathetic & its offerings were mostly plastic! Zorro, Superman, Robin Hood & such as the Count of Monte Christo & such adventures of precision were much more endearing & enduring to me! But in this "Batman Begins" atmosphere, situations are well built in this impressive production.

The child into youth evolving into a Batman superhero, is credibly developed in his circumstances beyond his control or will. The fears & the experiences of the young 'bat boy' echo into his head & his being! His heart & soul are crushed, yet prevailing evermore into something greater! This is a quality production, that seems to have evolved with much wisdom & insight & empathy, from producers & cast & crew committed to their enterprise.

"Batman Begins" is suspenseful & entertaining & gripping! It binds the heart & soul & mind of the viewer, into its concept & dimensions of fairness & justice & integrity.

What more can a quality movie hope to do?

10.title: Now this is a REAL superhero Movie - Executed Flawlessly - spiderman's nothing!
10.content: Oh man! got no words... The utmost immensely amazing prequel doesn't at all seem a bit like the rest of the franchise I mean in the midst of action summer movies that have been ridiculously nothing but utter disappointment, specially all the prequels, This is ONE HELL OF A TERRIFIC production in every aspect which tells that even superhero movies can be an INSTANT CLASSIC! I was just expecting another batman movie..but i was stunned by the fact that despite of the xtremely cool action and effects work, the basic idea behind this project of a man's transformation into something like Batman can be shown with such execution and Chistopher Nolan's dark & dramatic film-making with D.Goyer's surprisingly perfect script. This isn't just thrilling action at the movies..its got all the talents like acting,plot pacing and twists etc that make an all rounder classic. Now stop reading, just clear your mind of any doubt and go watch the best summer movie in recent memory... Batman Begins has it all for every kind of movie lover!

10.title: bravo to his Royal Darkness
10.content:
So many times style rules over substance, leading us to true disappointment. For a change, Hollywood has taken the mythic tale of the dark crusader and made it into a truly satisfying movie-going experience. Bruce Wayne's dual-sided personality is finely detailed, with his evolution from a scared child to a superhero.

The film explores issues of morality, vulnerability, loyalty, ethics, and more. With the help of an outstanding supporting cast, the story takes flight, allowing the audience to partake of both a fantastic array of amazing gadgets and special effects; yet the audience's emotional level never stops feeling real. Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Gary Oldman prove themselves once again three of the finest contemporary actors.

The film, however, belongs to Christian Bale, whose portrayal of the Dark Knights shows a range of emotions rarely seen in a film of this type.

I'm glad someone finally got it right.

10.title: They Finally Got It Right
10.content: When this Movie opened up on Wednesday i was kinda nervous about seeing another Batman film, I was so disappointed with the Batman and Robin Movie that came out in 1997 i told myself there's the end of the batman franchise. But then came June 15th 2005. And the release of the next Batman movie with an entire different cast and a different director and writer.. and now i must say that David Goyer and Christopher Nolaa have finally set things right in the Batman movie Franchise. This movie is more darker and more better than the previous four movies and i must say it puts all of the previous four movies to shame... After i got out of the theater i called up my sister and told her "THEY FINALLY GOT IT RIGHT" which meant i love the movie. Christian Bale plays a wonderful Bruce Wayne and a wonderful batman, and i think Batman Creator Bob Kane would be proud of what has happened with this latest Batman Movie.. This movie goes threw him seeing his parents murdered by Joe Chill, With Meeting and being trained by Ra's AL Ghul and then becoming the batman this movie is an action pack movie.. Seeing Gary Oldman play policeman Jim Gordon{not police commissioner} is great. Michael Caine as Alfred is great. It has an all star cast in this movie like the Batman movie of 1989 did.. so people please see this if you haven't because THE BAT IS BACK AND THEY FINALLY GOT IT RIGHT.

10.title: Wow!
10.content: Just when I thought the franchise was lost, it was saved by everything a batman movie should have - a great director, amazing writers, superb (and extremely realistic) effects, a great cast and a phenomenal storyline. "Batman Begins" has all of these thing and then some. While they could so easily have recycled the joker or the Penguin to be the villain, the writers did something far cleverer and drew from Batman comics featuring the not so well known villains, and (well, at least as they are played in the film) the more realistic villains, for in this reinvention, Gotham needed to be a real place in our minds, and bright purple coats or bright green spandex hardly help us to buy into the world. Despite the fact there is a man dressed like a bat roaming the streets, the world around him and his set-up is so real, it doesn't matter. This also allows for more, 'eccentric' villains for the obvious sequels, as this world is so well created. 10/10 - extraordinary!

10.title: Genial
10.content: The film was super good. From the story to the cast to the action. Better than The Dark Knight in my opinion, but worse than The Dark Knight Rises.

10.title: The Dark Knight Returns...!!!
10.content:
Last night I went to see the new Batman picture. I love what Micheal Keaton, Michelle Pfeiffer, Jack Nicholson and Tim Burton did in the first and second Batman Motion pictures and I was thrilled and frightened when I heard that Christian Bale would now pose as the Caped Crusader. He is an incredible actor without doubt, but I was not sure if he fitted 'my image' of Batman. Now I know better, this guy is Batman! As much as Micheal Keaton is for me, as much as the Comic book hero! Now Batman lives in a real run down big city, that leaves you yearning for a dark knight! Everything feels so real!

Christopher Nolan really hit the nerve. Even without the super-duper Batman villain Joker, who alone is reason enough to make a movie, he created a fast paced, character and conflict driven action movie that I rank among the best superhero movies next to X-Men 2!

10.title: very rarely does a film so immensely satisfying on so many levels come along...
10.content:
I wasn't excited about the prospect of Batman Begins. The film is based on the DC comic THE BATMAN(and, unlike the last 4, its faithful AND fun) and comes from indie king Christopher Nolanimer. It's an attempt to revive the batman franchise, a franchise dead sense mega failure of Batman & Robin starring George Clooney and Arnold Schwarzenegger. The cast for the movie was good-it continues the batflick tradition of big name actors. The trailers made it look good and serious, and the marketing was heavy. The only drawbacks were that I felt that Batman was a character that when made too serious, it might not be fun. Luckily, my expectations were completely confounded; Batman Begins is a sensational blockbuster.

Despite its origins, the plot is by turns exciting and surprising. Young Bruce Wayne sees his parents murdered before him. He leaves the world behind, and trains as a ninja. Upon returning to Gotham City he becomes Batman. His first task is to bring in Carmine Falcone, but in the process he uncovers a plot against Gotham involving horrifying villain the scarecrow and an old foe.

Katie Holmes and Gary Oldman strongly portray Batmans two allies while Michael Caine shines as Alfred, who is busy trying to keep Bruce Wayne sane. Morgan Freeman is hilarious and better return for the sequel, Rutger Hauer is good as the snobby businessman, and Liam Neeson and Ken Watanabe are quite the villainous duo in the "league of shadows".But this film is stolen by two people: first, unknown Cillain Murphy gives what will go down as perhaps the most memorable villain since, well, Jack Nicholsons Joker. Hes so normally creepy yet there's a trusting sense in him. But the film is really stolen by Christian Bale. He is the undisputed star in a inspired dramatic performance. Hes also quite easy on the eyes, and can kick some serious butt when needed. Some of the action is breathtakingly exciting, particularly one spectacular fight aboard the stunningly real monorail that runs through the canyons of gotham, and the batmobile chase is incredible. But perhaps the most praise worthy element of the production is Gotham City-of the art and special effects don't get Oscar nominated then this is biggest robbing at the Oscars since Titanic won best picture. Its so grand in scale, I don't think I've ever seen a modern city so big in a film, yet its style and darkness is so real. All it does is add the experience. The score, by James Newton Howard and Hans Zimmer, is yet another Oscar worthy item in the film.

But what makes Batman Begins such a triumph is the ease with which it leaps between styles. The film unexpectedly has some great comic moments, but also manages to be exciting, scary and moving. Flashbacks of Bruce Wayne and his father are quite moving, the villain scarecrow a lot more threatening and intimidating then one would expect. From this hybrid premise you feel many directors would have delivered a half-baked pastiche but Chris Nolan has come up with a genuine swashbuckling epic loaded with drama, comedy, and romance. Batman Begins. is, in short, awesome. You cant take your eyes off the screen. Its going to be a monster on DVD sales and a sequel will be eagerly anticipated. I didn't think I'd be saying this, but Batman begins is the ride of the summer.

10.title: Arguably the finest comic adaption ever made
10.content:
Let me start this review off by saying that I had only a mild interest in seeing this film. The Batman franchise had run it's course, I figured, so why do we need yet another bad commercial blockbuster? What more could be said about the character that hasn't already been beaten to death? And furthermore, I grew up in the 70's loving Adam West's Batman and The Superfriends (where a hero = major virtues, 0 faults), so I've never been crazy about DC and the film industry's tiresome desire to convince everyone that the character is some dark, brooding disturbed being who strikes fear into the hearts of the enemy (come on, how frightened would you be if a guy in a goofy leotards or a rubber suit confronted you?). The Batman I loved smiles, escapes from giant snow cones, and stops the Penguin from stealing the Hostess fruitpies, and that's just the way I like to remember him. Well I'm happy to report I'm accepting the "modern" description of this character, thanks to this film.

This film is a darker, sometimes frightening retelling of the Batman legend (not recommended for small children so take heed), with a plot that draws you in, superb directing, and excellent acting, which is no small feat considering the subject and the potential for unintentional laughs (are you listening, George Lucas?!). There's no dumb rollerskating-type villains in neon or silly brain sucking machines (OK, I liked Batman 3 for it's campiness). We care about these characters and their relations are true and heartfelt (particularly Burce and Alfred's relationship). If I had to offer any negative criticism, it's that I found that the casting of Katie Holmes and Cillian Murphy to be a bit unbelievable considering their stature in Gotham (one's a DA, the other the head of an Asylum)and the fact that they both look to be about 18 (yeah, I know Katie's 26 and Cillian's pushing 30, but they sure look like they're about 18 and it seemed like their casting was a deliberate attempt to draw in younger audiences). Their acting was fine, however.

All in all, right up there with X-Men 2 as one of the best films based on a comic book hero ever made.

10.title: Swear to Me!
10.content:
Finally a great Batman movie. I'm just gonna throw all objectivity out the window right now and say that I absolutely love this movie. It's a lot like Superman I in the sense that even though it's not realistic, it feels like this movie could have really happened.

I never thought much of the other four Batman movies. The first two were too villain centric and Michael Keaton's portrayal of Batman was stiff and boring. There was no sense of depth to Batman, he was just Batman because he was supposed to be. He was given second billing to Jack Nicholson and Danny DeVito. Then the third and fourth movies were all camp and stupidity. They insulted not only fans but any person with an active pulse.

Then came this movie. This one completely ignored all the previous Batman movies and started over again. Good move. Batman is given the main stage and we the audience find out about what motivates a billionaire play boy to dress up as a giant bat and fight crime. Batman has three villains to deal with in this movie and none of them over shadow him. Liam Neeson and Tom Wilkinson both do good jobs at chewing up the scenery without looking silly. However the best job is done by Cillian Murphy. His Scarecrow is scary and sadistic. I hope Heath Ledger does the same thing for the Joker in the next movie.

I highly recommend this movie to, well everyone. I really enjoyed it and hope that they make at least two sequels that are as good as this movie. I can't wait until 2008 to see The Dark Knight. For the first time I think Batman is headed in the right direction when it comes to the movies.

10.title: The Dark Knight ... I mean it!
10.content:
They finally got right. This is a rustier Batman, more brutal and grittier. And the most important ... REALISTIC!

The Cast: the whole cast was brilliant (Katie Holmes character Rachel Dawes was weak tough ... sadly enough). Christian Bale did an extraordinary performance as Bruce Wayne. And Bruce (not Batman) is in it 45 minutes in the film until he becomes Batman, so it's important to have an comptent actor to potray him. Michael Caine, as usual, did a perfect job as the good butler/father figure Alfred Pennyworth. The villains was very good and scary (especially Scarecrow/Johnathan Crane)

Story: the story is dark and original. The script was perfect Batman and was perfectly executed, kudos to Christopher Nolan and rest of the crew. The dialogue was very good and believable.

Other: the music is not Danny Elfman style, but new and better. The cinemotagraphy was perfect. A highly recommended movie, WATCH IT!

Wonder how The Dark Knight will be ...

10.title: You have to see this film!!!!!
10.content: Clearly the best Batman movie of all time and one of the best films of the year. Everything from the acting, the action, and the score was terrific. Although the films title is called Batman Begins, its not a prequel or a sequel to any of the past Batman movies. Thankfully, WB decided to restart the dieing franchise and bring the Batman to its deserved glory. What's also great about BEGINS is that the film put a lot of emphasis on the Batman/Bruce Wayne character's. There was too much attention on the bad guys in the previous films, that it made Batman a supporting character. Anyways, stop what your doing, and see this movie. Even if your not a Batman fan, you will still enjoy its epic story, great characters, and intense action.

10.title: outstanding
10.content: This movie is outstanding in almost every respect. Not only is it arguably the best movie of the genre, but it should be considered a very good film on its own merits. I left the theatre feeling as if I had just watched an extremely well-crafted and engaging movie that happens to be about a superhero. The cast is great from top to bottom -Bale perfectly finds a balance of emotional complexity and moral growth that needed for this realist rendition of the comic book hero. Gary Oldman is great as a conscientious cop and, even though she might have been corrupted by that alien scientologist Tom Cruise, Katie Holmes does a credible job as an Assistant DA with the right amount of moxie, faith and determination. Caine, Freeman and Neison are, as usual, excellent despite the fact that the former two feel a little under-utilized but they more than make up for it by capitalizing on the screen time they were given to work with. Definitely a movie not to be missed this summer and one that should be seen on the big screen.

10.title: One of the most brilliant superhero films of all time
10.content:
Batman is one of the most popular superheros of all time. I, for one, have grown up reading Batman comics. Therefore, I look forward any film (animated or otherwise) that involves Batman. However, Batman Begins stands out as the best superhero film of all time. Why, you may ask.

Batman Begins is not only a brilliant portrayal of the story of Batman, but it also happens to be a remarkable effort at film-making. I have followed the career of Christopher Nolan very closely and this will be remembered as one of his landmark films. Christian Bale gives the performance of a lifetime and its amazing to see how such good talent goes unnoticed for so long. Gary Oldman is reliable as always and doesn't take the focus off the main character. The cast in general was extremely good and a special mention should be made of Liam Neeson and Ken Watanabe. They bring real character to the story.

The most outstanding feature of the film is the fact that it humanises the character of Batman. We see the transition from Bruce Wayne to Batman. It is interesting to see how the characters look so real, although the film belongs to the fantasy genre. The audience is left to decide which role (Batman or Burce Wayne) is the actual masquerade.

If you haven't seen this film yet, GO watch it! I would like to stress again that this film DOES not belong to the earlier lot of semi-dark/comedy films with Clooney, Jim Carrey, etc. This film is absolutely true to the character of Batman; it is dark in every sense and leaves you captivated. Enjoy!
