10.content: I was 50/50 to watch this movie thanks to G. Lucas' Star Wars Episode III, I thought that was the movie of the year for everyone and other movies would come second, before I say, "Heck, Batty rules,' I would also like to say to both Tim and Joel, "Gee, guys, thanks for the memories and hello to Chris. Tim made Batman looked like a kid on the block, off course when the movie was released back in 1989, everyone was expecting for the infamous blue caped crusader with gray shirt and tights and the yellow oval shaped with a black bat on it to emerge from the screen but no, he made batty wore all black spandex. And whats with Michael Keaton as Batman? Sure, he's ugly to be a hero but that doesn't mean he can be the Caped Crusader. Val and George were both awful as Batman, well, I can't blame them because Joel wants his Batman to be all campy like the 60's show. Then came this Nolan guy. I just wanna say to this Nolan guy.. you made Batman look good, man. I love to say this and to you all movie-mongers Batman Begins is 2005 Best Film. 'Nuff said. Members of the Academy Awards, you have awarded, in fact named LOTR - ROTK 'best picture', I'm very sure that this Nolan's movie on Batman deserves to win the best picture category as well and award Nolan for best director, this goes to the members of the BAFTA and Golden Globe as well. What do I get from all this? Satisfaction and immortalize this movie into a DVD form when it comes out later this year, I hope Nolan has the same format as Jackson's LOTR Extended Versions, I can't wait for all the special features on this movie when it comes out in DVD form. Bale, you're the best Batman; Caine, you take care of Brucie for me, you rock, man; Freeman, you're already a legend next to Guiness' Obi-Wan Kenobi and Katie, please marry Tom, he's waiting for you by the phone. My bros at Warner, keep it up. Thanks for Batman Begins. Nolan, you... who is this Nolan, guy? Hahaha, that was my expression when your name showed up scrolling through the screen as its director, I went, "Who is this Nolan, guy?' I thought this movie was directed by Spielberg or Eastwood because it was so flawless and so entertaining, I even shed tears when Bruce's parents got shot, in fact there are so many touchy scenes that you won't find in Star Wars, heck, this movie is so way better than Star Wars. Please make this movie the biggest hit of this summer so Nolan can make more sequels for Batman. Shame on Viggo and Daniel Day for not wanting to participate in this movie of the year! I'm wearing my old Batman black tee-shirt right now and thinking of Nolan.

10.title: Awesome
10.content:
First and foremost, Christian Bale's portrayal of Bruce Wayne/Batman is nothing short of phenomenal. He brings a depth and complexity to the character, exploring Bruce's journey from a broken soul seeking vengeance to a symbol of hope and justice. Bale's performance as both the tormented billionaire and the caped crusader is a perfect balance of intensity and vulnerability.

Christopher Nolan's direction is masterful, giving the film a gritty and realistic tone that grounds the superhero story in a believable world. His attention to detail and commitment to practical effects create a visually stunning and immersive experience.

The film's narrative is a gripping and compelling exploration of Bruce Wayne's transformation into Batman. It delves into the psychological and emotional aspects of his character, making him more than just a crime-fighting superhero. The exploration of fear as a motif and the themes of redemption and justice add depth to the story.

The supporting cast is stellar, with standout performances from Michael Caine as Alfred, Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon, and Liam Neeson as Ra's al Ghul. Each actor brings nuance and gravitas to their roles, enhancing the overall quality of the film.

The action sequences are well-choreographed and thrilling, showcasing Batman's combat skills and his arsenal of gadgets. These scenes are both entertaining and integral to the character's development.

Hans Zimmer's score is a perfect complement to the film's atmosphere, adding tension and emotion to key moments.

In conclusion, Batman Begins is a superhero origin story done right. With its stellar performances, intelligent storytelling, and compelling character exploration, it laid the foundation for a groundbreaking trilogy.

If you're a fan of superhero films that go beyond the spectacle to delve into the psychology of the characters, Batman Begins is a must-watch. It's a dark and captivating exploration of the origins of Batman that will leave you wanting more. So, don the cape and cowl and immerse yourself in the gripping journey of Bruce Wayne as he becomes the legendary Dark Knight!

10.title: One Of The Best Super Hero Movie Ever Made
10.content:
The words 'substance' and 'blockbuster' are rarely found in the same sentence. Nor indeed are the words 'auteur' and 'commercially reliable'. But Christopher Nolan is living, breathing proof that the two can come together and make astonishing work. Having won over mainstream audiences with Memento and Insomnia, Nolan uses his particular blend of non-linear story lines and visual hyper-realism to breathe new life into a long-dead franchise.

With all the acclaim being accorded to The Dark Knight (most of which it deserves), it is easy to forget just how good or how strong Batman Begins is. It's not just good by Batman standards, or by prequel standards; it has its own, stand-alone identity, a headstrong independence which defies and ignores all that has gone before it. Gone are the Gothic spires of Tim Burton's Gotham City, or the day-glo camp of Joel Schumacher's costumes. This is a new whole new world, in all its meticulous and frightening glory.

All of Nolan's films are stunning to behold, but Batman Begins takes his craft to new heights. He is famous for not using a second unit, allowing him to supervise and construct every shot just the way he wants it. This means there is no jarring difference between the film's dramatic scenes and the external effects designed to show us the city. Even in the most effects-heavy parts of the film, we never question who is behind the camera, guiding these scenes and determining their significance.

Nolan has the same gift for visual verisimilitude as Ridley Scott, whose masterpiece Blade Runner was a major influence on the young filmmaker. Both directors are able to construct seamless, immersive worlds on screen which are simultaneously strange and familiar. They have a beauty which both comforts and surprises us, allowing the filmmaker to play with the clichés and always come up with something new. But while several of Scott's films are truly style over substance (Legend, Someone to Watch Over Me), Nolan has yet to make a film which forsakes narrative substance for the sake of visual splendour.

What makes Batman Begins so rewarding, so gripping, and arguably so radical, is that there is a constant and unrelenting focus on the story. No matter how much we jump back and forth in time, or how many bad guys get hit, we never doubt that the movie is in control of itself and is yearning to move on to the next important piece of character development. The fact that we have to wait an hour before Christian Bale even dons the bat-suit is a clear sign that the filmmakers want to do this properly. They have avoided falling into the trap of either the original films, which often put the narrative on pause for a kid- friendly set-piece, or the Star Wars prequels, which waded through years of turgid back-story for a few minutes of vaguely dark action.

Mark Kermode once described this film as "a little independent, weird, art movie, trapped within the body of a $140m blockbuster." And he wasn't far off. Batman Begins is much less a superhero film per se than it is a detailed philosophical examination of the nature of fear and morality in a chaotic world. Both our protagonists and his many enemies have fear and intimidation as their source of power -- the former by their bribes and weapons, the latter by stealth and an incorruptible desire to do good. But rather than keep it as a straight fight between good guys and baddies, the film questions the motivations of our hero on a frequent basis. The supporting cast, particularly his old flame, push him on his motivation for doing what he does, in the way he does, regardless of how little they actually know.

This is a film in which the desire to do good can so easily be blurred into the desire for power; in which the lines between justice and vengeance are frequently re-drawn; and in which the triumph of good over evil is neither complete nor reassuring. In the film's closing scenes, Gary Oldman warns Batman that he is potentially doing more harm than good; this enemy may have been extinguished, but a darker menace lurks on the horizon which will be harder to defeat.

At the centre of all this is the idea that to defeat evil, one must understand it and even adopt part of its methods if the ends justify the means. The League of Shadows, headed up by Ra's al Ghul, are a symbolic forewarning to Bruce Wayne of what he could become should he fully embrace his fear. Liam Neeson's character is a Nietzschean figure, who has channelled his desire for justice so purely that it has consumed all his remaining humanity. Bruce Wayne should if anything be more brutal, since he wishes to atone for the death of his parents. But when he is asked to slay the farmer, his humanity intervenes and he refuses. This pivotal scene confirms Wayne's incorruptible nature; he may become feared, but he will never let the fear become him.

10.title: Definitely the best movie of the Batman Franchise!
10.content:
My top 3 Batman Movies:

1. Batman Begins 2. Batman 3. Batman Returns

I've already forgotten any other of the Batman films outside of these 3. I was very excited to see DC comics make its way back into the film industry. Christopher Nolan did a superb job of telling the origin of Batman and bringing the viewer inside the thoughts and feelings of Bruce Wayne. Christian Bale was the perfect fit for Bruce Wayne and Batman. The visuals and mood of this film took Tim Burton's originals to a new level. Even though I did not completely like the criminal plot that Batman had to stop at the end of the movie, I cannot fault this movie. The main point of this movie was bringing Batman to Gotham and the wildly hatched plans by crazy minds have always been a part of the Batman story, even if they are not believable or make complete sense. This is a must see for anyone who has like the first 2 Batman movies and want to see something that is on the same level or better than those. I know that Darren Aronofsky was originally set to be director of this film, but I think his style may have gone overboard on the film, while Christopher Nolan was able to provide the perfect mix of coherence and darkness and madness that is a part of Batman.

10.title: A Beautiful Comeback
10.content: Going in to the theatre, I was rather skeptic about the quality of the performance that I was about to see, however I have to say that the Batman series has made a comeback that is absolutely unsurpassed. For those of you expecting to see another Batman and Robin: tough luck. This is a quality production, which although not quite in the tone of the previous ones, is still a masterpiece. It starts out a little bit rickety with childhood and adolescence scenes, but believe me these are very necessary for the plot. The essential story line is like this: during the time when Bruce's parents are killed, Gotham city is in a horrible depression and although his parents are attempting to fix this, they are not capable to do much. They are then killed by robbers as we all saw in the original Batman except with a few tiny changes, which really aren't that important. Bruce grows up a sad, depressed boy who is forever brooding about his parents' death. After a bit, when he is perhaps 20some he leaves do understand the dark mind of a criminal, already brooding the revenge of his parents. He encounters an organization that trains him and then attempts to use him to destroy Gotham City. He has a little bit of a conflict with them (to put it lightly) and then goes home to begin his fight against crime. What he doesn't realize is that the worst is yet to come.

10.title: Amazing new Batman movie -- by far outshines the rest!
10.content:
What can I say?! Got to see an early screening of the movie today and it BLEW MY MIND! The storyline and the dark setting very much tie in with the comic book and so many parts have been thought out so very well and intricately.

No other Batman movie will compare once you have seen this! Truly fantastic!

The effects and the twists make the movie SO much more than the previous ones and every second seems to have something to grip you.

Go see it as soon as possible.

Batman is back and better than ever!

10.title: 'Batman Begins' is why I love film!
10.content: Saw 'Batman Begins' yesterday and am absolutely over the moon that Christpher Nolan had the balls to go his own way, and make a film which is not afraid to embrace darkness. What a wonderful piece of film-making this is, and I have to call it beautiful because it is a near masterpiece. I wish that like 'Lord of the Rings', they had filmed back-to-back because I feel the same sense of anticipation and need to see the next instalment. The casting is excellent and Christian Bale inhabits his role but does not let it overwhelm him. Michael Keaton never appealed to me, and I actually found Burton's 'Batman' to be a great disappointment. It represents all the hideous excess of the 80s, with too much pop music and self-indulgent performances. In fact, the only duff note in Nolan's film is the music which is overbearing at times, and loud to the point of deafening. I could go on and on and haven't said half of what I want to say, but if you love film you will love this brave and brilliant 'Batman'. This is only the beginning.

10.title: What good movies used to be like!!
10.content:
I have been very critical at what Hollywood has been feeding us lately at the theater.

BATMAN BEGINS, begins a revival of what good movies are supposed to be (hopefully), NOT effects driven, but character and STORY driven with realistic effects that complement the story, not TELL it.

Christian Bale plays the Character of Bruce Wayne, putting the other Bruce Wayne's in previous movies to shame. With his chiseled features and exceptional acting, he brings this character to life. (check out Spielberg EMPIRE OF THE SUN)

The supporting cast, Michael, Caine, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman and Rutger Hauer are the icing on this masterful cake. Bringing the movie together like few do anymore.

Go see this movie while it's in the theaters. The effect of seeing it with an audience will prove to make it more exciting! Also, visit a theater with a good sound system. The sound in this movie is great.. If you one of those people who still think movies are the same in any theater, you are mistaken. It's a scientific fact that you're senses rule you while in a movie. Think if you could interact with a movie with your other senses?

This movie combines everything you want in a movie and more, and is suitable for mature children over the age of 10. (you know your kids, if they have seen all of the HARRY POTTER movies and have come out fine, then you're OK..).

It is a loud movie with some scary moments, so use caution with your under 13's.

I hope you enjoy it as much as I did!

10.title: Better than Tim Burton's Batman?
10.content: Do I dare say that it was better than Tim Burton's Batman? Yes! It is better than Batman 1989. Christopher Nolan's Batman is an improvement to the franchise. Don't get me wrong, I like Tim Burton's Batman but Nolan's Batman Begins made this movie more dark. The acting is good also. Perfect cast too. Christian Bale's acting was superb, Liam Neeson was amazing, and Katie Holmes was brilliant. Plus, the music was an improvement too! Hanz Zimmer always makes the best scores, it makes the movie more emotional, dark, and interesting. There were funny parts in the movie also. Well, only a few. I also liked the script. This has got to be the best superhero movie I have ever seen without a doubt.

10.title: Absolutely GREAT

Batman Begins is absolutely PERFECT!

Go see it ! :) R. Macmj

10.title: Blows the other excuses for Batman movies out of the water
10.content:
I was very lukewarm about seeing Batman Begins when it came out. The Tim Burton movies were okay, if a little cheesy. Batman Forever was fun to watch, but it had no story and butchered the character of Two-Face. Batman and Robin was a flat-out abomination.

I was shocked at how good Batman Begins was. I'd go as far as to say Begins has become one of my all-time favorite movies. It was the complete package- good story, complex characters brought to life by the stellar acting, and the action scenes were very well executed.

The decision to reboot the story saved the Batman franchise. And Christian Bale, who I hadn't been familiar with before seeing the movie, did a great job of making Bruce Wayne a complex character and showing his struggles of balancing his desire for revenge with true justice.

Michael Caine makes a terrific Alfred, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman also give their usual good performances. But to me, the two standouts were Liam Neeson as Henri Ducard and Cillian Murphy as Jonathon Crane/Scarecrow. Neeson uses his mentor image to good effect with a nice twist involved and he plays off very well against Bale. And Murphy steals every scene he is as the creepy psychologist Crane who is up to no good.

Fantastic movie in every aspect. Christopher Nolan has gained so much confidence from me from this movie, that I trust him with the selection of Heath Ledger as the Joker for the sequel, a bit of casting that I would usually take with some skepticism. But after Begins, I give Nolan the benefit of the doubt with little hesitation.

The other excuses for Batman movies are a joke compared to this. This is what a Batman movie should be. 10/10.

10.title: Best Batman ever.
10.content: everything about this movie was just fantastic: direction was great, casting was flawless, cinematography was awesome, etc etc. Christian Bale is the perfect fit for Batman, changing from a tortured and saddened soul to the crime fighting dark night. Supporting cast is brilliantly played, and they all take their roles very very seriously. Director Chris Nolan got it right, and explored a dark and mesmerizing story of how Bruce Wayne Became the Batman, and how the Batman became Gotham's last hope. 10/10, go see this right away, i don't think anyone could not not like this movie, yes the only complaints are that Katie Holmes cant act (honestly she did what she was supposed to- i saw nothing wrong in her performance), and that the fight scenes were choppy (yes- but i did not mind in the slightest bit). Nolan and team have recreated and recharged the Batman Franchise, and boy is it better then ever!

10.title: They finally got it right!
10.content:
Go see this film. That's it. Go see it! OK, more info... After years of watching one of the greatest comic figures ever created get abused and nearly destroyed by Hollywood, I was overwhelmed by how good this movie was.

This is one of the rare movies that's actually worth the price of admission, even more so if you're a Batman fan.

10.title: Excellent revival of a once dead franchise.
10.content: I may not be Batman's biggest fan, just a fan of certain interpretations, Nolan's is by far my favorite. I love this batman because Chris Nolan and David S. Goyer never raise the question of weather or not he's crazy, but how far is he willing to go to protect the city he loves, that his family made their mission to better. Bruce Wayne is my favorite film superhero, next to Peter Parker because of his humanity, and his dedication. Batman Begins' message is a very human one, we fall so we may pick ourselves up. It explores this message beautifully. Christian Bale plays Bruce Wayne and masterfully brings David S. Goyer's script to life. Michael Caine is Alfred Pennyworth, he is absolutely convincing as one of Bruce's surrogate father. Morgan Freeman as Luscious Fox, enough said. Liam Nesson was perfect as Ras AL Ghul and I would've liked to see more of his character. Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes is...okay, probably the weakest of the cast. And finally Gary Oldman is perfect as Commissioner Gordon. In short Batman Begins is a great character study, with a great script, and immersing atmosphere.

10.title: Outstanding
10.content: I felt this movie was an excellent prequel to the first Batman movie. It has excellent humor and action. The actors are likable and it reveals more of the underlying beginnings of batman. I found it to be better than most of the later batman movies, although in my opinion, I don't think any of them will be better than the first. The actor in this batman is a believable character and before you know it you are routing for him. So in that sense I really liked the actor I think he did an excellent job. There is plenty of action in this movie to allow the guys to enjoy the movie. It also introduces new villains in this movie, I was surprised because I expected the villains from the first movie. It explained a lot of the origins of Gotham, and several different aspects and goes more into depth. I definitely enjoyed this movie and if you like action movies this will be a fun one to watch.

10.title: Truly one of the greatest films to grace the screen.
10.content:
I love Tim Burton. He is a genius and his wacky films are a staple of originality in this world of cookie cutter films in the cinemas. Yet, of all his films the one I could never get into was his Batman. You can call it a B-movie, I call it the true meaning of the descriptive word "cheesy". So I was cautious of this film. Some fantastic filmmakers came together for what I had decided would have to be a VAST undertaking in order to make up for the lost series. Apparently, Christopher Nolan and Co. had exactly the same idea as myself. This under-taking was done with by the hand of master filmmakers, and the result is one of the most fulfilling pictures I have ever witness in my few short years as a being and born film lover.

Acting:10/10 Christian Bale is perfectly cast as the title role of Batman. I never would have thought of him as Batman, and to be honest it would take some guts to go to Warner Bros. suggesting the at the time 120 pound actor of The Machinist. Yet Nolan had the idea, and it ended up very rewarding. Tom Wilkinson (The Fully Monty) plays a great villain as Falcony, a crime boss who runs Gotham city with a steady and cocky hand. Michael Caine plays Alfred well, making his Alfred a fatherly character, instead of a pointless character as done in Batman 1,2,3,and 4. Liam Neeson plays a very good villain, shady yet you owe him respect as he is Bruce Wayne's mentor. It is a tough position for a character and he pulls it off with menace and focus. Gary Oldman again proves he can turn invisible, giving a perfect performance as Gordan. Another masterful actor giving yet another masterful performance. Cillian Murphy (a personal favorite actor of mine) gives an amazing, stunning, icy, and wholly entertaining performance as Jonathan Crane, the villain with brains. He is one of the most promising up and comers in the business. Many other side dish actors (such as Rutger Hauer) give supporting performances of fantastic quality. THE perfect cast.

Writing: 25/10 David Goyer and Nolan collaborate into one of the best scripts I have ever read. It is layered, humorous, moody, dark. Forever twisting and turning giving comics a new name. Unlike the insufficient Fantastic Four, the writers gave a script for people of an IQ bigger than their shoe size. Not that dumb flicks aren't entertaining, but us often film goers often want a little more, and by God Goyer and Co. give give us more than "a little more". I really cannot say enough for the script, and I must say, I am a man who likes to talk.

Directing: 15/10 Christopher Nolan, the man behind this origin story, gives it a power. There is not "cheese factor". It is realistic, and dark approach to an epic story. If only Tim Burton had decided that comic's were something that could be taken seriously, and not just entertainment for the kids. A fresh approach to an old classic makes a film that leaves the original in the dust, ashamed of itself for being so low. If only all remakes and sequels could be handled as such, then the film industry would be a bright and shining staple of our country. Though sadly most movies are not even half as impressive, and the film business is running out of juice because the men who own and run it have no idea how to do so. It hearts me, and there days I wish I could care less. But my heart is bought and paid for to the industry. I can only hope this films inspires others, and the others, inspire other others, until film is gleaming again. Fingers crossed,eh?

Special Effects: Truly stunning. Very few CGI shots are in the film. Most of the film is done practically, and it is like the film, a fresh and stunning twist to todays world. To have a man fly over the city with not a single computer generated image is an amazing feat.

Cinematograpgy: An Oscar nomination well earned, a win well deserved. The pain of doing things practically is camera trickery. And it's flawless. It is shot beautifully, not much more is able to be said.

In the end every time this I see this film I am paralyzed. It is too powerful, shaking you around and spitting you out like a roller coaster. One of the best/most memorable films I have and will ever see.

Final Grade: A+

10.title: Realistic approach paid off
10.content:
Christian Bale IS Batman.

Michael Caine IS Alfred.

The rest of the cast is equally good. The plot and effects are just as good as I expected. 10.title: The Dark Knight's Ultimate Incarnation
10.content:
I'm not here to tell you the plot of this movie. A review should not do that. I'm not here to blast off about my opinion mindlessly. I am certainly not here to demand everyone like this film.

I'm here to advise you, from one film-goer to another, that "Batman Begins" is officially worth your notice, comic book fan or no. Hollywood simply does not put out films like this very often.

Christopher Nolan's epic Batman origin tale is very different from the other movies made about the Dark Knight. Unlike Joel Schumacher and (to an extent) Tim Burton, Nolan is not interested in Batman's toys or his neuroticism nearly as much as he's interested in the city at stake, the people inside of it, and most of all the man who wants to save both. Ironically, this focus on human drama makes the toys far cooler and the mystique far more legit, because the film never feels like it's leaning on them.

Credit is owed to every single member of the cast, but some more than others. Christian Bale nails it, but the fans and the critics were pretty sure he was going to; he is the only man for this job. Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine have so much class and style it comes out of their ears. Liam Neeson, often jeered at for supposedly reprising his role as Qui-Gon Jinn here, actually constructs a vastly different type of tutor than his old Jedi master: a brutal, frightening, unforgiving man whose complex motives and dangerous beliefs are manifested perfectly throughout the film. He is as engaging as Bruce Wayne without ever upstaging him. We get the sense this man could have become Batman himself long ago, but did not. Also worth mentioning is Katie Holmes, who is getting collateral flak from fanboys displeased by her casting. Disregard such flak. She does a fine job, shaming Kim Basinger's helpless damsel and creating a real moral challenge for Bruce Wayne.

The last time David S. Goyer took part in writing a movie, he constructed the unforgivably bad "Blade: Trinity." When I saw it, I became very concerned for this film. It is now clear that Goyer had to hit his career low before he could nail his high. Although he has done some very enjoyable work in the past, this is the best film David Goyer has ever had anything to do with. All of the "Blade" trilogy combined can't take this beast for raw power.

Christopher Nolan, however, is still the man that ran this show, and had the vision for it in the beginning. As such, he is the man who deserves the biggest applause. He has succeeded in making a super-hero movie about something, a movie which completely succeeds in telling a rich, complicated story about what fear can do and how to overcome it. This theme is not subtle or passive, but actively influences every second of the movie, giving it incredible continuity and focus. Nolan gets the applause for that more than anyone else. It is his achievement that this film is so finely crafted; he was the beating heart of this animal, and he brought it to glorious life.

Underestimate "Batman Begins" at your own peril.

10.title: Delivers and then some
10.content:
I saw this film on a special staff preview as I simply could wait the extra 12 hours as I am a huge superhero fan on all levels, from Spiderman to Smallville.

I was slightly sceptical about this film in the beginning because the last batman had seriously rocked my foundations of support. Although after I watched a "making of" on MTV it eased my nerves slightly because you could clearly see the class of the film showing through.

After seeing this film I couldn't have had a greater sense of indescribable.....well....bliss. This is by far on of the best "superhero" type film that I've seen lately, better than the Punisher which I also rated highly. The film is so fast; if you blink you will miss it. The action comes at you from all directions and it isn't just mindless fighting, its carefully choreographed martial arts which you would more expect to see in a matrix film.

It wasn't until I came on here to spread the word of amazement, after calling my friends, that I read that it was an incredible 2 hours 40 minutes. There wasn't a dull moment, you couldn't take your eyes off the screen through fear of missing an important plot point or some high class action This film delivers every single thing that a batman film could ever hope to and then some. All the Bat-gadgets, a gorgeous girl, action and of course Alfred. This film also has a slender dab of subtle humour running through out the film which are funny enough not to ruin the film as with Batman and Robin, yet just enough to make u chuckle.

So all in all, best batman film ever and easily in the running for best superhero film ever. It also deserves to be in the IMDb top 250.

Joe Moore

10.title: WOW! This is how it is supposed to be!
10.content:
I'm one of those folks who was going to give this the benefit of the doubt for several reasons, even though the last two films with the "Batman" label on it truly disappointed despite the A-list stars who were in it.

To the audience, forget EVERYTHING you know about Batman and what you've seen in the other films. This one truly stands alone.

I will say this film DOES NOT DISAPPOINT IN THE LEAST!!! Bale's Batman is very believable. If you are familiar with Bale's work, including Equilibrium, you know he can deliver as a leading man, and as an action star. Nolan did a great job setting up Wayne's father as the type of guy you wish every child had for a father with tons of dough to boot (though some women may not like that the mother kind of comes off as arm candy). So off the bat (no pun intended), you feel deeply for this kid since he lost his father, who incidentally was a good man. What I like a lot were the elements taken from Frank Miller's Batman: Year One. It was just enough for the comic book geeks, and since Miller is a great writer anyway, it makes you believe that this billionaire decided to take this interesting pilgrimage to purge his soul.

Holmes balanced the damsel in distress and the strong, modern woman very well. A scene in particular (spoiler) that makes you like her in an odd way was when she smacks Bruce Wayne... TWICE! It's not for any pass he made on her or anything, but it defines the type of relationship her character and Wayne shared growing up that she would have the type of authority in his life to be permitted to do such a thing. Her comment that followed sealed that relationship.

Caine, as always, delivers. It's nice to see that Alfred has more to him than butler/man-servant. His genuine concern for Wayne while having a slight parental guide to him is very warm.

Freeman... you can't really go wrong with him.

Hauer... a man who has paid his dues in entertainment; it's nice to see him working A-list films again this year (Sin City and here).

Murphy... if you've seen 28 Days Later, you get these waves or recognition as the film goes on, and they're creepy (probably because the aforementioned film was very disturbing, which is good because his character here is creepy).

Oldman... it's nice to see him as one of the good guys.

Neeson... he's the man, and will always be. Perfect at playing the teacher-mentor type, he also brings more prestige to the film like his colleagues Caine and Freeman. You always get the impression, the minute you put a sword in his hand or engage him in mortal combat, that this man knows what he is doing.

My only gripe: Fight scenes. Though they are very good in general, it is difficult to see or make out what is going on, who has the upper hand, etc. All you pretty much know is that someone is getting a beating.

Hats off to Nolan, as he breathed life into the Batman franchise again after the last two films started the autopsy and almost buried it. Like a Phoenix, it is born again from the ashes. Also, the ending was perfect, as it left you begging for more... then the credits roll, you look at your watch and realize that 2.25 hours have passed...

If this film fails, shame on you, the patron who did not go and see it. Think of it this way, slap Schumacher in the face by paying the money for Nolan's vision of the Bat...

10.title: The Batman we've all been waiting for
10.content:
In the first Batman, we had some stiff acting but an overall good film. In the second one we had an even better film. But after, the series dropped like a sack of potatoes. Behold, the newest Batman film, Batman Begins.

This movie is very, very dark and a bit frightening. It has some great villains such as the classic Scarecrow and the awesome Ra's Al Ghul. Batman Begins sticks to the comics a lot and includes a lot of important history of his. This great film is also very realistic. This is what all superhero films should like. Batma Begins is truly the beginning of what will turn out to be a great series.

10.title: The kind of Superhero movie America has been needing
10.content:
The incredible success of superhero movies, such as X-men I and II and Spiderman I and II, has left a bad taste in my mouth. Not that X-men or Spiderman franchises are bad. I for one am very much looking forward to Spiderman III, the problem is, that both movies are much too Americanized. And the following formula used for the movies is why: 1. Focus on heros that suffer ridicule because they have supernatural powers. 2. Make sure to get a couple camera shot of shapely woman, but remember to keep a PG-13 rating. 3. More scary the villain, the sweeter the success of the hero(s). 4. Keep the plot SIMPLE.

Batman, however, is not some cookie cutter summer blockbuster movie (although I do hope it does well at the box office). And this is why it is different, and better then all the other recent comic book to big screen adaptations: 1. Batman doesn't have any superpowers, so he's much more relate-able 2. No slutty shots of girls to cheapen the movie. 3. More complex and purposeful the villain, the sweeter the success. 4. Plot is complex enough, so as to not be overly predictable.

In a nutshell, I personally left the theater after seeing Spiderman 2, very entertained. After Batman Begins; a better man.

10.title: Finally, something to talk about this summer
10.content:
So I think we all have watched our fair-share of comic book movies in our day. Its not a surprise that some have succeeded and that some have failed. What we have here is a great example of just how good this type of film can be. I just walked out of the 12:01 showing of Batman Begins and I was blown away.

What we have here is Christopher Nolan taking the Batman series and resurrecting it. Nolan has done a fantastic job in the past with both "Memento" and "Insomnia" and he's equally successful here. This is no little accomplishment; anyone who has seen the last few Batman films would agree that it is not difficult to make a bad film. Also to be taken into consideration, Nolan is telling the tale of how it began. Where others have had their Batman waiting to take flight, Nolan was forced to create his own.

Onto the film. The beginning of the film focuses on creating Nolan's Batman. This part is heavy on the dialogue and light on the action. This works wonders because far too often we see directors avoiding the foundation that Nolan embraces here. We meet characters, villains, and our hero at this time. Without getting into too much detail, Bruce Wayne is away from Gotham for a portion of time to find himself. Once he succeeds, he returns to explore the city for what it has become.

I'm trying my hardest to avoid detailing the plot, because it was too entertaining watching it develop before my eyes to reveal its fun. What I will tell you is this. The film is dark, very dark. This may be hard to believe, but it is much darker than Burton's Batman, and thats saying something. Bale plays the role well, as does the rest of the cast. Pay particular attention to Cillian Murphy who outshines the rest. His portrayal of Dr. Crane was on target, to say the very least.

Overall, Batman Begins is a huge success. The film allows for a plot to develop and does not rely on special effects. When CGI is used, its used to perfection (the railway running through Gotham is gorgeous). I would recommend the film to anyone for it requires little knowledge of the Batman series, and is overall a great film. The summer may actually be worth sweating through this year.

10.title: The Dark Knight Returns
10.content:
Not since Tim Burton's Batman have audiences seen this brooding dark comic figure hit the screen. Directed by Christopher Nolan (Insomnia, Memento), this new adaptation of Batman's mysterious beginnings delivers in full!

Best Batman movie ever, possibly. Best movie this year so far? Definitely.

Christian Bale is now my second favorite dark knight, and could easily be the "young" Michael Keaton. The story is not just action packed with Ninjas and incredible fight scenes, but it is rich and entertaining. As a bonus for Batman fans, the story's themes were very true and honoring to the comic series.

Plus when you have a supporting cast of Michael Cane, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman and Rutger Hauer(oh yea, and Katie Holmes) how can it miss?

This movie's arch nemeses was the Psychotic Scarecrow played by Cillian Murphy. (Cold Mountain, Girl with a Pearl Earring) Aside from the on screen violence, Mr. Murphy's scary performance might be too much for younger frightened viewers.

The themes of Batman Begins shifted from "Finding your path" to "Fear" until ultimately landing on "It's what I do, that defines me." Trying to land a trade-mark catchphrase like,oh, I don't know.With Great Power comes Great Responsibility? (COUGH! Spiderman!)

Bruce Wayne struggles with an identity crisis (No, duh) and is torn between the man who he was born as, and the man he was destined to become. Not really likening the "rich playboy" persona the world expects of him, and grappling with his own fears of his parent's death, Bruce decides to adopt a persona that allows him to be true to his feelings and fears and dawns a black cape and cowl to change Gotham City for the better; one punch at a time.

10.title: if you watch this movie you will not be disappointed
10.content: When you watch this movie you cant help but feel a smile warm over your face...Nolan definitely gets everything right..with EVERY aspect of the movie...Usually when you watch a movie you sit there and say to yourself...OK...where is the cheese factor...in this movie, that never happened..Christian Bale was a spectacular choice, his dialog was particularly well written in my opinion. All of the acting was wonderful....i haven't seen a movie..let alone a superhero movie put together this well in a long time...no one could be disappointed. This is the way children should grow up seeing superheros...amazing!! Its definitely worth seeing first run.

10.title: The best from The Dark Knight trilogy.
10.content:
This is the type of movie you'll watch on repeat and never get bored by. I've seen TDK many times and I always get goosebumps at the end; I've seen TDKR a few times and it's a great movie; Batman Begins triumphs both.

What Nolan did was create a masterpiece and raised the bar of story telling in a comic book movie to an insane level. Many directors have been trying to replicate it ever since.

Batman Begins isnt a generic comic book movie but a crime saga with dark undertones of brooding corruption.

A Masterpiece.

10.title: What a movie!!!!!!
10.content: I was dubious before the screening of Batman Begins  I indeed felt the fear (coincidently this is the theme of the film) of disappointment. Schumacher's effort was as camp as a row of tents and relied heavily on Fx, silly gadgetry & overblown villains to wow and amaze us  sorry Mr Schumacher you failed miserably. Burton's world was better and his typical dark eeriness made the film enjoyable, but it still lacked the edge of the early Batman comics. Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins however has raised the bar so high even Spiderman with his fantastical web shooting powers couldn't swing over it. This film is surely now the benchmark we have to mark future comic book films by. Nolan's Gotham City is for want of a better word 'real', it could be any major city in the US and that's part of this film's huge appeal. The writing and plot are first-rate, I was relieved as my expectations of the writer who gave us XMEN and the Blade trilogy was very high  he hit the nail right on the head and knocked it in with a single blow. As for the bat himself played by Christian Bale  all I can say is he's truly tremendous in this role and is now the only person I could ever see in the infamous bat cape. He acts his socks off in this film and what a show he gives us  brooding, dry (watch out for the birthday party scene), injured as Bruce Wayne and then as his alter ego he rules - terrifying Gotham's villains as well as kicking the crap out of them. This is definitely Bale's film but the support of a stellar cast makes this film truly great. Liam Neeson, Cillian Murphy (excellent as the Scarecrow), Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman & Michael Caine are fantastic is their roles. My only nit pick would be Katie Holmes never quite impresses as Bruce's childhood friend Rachel Dawes, don't get me wrong she is by no means below average (just see Pieces Of April for example) but it is hard to see her as a grown up Assistant DA  I blame Dawson's Creek Also Tom Wilkinson's crime lord character Carpone is a little too hammy for my liking, disappointing as he is one of the best British actors around at the moment However minor issues aside this is an excellent film for adults and teens alike  a word of warning for parents, the 12A certificate given in the UK is a little lenient in my opinion  some scenes (mainly the scarecrow fear scenes) are a little too much for the little 'uns. You have been warned! Overall rating *****

10.title: everything that is cool about batman
10.content: very little to say. from the very first rumors about batman begins i enjoyed every minute of it. the film has some choppy action scenes but overall is brilliant and very well cast. cool good guy and kick ass villains, exactly what one should see in a comic book movie. making comparissions to other comic movies is unfair, because with the exception of the spider-man franchise, batman beats all the others up with his bare hands. OK not exactly bare hands but you get the point. the x-men franchise is also very well done, but the problems with the first and third ones overshadow the good things about each and as stated i have very few complaints about batman begins. OK, i found one: too much katie holmes. but too much katie holmes can be a good good thing.

10.title: WOW!! Batman Begins!!!!!
10.content: An excellent, well-conceived, well-acted and exciting movie. I loved Batman Begins! Christian Bale is the best Batman to date in my opinion. No one has ever done the "Batman voice" as well as he. No other Batman has been as intimidating. His dark and brooding Bruce Wayne was also well done. I saw this movie today and I will probably go see it twice more in theaters. I will get the DVD on it's first day of release. Again, a fine, dark, dramatic, well done film all around. The one thing I would perhaps consider missing is a powerful Batman music score.I just remember how moving Danny Elfman's Batman theme was in the original 1989 Batman. But, I can live without that. Everything else more than makes up for that small detail. This movie works on so many different levels. I can't stop thinking about it! I am eagerly anticipating the sequel. 10 STARS!

10.title: Ever dance with the devil in a pale moon light?
10.content: Now this was a superhero movie. From the opening to the end of the movie it was fantastic. THis is a fan boys wet dream, especially if you like katie holmes..i personally don't, but i try to remember that part of that one movie where she was topless..yeah..thats good stuff. Anyways, Bale did an awesome job, and is the second best batman next to of course Michael Keaton. I am excited that they are doing a sequel..perhaps redo the whole batman line up in this new way? Maybe Mr. Freeze won't be a giant body builder, and Gotham city won't be all "raved" out?!? That would be nice. I must of watched this movie over and over and over and every time i watch it, it gets better. Did you notice little barbara gordan in the house? I love the fact that this movie was as "dark" as it was, because thats the only way to do it. Maybe that's one of the reasons the first two batman movies were so damn good, and did so damn well. The King of Comics to Movies, the Batman is back on top.

10.title: Finally the Batman Film we've all Benn Waiting For..........
10.content: Batman and Company has outdone themselves with batman Begins. Ladies and Gentlemen GET TO THE THEATERS, GRAB A BAG OF POPCORN, AND A LARGE COKE, SIT BACK AND ENJOY THE RIDE!!!! This is truly the beginning of a new Batman era! The Movie starts off explaining and showing us viewers how it all began....from early childhood to the death of his parents etc... the beginning of the movie explains the part of Batman nobody ever knew or expected. once things picked up pace the climax hit and stayed through out the whole movie... Number one..This movie is very serious no more Cloony,Keaton that era is over. number two..the movie is very political and economical. Finally a Batman we can all watch.. This is a great movie!!! I Highly recommend to anyone is ready for a change of pace, even if you previously Hated Batman you'll absolutely adore it ( i did).I also would like to say.Batman is very clean and in some parts even funny! Its everything plus more.... thanx ya'll -tornadopark

10.title: The Batman franchise is saved.
10.content:
I am not a comic book fan. However, as a non-comic book fan and as somebody who judges superheroes from just their outside appearances, I have to say that Batman is my favorite (followed closely by Spiderman and Superman). The reason is that Batman is human without any real "upgrades." Every other superhero has had something happen to him/her to make them special (Spiderman got bit by a spider, Superman is not human, etc..). I have always liked Batman because he is human without any character advantages that the others have (other than those "wonderful toys" of course).

That is also one reason I enjoyed Batman Begins so much. This Batman is a very flawed human who becomes Batman through a conscience choice (another thing that most superheroes don't have, choice). The only thing that he has going for him is a very powerful corporation that can produce all the tools he needs to become Batman.

Here are some of the other reasons I enjoyed this movie.

1. This Batman takes place in the "real" world. True, it's a modified world, but the real world none the less. Gotham in this episode does not seem to be otherworldly like the other Batman movies. In addition, everything Batman does to become his alter-ego seems to be at least slightly possible.

2. I loved the explanations of how Batman became Batman and how he makes use of his company to produce the tools he needs. In the other Batman movies, we just assumed that Wayne had the resources to become Batman from some mysterious place. Here we know where the batsuit and Batmobile, and everything else comes from. I also really liked the backstory.

3. The acting was also very good. Christian Bale was the biggest surprise. I haven't seen him in many movies, and I was not entirely sure how he would do. But, he was very good as BOTH Bruce Wayne AND Batman. He had a very dark quality that Batman MUST have (in my opinion). Morgan Freeman was also a very good choice. He is good in just about every single movie he is in no matter how good or bad the actual movie is. Michael Cane as Alfred was just a genius move by the producers. He has a classic quality in his acting. But he also provides some of the best comic relief in the movie (there is some, but not a lot). Garry Oldman as Gordon is another genius move. I have enjoyed him since he was in The Fifth Element. He is a great actor who provides the low-key attitude that Gordon should have. I really liked that Gordon has a central role to play in this movie, and Oldman is good at it. The ONLY actor I did not like all that much was Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. I understand this character is simply to give Batman a female character to play with (all Batman movies should have at least one female in it). But, Holmes is just not very good. She seems to be very plastic and not very believable.

Well, that is it. There are many other reasons to like this movie, but I have covered the important parts. There are some minor plot holes and such in the movie, but they never take away from the overall fun of the movie. This is without a doubt (at least in my mind) the best in the series. I really liked the first Batman, but this one is better. A must see for anybody even if you are not a comic book fan.

10.title: Everything about this movie was awe-inspiring
10.content:
The action sequences, the backstory, the characters and most superb of all- the CAST- make this one of the best movies of 2005. The entire film was a delight for the senses, and I as I came out of the first showing, I got right back in line to buy a ticket for another showing next week.

Christian Bale is in superb form here, striking the perfect note as the confident, young, Bruce Wayne, but also there are notes of vulnerability that he brings to the performance that make us truly believe how tortured he is inside. Liam Neeson was in excellent form as Wayne's teacher/nemesis and has proved yet again what an asset to the movies he is. Michael Cain and Morgan Freeman have graced us yet again with brilliant turns in characters that they were almost born to play.

Cillian Murphy was the ultimate villain, with an appearance so striking that he stole every scene he was in. The only weak spot was Katie Holmes, but it was not enough to detract from the film. Gary Oldman brought such an intense believability to his character, showing us his good, humble roots, that we can forever say goodbye to the fat, cartoonish Comissioner Gordon from the previous films. The ending leaves open the possibility of a sequel as well, so there is much to look forward to.

Finally- this movie is not suited to children. Though it gets a PG-13 rating for lack of strong language and nudity, there is a lot of violence and subject matter too difficult and scary for small children to tackle. I wouldn't recommend this movie to any child under the age of 10, or maybe even 12.

10.title: .......Pure Cinematic Excellence
10.content:
What more could be said, this film has everything that the previous "Batman" films did not have. It was awesome, from the first frame till the credits rolled. At first, I was skeptical, but then I started to lighten up. I really wanted to give this one a chance, considering of course I love the Batman franchise. Then finally, I saw the trailer for the film.......I knew from that moment on that this film was going to be a hit.

So, I took off work yesterday to go see the film. Sadly, at the time I went, very few people were in the theater. Nevertheless, I sat down......waiting for the film to begin. I knew that went the film opened up -Opening title with the bats-, that I was going to be in for a real treat. Then when I heard the score from Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard, I knew without a shadow of a doubt that this WAS Batman.

About the film overall:

I loved this film, I cannot stress this enough! It had me wanting to know more, like why was Bruce Wayne in Asia, or How did he become the person who he was destined to be? I assure you, all questions will be answered. To be very honest with you, I really wasn't a hardcore fan of Batman(IE, knowing every bit of trivia, having all the comics and wearing costumes and such.....most of my time was spent with Alien, Predator, or Terminator), but if Hollywood is to continue to make this NEW series of Batman films on par with Batman: Begins, I will be. I could easily see this being a very successful blockbuster series.

I payed $7.75 for my ticket......and it was money well spent. For a movie of this quality, I would be willing to pay more if need be. If you are able-bodied, can drive, or just like movies in general......quit reading my review and get up and go see this movie now! You will NOT be disappointed.

10/10

10.title: Batman does in deed return....
10.content:
Being a Batman fan, this is film I have been waiting for since 1997. Christian Bale is the perfect Batman and is scary as hell too. The bat-mobile can kick the crap out of Michael Keaton's little bat-mobile he had and Cillian Murphy is amazing as the Scarecrow. Liam Neeson was great as the mentor Henri Ducard and Michael Caine was great as Alfred.

Chris Nolan really has an amazing job. The action is top notch and the story is engaging. This movie eclipses Burton's "Batman." Everything about "Batman Begins" is perfect. It is the best Batman movie ever, the best comic book movies ever and just one of the best films of the year. This truly is an amazing film.

"The Burton Schumacher movies were about the Caped Crusader, this one is about the Dark Knight." ~NY Post

10.title: Very good direction. Good story. Very well made
10.content: Good story. Very well directed. A lot to learn from the movie

10.title: Great One,
10.content: Little slow to start with, I mean they spend almost 45 mins showing Bruce Wayne's background and training and crap....but interesting to some sort. Michael played it well and the villain was great as well. A good change to Alfred, Katie Holmes has a decent role. ONe guy who stands out is the "the scarecrow(doctor) great role and great job his appearance and style suits his character. Overall I am not a big batman fan but after this movie I am. Have fun watching it and be patient it takes a while before the action starts. Also the car is awesome, looks preety cool and fearsome. Some great action shown during Batman's training and cool gadgets as usual. A brief role for Morgan freeman, but definitely no questions about his performance as usual. Lots of Bats. Cheers

10.title: Very Realistic
10.content: Just saw this on opening night and I thought it was amazing! I was expecting this movie to be good but this just blew me away! The best part about this movie was that the concept was realistic. Everything seemed plausible. Batman Begins really gets in depth with Bruce Wayne's character, which is really great. We see the real side of Bruce, not just the tough guy with a mask. The new elements such as flight, tank car, technology, and armor, made the movie slightly different from the comics, which was nice because it gives the audience a whole new feel to Batman. Some of the fight scenes were hard to comprehend, but I'm assuming it's because Batman moves so fast it's hard see what's happening. Other than that I thought this was one of the best superhero movies I've ever seen.

10.title: Batman Begins-Just Damn Good!
10.content:
I work the graveyard shift, but put off going to sleep, just to catch a noon showing opening day and I have to say it blew me away. Even without batman's appearance in the first hour, you are still captured by the visuals and story of Bruce Wayne discovering himself. Just as Spielberg eludes us with the shark in Jaws, so here does director Noland show only brief glimpses of the dark knight until he is finally revealed in a great movie introduction.

Major praises goes to the casting director who put together an amazing cast here. Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman, Cillian Murphy, Ken Wantanbe, Michael Caine, and the always great screen presence-Liam Neeson. Christian Bale was born to play this role. I have nothing against Michael Keaton, but Bale's dark on dark characterization is essential to escape the hammy, nipple-suited wearing George Clooney.

Director Nolan has join my ranks of favorite director alongside Lucas, Spielberg, Cameron, Ridley Scott. Nolan's dark atmospheric approach is well-suited to the film.

I had my doubts at first about the film, but all that went away as soon as you see the Dark Knight perched on the rooftops of Gothman accompanied by Hans Zimmer/James Newton Howard's fantastic score.

This is not a sequel, not a prequel. Its a reinvention of the Dark Knight's legacy and oh, its so good!

10.title: Better than Spiderman, but not quite as good as Batman (1989)
10.content: The plot was really cool. You'll enjoy seeing how Bruce Wayne becomes Batman in this really cool alternate world of Gotham. You'll see such classic characters such as Alfred, Gordon, and Bruce Wayne's parents. The effects looked good. The fight scenes were cool. Batman's costume looked like what you'd expect from a Batman movie today, but it's a bit different. You'll really fall for this Bruce Wayne. The characters are all played very well and very likable. In my opinion, it was better than the Spiderman movies, but not by much. This movie was a tiny bit more believable than Spiderman; which makes it really fun. I still don't feel it's a better Batman movie than the original from 1989 per se. Furthermore, it's not supposed to be an apples-to-apples comparison to the originals. However, I enjoy the fact that it's an alternate story line and maybe we'll see some more movies in this new Batman franchise. They can make Batman fight some of the original villains and do it right this time. This movie has some cool twists too. The director did a good job putting this together. You'll really enjoy it.

10.title: Best Batman movie
10.content:
After being disappointed with Episode 3 and going into this movie with low expectations, I was blown away by how well this movie was put together. Everyone must have let out a synchronous grown when they heard they're making another Batman movie because the last three have been major letdowns.

Batman Begins is one of those movies where the previews leave you thinking the movie is going to suck. This flick had everything: action, plot, script, suspense, and *gasp* acting. Some parts it had me on the edge of my seat, others had me so engulfed with the movie that I forgot I was even in a theater. Do yourself a favor and go see this movie. You won't regret it.

10.title: A movie that rivals the first.
10.content: Batman Begins is one of the best movies I've seen in a long time. This is not a phrase I use lightly. The rest of the summer movies have their work cut out for them. Even though it is a comic-book, superhero movie, I found it to very believable. A very strong plot is supported by a tremendous cast. Christian Bale IS Batman. Michael Caine plays a flawless Alfred. Liam Neeson is excellent as an antagonist. Gary Oldman lays the groundwork for future films as Detective Gordon. The movie is a must see in the theater. We are even planning on finding an IMAX showing to see it again. I hope you enjoy watching as much as my friends and I did.

10.title: Un-Noticeably Absent
10.content:
I just saw the film last night and thought it was great. I loved the Burton version and didn't think this one could blow that one out of the water but it did.

What I didn't notice while watching the film but realized afterward is that there is no Musical Theme to the film. Sure it has a great score, but it emphasizes the mood, the action. There was no sweeping John Williams/Danny Elfman score that all.

To me this is one of the smartest decisions they made because not once while watching this did I feel like I was watching a comic book being brought to life. Instead I was engaged in the drama/action/mystery of it all.

10.title: class
10.content: this is a film which really has to be seen, super hero fan or not. i liked bat 1, 2 and 3 were OK, i wont mention 4 (woops i just did sorry), but forget everything about them 4 films and start again. this is truly the great super hero film, above x men 2, all the supermen films, and even the brilliant spider man 1 and 2. bale is hard,dark and just nutty enough to be the dark knight. this will help you forget about Arnie as Mr freeze.Gotham is a horrid and dark place as it should be, the villains are not over bearing or scene stealing , and the ending had me gagging for more from the caped crusader. any negatives, I'm not the biggest fan of Mrs tom cruise but even she is not that bad.enjoy.

10.title: The best superhero movie of the century
10.content:
Batman begins was simply excellent. Words cannot describe how impressed I was with this movie. Well actually I can and here are some of the things that I thought made Batman Begins so spectacular.

The Acting! Liam Neeson played his part so well as the main bad guy. We don't often find him playing the bad guy in a movie so we think that he can't do it well this is totally wrong. I believe that he actually plays the bad guy sort of role better is he acts like this every time because he is bad. Really bad! Then there is Michael Caine as Alfred. He was also really good and if any humor or warmth came out of the movie then it came from him.

The story! The story was simply great. Director Chris Nolan could not have got the story more correct. It is about (obviously) Batman as he begins training with someone who will in the end turn out to be the bad guy and then returns to Gothim City to fight crime and show the city of Gothim that there city is not lead by the corrupt.

If you are looking for a movie that is about a superhero battling his inner demons then don't see Spiderman 3! Definitely see Batman Begins which by the way, I reckon should have won at least two Oscars but it did not even win one!

10.title: Batman Begins = the best batman movie of all time
10.content: This is personally my favorite movie, and there are a great amount of good movies out there, this one is just amazing. While the film is far from po-faced, Nolan takes the material seriously, nailing the emotion in the story of a damaged child who grows up to work out his demons through violent retribution. Bale plays Wayne as a wounded, determined human and Batman as a raging, relentless beast. Influenced by Frank Miller's seminal comic Batman: Year One, this is easily the most engrossing and faithful screen adaptation of his adventures. It is also the most intelligent and entertaining. The franchise is reborn. Embrace the Dark Knight's return. Oh and did I mention, THE BEST BATMAN MOVIE OUT THERE, FAR BETTER THAN.... "BATMAN, BATMAN RETURNS,BATMAN FOREVER, BATMAN&ROBIN" the directors just completely ruined batman's history except for Christopher Nolan and his team crew.... they're our only hope with all future comics.

10.title: Deserves all the praise and accolades
10.content:
I admit, Batman Begins is not without its weaknesses. For instance, the first act, which details Bruce's training in Asia, is shot like one long trailer. It alternates between flashbacks from Bruce's childhood and quick training lessons from Bruce's mentor, the mysterious Ducard (Liam Neeson). I found myself wondering when the film would settle into the real narrative. Another weakness is Katie Holmes, who is not quite believable (seems too young, perhaps?) as an idealistic Assistant D.A.

However, its strengths are so many and so great that I consider this the best Batman film to date. Aside from Holmes' mail-in, the acting is top-notch across the board. These big-name stars were not hired simply to sell tickets, but because they translate their comic-book counterparts to the big screen with honesty and authenticity.

A buffed-up, post-Machinist Christian Bale is hands-down the best Batman/Bruce Wayne yet. Severely buffing up after that 120-pound role, he communicates Wayne's inner complexity appropriately (yet we understand that Wayne is no saint himself), while still landing a few appropriate one-liners with dead-on timing. And, most importantly, he doesn't over-cheese the Dark Knight as previous actors have. Michael Caine resonates as a compassionate Alfred; Morgan Freeman's grinning turn as Lucius Fox makes for a great ally for whom the audience can root; Tom Wilkinson is an apt, slightly over-the-top Carmine Falcone. Cillian Murphy is a real treat--it's impossible to imagine that he auditioned for the Batman role, since he seems to revel in the sinister Dr. Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow. And rounding out the long list of major players, Gary Oldman tries his hand as good-cop James Gordon so convincingly that, for two hours, we forget the dastardly villains he's expertly portrayed before. While none of these roles are bit parts, I found myself wanting to see more development and simply more acting from these guys.

Supported by a faithful, dramatic story (with some nice twists), a fast pace, and some wonderful conceptual imagery by director Christopher Nolan (his personification of fear is simply masterful), Batman Begins is a spot-on hit even aside from all the action. Some have cited the fight sequences as a major weakness because of the quick edits and gritty fast pace. Nolan's tactics, however, succeed in allowing the fight sequences to actually develop the Batman character. More than in the previous Bat-films, the audience finally understands just how Batman uses fear as his greatest weapon.

Finally, the Batman tradition is restored to its mythological status. Our hero is still misunderstood, untrusted, and fearsome. His world, his adventures and his evolution are made so that we can believe they someday could happen, even though they never would. Most moviegoers should find everything they want here. Like Bale, a summer blockbuster can achieve great things if it has some meat on its bones.

10.title: Awesome Movie
10.content: I thought it was a great movie. I convinced my girlfriend to see it with me and she loved it. She never watched another Batman movie. I thought the dialog was excellent. I really enjoyed the long introduction to how Bruce Wayne becomes batman. The movie really builds well so that my willing suspension of disbelief is enabled. I wouldn't of gone to see this movie if Christopher Nolan hadn't been the director unless I heard that it was good. I liked the first two batman movies. But I felt this was far and away the best one made. I pray that they make a sequel directed by Christopher Nolan. It was the best movie I saw this year and I watch lots of movies in the theatre. It left me thinking YES!! as I walked out of the theatre. I haven't been this stoked on a movie since The Matrix or maybe even Pulp Fiction. I went see Pulp Fiction ten times in the theatre . I probably will only see Batman Begins 2 or 3 times. I am very happy with the movie though.

10.title: An action movie that's worthwhile
10.content:
I usually run the other way if I'm invited to go to the movies with friends when they're headed to see an "action" movie. How many times have I lived to regret it if I fail to heed my aversion and end up going anyway?...Too many! Prime examples: Any of the Star Wars series (after the initial episode); Lord of the Rings; most of the previous Batman attempts.

Christian Bale is a standout as Batman/Bruce Wayne, and Liam Neeson impressive as Ducard. Cillian Murphy's Dr. Jonathan Crane will make your skin crawl as you contemplate his evil mind.

Batman Begins exhibits a robust script, an ensemble of superb actors who get to demonstrate their superior skills, special effects that largely serve the advancement of the plot (instead of simply exist to overwhelm short attention spans), and a story that manages to entertain. After all, isn't that the idea?

10.title: The Batman movie many have been waiting for...
10.content:
Without giving anything away, I must say this was the most spectacularly thrilling and uncertain film I've ever seen. Uncertain in the fact that you could never be sure of things, as in the case with...well, you know if you've seen it. Those who haven't, unless you are a die hard Schumaker fan, go. Just go.

Now, I have been a die-hard Batman 1989 fan for the longest time, and I thought nothing could beat it. But let me tell you, Begins did. It wasn't REALLY better, because 89 was VERY good, but it was better by a margin. Everything was based in a realistic setting, which to me was very nice, because everyone says that Batman can never be real. Well, look there, and guess what, Batman is the most realistic comic book character you will ever see. I have always loved Batman, and there is one thing that all the other films, even 89 lacked, and that thing was...fear. Batman doesn't use superpowers. He uses fear, the legend that he has become, to deter criminals. He uses the shadows and his costume to project a deep fear into his opponents, which gives him the edge. I was so glad when I saw this movie, that 1, there were no DUMB neon suits, which a realistic Batman would never wear. 2, it explored the IMMENSE training that Bruce Wayne undertook to become the Batman. Batman has trained in every single martial art ever known, and worked his body to be as fast and as agile as possible. As you saw in the "dock" scene, he moved so fast, that all you saw of him was glimpses. An ear there, a fist there, and all around, enemies flying back or to the ground. This is what Batman is all about. He puts fear into criminals hearts because he is THE BEST. He comes out of the shadows and disappears without a trace. He takes out twenty armed men, silently and efficiently.

Now, I'm sure, if fact I know that many are going to nitpick and find something wrong with this movie. But I'm not really going to put it against them. You just can't satisfy some people. This movie has so few and miniscule flaws I don't even know where to begin. The plot. Well developed. Scratch that, extremely well developed. The story is as easy to follow as any other movie ever made. The intricracies of the characters are fully developed, giving you a sense of the personal depth of the characters. The suit. Oh, when I saw this suit for the first time, I thought, "Man that looks weird." But then I heard that Nolan was going for as realistic a movie as possible. Then I thought, "Well yeah, something that can stop bullets and knives and almost anything can't be expected to look perfect." This suit is by far the most realistic, and stylish even in it's realism. Sure, I loved 89's suit because it was well sculpted, but that is exactly why this is a different movie. Batman 1989 was just that. Batman, in 1989. This movie, is Batman, starting out in present times. Thats why it looked not quite as stylish as people may have wanted. The fight scenes. A lot of people said the fight scenes sucked. Well, you have issues. I thought that some of them were a little fast, but not too fast. They were almost perfect. Sure, the sword scene kinda moved around a little too much and jumped, but hey, overall it wasn't that bad. The car. Just because it isn't a smooth looking vehicle doesn't mean it isn't the Batmobile. Once again they wanted realism, and this car was real. Believe it or not, this car does everything in real life that you see it do in the movie. EVERYTHING. It jumps, it accelerates past 300 miles an hour. Many of the chase scenes were filmed around 105mph, whereas most chase scenes are filmed at 50 or 60. This car is unbelievable. It does jump in real life, up to 60 feet in fact.

This is the Batman movie for me, and I dearly hope you will go see it, because you will be amazed. It is the best movie of the summer, and the best Batman movie of all time. The best comic book movie of all time. Watch it, because when you walk out of that theater, you will feel as if there is hope in the darkness...

10.title: As of today...this is the greatest SuperHero movie ever created.
10.content:
One word: AMAZING! Something that should be understood about this film first off, this is not a movie for young children. I'm a 32 year old man and there were parts in this film that scared the **** out of me.

10.title: Batman Begins is quite simply the greatest comic book movie ever made
10.content:
Batman Begins is quite simply the greatest comic book movie ever made, and one of the greatest films ever made. With the trilogy now completed, it's appropriate and easy to look back and realize the full brilliance of the film. The introduction of Ra's Al Ghul and The League of Shadows as the villains allowed the final chapter to feature Bane in a plot that came full circle. To know Bruce, Alfred, and Gordon at the beginning of their careers allowed us to appreciate Bruce transforming into Batman, Alfred's growing father figure role, and Gordon's climb to commissioner.

The plot is complex. When Bruce witnesses his parents' death, he travels to Asia to learn about the criminal underworld. Along the way he meets Ducard and The League of Shadows who train him in the ways of ninja. Bruce escapes The League after learning of their plans to destroy Gotham. He returns to Gotham and takes on the alter ego of Batman to fight crime and return Gotham from the cesspool of criminals that rule the city.

The hero origin story has been seriously overplayed over the past 10 years. They're a dime a dozen and follow the same arc. What makes Batman more compelling than the others is that he's just a human that actively acquires his powers. He wasn't bitten by a radioactive spider, or shipped off from Krypton, or born as the God of Thunder. He's a tortured soul who finds relief in this alter ego he creates. The story of Batman isn't about Bruce Wayne, it's about Batman.

Batman Begins does the best job of showcasing the central character whereas TDK focused heavily on The Joker and TDKR on Bane and Lieutenant Blake. Christopher Nolan's touch is on every element of every frame. There's a scene after Bruce returns to Gotham where he has to act like he's having fun running around town in his sports car with European Supermodels. Leaving a party at a hotel, he runs into his oldest friend, Rachel Dawes. He tries to convince her that what she sees isn't him, but it's all for naught as the women in the background yell "We have some more hotels for you to buy." Nolan decides to drown out the sound, choreographed perfectly with the visuals as the sharp focus is on Bruce's tortured face, with the car and women heavily blurred in the background. It's one of the greatest shots ever captured.

Director of Photography Wally Pfister deserves much of the accolades. He frames Gotham in an almost sepia hue without the Instagram cheesiness. It works to showcase this the poverty and depression of the city yet give it a very comic book feel. This may be a realistic version of Batman, but it is still Batman. Much has been made of the action sequences being the largest weakness of the film. I agree that the hand- to-hand combat scenes are disappointingly weak. They're shot too close and edited too choppy. The rest of the action, mainly the Batmobile chase sequence, is skillfully handled. The fear in Bruce's voice channels to the audience as Rachel fades further and further from reality after being blasted with Scarecrow's fear toxin.

For the aforementioned chase, Nolan relied on no visual effects, even as the Batmobile flew across rooftops and through narrow underground roads. Nolan found a sort of empty playground in Chicago's upper and lower Wacker Drive that allowed for the chase to come to life as realistically as possible.

Much of the realism is thanks to the incredible cast. There's no over the top scene stealing actors here. There is terrifying amounts of talent. Christian Bale is the perfect choice to play the dark, brooding Batman and emotionally detached playboy billionaire Bruce Wayne. One of my favorite actors, Michael Caine, plays his butler/confidant/father figure, Alfred. Caine is so detailed that he gives Alfred just a slightly different tinge of his cockney British accent so as to be more appropriate for a butler. The cast is filled out with pitiful lesser actors like God, a.k.a. Morgan Freeman, perennial bad ass Liam Neeson, accent chameleon Gary Oldman, and ol' blue eyes Cillian Murphy.

Aside from the action scenes the biggest complaint has been the casting of Katie Holmes. After seeing TDK, I'm sure a lot of people wanted Mrs. Holmes back. The truth is that much of her negative press was centered around the Tom Cruise Scientology scandal. The character of Rachel Dawes was one of the weaker points of the first two films. Holmes isn't to blame. If anything she held her own against some of the greatest names in the industry.

Begins plays much like a great gangster film with all the right hints of comic book fantasy. Even if TDK and TDKR were never made, Batman Begins exists fully in its own skin. There is the Joker cliffhanger at the end, but you don't feel like the rest of the movie was setting you up just for the cliffhanger like every other big blockbuster these days. It's these subtle differences and detailed touches that make each frame of this movie such an absolute wonder to behold.

For more reviews like this one as well as other movie musings, go to http://thethreeacts.wordpress.com/

10.title: A thankful fan.
10.content: This is it. The quintessential film that truly defines not just great movie making but also does justice to translating the magic of comic books to the silver screen. Forget the previous Batmans, Spidermans, X-men movies and you would insult the film to even compare it to the embarassments that were Daredevil, or Elektra. This movie beats all. 10.title: Amazing
