The action was well done and very realistic. This movie is better than the original. Despite Katie Holmes not looking the part it dosen't really take away from this excellent movie.

10.title: The Bat is Back!
10.content: What can I say that hasn't already been said. I love this movie! The acting is great. The story is great. The visual style is a mix of noir and gritty surrealism. The villains(Cillian Murphy in particular)are finally menacing and not a bunch of goofy looking morons making lame jokes, as in the previous two "Batman" films. I also must agree with many others that Christian Bale may well be the best Batman ever. This movie also had a surprising amount of humor, so as not to drown itself in complete seriousness as some critics were suggesting it did. I loved everything about this film, but my favorite part is the little surprise Nolan has waiting for fans at the end. If you haven't seen this movie yet, I suggest you drop everything and do so. If you have, then see it again, as I intend to do! 10/10

10.title: Much better then expected!
10.content:
Save your $10 on Star Wars we all know how it ends... Batman Begins is awesome. Perhaps it's from severe disappointment after the last two Batman movies; I must confess my opinion may be a bit jaded because of the last two. I may even go so far as to say that it was better then the Tim Burton version (which I thought was incredible).

As a side not I would like to explain that this story line is new it does not follow any of the previous Batman films, and that's a very good thing, I assure you. This Batman is different from the last four altogether. Noland spend a lot of time (about 45 minutes) setting up Bruce Wayne and Batman as characters. The audience has a vested interest in whither they live or die and what happens to them. This is something that the last four all lacked and I think it shows.

If you're looking for a comparison this film follows more along the line of Tim Burton's version. It's darker. It also has a sense of realism, Batman was not just born with an arsenal of gadgets and a bat mobile he bought them, borrowed them. This film shows how Batman learns as he goes along and adapts to challenges that he runs into.

I felt that this was one of the best comic-book movies I've seen. It was realistic and has both story and character development, I honestly can not wait to go and see it again. As far a new series of movies I just hope that Noland and the crew bears in mind what happened with the last set of Batman films and when there going over the edge. But I would truly like to see what they have in mind for a series. I like the vision and tone of the story.

Honestly, I can recall the last time I came out of a movie theater and actually liked what I watched. I felt like I wanted to walk back in and see it again!

10.title: A Triumph
10.content:
I expected this movie to be enjoyable when I sat down to watch it. I was enticed by the trailers and was ready to be impressed. The first ten minutes of the film had me rolling my eyes and questioning every directorial decision by Nolan. Where was this movie going! Suddenly, it clicked. Ducard showed up in Wayne's cell and from that point forward I was in heaven. First ten minutes of skepticism forgotten.

Everything about this film I found fantastic. The performances, for example. Brilliant. Christian Bale shines as Bruce Wayne in a way Keaton never could have. Michael Caine provides some dry humor while being utterly believable as a caring confidant. Cillian Murphy's understated Crane was deliciously creepy and smug, and the Scarecrow scenes were inventive and fresh. Liam Neeson was goddamn extraordinary. Rutger Hauer/Morgan Freeman were decent, and Katie Holmes serviceable.

I wish the other Batman films had never been made. This is not a prequel, folks: this is a re-start. Burton's films, while in line with his body of work (quirky, creative masterpieces), are NOT true Batman films. Keaton sleepwalks through the role and Batman is done a disservice. Bale nails both Wayne and Batman in a way never captured in a live-action film before.

Found the scene where Bruce's parents are murdered surprisingly powerful. Nolan truly is a dramatic talent. THe entire Bruce Wayne backstory borders upon brilliant, with bale and neeson proving they are incredible actors who can deliver a believable yet forceful performance.

Yes, the action is choppy, and yes, the film ends jaggedly. What happened in the aftermath of the fear toxin? Never explained. Very minor quibbles. These are the only faults I can find with this film.

The score is perfect, the performances fantastic, the writing very decent (some corny one liners could have been excised, but who's counting). All in all, an incredibly film that I saw twice and loved both times. This movie needs to be enjoyed by everyone, so that a sequel can be made. Please see this movie. Nolan can learn from his mistakes and improve upon his triumphs. The next film can only get better. See it so there will be a next film! And forget the crappy Burton Batmans ever existed - these movies are different and better.

10/10

10.title: Batman: Year One
10.content:
Albeit not containing some of Batman's more notorious foes, 'Batman Begins' really is the most complete Batman interpretation to date. A marked improvement over Joel Schumacher's toyetic, bland take or the campy 1966 'Batman' and an elaboration of the Gothic, dark undertones of Burton's films, Christopher Nolan has created a more contemporary Batman which leaves a far more believable impression.

If not a comic buff, have you ever asked yourself, just as Alfred asks Bruce in the film, 'Why Bats?' We've finally been given that ever so desired backstory. Burton's 'Batman' in 1989 introduced a charged superhero without giving us the reason for his drive. Here, we see the events as they transpire, how Bruce Wayne abridges into the Batman persona and it helps us to better understand the motivations behind Nolan's rebooted Caped Crusader.

Jonathan Nolan deserves much praise for an extremely well penned story which incorporates elements of a corrupt, degrading society and those few trying to rebel against it. The sets are extremely reflective of this notion. The depiction of Arkham Asylum and the shanty town with the more affluent city revolving around it, separated by a small body of water illustrates the fact that the heart of Gotham's problems lies in the heart of the city, a part of the two-tier society but also not a part of it. Tackling issues such as those makes this superhero flick so relevant to today's world that even those who aren't regular superhero fans can enjoy it.

Both villains were embodied with mindsets so true to their comic book namesakes but Ra's Al Ghul doesn't have his traditional superpowers whilst the Scarecrow doesn't utilise anything but simple chemistry. Constructing that DC Comic fantasy world wasn't Nolan's intentions. Unlike Joel Schumacher for instance, his aim was to create a universe wherein Batman and his villains are all human beings set in a real, plausible world.

I really believe this portrayal strikes an excellent balance between Bruce Wayne and Batman and connects the two well. We see both a formidable, complete, physical Batman and a convincing façade as Bruce Wayne. The fact that Christian Bale wasn't a huge, well renowned actor gave him more room to make his mark. He brings out the most admirable and most believable iteration of Batman to be seen in the last couple of decades.

The film also saw the re-introduction and re-characterisation of people such as Lieutenant Gordon, Lucius Fox and Alfred who either had a subordinated role in the earlier films or were not present at all. Nolan makes it seem a travesty that they weren't explored properly previously after how well their roles are thought out and how superbly they are personified by these actors. Katie Holmes' performance however was a bit tiresome and absent of strength in her personality. Rachel Dawes' connection with Bruce Wayne was less than good. But in the end, that's just a Hollywood cliché and necessity. Batman has never really needed a love interest like Superman or Spider Man.

Some of the best Batman stories have dealt with darker, more impactful material and 'Batman Begins' strives for that angle where it succeeds magnificently. I would like to let you in on a post review secret disclaimer in case it hasn't been that obvious: I am a massive Batman fanatic. This spellbinding take on the Dark Knight earns more than just my stamp of approval.

10.title: Nolan Creates Greatest Caped Crusader of the franchise.
10.content:
To simply call this the greatest installment of the Batman franchise, actually demeans this film. People should actually look upon this film as it's own entity. This Batman shares nothing with it's predecessors. A new look, a new Batmobile, a new dark feel to the story.

It dives deeper into what drives Bruce Wayne. What makes this man dress up like a bat, and hunt criminals from the shadows of night. The story allows us to make this transition, this journey, with the young Bruce Wayne. To learn what drives him. To feel his pain, to experience his experiences. Christopher Nolan, takes us deeper into the heart of the hero, than any other director has with any other comic book cross over. The story answers a lot of the questions I've always had, that many people have had, involving Bruce Wayne and his alter-ego.

Christian Bale is phenomenal as Wayne, as is Michael Caine as Alfred. I was fearful at first with the choice for the female lead, fearing that Katie Holmes, was not mature enough to tackle such a role. Thankfully, I was wrong, and not only was she believable in her role, but she was outstanding.

Unfortunately, I can only give this movie 10 out of 10 stars, as it deserves many more. It's by far the biggest movie of the summer. It's the way Batman was meant to be seen. My hopes are that Christopher Nolan remains at the helm for the undoubted sequels, that are to come. Batman has always been one chromosome away from being that which he despises most, the criminal. The Batman is meant to be dark, gritty and brooding, NOT bright, colorful, and campy. If we wanted that, we'd all watch Scooby-Doo.

"Batman Begins" is a MUST SEE for the Summer of 2005. If you liked "Episode III", you'll love Batman Begins!

10.title: Wow!!! Excellent!
10.content: I must say that i left the theater ecstatic! A must see!!! This is the best ever super-hero movie that has been made! Christian Bale's performance is remarkable, as well as Liam Neason's. Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins is the movie hit of the summer! And who says Batman isn't a super-hero just because he has no super powers? In this movie there is plenty of suspense and plenty of chilling scenes! The movie is jumpy at points and does contain a few disturbing images but none the less this blockbuster is a smash hit and deserves to be seen on the big screen in the theaters! You will leave the theater absolutely pleased with the wonderful work of cinematography!

10.title: This starts it all over
10.content:
O.K. To begin with, three Batman fanatics and an X-Men girl. All three of the Batman freaks at the end-" That makes me wish they'd redo ALL the other Batman movies."

Me, I figured no one could pull off a better Batman than Michael Keaton, his darkness and yet heroic side. I'll admit, Bale was about equal. Also, Gary Oldman as Lt. Gordon, excellent choice, the previous ones didn't even look like Lt. Gordon, much less pull off the appearance of supporting Batman.

The crew of this film did what I thought couldn't be done, MADE ME WANT to forget every other Batman film like it was the first attempt at a Batman film. I already forgot the more futuristic-looking "Batman Forever" and "Batman & Robin".

This movie is a must see for all those Batman fanatics, comic book geeks, and movie-goers out there.

10.title: The Godfather of Reboots
10.content:
I believe that Batman Begins depicts Gotham and the titular character as originally intended. Despite the fact that DC has received a lot of recent flak, Marvel, James Bond, Mission Impossible, and even Jason Bourne have quite a few reasons to thank this entry into the Batman canon for their own reboots and/or reinventions.

Christian Bale plays a conflicted Bruce Wayne/Batman in a way that helped James Bond rediscover his similar feel and origins a year later in Casino Royale. Bale handles the role well, particularly in the early pre-Batman scenes and later playboy billionaire ones. Kudos also to Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, and Liam Neeson who provide bits of irony, comic relief, and even introspection here and there. I would also recommend the short animated anthology Batman Year One, from which Batman Begins gets much of its story.

I also enjoyed Cillian Murphy as the creepy psychiatrist Dr. Jonathan Crane and Michael Wilkinson, who makes a terrific gangster. Katie Holmes received some criticism for her role, but I was not strongly offended by her acting, though she is one of the weaker points in the film.

The best character in the film, and the overall trilogy but particularly in this film, is Gotham City itself, which comes across as one of the best dystopias in film history. The Narrows may be lost, but Batman Begins put the genre in capable hands and sets a high bar and deserves the full 4 out of 4 bat signals.

10.title: A real comic adaptation
10.content:
Finally, a real adaptation of a comic book that doesn't insult your intelligence, hasn't been diluted by movie exec committee thinking and breathes fresh life into a genre which has been rather stagnant of late.

The fact is that this film has raised the bar so high, the only other comic book film that can stand alongside this is the forthcoming "The Dark Knight" and in my opinion "Hulk". Even the Spiderman trilogy, as well executed as it was, has been overtaken as the best superhero film ever.

The reason why this film was amazing is that it gave credibility and humanity to the hero and the people around him, not just fancy weapons and a shoehorned in love story.

I don't want to say anything about the plot, acting, cinematography or the direction except to say watch it!!! And roll on Summer 2008 for The Dark Knight!!

10.title: A super-hero movie about a real hero
10.content:
Fans of the series rejoice in the truly awesome "Batman Begins".

Director Chris Nolan brings us an exciting and intense Batman movie that most of us have been waiting for since Batman Returns, and it is has revolutionized the series beyond leaps and bounds.

I will begin with that casting, Christian Bale is in my mind the new Batman without hesitation. He brings back the dark knight feel that Kilmer and Clooney lost. He also brings a genuine fear to the character that allows us to realize why the city might be afraid of its own shadow.

Michael Caine is an Alfred who is finally a character with some emotion and a real intensity behind all his lines, he no longer feels like a stock character. Master actor Liam Neeson commands the screen when ever he is on it, and does the film an unlimited number of wonders. It's difficult to imagine anyone else in his role. And finally, Cillian Murphy plays the perfect villain with an almost innocent sense of evil that is very difficult to put into words. There are also strong performances from Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, and Tom Wilkinson.

I was on the edge of my seat through out nearly the entire film, I was always wondering what was going to happen next or where Batman was going to pop out from, and when he did decide to the adrenalin rush that followed was worth seeing the movie for in itself.

My favorite aspect of this film was its feel of realism, it wasn't over done of fantasized in nearly any way, and we feel that we are watching a man who is doing what we feels he must, and that what we are watching may all possibly be happening in some dark city right now. We are able to see eye to eye with the caped crusader in many ways because we have all experienced loss, and have often done nothing about it. But it is the fact that Batman takes the law into his own hands for justice that makes him the hero we love to watch.

The only thing I could complain about in this film is that there was perhaps not quite enough of Batman on the screen, and maybe a little too much Bruce Wayen. However this is justified by the fact that it is a prequel and it isn't until somewhere in the half point that the Black Knight makes his triumphant appearance.

All and all it is nice to see a film that wasn't afraid to say "all right, this is the way everything happened and you're going to like it", but this this film does, and it might have been considered a gamble, but it pays off in the end, because we now have fresh start to the Batman legacy.

10.title: The best movie since Batman (1989)
10.content: This is the best movie since Batman (1989). Christian Bale, like Michael Keaton, played the role darkly. It begins with a young Bruce Wayne falling into a well while playing with Rachel Dawes, who eventually becomes an assistant district attorney. Young Bruce has a fear of bats. They go to theater, and Bruce begs his parents to leave. They make the fatal mistake of going into the alley, where they're robbed, and killed, by Joe Chill. Fast forward a few years. and we see Bruce Wayne returning to "Stately Wayne Manor," as it was called in the series. Bruce is trained by Ra's al Guhl, and returns to Gotham City to save it from the Scarecrow, and Ra's al Guhl. the mastermind behind the plot to make the people of Gotham mindless with fear. Batman stops them. Sergeant, by the end of the movie, Lieutenant, James Gordon, the future police commissioner, tells him about the Joker. Setting up the next movie.

10.title: Batman Begins is Off the Hook!
10.content:
I realized in the wee hours this morning that Hollywood has been presenting us with more recycled, reused garbage than I ever allowed myself to see before. Batman Begins has opened my eyes. From the first few minutes of this film I was keenly aware that I was watching something completely original. The tone that Chris Nolan and cinematographer Wally Pfister have created for this movie is something entirely new to me. It is more epic feeling that Gladiator and drew me effortlessly into the depths of the film. Yes folks, it's true, I loved Batman Begins.

I admit I am not an unbiased viewer. I wanted this movie to be brilliant more than anything in the world and damn it I knew it would be brilliant. I can however offer a distinct look from the Batman aficionado angle. As a girl who has a thorough appreciation for the intricacy and depth of the Batman comics I was grateful for the enormous effort made to create rich characters. Every character in this film has depth. It's simply stunning. On the other hand I can see how the average person who does not have a comic book background might ho-hum at this sort of movie. Some don't want to have to think and some don't want to have dynamic characters. Needless to say there is enough action here to satisfy even the basest viewer.

Christian Bale steals the show. He is magnificentdare I say, Oscar-worthy? He seems to have a solid grasp of Bruce Wayne and his many personas and plays them all with fierce determination. The filmmakers were so confident in their choice that they often let the camera dwell upon him for lengthy moments so we can see his emotions and practically feel them as well. There are very few actors who are capable of such a feat (that would have been appropriate for the role). Some scene's left me giddy in my seat, swearing under my breath because I couldn't believe how utterly unhinged Bale was as the bat (Flass's interrogation comes to mind).

And did I mention the score? While on it's own it feels a little disjointed, the score takes these brilliantly crafted moments and adds that buttercream frosting onto it. There is one particular scene in which Batman is in the Narrows facing Dr. Crane (involving a bit of fire) where the music is absolutely perfect. You feel like you're failing with Bruce when he does, you feel like you're angry when he is it's crazy good. It's all because of this excellent soundtrack.

The supporting cast is unparalleled. They disappear into the story as if they've never starred in their own film before. It's amazing. Michael Caine's Alfred is probably my second favorite role after Bruce. He delivers a fantastic performance that wrenched my heart many a time. Gary Oldman was convincing and sympathetic. He is Gordon. Neeson so good. Even Katie Holmes did great and I knew she would surprise me. Even among all these great talents she did not stand out negatively. She blended in pretty well with the rest.

The production design for this movie is going to win an Oscar. That's my prediction. Gotham looks stunning, sprawling real. Everything was real about this movie. I don't think I've ever been so drawn into a film before. My adrenaline was rushing so much I was able to drive through the night three hours back to my parents house in Eastern, MA. Whoa, man. Whoa. My heart thumped under my ribs throughout. I could not control my incredulous potty mouth. No movie has ever had this kind of effect on me.

Before I saw Begins I'd already bought tickets to see the show three times this week. For good measure I'll be going a fourth time. Five stars dammit!

10.title: Just great
10.content:
I just loved it, this is THE Batman I always wanted to see... Like every other movie it has his problems, it's not perfect, but for me it was. The story, the cast, the costume, the batmobile, the voice... I loved everything. Everything that had to be said was said by tons of reviewers : the good points, the bad points... There's no comparison to make with the others Batman movies. Tim Burton did a great job, but it wasn't exactly the Batman from the comics... What we have here is the closest thing we can have and it may be even better in the sequel... Batman Begins is the perfect beginning of a new franchise...

I just tell you that : go and see it, make your own opinion... this is all a matter of subjectivity, and how YOU will see the movie...

10.title: Nolan pulls it off
10.content: As the movie started, I commented to my friend "please let this be great." And it surely was. Nolan does an amazing job in bringing the franchise back into focus and gives us hope of a bright future for Batman. The casting is incredible (although Katie Holmes is a little weak in her role). Michael Caine and Christian Bale have such a strong rapport together on screen. The way they bring Alfred and Bruce to life is what pulls the Bruce Wayne story fully together. Christian Bale is far and away the best fit of any actor to play the Batman role (yes -even better then Keaton). He shows everything - wit, menace, charm, rage and I look forward to seeing what he brings to the characters in the future. And the ending is very strong in terms of where you hope to see the characters moving forward and that not all is saved in Gotham. I pray for future Nolan Batmans starting now and whatever you do - go see this movie.

10.title: Hands Down...The BEST comic movie I've ever seen!!! Hats off to Christopher Nolan.
10.content: Please, Please, Please, keep this director for the next 3 Batman movies! I love most comic movies. When I say most, that means some leave me pretty disappointed...as the past 3 Batman movies had. They were just "ok", but they really didn't leave you impressed with the storyline. The fact they flip-flopped so many actors in the past to play the part really left the character cold as his bat cave. They were just a lot of Hollywood flash and spectacle; a real waste of Jack Nicholson's major talent...he'd be awesome as the Joker in the next one (wonder who will be the next one?) If they do run this series of flix; they have got to keep the director...my recommendation for the Riddler would be Johnny Dep...he'd lend a new twist to things. Jim Carry was just too weird. Spiderman and Superman used to be my favorite but my favorite now just blew those two out of the water!

10.title: It gets it all right
10.content:
I was expecting just another Batman movie, although I had heard this one was quite good and allowed myself to hope it would be. I walked out of the theater thinking they got EVERYTHING right.

Intriguing plot, perfect casting, impeccable pacing, special effects that were beyond what was necessary without being distracting, amusing without being silly, truly frightening in parts, and the best job of rationalizing and explaining everything about the world of Batman... This was a great movie.

I'm going to have to see it again. I just can't believe I've finally found a film that gets everything right, and with a licensed property even.

10.title: The Dark Knight as he was meant to be
10.content: The Batman movie we have all been waiting for. What was hinted at in Burton's films and utterly forgotten in Schumacher's attempts comes to life. Bale is Batman. Period. This movie is also proof that there all no small parts, just small actors. And there are NO small actors in the film. Each character is wonderfully drawn and essential to the plot. While we don't see enough of Freeman, Oldman, or Cillian Murphy as the Scarecrow, their brief appearances are nonetheless enjoyable. The Batmobile - which is a silly misnomer here - is more tank than joyride vehicle. It has a function and purpose and is seen just enough to prove both.

10.title: This is one of my favorite films ever, it's left such an impact on me. This is the film that got me back into Batman.
10.content:
This is one of my favorite films ever, it's left such an impact on me. This is the film that got me back into Batman.

How did this film do so? Well, Christopher Nolan is a simply exquisite filmmaker, by writing his film out-of-order... And by doing a fascinating character study for Bruce Wayne. By pinpointing that Bruce Wayne is truly the mask, it's Batman... What an amazing idea, and a great way to dive into some psychology. The villains in this film are also amazing - Whilst the villains aren't the most theatrical, changing these villains to fit a more realistic world works amazingly. Falcone is a force to be reckoned with, Ra's Al Ghul is great for moral issues, but the stand-out here is Dr. Jonathan Crane, played masterfully by Cillian Murphy... Despite his limited screentime, he leaves such an impact. The rest of the supporting cast, from Rachel, who compliments Batman so well, Alfred, who is the emotional core of the film, Jim Gordon is played so well here, and Luscious Fox is a great addition here. The action scenes are fast-paced, and the commentary on fear is so good... It's truly made me think so much. My favorite of The Dark Knight Trilogy, and my favorite Batman movie. I love it so much, and I would love to re-watch it and only continue to get immersed in this world.

10.title: I absolutely love this movie, but still, i prefer the original with Michael Keaton
10.content:
I saw Batman Begins yesterday where I live, and I have to say this is I was pleased. you might say that I was expecting this to be amazing because don't get me wrong, it was made by one of the best directors in Hollywood, Chris Nolan. And now that I got to see it, I have to say that it was amazing, BUT I am not going to say that there were NO disappointments, which is one of the reasons why I loved the original more.

I am going to compare Batman Begins to Tim Burton's Batman. Why I loved the Original Batman was all because of Michael Keaton, and plus, it's also an All-time favorite movie for me. The real disappointments were some of the things with Christain Bale as Batman, which were a few things; A)The mask was crap, and it sorta made him look like the George Cloony version of Batman, B)I didn't like how he would disguise his voice when he was Batman, and finally C)He sorta had a little bit of a lisp in parts, or a slur, whatever you want to call it. Other than that, he was the best Batman/Bruce Wayne yet. Michael Keaton as Batman however was my favorite because he just suited the role the best with his presence and acting. Also, because he didn't have to disguise his voice, and he didn't look like George Cloony.

With the new Batman, we got to see him do things that he never really did get to do in the original, like Fly, release the bats, and everything else. Which was a huge factor to making this movie one of the best movies I've seen this WHOLE year. Just minor disappointments of how Batman talked and looked, thats it. I am still going to give it a 10, a BIG 10, because my disappointments were just minor. Go see it now

10.title: Good film
10.content:
This film is very well done. This film is not a prequel to the others, rather it is its own story.

The style, the effects, the acting, the story. Everything was very well done.

I loved liam Neeson in this movie, in fact, he was the primary reason I wanted to see this film. He is one of my favorite actors. He did a great job.

Also, I am totally obsessed with the Japanese culture, so the Ninja thing at the being very much impressed me.

This film had a good story line, something unexpected, I loved this film, and there are plenty of plot twists to make it even better.

The cast and acting was great. Liam Neeson was awesome, Morgan Freeman was quite funny, Christian Bale was very convincing, and What is the name of the guy who plays the Scarecrow, the entire movie it was bugging me because I couldn't remember.

Anyway, this is a great film, one of my favorites, and I highly suggest seeing it.

10.title: Best Batman yet!
10.content: I've never been a big fan of the live-action Batman films, but this one is so different! Although darker than most people may expect, the action and acting do not disappoint! Christian Bale is amazing as Bruce Wayne/Batman. If you can look past her recent publicity chaos, Katie Holmes does a fine job as Rachel Dawes (I also recommend her film "Pieces of April"-excellent as well!). I have to say it is a treat to see Gary Oldman in another non-villainous role (Sirius Black, anyone?)! With Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson and Tom Wilkinson, the cast couldn't get any better! The set locations are beautiful, especially the scene on the ice between Bale and Neeson. I HIGHLY recommend this film!

10.title: Review Style comment
10.content: If you are a batman fan this is the movie to see. We start at Bruce Wayne's beginnings and travel with him as he trains to become the Dark Knight.The script was approved by DC comics and therefore holds more truth to the original story than the "Batman" movies before it. Christian Bale was a really great casting choice as he has the duality to play both the suave Bruce Wayne and the haunted Batman. Micheal Caine, Liam Neeson, and Morgan Freeman played their characters with the great skill that we've come to expect from these legendary actors. Cillian Murphy's portrayal of Dr. Jonathan Crane was amazing and complex. I look forward to the next movie in this remarkable new series.

10.title: A stunning representation of the Dark Knight
10.content: I have never enjoyed any other film more than this glorious tale of the origins of the Batman. I am not a comic book reader nor a major fan of any characters like Batman, but when I saw Batman Begins, I was excited into watching every super hero movie I could lay hands on, sinking down to the pitiful Daredevil and rising to the impressive Spiderman. Burton's Batman was tolerable, but Nolan's is genius. Christian Bale out-performs Michael Keaton completely, and the rest of the cast surrounds Batman with humanity and kindness (Alfred, Rachel, Lucius Fox) and cunning, ruthless evil (Neeson, Dr. Crane, Valcone...). I am anticipating the sequel to this movie more than I have ever anticipated the release of any movie before, and more than I will probably ever anticipate the release of any other movie.

10.title: Batman Begins
10.content: I just saw the movie and it rocks. This is by far the best of the Batman Movies. Even considering that it is 16 years since Batman 1 came out, this film serves the Batman franchise better than any before it. It's absolutely horrifying in some scenes, I'm surprised that it's only pg-13. Overall, every scene in the film, outside Wayne Manner, is gritty, intense and brilliant. I'm a HUGE Batman fan. I've read and over the years injested the darkest Batman stories told. Including The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Year 1. This film not only stays true to that vision of Batman, but expands upon it. Everyone from the Die Hard fan to the casual movie goer should be satisfied with this portrait of Bats/Wayne. The casting, the directing, the sets, the makeup, the wonderful toys, all make the viewer wanna go out and kill Paul Allen and forget about it 5 minutes later. This movie gets 2 Bat ears way up. SEE IT! If you can see it on IMAX!

10.title: Star Here
10.content:
Simply put, Batman Begins is the best of the bunch.

I was one of those kids who saw Tim Burton's first Batman film 5 times in theaters (just the way it worked out), and I don't even think twice about ranking Batman Begins first.

There are a lot of long reviews on this one. I just wanted to keep it simple.

First, Bale's the best Batman you'll ever see. Second, Morgan Freeman seems to enjoy it. Third, Christopher Nolan has fashioned a Batman that will stay in your mind and constantly make you think back on it for weeks to come.

There are so many quintessential Batman moments in this film that it easily seems to out-duel all of the best aspects of every previous Batman film all at once (forgive me animated series fans).

Finally, the reason why I can't stop thinking about this film is because I still can't believe it. From the sheer anger of Bale flat out screaming and terrifying detective Flash to his playboy restaurant swimming pool, there's just nothing else that tops this.

Final say at this point for the summer: go see Star Wars 'cuz it's like riding on every single Disney ride for the first time all at once and all in the span of two hours. Amazing. And go see Batman Begins because it's the most surprisingly original film of the summer and a worthwhile relaunch of a franchise that's worth a damn.

Peace & Popcorn

10.title: movie of the year!
10.content: gonna try to make it short and sweet. Batman begins is the best batman movie to date by far, and the best comic book movie ever. Christopher Nolan has totally revamped the batman franchise. Christian bale was born to play the role of batman, he was superb. Liam Nesson totally steals the show as Henri ducard or should i say Ra's AL ghul. The action is pretty good and well coordinated. Not only is the scarecrow creepy but batman is pretty scary himself, he really scares the crap out of the criminals. All the supporting actors did a fantastic job, even Katie Holmes did pretty good as Rachel Dawes. I cant wait to go see it again. If you haven't seen it yet, i HIGHLY recommend you go see it right away.

10.title: Batman...the way it was meant to be
10.content: OK, let me just preface this by saying that I have been waiting for this movie for years. Ever since the debacle that was "Batman and Robin," I wanted to see Warner Brothers go back and get Batman right. Having waited so long, I was worried that, when the time finally came, I was bound to be disappointed. Fortunately, I was not. Not only has Batman been brought back to respectability, but it has exceeded the Tim Burton films by a mile. While they may have been entertaining flicks, one has to admit the first two Batman films, or any Batman film for that matter, was never about Batman. They were always about the villains, and it always made me feel somewhat shortchanged. Psychologically, Batman is the most interesting superhero around and none of the films ever got what he was all about. "Batman Begins" turns that all around and gets everything right that all the other movies got wrong. Batman/Bruce Wayne is finally that tortured and confused individual he was always meant to be: a borderline psychotic, only one step away from going down the path of the criminals he battles. Overall, the acting is first rate, the story is excellent, the direction is slick and the action is exhilarating. The only downside of this movie is the fact that now I have to wait another few years for the next installment.

10.title: Thoroughly Engrossing
10.content:
All of the small details are here and done to perfection. Little touches of humanity, such as non-verbal communication between the characters and effective (and entertaining) social banter, such as Bruce's "birthday speech" help make the world of Batman familiar - making all its outlandish happenings exciting rather than simply unbelievable.

Great acting, great script, and perfect casting. Caine, Freeman, and Oldman could all be competing for this year's best supporting actor (although I would have to give it to Oldman...he creates so much with relatively little screen time).

Definitely the best Batman and one of the best films I have seen this year. Nolan has a style that really draws the audience in...fast-paced and engrossing.

10/10

10.title: Cast, story, direction awesome: The best comic book movie ever!
10.content:
Batman is probably one of the most intriguing and interesting superheroes ever. He doesn't have any superpowers, but relies instead on his gadgets and, most importantly, his brainpower. He also has one of the most mysterious and thought-provoking origins, which have never been fully explored until now. In the past, Batman was chalked up to heroic rescues and exciting action sequences, but his reasons for doing his heroic deeds was never really shown. But in this film you get both.

The story is superb. Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale), in his twenties, disappears from Gotham City and is placed in an Asian prison. Time there causes him to dwell on his traumatic childhood, particularly a run-in with bats, which are his main fear, and the murder of his parents. A man named Ducard (Liam Neeson) trains him to join The League of Shadows, but when he learns more of the organization and disagrees with it, he flees back to Gotham City, which is now teeming with crime due to Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson) and his thugs, who slip through the fingers of the Gotham City Police Department thanks to Dr. Jonathan Crane (Cillian Murphy), much to the chagrin of Brice's childhood pal Rachel Dawes (Katie Holmes). When Crane plots to make fear fully rule Gotham City, it is up to Wayne, in his dark disguise, with help from Dawes, mechanical genius Luscious Fox (Morgan Freeman), his trusty butler Alfred (Michael Caine), and the only just cop in Gotham, James Gordon (Gary Oldman), to put an end to the terror that threatens to destroy it.

The cast is excellent. Christian Bale takes on the dual role of Bruce Wayne and Batman skillfully and brilliantly. He simply is Bruce Wayne. He is the best Batman to ever grace the screen. Simply inspired casting. Michael Caine is the perfect Alfred, bringing much humor to many scenes. Caine's Alfred seems to care deeply for Bruce, and often guides him through difficult trouble. Many people have called Katie Holmes's Rachel "thankless," but I do not see that as the case. Sure, the Batman's love interests have been thankless in the past: brainless, damsel-in-distress types, but (and it has been said here before) Holmes's Rachel is strong (wielding off Gotham's bad guys with her taser) and sexy, yet sweet enough that we see why Bruce loves her. She is his conscience, teaching him the difference between revenge and justice, a very important foundation to Batman's beginnings. Holmes, a very capable actress, brings weight to this slightly underwritten role. She makes Dawes a person with heart and one who also provides guidance to the lost Bruce. Holmes and Bale are a good match, though their chemistry is never fully explored, since Rachel decides that Bruce is hiding behind the mask of flippant playboy and needs him to take off that "mask" and let his real self (Batman) shine through. I really hope that she does not disappear like Batman's love interests in earlier movies. Freeman, Wilkinson, Oldman, and Murphy turn in excellent supporting roles, particularly Murphy whose turn as Crane is quite creepy.

The atmosphere is great too. Gotham looks a little futuristic, with a monorail that bisects the huge city, but it is believable and seems real. It is very gritty, just as a city full of crime should look. It is not slick, like Spiderman, but dark and soulful and is really great. Nolan's hit gold here. 10/10

10.title: The Bat Is Back!
10.content: After many years in limbo The Batman has finally returned. Far from the neon lights and bat nipples brought to the series by Joel Schumacher we get to finally see the character as he should be...dark. Like most people I had my reservations about another Bat movie; and with the bad taste left from Batman & Robin I think that's a valid reaction. Fortunately Chris Nolan has more then proved himself as a competent and creative director. But of course all the credit cannot go to Nolan; David Goyer's fantastic script managed to breathe new life into a once dead character. Such a superbly written story not only focusing on the emotional story of Bruce Wayne but also the psychological. For once we get to see beyond the Batsuit and delve into the troubled life of the Dark Knight. In previous incarnations of this character Batman is the central focus. Stories have been compromised in order to show Batman in action. However in this case it is about the man behind the mask and deep fear and anger he feels. It is not a story of Batman but rather a story of Bruce Wayne. What cannot go without mention is the outstanding cast that has been brought together. Ordinarily such a star studded cast is a sign of compensation for a weak movie; but this is far from the truth. Every actor pulls their weight no matter how little screen time they may have. This works marvelously as it shows the characters as real people without dramatizing their personalities. These characters are not larger then life but rather people coping with their bleak surroundings. Christian Bale is perfectly placed as Bruce Wayne. His performance is serious yet can still act the part of the playboy billionaire. He also has that slightly psychotic look in his eye that made Michael Keaton such a pleasure to watch. This is by far the best comic-book movie to date. It doesn't go way over the top and it knows how to have fun. While it has flaws it can be forgiven since it is still a movie about a guy dressed as a bat. Defiantly the most enjoyable film of the year. 10/10

10.title: This movie was the greatest comic book movie ever, etc, etc.
10.content:
This is my first time posting on IMDb.com. I've been reading all post both positive and negative, though positive outweighs the negative I must say. This is my review and recommendation.

I am a life long Batman fan, I like the original 2, Burtons works, but a lot of things always bugged me about those movies, too many changes to characters, stories, and in all honesty those films to me, were NOT BATMAN. Then came Schumaker and well I wont get into those.

With this film, before I knew what was going on a lot of things I cringed at, like the way the Batmobile looked, having Ras Al Guhl played by an Asian actor. As time went on though and I saw the trailers everything began to sit better with me. Then I saw the film, I had high expectations for this film and then thought maybe I shouldn't, but then it not only met my expectations, it blew me away. From the second it opens with the music and the bats and the children, to every kick *** fight scene. Yes I will admit some of them are filmed a bit too close but I know there is a reason for that. You see what you need to see. I am the biggest purist when it comes to Batman, and this movie did it all for me and gets me so unbelievably giddy for a sequel I can't imagine being able to hold still for two or three years.

My rating this film is a 10, A+, whatever, my recommendation go see this film, whether your a Batman/Comic Book fan or not, its filled with such a great story and so much action, and is so bad***, that you will get your moneys worth and will like it very much. A friend of mine who has never read a comic in his life from what I know of him, said this film was Amazing.

Go see it, now, please OK thank you./

10.title: Somewhere in California, Schumacher Gently Weeps
10.content:
The brain is like a video tape recorder... it will remember whatever you put on tape, easily erased and replaced by another image. Batman begins has successfully washed the memories of the previous two Batman movies down the commode.

What a great movie. Perfect casting, despite the mousy, teenagerish Holmes cast as a tough talking District Attorney (gladly no forced performances of her in action in the court room.. maybe one scene i cant remember). I especially enjoyed the casting of Cillian Murphy as the Scarecrow. A preppy neat metro-sexual type, nerdish but slightly off, as if you cant put your finger on it but there's something wrong with that Crane guy. It's always the quiet ones.... The hallucinogenic scenes are done quite well without needing much over-the-top CGI. A deliciously dark tone to the movie, needed like a shot in the arm.

I think what everyone agrees with here is that this is not if not the second best, THE best Batman movie (next to the 1960s movie! :-) I'm sorry i love the schtick of the Adam West era Batman). Even more so, you can actually envision this being almost believable, as this dark and dingy world we're thrown in is somewhere we've either been or can be in if we don't keep our cities safe.

Bravo.... A classic hero movie.

10.title: Batman's Begun with undeniable entertainment
10.content:
Cris Nolan draws a master piece once more (previously in Memento).. apparently he is very "Handsomely efficient" in telling past stories. This batman WILL make you forget there was ever any Batman before this.

Mr. Bale in Bat suit looks much better, and without as well.. and the cast, without a doubt has been awesome. Michael Kane as in Alfred I thought the most appropriate. And on the opposite side Katie Holmes looked absolutely stunning.. just how a comic super hero's girlfriend should look like.. Morgan Freeman was not what one would except, but he did not much to do in the film either.

The special effects were awesome, Gotham looked more realistic and one can actually relate Gotham to the Comic Book Gotham we see. All in all ..the best treat for summer yet.. an undeniable entertainment

10.title: Best Batman movie ever!!!
10.content:
Batman Begins is the best Batman movie to date. It puts the previous movies including the Tim Burton films to shame. Unlike the the other Batman films Batman Begins is focused on Bruce Wayne/Batman not his villains(usually played by high-profile actors like Jack Nicholson as the Joker and Jim Carrey as the Riddler). Chris Nolan has done a great job to explain why Bruce Wayne became Batman, and as we all know he witnesses the murder of his parents firsthand, but Nolan adds more to that but you will just have to see for yourself no use in ruining a great film here. It also sets up for the sequel pretty nicely.

Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, Cilian Murphy, and surprisingly Katie Holmes all do great in their roles, but Christian Bale is the true star of the Batman franchise. Bale looked as if he was born to play Bruce Wayne/Batman in the film, just like Christopher Reeves was born to play the Man of Steel. Bale does a great job in making Wayne turn into a monster whenever the mask is on. Bale also did what Keaton, Kilmer,and Clooney failed to do, to be Bruce Wayne "and" Batman. Keaton was good under mask but never fit the role for Bruce Wayne. Kilmer was good at being Batman but a poor Bruce Wayne. And Clooney the role was never meant for him in the first place. Whenever Christian Bale is mentioned one word will come to mind "BATMAN"

10.title: Excellent Batman Film
10.content:
-Excellent rendition of Batman on the big screen.

-Wisely develops the characters for almost half the movie before Bruce first wears the costume. Especially, addressing Bruce's motivations and goals at doing something so extreme (becoming Batman).

-The chaos of the fighting scenes, while hard to understand for some people, most accurately portray what Batman is doing to his enemies.

-Gives Batman a grounded sense of reality, without loosing an "other-worldly" feel.

-Introduces much of the film-viewing audience to aspects of Batman's rich character that has thus-far gone untold on the big screen.

-I look forward to the sequel, as there is still so much more to explore in the Batman mythos.

-To anyone who, after watching this, is interested in high-quality works involving Batman, I recommend:

Comics (traditional renditions of the character): -Batman: The Long Halloween, and its sequel Dark Victory -The Killing Joke -Batman: Year One -Batman: Blind Justice

Comics (alternate views of the character, or "What-if" scenarios): -Batman: The Dark Knight Returns -Gotham by Gaslight

TV: -Batman: The Animated Series (first three seasons) - The most complete single vision of Batman, and one of the best. Possibly the best. Dark and mature, the best episodes of this series are truly exceptional television.

Movies: -Batman Begins (obviously) -Batman (1989) -Batman Returns -Batman: Mask of the Phantasm (Batman: Animated Series movie)

10.title: Batman
10.content:
I thought this movie was way better than the other Batman movies. It seems more realistic. From how he came to be to his equipment. The cast that were in this movie made it better, especially the veterans of movies like Michael Caine and Morgan Webb. The storyline itself is easily understandable and you can follow it. I would rather have this movie and more like it to watch than the previous ones that were made. Especially if they get Mark Hammel to play the Joker like he did for the cartoon.

But there is one plot mistake. The machine that is used to evaporate water should have evaporated the blood in people, too because blood is mostly water. But who really cares? It was a good movie.

10.title: A superhero movie with chutzpa!
10.content: I try to avoid superhero movies because they are usually formulaic garbage, but not this one. The casting was superb, the story was superb, the sets were spectacular as were the special effects. Christian Bale as Batman was charismatic and realistic for a fictional character. Dare I say Oscar? The Movie is necessarily violent but not overdone. This is dark adult fun. It is also about overcoming fear and knowing the difference between revenge and justice. This is a smart movie with a man in a superhero costume. You know a movie is good when you leave the theater and you want to become the protagonist! Quick to the batcave!

10.title: Astonishing!
10.content: To be honest, I always thought that the people supporting DC Universe were the ones not being able to agree on that the Marvel made better movies. The ones that tried to be different as they felt insecure about their own intelligence. This made to think twice. Batman Begins isn't only exciting, also, it's smart on its own way. The movie is filled with wise quotes and most importantly, it delivers what most movies can't do. A message. Not only it exceeded my expectations, but filled me with the memories that'll never be forgotten. Shortly, Christopher Nolan is the best director ever!

10.title: Perfect. They finally got it right. Forget everything you know. Batman truly begins as intended all along.
10.content:
Blown away. Nailed it. Perfect.

The other films barely scratched the surface of this characters depth and darkness. They resembled the character in costume and name only sadly. This film respects the comic characters true core beliefs. They go out of the way to underscore them. Long time Batman comic fans will be amazed and stunned, but not surprised, we knew it all along. And now Hollwood has finally figured it out.

The score is powerful and appropriate. The casting excellent. The world very real. This film resonates. It is not a great comic movie. It is a great movie period.

10.title: Forget the other films. Batman begins from here!
10.content:
After the debacle that was Batman & Robin, the franchise is reinvented in a dark, somber way that the comics always sought, and it is done with great style. Without loads of CGI a la Spider-Man and Hulk, etc, this new incarnation of the Dark Knight is indeed dark.

Chris Nolan, while not known for massive blockbuster type movies, has taken the Batman story and knocked it out of the park with this film. From the casting to the story to the actors and the production design, this film is a home run.

Christian Bale as Batman/Bruce Wayne truly gets inside the psyche of the character and is utterly convincing in his portrayal of a man compelled to stop evildoers in Gotham City. He brings a new level of intensity to the role that has been sorely missing. The contrast of his Bruce Wayne and Batman characters is perfect and he has some truly funny moments as the carefree millionaire playboy.

The supporting cast is top-notch. Michael Caine as Alfred is an inspired choice, and Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox steals the scenes he is in. Gary Oldman as a young Lt. Gordon really ups the ante as the lone good cop left in a city of crooked police. Cillian Murphy is great as Dr Crane/Scarecrow and Liam Neeson is terrific after some disappointing turns in Kingdom of Heaven and Star Wars. The only real weak link was Katie Holmes - simply due to the fact she looks only about 17 years old! (Sorry Tom, but it's true)

Gadget wise - this film has it stacked. Not only are they cool, but the audience gets a briefing on how it works, so when Bats pulls one of them out you're not left rolling your eyes thinking "How the hell can he do that??"

The Batmobile was something I wasn't sure about when I first saw the pictures, but rest assured - this thing is fast, tough and lethal!

The decision to opt for less CGI and more practical effects pays off nicely since it doesn't disconnect the audience from the action the way it did in Spiderman and other superhero flicks.

The script by David Goyer is probably one of his best in recent memory. Gone are the cheesy one liners and silly plot schemes. Sure, the plot is a tad over the top, but this is a comic book film - not Hamlet!

Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard teamed up to bring a score that while totally different from Elfman's, suits the film perfectly.

The only real complaint I have with the film was the fight choreography. The camera seemed to be a tad too close to the action to really figure out what was going on when the fisticuffs flew.

All in all, a terrific restart to the franchise that was sorely needed. I walked out of the movie wishing the sequel was already made. The set up that was created at the end was nothing short of flawless.

For anyone who has never seen a Batman film, this is the one to start with. For those who have seen the other four films - forget them, and see this. As a warning to parents though - this film could be too intense for little kids who are expecting the Batman they watch in cartoons, so get a sitter and leave them at home. The PG-13 rating is well deserved. Probably the best film I have seen recently - and that includes the new Star Wars film. If you want a great story with high caliber acting and some great popcorn munching fun - catch Batman Begins. You won't regret a second of it. I will go so far as to say this is a superhero film to rank up there with the original Superman.

10.title: Review of "Batman Begins"
10.content: What to say about "Batman Begins"? Gee, I dunno' how bout' the fact that it single-handedly changed my entire point-of-view on life itself - yeah good stuff I'd say. Christopher Nolan, that is all. What Nolan did here is something incredible; not only did he resurrect a then-dead franchise name, but he catapulted everybody's attitude ...toward Batman to a more serious level. By using his Memento-style Non-linear storytelling techniques, beautiful cinematography, and insanely witty and provocative dialogue, Nolan created the most captivating superhero yarn to date. I don't give a crap what people say; Christian Bale is the best Batman actor. I've never seen any of the other Batman actors put as much effort into this movie as Bale did. He really, and truly played a landmark role in this movie and he successfully managed to encapsulate the Batman/Bruce Wayne that Mr. Bob Kane created. Every other actor in this movie is badass. Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman? Are you kidding me? Amazing supporting cast. One of my most favorite soundtracks too. Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard really did something out of the box for this film, but they also did something quite beautiful and appropriate. Overall, this movie is one of the most influential movies I have ever seen. It managed to portray every aspect of Batman's origin to a tee. Truly, a masterpiece.

10.title: The Batman you've been waiting for since Burton's first...
10.content:
I'm not going to go into a lengthy review because my bladder is painfully full from the coke slushi I had during the opening of Batman Begins. That being said...

If you even REMOTELY liked the first Batman movie with Michael Keaton, you owe it to yourself and all of your loved ones to redeem the Batman franchise that George Clooney so woefully burned to the ground with his infamous tenure as the Dark Knight. 10.title: Utterly fantastic!
10.content: You would really have to go out of your way to dislike this movie. It's settings are darker and stylistically superb. The acting and characterization were phenomenal and told the story well. Especial standouts were Christian Bale and Cillian Murphy (though Liam Neeson is always a treat), but I thought it was wonderful that the movie captured the essence of Bruce Wayne's excellent support network. No one, not even Batman, can do it completely alone, and everyone needs motivation and emotional support. Katie Holmes's character, though not badly acted, just wasn't fleshed out enough for my taste--she was also aggravating in that nothing really seemed to please her. Finally, this movie is definitely an owner. I found it inspiring and entertaining.

10.title: Awesome, best Batman Ever
10.content: So batman is back. First of all i had the Fear that all best scenes were shown in the trailers. But after all it's clear that Nolan did a very nice Job. Christian Bale plays at his best. Very high Level. The Action is well chosen and not overpowered. By the way the only light disturbing thing is that Katie Holmes looks a little bit to much like a teenager. She plays her role very good but looks definitely to young. In my opinion Christian Bale is showing his best performance since American psycho. Michael Caine plays also very good. The other actors like Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman and especially Liam Neeson were also good chosen because each character plays his role in a very kind and beautiful way. So keep on Mr. Nolan and everybody should enjoy this incredible movie.

10.title: The best "Batman" movie ever!
10.content:
This one seemed the best because it was dark and yet real. It seemed this producer tried to put together a plot based on the idea of: what would it take for a normal real person to be willing to become a dark superhero? I always liked Batman most because he did not rely on super "powers" like Superman, or experiments-gone-wrong like Spiderman or the Hulk.

The best part of this one, though, is the relationship between Lucius Fox (the guy who creates the gadgets) and Bruce Wayne. It's so wink-wink-I know what you're up to but I won't say it, just the way it would be in the real world. Example, one of the best lines: "Mr. Wayne, if you don't want to tell me exactly what you're doing, when I'm asked I don't have to lie. But don't think of me as an idiot." Can't wait for the sequel, with a Joker who seems more psychotic and criminal than Jack Nicholson's Joker to square off with a Batman who seems more passionate about what he's trying to do than Michael Keaton's character ever did. (That, and I can believe Chistian Bale beating up on bad guys. Michael Keaton beating people up? Please. Stick to Beetlejuice...)

10.title: Best Batman so far
10.content:
*I don't name anything but sort of allude to certain parts in the movie*

I have always been a fan of the Batman movies and was pleased with the Tim Burton versions.

This one was amazing on a whole new level. The characters are developed as much as they can be in a 2 hour movie. You see WHY Bruce chose a bat as his figure to strike fear, you see how the people around him deal with it, you see HOW he becomes what he is. Its just done SO well in such a small span of time. He is frightening, not cheesy. Which is hard to do to a guy in a bat outfit. And you see how he got all those wonderful toys.

The casting was great. Not a big Katie fan, but lucky enough she wasn't in it too much. Christian Bale did a great job bringing Batman to life. Gary Oldman was amazing as Gordon, and you just HATE some of the other guys (don't want to give too much away) because of how well they played the characters. Also what made it great was it's not about 1 certain bad guy, there are a lot of bad guys on different levels. The whole city is full of bad people. Which leaves it open to so many possibilities of what's to come. I don't know how I feel about what was showed at the end for what might be in the next Batman movie... a certain bad guy...

I walked out of the movie afterward HAPPY I went and saw it. I haven't been able to say that about a movie in a few years. I look forward to the next one. I just hope they keep the same crew!

Go see it.

10.title: Finally done right!
10.content:
After years of failed Batman movies and a franchise that almost sunk itself, it's very refreshing to say that "Batman Begins" proves to be a winning entry to the series of films that have preceded it.

Dark, stylish, well acted and directed, "Batman Begins" should prove pleasing to both the die hard Batman fans, as well as just the regular movie-goer.

Quick Plot summary: We begin with Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) at a refugee camp, being held as a prisoner convicted of theft. He is recruited by Ducard (Liam Neeson), who advises him that he would like him to train with Kung Fu Master Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe) when he gets released the next day.

After being released Bruce travel to Ra's Al Ghul mansion where he learns how to be a Kung Fu master capable of kicking some serious booty.

After his long absence (7 years) from Gotham, and with the city in peril; Bruce decides to travel home with hopes of rebuilding his childhood town. During this process he decides that in order to save the city, he must do so undiscovered; and through a series of events our beloved Batman is born.

He enlists the help of Alfred (Michael Caine) and a co-worker of Wayne enterprises Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman) to help him build his bat cave; gadgets and assorted gizmos.and of course his awesome Batmobile.

He then sets out to stop Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson), the cities corrupt crime boss & also Dr. Jonathan Crane (Cillian Murphy) a.k.a "The Scarecrow" who have been reeking havoc and skillfully avoiding any prosecution from deputy D.A. Rachel Dawes (Katie Holmes), who also happens to be Bruce Wayne's childhood playmate/crush.

"Batman Begins" is edgy and well polished, with some nice fleshed out character development and some great acting. Cillian Murphy's Scarecrow is quite a nightmarish vision, and Wikinson's crime boss Carmine Falcone is as scandalous as they get.

Bale does a great (if not the best) job as "The Dark Knight" and Caine proves himself to be a most worthy and caring Alfred. The actions scenes are pretty awesome as well, as is the look of Gotham city. The film leaves us with the possibility of a sequel as well, including the mention of one of Batman's most notorious villains. One can only hope that Joel Schumacher doesn't get anywhere near it! Just a great superhero film all the way arounddefinitely recommended!

10.title: my first review/comment thinggy ever, and i've been with IMDb for about 5 years
10.content: Batman Begins was easily one of the best movies i have ever seen, i'm not a batman fan-boy or anything but wow this was about as close to perfection as movies get. lets start with the cast, not a single slacker acting wise in the bunch scarecrows effects were scary the new batmobile is the shizz it didn't have anyone shouting NOOOOOOOOOOOOOO like another far inferior summer block buster. if this movie is out sold by star-wars its proof that there is no god. words can no explain how wonderful this movie is, the comedic parts those sparse (as is with batman) were very funny and quick. 10.title: Back to the beginning
10.content:
I seem to be commenting on all the Batman flicks at once.

I saw this the other day, only a few after seeing the original Batman, and I can say this is truly in the spirit of the Batman. Appreciably dark, angry, and stormy, with an interesting history. We learn about where & how Batman learned his skills. We also learn a lot more about his parents, what kind of people they were, and what kind of teachings they gave Batman. Katie Holmes was less than great but her role was fairly minimal, other than to be the required DID (damsel in distress).

The Batmobile was stunning, even better than before, and some of the shots were beautiful. The Scarecrow was genuinely scary.

Another good movie to watch.

10.title: Best hero movie ever made
10.content:
When I first went into the theater I had already read all the reviews I could, and they were all glowing. Movies always get at least one bad review somewhere but this one did not. So right there I went into it expecting a lot. I mean a LOT!! Never in my wildest dreams could I have imagined that a movie could surpass my fully inflated expectations.

This did.

I'm hearing a lot of sequel buzz but I almost hope they don't make one. I just don't think another Batman could ever top this one. This movie is fantastic. I spent the car ride home in awe of what I had just witnessed. Everything good you hear about this movie is true and then some.

The casting was perfection. Truly. From Cillian Murphy to Christian Bale (who is HUGE again after the Machinist) to Gary Oldman right down to Katie Holmes. (whom I expected very little from) However when your scene partner is Christian Bale, it helps.

Batman fan or not, this movie is everything one could ever want in a Batman movie and I loved Tim Burton's Batman. It's extremely dark, well acted and funny too.

The main reason this film is so good is how much character development there is. They make it a priority of the film to get inside the head of Bruce Wayne. Showing you how this man could become a creature. How he could become something else. Character development, focus on plot, and lots of cool action to spare. This film successfully brings Batman into our reality. Gotham city is no longer some fictional far away city. Gotham city could be any random city in our reality, and we finally see Batman in our world.

I have to stop writing now because I'm going to see it again. I'll tell you nothing more of the film. It speaks for itself.

Louder than any hero movie I've ever seen.

10.title: Definitely the best!
10.content: Don't get me wrong, I still think that the 1989 Batman is a great movie, but with a much darker tone to it, Batman Begins takes the cake. I work at a movie theatre and saw it 2 days before it was released, and it definitely lives up to it's expectations. All the cast did a great job of portraying the characters in the DC comic. The best part is that there is actually a story to it, not just mindless action. It's the story of how he becomes Batman for crying out loud, hence the title Batman Begins. Definitely worth the 10 dollars to see it at a movie theatre. Batman fan or not. Hope to see more to come of Christian Bale as Batman.

10.title: Batman Begins is number 1!!!
10.content:
As a reader of the comic, and a fan of the first movie, I was skeptical of this new incarnation of the Dark Knight. I was completely surprised and happily so. Christopher Nolan did a fabulous job in re--creating Batman the way he was supposed to be, a man on a mission, driven by his past and a devotion to Gotham City. Nolan also portrayed the reasons Batman became the way he is and how he got those wonderful toys in a way that is reasonable as well as plausible. In many ways this Batman is the most believable and entertaining of all the movies to date. Even the villains are understandable, and not left to the philosophy of "you have to believe it because its part of the movie." That sad philosophy was liberally applied to Batman Forever and Batman and Robin, and subsequently were duds in the eyes of true Batman Fans.

All in all, Batman Begins is by far the best, and I hope to see more from Nolan.

10.title: I love this movie
10.content: I absolutely love this movie i have watched it so many time i almost have it memorized. I am the biggest fan of BATMAN and i can will sit and debate the topic of who is better out of spider-man, superman, and batman for hours. The actor and actresses really fit the parts and did an indescribably amazing job!!! The movie was more than i expected it to be and i will watch it again and again. If you have not seen this movie yet i highly suggest it!! if you like the original batman movies i can promise that you will love this even more!! i think many people will love this movie if you can just take a little time to watch it and you will want to add this movie to there collection!! thanks for reading reading watch the movie!!!

10.title: Batman Begins, Begins Something Great!
10.content:
After Seeing Batman, i had doubts ever since the atrocious Schumacher films came out, and were disgracing the Batman films everywhere. Upon hearing Nolan directing this movie i was surprised and excited, after seeing such movies as Memento and Insomnia, which were amazing, I had to think can Nolan pull This Batman movie off, can he re-create the whole series over again, and hope our cape crusader won't die and be embarrassed once more in a movie? Amazingly the whole film works.

The movie starts with Bale in prison, as of yet we don't know why he is there. But Bruce Wayne has a skills of martial arts and attacks anyone who dares attacks him. We then meet Henri Ducard, who trains Bruce to become an ultimate weapon and seeking that those who deserve justice, get justice.After Bruce Wyanes parents were murdered in front of him when he was child he has sworn justice ever since. The League of Shadows in which Wayne wants join is run by a criminal under lord name Ra's Al Ghul, who's method of Justice is beyond what Wayne wants. Wayne kills Ra's and then runs back to Gotham to become a sworn protector.

As we look back in the past the open thing this movie runs on is fear. We learn Bruce Waynes fear, and the fear of everyone in this movie so brilliantly done. Gotham is bleak disgusting and looks as if it should be scrapped and torn down. Run by gang lords and drug users who get off Scott-free. Bruce Wayne is sworn to protect Gotham and bring down crime. He puts fear into them by what he used to fear Bats, as he becomes Batman. The movie has amazing acting and cinematography in it, the way you fear Batman and Scarecrow in the movie, is unlike anything, especially when we see the fear gas injected. Most of all it has a cool factor on it. Bale pulls off Batman with ease he plays the billionaire playboy amazingly, and Batman all at the same time. Neeson, Oldman and Freeman all make great supporting roles even Holmes does a good job with what she has, and shows she can act. But the real reason is to check out Cillian Murphy who may not be a big star yet but he's coming towards, he performs Scarecrow and Jonathan Crane amazingly, he sometimes becomes so creepy it makes your skin crawl by the way he talks, and then shows how he puts fear into others and the plan on Gotham as well.

The effects were amazing we finally have a movie where CG isn't everywhere we look and that it's down to good Ole action and storytelling. The Wachoski Brothers can learn a few tricks as could George Lucas, CG is not the whole movie but the actors and storytelling make up for everything to make an amazing movie. The Batmobile is beyond cool, in one sentence I Gotta get me one of those. The action scenes when he's doing his hand to hand combat could've been pulled off better, it was close up and hard to see what was going on, kind of like Bourne Supremacy, but none the less this movie just rocks.

Bravo to the new Batman, and Mr. Nolan for saving him all together. While the movie isn't perfect, it's just as close to being there. 10/10

10.title: great movie do not miss it
10.content:
this movie has been a great experience ... its difficult to portray a character with no superhuman powers but capable of doing amazing things with the help of his intelligence,will,money and of course his learnt fighting techniques .It actually raises the question of credibility because you do not believe what you are seeing but this movie is amazingly satisfying regarding credibility.You can actually see a well laid sequence of logical events leading to the making of Batman and even the stunts aren't that logic defying .Christian Bale has been able to do justice with the character.... he has this quality of being mysterious but at the same time a next door guy you can relate to.His voice modulation has been great ...from Bruce Wayne to batman.Katie Holmes has been satisfactory. Mr. "Fox" has been great as always.The plot hasn't gone astray as generally is the case with other superhero movies ,with action being the overriding factor...here one finds a near perfect balance of action and emotion.Will recommend it to everyone who wants to see a good movie.

Looks like the best superhero movie ....

10.title: The Best Batman Ever 4 stars
10.content:
Batman Begins is clearly the best Batman movie ever made. It was actually better than Batman and Robin. The movie has great cast and proves to the fans of Batman that the director knew exactly what he was doing.

The action scenes are fantastic, the acting is very well done and the entire cast gives Oscar winning performances. The most noticeable performance's are by Gary Oldman, Liam Neeson, and Christion Bale (Sorry for spelling any names wrong).

The entire movie is absolutely phenomenal. It has great character development, great drama, and great special effects. One of the best movie's of this year and the summer. I can't wait see this movie again.

10.title: What else to say but EXCELLENT?
10.content:
I was ready to go right back into the next show. Although nearly speechless, I'll try to explain what makes this movie the greatest cinematic experience to me since LotR.

The story, acting, directing, simply all the ingredients, were perfect. Christian Bale IS Batman and Bruce Wayne (very important). While the movie is quite long, you wouldn't want to miss a second as the child Bruce goes through his painful development to become what is Batman. It's believable. All the supporting roles add what the movie needs, it's fun to watch Freeman, Caine and the others. The dialogues (even translated which is usually the death blow to mediocre ones) are great and the Sound track too! Gotham city is awesome. I could go on telling you forever. Minor inconvenience is Katie Holmes who's not doing bad at all, but fails in one key scene to bring IT across. Thankfully Christian Bale is not stopped by that. And I'm grateful that the fights don't show every single kick and hit. You get to realize that there's a dangerous fight but you don't have to watch every single movement. Still, it's not made for children, and although I like bats, I'm going to watch out for them in the next cave I enter.

THANK YOU Christopher Nolan!!!

PS: And I love the new outfit!

10.title: Easily the best comic book to film movie
10.content: This is defiantly better than the old batman films. They were good but just lacked the action and acting. The new batman brings a new look to batman. I think Christian Bale plays batman really well and he is a lot better than previous batman such as George Clooney, Val Kilmer. Micheal Keaton was the best one from the previous batman. The action sequences from batman were very entertaining, especially the car chase in the new bat mo-Bil and thought they did a good job the car. The story was brilliant because it showed us a new villain those that didn't read the comics or watch the cartoon. Cillian Murphy played the scarecrow very well and i'm sure scared a few people with his performance. This movie is very entertaining and i'm sure everyone will be glad to see batman back at it's best and good too see they have found the right actor for the role of batman.I am defiantly looking forward to the Dark Night hitting the cinema June 2008.

10.title: One of the Best comic book movies ever made...
10.content: This movie was so perfectly scripted it should stand as a model for all other comic book superhero movies... what thrills most of us comic book fans is how the hero ends up on his journey and what lies beneath that makes them become and conquer their fears and embrace a new life as a superhero... this movie not only spends a perfect amount of time delving into Batman's origins but also is finally well acted and not over the top like the other ones, or like Spiderman or Daredevil that are so concerned about the action part that they forget the character development and their super power skills.. which in this case is the main part of the movie. Hopefully it will make the Hollywood ignoramus that is blowing out all of these remakes finally realize that people will pay for well scripted character driven stories with great directing and acting...but it all starts with a great script. Even with Katie Holmes who is totally miscast and couldn't act out of a shoe or be considered a heart throb even with the tantallating tight shirt shots she just is inconceivable as a DA Assistant and perhaps might fit as the DA's secretary at most...she is TV material and not a film star.. even if she is engaged to Cruise.. but even her bad acting doesn't spoil such a great film. Enjoy and you'll definitely get your monies worth if you enjoy classic comic book stories!!! A big 10 plus for Batman

10.title: I am the night
10.content: This is a brilliant take on Batman. There isn't much to say that hasn't already been said. This is the best Batfilm to date, period. Christopher Nolan and David Goyer and have turned this character into what its spirit always was, a real man. The narrows, the slums of Gotham City, look like something straight out of Ridley Scott's Blade Runner. The skyscrapers are beautiful and displayed in mesmerizing blues. It is the first "superhero" movie to take itself seriously. This movie is dark and edgy, like a film-noir of the 1940s. This corrupt journey into a seedy world is cool escape from the laughable circus of Gotham that Joel Shumacher created in the late 90s.
