The use of villains in this movie, although seemingly sparse, sets up the road to the rogues gallery we are all looking for. The little cliffhanger in the end lets you know what is in store for the franchise, and I can not wait.

10.title: "It's not who I am underneath, but what I do that defines me."
10.content:
Very, very good movie. Easily the best comic book movie ever, and that's saying a lot because I loved Hellboy, The Punisher and the X-men and Spider-man films.

The cinematography is brilliant. We're finally seeing Batman in 2.40:1, folks, and it shows. Every shot is composed wonderfully, and the darkness is almost like a character in itself.

It's so much better than the first four Batman films that they can't even compare. Every member of the cast shines, particularly Bale. He's definitely the most convincing Batman we've yet seen.

They need to make, like, six more of these movies.

This is just a masterpiece. Everyone do yourselves a favor and go see it as many times as you possibly can.

10.title: Now we know where he gets all those wonderful toys....
10.content:
The personality of the Bat Man is brought into focus....how a boy, heir to an empire, loses his parents by gunshots from a mugger, feels guilt over it that he may be responsible do to his own fear which caused them to be in the wrong place at the wrong time....how that boy grew up waiting for the day to take revenge, only to have it snatched away from him moments before that moment of truth which may have caused his life to have taken an entirely different direction....having lost that opportunity, wanders the world to get close to the evil element within, in an effort to understand it and perhaps successfully combat it.

Fate steps in when a secret organization, dating back over a thousand years, embraces him and teaches him fighting techniques so he can lead them in their twisted vision of saving Gotham City by destroying it's civilization because it has become too corrupt. Only Bruce Wayne didn't comply...instead vying to fight the corruption in order to save the few good people remaining...and ultimately, having to fight the very person/organization who trained him.

Excellent story, excellent cast, excellent direction, excellent visuals, excellent movie.

10/10

10.title: Everything you want from Batman
10.content: I've been waiting for Batman Begins since the news that Christopher Nolan was going to direct.I've waited so long and i was not disappointed in the slightest bit. In fact, I believe it achieved something that other comic books movies have failed to achieve. Christopher Nolan has taken this dark comic and made it into exactly what it should be...a dark and terrifying reality for the characters in Batman. I have to admit when i heard David Goyer was writing the screenplay i was a little worried. But, then i heard Christopher Nolan was writing it alongside Goyer and i could expect nothing less then greatness. Batman Begins takes you into the character of Bruce Wayne like no other Batman movie has. Bruce Wayne is nothing but a man filled with hate. Christian Bale is amazing. By far the best choice for batman ever. Batman begins is something daredevil wished it could've been. Batman Begins is the movie that future directors working on comic book movies should strive to even compete with. You can't expect anything less form a cast and crew this great. Batman Begins is by far the best movie of the year so far.

10.title: Makes the Tim Burton movies look like the old TV series
10.content:
But this film has to be the best thing for Batman fans since the first film. This film has provided the fans and new comers a deep and darker insight in Bruce Wanes world.

Oh and if you like the Batmobile you ain't seen nothing yet. The Batsuit looks better as well, though it lost the old logo we're familiar with.

Also in this film is a great cast of actors and a great performance from Bale as the caped crusader.

I liked all of the other four films though this brings back what made the Tim Burton film's great. Whilst at the same time making them look like the TV show and the other two films.

Overall with heart stopping, on the edge of your seat action that will truly take your breath away.

If you can't see it on IMAX go to the theatres. If you can't see it on either you will be kicking yourself.

Unless you have a seriously good surround sound system and the biggest television set on the planet.

10/10 all the way

10.title: Awesome!
10.content: This movie was awesome! It is the best Batman movie ever made. This is what the first Batman should have been like. Christian Bale is Batman in this movie. The film, itself, is dark & scary. And one of the best elements is that Nolan & Goyer has actually made Bruce Wayne/Batman human. He is a mere mortal trying to fight his fears and demons and he fights it with his Bat persona. And the way Batman walks and moves is what I have always envisioned him doing. NOt like in Burton's flicks, where Batman was stiff and slow. Batman is all about being sly, quick, and scaring his foes. This film is definitely worth the price of admission. All Batman fans rejoice! This is the real deal!! One very minor weakness of the film is Katie Holmes. The romance between her and Bruce Wayne seemed forced. But it was very minor. All in all, it rocked! I saw it 5 days after it came out, and the audience I saw it with gave a very loud ovation when the credits began to roll. Tell everyone you know that this film rocks. I think that there are people out there who were extremely disappointed with the forgettable Batman & Robin, that they may not give this film a chance because of that. Those people are missing out. I can't wait for the next one. Batman Continues...!!!

10.title: Even better than previous big-screen interpretations
10.content:
Wow. That is all I could say after leaving this film about a half hour ago. Even now as I am writing this, I am still in awe as to how Nolan captured the true spirit of the Batman comic book franchise; not done properly since the animated series (and the animated movie "The Mask of the Phantasm"--which I HIGHLY recommend).

"Batman Begins" is even darker than Burtons' vision, and oh so much better. It delves deeper into the psyche of Bruce Wayne's character, which gives him more purpose, and even answers Jack Nicholson's (The Joker in "Batman" 1989) question of where he gets those wonderful toys. Even the shaky character of Rachel Dawes played by Katie Holmes wasn't too hard to stomach most of the time.

I strongly recommend this movie to everyone--especially those upset with the recent Batman movies.

10.title: Almost as good as the first two
10.content: The story was good over all. Only Katie Holmes looks more retarded then Peyton Manning. With the exception of Katie Holmes, the acting was phenomenal. The fight scenes were terrible, actually I don't think I even actually saw a fight seen in the whole movie all it was was shaky camera work. Christopher Nolin did an excellent job though. There were only a few problems or things that were not explained. I am sure if another one is made the movie will be much better. Hopefully Katie Holmes will not be included in the next cast. She is to skinny, in Disturbing behavior she had boobs. Now she has ribs. She is gross looking, it is a shame that it is cool in Hollywood to look like you have anorexia nervousa.

10.title: Best movie of the year, Greatest comic book film of all time.
10.content: Wow is all I can say. I left this movie feeling the greatest Joy I've had at the movies this year. Words can not describe the thoughts that went through my mind as I watched this great film. Let me just say thank you. I would like to personally give thanks to: Christian Bale, Michael Caine,Liam Neeson,Katie Holmes,Gary Oldman,Cillian Murphy,Tom Wilkinson,Rutger Hauer,Ken Watanabe,Morgan Freeman. I can't forget David S. Goyer for writing this excellent script. Christopher Nolan Thanks for Directing this Flawless Masterpiece. Warner Bros. Thanks for allowing this great Cast and Crew to Give the world Something that can be Cherished, by Batman Fans for many years to come.

10.title: best comic-book movie EVER.
10.content: better than Spider-Man 2. better than Superman. better than even the lauded Incredibles. this is probably the most faithful adaptation of source materials of any film (Sin City was not an adaptation, it was a change in media. and i still have not forgiven Peter Jackson for cutting the Scouring of the Shire). much like the amazing Batman: The Animated Series, this movie is not a literal translation of the comics, but an amalgamation of the themes therein to tell a new story. the movie (thankfully) eliminates the previous films from continuity, creating an amazing new universe. Gotham looks and feels real. you cold believe that it exists (unlike Burton's Gothic nightmare or Schumacher's neon hellhole). the characters are lent an air of realism and gravity by fine actors taking their roles seriously. Wilkinson, Murphy, Bale, Freeman, Caine, and Neeson all turn in stellar performances. the movie forgoes the primary mistake of the previous films and focouses on Batman instead of the villains. and speaking of villains, there's a slew of them (fans should keep an eye out for Tim Booth's Victor Zsasz). Carmine Falcone, Ra's Al Ghoul, Henri Ducard, and the Scarecrow are all great. fantastic film and an amazing rendition of the dark knight. my only gripe was the casting of Flass, who turned from a square-jawed blond buzz-cut Green Beret to Bud from Memento, but i can live with that. and the villain reference at the end had me applauding.

10.title: A great way to begin The Batman franchise....again!
10.content:
Since his first dramatic appearance in Detective Comics in 1939, Batman has grown to become a pop-culture icon. From movie serials in the 40's, to a classic campy TV show in the 60's, to a solid animated series in the 90's, fans have thrilled to the super heroics of this unique character. However, as a film franchise, he has brought results that were somewhat less than impressive creatively. While the Tim Burton directed films, BATMAN and BATMAN RETURNS were stylish and dark, they also suffered from plot holes you could drive a Batmobile through. Then Joel Schumacher introduced a Day-Glo sensibility to the Dark Knight in BATMAN FOREVER, before drowning the character in ludicrous costumes (a Bat suit with nipples???), pun-filled foes, and whiny sidekicks in the lousy BATMAN & ROBIN. By then, Batman as cinematic property had become a laughingstock. Fortunately, indie film director Christopher Nolan reinvigorates the franchise in glorious form in BATMAN BEGINS, a reboot of the Batman legend that, for the first time, puts the focus squarely on our hero and not on the over-the-top villains of past films. Nolan also bases the film in a strong semblance of reality that allows the audience to not only accept the possibility of the winged vigilante, but embrace it as well.

Most fans already know the story of how wealthy Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) loses his parents when they are slain during an attempted robbery, but the movie also tells how he chose the bat as his symbol, as well as the steps needed to become the avenger of the night that he turns into. Disillusioned and frustrated by Gotham City's corrupt judicial system, the young Wayne goes abroad to study the criminal mind. Later, while locked in an Asian prison, Wayne is recruited by the enigmatic Ducard (Liam Neeson), who offers him a path in which to focus his anger and hone his skills. Wayne eventually joins his new mentor as a recruit in the mysterious League of Shadows, headed by the sinister Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Wantanabe). Eventually, Wayne realizes that he cannot follow the League's extreme methods of dispensing justice and returns to Gotham to forge his own way. It soon turns out that Wayne's return is just in time as Gotham falls prey to a fear epidemic engineered by the twisted Dr. Jonathan Crane AKA "the Scarecrow" (Cillian Murphy) and a familiar figure from Wayne's past.

From the top on down, this film is blessed with a solid cast that adds wonderfully to Nolan's vision. As the title hero, Christian Bale blows all other Batman portrayals out of the water with his intense and scary take of the role. This is a Batman that you not only fear, but can relate to as well. In fact, he turns in the definitive performance. Michael Caine adds warmth and humor as Wayne's trusty butler, Alfred. Liam Neeson does a great variation of his usual mentor roles as Ducard, a man with his own surprising secret. As an assistant DA and Wayne's childhood friend, Katie Holmes does a nice job with what is basically a thankless role. Cillian Murphy makes for a perfectly creepy Scarecrow, while Morgan Freeman is solid as usual as the man who provides Batman's wondrous car and gadgets. Gary Oldman is wonderfully cast against type as Jim Gordon, one of Gotham's few honest cops. The scene in which he drives the tank-like Batmobile is a sheer delight.

The screenplay by Nolan and David Goyer (who wrote the BLADE films) is awash with characterization and motivation...something that you don't see in many comic book films as a rule. In fact, you get so engrossed by the proceedings that you almost forget that you are watching a "superhero" film in the first place. The special effects are used to enhance the story and not overpower it, while the set design pictures a Gotham that is a unique cross of Chicago, New York and Hong Kong. If there is a flaw, it lies in some of the fight sequences. Done in close-ups and quick cuts, they can get frustrating for those who want to see more of Batman's fighting style. However, this is very minor since the story never ceases to grasp your attention.

In the end, Nolan and his superb cast and crew succeed in achieving what was once thought impossible: the resurrection of a film franchise that, if not dead, was at least on life support. As a result, Batman is once again flying high and BATMAN BEGINS is a film that I wholeheartedly recommend.

10.title: best batman ever
10.content: This movie was excellent. Mr. Bale was superb as batman and all the special effects were tremendous. I was mesmerized through the majority of the film and thought the bat mobile and the bat cave were the best yet. Michael Caine was excellent, as well as Morgan Freeman. The actor playing Dr. Crain was amazingly convincing as a villain. I am not a comic book fan but have always enjoyed the batman movies because of the batman show that aired on TV when I was a child. The first two Batman's with Michael Keaton were so excellent, that the others paled in comparison. But this batman far exceeds the Keaton films. One of the best parts of the film was that the director chose to literally "lighten" up the series. That was one of the failing points for all the other Batman's was the eerie darkness. This film had a perfect balance of light and dark. The bat mobile was just amazing and the batman flying sequences were really cool. I would recommend this movie to anyone who likes a movie with a good plot and action packed. Do not miss this film.

10.title: Its about time!
10.content: Batman fans, and superhero fans of all creeds, will not be disappointed with Batman Begins. At last we have a serious, and entirely believable Batman - without the "camp" - for lovers of the superhero genre or anyone who loves pure escapism. Christian Bale makes an excellent (and sexy) young caped crusader, but Micheal Caine almost steals the show as Alfred. The movie has just the right amount of atmosphere to make it compelling, without making it overly brooding. The script is excellent, and the plot moves along well, with lots of action. (I didn't feel that there were any boring bits, so make sure you get your snacks and visit the rest room before the movie starts!) The character development is more than I'd hoped for and was really, really refreshing.

10.title: This is bloody brilliant
10.content: Just came home from this movie. I have got only one word to describe it. BLOODY BRILLIANT. I don't if you are a bat fan or not. But go see this. This could be one of the best movies in 2005. Christian bale is outstanding in the role. So are others. The action scenes are tight and edited to portray how a ninja would fight. Special credits should be give to Christopher Nolan for single handedly reviving batman franchise. The movie took a while to describe the person behind the mask, Bruce Wayne's mind. The only negative is Katie Holmes's character. She was not well defined and she doesn't look like an attorney either. I would seriously recommend this money. Well worth your money. 10/10

10.title: A Superhero Movie with plot, that excites and intrigues
10.content:
I'm not going to get into the details about how the movie changed my life or anything like others seem to ramble on about, but I have to say that the new batman movie was perfect, minus the few little corny bits (very few) that have come to in the years to be batman, and can't be forgotten.

Christopher Nolan made a superb movie out of batman, full of development of the psychology of a man that take justice into his own hands. In the past Batman was just this vigilante that just appeared out of the clouds of Gotham to save the people from the scum of the city. Now I loved the Tim Burton versions and what it did, what it had to do to entertain the masses and bring batman back into popularity after decades of hibernation, but this on took that and showed that batman was nothing more then a confused man that was torn from his family and was seeking a purpose in life. The development of the entity of batman and his suit/toys, was a story we all wanted to see, and we got everything that we wanted out of it.

THis movie did more for me than both spidermans combined with respects of keeping it down to earth and making to story relatively believable. Christopher Nolan deserves to be well recognized for his achievements in bringing back a hero that we all loved and Joel Schumacher made a joke of. This movie by far is the best superhero movie made, because it kept two feet squarely on the ground but made you want to jump up off of them and cheer for the hero.

10.title: One of the best movies of this century...
10.content:
After the abysmal attempt at directing by Joel Schumacher in Batman and Robin, I didn't have much faith in another movie coming out and surprising me at all. But on Sunday, that all changed.

When I heard a new Batman movie would hit the cinemas in June, I was excited (being a fan of the comics) when I heard they were going for a darker approach to re-invent the Batman franchise. 'New director: Christopher Nolan' shocked me, when I heard he was British and wanted to do his best to make this brilliant. I thought there were some strange choices for the actors to play the different parts. For example: Michael Caine as Alfred, Liam Neeson as Ra's Al Ghul and Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon.

So on Sunday, 19th June, I went into the screenings hoping for everything I had wanted the movie to be; when I came out, it was like a dream had come true. I have to say, the film was f***ing amazing, and Christopher Nolan has created the best super hero movie yet. The first time you see a glimpse of Batman is where he's thrashing the drug dealers working for Valconi, and as Valconi looks out his limo window, he can see them all be pummelled to pieces. He loads his shotgun and grunts under his breath: What the hell are you? And once you hear those words, two hands rip him out of the car, and Batman is revealed as he growls: I'm Batman. And knocks him unconscious.

Whoever loves Batman has to see the film, it's a real, spectacular treat that needs to be savoured and cradled until it kicks you in the face and shouts: III'M DAAAAAAAAAAARRRRRRRRKKK. It's actually very intimidating. It has the best actors of the Batman films, the best storyline, the best Batman: Christian Baile and the best director.

10.title: The best Batman
10.content: I grew up on the Tim Burton Batmans. I love the Tim Burton Batmans. I mean....Michelle Pfeiffer in the catsuit pretty much put me through puberty right then and there. So when I say that this movie blows Burton's out of the water...I do not say it lightly. This is Batman in the real world. Gritty, realistic(as much as a comic book movie ever will be) and full of 3 dimensional characters, fantastic action scenes, and the incredibly engaging story of how Bruce became the Bat. The acting is superb(some of the greatest actors alive today are in it), the music is outstanding...some of the most pulse pounding and engaging music I've ever heard in a film. Christopher Nolan is rapidly becoming a force to be reckoned with, turning out one outstanding movie after another. Seeing this movie in IMAX was one of the greatest movie experiences of my life.

10.title: A Fantastic Start
10.content:
The Dark Knight Trilogy has always been a series that I've been lukewarm on. I remember thinking that Begins was passable, Dark Knight was good but overrated and Rises was just bad. However, on a recent rewatch I found myself eating my words. Batman Begins gives a brilliant new origin story for the dark, gritty and more realistic version of Batman for the modern era.

So let's start with the negative. For me this was the final ten minutes of the film. Considering Bruce's main point to the League of Shadows was that the compassion and refusal to kill was what separated those in authority from the ruthless criminals of the world. Then in the final showdown Batman willingly leaves Ducard/Ra's on a crashing train knowing full well he's going to die.

I presume this is just an issue I have with this but it rubbed me the wrong way after trying to prove that compassion and mercy was effective.

However, now we get to the positives of this absolute thriller. So first we have the main cast of this film: Christian Bale, Michael Caine and Cillian Murphy.

Christian Bale offers a brilliant performance as the main protagonist of the film. He plays Bruce Wayne differently to the previous actors in the role. Michael Keaton portrayed Wayne as an eccentric and reclusive man. Val Kilmer (who is criminally underrated in the role) tried to give more depth to Bruce where we saw the extent the death of his parents had upon him. Finally, George Clooney gave a more bland and average millionaire.

Bale provides the playboy façade that really fits a modern adaption of the character of Batman while also managing to carry his humanity and deep vulnerability which is explored during his scenes with Rachel and Alfred. He also portrays a Batman that really emphasises the use of fear. The two scenes where this was most present were during Batman's capture of Falcone and the famous "swear to me" moment, both of which were played more as horror rather than action.

Michael Caine plays Alfred as a wise mentor and father figure to Bruce and has some brilliant scenes with Bale which is always a joy to watch.

Finally, Cillian Murphy plays the Scarecrow and I adore him. He provides a truly menacing touch to the role of Johnathan Crane and was my favourite antagonist of the film.

The other main positives were the direction and plot. There was nothing too complicated in the narrative and it all flowed very well while also looking gorgeous.

Overall, Batman Begins is a strong start to this trilogy and I'd recommend this to any fan of the superhero genre. If you haven't watched this, do it now.

10.title: Bruce Waynes life leading to his becoming Batman
10.content: Christopher Nolan does an excellent job in having the story flow. From the beginning credits the movie draws you in. The parents murder scene which has been different in all of the scenes is the best of all the batman movies. The beginning does a great job of explaining the early history of Gotham City and how Bruce Wayne became the Dark Knight. The movie perfectly describes how Bruce Wayne got so good in the field of martial arts and where the Batmobile and the suit came from. At first sight of the Batmobile in the trailers is that it is a cumbersome tank. This is disproved with the awesome speed and power it possesses as it weaves in and out of highway lanes. Christian Bale does a great job in showing the dark side that George Clooney and Val Kilmer could not bring to the screen. Overall it is the best movie I have seen this year; a must see.

10.title: Batman Gets Justice
10.content:
As a movie, Batman Begins is outstanding. As a Batman movie, it's damn near perfect.

The three main men behind this production, Nolan (director, co-writer), Goyer (co-writer), and Bale (lead actor) understand and respect the source material, the Batman comics. They understand Batman has been continually published for nearly 70 years because he is a fascinating character. A character that has never been fully realized on film - until now.

Christian Bale is part of a phenomenal cast including Michael Caine (Alfred is a joy), Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman (Gordon done right - finally!), Morgan Freeman, Rutger Hauer and many others. Even Katie Holmes was a lot better than I expected.

Some critics have complained that this movie lacks humor. I laughed a lot, at the right places, and for the right reasons. This movie proves you can have humor in Batman without camp, and without turning it into a spoof. Didn't you get the memo?

This film is constantly surprising, constantly inventive, and constantly engrossing. How anybody can say this movie is too long, too slow, or too talky is beyond me. I was captivated, yes captivated, the whole way through.

10/10

10.title: Amazing!
10.content: This is the Batman movie we've been waiting for! They finally got it right! The spirit of the character is fully captured, especially in the car chase/birthday party scene, where the Batman/Bruce Wayne duality is explored better than any previous effort.The film really takes it's time with Bruce Wayne, showing his journey to becoming Batman and making it seem a bit more believable than a guy just putting on a suit and punching people. It was good to see Jim Gordon well represented too, as one of the most important characters in the comics, he is essential to the Batman saga.A lot of stories from the comics were mined to good effect, taking the best of each. Cataclysm, Year one, Secret Origins, etc. were all represented, culminating in perhaps the best super hero movie ever, and definitely the best Batman so far.

10.title: Batman Begins, FINALLY!
10.content:
This is THE Batman movie. Everything before it was a waste of time and everything after it will have a lot to live up for.

Of the previous four Batman movies, the only one that comes close is the first. This movie basically rewrites the whole franchise and it rewrites it the way it SHOULD have been written the first time.

Basiclaly, this movie captures the spirit of Batman like no other movie. Exceptional acting by all parties certainly helps, but the key strength of this movie is the writing and directing.

The story is very well written (though I found the bit about training with some secret Ninja society a bit weird for Batman, I guess they wanted to explain his excellent martial skills). The story starts slowly and nicely to introduce you to the personality of Brude Wayne, but it is not cheesy or over simplified. The biggest Achilles-heel of modern Comic book adaptations (like Spiderman, Hulk, Daredevil) is that, with the exception of X-Men, they are written with 12-13 year-olds in mind. The dialog is watered down and many of the details are ignored and sacrificed for high-octane computer generated action scenes. This movie does the right thing, it tells a solid good story knowing that it will be loved by grown-ups and kids as well. The movie has no shortage of cool gadgetry and nice action scenes mind you.

The directing is where the movie gets a 10. The movie succeeds in capturing the spirit of Batman comics. Batman is always there, always watching, brooding, creeping. The creepy, chilling sense of some of the comics, the scary moments, the deadly efficiency of the Dark Knight is in full display. The hallucinations induced by the doctor in the movie will scare you pretty good while the clever sarcasm of Alfred will bring a smile to your face.

The outfit is probably the best similarity to Batman ever, the supporting cast (especially Michael Caine) offer a wonderful refreshment throughout the dark (and rather far-fetched) plot that unfolds. And of course, the main dish, Christian Bale is amazing. He does the best Bruce Wayne/Batman combo ever.

10.title: So this is what a comic book movie should be like!
10.content:
It's difficult to describe how great Batman Begins is. It succeeds not merely as a superhero film (though I hate using the term because Batman is not super, he works hard to have his abilities). The audience gets to see Batman's development here - Bruce Wayne's troubled psyche and the emergence of his true persona, the Batman. I absolutely loved how director Nolan made it clear that Batman is who Bruce Wayne really is.

Kudos to Christian Bale, the greatest depiction of Batman and Bruce Wayne ever.

Kudos to Michael Caine, who brought great heart to Alfred. Alfred is far more developed in this film. His relationship with Bruce is an awesome thing to bear witness to. Alfred was entrusted to be Bruce's guardian and clearly took the job seriously, but he goes along with Bruce's plans to become the Batman and helps greatly in the creation of the hero (antihero?).

Kudos to Liam Neeson for playing Henri Ducard (and - SPOILER - Ra's Al Ghul, or is he?).

I loved seeing Bruce making the "batarangs" - more like bat-shaped Chinese stars. Loved that they showed us some trial by error for Batman.

Kudos to Gary Oldman. We finally see the relationship between Gordon and Batman.

The plot is great. The development and pacing is superb. The action scenes are dizzying, very intentionally. Batman is scary, snatching criminals up from the sky - scary stuff for the baddies. Batman's first trip out is the best ever!

Batman Begins is not just a great comic book film, it's great period. Unfortunately the Academy won't give it any consideration because it's Batman, but what a film!

10.title: WooHoo
10.content: Best Batman movie ever! With this movie, I believe we can usher in a new era of believable Batman movies, free from camp. The real kudos here belong to David Goyer & Christopher Nolan whose story is by far the best adaptation of a comic book origin story in recent memory with a totally unseen turn. The film also does the best job of explaining in realistic terms how it is that batman and his wonderful toys can exist. The casting is almost flawless with Christian Bale being by far the best Batman AND Bruce Wayne and the supporting cast is equally well suited to their roles. For those of us who were about to swear off Batman movies all together, this film is a bright light of hope for the future of the franchise.

10.title: The one thing I can't get past....
10.content:
The League of Shadow's plan to "destroy" Gotham is to release a panic-inducing toxin that will "rip Gotham apart through fear." I just don't buy that.

It would be much more believable if they were releasing a nerve gas or something that killed people almost instantly. But a panic-inducing toxin? Is that supposed to scare people into killing each other or something? I just don't see how that is supposed to destroy Gotham. Whatever the reason, the story didn't provide much logic for how that was supposed to work.

Other than that, it's still a great movie that I never get tired of watching. 9 out of 10 stars.

10.title: Batman Begins is a Cinematic Masterwork
10.content:
There really is nothing like it. Totally original film-making, it's awe-inspiring, gripping from beginning to end. As a film lover, I hesitate to use masterwork unless the film is absolutely a miracle of achievement. BATMAN BEGINS is such a masterwork.

Sure, it portrays violence throughout the film yet for those who abhor such violence, this film is the rare exception because underneath, we are witness to the process that makes a human being ethical who is dedicated to justice.

This is not your typical superhero epic about good and evil, though good and evil are both inherent to the story line. After all, the film is based upon the good old American (World) values of good triumphing over evil.

The film shows us in graphic detail how the Batman legend came into existence. Though the scenes are fantastical, the story is believable. Bruce Wayne's transformation into Batman is as heroic as you'll ever see. The message is about facing one's greatest fears and pushing through them, no matter what.

Hans Zimmer's musical film score is among the best I've ever heard and is equal to the awesome image making. The film is many steps ahead of the earlier Batman films and stands out sharply against the background of its Superman and Spiderman competitors.

As skilled an editing job as you'll ever see. Breakthrough cinema, an experience I'll never forget.

10.title: This film is a sight for sore eyes
10.content:
After four attempts from two different directors, the third, Christopher Nolan (Memento), gets it right. Batman Begins picks up in the beginning (hence the title), as Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) is in what looks to be a Japanese prison camp. Flashbacks work well for this film, as Wayne's childhood is revealed with much more depth than the original four films depicted. As Wayne is tracked down and trained by Ducard (Liam Neeson) more and more is revealed about his parents' death and his awful fear of bats.

The cast is full of Oscar worthy talent. Michael Caine plays the loyal Wayne butler, Alfred with Morgan Freeman as the weapons specialist, Luscious Fox. But it is the young talent of this cast that steals the show (Except for Katie Holmes.sorry sweetheart). Christian Bale is the best Batman to date and Cillian Murphy masters the villain role as the brash psychologist, Dr. Jonathan Crane, aka Scarecrow.

I am most impressed with the realism brought to the film by Nolan. Don't expect any comic book colors and set designs. This film is a true masterpiece of darkness and vengeance. The new Batman costume itself is even darker, showing the anger that fuels our heroes every action.

This film is a sight for sore eyes in this summer slump of blockbuster hits. I am very much looking forward to seeing the next installment of the franchise, but please, no more Val Kilmer of George Clooney as the caped crusader. Keep Bale!!!!!!

10.title: The best 'super-hero' movie ever.
10.content:
Do you remember when you were a kid and you had a fantastically outrageous dream, then a few years later your dream somehow came true and it was amazing? Well, picture that on a massive scale and you have the EXPERIENCE that is Batman Begins. I'm sorry to say Tim Burton fans, but you no longer have the definitive Batman film. This movie surpasses every super hero movie before it in every way. The cast comes through in phenomenal form, and Christian Bale IS Batman. Special effects are top notch, and the cinematography and Nolan's signature 'flashback storytelling' are both present and do their jobs wonderfully. The city of Gotham is believable, almost REAL, and you really get a sense that this could be how a legend is born.

Bottom Line: I usually hate sequels, with Batman Begins, I can only hope that Nolan remakes the whole franchise.

10.title: Batman Reborn.
10.content:
I've waited a long time trying to find the right words to express my thoughts about this film. I have read some incredibly great reviews on this title that put it on a pedestal. But nothing compares to the movie itself. I'm not here to write a synopsis, but I will tell you this. The ending gives me goosebumps, every single time I see it.

This is a story about self-discovery. About fear. And about justice. It is about man who struggles to deal with his anger and his guilt and who uses those feelings to fight those who harm the innocent.

Nolan is a different kind of a film director in more ways than one, but when it comes to comic book adaptations he has changed the game.

His vision here, inspired to bring together heavy talent for comic book movies instead of cheap B-list actors. His Batman is the reason we have Robert Downey Jr. in Iron Man and Edward Norton in The Incredible Hulk. I thank him for that.

And everyone else who had a part in it.

10.title: this movie ... was absolutely amazing
10.content:
i honestly feel that this is the best batman. i was a huge fan of the original franchise (one and two that is) and how michael keaton portrayed batman back then. after keaton though, i was disgusted with val kilmer and george clooney taking the part. they just don't have the batman feel to them ..

however, Christian bale i feel did a better job then all three of the previous batman's. he was amazing in this part, in fact i would go so far as to say that this was the part he was "born" to play so to speak.

now, as for the movie itself, it was excellently done by christopher nolan. i loved his work in insomnia and memento - especially memento - but this blew my mind. it gives you a very good look at how batman .. well became batman. i mean we always knew that bruce wayne was fighting criminals because of how his parents died, but this gives you a good look as to how he learned how to fight, and a little bit more behind the whole scheme of it.

i wont say anything more, because i don't wanna ruin the movie for those who haven't seen it yet. but there's always that one sleeper movie of the summer, the one we all expect to be okay, but not the blockbuster. this absolutely owned war of the worlds .. and it will be the summer blockbuster of the year in my opinion. best movie since sin city that i have seen at least.

there better be a sequel .. and it better have Christian Bale as the new batman for this new franchise.

10 out of 10, excellently done.

10.title: Darker and Excellent.
10.content: This movie redeem all the previous ones. I just hated and loved as well the other because of the characters depicted, when all the villains were the center of the attraction in all of the prequels. Hated Clooney, Kilmer and Keaton. They didn't represent the intrinsic agony and madness of the real Batman that we all must know. Though I think that the villains before like Michelle Pfeiffer and Danny De Vito were irreplaceable because they were so good, or even a very old Nicholson to represent the Joker, in this one it lacks something that left me with something a little bitter. But the essence in this one movie it's all about Batman and that's what I liked the most. Christian Bale was terrific and has captured that real spirit of dark justice. The rest of the crew, except for a little few, were an excellent choice. I'm very sad that the Academy doesn't always think that this kind of movies should get an award in some categories like best original score more than the usual credits about the special effects, because if it would be in my hands I'll put this movie in a very high position. Director Christopher Nolan made a good job in my opinion. Enjoy it.

10.title: At last, a Batman film about Batman!
10.content:
Tim Burton's Batman films were needed at the time, they did help erase the image the 1960s series had left, but he didn't have a clue how to handle the character. Sure, he had the right atmosphere, the right sets, the right costumes, and above all, the right music with Danny Elfman's Bernard Hermannen-inspired score, but Batman remained a tortured, lonely, and uncharismatic figure. Michael Keaton was physically miscast since he couldn't pull off the annoying arrogant playboy type in Bruce Wayne, neither had the necessary physical presence to handle Batman. It sure didn't help that the villains were given more screen-time and had way more charisma. Joel Schumacer took over the series and brought it back to the 1960s camp the Burton film were trying to erase, and while he was more comfortable with the Batman character than the previous director, he didn't have a clue how to handle the atmosphere.

Well, enough with all of this, after Schumacer ruined the series completely, a re-start seemed like the smartest thing to do since none of the previous films really captured the true spirit of the character at all. And here comes Christopher Nolan, director or Memento and the Insomnia remake, to do the Batman movie fans had been waiting for a long time. Screenwriter/director David S. Goyer was in charge of the script, borrowing elements from Miller's Year One, he crafted the quintessential Batman script, avoiding all of the mistakes Sam Hamm and Akira Goldsman committed in the past.

Christian Bale takes over the role played by nearly eight actors in the past, the film opens with a runaway Bruce Wayne starting his ninja training with Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson) and his leader Ras Al Ghul (Ken Wantannabe) in the Hymalaias. As this happens, we flashback to twenty years ago, when eight-year old Bruce lost his parents to a thug (not the Joker like the first film) and swore his revenge against criminality. Bruce doesn't become Batman automatically, he nearly considers killing the murderer of his parents later on.

It's moments like Bruce throwing his gun at the sea that make Batman Begins different from nearly every previous big screen Batman representation. We finally have a film about Batman and not the villains. Not that there are no strong villains in this entry at all. Once Bruce's training is over (as he disagrees over Ras' brutal crime fighting tactics, enforcing the rule in the comics that he doesn't kill) he returns to Gotham City, which has been taken over by ruthless mob boss Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson) and his main thug Dr. Jonathan Crane (Cillian Murphy) a criminal psychiatrist who is later revealed to be the classic villain The Scarecrow. Murphy doesn't have as much screen time as Jack Nicholson or Danny DeVito, but for once we have a Batman villain that is actually menacing, a villain that doesn't dance to Prince records and doesn't wear puffy shoes and colorful costumes. His specialty of infecting his victims with fear-inducing gas gives room for some pretty nifty hallucination sequences.

Gotham City is not the studio-bound 1940s noir look by Tim Burton, neither the psychotic neon-bathed wonderland from the Joel Schumacer entries. Instead, this is a realistic city, filled with slums (the Narrows) and to an extent inspired by Ridley Scott's futuristic rain-soaked metropolis in Blade Runner, a film Nolan showed to his crew before shooting began.

Many people have criticized the action sequences for their fast editing techniques and the fact that we never see Batman, but that was pretty much the point. Batman is supposed to be a dark figure, we are not supposed to get a good look at him during the confrontations. That is not to say the film's action sequences don't deliver. While it takes its time to build up characters and situations before the rumbling begins, the bat-mobile chase puts the loud theater speakers to the test. The final action set-piece taking place inside a speeding train is better than it sounds, we finally have a good climax in a Batman film for once rather than the Dark Knight destroying the villain's lair.

In terms of acting, few films out there have a cast this good. Christian Bale is by far the definitive live-action Batman ever shown on screen, he perfectly handles the character's split personality from the snobby playboy to the Dark Knight, even the voice changes, not to mention he looks great in the costume. Morgan Freeman and Michael Cane both play good mentors to Bruce, and even knowing Cane doesn't look like the part as much as Michael Gough, he has great chemistry with Bale and we finally see their relationship sparkle. Even actors with small parts like Rutger Hauer, who plays Bruce Wayne's main enemy at Wayne Enterprises, shine. Unfortunately, Katie Holmes is the only weak link here. Script-writer Goyer took a big liberty of creating this new character who means a lot to Bruce (she was his childhood friend) especially for the movie, and while she is more interesting than the previous romantic interests in this franchise (except for Catwoman obviously) she doesn't look very comfortable in the scenes where toughness is required. And last but not least is Gary Oldman's note-by-note perfect role as Lt. Gordon, a hard-working honest cop who, like Batman, fights against corruption. For once we get to see the Batman/Gordon relationship that was never explored in the 1989/1997 film series, maybe afraid it would turn as campy as in the 1960s TV show with the Bat-phone.

Few summer blockbusters work as much as Batman Begins. Never so much fun and energy was felt in a theater since the release of Kill Bill: Volume 1 in 2003. Chris Nolan has not only resurrected a dead franchise from oblivion, but done a film few super-heroes could have the honor of having. The summer of 2005 doesn't get any better than this.

10.title: Crispin Glover
10.content:
This movie was amazing yes. 10 out of 10. we all know this by now. Now. the question is... who will be the Joker.

.... Crispin Glover.....

if not Glover.

Crispin, must be involved in this trilogy.

Do I have any seconds?

I feel the darker, more alternative, cast for this film was perfect.

The only one missing is him. Depp is knee deep in a fame he may never be able to escape.

Luckily Crispin Glover is still disturbed enough to the point where he could plan an amazing Joker... or Mad Hatter?... or damn near... any villain in this series.

10.title: The Best Superhero Movie Ever
10.content:
As a long time fan of the Batman comic, I have been waiting for a movie to get Batman right. The Tim Burton Batman's were average at best and the Schumacher Batman's were flat out terrible. Finally, a Batman movie that does not focus on the villains but on Batman. The use of the villains was excellent and Cilian Murphy was great as the Scarecrow. Cool to see Ras Al Ghul finally make the big screen. I hope they don't get into the supernatural aspect of the character as the comic book did, as this series of movies seems to be more focused on the "real world." I thought Gary Oldman not playing a psycho for once was a refreshing change and he was excellently understated as Gordon.

People have complained about there being too many villains. I thought these villains needed to be present because this was an origin story and set up the rest of the franchise with endless possibilities. People have also complained about the Rachel Dawes character. Well I was shocked at how good Katie Holmes was in this movie. I guess the Scientology has not totally messed her up.

This was the best superhero movie ever made. I am a huge fan of the Spiderman movies and I think Raimi has nailed the character, but Nolan not only nails the Batman character, he has made a real kick ass action flick to boot. I cant give this movie anything but 10 out of 10 and it has moved into my top 5 favorite movies ever.

10.title: Best Batman ever
10.content: Fantastic movie! The story tale is great, the actors are good, and the film is amazingly entertaining for anyone really into comics. Breathtaking, loaded action, a touch of feelings, and beautiful pictures. Go for it! It relates the beginning of Batman, and is pretty close to the story line that you'll find in your comics. You really got into the film, and also one might guess the outcome, the rebounding action keeps you sticked to your screen. Batman Begins has nothing much in common with it's predecessors. The film's quality, the pictures, and the content does reflect both a comics style and a good action movie's expectations.

10.title: A great epic comic book movie
10.content: Batman Begins is the best Batman movie since the underrated Batman Raturns. We see Bruce Wayne as a three dimensional character and doesn't just put out which villain will try to kill Batman next. We see the pain that Bruce Wayne must go through to become Batman. He must not only confront his own demons but the demons that are tearing Gotham City apart. This movie best resembles the comic book which it is based on. The cast is perfect with Christian Bale, Katie Holmes, Michael Caine, and Liam Neeson among others. Though the movie is nearly 2 1/2 hours in length, I was mesmerized every minute I was watching. I put Batman Begins up there with Star Wars Episode III and the underrated Kingdom of Heaven as the three best movies of the year in what has been so far a mediocre year for movies. The low box office numbers for this year have been because of the low quality in movies. I think studio executives should look at Batman Begins and see how big budget blockbusters should be made. 10/10

10.title: The best movie of the year
10.content:
This is probably the best movie of the year without any doubts. It is a complete movie and keeps you engrossed throughout the movie. It has a very good story line, very good special effects, good editing. The only thing this movie lacked was a good sound, as sometimes the sound was very feeble when the actors are talking.

Unlike War of the Worlds which had all the hype and no substance, this movie has all the substance. Wish they built the hype like War of the Worlds, then they would have got much better audience turnaround for the movie which it fully deserved. The acting is very good. The portrayal of the character 'Scarecrow' is very good, I just hope there was more of his character in the movie. But overall: A marvellous movie....Movie of the year !!!

10.title: Begin to Pick Ourselves Up From Other Films
10.content:
Why do we fall, Bruce? So we can learn to pick ourselves up again.

Lots of less than stand up Batman movies, lead to this: the beginning of the silver screen picking up the Bat.

10.title: Batboy strikes today? More than ever!
10.content: SPOILERS: Batboy is a tale as old as time. I can liken it to the heroes journey! Where the main character travels from the comfort of their home into the unknown. Michael Myers lost his parents? I feel so bad for him! So in character though! When I look at Mikey I see batboy! This movie also features same soundtrack as Will Smith in Arabian Nights by Disney??? Maybe it was Paladin? Btw, um, did you know Bluey is a show about a blue dog named Bluey. My daughter and I watch Bluey every night, and the lessons it teaches are perfect for children and adults alike. My child is an adult and I am my child. Okay so, also Angry Video game nerd insulted me one time. It made me very upset and I wish batboy was there to protect me and my sensitive ears from the verbal slander that James Rolfe (R O L F E like from Edd Ed and Edson) spat onto me. Thank you I love you.

10.title: I've seen it and it is beyond AWESOME!!!
10.content: This movie is the best film to come out all year and will probably rank as one of the best superhero movies of all time along with Superman and the first Spider-Man. The action, pace of story, and acting is top notch. Although Katie Holmes was the weak link in what is a otherwise superb cast she doesn't hurt this movie at all with her role. Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox and Michael Caine as Alfred are perfect. As for the man himself Christian Bale IS the Batman. Compared to past Batmen he owns them all!! The action sequences are well thought out. I'm definitely feeling the car chase scene with the Tumbler flying over rooftops. Cilian Murphy as Dr. Crane/Scarecrow is very good. I'm very looking forward to more Batman adventures with Christian Bale and Chris Nolan directing.

10.title: My comment of Batman begins
10.content:
Batman, this movie is quite exciting. It mainly told us how did Batman begin.Now, I am going to talk about what is this movie mainly covered.

Wayne was born in a rich family. One day, his family were murdered, he began to go around the world and think about how to exterminate those bad people.Finally, Wayne is success and the world became fair in the movie.

After I watched the movie, I discovered that this world is no longer fair and if you want to success, you must be confident and don't always trust or order others to help you. Lastly, I think this movie is excellent. The background music is perfect. Also the actors and actress are very good. Their performance is good. They know what the audience would like.

10.title: Batman Begins is the best comic book movie to date.
10.content: Batman Begins is, by far, the most successful and accessible film in the comic book movie genre. It stays true to the feel of the source material and the continuity is superb. The performances were quite impressive - particularly those given by Bale, Caine, Freeman, and Neeson. The film never misses a beat. It is interesting and informative, without becoming didactic. You aren't left with any questions once the credits roll, perhaps with the exception of "So, when is the sequel coming out?" Christopher Nolan has breathed the breath of life back into the franchise, eight years after the release of the disappointing and over-the-top "Batman and Robin".

10.title: An amazing rebirth of Batman
10.content: Without going on and on about the specifics of the movie(WATCH IT YOURSELF!) let me just say the feeling of walking out of that theater is something I haven't felt in awhile and from a Batman movie no less! Christopher Nolan has taken the Batman franchise and set new standards for writing and direction in this genre. Whether you agree with the storyline or not, you must recognize how well this film was made. I loved the fact that Batman is not this cartoon character for kids anymore, this was a grown-up film with a great sense of realism. Christian Bale is outstanding as the lead, I can't compare him to Michael Keaton but I can put him in the same boat for sure. The best thing about this film in my opinion is how the movie draws the audience in. At the risk of sounding too cheesy, Batman Begins appeals to and engages all the senses with its sound, action and cinematography that absorbs you into the movie. Definitely worth your time in watching which is hard to say for many films these days.

10.title: In depth look at how Batman came to be
10.content:
Christian Bale is an ACE!(besides being a total heartthrob)...Finally, some back story and explanation for how Batman came to be. Besides being action packed, which gives all of the classic Batman fans what they need, there is a real plot besides a homicidal maniac creating chaos in Gotham City. Be prepared for a very dark storyline that follows Bruce Wayne on his path from childhood, through his training, to when he finally becomes Batman.

Christian's portrayal of Batman is unique and oppressive (as he was meant to be). The voice changeover from Bruce Wayne to Batman is very dramatic and effective, a really vivid metaphor for the two characters he plays. Batman is as we have never seen him, dark, oppressive, and terrifying (but in a good way). You are also sympathetic, as you are drawn into the character of Bruce Wayne. Be prepared to be sucked into this story, and anticipate a new beginning for the character Batman to appeal to interest more than the villains. The best Batman movie I have ever seen, Christian is a surprising, but inspired choice! Hope to see more, and hopefully Batman will stay as intriguing in any sequels as he was in this movie.

10.title: Excellent!!! Just plain and simple excellent !!!
10.content:
Well, I always loved the Batman movies. But in the later years, as I grew up, I have found them more and more over the top comic book like. Okay,Batman IS originally a comic book, but they tried too much to make a cartoon out of a real movie. Especially when it came to the villains.

Don't get me wrong, I laughed my head off, at Jim Carey as The Riddler, and Tomy Lee Jones was okay as Twoface. and And Jack Nicholson as The Joker was excellent, even Arnold was okay. But Danny Devito's The Penguin, made me want to puke. As always, Danny did a good job, but the character almost destroyed the movie with its outrageously disgusting parody of a comic book villain.

Well, enough about the old ones. Batman Beginns, Is on an entirely other level of quality. The plot is extremely much more thought through. Every detail has been made more believable. Especially how Bruce Wayne came to be Batman. To my great joy, they dropped the more or less psychotic avenger attitude of the previous Batmans. Here is at last, a sane Bruce Wayne!!!! The guy who played him, did an excellent job portraying a person who actually manages to defeat his inner demons. All right, there sure is an element of vengeance in his fight against crime. But his main motivation is to do something with what has happened to his beloved city. He like his father, sees the pain and suffering of other people, and does what he can to help.

Ironically it is the main villain who helps him become a whole person, who learns him how to discern vengeance from justice. That being said, Liam Neeson was incredible as an villain. He perfectly portrayed a person who in a way had noble intents, but who had strayed off the path, and into madness. It was this example that showed Bruce how not to be. Liam's character had let himself be consumed by vengeance, whereas Bruce thanks to seeing that, managed to stay on the right track.

I must say that when I first saw Liam, I gave a inward sigh. I should have known better, but I highly doubted he would be able to portray a villain, as he always seem to be some sort of a "hero". But his characterization hit bulls eye. I actually shuddered in discomfort a few times, from seeing the fanatic madness, of his character. In my opinion, he is by far the best Batman villain so far.

There is not much to say about Kate. She did the job in a good but not very memorable way, and I think that she looked much too young to have the kind of job she had.

Gary Oldman on the other hand, did the best characterization of Commissioner(I know he wasn't that yet in this movie) Gordon, to date. It always amazes me to see how much of a chameleon this actor is. If you see this movie, and then you see The Fifth Element It is almost unbelievable that it is the same actor who plays Zorg and Gordon.

Morgan Freeman is one of those actors that hightens the quality of a movie simply by being there. And so it was in this movie to. He has this PRECENSE on screen, that very few can duplicate. He managed to make this in fact very small role, into one of the major characters of the movie.

The butler. I am sorry to say I don't know the name of the actor. But I was glad to see that they had kept true to the only realistic character of the old movies. Although there was a new actor, he managed to pick up right where the former was, with his characterization of a loyal butler, who becomes sort of a surrogate father to Bruce. And this time we got to see more clearly the deep friendship that was between the two of them. Alfred, really was more of a dear family member, than an employee.

I am sorry, I seem to have taken off completely here. I'll try to stop now. JUST RUN TO THE NEAREST CINEMA AND SEE THIS MOVIE. THIS IS WITHOUT DOUBT THE BEST BATMAN MOVIE EVER!!!!!!!!!!!!!

And think of this! They are already planning a new one! I sure as anything will be there!!!

Well, thats all folks.

10.title: Batman's Back
10.content:
Batman is back and he does not suck. These are good things. This movie does the first two movies justice. While in parts it might reflect a non-super hero movie, it is something the series needed. This movie never lets you forget that Batman is indeed just a man trying his best to make Gotham a better place.

I thought that Nolan did an excellent job of directing. It was good to see a gritty and subdued Gotham and not something all lit up in neon and weirdoes. Just a dark city, filled with corrupt people, good old bad guys, mobsters and some good people, covered in wetness and darkness, which is more real life. Bale does a great job of playing playboy Bruce Wayne when he needs to, and switches to his more hard core persona of Batman. They felt like two different men. Well done.

10.title: Christopher Nolan
10.content: I was very angry when the image of Batman, who was originally directed by genius Tim Burton, was almost destroyed by Joel Schumacher with Batman and Robin. When I heard about that there was to be a movie number 5, Batman Returns, I wasn't sure what to expect. Could the image of Batman be saved? Director Christopher Nolan has made a masterpiece. Batman Begins is without any doubt the best Batman-movie, and that's coming from a big Tim Burton fan. He managed to let the audience watch the movie without thinking of the horrible movie the came before it. He goes his own, new ways in making Batman Begins and made, like I said, a masterpiece which I don't think can ever be matched (That is, in making Batman movies). I hope they will make another movie with Nolan. He has restored my faith in the Batman movies. Batman is my favorite hero and I would just like to thank Christopher Nolan for make this movie. Thank you.

10.title: The Best Movie Of The Year So Far
10.content:
There was a lot of speculation on how Batman Begins was going to turn out. All I heard from people before the opening was how the people working on this movie were going to make this worse than the others. Well, let me tell ya folks everybody who thought the movie was gonna be a bomb and be as bad as the others was dead wrong. Batman Begins is the best batman to come out, and it is also my favorite movie of the year so far.

A lot of people said that this movie dragged on. Oh it did not drag on at all. It kept my interest the whole film. I was disappointed to see the credits roll. I've seen all the batman movies and I'm usually bored halfway through, but not this one. This movie will keep you hooked because it combines drama with action, while all the other batman's just had mindless action and dumb plots. It really shows in this batman that the producers, writers, and director took their time in making this film and making those years that it took them to put it together pay off. This movie also shows that you can make excellent sequels in Hollywood if you JUST TAKE YOUR TIME. Apparently most writers and directors don't hear that and just rush a movie and make it only a one year gap from the previous film. Us movie goers do not need a sequel year after year, but apparently in Hollywood they think we do.

Christian Bale is magnificent as Batman. It seems like he was made to play batman. He is built like batman, and he has that same gruff voice as Keaton had when he was batman. He really nails it when it comes to this role. At first I was kind of worried that he was playing batman but my worries were put to rest after i saw the movie. I prefer the story line but a lot of parents will not want to take their younger kids to see this as it is a little frightening and dark. Also kids will not like the length of the movie because it is close to two and half hours. But for all you who have no problem with the darker story or the length then get out and go see this movie.

10.title: Batman Begins
10.content: Before going to see this movie i was a bit unsure of what to expect, After the woeful 'Batman and Robin' this film was surly going to be an improvement?! My apprehensions were laid to rest though because this film was excellent from start to finish. This Batman film is actually about BATMAN and focuses more on how and why Bruce Wayne became the caped crusader. The cast is excellent with Morgan freeman and Michael Caine in top form but the real star is Christian bale, who gives a very realistic and dark performance as Batman. The fight scenes are excellent, the story is fantastic, this is how comic book films should be made!!

10.title: The foundation of the Dark Knight!
10.content:
As a kid, you love everything about Batman. You know he's Bruce Wayne, he's a billionaire, he has the Batmobile, the Bat Cave, a butler... he is Batman! But, as you get older, you ask HOW did he get to becoming 'Batman'??

Well, that is where the genius work of Chris Nolan comes in where he breaks down and gives you the answers of how Batman really becomes BATMAN!

This is a brilliant story and movie from the ground up of Bruce Wayne's troubled upbringing and how he fits into a society of mistrust and crime.

From start to finish, this creation of Batman is satisfying and makes you say, "ah, I see now...". No one else could gave done a better job than Nolan with this movie!

10.title: All the four previous movies should have been like this one...
10.content:
Excellent movie, astonishing atmosphere with very good music, the city is dark and frightening as it should be, the villains are fearful, the story is above the average of nowadays comics adaptations. Acting is very good, Michael Caine-Morgan Freeman doubles is just unbeatable, Christian Bale is just perfect, as always, and even Katie Holmes is convincing as a DEA prosecutor. For me the best was Cilian Murphy: I scared my pants of the face and those eyes of the young psychiatrist...

Two thumbs up, it really worths the money for the ticket. I am looking forward to the DVD release. Call me a fool, but Tim Burton should go and take lessons from Christopher Nolan...

10.title: Finally, a Batman Movie.
10.content:
If you go to this movie and you are a die-hard comic book Batman fan you will not be disappointed.

If you liked the previous Batman movies, you will probably be surprised how much better this take on Batman truly is.

But if you even thought that Batman should stayed the way it was previously portrayed through the Tim Burton versions, you should probably spend some time visiting a nearby bookstore that sells graphic novels and real some of the better graphic novels before continuing with this review.

Why?

Because this movie is perhaps what most die-hard Batman comic book fans wanted the first time around. A big reason may be that for at least the last 15 years the writing for the Batman comic books have been very edgy and in many ways far more cerebral than what Tim Burton gave us way back when. Batman is considered the "Dark Knight" and also the "detective" -- the everyman forged by circumstances and haunted by a past of regret and misfortune to become something more than the mere law enforcement crime fighter.

Does this make it as carefree and enjoyable as, say, MR. AND MRS. SMITH? Maybe not. But satisfying?

Yes.

The campiness that was evident in the comedic Batman series of old was not something that most of these diehards probably care for nor desire to see in their superhero.

And why would they? After seeing what graphic novels could truly become through the works of Frank Miller's THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS, BATMAN YEAR ONE, and Alan Moore's THE WATCHMEN (not a Batman storyline but something quite exceptional and worth mentioning), it seems that the expectations of Batman was to create something edgy, that was in many ways based in reality and above all, brooding and logical.

That is what we get when we see BATMAN BEGINS -- a somewhat realistic storyline that explains via the many cause-and-effect events why a young man suffering the haunting death of his family would find no other recourse than to don a batsuit and prowl the night.

This is not a film that is so fantastical nor focused on the weirdness of the badguys (the previous movies should have really been titled, JOKER, PENGUIN, and THE RIDDLER, not BATMAN since Batman was really more of an afterthought of the series not the real focus of the stories). Rather BATMAN BEGINS is really the first cinematic story about BRUCE WAYNE, who is also BATMAN.

And that makes this story far more overdue and interesting than what came before.

What haunts the entire premise of Batman is in fact the question of WHY:

Why would someone even consider donning a cape and all to fight evil?

Why would a billionaire who supposedly has so much money and therefore influence, still resort to such means?

Why wouldn't he simply try to inspire community development via civic activities?

Why wouldn't he take the Capra-esquire view and become a philanthropist -- giving away his money to the needy like MR. DEEDS GOES TO WASHINGTON?

Why not simply use his money to become influential within the court system to try to fight justice that way?

And how does one exorcise one's demons if one lives with the guilt that one may have contributed to one's own parents' death?

How would he face his fears?

Would he allow his personal hatred to warp his mind, to make him weak, and transform himself into the very thing he despises? Does he become the cowardly lot that he despises due to his intense hatred? Yes. We see this in the story and how it took the dignity and outrage of those he loves to snap him out of his cowardly ways.

All of these questions are addressed in a very logical manner. And as a result it becomes a very analytical view of the nature of man.

WHY is the question being asked in the movie -- something the filmmaker does an incredible job answering.

Why does one man become a criminal and another a crime fighter? What kind of roll models such as RA'S AL GHUL and the LEAGUE OF SHADOWS provide young Wayne, and why do the ninja suits that Ghul's forces use, make it almost inevitable that young Wayne would create the Batsuit? Why does the rhetoric of Ghul's henchman, DUCARD, make it logical for Wayne to choose a Bat as his persona?

In the comic book world, Batman is considered the "modern" detective -- a thinking man (but also fallible) who, by his own force of will and intellect -- wages a war against the darker aspects of humanity.

BATMAN BEGIN succeeds because it never forgets this fact.

10.title: The Best Batman Film Ever
10.content:
this film is definitely one of the best superhero movies of all time. It's not the best I've seen (spiderman 2 gets that place) but it was flawless. the music was good, the acting was good, the writing is a masterpiece. it seems so believable that this could really happen that you feel like you could do it yourself. the gadgets are awesome, now I'm not a fan of batman since batman beyond went off the air, but I could watch this film over and over again. the writing is good because what you don't expect is what is coming and a recurring theme and difficult problem will make you think "how the hell is he gonna get out of this?"

this movie is great, if you like batman, superheros, or just a good flick, check out this master piece.

10.title: What chance does Gotham have, when the good people do nothing?
10.content:
What can I say that hasn't been said already? I can say "WOW", but does it carry the same emotion that everyone else speaks about? I don't know, but for me, this was the best summer blockbuster that I have seen in 2005. Christopher Nolan has done his homework, stayed true to dark, graphic stories that follow this hero, and set in place a cast that equally carry the weight of this film on their shoulders. I remember saying to a friend that the reason this film worked was because of the cast. In previous Batman films, we struggled between the over-acting of some, the celebrity status of others, and some that were just plain goofy, but now Nolan has given us a cast that carries this film into a whole new ballgame. They want to be there, they want to embody their characters, they want to give birth to this Dark Knight, and they do. When I first heard about this film being in the pipeline, I was concerned about Christian Bale taking on such a role that has been demolished by the heavy-hitters of Hollywood. Could he do it? I had faith in him, but did everyone else? Apparently they did, because he is the most powerful representation of this tortured figure ever to come out of comic book Hollywood. I applaud his work, appreciated his toned down approach, and cannot wait for him to come back and prove that he is this winged freak.

Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Rutger Hauer, Tom Wilkinson, the AMAZING Cillian Murphy, Linus Roache, and Ken Watanabe. With names like this you know that you are walking into greatness. I was worried at first about Caine as Alfred, but with the greatest of ease he turned what could have been the comic character of the film into this powerful voice of Wayne's conscious. It was incredible.

While I give so much credit to the actors, I need to equally pay respect to Christopher Nolan. Not since Sin City did I feel like I was watching a graphic novel, a comic, come alive on screen. His ability to frame each shot like a moment in the books, create these breathing characters that you can actually believe exist, as well as tell a story that has been corrupted by the Hollywood recycling machine takes talent and Nolan did it. I have been a huge fan of everything that Nolan has touched. I used to give Memento out for free at the video store just so people could experience the magic that he has. I was a fan of Insomnia and even Followers. I get excited to see his work because it changes with each picture. You never know what you are going to get when you watch a Nolan film, but you can guess that it will be dark and come from his heart. I saw it in his earlier films and it shined brightly in Batman Begins.

If I had to say anything negative about the film (which is hard to do) there would be two aspects that I would mention. The first is Katie Holmes. I just didn't like her character. She was underdefined and basically eye-candy for the younger Dawson's Creek audience members. She was worthless, perhaps it was the Tom Cruise media mud-bath that seems to have ruined our newspapers these days, but she just felt plain to me. She didn't make the cut. Then, there were times where you could tell that Bale was really forcing a grumbly American accent. Nothing too wrong with this, but it just felt forced. These were minor insecurities that I had with this overall brilliant film.

Outstanding. Perhaps that is a better word for it. I could see this film again and again. From the opening frame to the final moments of battle I was pulled from my theater seat directly into the film. No other Batman film has done that for me. I remember falling in love with Keaton as the Dark Knight, but I think Bale even gave him a run for his money. Nolan created the perfect tone and story for our disturbed hero. He took the goofy elements from Burton, erased Kilmer/Clooney, and brought us back to our roots. This film was perfection on a stick.

Grade: ***** out of *****

10.title: Achievement
10.content:
To turn a cheesy hero comic into a serious film with serious and dark characters is an incredible achievement not really surprising from the director of Memento and insomnia. Katie Holmes suits the part well however it is a little typical in terms of female heroins in comic book adaptations which is a shame as I am sure she is a very capable actress. Christian Bale as usual plays his part brilliantly bringing his own uniqueness to the character, Equilibrium, American psycho. The fight scenes are badly filmed and unclear but this was done on purpose I feel as the badly choreographed fight scenes from previous batman films which look like they belong more on stage than on screen would not fit this film at all, the batman depicted here who flies in grabs an enemy and is gone within seconds really supports the idea of the character using fear against foes.

The main villains were excellent which is not always the case when trying to adapt comic characters to film but the scarecrow is really very cleverly put to screen. Its a shame that there's not really a lot more room for a sequel without going forward after the whole bat girl and robin thing but perhaps they could squeeze one in before the joker in the initial batman film.

If you like the original more sinister batman films and are a fan of clever comic book adaptations you wont want to miss out on this.

10.title: Please make a sequel!!
10.content:
Having been disappointed time and again by Hollywood's interpretations of not only Batman, but superhero's in general I was very skeptical going into this movie. There have been a few good superhero movies over the years (most recently Marvel's Spider-Man movies), but this movie is now at the top of my favorite's list! Great writing, wonderful acting, an amazing cast... and they even managed to make the Scarecrow scary!! Thankfully the apple HAS fallen far from the tree w/this installment of the Batman story. I did love Tim Burton's original Batman film, but this is a much more serious look at Bruce Wayne and his alter-ego, Batman. To the creators credit, they didn't employ any of the tactics used by Joel Schumacher, who single handedly dismantled the Batman Franchise in the 1990's.

Wonderful movie! Please tell your friends to go see it so that the studio will recognize the demand for a sequel!

10.title: Batman Begins Truimphs over the past 4
10.content: I was always a fan of batman. After batman and robin came out, i always felt as though the movies were never about batman in the first place, but rather about the villains. that past movies actually did a poor job in explaining The Batman. Finally, Nolan comes along and delivers the best batman flick yet. Though its not as dark as Burton's BATMAN RETURNS, this movie wins all votes in all the bat-movies. Finally after 7 years, Nolan puts the stop to the campy batman that Joel Schumacher started getting into. This movie has it all, a completely amazing cast, Christian bale does a beyond wonderful job as Bruce Wayne/batman. Katie Holmes in my opinion was great, Gary Oldman was the perfect Gordon and Micheal Caine did a great job as Alfred. Most people do say that this movie went along too slow and that batman doesn't appear till the 2nd half of the movie, well its Bruce's life and it talks about how he develops in this symbol and so this is acceptable. Batman Begins is a beautiful film created by Nolan and Goyer, it really brings the batman character to life at last.

10.title: DC Should Be Proud of Themselves
10.content: Finally, DC is back in the race to make good comic-based movies. After horrible movies like the Spider-Man, X-Men, and Blade franchises, DC comics finally decided that it was their turn. I was sceptical at first, because I had the idea that Marvel had already saturated (and completely ruined) the comic-based movie market. But perfect casting got me really excited several months before it was even released. Christian Bale stepped out from his role of Patrick Bateman in American Psycho, and played a completely different kind of psycho, a vigilante. Gary Oldman (Hannibal, Fifth Element, Air-Force One), in a rare "good guy" role, made Jim Gordon a supporting cast member, rather than just an annoying fat guy to call Batman whenever he failed at his job (like the previous Gordons in the other Batman movies). Supporting roles from Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Rutger Hauer, and Katie Holmes made Bruce an important aspect of Batman's life, as well as added to the movie's star-power. The villains of the movie, Ken Watanabe (Last Samurai), Cillian Murphy (28 Days Later), and Liam Neeson (Star Wars) were absolutely perfect. Not only did the director (Christopher Nolan) embrace the classic ideas of the characters and their stories, but he also added to them, making them extremely realistic and very believably scary at the same time.
