The best part of the movie was definitely the directing style. Nolan, previously directing Insomnia and the cult-classic Memento, captured everything that is so alluring about the Batman universe. Casting was brilliant, the screenplay was original and heartfelt, and the overall mood of the movie was just plain epic. The characters of the comics came to life on the big screen, and made the viewer care what was going to happen to them. The chemistry was there, and this would have to be not only the best movie of the year, the best batman adaptation ever, and the best comic-based movie in a long time, but quite possibly, one of the best movies ever made. Props to Hollywood for not blowing this one, and props to DC for finally putting Marvel in their place, showing that you don't need super-powers and stupid jokes to make a good comic-based movie. The only thing I didn't like about Batman Begins, was the lack of things to complain about in the movie. I went in, expecting another flop like Batman & Robin, but was disappointed with the twists, the turns, and the overall excitement that never left me throughout the entire film. I think the best part about the entire movie for me, was the closing scene. Gordon looks at Batman, after assembling the Batsignal, and tells him that there is a new freak in town, leaving a calling card. It's joker. Batman leaps off the building top, and Gordon stops him, saying that he never thanked him. Batman looks at him, partially smiles, and then proceeds to tell him that he'll never have to. Anyone that dislikes this movie obviously fell asleep or just plain didn't see it. It is flawless in every way, and I am planning on going to see it again very soon. Hope to see you there. 10/10

10.title: FINALLY: The Real Batman
10.content:
WARNING: This review contains spoiler material. If you have not seen "Batman Begins", I must insist that you do not read this. "Begins" is a great film, but you can only get the full effect if the entire story is fresh to you.

I have been a Batman fan all my life. When I was a baby, my mom got me a Batman pajama set (complete with cape). I was three when the 1989 film came out, and I was hooked on Batman from that point on. And now, 16 years later, that film has finally been surpassed...

Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale, American Psycho) witnesses his parents' murder at the hands of Joe Chill (Richard Brake, Cold Mountain), a "desperate" criminal who loses his cool during while trying to mug the Waynes.

After several years of ninja training under crime lord Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe, The Last Samurai) and Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson, Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace), Wayne returns with his butler Alfred (Michael Caine, The Cider House Rules) to a overly-corrupt Gotham.

While leading his life as the beneficiary of Wayne Enterprises, run by power-hungry Richard Earle (Rutger Hauer, 'Salem's Lot), he forms his crime-fighting persona with the help of Alfred and Wayne Enterprises Applied Scienctist Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman, The Shawshank Redemption). He puts his fear of bats to his advantage, and becomes The Batman.

The Batman teams with police sergeant James Gordon (Gary Oldman, Bram Stoker's Dracula) to fight crime boss Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson, Normal) and demented psychiatrist Dr. Jonathan "The Scarecrow" Crane (Cillian Murphy, 28 Days Later).

The film also stars Katie Holmes (Dawson's Creek) as Wayne's love interest Rachel Dawes, Linus Roache (The Forgotten) as Thomas Wayne, and Mark Boone Junior (Memento) as corrupt police sergeant Flass. "Begins" is directed by acclaimed filmmaker Christopher Nolan (Memento), and written by Batman-comic alum David Goyer (The Blade Trilogy).

This film is everything a Bat-fan could want, and has an ending that both takes your breath away and sets up the sequels flawlessly.

I give "Batman Begins" a solid and relentless 10 out of 10 (more like an eleven!)

10.title: Best Movie You'll see this year....
10.content:
i have great respect for the Batman series and i went to see the movie with a little doubt. After all, this isn't Christopher Nolan directorial territory, and i've seen bale in only one movie before(shaft).

It's hard to describe how great and amazing this movie is without revealing a little of the plot, but i'll try my best...

This is the best Batman ever made, it even beats the tim burton version (which was my fav. till BB showed up), all the actors delivered top-notch performances and were bringing their A-Game along with them.

Bale is a perfect Batman. He truly portrayed him as the tormented, dark, and troubled character that batman really is and i hope that he remains true to the project and that there are many more batman movies for him in the future(with Chris Nolan of course) So, finally, if you're a batman fan, this is a must-see movie and even if u want an action adventure movie with a great cast and great acting this is the summer movie for you.

10.title: Christian Bale is Batman.
10.content: To my surprise I have to say this is now my favorite Batman movie yet. Why? Simply put, they finally have cast the right guy to be Batman, a Batman that can stand tall and carry the movie without the help of overly flashy villains who simply say one liners and have stupid plans that really go nowhere. Bale is great as the caped crusader as he actually looks the part both in face and in stature. It also helps that he has the voice for it as he doesn't have to whisper to sound tough. Sure Keaton has his backers, but he gets to many points simply because he was the first (though he was better than Kilmer and Clooney). We have an interesting plot here about how the Batman came into being and believe me he is first and foremost in this flick. The villains are good, perfect casting for the Scarecrow and he is like the comic book, but never does he overact and try to steal the show he is just an element of the plot. All the actors here were good, the story was good, simply put this was Batman as the Dark Knight, and yes this movie was dark. In fact, a bit more darker and an R rating might have been more appropriate. The action is great as no longer does it rely mainly on computer generated graphics, but more on stunts. The city of Gotham also looked great as it looked like a real city rather than a caricature of one with all the action taking place on one obvious set or another (ala the last two Batman movies). A nice twist was thrown in here and there as well, though I thought it was headed in the direction it went. The Batmobile looked rather cool too, it matched the one of the first and second movie in that it looked like a real vehicle rather than just a big toy. So if you go see this Batman, don't look for a goofy embarrassing comedy, but rather a sleek, dark movie more reminiscent of the Batman in the comic books.

10.title: The Dark Knight Detective Is Back! And Thank God (and Christoper Nolan) For It!
10.content:
Batman Begins is the starting point for a new filmic franchise featuring the venerable and venerated Caped Crusader, and it is, most likely, and in this humble reviewer's opinion, the best depiction of Batman and his mythos ever put to celluloid.

Director Christopher Nolan and screenwriter David S. Goyer flesh out the origin and pathos of Bruce Wayne and his rise to the self-styled guardian of the grim and gritty metropolis of Gotham City. Finally, the audience is given a glimpse of Bruce's world travels and training in the fighting arts. We see when, how, and why Bruce Wayne chose to don the cape and cowl of the World's Greatest Detective.

Batman Begins is a realistic, firmly-planted-on-the-ground depiction of the early career of Batman and his alter ego's recapture of the financial empire established by his murdered parents. It is a subtle, almost low-key film, with the obligatory fighting and explosions, but more of a character study why a man would chose to fight crime dressed as a bat.

Christian Bale is Batman, just like Christopher Reeve was Superman and Tobey Maguire is Spider-Man. He embodies the triune role of the real Bruce Wayne, a tortured soul yearning for justice, the public Bruce Wayne, a foppish, slurred playboy, and the Batman, a frightening force of nature vowed to rid his city of evil and injustice. Bale brings all of those aspects to life, physically, mentally, and emotionally.

Of the supporting cast, the true highlights are Michael Caine as the stalwart, fatherly Alfred the butler, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Wayne Enterprises' Applied Sciences Head turned steward of the family company, and the best of all, Gary Oldman as Police Sgt. James Gordon, Batman's staunchest, albeit originally reluctant, ally in his war on crime. Oldman looks and sounds just like all comics' fans' idea of what Gordon should look and sound like. Gordon is also given something to do this time in a Batman film, and in the end, helps to literally save the day. The creation of the unlikely partnership between the Dark Knight and Jim Gordon is a linchpin of this film, and is a moving and integral part to the movie.

The villains are not over-the-top neon-colored weirdos. They are realistic people played by Cillian Murphy as the corrupt psychiatrist Dr. Jonathan Crane and Liam Neeson as the duplicitous Ducard/Ra's al Ghul. Murphy is very good as the slimy and creepy Crane/Scarecrow, and Neeson is as great as ever as the true "Demon's Head." The true villainous standout is Tom Wilkinson's turn as mobster Carmine Falcone, the last of Gotham's "normal" bad guys before the city becomes plagued by Batman's unique and grotesque rogue's gallery.

There are few things to complain about in Batman Begins. If I had one complaint it would be that we didn't see enough farther shots of Batman fighting hand-to-hand, making the action quick and hard to follow. As for Katie Holmes' Rachel Dawes, I think she did a good job with what she had, and you can't really fault her for that.

The last scene of Batman Begins sets up not just a sequel but a true film series. Batman, summoned by the now Lt. Gordon and his Bat-Signal, and Gordon firmly establish their alliance, and we see that the "theatricality" of the Batman's modus operandi has inadvertently brought forth a new crop of criminals, one who Gordon reveals leaves as a calling card, a Joker.

As Batman gets to work, Gordon tells him, "I never said thank you." Batman's reply, "And you'll never have to."

And that, my friends, pretty much says it all. Batman Begins is one the best comic book/superhero adaptations ever created, and those of you that have shied away, still smarting from the not-so-great Bat-films from '92 to '97, do not fear. Batman Begins is so much better and so much more.

Highest Recommendation!

10.title: If it weren't a comic book
10.content: OK, so it's not likely to ever actually occur in real life, but if the Batman story were "based on a true story", it would have to resemble this version a hundred times more than any other Batman-based theatrical release or television show before it. Many of the previously taken-for-granted aspects of Batman/Bruce Wayne's motives, abilities, and "tools-of-the-Batman-trade" are explained in as reasonable a fashion as they ever could be. Casting for the lead is perfect, with the expertly-earnest Christian Bale believably obsessed with his mission, buff enough to succeed at the athletic aspects of being a super-hero, and attractive & charming enough to pull off the playboy cover identity. The fight scenes are more true-to-life than most films, letting the action get lost in a blur of confusion rather than over-defining the technical details made me feel as if I was in the middle of the action. The movie-ending first mention of "The Joker",(of the presumed sequel),has me on pins and needles. Apparently there is much speculation about who will play the Joker. Whoever is cast will have his hands full making the character as insane as he needs to be while not seeming silly in the more "adult" format. I'd hope for extensive biographical work to explain Joker as well as Batman has been explained here.

10.title: Epic Comic Movie For People Who Don't Like Comic Movies
10.content: I'm pretty much obsessed with comic book movies. I've bought every Marvel film released over th last few years and always eagerly look forward to the next ones. Of course, I was anxious to see how Batman Begins turned out as well. As much of a fan of comics and comic movies as I am, I was weary of the new Batman release suffering the same fate as all its predecessors. Michael Keaton is just too much of a bitch to play the dark knight, and Joel Schumacher's interpretation made Adam West look like General Patton. The new movie however is great. And more so, its well made with a great storyline. Even if you aren't a particular fan of comics you should enjoy this movie. It just might be the greatest comic film released to date.

10.title: best bat film ever two thumbs way up
10.content: I won't try to spoil anything but overall the movie was better than any batman movie before, and even if it had no batman in it at all it was still awesome.i lied spoilers ahead the end of the film is when not Sgt but Lt. Gordon gives the signal to batman and he basically asks what he could do for Gotham, and he tells him about a double homicide that was committed, and that the man jumps from building to building, he wears a mask also and he leaves a calling card! behind and i was flipping out at this point and if your a complete idiot at this point and don't get the calling card idea Gordon shows it to batman and the card is an ace of spades just kidding the card is a joker! but who will be the joker? that is the question.

10.title: At long last, Justice is served for a Batman film
10.content:
There is a part of me that is at odds with most movie goers. My opinion of the Batman films starting from 1989 is not just that the last two were bad, but that they were all bad. Burton and Shumacher's vision of Batman and my vision are just too different, I suppose, and while I appreciate a number of Burton's films, I was rather convinced the Batman franchise would simply never amount to true greatness (Nicholson's usual stellar performance notwithstanding).

Sometimes, being wrong is the most wonderful thing in the world.

The journey of Bruce Wayne is a great way to introduce one of the most recognizable comic icons of the last century. The contrast between this and introducing him as a fully suited Batman is a stark one, and is reminiscent of an older method of telling stories which has unfortunately declined in the last couple decades. What is truly inspired is that the bat doesn't really appear until about halfway into the film, leaving character development to take precedence.

That is not to say that Bruce Wayne unfolds perfectly before the viewer's eyes. The film manages to set up some major "bullet points" of Wayne's life story and for that it deserves credit. Yet somehow, there was just something missing. It is quite possible that Bale and Holmes never made a real connection or chemistry, upon which much of the personality growth of Wayne rests. Whatever the reason, this didn't quite work. The cast was generally excellent, with the legendary Liam Neeson stealing the show as usual. This one particular element is the only hitch.

One final criticism. Perhaps it is just an inherent flaw in Batman when it comes to film, but I just couldn't take it seriously when Bruce Wayne in the Batman costume appeared on screen. The action sequences were fine. Watching a guy in a bat mask deliver serious dialog, however, just looked silly no matter what context I tried to place it. Perhaps it is possible to make a more serious looking bat suit, but this one was too comical to suspend my disbelief.

Don't let the little flaws ruin a great film. Batman has finally been done right.

10.title: Dark, Gritty, Violent. The film Batman should be.
10.content:
After 1997's "Batman & Robin" you would think the Bat would have run its movie course but this has changed all that with a restart to the franchise and giving the Bat new wings, Memento director Christopher Nolan gives the Batman franchise new hope.

Set in the early years of Millionaire Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale), a man scarred by witnessing his parents murder as a child and traumatized by Bats by falling into a cave of them. He has traveled the world with such hatred and anger for criminals he ends up under the wing of Ducard (Liam Neeson), a man who is a part of a cult who bring justice to the guilty in their own way. Trained in the martial arts, Bruce heads back to his home of Gotham City. A city that taken his mother and father years ago. With the help of loyal butler Alfred (Michael Caine), Gotham City's last decent cop Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman) and Wayne Enterprises employee Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman), Bruce transforms into the legend Batman. A night stalker who strikes fear into the hearts of Gothams underworld when the police wont do nothing. But the rise of a drug lord who is threatening Gotham's water supply and endangers the life of Bruce Waynes childhood sweetheart Rachel Dawes.

It seems Comic Book adaptations are being done right e.g. Spiderman 1 & 2, Sin City, X Men and Daredevil (Directors cut underrated). And we have those that are laughable like Catwoman which is a poor excuse for a movie.

The casting in this is to die for: Christian Bale (The dark knight is played perfect down to a tee) Morgan Freeman (Everything that hes in) Gary Oldman (For once not a villain) Liam Neeson (Very good role) and Katie Holmes (Very underrated actress) and a host of other brilliant actors, Check out the IMDb cast list to see.

A very very gritty movie indeed. Joel Schumacher may have killed Fortever and Batman and Robin but Chris Nolan is now one of my favorite directors. The dark knight simply hasn't looked so good.

10/10

It's not just a great comic book film, or a great action film, or a great adventure film, or a great gangster film, or a great noir film. It's just a great film. Chris Nolan can do anything, it seems, and I look forward with great pleasure to see what he's up to. 10.title: The Blade Runner of comic book movies!
10.content: I have seen this movie twice now. The first time I saw it I thought it was a movie of two disparate halves. The first, all origin story, I thought was too slow and clunky; the second half, my favourite, all action and emotion. I was reminded of Superman the movie in fact, a film I can only watch after skipping the first forty-five minutes. After a second viewing of Batman Begins though, I appreciated the beginning much more . I see it now as a cohesive brilliant whole with tight, clever dialogue, powerful lingering images, stirring music (like Superman I came out of the cinema humming the main theme to my myself), great acting across the board (yes even from Katie Holmes!) and enlivened with rousing, glorious action set pieces. I mentioned Blade Runner in my summary. That masterpiece is clearly an influence on Nolan; the hard, gritty look of the city, the old school special effects (no Playstation-like imagery here).I think Nolan may even have sneaked in a few Blade Runner homages in the shape of the hot-dog stand guy, the cyclists weaving through the smoggy streets of the Narrows. In fact one of the distant shots of that place had me grinning like the Joker himself! But I do Mr Nolan a bit of a disservice here. His film is a major achievement in itself. Quite simply, it is the best film I have seen since The Matrix and like that fine film, fully expect it to be regarded as a modern classic!

10.title: Great MOVIE...get it MOVIE...not prequel, sequel, weird spin off....You have to watch it....truly one of the best this year

Excellent movie overall with a great cast

The story was believable, enjoyable and perfect for a theater experience. It may not have been wholly true to the comics but as a movie by itself, it was good...perfect in almost every way..Much better then the previous Batman attempts made... They not only chose an outstanding actor and supporting actors but great characters and story lines... Absolutely loved the experience and felt the chills a good movie should have...not many have had those...even better-excuse me- than ROTS and thats as a star wars fan...

Downs There are some awkward dialogue like throwaway lines BUT the pacing of the movie was PERFECT...The plot had its twists but wasn't too hard to follow and made one hardly realize time passed by...I was shocked that it had been over 2 hours...Really hardly felt like such... Acting ...was good although I like many felt wasted talent...the bad jokes could have been replaced with supporting character development such as Fox(used disappointingly, only as a tech guy-, and Gordan and the villains, Falconi got put away too quick and there wasn't enough of a back story for The crazed fear obsessed Dr. Crane, however a great and chilling villain, had a foggy background as there was no discernible drive...Falconi had greed but Crane??-... Christian Bale's voice was....bearable to say the least... Liam Neeson as usual had an excellent performance as Ducard well as Morgan Freeman always, Gary Oldman a true chameleon, this time a good guy Michael Caine perfect in his role in every single way, truly. A great, eerie performance from Cillian Murphy as Dr. Crane... Worst character ...was sad to say Katie Holmes as Rachel...not to say she is really a bad actor but it was just bad scripting as the words felt...dry...she acted too much the part of the "girl next door" character and lost credibility as a DA assistant as well as pushing the whole good people thing too far...

The only mistakes I think were there were listed above Really great movie experience...

10.title: Awesome!
10.content:
I love films and because I do I rarely go to the theaters, since most modern films are consistently disappointing or are laden with heavily political (read: leftist) views in order to influence political neophytes. But I digress...

I was pleasantly surprised after seeing this film. It is a vast improvement over Tim Burton's "Batman," and don't even get me started on his sequel "Batman Returns." The director, Christopher Nolan, actually tells a story so well that you believe that it is plausible that a character such as Batman can exist. The script is very strong.

Christian Bale is undoubtedly the best Batman yet and the supporting cast--mostly Brits thank God--are equally outstanding. Even Katie the Stepford Wife was tolerable. I also have to commend the young actor who played Bruce Wayne as a child. He was outstanding. If George Lucas picked this kid, "The Phantom Menace" would have been a lot more watchable.

While I loved Danny Elfman's Wagnerian score from "Batman," the string-based score in this film is even better.

This is one of the best films of 2005 and gets better with repeated viewings. Outstanding job by all!!

10.title: Wow!!!
10.content: Finally someone got Batman right! A pleasure from start to finish, performances were great with chemistry to spare between all principals. The only quibble and it's a minor one is that there were times when Ms Holmes was on screen that she looked like a teenager trying to throw paper airplanes at the major crime bosses, but she still managed to make me care about her thru the entire project. Christian Bale makes a reasonable Batman but just about anyone can do Batman with the iconic nature of the character and that suit, it's as Bruce Wayne that Mr Bale really shines as he manages to show the conflicted nature of what he needs to be as Bruce and do as Batman as well that makes the character sympathetic on all levels. Overall a great effort by all concerned and I'll be in line for tickets to however many more of them they want to do.

10.title: A movie that stands alone, and not just as a "Batman" movie.
10.content: To prepare yourself to see this movie, forget everything you know about Batman. This sounds clichéd, and it is, but this is the best advice I can offer you. Forget Joel Schumacher (if you haven't already), and, although we may love Tim Burton, forget him too. Prepare to see the genesis of a superhero in the most plausible, realistic sense. Expect plenty of action and fight scenes, but expect them to be embedded in a deeper context, as opposed to the the mindless "pow" and "zowie" days of Batman. We've seen superhero movies well done (the Spiderman movies, for example, are generally regarded as well done), but we have yet to see the story of a superhero treated as what it has represented, from its creation to its popular context. Batman is not just some fantastic, idealistic crusading crime fighter who, in the end, makes everything better and loves everyone. Batman is foremost a man, flesh and blood, before he is anything else, and Christopher Nolan ably presents the conflict within Bruce Wayne that inevitably gives rise to the Dark Knight. He gives Batman, and even Scarecrow and Ra's Al Ghul plausibility, and makes the action, even the car chase, mean something - he makes you care what happens to Bruce Wayne, and he makes you think about why he's doing exactly what he's doing. You will find yourself in awe not at an awesome batmobile, an awesome batwing or an awesomely terrible batsuit with nipples, but at the awesome power one man, fueled by both a psychotic rage and an idealistic compassion, can come to possess. Batman Begins is not only the best superhero movie made yet, but one of the most ably accomplished action movies of all time.

10.title: Dark,impressive ,Realistic ,grim and with a stellar cast
10.content: This movie does one thing very well it sets the scene for the appearance of batman brilliantly .We See Bruce's torment and pain his burning desire to help the people of gotham .It finds a way to make the essentially silly concept of a man in a giant rubber Gimp suit not only plausible but also quite scary.It explores who bruce is what kind of place he inhabits and how he learned his craft.Also very wisely keeps batsy off screen long as possible .His appearance is sometimes augmented by the hallucinations of his opponents making him into a full fledged demon beast.Each of the cast get a chance to shine with their character acting and the ability to make the silly believable. The action is fantastic sword fights, street fights ,pitched car battles and a train to round it all off.This movie works on every level as drama, dystopian horror and of course sweet sweet action. Shame about the sequels really

My complaints were I didn't like the fight scenes that much, you can't see what is going on most of the time! The Batmobile in the 1989 movie looks much cooler to me.

I think there has been too many Batman movies in recent years for me to really get excited about a Batman movie again. Batman (1989) Blew me away more than this. I guess it is because it was the first movie that took Batman seriously. But Batman Begins is close to it.

10.title: Better than the Spiderman franchise (a micro spoiler)
10.content:
This is the best of the Batman movies (the Tim Burton original hasn't worn well). The only screen Batman that is even richer is Batman the Animated Series.

Here, though, almost all the details are right, both plot bits and the fun business, like the logical development of the gadgets. It strikes a good balance between action and psychology, without overdoing either one, though the car chase is too protracted for my taste. The dialogue is well balanced, too, with some memorable lines and dramatic effect. Some of Liam Neeson's early Ducard lines are a bit strained, but he invests them with as much as he can.

The only other slight complaint I have is they can't resist investing it with too many foes, including an awkward villain juxtaposition, which I won't spoil. These are all nits, though. It's exciting, fun, and emotionally rewarding. I can't wait for the juggernaut of sequels.

10.title: Great!
10.content: Quite simply - this is the Batman movie true Batman fans have always wanted to see. It begins with the experiences of young Bruce Wayne as he encounters true fear for the first time, then witnesses his parents murder. Then it flashes forward to the day his parent's murderer is released from jail after turning informant for the DA's office. We see Bruce struggle to find meaning in the fact he is robbed of the chance to get revenge when the object of his hatred, the murderer, is assassinated by a mob boss's lackey just before Bruce would have killed him with a gun. Thus begins Bruce's 7 year journey to understand the criminal mind, and his concurrent search for the skills to combat criminality and true evil with justice.

10.title: Best Batman yet
10.content: "Show me a hero and I'll write you a tragedy." -F.Scott Fitzgerald In the story of Batman Begins we are given the story of a young boy who sees crime first hand, at the death of his two parents. The movie is a first for Warner Brothers that depicts a more accurate version of the Dark Knight played very well by Christian Bale. At the beginning we see Bruce Wayne as a man who is lost. Searching Asia for answers to his past, why people commit crimes is his main driving force? Through all of his travels he becomes truly lost in his own journey. He is then met by Henri Ducard played by Liam Neeson who offers him answers and direction. He is more like a father figure to the searching Bruce Wayne, who adopts his role as mentor, and teacher. He begins training at the league of shadows, and starts to learn about himself more than ever. During this time we are given glimpses of Bruce's past and see why he is such a damage person. Seeing the tragedy of his past unfold through flash backs of his childhood. Then through training we uncover the real theme of the movie which is overcoming your fears, making them your weapon. This is the main theme which is used throughout the entirety of the movie. We learn that Bruce's greatest fear is bats, or so we think it is merely a trigger of an event prior to the death of his parents. He secretly blames himself, for their deaths, and using the fear of bats to cover up his true emotions. When he was young he was playing with Rachel Dawes played by Katie Holmes, he steals an arrow head she found at his mansion and as he is running to hide he falls down an abandon well. Bruce is completely engulfed by bats as he lies at the bottom of the well with a broken leg. This is where we first get a glimpse of his fear of bats, trembling and helpless he finally sees relief from his torment as his father descends down the shaft to rescue him. With the use of a very organic sound the director Christopher Nolan uses natural bat sounds to capture the audience's attention. The shrieking of the bats throughout the movie almost makes the hair on your neck stand up. During these flashbacks of his past Bruce is receiving training from Ducard on how to utilize your fear to make it your strength. Obviously Ducard sees the potential in Bruce, but it is not how he truly sees himself. Ducard wants Bruce to return to Gotham and destroy it after his initiate in the League of Shadows. At this moment we see the true hero come out instead of wanting to please his mentor, when asked to kill a murder he simply shakes his head in refusal of the last test. Showing the true nature of batman coming out, a true moral core unlike most men we see today. No matter how much he is pushed he will not resort to becoming a common criminal, after this he has to fight his way out. After he is free and he brings Ducard to safety he is then met by Alfred Pennyworth played by Michael Caine, his family butler and close friend. He is instrumental in the creation of Batman's outfit and tools. Upon his return Bruce is fixated on creating a symbol that the citizens of Gotham can unite under. Upon discovering a bat in the clock in the library Bruce discovers the secret areas of the southwest corridor. Alfred quips at Bruce, "In the Civil War, your great-great grandfather was involved in the Underground Railroad, secretly transporting freed slaves to the North. And I suspect these caverns came in handy" (Goyer, Kane & Nolan, 2005). This is now where Bruce starts to develop the idea of the Batman, he confides in Alfred that bats actually scare him and that's why he chose the image of a bat as his symbol. This is where he divulges to Alfred his plan to use his greatest fear as a weapon against evil doers. "People need dramatic examples to shake them out of apathy and I can't do that as Bruce Wayne. As a man, I'm flesh and blood, I can be ignored, I can be destroyed; but as a symbol... as a symbol I can be incorruptible, I can be everlasting" (Goyer, Kane & Nolan, 2005). Thus one of the best depictions of Batman is made from his fear to the bad guys' nightmare. Really utilizing the original archetype of the Batman we all know and love from the comics that they originated from. Using fear as a weapon to attach the bad guys and make them scared to go out at night and harm people. Making him Gotham's Dark Knight, the defender of the week, a real hero the type of hero we need.

10.title: My favorite movie
10.content:
I was excited to see Batman Begins, possibly more excited than I had been about any other movie since Tim Burton's original. I expected that, at best, it would be as good as that film. I cannot convey my astonishment to find that it not only surpasses every other Bat-film, any other summer movie (Jurassic Park, Spider-Man 2, Star Wars: Episode III), but also most of the films that have been released in the last thirty years.

It's an adventure on the grandest scale, a human drama with real, heartfelt emotion toward its characters AND the coolest superhero action flick ever made. The level of satisfaction I felt leaving the theatre is unparalleled by any other film. It's a film that deserves to be a huge success, and it's cool enough to become one of the all-time highest grossers. I LOVE this film, and am proud to tell people that Batman Begins is my favorite movie.

10.title: An Honest Review
10.content:
Of the four "new" Batman movies (I have no idea what to call the Clooney mess), Batman Begins takes the trophy. Although the original Batman starring Jack Nicolson and Michael Keaton will always have a place in my heart, I must say that Nolan's treatment left me with no negative criticism. It seems that lately I've been hit over the head with a huge computer-animated hammer. As someone who has worked in stop-motion animation, I hate to walk away from a movie counting the scenes when a character was floating above the floor that he/she/it was supposed to be standing on. It's a deal breaker for me. Batman Begins should be required viewing in directing school as an example of how to use computers when making a movie.

Much like the refreshing live-action aspect of the film, the casting and even the script are dead on. Michael Caine definitely kills it as Alfred, and the aged Rutger Hauer is a nice touch. Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman are quite well placed and handle their parts perfectly. I judge Christian Bale's performance against Michael Keaton and - well, I guess I just judge it against Michael Keaton. Keaton's Batman/Bruce Wayne was a completely different character than the Batman Begins hero. Bale's role is that of a human character; certainly more than just a rubbery guy in a cape and a secretive millionaire. For this, it is almost inappropriate to compare the two. Rest assured, Bale's wit and demeanor - and even his appearance - are definitely what Batman/Bruce Wayne should be.

I haven't been able to figure out why so many movies are directed at a the ADD demographic. If a character flashes a gun at another character, I don't need to hear him say "I have a gun, and if you make me mad I might shoot you." It was a nice surprise to actually WANT to pay attention while watching. Undeserving monologues are non existent, and the jokes are kept to a minimum. The one liners somehow work to intensify the action, rather than just embarrass the audience, and the technical jargon passes as relevant and even authentic for the most part.

Lastly, the action is top notch. The mystique of Batman is directed into the fight scenes in a manner that I can only accurately describe as thrilling. Even those who have seen nothing more than the film version of Batman know that symbolism plays a huge part in his story. Batman Begins provides a flawless explanation not only of the origins of this symbolism, but of it's practical use by a crime fighter with pointy ears. That may sound somewhat cryptic to those of you who haven't yet seen the movie. My suggestion to you is to spend the small fortune that it will cost to catch this one on the big screen. It's definitely worth it.

10.title: Batman rises from the ashes

At first i thought this could be another cheesy Batman movie but since i am a big batman fan, i said to myself : maybe this time will be different so i went to saw it with some of my friends and after watching the first 30 minutes I knew it was worth it. 10.title: Absolutely spectacular, brilliant, 20 out of 10 stars!!!
10.content:
Let me start off by saying this was one of those movies I had virtually no interest in seeing. Generally speaking, these kinds of movies just "aren't my thing". A friend of mine (who IS into these movies) wanted to go, so I tagged along. We saw the movie in imax (2-D) at Jordan's Furniture (sorry I couldn't spell imax in all capital letters, the IMDb's robots picked it up and considered it shouting).

Especially when I heard that the movie is well over 2 hours long, I expected to be asleep before the opening credits finished. But I barely even blinked throughout the entire movie, much less looked at my watch. This movie was an absolute masterpiece.

The story, casting, cinematography, score, and overall experience were all just incredible. Christian Bale was *fantastic* in the leading role (the fact that he's very easy on the eyes doesn't hurt much either). I can honestly say that not a single second of the movie was "cheesy" or "over-produced" or "too far-fetched" (three attributes that I usually apply to movies of this type). It had just the right mixture of action, adventure, crime, fantasy, thrills, and even a few laughs and an occasional tear to my eye. The perfect recipe for a perfect movie.

If you do see this movie, I *highly recommend* you see it in imax if you have an imax theater within 100 miles of where you live. In my opinion, this great movie deserves absolutely nothing less than the experience that imax gives you. It is a movie that I will not soon forget.

10.title: A new definition for action movies
10.content:
Batman Begins sets the bar for action/super hero movies in the same way that James Bond and The Matrix did in their own way.

The story and the rationale behind the chaos that becomes Gotham fits perfectly. Tone and mood in its solitariness and relentlessness of the Batman is captured brilliantly. Clever writing, excellent acting (except for a fairly weak Katie Holmes), superb directing, cinematography, and especially the music of Hans Zimmer puts this movie in on another level - the level of high quality movie making.

My prediction - Oscar nomination for Best Picture. And while it will likely not win, the realization of what an intelligent action film can be all about has been created.

10.title: A great new genre of Batman
10.content:
Wow, this is a whole new genre of Batman. The story is intelligent and moving. This Batman movie is much less of a comic book story than the other Batman films. There was even some profound spiritual wisdom sprinkled here and there. Bruce Wayne growing up and how he became the powerful Batman is very believable and is a whole story in itself. Christian Bale is as good as it gets as batman. Sort of reminds me of Sean Connery never being surpassed as 007. I want one of those Batman cars. It is the best ever bat mobile; all the advanced weaponry stuff is the best. I'm led to believe that a sequel is being made.

I would have liked to see Gary Oldman as the straight detective have a larger part. Gary is such a great talent. The only weakness I might mention is that there could be stronger female roles on the good side as well as on the bad side. I love strong intelligent women.

10.title: Christopher Nolan, the name is enough

It seems to be a bonus to see so many legends in one frame.

With great action, strong plot and memorable acting that Batman has arrived with a bang.

10.title: The best Batman movie so far.

Now I can't wait for the sequel.

10.title: Get the man knighted already!
10.content: Batman begins and so did Christopher Nolan's genius! This is probably the greatest superhero origin story movie of all time and it will so remain forever. Christian Bale will always be the best Batman and Katie Holmes' phenomenal performance here was really missed in "The Dark Knight."

10.title: The Beginning of the Greatest Superhero Trilogy ever.
10.content: It's simple. This is the beginning of the best Superhero Trilogy of all time. Nothing can touch these three, beginning right here. (And as they unfold it's clear how tightly they mesh together). Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson... the only weak spot in this movie (and the next) is Rachel Dawes. 10.title: Bats is back to the spotlight!
10.content:
When Batman Begind was announced ,they were already several attempts to bring back Batman to the Big Screen after 1997, but all of them failed. Then Christofer Nolan fresh after Memento, was hired in order to direct this movie and he cast Christian Bale, who had made a name for himself with roles in American Phycho(2000), Equilibrium(2002) and the Machinist(2004),but he hadn't become an A-list actor yet. In general although the team for this movie was looking good, everyone was worried that this would be a flop many criticized the cast of Bale as "not Batman enough".

Then the flick came out in June of 2005 and took the world by storm, for it wasn't just the film fan wanted ,but also the one which they needed and deserved. Now it may made less than the Batman of 1989, but comparing it in box office numbers with the rest of Batman film, it was the second in the list. As for the audience and critics loved it for its darker more realistic tone and the felling that it wasn't just a superhero movie,like the Spiderman movies and X-men, but a crime drama ,with a vigilante in an awesome Batsuit and some terrifying villains to face.

Now let's see why the film rocks: Firstly the casting is close to pitch perfect, everyone from Morgan Freeman's Luscious Fox to Micheal Cane's Alfred and Garry Oldman's James Gordon are as good as they could get and the cherry on top Christian Bale as the Caped Crusader, one of the best casting choices in superhero history and in film in general. He is totally in his role and you really come to understand why he turn to such extreme ways to fight crime.

Secondary the designs ,from the Gotham City area ,to the Bat Cave and prisons are great. The show stole two thing the Batsuit and the New Batmobile, the Tumbler. The suit itself is great,though a bit bulky to say the truth, but the design and the gadgets on it are so realistic that at times you think "wait can this be real?", as for the Tumbler, it is my personal favorite Batmobile for it gets it anything right that is necessary for a good Batmobile, the mobility, speed and usefulness and it adds to it some tricks that are too awesome to write them down ,just go watch!

Finally the last part that made me give to the film a 10 out of 10 was themes. In short the main was fear and how do you deal with it, for Batman is at his core than victory of man over fear against pain, injustice and for a minor theme inside the flick ,the legacy you are going to leave after you are done. The second major theme is the definition of justice and here is where the other core value of Bats comes out, he refuses to kill, no matter the situation for as he says "I am not going to become the enforcer of the law!"!

In the the film's impact can be seen in the cinema as well in the Bond series, Star Trek and to the X-men films after 2005. In short this is one of the most historic films in the superhero genre and many non- superhero films also have elements of it in them. To EVERYONE go watch it immediately!

10.title: 'Batman Begins' establishes the origin of the best superhero trilogy
10.content:
This movie perfectly displays the origin of Bruce Wayne on his journey to becoming The Batman from the moment his parents are killed. What I really like about this movie his how it shows Bruce's relationship with bats. From the first time he saw them in the cave he fell into, Bruce is shown to be afraid, and almost mesmerized by the tiny furry animals. He eventually accepts his co-existence with bats when he re-vists the cave, and calmly lets bats swarm around him. In some scenes he treats bats as his allies. This relationship with bats is displayed throughout the entire trilogy, and is what makes Christopher Nolan's vision of Batman stand out. After the movie establishes Bruce's origin, it brilliantly and accurately shows Bruce's path to becoming Batman, from him forging batarangs, to the creation of the Batsuit, to the first time he busts criminals. This movie also contains the first appearance of import Batman/Gotham City related characters. Those being Alfred Pennyworth, Lucius Fox, and Commissioner Gordon. Each one of these characters are displayed perfectly, and each have the perfect actors for their roles. Of course, in most superhero movies, the hero isn't paired against casual city criminals. they eventually are given a challenge, when they are paired against the antagonist. Bruce does have experience from his encounters with the League of Shadows, he isn't quite ready to take on a criminal cancer within the depths of Gotham City, the notorious Scarecrow. The twisted villainous character gives Batman the true test of fear.

Overall, Christopher Nolan sets his Batman trilogy on the right path with this movie. Everything about this movie appeals to Batman fans, or superhero fans in general. Everything about the movie is great. Christian Bale takes on the role of Batman and does one of the best jobs as the character to this day. The movie accurately captures the character "Scarecrow" and tops it off with the League of Shadows and Ra's Al Ghul. This movie is absolutely perfect, every DC fan should see it. 10/10

10.title: Wow - They finally got it right!
10.content:
Okay, I've now seen this movie 5 times, and I can't believe I want to see it again. It just gets better and better. For those of you who have only seen it once or twice - go back! There is so much detail, everything is incredibly well crafted. Did you notice the truck as it left a blazing Wayne Manor? Christian Bale is amazing. What I found most remarkable is that he managed to rebuild his body from a 121 lbs. in "The Machinist" to 220 lbs. for Batman in only 5 months (check-out the articles on MSNBC or USATODAY for the details). When I read that, I knew the film would be fantastic. Imagine the self-discipline and control to gain 100 lbs. of muscle in only 5 months! He brings that personal level of intensity to the role; and it pays off big time.

As to those who didn't like the action sequences because of the lack of clarity, light, etc. - I say - that was the point!! The idea is that the bad guys can't really see him; they get glimpses. Remember, "men fear most what they cannot see." By cloaking the action sequences in short, dark sequences the terror levels increase. This film is a psychological thriller that happens to be based on a comic book character.

For those who don't like this film; I just don't think they really paid attention. "Batman Begins" respects the audience enough to expect us to listen and accept that what is said is important and that Bruce Wayne will act accordingly. Bravo!!

10.title: A Captivating Origin Story that Rises Above Expectations"
10.content:
Batman Begins, directed by Christopher Nolan, is a phenomenal superhero film that revitalizes the Batman franchise with its gritty realism, compelling storytelling, and exceptional performances. Serving as a powerful origin story, the film delves into the complex psyche of Bruce Wayne and offers a fresh take on the iconic character, solidifying its place as a standout entry in the superhero genre.

From the very first scene, Batman Begins grips the audience with its atmospheric tone and captivating narrative. The film immerses viewers in the dark and brooding world of Gotham City, expertly establishing a sense of realism and grounding the superhero tale in a believable context. Christopher Nolan's masterful direction brings a level of sophistication and depth to the story, elevating it beyond a mere comic book adaptation.

Christian Bale's portrayal of Bruce Wayne/Batman is nothing short of outstanding. He brings a raw intensity and emotional depth to the character, capturing both the vulnerability and the relentless determination that define Batman. Bale's transformation into the caped crusader is awe-inspiring, and his nuanced performance anchors the film, making Bruce Wayne's journey from a broken soul to a symbol of justice all the more compelling.

The supporting cast is equally impressive. Michael Caine delivers a delightful and memorable performance as Alfred Pennyworth, Bruce Wayne's loyal butler and confidant. Gary Oldman shines as Jim Gordon, portraying the future commissioner of Gotham with nuance and sincerity. Additionally, Liam Neeson brings gravitas and complexity to the role of Henri Ducard, Bruce's mentor and guide.

One of the film's greatest strengths is its exploration of Batman's origins. Batman Begins takes the time to delve into Bruce Wayne's transformation, his training with the League of Shadows, and his quest to find justice in a corrupt city. This focus on character development allows for a deeper understanding of Batman's motivations and establishes a strong foundation for the subsequent films in the trilogy.

The screenplay, co-written by Christopher Nolan and David S. Goyer, strikes a perfect balance between action, drama, and philosophical themes. Batman Begins delves into moral ambiguity, the nature of fear, and the complexities of justice, adding layers of depth and intellectual engagement to the superhero narrative. The dialogue is sharp and thought-provoking, inviting viewers to contemplate the blurred lines between heroism and vigilantism.

Visually, Batman Begins is a marvel. The film's striking cinematography, gritty production design, and seamless blend of practical and digital effects create a visually immersive experience. The action sequences are skillfully choreographed and serve the story, emphasizing Batman's physical prowess and strategic brilliance.

In conclusion, Batman Begins is a triumphant and captivating superhero film that successfully redefines the Batman mythos. With its engaging storyline, stellar performances, and a level of depth rarely seen in the genre, the film sets a new standard for what superhero films can achieve. Batman Begins lays the groundwork for Christopher Nolan's acclaimed Dark Knight trilogy, leaving audiences eager to witness the continued evolution of Batman's complex and compelling journey.

10.title: "Why did the batman franchise fall? so it can learn to pick it's self up"
10.content:
In 'Batman Begins', Christopher Nolan's suburb introduction to the caped crusader, fear drives the story. Fear must be conquered but fear is also used to conquer. Bruce Wayne must stare his fear straight in the eye to truly become the symbol of justice he intends to be. The film uses the thematic nature of fear to drive the story and the character of Bruce Wayne, it makes the film a satisfying whole.

'Batman Begins' is a brilliant opening film to this reboot of one of pop cultures most popular characters. It is brilliant because it defines how and why Bruce Wayne becomes the man he becomes and the symbol of justice in which he chooses to fight fear. In the opening act two major things happen, one when Bruce Wayne is a child falling into a well on the grounds of Wayne Manor. He is trapped in a dark, lonely place, confronted by hundreds of bats. The other event is the murder of his parents, in front of his own eyes. This was a result of Wayne's fear resulting in him asking to leave a play the family were attending. Fear, guilt and later anger consume Bruce in regards to his parents death, part of him wants to avenge their deaths but another part knows that there is a greater responsibility, one that he must oblige to. This is spurred by his fathers own efforts to clean up the streets of Gotham, in his own way.

The opening act so adeptly introduces us to the character of Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) and what drives him, it also introduces us to 'The League of Shadows' , Ra's al Ghul and Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson). The scenes between Neeson and Bale are fantastic in setting up Wayne's strengths and weaknesses. Ducard refers to compassion being a weakness that enemies will not share but Wayne insists that is what sets him apart. Of course if he did not have that compassion he would be a villain.

In the second act we are introduced to the character of Batman. Batman is Wayne's way of using a symbol of fear against his enemies. It is this element of fear mixed with the compassion that mark Wayne as an interesting character. To do this he must create a mask, to do this Wayne needs his own company - particularly the applied sciences department and Lucius Fox - to gain the resources he needs, including weapons, Armour and heavy duty vehicles! The film is essentially a number of larger and smaller introductions and both the introductions to Wayne and Batman are exceptional because the thematic elements as to Wayne's motivations are always at the forefront of the story.

The second act also introduces us to the major plot of the film that lies beneath the true intentions of the film - and to be honest fully tie back into those intentions. We are introduced to Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman), the first of Batman's allies, the only honest cop in Gotham. We are introduced to the criminal component of Gotham with crime boss Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson) and Dr. Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy). We are also introduced to Rachel Dawes (Katie Holmes), the childhood friend that Wayne still cares about. The plot largely has to do with the misplacing of a devise that can vaporise water. Scarecrow is working for someone who wants to use that machine to cripple Gotham, by running drugs through the water system thus allowing the toxins of the drug to be inhaled by the poor citizens of Gotham. I fully expected the film to be weaker once this plot was introduced but the man behind this diabolical plan happens to tie in with Wayne's beginnings on the path to becoming Batman thus the film ultimately comes full circle by the end.

There are so many elements that I love about this film. Not just the thematic elements but the design elements, the Tumbler acts as the armoured tank version of the batmobile. It is robust, bulky and angular. It is a perfect machine for this new Batman, one that is based more on reality than previous incarnations but when that has a darker and more dangerous appeal. I love some of the images from the toxins that Scarecrow uses with his mask - or the images we see when the toxin has been released, such as Batman looking like the devil or the surreal image of Scarecrow riding a fire breathing horse.

Christian Bale is the perfect choice for Bruce Wayne/Batman. To be honest it doesn't take much to play a decent Batman, as long as you are physically cut out for the role but in Wayne, Bale is able to play the role as a conflicted, angry man who uses fear to drive him. He is also really good at being the philanthropist arsehole, the other mask Wayne sometimes uses to turn attentions away from any suspicious activities he may be up to. Mostly all of the cast are great in their roles, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Liam Neeson especially, but Holmes is absolutely miscast as Dawes and rightly replaced in The Dark Knight.

Overall though, this is a brilliant introduction to an iconic character or characters. Nolan proves he was up to the task of taking on such a hot property and being able to deal with a big budget production, in fact this is only the beginning of what he could achieve. A cracking film all round.

10.title: "Sometimes ... a man rises...from the darkness ...", and sometimes a movie does too, and this movie is the proof!
10.content:
1989-1992 Tim Burton made two classic Batman films ("Batman" and "Batman Returns"), just great and must-watch movies. In 1995, Joel Schumacher did "Batman Forever", which actually was a good movie, but with only a good and perfect performance (Jim Careey -The Ridler). And then, in 1997, Schumacher completely ruined the franchise with the film stupidly stupid "Batman and Robin", ruining and destroying the Batman franchise forever, being vanished from Hollywood what seemed to be forever. Eight years later, in 2005, it was given the task for Christopher Nolan to resurrect the franchise from the dead, some liked the idea, others thought it was going to be another horrible movie, and it was?! Far, FAR from it!

"Begins" tells the story of Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale), who as a child saw his parents die in front of him during a robbery. Years pass and Bruce returns to his hometown Gotham City for the final judgment of Chill, the murderer of his parents. Bruce planned to kill him with his father pistol at the end of the trial. But before Bruce could have the chance, a woman kills Chill at close range, because Chill had secrets from the big criminal mind of the city, Carmine Falcone (Tom Wikinson). After that Bruce leaves the city and begins a journey around the world with the mission of knowing and understand the criminal minds and tries to somehow tackle corruption and violence of his city. And then he meets Ducard (Liam Neeson) who offers Bruce the chance and the weapons to fulfill its mission. Months later Bruce returns to Gotham with the help of his butler and best friend Alfred (Michael Caine). Now more mature and decided, Bruce begins to do justice with his own hands, but not as the man Bruce Wayne, but with his new identity, "Batman".

What Nolan begins to resurrect the franchise is not only putting the story more mature and also full of action without exaggeration (not lacking in this film), is doing the character of Bruce Wayne relevant. In previous films, Bruce Wayne was only the rich guy who decided to do justice, and his main concern was to hide his superhero identity out of the press. Here, it is also that, much better, but also humanizes the character. For the first time we see the man behind the mask, making him a relatable character (thus, making us finally to worry about his character). All thanks to a superb storytelling that Nolan gives the film, giving dialogs tat flows perfectly to the characters and for the first time a superheroes movie really well written and also we feel that everything in the story is real, that it could really happen in our world.

Nolan was only known for the magnificent "Memento" and the underrated "Insomnia", both were known for their realistic style that works very well in this movie as well. Since Batman's car and gadgets, all with their scientific explanations (all possible, look it up), and even the Gotham City (filmed in Chicago). Nolan makes Gotham the economic center of America, but also the center of corruption and violence (New York ¬¬¬¬¬¬¬¬¬plus Chicago). Making with the obscure style of the first films of Burton, while keeping the realism.

Great story and excellent direction, but also their characters guarantee the final success. Nolan surprisingly, even not faithfully following the comic-book, he manage to bring to the movie many of the characters (even some that not major fans knew that existed). Christian Bale simply superb both as Bruce Wayne and Batman (in my opinion the best Batman actor who ever had); Liam Neeson as mentor (and a surprise later) simply excellent; Michael Caine is superb, capturing the spirit of Alfred , loyal and funny; Gary Oldman also captures the spirit of Commissioner Gordon perfectly, stubborn and smart with a hatred of injustice and corruption; Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox (nor I knew he existed), the inventor of the hero's gadgets, and captures the right philosophy that he and Bruce Wayne had in the comic, if Lucius knew or not that Bruce was the masked man, always a mystery.

Even not faithfully following the comic and realizing the dreams of fans, Nolan resurrected the franchise completely. Managing to capture the spirit of the only superhero without powers, putting a dark and even a cop-thriller tone to the history. Also bringing heart and soul to the character of Bruce Wayne, and all the other characters thanks to an excellent narrative; superb direction really well action packed. What at first was to be a prequel to the classic Burton was the great beginning of one of the best trilogies ever made.

9/10

10.title: Batman has TRULY began!!

I must truly say that the dialog, script and the setting of Gotham City is perfect but special mention must go to the creators of the new Batmobile. It is AWESOME! the structure of the vehicle, the chase scenes... fantastic to the very end.

Last but not least, i would like to thank the team of Batman of choosing the right concept and theme for Batman - fear, that will grip the hearts of villains and criminals alike. And for all those out there guessing who the next villain will be... he will be back by popular demand, playing Batman's arch nemesis, and all batman fans out there will be eager to find out who will be casted into that role.

Thank you to all that contributed to the perfect movie for all Batman fans worldwide

10.title: Batman Begins: A Perfect 10/10 Masterpiece
10.content:
Batman Begins (2005) is nothing short of a cinematic triumph, redefining the superhero genre and setting the gold standard for origin stories. Directed by Christopher Nolan, this movie flawlessly captures the essence of the Dark Knight, combining rich storytelling, stunning visuals, and a powerful score to deliver an unforgettable experience. It's the perfect balance of character development, action, and thematic depth, earning a well-deserved 10/10.

Story and Character Development At its core, Batman Begins is a story of transformation. It brilliantly chronicles Bruce Wayne's journey from a grief-stricken orphan to Gotham's savior. The narrative is meticulously crafted, taking its time to delve into Bruce's motivations, fears, and moral struggles. His time training with the League of Shadows, guided by the enigmatic Ra's al Ghul (Liam Neeson), is compelling and gives the film a grounded yet epic feel.

Unlike typical superhero movies that gloss over the "why" of a hero's journey, this film explores every detail of Bruce's psyche and his decision to become Batman. Christian Bale's portrayal is pitch-perfect, embodying both the tortured soul of Bruce Wayne and the determined, morally driven persona of Batman. His duality as a flawed human and a symbol of hope is beautifully realized.

Supporting Cast The supporting cast is equally phenomenal. Michael Caine's Alfred brings warmth and wisdom, serving as Bruce's moral compass and emotional anchor. Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon is earnest and relatable, providing a grounded perspective amidst the chaos. Morgan Freeman's Lucius Fox adds a touch of humor and intellect, while Liam Neeson's Ra's al Ghul is a complex and menacing antagonist with a philosophy that challenges Bruce's ideals. Cillian Murphy's chilling performance as Dr. Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow is an added bonus, making every scene he's in utterly captivating.

Cinematography and Direction Nolan's direction is masterful. The way Gotham City is portrayed-gritty, shadowy, and oppressive-perfectly mirrors the tone of the story. Cinematographer Wally Pfister captures the darkness of the city while still creating visually stunning set pieces. From the haunting bat cave to the chaotic narrows, every setting feels alive and integral to the story.

The action sequences are a testament to Nolan's attention to detail. The fights are raw and visceral, showcasing Batman's skills while maintaining a sense of realism. The Batmobile chase scene is thrilling, combining practical effects with clever cinematography to deliver pure adrenaline.

Themes and Depth What truly sets Batman Begins apart is its depth. It's not just a superhero movie; it's a film about fear, justice, and redemption. The exploration of fear-both as a weapon and as a personal hurdle-adds layers of complexity to the story. Bruce doesn't just fight criminals; he fights the fear within himself and uses it to inspire change in Gotham.

The moral dilemmas posed by Ra's al Ghul's extremist ideology versus Bruce's belief in justice create thought-provoking tension. The film's themes resonate beyond the comic book world, making it as much a philosophical drama as an action blockbuster.

Music and Sound Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard's score is a masterpiece in itself. The music perfectly complements the film's tone, with tracks like "Molossus" amplifying the intensity of key moments. The score's balance of haunting melodies and triumphant crescendos makes it unforgettable.

Conclusion Batman Begins is everything a superhero movie should be-and more. It's intelligent, thrilling, emotional, and visually stunning. Every aspect of the film, from the cast to the cinematography, direction, and score, comes together to create a masterpiece. It doesn't just tell the story of Batman; it redefines what the character stands for and cements his place as one of the most compelling heroes in cinema.

A perfect 10/10, Batman Begins isn't just a great superhero movie-it's a great film, period.

10.title: Chris Nolan's gonna get a lot of work after this.
10.content:
This is the best Batman movie ever made. Christopher Nolan has managed to blend the perfect mix of action, drama, and horror. Christian Bale is the second best batman next to Michael Keaton. The performances are well done and the cast is A list. Though I preferred the Tim Burton style set direction to this one, the eyes are still treated to a dark Gotham. The chase scene is exhilarating and the toys and bat mobile unique. This one is the first to dive deep into the background of batman not only through flashbacks, but taking us through his training, and inner demons. The theme and the enemy chosen was a triumph to pull the franchise out of the deep hole Joel Schumacher put it in.

Cilian Murphy's portrayal of the scarecrow is creepy but not over the top like so many other comic book villains. The script is strong and definitely more complete than the last three, with compelling dialogue. The score was not quite as well done as Danny Elfman's original, but it is satisfying enough. Cinematography is for the most part very nice, but sometimes a shifty camera get's in the ways of the fight sequences, however giving you the sense of swift brutality delivered in every one of the bat's blows. This is the first batman to really have a twist in it, and this one still leaves the story at a cliffhanger, for instance the last scene when it is revealed that the likely next villain is the joker. There is also a great amount of detail in this movie, and it stays truer to the graphic comics. Lieutenant Gordon has yet to become a Commissioner.

All in all a movie done as well as it could be, perfect cast, perfect director, perfect theme.

10.title: A superhero movie that is uncharacteristically realistic
10.content:
Batman Begins Directed by: Christopher Nolan

The Dark Knight makes a triumphant return as Christopher Nolan directs a restart of the popular "Batman" franchise. It has been eight years since a Batman movie of any kind has been released, and it was well worth the wait.

PLOT: Unlike the previous four movies, "Begins" explores the main origins of how billionaire Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) became Batman. The audience is captivated into a world that for once, takes place outside of Gotham City, as Wayne seeks to join the infamous League of Shadows (lead by Ra's Al Ghul- Ken Watanabe). His journey takes him into Asia and is trained by Ra's right-hand man Ducard (Liam Neeson). Wayne, still trying to overcome the loss of his parents, learns he needs to control his fear and unleash it on those who use it as a weapon. In this case, the fear is bats. Steadily, Wayne transforms into Batman and begins his quest to restore justice in Gotham City.

CHARACTERS: Bale delivers as Bruce Wayne and Batman, something many feel was a hard task to accomplish in the previous four films. The audience can actually see a difference between Wayne and Batman, and they are easily two different characters. As usual, Liam Neeson plays the mentor role, and does a superb job in the process. Many complain that Katie Holmes, who plays love interest Rachel Dawes, was not suitable for the role. It is a little distracting, but not enough to tear one away from the movie. Michael Caine fits Alfred like a glove, and I've always been a fan of Michael Gough. The performance that stood out for me though, was Cillian Murphy's representation of the Scarecrow. He is downright creepy, and his performance is right up there with Jack Nicholson's Joker. Supporting actors Morgan Freeman (Lucius Fox, Batman's version of "Q"), and Gary Oldman (the determined future-Commissioner Gordon) solidify this outstanding cast.

ANALYSIS: "Batman Begins" is uncharacteristically realistic for a superhero movie, but this is one of the movie's best qualities. The audience actually believes that a Bruce Wayne's self discovery is indeed possible, which grips them into thinking a story like this could actually happen. The realism comes down to how Batman got his costume, something the audience never understood or even cared about until now. This is what I liked most, how believable it was.

BOTTOM-LINE: Superhero fan or not, this is a must see. Outstanding. 9/10

10.title: Perfect Batman
10.content:
This is truly the correct incarnation of Batman. There is so much happening in this film, and yet none of it seems rushed in any way. It is a true comic book film, yet it never seems campy or even very unrealistic.

The strongest point is easily the cast. Christian Bale portrays Batman and Bruce Wayne both with such realism. Perhaps a key point is that Bale avoids trying to make Batman look like Bruce Wayne in a batsuit. Bale realizes that to a degree they are different personalities, and he conveys this in just the right way. Cillian Murphy is wonderful as Jonathan Crane, and even Katie Holmes, who is way too young to be a lawyer, manages to perform her role with excellence. The real treats are Michael Caine, who is truly the perfect Alfred, Morgan Freeman, who adds a bit of down to earthness, and Gary Oldman, who makes Jim Gordon a likable guy who grounds Gotham in a sense of reality (after all, not EVERY cop can be corrupt!) Batman Begins really succeeds when it is explaining how things come together. You can actually start to understand the mysterious (and previously silly) aspects of the character. And Bale does such an excellent job of creating the character through real emotions that real people feel.

And of course, the direction of Christopher Nolan has brought it all together so well. This is a great film. To call it the best Batman movie is to simply not do it justice. I have always believed Batman was the purist, most praiseworthy superhero. Now we have a film that does that ideal justice.

10.title: Surpassed all expectations
10.content:
It's one thing when you have low expectation for a movie and it is a pleasant surprise. It's another thing when you have high expectations and the movie still manages to completely blow you away.

"Batman Begins" just works. The script, the plot, the casting, the effects, the psychology of it all tie together in an exceedingly complete package.

One very nice surprise is that, for the most part, the movie manages to leave the comic book "super hero that defies all laws of physics" behind, and shows Bruce Wayne as a human being. The story is much more dramatic, and realistic, than any of the other Batman movies - yet manages to answer some of the dangling questions, like - how does Bruce Wayne have the resources to build all the toys in the batcave.

A final comment is that the Imax version is the way to see this Batman Begins! This is one movie that really does justice to the incredible picture and sound of the Imax format.

10.title: Batman Begins
10.content: Batman Begins, is based upon the Batman comic books and is a prequel to the previous Batman films made. The film takes place when Bruce Wayne (Batman) is an eight year old child who lives with his rich parents in Gotham City. His father Thomas Wayne, owns the Wayne building and and tries to do good for the city. One day after leaving an opera Bruce's parents are killed by a robber and Bruce is raised by the family butler Alfred. When he gets older Bruce travels and on the way is taught martial arts and several years later returns home when he was presumed dead. Bruce gets a job working at his father's company which was left to him and he sees how the city is run with corruption and violence so he plans to use his martial arts skills for good. Bruce meets Lucius Fox, a scientist at the Wayne building who he has discovered has made several weapons and a suit which was meant for the army. Bruce takes the equipment and alters it a bit and soon becomes Batman and tries to right the wrong in Gotham City by bringing down the various evils. Batman currently has to take down a drug lord and a doctor who is releasing his toxic drug in the water supply of the city. Batman Begins, has good direction, a good script, good performances by everyone involved, good original music, good cinematography, good film editing, good production design, good art direction and good set decoration. I was a big fan of Batman and Batman Returns, and I remember liking Batman: Mask Of The Phantasm and the animated Batman series as well. I however did not like Batman Forever or Batman And Robin, so I wasn't quite sure if I would like this film or not. One reason I liked Batman and Batman Returns so much was because of the dark atmosphere and setting provided by director Tim Burton for both films which was sorely missed in Batman Forever and Batman And Robin. I must say that I was very pleasantly surprised with Batman Begins. The film has a great story that at times is serious and at other times very entertaining and original. The film is also engaging, stylish, well acted and well made, is entertaining with a lot of action, it is fun and unique. Actor Christian Bale makes a good Bruce Wayne/Batman and I liked how the film's director Christopher Nolan didn't use a lot of CGI for some of the effects. The film is good looking and has a nice dark futuristic type atmosphere and the film as some good art and set decoration. Batman Begins is the first real surprise I have had with a movie in theaters this year so far. I really thought the film would just be a dumb action film that would be quickly forgotten but I was sure wrong. There is a lot more to this movie than the action and it is very thought provoking and engaging. And then we get the action and the film is very entertaining. This film works on many levels and hits all the right keys to being a perfect superhero film and is just as good as the original Batman from 1989 by Tim Burton. One of the best action films I have seen in years and a true masterpiece. One of the best films of the year.
