10.title: 'Batman Begins' Nails Lure of the Dark Knight
10.content:
Anybody who was skeptical of 'Batman Begins' couldn't be blamed if they were imagining that it would be similar to the Batman series in the late '80s and '90s, particularly the last two films. However, those skeptics can be relieved when seeing this reinterpretation of the Dark Knight.

Christopher Nolan's film-noir style suits Batman much better than Tim Burton's German-expressionistic style did. The noir-style beautifully captures the essence and mood of Gotham City, setting the stage for an interesting story about the origins of Bruce Wayne's doppelganger. The origins is definitely the best attraction to the film, as the audience grows to understand what makes Batman tick and why his brooding character acts the way it does.

Bruce Wayne is born to a wealthy couple, as his father is the president of Wayne Enterprises in Gotham. Despite their immense wealth, the Waynes teach Bruce enough solid, character-building principles to maintain enough of Bruce's moral goodness despite the fact that his parents are murdered when leaving a musical- a musical that was left early due to Bruce's fears of bats.

Later on in life, after forgetting who he is and the legacy he carries, Bruce understands that he needs to make something of his life. This leads him on a crusade to master combat skills and use the lessons learned from his father to become one who "prey on those who prey on the fearful." Conquering the fear that placed his parents in the front of death, Bruce takes on the menace of his former mentor despite the fact that Gotham's citizens have yet to understand what he is all about. 4/4 stars

10.title: A beginning like no other
10.content:
It's been 16 years since the world was introduced to BATMAN on the big screen and oh, how we cherished that film and the sequel that came after it. I say sequel, because the "other" two films that came after BATMAN RETURNS were a disgrace to the comic book franchise. The truth is, it's been almost 9 years since George Clooney graced us as the caped hero and that was just about long enough for me to forget about how stupid and cheesy it and it's predecessor really were. Luckily for us though, time heals, so by the time the idea for BATMAN BEGINS was released to the public, I think we were all ready for something new and exciting. And I must say we got what we wanted, plus 100 times more in what many critics, including myself, are dubbing the best BATMAN flick yet.

With a cast like the one in BATMAN BEGINS, it's hard to single out just one actor. Even before seeing this film, I felt like no other actor would match Michael Keaton's performances in the first two BATMAN flicks, but Christian Bale did, plus some. And Bale (AMERICAN PSYCHO, EQUILIBRIUM, THE MACHINIST) wasn't just good, he was convincing, yet raw, which played nicely to the story going on. Bale brought all the anger into the role that was needed and just ran with it. But, that wasn't all. He was great without the cape too, cracking jokes and pulling off that playboy charm we all love in the Bruce Wayne character.

Playing opposite Bale was such screen legends as Michael Caine, playing Alfred Pennyworth, Morgan Freeman, playing the tech-savy Lucius Fox and of course Liam Neeson, who was excellent as Ducard. But, at no point did any of these screen legends overpower Bale, which was needed to keep the focus on his character. Not even Cillian Murphy's Scarecrow, who was brilliant, overpowered Bale's Batman. And in reality, there probably could have been more Scarecrow/Batman exchanges, but who knows, maybe there will be in the next film. Filling out the rest of the powerful cast was Katie Holmes, who was good in her small role as assistant D.A. Rachel Dawes and Gary Oldman, who played a very convincing Jim Gordon, the last good cop left in Gotham.

The one thing that is almost undeniable in BATMAN BEGINS is the amount of detail that was put into it. I can't think of anything that was missed or didn't flow with the rest of the story. That says something about director Christopher Nolan's (MEMENTO) work ethic, who is really a rookie director. It's clear he worked hard with screenwriter David S. Goyer (BLADE trilogy) on making sure he gathered all the right information on the cast of characters included in his film. Detail like that and the detail surrounding Batman himself was enough to ignite this film into something bigger than itself.

I think the one aspect that defined this film was how well the story was molded into the action and special effects, something George Lucas obviously forgot to do with STAR WARS: EPISODE III  REVENGE OF THE SITH. Nolan did wonders with Goyer's story and made sure the effects around the story were not overdone, a key to films like this. The one aspect of the action that caught me by surprise though was Nolan's camera work with the fight sequences of Batman. Instead of just having a big open fight sequence, Nolan chose to use Batman's undeniable scare tactics on his victims as the biggest weapon, almost like an element of surprise. And you know, some critics say this film could have been better visually, but I disagree. I think the balance between the story and the special effects was perfect, right down to some of what I call the "money shots" of Batman flying or standing atop a building.

With two films to go, BATMAN BEGINS was the ideal start to refuel this once famed franchise. With a script that couldn't have been better, director Christopher Nolan earned his worth in Hollywood by producing one of the best adaptations of a graphic novel in recent memory. If you didn't know who Christian Bale was before this film, you certainly will after it, in a movie that almost makes you forget about any previous BATMAN flicks, which is a feat like no other if you ask me.

A+

10.title: Unprecedented
10.content:
I could never have imagined that this next Batman film could have been as good as it was. I got the chance to see it for free a week before it opened at a sneak preview, and that was surely the best money I ever spent.

If you think that Batman means armored nipples and cheesy villains, you're in for a surprise with this new rendition of the Dark Knight's origin. Christopher Nolan has not only done an amazing job with the direction, but he and David Goyer have written and remarkable script with amazing characterizations. This is what causes the movie to rise above the regular action adventure/superhero formula, the motivations and personalities of the characters.

The action/chase scenes are heartpounding, and the unfolding and twisty plot nothing short of brilliant. I think Christian Bale is perfect as a Bruce Wayne in the process of maturing into the Caped Crusader. The first time he donned that suit send chills down my spine.

Go see Batman Begins. It may easily be the best superhero film yet made. I can only hope the rumors about a trilogy in the works are true.

10.title: My first Bat-Movie.
10.content:
I've been reading Bat comics for some time now, but ironically, never sw any movies. Eciding to start with this one, I was not dissapointed.

You know that stereotype that action films don't have any meaning or philosophy in them and are just one big fight scene? Totally not the case with Batman Begins. This movie breakes that stereotype like a giant breaking a bug. The fighting scenes are amazing, sure, but this movie also has a meaning to it. A meaning about justice and revenge, battling villains and becoming one of them.

This movie is set in a human world. Bruce is just a person. And while I can't imagine how hard must it be to have a life as hard as Bruce's, we can relate to his actions if we really think about what we will do in this situation. I don't think they had a world 'supervillain' said ones in the movie, even though there are supervillains. It's just a human take on them, where you also can relate to supervillains sometimes. A big example is the Scarecrow.

I loved how they placed all the Bat elements in the real world. You should've seen my reaction when I first understood what is Bruce transforming that cave full of bats into.

Batman Begins is a must-watch. It may not be the best movie I've ever seen, but it's definitely good.

10.title: Finally, a Batman movie about Batman.
10.content:
Batman movies in the past have always been about the villain. While villains are often what makes a piece of fiction truly captivating, developing intriguing villains should never be at the expense of developing the main character.

Batman is a character who has CHOSEN to develop a second personality in the way that some people who endure personal tragedies do subconsciously. This is a truly unique decision as most of humanity tries to grieve by moving on with their lives and remembering the good times. Bruce Wayne chooses to become Batman. The question that no other film has really explored is WHY the heir to a billion-dollar enterprise would make such a decision. No human in history has ever made such a decision to my knowledge, so Batman Begins had a hard sell to pitch.

This is the movie's greatest strength. Rather than shying away from this crucial question, Batman Begins embraced it and used some 2 hours and 14 minutes to explore the answer. We are given, for the first time, a real Bruce Wayne to go with our Batman, and the villains are secondary. Perhaps in sequels it is more appropriate to focus on the villain(s), but not before we have a movie explaining who Bruce Wayne is. Finally we do, and there is a decent amount of time explaining that Bruce Wayne has become Batman, and now Bruce Wayne is the real mask, the real charade. Somehow that makes all that is unbelievable about Batman come to life and seem, in some impossible way, to be possible.

On this film versus Tim Burton's 1989 Batman (a large topic of online debate). Burton's Gotham City and depiction of Batman had an atmosphere and world that truly felt like it could produce a character such as Batman, and it really sold us on the Joker. What it did not do was sell us on Bruce Wayne (a mistake that continued for three subsequent films and one more director). When Batman took off the cape and cowl in the 1989 film, Michael Keaton looked the part and performed well, but there was no dialog or plot development leading us to believe that Burce Wayne had any inner turmoil. The reclusiveness of the Bruce Wayne played by Keaton (and three subsequent actors) made the entire film unbelievable. If Bruce Wayne hid away in his mansion nursing battle wounds and was one of the few men alive with the means and motive to become a vigilante AND was generally anti-social, then surely he would be discovered as Batman very quickly.

Of course Bruce Wayne has to be all those things Michael Keaton portrayed him to be: reclusive, introverted, and quietly furious with the world that murdered his parents. It wasn't that Christian Bale is a better actor than Michael Keaton, necessarily, it's that Batman Begins generally does a better job of explaining the reason for Wayne's fury. also, we believe the Bruce Wayne of Batman Begins could keep his moonlighting a secret because he takes measures to build a public image counter to his nature by making himself appear to be the quintessential playboy.

The 1989 film created a beautiful, film noir depiction of Gotham that I love. The 2005 version kept that dark image of Gotham and gave it an almost industrial feeling that mimics that of the city in Blade Runner. Both approaches work because they evoke a feeling of dark desperation. Burton's noir approach didn't work as well when he took it beyond the scenery to the story. Gotham can't be like a Bogart film because it admits that there is a world outside Gotham that is peaceful and normal. Gotham City is supposed to be PARTICULAR in its darkness, and though it scenes are welcome to be dark and evil, it must stand constrastly to the rest of the world and to some of its citizens. There were no brighter elements to the Burton film, no characters that truly seemed innocent. Who was Michael Keaton trying to save?

10.title: The Essence of the Batman Creation
10.content:
Bruce Wayne is the only one true human superhero.

The reason for his triumphs as Batman are primarily due to his personal tragedy at the loss of his parents to a criminal, following the crucial decision to prevent such tragedies while faced with nothing else.

During his self-destructive phase, Bruce Wayne sought training in the martial arts schools that could not be found in western civilization. By the age of twenty two, he acquired enough skill to take on six men at once. As Batman, he would later become the victor of nearly every battle with humans and non-humans alike, wherein, his own all-too-human flesh and blood vessel inevitably brushes death many times, saved mostly in part to his intellect and sagacity, as well as the care of a precious few. His much-too-close experience with victimization as a child, following the personal pain of his loss, has led him to make analytical observations and studies of the criminal element, thusly granting him the utmost awareness of their world. This is what primarily sets him apart from government officials and law-enforcement agents. It must be said that although he operates outside the bounds of the law, he remains within reason, which makes him different from the usual vigilante out for revenge. Hence, in his beginning years as the Batman, he is misunderstood by the law, which later becomes rectified through his friendship and trust in commissioner Gordon as well as his reputable actions. One of his greatest principles is that he will never take a life unless absolutely necessary or to save his own.

An atypical missionary, Bruce Wayne's initiation of the Batman identity was for detective work above all else. At first, he lived to save the city he has always known and to honor the names of his late parents. In the later years of his career, he lives to fight injustice more so than ever. This brought him to assist in the fights alongside real superhumans (with a diverse array of superhuman genetic resources as opposed to simply being a physically healthy, financially wealthy pretty boy with a post dramatic stress disorder) when called to. But the near victimization he experienced as a child and other survivals of smaller life-threatening proportions are the primary motives of what he fights against today as it is written in the books. It can be said that the powers of this particular "superhero" comes from within and manifests themselves physically and mentally.

Batman Begins is the only comic book adaptation that has captured the essence of the origins of Batman.

10.title: The Perfect movie
10.content:
I've been a fan of Tim Burton's two Batman movies since forever. I truly believed that he had captured the batman character and the villains in the perfect way. Then Joel Schumacher came along and basically ruined everything I had loved about the first two movies. And so I gave up and assumed I would never see another decent Batman movie again.

Then Christopher Nolan came along and not only proved me completely wrong but made a batman movie that is an even better depiction of the caped crusaders than Tim Burton's classics.

But not all of the praise can go to Christopher Nolan. All the actors made their characters perfect; Christian bale is perfect as batman/Bruce Wayne because you really believe that this character will dress up as a bat and fight crime in order to avenge his parent's murder. Michael Caine puts in a great performance as Alfred and Cillian Murphy is a frightening, psychotic villain (even if he is a little under-used... but no matter cos I hear he's coming back in The Dark Knight!) Even the Batmobile (or Tumbler) has replaced the original movie one as my favourite. When I first saw photos of it I thought it was a joke. I genuinely believed it would be the worst bat mobile ever. But when I saw it in the cinema it looked AWESOME! The script/story was as good as they get these days. It wasn't too far-fetched so you could still watch this movie and relate to the characters but at the same time it had that fantasy/superhero feeling to it.

In my opinion; the best movie in recent years.

My only worry now is that The Dark Knight (sequel to Batman Begins) will not live up to our expectations. But I have faith in all the cast and crew.

10.title: Batman Begins...and Delivers
10.content:
I saw Batman Begins last night and as I expected, this movie delivered. Christian Bale puts on a wonderful performance as the caped crusader/Bruce Wayne. While watching you really see a difference between the Bruce Wayne and Batman persona.

Christopher Nolan has turned the Batman Franchise around after Joel Shumacher nearly destroyed the franchise. Dare I say it may be better than the original Tim Burton Batman. This film is dark the way a Batman movie should be. It delivers both a comic book feel with a sense of reality. The problem with Joel Schumacher and his direction is that the his Batman had too much of a cartoon feel that you couldn't connect with any of the characters. There were too many characters without any objectives. The characters in Batman Begins all have an objective which is what makes a screenplay a success.

The film also explains how Batman became Batman. All the other previous films explained the origin's of the villains but we never really knew how Batman became Batman. We barely knew why he became Batman. This film's main focus is Batman. The original Batman focused on the Joker, Batman Returns was a story about the Penguin, Forever focused on the Riddler and the fourth Batman focused really on a relationship between Batman and Robin. This one is all about Batman and the man behind the mask. This film also illustrates how Batman gets his "wonderful toys" and how he comes up with his name, his symbol.

And don't worry, there are villains in this film and their motives may be a little cartoonish but like I said earlier, this film does give you a little of that comic book feel to it. I don't want to spoil any of the movie for you so I won't give you the plot but trust me, you will enjoy this film **** out of ****

10.title: Wow
10.content:

As soon as the film started i knew i was not going to be disappointed, the film was just fantastic. Christian Bale is batman, he is dark and serious and yet as Bruce Wayne he is handsome and charming, something i never thought any of the other Batman films accomplished. The supporting characters are all good especially Cillian Murphy as the scarecrow who manages to look sweet and innocent and yet incredibly creepy at all the right moments. The only character i was disappointed with was Rachael played by Katie Holmes who seemed to me out of her depth in amongst so many great actors, but this was a minor disappointment.

Friends that i went to see it with were from all different perspectives one who had never seen batman (who enjoyed it although she was a little confused in some parts), one who had only seen Batman and Robin(shudder) who also enjoyed it and the other who thinks no one can beat Michael Keaton as batman( who enjoyed the movie but still stands by Keaton). 10.title: Nolan transformed a new Batman.
10.content: The first time I saw it, I knew it was the best film in the Batman Franchise. Not only because today we can do whatever we want to do because the film industry broaden its limitation, and taken a new step in visual greatness. If we compare the four Batman movies in today's, the special effects had improved and if Batman wishes to blow up a solid concrete in the rooftop, he can easily do so, very realistic and not cartoonish. But I don't really care about the special effects they put in the movies. It's not the point, the real reason why I love this film is because it was directed by Christopher Nolan (Memento, The Prestige); with his powerful style of directing that will blow you away with its amazing lines, and his cast did a very very strong acting, including the veteran actor, Michael Caine as the ever faithful Alfred Pennyworth, the butler of the Wayne family. And of course the supporting actors, Gary Oldman as Sergeant and soon-to-be Lieutenant Gordon, Liam Neeson as Henri Ducard, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox (same with Q in the James Bond movies). Christian Bale's Bruce Wayne exceeded all the actors that had played it (Michael Keaton, Val Kilmer, and George Clooney). He did a great job of being a billionaire and a playboy, and of course being his alter-ego, Batman. Tim Burton and Joel Schumacher had handled it, but no one does it better than Christopher Nolan! Batman Begins is all about conquering fears and preventing Gotham City from self-destruction. It was delivered to us wonderfully entertaining like Nolan's other films. The transformation of Bruce Wayne to the creature he had feared all his life and his reason for being the Gotham City's Dark Knight is so powerfully shown to us. The Gotham City is dark, dirty and full of criminals everywhere like it always was. Nolan's Gotham City structure is quite amazing, it is darker and had a more realistic tone than the other Batman movies. The film focuses on its people and the humanity. Hans Zimmer's score brought a heavier theme. Batman's first contact in the screen was one of the finest moments in the film, you don't know where he is, where he's coming from and who's his next target. The scene where Batman was talking to Gordon, and when Gordon replied to him he's gone is a cool thing, he did it many times in the film. Whenever Batman is in the screen you can't stop watching him, he's a powerful force in the screen, and he'll just let you drop your mouth when he's making his moves. There are many great scenes in this film, keep a good look at those when you watch it, I've already seen Batman Begins five times, and it's not hard to tell that I'm a big fan of Batman. Scarecrow is the perfect antagonist since it is all about fear, he completes the entire idea of the film. But who's missing in the film? It's the crazy freak, Joker, the archenemy of Gotham's Dark Knight. In the last scene you'll know that he will be the next chaos maker in the next picture.

10.title: Is Batman Begins The Best Batman Movie? (Spoiler Free)
10.content:
You bet your a** it is! I just got back from a showing of the latest Batman installment, and while I have always held Tim Burton's BATMAN in very high regard, it in no way matches the brilliant story and directing shown in this newest installment.

Christopher Nolan (memento) directs from a script penned by David Goyer (Blade 2). The story shows how Bruce Wayne became BATMAN. Now previous entries in the Batman franchise were good in their own right. Tim Burton of course delivered us a great film in 1989, due in part to the performances of Michael Keaton, and of course Jack Nicholson. In the newest film, we have a new Batman, played exquisitely by Christian Bale, and of course a new villain, Scarecrow played by Cillian Murphy.

The Performances in the film were top notch to say the least, from the fear ridden and guilt consuming Bruce Wayne to the maniacal paranoia's of Cillian Murphy. What was executed flawlessly was the direction of the picture. Chris Nolan, still shows us that after 3 films he has what it takes to tell a great story with superb direction. My only complaint in the whole film was the camera work done during the fight sequences... *** Chris... Move the camera's back so we can see the beatings taking place. *** I will admit I did roll my eyes a few times at the over dramatic delivery of Batman's lines from time to time, but it was easily forgotten as the story unfolded. Each performance from Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, & Gary Oldman was terrific and well honed, and you felt for every one of these characters. Liam Neeson gave a truly enlightening performance, where was this performance during Star Wars Ep. 1 I ask... I guess he saved it for Batman Begins.

Chris Nolan succeeded on many lines with this film... Joel Schumacher should take notes, as should a lot of director's of superhero comics turned film. However, Chris cannot get all the credit. David Goyer had a truly superb script, and Warner Brothers should be on their knees kissing his feet thanking him for such a great story. I read the Batman begins script early last year and I told everyone I knew that this is the Batman movie to go see.

This entry into the franchise runs a little long, it comes in around 2 hours and 25 mins, but it goes by so quickly because you are just engrossed in the story from beginning to end. Now while I praise BB for being the best Batman movie ever, I will also extend that praise to the team behind it, including the cast. One thing that I kept flashing back to while watching BB was Christian Bale's performance. His performance reminded me of the same performance he gave as Daytime stock broker Patrick Bateman in American Pyshco. I was smiling from ear to ear every time he would get into his Patrick Bateman mode. It was truly a joy to watch.

Now I know some of you have commented on the 8.6 rating this movie has received on the IMDb.COM boards... well let me tell you, it deserves a 9.5. So do yourself a favor. Turn off your computer, get in the car, head to the cinema, and buy yourself a ticket for Batman Begins. Then go into the theater, sit back and enjoy the ride.

Batman Begins is truly the best Superhero film ever made, and should be used as a model for all future superhero movies.

Rating 9.5 out of 10 Dj

10.title: This is how you start a Batman Franchise !
10.content: I've never come out of a theater feeling so invigorated about a movie! After the collapse of the previous franchise, I found myself long for a movie with a strong story and deep character development. I thought the best way to do justice to Batman was to probe his past and show the very evolution of 8 year old Bruce Wayne into emerging Dark Knight. Batman Begins has delivered on that-IN SPADES!!! Christian Bale has now emerged as the best Batman YET! One thing I had always hoped for is that Batman would finally exude as it's called in Detective Comics #33 (and again in Batman #1), "physical perfection." I knew after hearing that Bale got the part that we would get that. Beyond that I wanted a strong working relationship between Bats and Gordon; we get that. I wanted something of Batman's mastercraft of intimidating thugs; OH, do we get that! The story is compelling, the acting by all the big players is straight and top notch, the pacing is championship caliber, and the action sequences keep you glued to your seat. This is, indeed, the Batman film I've waited for, and feared all to long I'd never get. Nolan, Goyer, Bale, TAKE A BOW!!!

10.title: Amazing
10.content:
I just saw this movie today and I haven't been this amazed by a superhero movie since I saw Superman back when I was five. To me, everything about this movie was amazing. I don't even know where to begin.

The story this movie told was very well done. They took a few liberties with the Batman mythos, but the changes were definitely for the better. The acting was top notch. Liam Neeson plays his part to perfection. I had only seen Michael Cane in a few movies before, but I can definitely see why he is such a respected actor with his portrayal of, Batmans butler/father figure, Alfred, and all the rest of the cast are perfectly cast, including Cillian Murphy who plays the Scarecrow in a way that made me and the friends I went to see the movie with think of Johnny Depp for some reason.

The musical score was so good that immediately after the movie, I went to the Meijer across the street from the theater and bought the soundtrack. The action sequences were amazing. I was sitting at the edge of my seat during the whole chase scene with the Batmobile, and I can not remember the last time I went to a theater and was sitting at the edge of my seat. And the big climactic showdown at the end of the movie, I can't put into words the feeling I had watching it. You have to experience it for yourself.

I very rarely go to see a movie twice in theaters, and I honestly can't wait to get another chance to see this movie. I have never written a review for a movie before I wrote this one, but this movie was so good that I felt I had to. Believe me when I tell you this. This is the highest recommendation I have ever given to any movie.

10.title: Batman Begins is definitely Oscar material
10.content:
There have been so few movies released this year, which in my opinion would qualify for an Oscar.

But Batman Begins is one that definitely deserves nominations in several categories, especially for the acting.

I hope that nobody makes the mistake of avoiding this movie, because they didn't like the previous Batman movies, because this one is different. It sets a new standard for Super Hero movies, putting it into the same class as 'Lord of the Rings' as a fantasy movie. I hope that we will see more Batman sequels of this quality.

Christian Bale is really convincing as Batman, and this movie should put him in the category of a mega star. The movie has a great plot, tight scripting, and is emotionally moving. We get the back story of why and how Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) became Batman, and the exciting development of his character, and personality, including his darker side.

Director Christopher Nolan has created a great movie which will become in my view a classic.

Liam Neeson and Michael Caine were both very convincing, in their roles as well.

The movie didn't rely too much on special effects, although what there was, was very well done, and not readily identifiable as being special effects, which in my opinion is a disadvantage. This movie will definitely be added to my collection of DVDs.

Not wanting to create a spoiler, I will not say too much about the other characters, except to say that they are wonderfully drawn, and acted. I cannot think of a single performance by any actor, who didn't do this story justice.

Everything in this movie works, this is the first Batman movie that I have really liked.

The soundtrack by Hans Zimmer & James Newton Howard is excellent, and moving, and it sets the emotional pace necessary, and I will be buying the sound track as well.

10.title: Redemption
10.content:
Sadly, I've seen all the Batman films. Up until now, they were pretty much a waste of my precious time on this Earth. Then I saw "Batman Begins" and my jaw hit the floor.

Or as I call it, "Batman: the Apology" or "Batman Redeemed." This is the Batman that more than makes up for all the others. In fact, this is the only Batman movie you need to see. And you NEED to see it! This wasn't yet another director pasting the Batman name on their own twisted version of the genre - this is the de facto Batman, as he was, as he is, so accurately portrayed that DC comics themselves put their own mark of approval on it. You can tell that many scenes, images, and ideas were pulled directly from the DC archives, and even the most hardcore original comic fan would be hard pressed to find anything wrong with this film.

As a rule, movies based of comic book characters usually suck. Batman Begins is the exception to that rule. If you never see any other Batman movie (and for your own sake, don't), see this one. You won't regret it.

10.title: The film's strength lies in its grounded
10.content:
"Batman Begins" (2005)

"Batman Begins," directed by Christopher Nolan, is a masterful reboot of the Batman franchise that delves into the origins of the iconic superhero. Christian Bale delivers a compelling performance as Bruce Wayne, capturing the character's transformation from a tormented billionaire to the fearsome vigilante, Batman.

The film's strength lies in its grounded, realistic approach to the Batman mythos. Nolan skillfully explores Bruce Wayne's motivations and the psychological trauma that drives him to fight crime. The supporting cast, including Michael Caine as Alfred, Liam Neeson as Ra's al Ghul, and Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon, add depth and gravitas to the story.

"Batman Begins" also excels in its action sequences and visuals, creating a gritty, atmospheric Gotham City. The narrative is well-paced, balancing intense action with thoughtful character development. Hans Zimmer's score enhances the film's dramatic tension and emotional weight.

Overall, "Batman Begins" is a riveting origin story that revitalizes the Batman legend, setting a new standard for superhero films. It's a must-watch for fans of the Dark Knight and anyone who appreciates a well-crafted, character-driven action movie.

10.title: Christopher Nolan Is a genius **Partial Spoiler**

10.title: Wow!
10.content:
This move was superb! I am just in awe. After all those years of pathetic excuses for a a Batman movie they finally got it right. *bows to Nolan* Thank you, thank you, thank you!

There was actually good acting. Before the only good acting in Batman was done by Jack Nicholson as the Joker, Jim Carrey as the Riddler, and Micheal Keaton was an okay Batman. But this. This was just awesome. Christopher Bale was the perfect Batman. He was dark and brooding. I loved how he did the deeper voice when he was Batman. Liam Neeson was wonderful. Gary Oldman was perfect. Michael Caine was the perfect Alfred. I had heard a lot of bad reviews for Katie Holmes before I went, and I was expecting her to be terrible, but she really didn't bug me. Yes, she wasn't as good as the rest of the cast, but I don't think she did badly. And finally, my favorite, Cillian Murphy was perfectly evil and crazy! I've seen Murphy in a couple other things and he was always a good character, so even though I trusted he would do fine, I was curious to see if he could be evil. He was so awesome! In my opinion any time he was in a scene you automatically watch him. He took an (in my opinion) uninteresting villain and turned him into someone to be feared.

I was so grateful that there weren't any cheesy lines thrown in. In fact, I can't remember one line I didn't like. I went with my two sisters and my mom, and one of my sisters and my mom got a bit confused by what was happening. I think this is because they never read comic books, and as a result are not used to the plots that are involved. If you are not a comic fan it may be a bit difficult to understand, but I think if you pay close enough attention, you'll get it. This movie is definitely worth seeing!

10.title: Excellent

But my highest commendment actorwise would go to Liam Neeson. Liam was absolutely perfect. When he played Ra's al Ghul, he was so different from playing Henri Ducard. He did not alter anything about himself, but one thing: His personality. Liam knows how to become the character he's playing. His performance was absolutely enthralling. The other performers were extraordinary as well. Katie Holmes, Morgan Freeman, and Gary Oldman. The best commendment of all would go to Christopher Nolan and David Goyer. Excellent plot formation. Now that I've bored you by having you read all of this; I think I'll end it by saying: Batman Begins has an extraordinary cast. I think Bob Kane would be proud. If you want to see a movie that lives up to the legend...well...look no further.

10.title: The best Batman film ever!!!

He trains with the League of Shadows. He meets Lucius Fox, who is the scientific head of Wayne enterprises. He gives Bruce the car, weapons and equipment, and the suit. He learns that a hallucinogen is going to destroy the city. It turns out that the league is behind it. Christen Bale is great. Michael Caine, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, and Morgan Freeman were also good. We meet the Scarecrow, who was very frighting and cool looking. I had no regrets seeing this.

10.title: A New Spin on The Batman Mythology
10.content:
"Batman Begins," under the direction of Christohper Nolan (Memento), breathes new life into a franchise that was nearly demolished with "Batman And Robin." Christian Bale's Bruce Wayne/Batman is more dark than Michael Keaton's version. Bruce clearly has issues with bats and the death of his parents (His fear of bats caused him to want to leave the theater the night his parents where killed). Gotham City is a cesspool of corruption, with gangster Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson)running the town. During Bruce's journey, he is soon trained by Ducard (Liam Neeson)to perfect his fighting skills. Working with a cult run by Ra's Al-Ghul (Ken Watanabe), he starts to take shape into becoming The Dark Knight.

Returning to Gotham City, Wayne sees that things have gotten worse. With the help of Alfred his butler (Michael Caine),Luscious Fox, an employee of Wayne Enterprises (Morgan Freeman)and the assistance of a policeman named Gordon (Gary Oldman, playing a good guy for once), the legend of Batman grows. However, with Falcone and The Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy)trying to run Gotham City, it's not an easy task. Plus, there is an unexpected wrinkle in the mix as well.

With the exception of Katie Holmes as Wayne's childhood friend (And prosecuting attorney)Rachel Dawes, all of the performances are first rate (Particularly Oldman, with a bit of comedy relief). It is also interesting in seeing how the Batcave and The Batmobile had evolved (The Batmobile looking like a huge ATV). There is lots of action from start to finish, and a glimpse of things to come (Particularly a playing card with a joker on it!). I am looking forward to what comes next.

10.title: There will never be a better Batman

10.title: Absolutely stunning

I was surprised at how dark it actually was! I was hoping it would be dark and thought it would be, but there were some demented parts that were shocking to me. So trippy! The casting was great and the storyline was fantastic. Maybe the only problem I'd have with that is it might have been even cooler if Oldman were the bad guy! Couldn't Rachel have driven a nicer car than a Ford Taurus? Overall it was top notch and I can't wait for the next one. 10/10 for me.

10.title: The way Batman should have been on the big screen long ago!!!

After the VERY average Batman movies of the 90s, "Batman Begins" is an awesome portrayal of the Dark Knight the way fans of the comic & graphic novels will appreciate.

The casting of Batman Begins is super (Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman)!! The dialogue is loaded with thought provoking pieces of philosophy. The action scenes are nail biting, yet not "campy" (in the sense that any CG special effects are hard to spot!).

Even non-Batman fans will love this movie. (My wife, who is not a Batman fan, thought the film was better than Star Wars Episode 3)! Kudos to an awesome & LONG overdue Batman film that takes the character & what he stands for SERIOUSLY!!

10.title: Batman Begins - Movie Review
10.content:
Directed by Christopher Nolan and starring Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, Cillian Murphy, Tom Wilkinson, Rutger Hauer, Ken Watanabe and Morgan Freeman.

After witnessing his parents' murders, Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) travels the world seeking the means to fight injustice. With the help of his trusted butler Alfred (Michael Caine), detective Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman) and his ally Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman), Wayne returns to Gotham and unleashes his alter-ego: Batman, a masked crusader who uses strength, intellect and high-tech weaponry to fight evil.

This movie is brilliant! This movie has great acting, great storytelling and great characters.

10.title: An excellent adaptation from the comic-book
10.content: I must admit it: I had my greatest expectations when I knew that Christopher "Memento" Nolan was going to direct a new Batman movie. The Dark Knight was always my favorite comic-book hero, and I was expecting a great movie adaptation since the last decent Batman movie: Tim Burton's "Batman Returns" (1992). But my expectations where greatly overwhelmed when I began to see "Batman Begins": surely, we don't have the the gargoyles and pointy towers that underlined the name of Gotham City in Burton's movies. We don't have the yellow and black Batman's symbol. But we have something far great: a dark, corrupted and violent city, where half of the authorities have been bought by the mafia, and the other half is waiting to be bought. Here, the Gothic atmosphere is given by the inhabitants of Gotham and their corrupted shadow leaders, not by the architecture. The plot of the film and the atmosphere reminds me a lot of the comic-book "Batman: Year One", written by Frank Miller, where the origin of the Dark Knight was re-written from a more modern perspective than it had back in 1940. Both the comic and Nolan's movie show us the events that pushed Bruce Wayne to wear the cape and the mask of a bat to fight against crime without killing. The emphasis is put in Wayne's physical and psychological development: he must achieve a state of perfection in both aspects of himself to control his own fear and use it like his most powerful weapon against the criminals. Even when we have a spectacular display of special effects, the power of Nolan's film is in his characters and they relationships. That's why the character of Jim Gordon (who was put aside in Burton's films) has taken a more relevant role. One of the most important relationships of the Batman comic-book is the friendship between Batman and Gordon, the only friend of Batman that doesn't know his secret identity. Anyway, I could write paragraphs and paragraphs about how Nolan achieves to create the darkness that has taken the hearts of Gotham's inhabitants, how he successfully writes an essay about the decadence of the civilization and the heroics efforts to save it, and the way he rescues the shadowy Batman of the comic-book, a hero tormented by its past and his uncertain balance between sanity and insanity.

10.title: One of the best movies I've seen
10.content: I usually have a hard time going to "action" movies as I'm easily over stimulated and my mind spends time trying to decipher the plot to the point of spoiling the movie for me. I am glad to say that while this movie was not slow it wasn't so fast that I couldn't keep up with it. The audience at the theater we saw it at seemed mesmerized. I don't recall seeing many people leave for snacks etc. I thought it had a good balance of action, and comedy a little dash of romance without being sick and some moving moments. It spoke of social problems without being so PC as to appear preachy which is also quite refreshing. I very good movie easily one of my all time favorites. I hope they make a sequel that is as good then I will really be happy.

10.title: One of the best movies I've seen in a long time
10.content:
First of all, I'm not a comic fan. I'm a frequent movie goer who doesn't care about any accuracy of comic-to-movie adaptations. I simply want to see a good movie. Batman Begins, however, is an excellent movie regardless of its comic book nature. As the matter of fact, it's one of the best movies I've seen in a long time. It deserves (at least) the top 100 movie of all time.

Nolan has done an amazing job capturing the world of Batman, making you feel as if you're right next beside Bruce Wayne, understanding him as person with enormous sense of vulnerability, anger and sadness. In short, it's like understanding your best friends' personal insecurities. It brings you closer to them while gaining tremendous affection at the same time.

Great story, great screenplay, great background drops (ie. magnificent and realistic Gotham), great acting (Even Katie Holmes acts very well. Too bad her baby-face gets in the way). Christian Bale has done an excellent job both as Bruce Wayne and Batman, acting as two completely different people. Overall, great great great great movie. Big thumbs up to Nolan and his company.

I'm concerned that some reviewers give this movie 1 out of 10 rating because of minor details like "joker is supposed to kill Batman's parents" or "Batman's city is supposed to look Gothic" and sort. I can understand their lifelong devotion to the comic book. Heck, this movie is not flawless either (so isn't GodFather). But to give Batman Begins "1" rating is nonsense. "1" is for the ultimate mediocre movies like "The Perfect Man" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded," certainly not Batman Begins. Batman Begins deserves at least "7." Plus, if a reviewer tends to give mediocre ratings because he/she likes to nitpick things to death, then fix that habit first before watching this movie. As the matter of fact, fix that habit before watching any movie at all. Just chill out and enjoy the show.

Some viewers might find the Batman Begins to be boring/dragging too long. That's understandable because for today's high-pace/fast-action standard, even GodFather would seem to be a very slow and dragging movie. Nevertheless, it's still considered to be the greatest movie of all times. Batman Begins is similar to that. One needs to calm down while watching the movie to notice all its finer details and characters. I've seen a lot of extremely crappy movies in my life that are much less than 2 hours long and felt asleep throughout, yet Batman Begins gets my full attention from beginning to end. That's quite an accomplishment for any movie that lasts beyond 2 hour.

Viewers should not expect this movie to be funny, mindless, and full-of-flashy-action. Thousands of other movies and their copycats already serve that purpose and are already out there in big bulks (especially in recent years). But if you want a much higher level movie, then watch Batman Begins.

10.title: Finally a Batman Movie Comic Fans can be proud of
10.content:
As a long time fan of Batman I have longed to see a big screen Batman that displayed the depth and power of the character I had come to enjoy while reading: Batman: Year One, Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Batman: The Long Halloween, Batman: The Killing Joke.

I longed for a Batman movie where Batman was not overshadowed by the villains he fights. When I first heard about this movie I almost screamed in pain, expecting another Joel Schuemacher insult to Batman. A movie that had more in common with the campy Adam West series of the 60's then the character I had come to enjoy in the comic books.

Walking in with no expectations I was blown away by what I saw. Here was a movie that not only reached the dark, film noir levels of Tim Burton's original Batman, but reached even farther. I could almost see flashes of Frank Miller in the script with I'm sure fans of Batman: Year One will recognize and enjoy.

I know some people don't like how the fight scenes were shot in this film, but I think they were perfect. You don't get to see all of Batman's style, but it makes the fights seem more real. Like you are there trying to follow a real fight between Batman and the thugs of Gothman's underworld. It heighten's the drama, and makes the movie seem less like just another Hollywood action film with crisp easy to see fights. If there is a sequel I implore Chris Nolan to leave the fight scenes like he did in this movie.

Batman Begins is filled with great performance from Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Liam Nieson, and Gary Oldman. But not even that all-star supporting cast can steal the light from Christian Bale. As Batman he delivers the sharp obessiveness that I had come to look for in Batman. For that is the Key in my mind to Batman, Bruce Wayne died the night his parents died, and in the pain of that night Batman was born.

10.title: Bats are nocturnal!
10.content:
The title of this comment is an actual line from the movie. Bruce says it when Alfred wakes him in the afternoon, the day after his first night out as a superhero. This is the kind of humor you can expect from the film. It sometimes appears in unexpected situations, which makes it that much better. The Batman films can't really be classified as comedy, but they all had funny bits, and this one is no exception.

That said, the action is certainly not boring. We get to see the young Bruce Wayne in flashbacks and nightmares, and we get a better idea of why he became Batman in the first place. Then we see him training, occasionally getting his butt kicked, and learning how to navigate Gotham City as a shadowy ninja-like crime fighter.

The actors all did very well, even Katie Holmes. That one surprised me a little. I'm no fan of hers, and I wasn't sure she belonged in a Batman movie, but she pulled off her character pretty well. Really, the female lead characters in the Batman movies aren't there to be realistic, wonderful characters. They're there as a contrast to the city itself - Gotham is huge, dark, Gothic, and filled with crime and other horrors. Each of the female leads embodied a different idealistic quality. The Katie Holmes character was the pretty assistant D.A. only interested in making sure justice was done in every situation. Remember Vicki Vale? The Kim Basinger character was the intrepid reporter looking to write a fair and revealing story about Batman, to show the world his true motivations. Blah blah blah. They're secondary, important to the plot but ultimately forgettable, for the most part. Katie Holmes was no exception, and she did a decent job of it.

Christian Bale was absolutely the right choice for this Batman. He has such a wide range of talents when it comes to acting, it's almost difficult to believe he's only one person. Really, would anyone think the same actor could play the lead in a live-action Disney musical about overworked children AND one of the best incarnations of Batman on screen? Usually not, but there you go. He's funny in the right places, and he's able to convey a lot of emotion with his face and voice, a talent that is all too rare these days. Also, his role as the psychotic Patrick Bateman in "American Psycho" proved he's got the chops to play dark and demented. I've thought of Batman that way since the early Tim Burton films, with Michael Keaton.

Michael Caine was the perfect Alfred. He was able to show us how much the butler really loved the Wayne family, and when the parents were killed he assumed the role of surrogate father to the grieving child left behind. Caine was also good at conveying that sense of aristocratic attitude I saw in the older versions of Alfred without going over the top.

I love Morgan Freeman, so I'm biased on this one. I love everything he does, including this role. Lucius Fox was every inch the eccentric inventor. He seemed like he was glad to see his creations finally put to good use. Plus, he got to ride in the car, and he got to show Batman how to use all the cool gadgets on the utility belt. Great role, played by the right actor.

At first, I thought Cillian Murphy was the guy from Eurotrip. I looked him up, and he isn't. While I can't quite remember what else I may have seen Murphy in, it doesn't really matter. I loved him as Scarecrow. It was interesting to me, to see what kind of villain Scarecrow really was. No super powers at all, no mutations, no gadgets except the mask and the psychotropic drug he used to work his evil magic, but it worked. Hey, Batman doesn't have any powers either. He's got gadgets though, and lots of training. Scarecrow has a background in psychiatry, drugs and a cool villain mask. And with these few tools he was able to bring Gotham City to turmoil within the course of this almost two-and-a-half hour movie. The mark of a great villain is his ability to do a lot of evil with very little power or help. This guy is one of the greats.

Really, there is no way to spoil this movie. I could sit here and type the script verbatim, and those who read it would still enjoy the movie. There would still be surprises, if only visual ones. It's worth the price of admission just to see what Gotham City looks like in this film. And they managed to make it look real, like a city that might really exist somewhere out there.

That's the word for this film: real. Batman is seen as a real guy, doing things other real people could do with the right training and enough money. Scarecrow/Dr. Crane is a realistic - if slightly unbalanced - head shrinker who simply gets overly fascinated by the mind of the criminal psychotic. Everything ties together in the end, and there is some good foreshadowing to get us hooked on the Batman story until the end of time.

10.title: "Gripping origin story, *Batman Begins* reinvents the Dark Knight with depth, action, and heart."
10.content: *Batman Begins* is a masterful reboot of the Dark Knight saga, directed by Christopher Nolan. The film explores Bruce Wayne's journey from a traumatized orphan to Gotham's vigilante hero, offering a grounded and gritty origin story. Christian Bale delivers a compelling performance as Batman, supported by a stellar cast, including Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, and Gary Oldman. Hans Zimmer's powerful score and the realistic portrayal of Gotham elevate the film. With its blend of emotional depth, thrilling action, and moral complexity, *Batman Begins* sets a high standard for superhero storytelling, redefining the genre for a new era.

So, we have a new story, we witness the birth of the hero himself, and it is done in a much darker way than the previous batman movies. It is, indeed, a good thing.

The story itself is very realistic, in my opinion. Christopher Nolan did a fabulous directing job. Christian Bale is definitely the hottest actor around. I mean it in the sense that he simply knows how to behave, how to perform, like very few know. He really is the perfect Bruce Wayne. The rest of the cast was also brilliant. 10.title: Awesome
10.content:
I have to admit I'm not really a huge batman fan. Batman always sort of lacked the 'superhero' magic for me. But I loved what they did with this movie. They took the 'lack of magic' and replaced it with deep, emotional connections and it wound up as a kind of introspective journey (for the viewer).

And I should know, by now, to avoid the forums what with their proclamations of Razzies, box office flops and "Katie Holmes sucked"s. The movie's just shot after beautiful shot (with lots of memorable lines) and I have no doubts in its success at the box office. Katie was great, given her small role; the others were perfectly casted (see who, above); and overall Batman Begins added up to a very wholesome and intelligently-crafted flick.

It's been a fair while since I've left a cinema truly satisfied; there always seems to be something missing. This, however, is a film that just has to be seen on the big screen. If not for Katie/Christian and some fun special effects, then for the sweeping shots of a truly realistic Gotham City.
