10.title: Batman Begins - Cinema bows to the Bat.
10.content:
Batman Begins, and he stars in the best film of our time. If this grosses any less than $400 million, and gets anything less than 4 stars from critics, Batman will seek ways to fight that injustice. Quite frankly, there's never been a more gripping film. Its a character-driven masterpiece, clocking in at two-and-a-half hours. The story is top notch, every cast member gives the performance of their career.

Gotham city makes for an astounding backdrop that no real city could top. The soundtrack, despite the lack of Danny Elfman's classic theme and cues, is terrific. The action, while regarded by some as chaotic, is perhaps the most thrilling blur of action ever unleashed on the big screen. Its intoxicatingly intense. This movie thrilled me from beginning to end, and likewise for everyone I know. Oh, and this Batman is angry. Are you ready to begin?

10.title: Batman has only just begun...
10.content:
In 1989, 'Batman' soared into Hollywood, breaking box-office records. Everybody thought that Michael Keaton was a lame choice, but soon grew to love him as the Caped Crusader, who also starred alongside one of the most known villains - The Joker. Yes, Jack Nicholson truly made the film what it was, and so is a classic in Tim Burton's list...

'Batman Returns' was next, once again starring Michael Keaton as the troubled Bruce Wayne. The villain was now 'The Pwnguin', played by an unusual choice - Danny DeVito. It seemed to work, but not everybody was convinced that this was the film that Tim Burton wanted to make. Selina Kyle as the infamous Catwoman, and Christopher Walken as evil Max Shreck.

'Batman Forever' was next - minus Michael Keaton, and minus Tim Burton. Not a very good sign, but Val Kilmer impressed (slightly) as Batman, but at least we had Jim Carrey and Tommy Lee Jones to accompany him. As for that, Michael Gough and Nicole Kidman as well!

I don't think we really need to say much for 'Batman and Robin', over then that it resurrected the franchise, well and truly...

Or so you thought!!!

Now 'Batman Begins' is here, the franchise has soared back into Hollywood, scooping number ones all across the world. Christian Bale steps into Keaton's, Kilmer's, and er, Clooney's shoes - and brings us right back to the beginning. After his parent's death, Bruce Wayne's life goes from bad to worse. He is thrown into a foreign prison, where he meets ruthless Henri Ducard - (an amazing Liam Neeson) - who brings Bruce to the master of the 'League of Shadows', Ra's Al Ghul, (A slightly flawed Ken Watanabe). Here, Wayne is beefed up to become the new master, but takes a dangerous gamble, and decides to bust villainy in Gotham City - cue big black cars and long black capes!

Director of 'Memento' and 'Insomnia', Christopher Nolan directs and makes the film something it isn't, a psychological mix of fear and vengeance. This is very different to every other film, but nobody should be complaining. These are the basis of the film. Each line in the film contains meaningful, emotional, witty truth; the script id truly one of the best in many years. Christopher Nolan has worked a masterpiece (again), and starts as he means to go on (he's signed up to do two more prequels)! You would call this film a prequel, but it is actually a dark biopic of Bruce Wayne.

As Nolan has now proved he isn't going to let Spielberg go easily, Tom Cruise had better watch out. Star of 'American Psycho' and 'Equilibrium', Christian Bale is fast becoming one of Hollywood's leading men. He has proved his devotedness - as a 12 year old in Spuielberg's 'Empire of the Sun', and losing up to 64lbs for his role in 'The Machinist' - and his status is growing by the second.

'Memento' is the film Bale didn't star in, whilst 'The Machinist' is the film that Nolan didn't direct - they are a perfect team up.

Cillian Murphy fares brilliantly as Dr Jonathan Crane, who scares people with his hallucinogen gas, which - when he wears his mask - turns him into the Scarecrow. Katie Holmes is above average as childhood sweetheart Rachel Dawes. Gary Oldman is brilliant as Jim Gordon, as is Tom Wilkinson as Carmine Falcone. But, as amazing as ever, Michael Caine is the best as Michael Gough's character - Alfred the Butler...

With one of the best scripts written for cinema, amazing set pieces and scary, atmospheric acting, 'Batman Begins' is an instant classic. The first hour is all talk - the last hour is pure action!

10.title: A Batman to Remember
10.content:
As fans of the Batman series we have suffered through two lousy movies at best. The years of Michael Keaton had long passed us by and George Clooney and Val Kilmer had shown us exactly what we did not want Batman to be. Today I can honestly say this has all changed. Christian Bale has rekindled a feeling for Batman that most of us have not experienced since the days of Micheal Keaton. However, the credit for this outstanding movie does not only lay with Christian Bale. Each and every person in this movie is what makes it so amazing. Christian Bale is to date the most believable Batman we as fans have witnessed. Katie Holmes (who I personally do not favor) did a great job as she did not overact her part in this movie. Morgan Freeman was his usual self as he put on a great performance with what little screen time he had during this movie. The special effects were amazing as were the fight scenes. I realize that Star Wars and Batman are two completely different arenas, but the fight scenes in Batman put those in Revenge of the Sith to shame.

Any true fan would realize that the bulk of the credit here should go to director Christopher Nolan. The man who brought us Momento gives another great directory performance with his interpretation of Batman. Truth be told this is not a movie for young children. This is not a Batman with a fake Gotham City and toys that all kids would enjoy seeing. Instead Nolan gives us a world of reality, one that each and everyone of us can relate to. To me that is the greatest accomplishment of Batman Begins; the fact that we can watch as viewers and actually relate to the slums and downtrodden way of life this movie portrays.

If you are a fan of dark movies with amazing action sequences I suggest you take a chance on Batman Begins. It may be a long movie (with running time actually being over two hours) but it will not seem as if the movie is two hours long. The action mixed with the amazing acting will make you remember what Batman was supposed to be: a dark yet driven person who would do anything possible to stop the plight that has hit Gotham City.

10.title: The Best Batman Movie Ever!
10.content: I just came back from the 7:00 showing and I loved it. This is finally the Batman movie I've wanted for so long. The beginning showed an excellent origin of Batman, like he deserves. Bale was perfect for the role, I loved his Batman voice. Also, his amazing gadgets and dark methods were incredibly portrayed throughout the film. The fight scenes were great, Batman actually fought like Batman, he stayed in the shadows and used his gadgets. The Scarecrow was frightening, Ras al Gual was sinister and evil, and the ending was great. I also loved when Bruce Wayne made pg 8 in the newspaper. It was very funny. Those of you who saw it knows what I mean. Defiantly the best Batman movie yet.

10.title: Finally, a movie worth paying to see again.
10.content: A movie I cant wait to *pay* to see again. Christian Bale is *perfectly* cast and I had misgivings about him a bit, but I am a fan of his. Stunts, action, plot all amazing. Very little CGI which was a breath of fresh air. Liam Neeson was just off the hook as was Michael Caine as Alfred and Gary Oldman rounded out the supporting cast very well. I wasn't too stoked about Katie Holmes considering all the "TomKat" hype but at least it didn't interfere with the integrity of the movie. They DEFINITELY got Batman right this time, and I have the Dark Knight and DK2 series by Frank Miller -- autographed. Show stopper: The Batmobile. I hope the production designer gets some type of kudos for his work because this movie came together perfectly. I cannot wait for the sequel and when the DVD comes out I'll definitely be pre-ordering because the extras must be jaw dropping.

10.title: Not just another Batman movie
10.content: I saw this movie the day it opened and I have to say, it was one of the best movies I've seen in a long time. I think the thing that really makes this movie is the fact that the makers didn't set out to simply spit out another Batman film. Instead, they made a great film that happened to be about Batman. The other thing about this movie is the amazing cast. However, it is not merely their presence in the film that makes it worth seeing; it is their performances and their willingness to fully take on their roles. Other Batman movies have had great casts, but the actors seem to be goofing off and not really trying to put on a good performance. This is because all the other Batman films were just that: Batman films. This movie, as I said, is an amazing film that happens to be about Batman. It makes every other cinematic attempt at telling this story look silly and half-hearted.

10.title: Best Batman Movie
10.content:
I've always been a fan of the dark knight, but not always a fan of the way that he was portrayed in movies. Christian Bale does an amazing job at playing up Batman's darker side and his dueling personality Bruce Wayne. Bale is by far the best choice for a Batman that there's ever been. Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman were also brilliant in their parts. This stellar cast really shines among a more than stellar movie.

Another big plus about this Batman movie was the cinematography. There were some very awe inspiring take your breath away moments in the movie where you could feel yourself being pulled in along side of the battles.

I would not however recommend this movie to the lighthearted who are expecting the 'cartoon' version. It's dark humor and personality are what makes it great. I will surely be seeing it again in theaters and owning it right away.

10.title: The completely remade image of Batman.
10.content:
**** out of ****

If there ever was a movie which could be not only so original, it would be great, but also would make us forget the other prequel movies of it, that movie would definitely be Batman Begins. Do you know when you watch a movie, and then you watch a sequel? Even if the sequel is always supposed to be different, even though at almost many times, it becomes imitation of the original, you still see some resemblance of the two movies, like same styles, same scenarios or same ideas. Maybe the sequel may evolve, maybe not. But Batman Begins is kinda different. Not only it is a movie that actually evolved a lot from its other prequels, but also a totally unique and brand new movie where you will not see many (or none) resemblances because the film-making changed completely to make us see Batman in a total different way.

In fact, when the movie ended and the credits begin to roll, I immediately told my friends that this is the first Batman movie. There wasn't any Batman movies before this one, this is the first. Finally Batman arrives at the big screen. For the first time ever. I know that this isn't true, but that's the feeling I had when I watched it. I don't know how the sequels will be (because if there is going to be three Spider-Man movies, why can't we have three Batman movies?), but the first one surely was a great start for (we hope) a great trilogy.

As a friend of mine even said: "This movie remade the batman image completely." Watch it and you'll agree right away. Batman Begins, nicely directed by Christopher Nolan, tells the story of the beginning of Bruce Wayne's life. How and why he became Batman. This time, the bat-man is played by Christian Bale. I still think that Michael Keaton is the best, but Bale was great too. At the party, the scene where Bruce Wayne says goodbye to his guests is one of the greatest proofs that Bale plays Bruce Wayne very good! Michael Caine is good also as Alfred (he never let me down in one of his performances), but still I find out that Michael Gough was much better, not only because of his performance, but because he really looked like Alfred. The rest of the cast includes great actors, some of them, very unlikely to appear in a batman movie, but they did. Cillian Murphy, Morgan Freeman, Rutger Hauer, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman and Liam Neesom. This last one is great as one of the villains.

Overall, Batman Begins is the batman movie. Even for those who are not fan of the comic books we'll sure to enjoy this movie, as in my country, many people really did. I just give a 9 out of 10, because I guess that sometimes, when you look at it, this movie looks like a crime movie. This happens because of the many sub-plots and because of the long-waiting for finally see Bruce Wayne in the batman costume. But getting past that scenes (which are not by any means, unnecessary, they're just the trigger to be pulled for us to see the rest of the movie), what happens next is of total delight.

10.title: "Batman Begins" his war against organized crime that threatens Gotham City.
10.content: This is the first installment in Christopher Nolan's nearly flawless-ans some would say flawless-Batman franchise. It covers the origin story of Bruce Wayne becoming Batman and his first big showdown to save Gotham City from "the criminals and the corrupt." This is, in my humble opinion, the best of all Batman, Super Hero, and Comic Book movies to date. Perhaps the neatest thing about this trilogy is that they don't feel like "super hero" movies at all. They are simply about one man taking justice into his own hands simply for the sake of GOOD. This movie is only the start to an epic trilogy, but when all is said and done I have to say that this is the strongest movie of the trilogy, going into depth of what Bruce Wayne has done with his past several years to become the hope that Gotham needs, and what he plans to do with his next several years. On behalf of all fans of ANY movie genre, THANK YOU to Chris Nolan and all who made this film and trilogy the greatness that it is. 10 stars for this one.

10.title: Finally a Batman movie about Batman
10.content: ***May contain spoilers*** Finally after sitting through watching Joker dance around to Prince, a obnoxious Penguin, Two-Face and Riddler chew an ungodly amount of scenery, and hear Mr. Freeze talk of not getting sent back to "da coola" we finally see a Batman movie that focuses on what the others didn't... Batman. While the others got bogged down focusing on the villain of the hour, Begins has the caped crusader in all his glory. Focusin of the fear that he uses to defeat his foes it is by far the best adaptation of Batman to grace the screen. And with 2 sequels in the works it looks like Batman will finally be done the right way.

10.title: Possibly the best movie ever made.
10.content:
I can't think of where to start, this is just such a great movie. When I first heard of this I thought of seeing it and thinking, hey it'll be fun. Little did I know that this movie would leave a lasting impression on my life.

Everything is perfect, even Katie Holms' acting was superb in this. (Not that she's a bad actress, I just heard some negative stuff about her) Batman begins explores the origin of the caped crusader, starting out in a desolate Chinese prison and ending in a clash of the titans hundreds of feet above Gotham. The music was dramatic and fast paced. The characters where incredible. The sets were were dark and true to Gotham. And the special effects were amazing. It doesn't matter whether your a batman fan or not, See This Movie!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

10.title: Incredibly Awesome!
10.content: If you're like me and the millions of other Americans bored to tears with the outbreak of big-screen ComicBook adaptations, you're also a little hesitant about paying to see yet another director blemish the name of the Knight in Black. Well I'm here to tell you, get up now and go see this movie! It is absolutely perfect in every way. I was completely engrossed in the story the entire way through. It explores so many deeper points of Bruce Wayne while also providing a good dose of the asskicking and blowingshitup-ness that every good SuperHero movie needs. In short, this movie (or series of movies, as they have signed Bale on for three movies already) is exactly what every Batman fanatic has been looking for.

10.title: Best Superhero Movie Ever
10.content:
I usually reserve judgment on movies until months after I've seen them in order to be able to properly reflect on how they compare with other movies...but in this case, it's safe to say that Batman Begins is the best superhero movie EVER! This is the way the movie should have been done in 1989 (begin a franchise with the character's origin...what a concept!!!). Let me also say that I've been an avid comic book collector for the past 25 years, to include Batman. I never liked any of the first four Batman films, although I gained an appreciation for the first Batman after watching the horrendous "Batman and Robin" by Joel Schumacher. I also thought Val Kilmer did a good job as Batman, despite the fact that he was burdened with a terrible script.

That said, Christian Bale's performance is the definitive Bruce Wayne/Batman. The story draws you in immediately and makes you understand why Bruce took his course of action in becoming Batman (much more believable than Anakin's transformation to Darth Vader). Supporting cast is the best of any superhero movie...check out the interaction between Bruce and Alfred, Bruce and Lucius, Batman and Gordon, even Bruce and Rachel (I'm one of the few who didn't think Katie Holmes' performance was that bad). Ra's Al Gould and the Scarecrow are great villains who don't steal the show from the hero (as in previous Batman films...actually making a Batman film about Batman--what a concept!!!) Top off great acting, a great story, pulse- pounding action, and the best Batmobile of the franchise, and you've got the best superhero movie ever (X-Men 2 is a close second, followed by the Spider-Man films and Superman I and II). A must see, and one of those rare films I give a 10/10.

10.title: An Incredible Start To An Incredible Trilogy
10.content: Batman Begins is like Batman's origin story. It has the whole parent death thing and the training but it is still amazing. While most people think that superhero origins are an incredibly boring start to films, this will put a smile on your face, ready for The Dark Knight. Christian Bale's superb acting and two brilliant villains give this blockbuster a 10/10 rating.

10.title: The Batman movie that we have all been waiting on.
10.content:
This is what Batman is all about. Not a nipple clad cartoon, but a Batman that uses fear and his well explained gadgets to terrorize the criminals of Gotham city.

The cast. What can you say about this amazing cast? Christian Bale shines as the caped crusader. Gary Oldman is a perfect young Gordon. Michael Caine is outstanding as Alfred Pennyworth. Cillian Murphy really stood out as Dr. Jonathan Crane. Ken Watanabe had a nice take on Ra's Al Ghul but the real star was Liam Neeson. His role as Ducard shows what an amazing actor he really is, and what a great mentor character he can pull off with well done dialog and directing. The only real trouble for me came from Katie Holmes. She looked very out of place and more like a lost teenager then a real district attorney.

This Batman was set in a very real world, in a real looking Gotham city. The technology was believable and the use of CGI was not over blown for the first time this summer.

This Batman had what so many others have been missing. A plot, a real character driven plot. Not a CGI driven effects show case.

Christopher Nolan comes through in every way for this film. Looking at Batman Begins compared to Batman and Robin, Joel Schumacher should commit sepuku.

10.title: Sweet!
10.content: It was a really awesome movie! Yes it was the best out of all of them! I really liked it and I urge you to go watch it now! Please, it is good I promise. I am no really a big fan of Batman , although I liked it as a kid, but it is like unbelievable that they would make a movie of Batman that good. Even us Jesus freaks like it because that is what I am but I still liked the Batman movie. I hope they make another one but just a little better than this new one that just came out. My sister Des is retarded because she probably wont like it but she says the new Charlie and the chocolate factory is going to be good but I can guarantee that it wont be as good as the old one especially since Johnny Depp is Willy Wonka, nobody is better at acting Willy Wonka then Gene Wilder!!! Thanks, ByE!

10.title: An amazing film from start to finish
10.content:
What can't be said that hasn't already about this film over the years since it's release? Christopher Nolan single-handedly revitalized the Batman character and made it legitimate cinema. I had low expectations for the film before it's release because I had not really followed much of it's development save for a few pictures on the internet here or there.

For those that haven't already seen the movie, it follows Bruce Wayne as he begins his quest to becoming Batman and bringing justice to Gotham City. It is a true origin story, and it fleshes out characters and their unique motivations in a very fresh and interesting manner. Though the beginning half of the film contains not one scene with Bruce Wayne as Batman and focuses more on why he becomes Batman, the latter is about his fight against an old nemesis and saving Gotham.

The entire film from start to finish is filled with great performances. Both Liam Neeson and Gary Oldman give amazing performances in this film. Christian Bale is also very good throughout, although when put next to actors like Neeson and Oldman, they slightly outshine him on screen. The weakest performance would have to be Katie Holmes, and even her's is not that bad as the District Attorney that is a childhood friend of Wayne's.

Nolan uses a deft hand to create tension and up the ante with every plot point, and his love of the material and the craft is unsurpassed in the superhero film genre. If you have not seen this film yet, go and find it immediately. It was one of 2005's best films.

10.title: Legend
10.content: This movie teach me about life on what we fear the philosophy is so deep I love this movie we must watch this Masterpiece I encouraging you all

10.title: They finally got Batman Right!
10.content: First I have to say that I hated every single batman movie ever made! And yes I especially hated Micheal Keaton as Batman,,,what a horrible choice. My main problems with the OTHER Batman movies is that they focus too much on the cartoony back ground and props, and the lack of intelligence that went into the story that basically only held the interest of a six year old. When I saw the trailers for the Batman Begins I thought it looked boring, the trailers did absolutely nothing for this movie. I walked into the theater with my mind made up that it was going to suck and I would hate it. Well I sure was wrong, because I believe that this is without a doubt the best comic book movie ever made! I was blown away! Well apparently everything I hated about the other movies the team that made this movie possible hated too. It has a REAL storyline, they take there time to tell you why and how Bruce becomes Batman. They didn't try to see how many "stars" they could pack into the movie. The background didn't look like you were in an amusement park. The story was well thought out and the movie was well acted. I am married to the biggest comic book fan you will ever meet, so I know that this movie is based on the Year One graphic novel, and he too loved the movie. Up until now my favorite comic based movie was X-Men 2, but Batman Begins blows it out of the water! This is without a doubt the best movie of the summer!

10.title: I love batman 💝
10.content:
The best thing is the story plotting that is beyond words. Movie complete each and every part, means you not feel that something remains incomplete. Then this type of movie satisfies my craving for action. The way how batman killed enemies is beautifully director as expected from the director Christopher Nolan. And i also love how characters repeat dialogues of someone other character in a cool way.

Now there are also some negative points like cinematography of hand to hand combat feels weak and some minor mistakes which can be ignored. But one thing annoyed me during the whole movie about resurrection of that ninja.

Otherwise this movie is best for action in theatres with popcorn 😋

10.title: Batman done right.
10.content: The gold-standard of Batman movies. Characters with depth, a movie with a soul. Christopher Nolan is a filmmaker's filmmaker and Bale kills it as Bruce Wayne and Batman.

10.title: batman begins (10/10)
10.content: batman begins is the best superhero movie yet. the best part is how they have taken a real approach to it. I've seen it 5 times and have learned something new every time. they casted the movie great , Alfred (michael Caine) does an awesome job , the Alfred character is much more than just a butler in this film. batman (christian bale) does a great job , the voice of batman was maybe a little overdone but you will grow used to it. you can actually believe in this movie. thats a good thing. the villains are done very well and you will dislike them all , you feel Batman's pain and want to see him get vengeance while also wanting to see him be a hero. Gordon (gary oldman) is a great Gordon and portrays the comic book Gordon very well. if your a batman fan its a must see. if your not a batman fan still go see it , i recommend little kids 7 and under not see this movie , it definitely earns its pg-13 rating. 10/10

10.title: A nice complex masterpiece of a comic book film.
10.content:
Batman Begins (5 out of 5).

Batman Begins is an awesome masterpiece of a reboot to the superhero franchise. Director/Screenwriter Christopher Nolan did a fantastic job-recreating Batman. Not by telling the same story like the previous Batman movies were we see the caped crusader facing against a new villain. Nolan takes us to were it all began. It is an origin story. We see Bruce Wayne doing everything for the first time. From jumping on rooftops without his wings or grappling hook.

The plot does not follow in a chronological order within the first hour of the movie. But it works great with Nolan's direction set up. It begins with a kid Bruce Wayne falling in an old water well and facing against Bats. Than it cuts to an older Bruce Wayne, imprisoned in a different country and comes across Henri (Liam Neeson) who is giving him a second chance at redemption. Bruce is left traveling through and coming across ninjas that are being trained for the league of Shadows. Then, it flashes towards a young adult Bruce who is visiting the trial for his parents murderer. And only to see Gotham city being corrupted. After Bruce training, he comes back to Gotham to be the caped crusader and to stop a bigger threat from the mob. And Dr. Jonathan Crane (Cillian Murphy) who is corrupted and plotting a threat to Gotham.

The plot was well organized. The script was fantastic. The action sequences are awesome. You have an exciting Batmobile known as the tumbler being chased by the police. Batman facing against criminals. And a villain scarecrow, which uses a toxic gas to make people see their own fears. The concept and setting is dark for a superhero film. But Batman is supposed to be in that direction.

Christian Bale was fantastic. Michael Caine, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, Cillian Murphy, and Liam Neeson were all great. Sure, there are some twists and surprises with the villains. And an exciting climatic battle with Batman fighting in a moving train.

Overall, Batman Begins is an awesome film. Nolan did the character justice. The script gave the proper treatment to the development and plot. The direction was sharp, clever, and exciting for an origin story. Plus the cliffhanger ending that opens for a sequel and the direction on the villain is great.

10.title: a must see
10.content:
I kind of lost trust in Hollywood when it came to Batman films since they totally butchered "Batman & Robin." How could you go from Tim Burton's masterpiece in 1989's "Batman" to that pathetic piece of crap "Batman & Robin"? So understandably so, I was apprehensive towards seeing this movie until I saw the extended trailer before "The Longest Yard." Watching that trailer and finding out that such esteemed actors like Christian Bale, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, and of course Morgan Freeman were in it, I actually felt compelled to see it out of excitement. And after watching it, I can safely say that "Batman Begins" is probably the best super hero movie I've seen.

Aside from several absolutely amazing action sequences and virtuoso, scene stealing performances by Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine, I'd have to say that the best thing about the movie was the overall character development. You could actually feel the tension between Liam Neeson and Christian Bale. You could understand Christian Bale's resentment towards society and the justice system after the death of his parents. You could feel Michael Caine's fatherly love and affection for Christian Bale after the death of his parents. And you could feel the trust in Gary Oldman as Gotham's last and only "good" cop.

All in all, Batman Begins sets a new bar as far as super hero movies are concerned. It has everything that the Spiderman movies had, plus more. Despite casting Katie Holmes, the only mistake made in the movie, it is without a doubt flawless when it comes to everything else. Definitely a must-see for the Batman enthusiast.

10.title: well done
10.content: Fantastically dark and morbid. This is the character Batman was meant to be. Christian Bale did a wonderful job, as did his supporting cast. It was refreshing to see such character development after watching George Lucas's meager attempt in his past three movies. This movie has found the formula: employ indie directors and actors and the story will sell itself. Batman Begins works on so many levels because it concentrates on substance over style, thus trumping its predecessors. Well done Mr. Noland and Mr. Bale. I look forward to seeing your next installment. My only concern is for the next episode. Who can top the performance of Jack as the Joker. We can only wait and see.

10.title: The Best Movie of 2005 so far!
10.content:
Saying this movie is the best thus far of 2005 is really an understatement! Christian Bale revived the ever so limp Batman series and injected our minds with a new view of Batman, the Human side.

The whole movie is based around fear, and using fear against enemies, and for Batman to use his opponents fear against them, he must first face his own. Thats where the relevance of the bats come in. This movie also has a more modern Gotham with much more modern problems.

The acting was well all the way around, I can't think of anyone who lacked in keeping my interest, INCLUDING Mrs. Holmes. The story was extremely well written and never went off path, always keeping you interested, and wondering who or what was next in the detailed plot.

Overall this is just a fantastic movie, anyone including Non-Batman fans like myself should go see it!

10.title: Batman grows up
10.content: I have now seen this movie twice and I must say it got better the second time. First, I loved how it explained events that happened unlike the other 4 films. I enjoyed the way Bruce ended up in the well, and why his family left the theater. The thing that was the best explained to me though was how they actually made the bat cave without having any professionals or anything install everything. Christopher Nolan's directing was spectacular. I liked the fact that he used as little CGI as possible making Batman seem more real. And the action scenes especially with the bat mobile were spectacular. The thing I loved most was the fact that it was darker than the last two, and gave the darkness look that the original comics gave. Best DC movie made yet.

10.title: A New Beginning
10.content:
This film is a great throw back to Tim Burton's original, and in many ways surpasses it. Here, Gotham city is back to it's Gothic atmosphere and thankfully, as far away from the campy nature of Batman and Robin.

The story of Batman's origins makes for a prefect film. Why this regular man, with no actual superpowers, becomes the Dark Knight is a great story. From the beginning, when Bruce Wayne is training with Ducard, to his transformation into Batman, the story is given a realistic edge to it that makes the characters all the more interesting. The reasons behind Wayne's choice to become Batman are made completely plausible through flash backs to his childhood. It's difficult to say more without ruining the plot, but it's actually a very interesting look at how fear can rule people's lives.

The action in the movie is reminiscent of The Bourne Identity, and earlier action flicks like Speed. There are great car chases and fight scenes. One fight scene in particular has a horror movie edge to it. The action mixed with the interesting story make this an excellent film.

Christian Bale makes a great Batman and a great Bruce Wayne, and not at all difficult on the eyes. I think he tops Michael Keaton and, since the film itself kind of rests on the shoulders of the actor playing Batman, it speaks to how good Bale is in that the movie is so good. Gary Oldman is fantastic as Lieutenant Gordon. It's nice to see him not play a psychopath . . . Michael Caine (Alfred), Morgan Freeman (Lucius Fox), and Liam Neeson (Ducard) also offer great performances. Cillian Murphy, who I have only previously seen in 28 Days Later - and who also auditioned for the role of Batman, but ended up being cast as Doctor Crane/The Scarecrow - proves that he is going to be an actor to watch for in the coming years.

The only person who falls short in this cast is Katie Holmes. She is by no means bad in the movie, but compared to the huge talent that surrounds her, she just can't quite compete. It's too bad that a better actress couldn't have been cast, but she is the only weak point of this film, and as I said, she's not even that bad.

So, I give this movie a 10 because Batman has always been my favourite comic book hero and this film made the movie franchise great again. Go see it!

10.title: The Best Batman Ever

10.title: They finally got it right!!
10.content:
This is the best Batman by far! Focusing mainly on character development, director Cnristopher Nolan draws viewers into the most in-depth, accurate, and entrancing story of Batman ever with a logical storyline and a cast full of Hollywood's most distinguished actors, including Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson and Michael Cain.

This is, by definition, the beginning of the great saga that is Batman. Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) is a man struggling to get through his adult life with the self-claimed guilt of his parents' murder on his hands and conscience. He eventually falls under the tutelage of Ducard (Neeson) and is trained in the arts of stealth, fear and harsh justice.

Bruce Wayne, upon return to Gotham City, regains control of his mansion and his father's company. He sets up the bat cave on his property to be the BatCave. At WayneCorp, shoved into a secluded basement, is Lucius Fox, the man who supplies Bruce with almost everything he needs for to be Batman.

As Batman, he strikes fear into the hearts of the criminals and villains who patrol and run Gotham. These include my favorite villain from the Batman cartoons (I don't remember him from the comics, but maybe I missed that one): Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy). Employed by Ducard, Scarecrow is dumping tons of a panic-inducing toxin into Gotham's water supply and Batman has to stop them from destroying civilization as they know it.

This is a perfect portrayal of the soul of Batman. Christian Bale was flawless and I like how they finally got Alfred away from being only a butler; Michael Cain plays more the role of a father figure than servant. I also love how 'real' this movie seemed. They made Gotham very believable and it seemed as though the suit, the cape, the gadgets and even the Batmobile could be logical products of present day reality.

10.title: Has a new era in intelligent movie making begun?
10.content: Amazing! I didn't think a "comic book" movie could get better--more coherent, compelling or intelligent--than Spiderman I. But it can, and it's called Batman Begins. Like all great sci-fi creations, this Batman movie has serious and poignant comments to make on the real world. Batman, a fantasy character, has very real moral, psychological and even existential decisions to make, decisions that have a correlation to ones we all face in society. How far will we go to do the right thing? Batman could have easily rationalized the excesses he was externally and internally tempted to take, but he chose to "do the right thing" in the face of overwhelming misunderstanding and criticism. In other words, he didn't attack or kill just because he could. He tried to be measured; he tried to help a bleak situation, not just exercise his machismo. Who'd a thought that nowadays we'd get a movie in which the effects and the carnage were truly subservient to the narrative? Glory, glory hallelujah. Have I lived long enough to see a new era in intelligent film making?

Batman is what Bruce Wayne became the moment that his parents were shot. Rather than possessing a focus for his rage as in the first "Batman", Batman is forced to take his vengeance upon the general criminal element in Gotham City.

"batman Begins" captures the essence of the character in rare fashion. When the movie ended, I clapped...and I haven't done that for a while.

10.title: Nolan, Goyer and Christian Bale Batman out of Goofham.
10.content: Having seen this film a 2nd time only confirms my initial take on it. This is an angry, ferocious, intelligent and thoroughly adult Batman. However it is a warmer film the 2nd time around. When Nolan was announced as the director to resurrect the Bat a couple of years ago I was thrilled. I knew he wouldn't screw it up. Let's face it the excellent MEMENTO and INSOMNIA weren't exactly laugh riots. The thoughtfulness that made those films what they are make BATMAN BEGINS what it is. Before we declare it the best film based on comic book character or story we must remember THE CROW. Bale is perfect as Bruce Wayne/Batman. He is brooding, tortured and deadly serious, but (like Brandon Lee as Eric Draven/The Crow) there is a real soulfulness in his work. He and Russell Crowe (from the greatly under-appreciated Cinderella MAN--the other great film of '05) dominate but never steal, the screen when they are on it. Also I loved Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Gary Oldham (refreshingly playing a good guy) and Morgan Freeman. There is not a single sour note in any work here and, yes, I think Tom Wilkinson as Falcone does a fine job. This is a film for the mind and the eye. Like Cinderella MAN the riches here are very abundant. When I was 1st blown away by Frank Miller's revisionist Batman in "The Dark Knight Returns" (and it unfairly maligned sequel), BATMAN BEGINS was how I hoped Batman would be translated to the big screen. BATMAN RETURNS came close (thanks to Keaton, Pfieffer and DeVito), but this Bat even blows that one away. This film has as much Frank Miller in it (along with some Alan Moore) as Miller's own SIN CITY. BATMAN BEGINS is astonishing. Note to Christopher Nolan and David Goyer: if you can pull off an R-rating I loved to see "The Killing Joke".

10.title: Batman Begins does more to define the character than any other batman film.
10.content:
I was 18 when I saw the first Batman movie. I won free tickets to the sneak-preview showing late on a weeknight. The theater was packed to the walls and everyone must have been as big a fan as me because we all ooo'd and aaah'd, cursed, laughed and whooped at all the same places. The experience was so unique to me that I felt a little of it every time I wore one of my batman t-shirts or hats for years afterwards.

At the time, I was sure that was the best comic-book hero movie that could ever be made. This feeling was reinforced after the other Batman movies were released. Sure, they were OK and it was cool to watch a character you love go through new adventures, but the movies were not as good overall.

I have to say that Batman Begins certainly has given me a new perspective. I still have a high opinion of the 1989 flick, but this movie rocks. It made Bruce much more human, and in my opinion, much more likable. I was surprised how much I liked Bale as Batman.

The focus of this movie is, obviously, how Bruce got started in the role of thug-busting. Turns out he spent some time in an Asian prison, hooked up with a bunch of ninjas that were led by a tag-team of ol' Rob Roy / Qui-Gon Jinn and the next-to-last-Samurai. This film had an awesome and very impressive list of cast members.

Morgan Freeman shows up as a Wayne Inc version of "Q" -- let's call him "W" -- who really knows how to hook a fella up. Full body armor, magneto-cable-guns, electro-memory cloth (used to turn Batman's cape into a glider -- how cool is that!?) and (the best for last) the Tumbler, aka Batmobile.

This was, beyond any doubt, the most kick-ass vehicle I've ever seen in a movie. These pictures really don't do it justice and you have to watch this movie if for no other reason than just to see it in action. One of my favorite quotes from the film came from a cop in a cruiser calling out a description of the Batmobile over the radio, "It's a black.... TANK!" One of my favorite scenes from the film was when the Gotham SWAT team were about to storm Arkam-asylum to capture Batman. How Batman handled this situation was such a creative and visual-delight that I don't want to ruin it for you or even try to describe it. Words would only cheapen it anyway.

10.title: Not a just a great Batman movie. It is both a great movie, and the BEST Batman movie.
10.content:
You know, I was really tempted to just rate this movie a 9. Do I REALLY want to give a Batman movie a 10? But that's the thing. I really can't see how this movie could have entertained me more. And I really can't shake the feeling that even if I had never read any Batman comic books, or never seen Batman in previous film and TV versions, this movie still would have affected me the same and sold me for life on this character.

This film operates at the level of Greek mythology. And like any great myth, it's simple enough for a child to understand and appreciate while simultaneously containing enough to intellectually stimulate adults too.

This movie certainly has enough to please everyone. And while it excels in all areas, it is not a movie that is simply about its meticulously planned set pieces, costumes, fight scenes, or action sequences.

It has a uniformly excellent supporting cast, easily boasting one of the best ensembles outside of a Robert Altman or Paul Thomas Anderson movie.

It has a director that has yet to make a bad film.

But most importantly, it has an entire crew that makes it immediately clear with every frame that they get it.

This is how a Batman movie is supposed to look, to feel, and to sound. This is who Batman is, and how he got there. They nailed it.

Any last lingering doubt is washed away by the scene with Batman, a little more confident but still a little unsure, taking down a group of criminals.

The scene is staged like most horror movies, only this time you know what is lurking behind the shadows, waiting to strike. And you're cheering for him. And it is FUN.

All this praise is not to say it is flawless. The nitpickers and naysayers will find cracks that they feel are big enough to sink the ship. Maybe they didn't believe Katie Holmes as an assistant D.A. Maybe they felt the PG-13 rating hurt the grittiness and sense of danger. Does it matter? Let them rob themselves of one of the most satisfying cinema experiences to come along in years. The rest of us will have a blast basking in the darkness, waiting for the bat symbol to once again pierce through the night sky.

10.title: Beautifully Crafted
10.content: Batman Begins is one beautifully crafted movie. There is something different about this movie which keeps you glued to your seats. Right from the opening sequence, the movie is gripping. Gary Oldman, as usual, walks through his role without much effort. Tom Wilkinson as Falcone does a decent job. Morgan Freeman in his role reminds me of Bruce Almighty. Nice to see Ken Watanabe (Ra's Al-Ghul) on screen, makes an impact as Al-Ghul. I have to make a special mention of Cillian Murphy and Liam Neeson. Murphy was chilling and creepy as the Scarecrow. Liam Neeson, I feel, was the surprise package in the movie. I would definitely rate this Batman movie as the BEST since Tim Burtons Batman. Even though I would be adding this movie to my DVD collection once the DVD gets released, I would still say that this movie needs to be viewed on the big screen. Well done Christopher Nolan and co. 10.title: Brits rule Gotham

Also great to see so many British actors (and Irish of course) practising their American accents so successfully. Some iconic scenes here including the moment where Bruce Wayne finally faces his fear of bats in their cave and the way he harnesses them to help him escape from the police, wonderful stuff. This compares very well with the fantastic Spiderman series but with a much better script and less cheese.

Here's looking forward to what Nolan does with the Joker, surely there must be a sequel here.

10.title: It could not have been any better. There is Nothing Else to Say!
10.content:
I swiped these comments from another reviewer, but he said it so well, & I wanted to get my 2 cents in:

One of the strongest features of the film, is the way that it manges to suck you in believe that a 'Batman' could be a reality one day. The technology is current, with no use of silly OTT weapons and gadgets, again making the film work by today's standards. Plus, we are not allowed to forget that Batman is still just a man under the costume and there are times when he gets a bit of a kicking and shows that he can be vulnerable too, something we sometimes forget when watching a superhero flick. Gone too, are the silly villains!!! Jack Nicholson was the perfect Joker but from there it went downhill. Thankfully, in this movie the bad guys are actually fairly 'normal' and manage to be menacing at the same time.

Which finally brings me to the cast. I always had high expectations for this film when the cast was announced. Let's face it, what a line up! Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Liam Neeson, Katy Holmes, Ken Watanabe and Tom Wilkinson are not to be sniffed at. Even an old favourite of mine makes an appearance: Rutger Hauer! Awesome. Actors of this calibre would never have gotten involved in this project if they didn't have faith in Christoper Nolan's talents and thankfully they took the leap...

For the comic book fans out there, waiting to see this movie, let me assure you that you won't be upset. Imagine the darkness of the 'A Death In The Family' and the 'Year One' story lines. I have never met a fan of Batman who didn't love these books. Well, this is the kind of Batman you can expect from Bale: Dark, brooding and tortured by his past, yet the hero we have come to love. For those of you who are not comic fans, then just look forward to seeing how Batman should be. This film is a credit to Bob Kane's original vision and a testament to all the talented artists and writers who keep the legend of the Dark Knight alive in the comic books today....

Thank you Mr. Nolan and thank you Mr. Bale. In fact thanks to everyone who worked on this film. Batman finally Begins from here....

10.title: The best comic book movie since "Superman"
10.content:
It's been eight years since the Batman franchise was left in inescapable ruins. Finally, the WB has brought Batman back to its roots - a dark, gritty, gloomy atmosphere. Although Tim Burton was known for his dark Batfilms, he relied on Gothic architecture and fantastic skylines. "Batman Begins" is dark in the sense that the city looks like it exists in the real world, overrun with crime and ramshackle buildings. Chris Nolan has not only revived the Batman franchise, but he will inspire future comic book movies to come.

Chris Nolan takes a new approach to not only a Batman film, but a superhero film in general. Instead of relying on supernatural imagery and special effects, this film focuses more on character development and a plot - something all of the previous Batman films lacked.

"Batman Begins" uses up the most villains than any other Batman film, but somehow Batman, or I should say Bruce Wayne, remains the main focus of the film. The main plot is the struggle Bruce Wayne has to face to become Batman, and the villains are all involved in minor subplots, whereas in previous Batfilms, the villains dominated the screen, even more than Batman himself.

Do not expect colorful, vibrant villains we've seen from previous Batfilms. Here, Director Chris Nolan aimed for a realistic approach, and succeeding in every way possible. When we watch "NYPD Blue" we don't expect whimsical and colorful villains, we expect normal people without harmonious outlandish costumes.

Watching the first hour of "Batman Begins" seems like an episode of "NYPD Blue" or "CSI." If someone who despised comic books and was unfamiliar with the Batman mythology were to watch "Batman Begins," s/he would never guess it was a comic book film until Batman makes his appearance during the second hour. That is how realistic this movie plays.

The cast is excellent in their roles. I had doubts about Michael Caine at first, being how he is such a well known star, but he plays his part of Alfred so well that one would forget he's Michael Caine and start believing him as Alfred right from his first lines of dialogue. Cillian Murphy is creepy and compelling as the loony psychiatrist Jonathan Crane, a man who you know is hiding something devious behind those eyes. Let us not forget Christian Bale, who is the second actor only to Michael Keaton to portray Bruce Wayne with sincerity, and he's more physically fit for the role, which helps.

The Cinematography is something we haven't seen in many superhero movies. Unlike the usual colorful superhero movies such as "Spider-man" and "Batman & Robin," this movie was filmed dark and artistic. It's as if the cinematographer thought he was making a sequel to "Lost in Translation." Trust me, it works. It's about time a serious Batman film was made.

Kudos, Chris Nolan and David Goyer, for not only reviving Batman, but for creating groundbreaking material which would improve superhero films to come. This is one comic book movie in which the actors, direction, and the screenplay take its source material seriously, which has not happened since Richard Donner's Superman.

10.title: The origin story of Batman and his attempts to battle the corruption in a dark Gotham City.
10.content: This is not the Batman from the 60's. The film masterfully depicts a much darker, more intense version of the famous legend. We are exposed to the complexities and inner workings of Bruce Wayne that ultimately cause him to take on the alternate identity as the city's masked hero. Bale does an extraordinary job in taking on the role of Batman/Bruce Wayne. He portrays the crusader in a more realistic fashion than past actors who have played the role. The rest of the characters in the film were also pretty well casted; particularly Gary Oldman as Gordon, who is not yet commissioner. It is especially interesting to see the origins of characters like Gordon in addition to how Batman came to be. Through this film we are able to see the background for the stories and villains we are used to. When attempting this, it is usually hit or miss. This film succeeded in all aspects and I recommend it to all fans of the legend or anyone who likes an entertaining movie. Well done. Let's hope if a sequel is made, it will live up to this film.

10.title: Not who I am underneath
10.content: Christopher Nolan brings batman to life with the origin story which had never really been told in on screen. Spending time visiting the cave, where Adam West and Burt Ward raced out of, from the 60s tv show, Nolan and David S Goyer knew they had to return to the roots of what made batman. What's interesting about this film is how much anticipation is created whilst the audience awaits batmans first appearance. With great storytelling we are invested into Bruce Wayne as much as we are batman. The suspense is so thrilling even before he puts on the cape and cowl. With different beliefs to his mentor and the league of shadows Bruce Wayne sets out to find his own purpose. Along with the amazing composing of Hans Zimmer And James Newton Howard we feel the fear and emotional pain of Bruce losing his parents. Henri Ducard becomes a new father like figure to Bruce and trains Bruce in martial arts whilst he has left Gotham. This film has outstanding sequences and great cinematography. Batman is seen in flashes at first like a horror movie creating fear in the eyes of his opponents. Comparing it with modern super hero movies there is a lot more genuine solidility with cgi only being used when it is absolutely necessary. From being filmed on location, to epic full scale narrows and batcaves being built, which is the foundations of this standing out among the rest. One of the most authentic comic book movies ever made. Whilst being a big James Bond fan Nolan even adapted to incorporating Lucus Fox into the mix as your gadgets man. Using state of the art army like gadgets almost everything you see in the movie can be done. With a variety of quality actors from Gary Oldman, Christian Bale, Michael Caine and Liam Neeson this truely is a movie to bring a comic book film to life at its highest level. A nice twist along the way, for me Batman Begins is not only the best Batman movie to date but also the pinnacle of all comic book movies. Where it all does truely begin.

10.title: How to do an origin story
10.content:
I think that the first iteration of Batman I ever saw was the Adam West TV series. You know, the one with nonchanging story lines, Joker with a painted-over mustache, Bat Shark Repellant, and "Na-na-na-na- na Batman" theme. Boy, have we come a long way since then. Christopher Nolan revolutionized the character. Tim Burton's version had already brought back the dark shadows, the heavy themes of duality and fighting enemies of your own making, the brooding and the melancholy. But Nolan took all that and updated it to the modern day. Suddenly it felt surprisingly plausible that someone might make the choice to fight crime dressed as a giant bat.

This is also one of the first films in ages to show as the origin of Batman. I mean, we all know the story. Bruce Wayne is the golden son of Gotham, but then his parents get killed in a random mugging and once he grows up he takes up the moniker of Batman to strike fear into the hearts of those that have terrified him so much. But we usually start long after he has become Batman. And the question often remains: Where did the learn all that? Sure, he's wealthy beyond belief so getting all kinds of gadgets is certainly possible, but you don't really learn to fight like he does without some form of training. And in this movie we get to see that training. And it is very entertaining and makes for a great cinematic experience, especially with Nolan directing. His nonlinear storytelling and visual style compliment the story perfectly and once Bruce Wayne begins his war against crime, he gives us a great version of one of the best villains Batman has ever had.

It's also a well-acted film with Christian Bale stepping into the boots of Bruce Wayne and Batman. I do think that he is a bit better Bruce Wayne than he is Batman and this is definitely the film where he gets to be Bruce Wayne the most, but his Batman isn't all that bad by any means. Even the infamous voice isn't as bad as people make it out to be, especially in this first film. And the supporting cast is equally great, with Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman giving us their absolutely A-game as Alfred and Lucius Fox, respectively. Not to mention Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon, though his best moments are still ahead in the next film.

Batman Begins is one of my favourite superhero films and one of my all-time favourites in general as well. Definitely my go-to example on how to tell an origin story. Check it out if you haven't already.

10.title: The real deal!

I'm really sad for this guy, because it's well know that playing a graphic novel character does not earn a Oscar, even if played brilliant like he did. Not to forget the rest of the cast! Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman (nice to see him in a positive role!) made the characters they've played to a perfect mix between sidekicks and father figures.

This is the real deal!

I hope there were not to many mistakes made - Still trying to get some practice in English again!

Greeting from Germany,

hjoe

10.title: A great movie!
10.content:
Batman Begins marks the 5th attempt at bringing the Dark Knight to the big screen. After the last two camp filled monstrosities (part 2 wasn't that great either), I was a bit hesitant about this one. Needless to say, I walked out of the theatre in shock and awe at how well the film was done. As Roger Ebert said, this is the Batman film I never knew I was waiting for.

A young Bruce Wayne witnesses the murder of his parents. He then sets out to understand the nature of criminality and the criminal mind. Years later, he is a prisoner in an unnamed Asian country, where he has nightmares about his childhood fear of bats where he meets a man named Ducard who takes him to the doorstep of Ras Al-Ghul. From this point on, Bruce trains to become a "symbol" that fights those who prey on the fearful.

Christopher Nolan and David Goyer's setup was brilliant, since this is undoubtedly the only Batman film that actually does Batman justice. The writers went above and beyond to make sure the story was believable. The inclusion of the Luscious Fox character (played by Morgan Freeman) adds to the believability of the Batman story. Bruce Wayne needs an array of gadgets and automobiles to fight crime, all of which were developed by Wayne's own company. The design for the batsuit is that of a suit that was designed for warfare. This is only fitting since Wayne declares a one man war on crime in Gotham City. Batman as a character was never supposed to offer the escapist, fantasy elements that Spider-Man or Superman offered. Most of the single entity superhero titles out there try and sell themselves on big explosions, heat vision, and big webs. In other words, the others make their money from the cheap thrills that are offered from the very nature of the character. Batman is just a guy sworn to fight crime; a guy who pushed his body and mind to the limits of human capability. They don't call him the world's greatest detective for nothing. From this stand point, Batman is more about the thick, complex plot structure and the deep, complicated, and usually dark take on each and every character (not to say the film doesn't offer any action). This is what makes Batman "the thinking man's" super hero, not to mention knowing that any guy walking the street could be Batman if he was driven enough.

Christian Bale's dark and brooding performance only adds to the gritty realism of the story. Bale truly captures the three sides to the coin; the public Bruce Wayne, the private Bruce Wayne, and the beast that is Batman. Bale's physical appearance just makes his performance that much better. One half is the filthy rich, billionaire playboy. The other half is a man who spends his nights jumping off rooftops and fighting thugs by the dozens. Alfred's relationship with Bruce does add that more humanistic touch to the film, and Michael Cain does a great job of showing how Alfred acted as a real father figure for Bruce as he grew up.

The only real downside is the presence of Katie Holmes. She just doesn't look her part. After Wayne comes back from the years spent traveling the world and fighting crime, Rachel is supposed to be near thirty, yet she still looks fifteen. I personally would have liked an even darker approach to the camera work. The images of Batman standing, hiding, or jumping out of the shadows with fog and lightning ripping through the screen would've been a real treat. But looking back on it, the film was supposed to be real and it is real, that's why it works.

I'm already looking forward to the sequel. Go watch this one, NOW!

10.title: Bats frighten me. It's time my enemies share my dread.
10.content:
Enter the world of Batman, or rather, Christopher Nolan's Batman. The genius behind "Memento" has taken an unexpected turn in his film career by directing a movie franchise that was previously shot down with titles including "Batman Forever" and the dreadful "Batman and Robin". It would take an immense amount of work to revive the franchise and to rid the audience of the image cast on them through previous batman films.

Nolan does just that. Completely rebooting the franchise from scratch, he tells the story of Batmans origins; what drove a billionaire heir to his fathers throne from riches to becoming his city's greatest protector. Nolan immerses the audience into emotional depth by telling the story that had yet to have been told. In previous incarnations of Batman, the villains are the interesting characters. Their stories are told. This film is different. Batman Begins tells the story of Bruce Wayne.

Nolan's version is one that was never thought of. Who knew that all a Batman movie needed was more character depth and less action and special gadgets? Though this movie focuses less on the action, the action that is in it is intense. The fight scenes are incredibly realistic and not special dancing that are seen in kung fu movies. Gadgets used by Batman are not only conceivable but current experimental technology.

One question I always had about Batman since I was a kid was "Why would someone who wants to fight crime just wear a bat costume?" Although Batman comics and the Batman: Mask of the Phantasm addresses this issue, Begins takes it into a new level and makes it to the point where it's no longer a mystery as to why bats, but it's point blank obvious as to why he chose bats. "Bats frighten me. It's time my enemies share my dread." An exceptional cast makes the story all the more compelling and epic. Liam Neeson, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Gary Oldman, Cilian Murphy, Ken Watanbe and (of course last but no where near the least) Christian Bale act with great conviction and devotion, creating the emotional feel for their characters.

The twists and turns in the movie leave the audience surprised and amazed. The choice of telling the story in a non linear fashion was perfect. The movie is without competition in it's franchise.

Superhero movies have finally grown up. Batman Begins deserves every bit of praise it gets.

10.title: DC triumphantly strikes back; The Batman has finally arrived
10.content:
For the last eight years, all of the die hard fans of DC Comics, and in particular, the long-suffering fans of the most mortal superhero of our time, the Batman, have watched in agony as comic book films reign triumphant at the box office, almost all of them with the Marvel logo attached. The X-Men films, the Spider-Man films, the Blade trilogy, and a few others are an example of their success.

Meanwhile, the DC fans have writhed in pain as the last time they could remember their caped crusader was when he wore a nipple clad suit and fought the governor of California in one of the worst movies ever made, Batman and Robin.

The DC fans went into exile, hoping, praying that one day their REAL hero would return them the way he was meant to.

On June 15, 2005, the day finally came. The Batman came back to cast his shadow on comic book cinema.

More importantly, from the moment the brand new DC Comics logo appeared before the movie, DC Comics finally sent the message they have wanted to send for some time: WE ARE BACK.

Batman Begins is a film that for the first time ever tells the story of how Bruce Wayne became the Batman, the dark knight of justice against evil in Gotham City. Instead of focusing on the villains of the film and how they rose to power, this movie, in a formula similar to Spider-Man, tells how Batman was created, and finally gives his character the depth that he deserves.

The story follows Bruce Wayne's life from the moment his parents died, through his teen years as he dealt with the loss, to the point where he realizes his ultimate vision of becoming Gotham City's symbol of justice, and the best part is that EVERYTHING is EXPLAINED.

When you watch this movie, you know WHY he is Batman and you know HOW he is Batman. He is never simply a crazed vigilante in a bat suit scaring people. His methods are logical and realistic and for the first time, you UNDERSTAND WHY HE DOES WHAT HE DOES.

The story is excellently crafted by David S. Goyer, who is capable of making masterpieces as long as he is paired with the right director, who in this case is Christopher Nolan, the genius behind Memento, Following, and Insomnia. At no point did this story seem too campy or unrealistic and at no point did it fail to draw in the viewer. Everything is clearly presented and highly engrossing.

The cast is excellent from top to bottom, even at its weakest link with Katie Holmes playing assistant D.A. Rachel Dawes. Christian Bale, in what might be his strongest role yet, is the perfect age and personality for the playboy of Bruce Wayne and more importantly, he makes you believe that he IS the dark, frighteningly vengeful Batman, with a voice and personality that scares EVERYBODY, good or bad.

Michael Caine is the perfect Alfred Pennyworth, the consort and friend of Bruce Wayne, Morgan Freeman is sharp and resourceful as Lucius Fox, the Wayne Enterprises executive with all of the wonderful toys, and Gary Oldman, after years of playing the bad guy in so many films, once again displays his versatility by bringing Jim Gordon to life, something that NONE of the other four films EVER did.

The villains do not take away from the attention paid to Batman and they do not dominate the story. They are there to do what they do, which is cause trouble and put a face on who the Batman fights. Tom Wilkinson, Cilian Murphy, Ken Watanabe and Liam Neeson are strong antagonists in this respect, doing only what they are supposed to be doing and not going over the top with their performances.

In addition, for the first time ever on film, Gotham City is Gotham City, a true comic book metropolis brought to life, displaying its true to life cityscapes while also showing its dark grittiness.

For awhile I always believed that the best incarnation of Batman was the 85 episodes of the Animated Series that appeared on Fox from 1992-1995. Now, with this new movie, the Batman looks better than he ever did. Warner Bros. and DC Comics looks as though they are finally ready to make amends for the past transgressions of the Batman franchise after seeing how attention to detail, depth and accuracy have benefited the Marvel movies in their success.

In the Top Ten list of Best Comic Book movies of all-time, Batman Begins sits proudly at the #2 spot, with only Spider-Man 2 slightly ahead of it at #1. My hope and faith for this franchise has been more than restored, and I now look forward to seeing the future films in this NEW Batman franchise, as well as the highly touted Superman Returns, and V for Vendetta, which will be in theaters next year.

Rejoice, all of you long suffering DC Comics fans. Our wait has ended. The monopoly of Marvel is coming to an end. The Batman is finally here, Superman is coming back soon, and there will be others to follow. DC COMICS STRIKES BACK!!!

10.title: Best film of 2005 so far!
10.content:
I have fond memories of Tim Burton's first Batman picture. I saw it when I was 9 and loved it to death but like many movies I loved during my childhood it just simply hasn't aged well. It's shallow, cheesy, and with the exception of a completely over the top performance by way of Jack Nicholsan has little to remember in the acting department. After the initial picture the franchise plummeted into movie hell with three sequels that are some of the worst movies ever created. This franchise was in desperate need of a reboots.

Well here it is ladies and gents. Batman begins is quite simply one of the best comic book movies ever made. Why is that you may ask; well it's because while respecting it's roots it realizes that films aren't comics and grounds the story pretty firmly in what could be reality. Finally you can believe that most of this stuff is actually happening. Christian Bale is hands down the best Batman/Bruce ever put to screen and thanks to the screenwriters he is given lots to work with. Finally Batman's motivations for becoming the bat are fleshed out beyond the sorry Joker killed my parents excuse. He is a fully realized character and Christian bale delivers one of his best performances yet.

Michael Cain is also excellent as the loyal butler Alfred. Cain delivers a warmth and sincerity that the obvious Alfred lacked. Again he is serviced by some great writing and he runs with it. Cillian Murphy as Scarecrow was a genuine surprise. The only thing I've seen him in was 28 Days Later and I wasn't prepared for how good he'd be. Liam Neeson has never given a bad performance and he doesn't fail us now. His character is simply one of the best villains I've seen in a comic movie. The other cast are equally excellent though they don't have much screen time. Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman are quite good as the Q-Like Scientist and innocent police officer respectively. Kattie Holmes didn't annoy me nearly as much as I thought she would, in fact she was actually pretty good and I believed in her feelings for Bruce.

The one weakness this movie has is the quick cut actions scenes. Some of them are fine but most of them are cut so quick in such dark scenes that it make it really hard to tell what's happening. This is really a small complaint for me because I prefer a great story over action scenes any day and boy did this movie deliver. I will draw this review to a close by saying that this is the best movie so far in 2005 and it will most likely be at the top of my top 10 end of the year list.

10outof10
