10.title: Batman Shines
10.content:
It occurs to me that we never really learned the Batman legend before. We never learned anything from "Batman & Robin" for those that unfortunately remember the film but there has never been a solid backstory about him until now. Director Christopher Nolan creates a dark and fun filled adventure of the caped crusader that penetrates his deepest fears and shows us that he is not only just a vigilante but a real human who is vulnerable.

It's about a young child, Bruce Wayne (Gus Lewis) who loses his parents, Thomas (Linus Roache) and Martha (Sara Stewart) one night and Bruce is taken in and raised by his butler, Alfred Pennyworth (Michael Caine). 14 years later, Bruce (Christian Bale), is still devastated by the loss of his parents and plans to take the law into his own hands when the justice system fails. His childhood friend, Rachel Daws (Katie Holmes) berates him for thinking of such an act so Bruce decides to travel the world in an attempt to overcome his fear and learn how to confront justice. After training with, Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson) and facing his fears, he returns to Gotham determined to stop the crime as a caper vigilante called Batman.

Christian Bale steps into the suit and is, arguably, the best Batman to date. It opens in a prison camp where Bruce is a prisoner enduring punishment as part of his journey into seeing evil for what it really is. He is rescued by Henri Ducard and he becomes Bruce's mentor. He teaches him how to sword-fight and how to control himself in the face of danger. Things go sour when Wayne refuses to kill someone as a requirement for membership and Ducard becomes his enemy. Wayne returns to Gotham City and sets his sights on Carmine Falcone (Tom Wilkinson ), a mafia boss who controls the city.

Christopher Nolan gives us every aspect of the Bruce Wayne story. We learn his fear of bats (childhood accident) and his hatred of criminals (his parent's murders) are the reason for his journey but also discovering himself and learning to face his true destiny. His family owns Wayne Corp. and is run by a seedy figure, William Earle played by Rutger Hauer, who was in the meaningless and disgusting shocker called "The Hitcher." He fits right in with this character. Morgan Freeman plays Luscious Fox, scientific genius, and Wayne's weapons handler who gives him the tools he needs. He gives Batman the Batmobile and it's a juggernaut on wheels. Batman's suit also has some nice upgrades as well. Gary Oldmen steps into the role of Lt. Gordon who will quickly discover Batman is here to do good. In the middle of everything, Wayne is torn between a love he has for Rachel Dawes and also keeping his identity a secret.

When Wayne puts on the suit and becomes Batman, the action starts and it doesn't stop. Now, the plot could take a simple detour and give us some story where Batman beats everyone up, finds the villain and saves the day like we have seen before but it doesn't. Batman has a motive and he knows what he needs to do. When he is revealed in the second act, there is a sense of fear and darkness looming over the character that we become anxious to see what he is going to do. The main villain of the film is the Scarecrow and his zany scheme spells psychotic trouble. He is played by Cillian Murphy and does a bang up job as a menacing presence for Batman to face. He plans to poison the town's water supply and drive everyone mad. This will prove to be a challenge for Batman because Scarecrow is not the only person he must face. A familiar enemy in his past might come back to haunt him.

I was a little nervous when I heard they were rebooting the series. I wasn't a fan of the last four films. Michael Keaton was a fun Batman. Jack Nicholson lost me when he looked like a clown from the 1966 "Batman" and Tommy Lee Jones didn't do it for me as Two-Face but this picture shines and finally gives us everything we want to know about Batman. The special effects add a monorail in the climax of the film to keep the intensity going and it's a roller-coaster ride you can't look away from. It's clear that Christopher Nolan has a vision in mind for Batman and I'm fine with that. I finally got the Batman movie I always wanted to see and you will enjoy it. Katie Holmes is fantastic at Batman's love interest and I hope to see more of her with the next one. I'm very excited to see what is going to happen next.

10.title: Batman Begins anew
10.content: I expected a lot going into this film, but I was blow away, the film is utterly the best Batman yet. Every aspect of this movie begs for many sequels, and with Christian Bales multi movie contract, I can only wait for more great Batman movies. And the cast! Just perfect, they fit their roles like that pair of shoes you never want to stop wearing. They did a great job of showing both Bruce Wayne and Batman as well, instead of just Batman and Batman without his mask. Christian Bale pulls off the angry Batman with ease, showing us Bob Kane's Dark Knight. Maybe they'll forget about the last 2 Batman movies like they did for Highlander 2 and 3 and remake them with this cast. Go see the movie, if you have, go see it again.

10.title: Throw away the others - THIS is the REAL Batman!
10.content:
This is by far the best Batman movie yet. I think the director must've been a true Batman fan as a kid, because the version of Batman portrayed in THIS movie comes closest to what I felt as I read the Batman comics of my childhood (40 years ago - sigh). THIS Batman is one bad-ass dude. One thing that made Batman so dear to my brother and me was that, unlike his fellow cohorts of the Justice League of America, Batman had no "special" powers other than those of human genius and strength (along with a seemingly infinite supply of money), and yet was second only to Superman in abilities (and he even topped Superman in problems of logic and shear "sleuthdom"). We always figured that Batman had to be more than just some angry super-rich guy, because that wouldn't have held up in the company of people like Superman and the Green Lantern. Batman was a very unique human - the type that comes along only once-in-a-billion times (or less). This movie gives a believable story as to how such a rare individual could come to be.

Christian Bale is excellent as Batman/Bruce Wayne. Finally, not some fop in a mask, but a truly complex character who can be genuinely frightening at times - the only way some guy jumping off of rooftops in tights would be able to maintain any sort of street cred! Also, Michael Caine is THE perfect Alfred - of course.

I really liked the creation of Lucius Fox (expertly handled by Morgan Freeman) - Batman needs a scientist/engineer as part of his "support team." I don't know why DC Comics never figured this out (at least they hadn't 40 years ago...).

The actors (esp. Liam Neeson and Cillian Murphy) portraying villains are just as good at being bad guys as the actors playing heroes are at playing good guys.

This is a movie based on a child fantasy, and so some willing suspension of disbelief on the part of an adult audience is needed. However, never before has a Batman movie made this so easy to do.

10.title: Thrilling, action-packed and expertly made superhero reboot
10.content: Batman Begins is Inception director Christopher Nolan's reboot of the famous Batman film franchise based on the DC comics superhero. Tim Burton and Joel Schumacher had both had their time in the Batman films, and Chris Nolan brings a completely new feel to it, concentrating on elements such as fear and delivering quite a dark, psychological film. It stars Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne/Batman, Liam Neeson, Cillian Murphy, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman, Tom Wilkinson and Ken Watanabe. The film starts by explaining Bruce's fear of bats and then travelling to Bhutan after his parents death and being trained as a ninja by Liam Neeson's Henri Ducard. Ducard teaches Wayne to master his fear and become more than just a man, saying that if he makes himself more than a man, committing himself to an idea, he will become an immortal legend. Bruce returns to the crime-struck and corrupt Gotham where he transforms himself into the double personality Batman, the Caped Crusader, to fight crime. He does this with the help of Alfred, his butler played by Caine who is like his father. Also assisting him is Sergeant Gordon (Oldman), one of the few cops who is not corrupt, Freeman's Lucius Fox, who provides Bruce with his equipment and childhood friend, now DA, Rachel (Holmes). Wilkinson plays crime lord Falcone and Murphy plays Dr Jonathan Crane, the fear-inducing Scarecrow. This film is fantastic in every aspect, with great acting, great action scene, an interesting plot and good themes. Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard's score is amazing, one of the best film scores of all time and Christopher Nolan does a superb job of directing. The only minor problem I had with it was that the Scarecrow seemed to be underused, and it sometimes starts to feel a little rushed in places. However, Batman Begins is a brilliant movie and the sequel, the Dark Knight, takes things to a whole new level. It is an epic start to a trilogy.

10.title: As Comic Book Guy might say: "Best Batman Ever!"
10.content:
I was pleasantly surprised at this movie, I mean "Wow". It exceeded my expectations by a long shot. Christian Bale was simply amazing to play Bruce Wayne.

This movie seemed to have explored more of the darker origins that surround Batman, and I found it to focus more on the hero, then the villain. I feel almost ashamed of saying this, but Christopher Nolan claimed Tim Burton's throne. Not only because this movie is better then the ones Tim directed, but because it delivered more.

"Batman Begins", also might I add is not for Children, as mentioned previously, it is a dark film, much darker then the previous films.

I haven't been much of a DC Comic fan, more of a Marvel, but Batman has always been a character I seemed to enjoy, and "Batman Begins" surely made me enjoy him more.

But what struck me the most about this movie, was Michael Caine. I cannot picture a better Alfred. He's comical, he's witty....he's got the accent! If you are a fan of the Batman saga, or maybe not, I strongly suggest you stop reading this review and head to your local theater to see "Batman Begins". You will NOT be disappointed!

10.title: The real start of Batman
10.content: Genius and unique Christopher Nolan presented us the reality of Batman in a legendary movie, one of the greatest superhero movies, especially the legendary performance of Christina Bell with a wonderful soundtrack. All I can say about this movie is 10/10.

10.title: Really great superhero movie!
10.content: This is in my opinion of the best superhero movies. It is really well scripted, with great dialogue, action scenes, and characters. It gors over the early years of Batman, and is a must see for anyone who is a superhero movie fan.

10.title: The Beginning of a Legend
10.content:
From Secret Organizations, Corruption, and one Man in a Bat suit(Who, clearly, *Does* have issues), The first installment in Director Christopher Nolan's Grand Vision of what the Caped Crusader would be in the real world(*Our* world) does it all.

The appropriately named "Batman Begins" tells the story of disillusioned son(and those around him) to the Wayne's journey to the Cape and Cowl, who, literally, does begin his quest for vengeance, and, ultimately, justice. From small and wealthy orphan, to the vengeful and intimidating figure we all know...Nolan's vision of Bruce Wayne's beginnings are presented in style by actor Christian Bale's outstanding, and, at times, heartbreaking performance of the billionaire playboy/ Vigilante hero.

Being a Thriller, Drama, and a Comic-Book Flick, "Batman Begins" appeals to moviegoers of all shapes, sizes, and tastes. You will cry in moments of sadness, cringe in moments of suspense and fear, and will really dig deep into the drama of the characters and their trials.

And so, "Batman Begins"...is...The *Beginning* of a Filmmaking Legacy, and a Cinematic Legend.

10.title: The Biased Critic: "Batman Begins"
10.content:
I have to be honest with you. I'm biased. I love Batman.

As a kid I was a comic book person (although not a fan-boy), and I always enjoyed Batman, whether as a campy 60s TV hero, or in the gritty 80s comic books. I was 14 the summer of 1989 when Tim Burton's "Batman" came out. It blew my pubescent little mind. I saw it several times, and ate it up like it was fresh popcorn.

"Batman Begins" tops it. That's sacrilege to a lot of people, and understandably so. But "Begins" is above and beyond the best Batman film.

One of its strengths is that it seems to take cues from "Spider-Man": tell a fluid, sensible story, explain the origins of the character, but spend most of the screen time exploring the relationships among the primary characters. And in a way, "Begins" is like a dark counterpart to the Spider-Man story.

But while "Spider-Man", with its splashy colors and frequent CGI, does a better job of making a comic book into a movie, "Batman Begins" succeeds in being the better film, creating a realistic world in which a Bat-Man, an ordinary man with no supernatural powers, could actually exist.

For example: there's a helicopter shot that sweeps over Gotham City about half way through the film, in which Batman is shown standing atop a tower overlooking the Gotham skylineand I got chills. It's that effective. As far as I can tell, it's just a stuntman in a Batsuit perched over a slightly-modified Chicago, but that simple shot absolutely conveys that "this could be real; this *could* really happen". And $100 million of CGI cannot buy those chills.

And that's another of the film's strengths: throughout the movie either it uses sets and models instead of CGI, or it uses CGI so properly (that is, sparingly) and so seamlessly that everything actually looks *real*. I hate to bash George Lucas when everyone else already has, but he spent countless millions making movies starring a Yoda *you can't touch* when he had a perfectly tried-and-true puppet that has depth and weight and texture (not to mention an actor's---Frank Oz's---actual *performance*). With "Batman Begins", it's the other way around: this is a Batman that is so realistic that he threatens to reach out and touch *you*.

Yet another strength: stellar casting. Christian Bale is a terrific Batman, hands down. Sure, there will always be debate among fans as to who's the better Batman, who's the better Bruce Wayne, etc. Again, I'm biased; I love Adam West. And I honestly think that every Batman actor has been good in his own way, even if the particular film he was in happened to suck. But Bale has both Bruce and Batman down in a way that is, I believe, most faithful to the true spirit of dichotomy in the character.

Oddly enough, with the exception of Morgan Freeman, the male cast is made up entirely of Brits, and they all shine. Of course, when do Gary Oldman and Tom Wilkinson not? And Liam Neesonboy, I hate to kick Lucas again, but *this* is what Qui-Gon Jinn should have been. Neeson's character is multi-layered, powerful, and compelling. Take his Ducard character, add morals and a few Jedi mind tricks, and you'd have an excellent Qui-Gon. His success in this movie makes it even *more* evident what a lost opportunity "Episode I" was.

My only gripe is the music. Hans Zimmer is a fine composer, but epic characters in epic situations deserve epic *themes*! Maybe Danny Elfman would have been wrong for the tone of this film (although I think nothe worked in "Spider-Man", didn't he?), but what about Williams? Glass? Even Horner when he's in "Star Trek II" mode? The music is background material in a movie that needs it to be textured for certain scenes, and thundering horns for others.

But that's the only thing that really bothers me, and even that's minor. The tone is perfect. The direction is excellent. The production design is not as immediately engrossing as that of the '89 "Batman", but great nonetheless. Everything that Batman has, from his belt to his cape to his cowl, seems real and imminently touchable. To me, that's indispensable.

The script, while not flawless, is tight and kinetic, keeping me guessing while watching a story I already *knew*. And far from being as humorless as a few critics (notably Gene Shalit) have said, there are many lines that crackle with dry wit, adequately balancing---but not neutralizing---the tension the director creates.

But the triumph of the film, I believe, is in the complexity of its relationships. In the comics, Alfred is not a doddering old queen (as in the films until now) but a superlative (if sometimes unwilling) partner, patching up all of Batman's wounds and supporting him in both of his personae. This is reflected in "Begins". In the comics, Jim Gordon is not a bumbling, overweight, gambling, nearly clueless police commissioner (as in the films until now), but a trusted adviser to Batman, and, above all, an excellent police officer. This, too, is reflected in "Begins".

My only regret is that "Batman Begins" will not be the cultural phenomenon of Burton's '89 "Batman". It hasn't been promoted as well, and it simply doesn't have the advantage of Burton's film, which came out at a time when the superhero film was thought to be dead. Now, because the Spider-Man and X-Men movies are so good (and hopefully, the upcoming "Superman" will be as well), it's simply *expected* that a new Batman film be good, and when it *is* as good as "Begins", it doesn't cause as much of a commotion.

I can only hope that this film is financially successful, and that I can spend future summers escaping the heat by watching Batman---*good* Batman---and eating it up like it's fresh popcorn.

10.title: Batman, has Finally begun.
10.content:
I am writing this review as just having been one of the first of 200 audience members in the entire state of Arizona to have viewed Batman Begins at an IMAX Theater.

let me start off this review by saying, that I have been following this movie for nearly 2 years, since I first heard it was in production, and have been just as eagerly been waiting for it then, as I was 20 minutes before it began.

now then. This movie, redefines Batman as a Badass. no more pussyfooting batman of old, no more "chicks dig the car." B.S, this movie was explosive, when Batman punched someone, the audience could feel it, it wasn't just a punch, but a PUNCH and when you see this movie, you will understand what I am talking about. Batman faces off against 2 villains in this film, Ra's Al Ghul, and The Scarecrow, suffice to say, fans of the comic book series, will not be disappointed in these villains, without giving anything away, I can't say anything further without spoiling anything. This movie follows the basic outline of the "Batman, Year one" series, and you never see the Bat-suit, until 45 minutes into the film. In those first 45 minutes you'll be taken to many different vast, and grand locations. And when we first really see the city of Gotham, it looks like an actual plausible city, not like some Gothic cathedral was vomited all over New York, but an actual plausible city.

Very little digital effects were used in this film (if any) and those that may have been used, I could not tell. Now, my main concern with this movie was the Tumbler, I.E the new Batmobile. It looks bulky and cheap. But when you see this thing in action, you can definitely tell it's a Batmobile Bruce will eventually twist and mold into the Batmobile we know and love by movie 2. (Please god, let there be a sequel, and let it be directed by Nolan) But, I will admit, like every movie, it has its flaws, I felt some of the humor wasn't particularly needed (don't worry its not cheesy like the last 2) but to me I felt a few comedic relief lines didn't need to really be there. I would have also liked more scenes of the underground, to really see the poverty of Gotham, but some may argue there was too much of that, really it just comes down to personal taste.

Anyways, to wrap this up, Great visuals without ******** CGI everywhere like directors are so darned fond of doing anymore, TIP TOP acting (Bale, Caine, Neeson, Freeman, how can you go wrong?) My Rating? 5/5 stars.

GO SEE THIS MOVIE

10.title: Great ride
10.content: I went to see this with my brother in law Monday night,and as my title line said it was truly a great ride.This movie showed Batman the way he was meant to be,a brooding soul traumatized by the murder of his parents,and driven by a sense a of justice.This movie did what none of the others did,explored the reasons he became Batman and how it transformed him.The Bat Cave has always fascinated me,so I found the scenes of how it was discovered and transformed really interesting,as well how he came to possess the Batmobile,suit,and the gadgets.Also,his surprise return to Gotham was cool.Hats off to the whole cast with the exception of Katie Holmes.Very cute,but her acting ability did not impress me.Christian Bale was awesome as Batman,he nailed it perfectly.As for Alfred,Michael Kane was unbeatable.Enjoy.

10.title: The Dark Knight Reborn
10.content: Okay, everyone that knows me knows I really love the first two Tim Burton Batman movies. However...Batman Begins is the best Batman movie ever. It explores the character's motivations with remarkable depth, and actually takes it's time letting the plot and characters develop. It's little over an hour into the film before Bruce Wayne ever even puts the cape and cowl on. This Batman is dark, and vengeful...more so than even Burton's Batman films. Christian Bale is wonderful in the role, bringing a truly brooding intensity to the Dark Knight, and Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon is perfect as well. The rest of the cast fits like a glove, as well (my only real complaint is that Ken Watanabe didn't get as much screen time as I expected, but it's just as well). What strikes me most about this movie is how believable it is: there's not a whole lot of moments where you look at the film and go "no way that could really happen". The characters are the heart of the story here, not their gimmicks or even their "wonderful toys". I truly hope this version of Batman continues on: If handled correctly it could knock Spiderman out of the running for best superhero movie series. 10/10

10.title: This is as good as movies get
10.content:
Christopher Nolan took a major change of direction with the bat. In the whole he did several things right and only one thing wrong.

The right things are as follows: Christian Bale, Liam Neeson (sp?), Michael Caine, Gary Oldman, Cillian Murphy, MORE BAT HISTORY, MORE ACTION (believe it or not), A totally awesome new vehicle, excellent script, more realistic gotham!!!!!!

The wrong thing: No Quotes from American Psycho....

All in all this is as good as films get..it only messed up by not transporting into the script a little Patrick Bateman..still if this doesn't win best film i will crawl in a corner and cry for humanity.....

LONG LIVE THE BAT!!!!!!!

10.title: Awesome movie
10.content: I loved this movie as it was more believable than the previous movies. The bat cave is just that, a cave. THe bad guy is just a person, not some toxic waste experiment. The vehicle is a military-like vehicle, not planes, boats and cars that require CGI to be cool. It shows how he developed his skills, his tools and his persona so it's much more believable than a character taken directly out of a comic book that is already 100% setup with all his gadgets that just happened to be sitting in his property. Where did Michael Keaton's vehicles, tools and utilities come from? Alfred sure as hell didn't build them! Go see this movie!

10.title: Holy Awesome Experience, Batman!
10.content:
Batman Begins is an awesome film. Its easily the best movie I've seen in theaters this year, far better than both Star Wars and Mr and Mrs Smith. Christian Bale delivers an excellent performance both in and out of the bat suit. I am gay for Bale!! OK well, no, I'm still straight, but Bale does an excellent job. There is a lot of action, a lot of drama, good character development.

A lot like Spiderman (1), this movie is an origin story and sets up Batman for more good movies in this darker, more realistic style. Goodbye batnipples (and good riddance), hello new age! It really is just a great film over all and I cant recommend it more highly. I'm eagerly awaiting a sequel, which all signs point to the classic villain, The Joker.

This film is darker and hits you with more surprises than you'd expect, thanks to the Scarecrow's gas. It really is sweet, and it even has ninjas. And we all love ninjas.

10.title: This film shows that good drama is much more important than the latest CGI effect
10.content:
I saw the film tonight and I was glad to finally have something to watch besides one fight after another. Batman Begins is film-making and not just a cheap advert for merchandise.

All the main characters had depth and were all real. The story allows the viewer to connect emotionally to the characters. That seems to be missing from most "blockbuster" fare.

It reminded me of the first Spider-Man movie and I enjoyed that one as well.

I am still a big fan of the 1989 Batman with Michael Keaton, but Christian Bale makes the role his own. When he has the suit on he is menacing yet he seems perfectly normal as Bruce Wayne.

Michael Cain turns in an excellent performance as Alfred. Morgan Freeman is really one of our great actors and his role as tech geek Lucius Fox is another feather in his cap. Katie Holmes shows her growing maturity as Rachel Dawes, Bruce's childhood friend and Gotham A.D.A.

This film shows that good drama is much more important than the latest CGI effect.

It deserves sequel and is easily the best of the summer so far.

10.title: Huge Improvement!
10.content:
60s: We saw the introduction of a huge popular TV series with comic-style, camp humour. The success lead it to an embarrassing (that's a positive comment) movie with four of Batman & Robin's top villains 70s: (none) 80s: A hugely successful & brilliant movie directed by Tim Burton & starring Michael Keaton (Batman) & Jack Nicholson (The Joker). 90s: Another great Burton film, Batman Returns , again with Keaton & also with Danny DeVito, Michelle Pheiffer & Christopher Walken. Joel Schumacher takes over as director & makes Batman Forever which is a fairly good film but his next one, Batman & Robin was a HUUUUUUUUUUUUGE letdown!!!!! 00s: Batman Begins..................

I adored this film when i saw it. Excellent! Full of everything. This film has made an enormous improvement comparing to that damn Batman & Robin tip! I find it quite amazing how it leads on to something completely different to at the beginning of the movie.

(spoiler (maybe)) It starts with Bruce Wayne falling down a ditch full of bats, as a youngster. Soon after, his hugely successful & rich parents are shot & killed. As an adult he joins Henri Ducard who works for the suspicious Ra's Al Gul. But after Ducard & Ra's train Bruce well he does not accept the culture of execution which go by their way of life. I'm not telling anymore (end of spoiler)

Great cast. Freeman, Murphy, Bale, Caine, Homes, Wilkinson, Watanabe, Neeson love em' all! Great characters. Batman is good & Alfred is far better than the last one. Rachel is the good female part (typical action romance). Mr. Fox was a very good character, the sort of typical nice guy that Freeman plays. Alfred has a lovely accent, good old Afred. Oh & don't forget those crafty villains. This time we have one of Batman's greatest foes (sometimes considered "the" greatest although we all know who most people consider the greatest), Ra's Al Gul. I thought he was excellently played by the actor that played him (if i said who was acting him I'd sort of give the story away, don't be confused). Secondly we have Scarecrow who is probably the scariest Batman villain ever. He was brilliantly played. Christian Bale is wonderful & he has a good change of voice. As Bruce Wayne he has more of a clever, happy voice but as Batman his voice is much lower.

This film will grip you to the max! It's tension is remarkable & the use of drama and acting will blow you away. The atmosphere of Gotham City is amazing & dark. That's what we need from batman. Darkness. But light as he's Bruce Wayne. It's great how the icy mountain contrasts vastly in comparison to Gotham City. A good variety of scenery & setting makes this film ultimate!

Batman's costume is very good & the material is much better & doesn't show off it's "rubber-ness" so much. The car is amazing. Apparently not much effort was made on it. So what, it's mighty! The bat-cave I love. Much more naturally located. Bruce's house is nice but I could've sworn it was filmed in the UK!

I have read many magazine's about this movie such as empire & have also been on many websites about it. Most of them say that this is a prequel to the Burton/Schumacher movies. They are wrong! Christopher Nolan has decided to start a whole new set of movies. I prefer it to be that way because I hate it when prequels are made afterwards. Most of them are frowned upon e.g. Star Wars, The Phantom Menace (very successful but i hated it) & the extremely unsuccessful Exorcist: The Beginning only to name a few. I'm glad that Batman hasn't made the same mistake. Phew!

In conclusion this was a brilliant movie which i can't help but love! Nolan, you have been wise.

10.title: Simply Superb
10.content:
OK I watched this last night and I am simply amazed. I would consider myself a comic book fan but Batman Begins makes other superhero movies look ordinary. This is without a doubt the single best superhero movie and it will be hard to see anything surpass this.

The film and story itself are very dark. It reminds us of how troubled a character Bruce Wayne actually is. The way his character is developed is also great. The action is superb and thank god it has very little CGI.

Up until this I would have regarded X Men 2 as the best superhero movie, but it easily surpasses that.

This movie succeeds in every department. It feels much more realistic compared to other superhero movies. It has villains who are actually not likable, usually in superhero movies you come out talking about how great the villains were. This movie does not allow you to do this. It makes Bruce Wayne/Batman the most interesting character. But what strikes out about Batman Begins is that it attempts to be serious and actually succeeds. Spiderman 2 tried this but was a bit like a semi chick flick, The Hulk tried it and fell flat on its face, but Batman succeeds where others failed.

The performances from everyone were great. This movie had a wonderful cast of acting talents and they all deliver. Christian Bale is the best Batman ever, he even surpasses Micheal Keaton. He delivers a brilliant performance.

And a special thank you to the man himself Christopher Nolan. Thank you for diminishing the sad memory of the previous 2 Batman movies. This is the Batman movie the world has been waiting for and I'm sure people are eagerly awaiting your next instalment in this franchise.

I recommend this movie to everyone. Its a superhero movie for a more intelligence audience and not just little kids.

9.5/10

10.title: ~~Beautiful Movie and Best of the Year~~
10.content:
This movie is just so Gothic and wonderful. Some critics complain that it's special-effects driven, but I argue that the beautiful scenery is the thing that adds to the effectiveness of the film more than the CGI, especially the parts shot in Iceland at the beginning.

The second thing that's really excellent about this film is the soundtrack, produced by Zimmer and Howard, which is just something else entirely. It's beautiful, dark and Gothic all at the same time, and really, really emotional. It was one of the first things I first noticed about the film when I saw it in the cinema.

And the third thing is the acting, which was wonderfully executed, especially the differences in beliefs by Bruce Wayne and Henri Ducard whilst Wayne Mannor is burning to the ground -_- That was a truly awesome scene.

~~Lostoyannaya

10.title: As a fan of the comics, this was perfect (SPOILERS!!! so you may want to not read on)
10.content: i have read a lot of batman and watching this was like the watching everything that i have longed to see. it was a perfect representation of the year one stuff written by both frank miller and jeph loeb. the attention to comic book details wasn't all there but that nothing to complain about. it was minor stuff like the fact that the wayne family saw zorro the night they died, not opera. but inversely, the integration of opera as a theme links right back to the comics because dr. wayne was supposed to be passionate about opera. the scare crow was great and completely creepy. the use of characters like carmine falcone and loeb were great and even the love sub plot wasn't over done. the action was fun and fast passed and kept you engaged. if you don't want to hear about the super awesome little thing that happened at the end, don't read past here for this is the SPOILER!!!! the joker is referenced!!!! it was awesome. go see it.

10.title: One Of The Best Comic Book/Superhero Films Ever Made. A Great Start To A Excellent Trilogy.
10.content:
Batman Begins is one of the best Comic Book/Superhero films ever made and a landmark film in the Superhero/Comic Book genre. Filled with great direction,wonderful performances and amazing Action scenes this is Christopher Nolan at his best.

Set in the fictional town of Gotham City,Batman Begins tells the story of a young billionaire Bruce Wayne(Christian Bale)who as a little boy saw his parents killed in a mugging and is scarred. When Bruce grows up and sees Gotham ravaged by Crime and death,Bruce decides to become a masked crime fighter and calls himself Batman. Now,Batman has to battle and stop the villain know as Scarecrow/Dr. Jonathan Crane(Cillian Murphy)while the same trying to save Gotham.

Batman Begins is a great Comic Book film that brought Batman back to the dark and brooding character he was. At first when I heard that Warner Brothers was making a new,rebooted Batman film I was not to excited mainly because I loved Tim Burton's Batman films and I thought the series should not be relaunched. But after Joel Shumacher's campy and candy colored films Batman Forever(which is not that bad)and Batman & Robin(no comment on that film)Batman and the Batman series was saved an rebooted by Christopher Nolan with Batman Begins and with this film gave us a great start to The Dark Knight Trilogy. What separates this film from other Batman films is that BB shows how Bruce Wayne became Batman and the complexity of the character Bruce Wayne. Nolan's film shows viewers how Bruce Wayne became Batman with years of training and building up to becoming a crime fighter with weapons,fighting skills and striking fear in the hearts of the criminals who roam the streets of Gotham City. Bruce trains as Batman in not only the physical and fighting advantage but also the mental advantage by using the dark and shadows. Nolan also shows Bruce Wayne trying to balance out being Batman and Billionaire Bruce Wayne and showing that while Wayne is grown up is still affected by the murders of his parents. BB also shows viewers trying to form and reform relationships because of Bruce's isolation from the city and it's people. What I also love about BB and The Dark Knight Trilogy as a whole is how realistic they are and that while they are Comic Book films they don't feel like Comic Book films. Nolan bought a realism and grittiness to Comic Book/Superhero film that had not been seen much with Nolan giving us a world where Batman could exist in the real world without question and the things that happened in the film are not fantasy but reality. The realistic style of The Dark Knight Trilogy has been imitated since. I also liked how Gotham City looks and is portrayed in this film because it is not the dark and Gothic look of the Burton films or the candy colored campy look of the Schumacher films but a realistic world a Film-Noir world where Gotham is surrounded by cloud,smoke and rain and where criminals rule the streets and it feels real and makes you feel like you are in Gotham. Gotham would play a much bigger part in the other two films. Nolan is a master at pacing a film and BB moves at a great pace and when you watch the movie you would think the film was 90 minutes rather than 140 minutes. The Action and fight sequences are well-done by Nolan and match the tone of the film and Nolan would raise the Action and fight scenes to greater heights in The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises. The ending of the film is great and Nolan shows viewers that with BB Nolan was just warming up and would give us much bigger,larger and more ambitious films in The Dark Knight Saga.

The whole cast does great jobs in their roles. Christian Bale is excellent as Batman/Bruce Wayne,with Bale bringing a depth and complex personality to the role. Michael Caine is wonderful as Alfred,Bruce's longtime Butler and friend. Caine has great scenes and chemistry with Bale. Liam Neeson is fabulous in his role as Ducard,a man who trains Bruce. Katie Holmes does a good job as Rachel,Bruce's best friend and love interest. Gary Oldman is great as always in the role of Cop Jim Gordan,a cop who helps Batman. Cillain Murphy is creepy and menacing as the Dr. Crane/Scarecrow,Batman's opponent. Tom Wilkinson is fantastic as Carmine Falcone,a Gotham City crime boss. Morgan Freeman is wonderful as Lucius Fox,Bruce's weapon and car maker. Rutger Hauer is good and memorable as Earle,an employee at Wayne corporations. Ken Watanabe is wonderfully mysterious as Ra's Al Ghul,Ducard's boss and associate. Mark Boone Junior is memorable as Flass,Gordan's corrupt partner.

The direction by Christopher Nolan is excellent,with Nolan giving the film an intense and dark visual style constantly moving the camera with over head shots while Nolan also does a great job with the Action scenes. Great direction from Nolan.

The score by Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard is brilliant and epic and matches the dark and visual tone of the film. A great score by Zimmer and Howard.

In final word,if you a fan of Christopher Nolan,Batman,Comic Book films,Superhero films or films or cinema in general,I highly suggest you see Batman Begins,one of the best Comic Book films ever made and a great start to a brilliant trilogy. Highly Recommended. 10/10.

10.title: Now THAT'S how it should be done!!!!
10.content:
I just returned from the midnight pre-screening of Batman Begins (2005) at my local theater, and the adrenaline is *still* coursing through my veins!! What a rush!!

To start, let me say that about three weeks ago, I rented Batman (1989), and let me tell ya, that film is fatally flawedI'm not even sure it qualifies as a film. To me, it was like watching a comic book in real time, and while I can see the appeal of this for some of the fans of the comic books, this will not suffice when making a film.

Now, that being said, Batman Begins (2005) is as close as you can get to a perfect film acquiring its source material from a comic book, and *this* coming from a huge fan of both the Spider-Man and X-Men movies. Granted, I love those movies and their some of my all- time favorites, but they're not even on the same playing field as this!

Not knowing anything of the comic series other that it exists, this is *exactly* what I desired to see when I first saw Batman (1989). And unlike that film, this movie does not intend to put on a show, but succeeds in making you *feel* the story. Bruce Wayne is incredibly well- written, and it's especially insightful to see flashbacks of when he was a boy.

The wry, sardonic humor is well-suited for the film, lucratively enhancing its dark atmosphere. The crowded theater housing 250 movie-loving citizens laughed simultaneously throughout the entire course of the film. The director expertly articulates his tightly-wound vision, compelling a film full of depth and personality to the big screen. Christian Bale was eloquent in manifesting a dark, wounded BatmanI don't believe anyone else could've done better. Through the course of the film, I truly believed in Batmanthat he was real and existedthat's how impressive his performance is. It was great to see Liam Neeson in another role, and he does well with the scant material he's given. Morgan Freeman and Katie Holmes fill out exceptional supporting roles, both portraying their respective characters so well, you really get a sense of who they are.

Even though most of us have seen four Batman movies, this film stands alone because despite that, you truly feel as if you're experiencing everything for the first time, as if the material's new and fresh, and this is primarily because it is so perfectly presented in this manner. From his first encounter with bats and how they've become a sort of demon he must continually exercise, his father's contributions to Gotham City, his family history and associations, the source of the one-of-a-kind weaponryeverything is just so thoroughly intriguing and enlightening in a way that you can't quite put your finger on. We learn not only why he is who he is, but how. By the end, I left feeling oddly inspired and almost on a high of sortsit was strange and yet refreshing in a way that I've never felt before.

VERDICT: Thoroughly engrossing and executed with precision and stylea milestone amongst all predecessors. HIGHLY recommended to all, whether you read the comics or not, whether you saw the originals or not, and even whether you like Batman or not. Set aside any and all notions you have, and do yourself a favor and go see this oneI PROMISE you won't be disappointed. This is NOT just a movieit's an experience.

9.5 out of 10.0

~AleXa~

10.title: How Bruce Wayne is a good martial art master and becomes Batman
10.content: When Bruce Wayne was a child, he feared bats, then his parents death was sad, but Bruce Wayne met Ral Al Glul and become a master of the darkness and becomes BATMAN, which Ral Al Glul, I feel who used Bruce Wayne in destroyed Gotham City. The Best Parts in the Movie, is when Ral Al Glul teach Bruce Wayne the ways of a Ninja. Then Batman AKA Bruce Wayne defeated Ral Al Glul in the Train, which killed Ral Al Glul with the Bomb in that train which almost destroyed Wayne Tower. But Batman is a hero who saved Gotham City from Ral Al Glul.

10.title: The best Batman interpretation ever...
10.content:
Hollywood has finally gotten it right - a dark brooding Batman with wit and intelligence that is not a caricature of himself.

Christopher Nolan is a master of story telling. I wanted to see how Batman evolved into the ominous crusader instead of the glossed over version spoon fed to viewers which goes something like this: He saw his parents die, so now he fights crime (insert cartoon villain next).

Christian Bale was fantastic. Michael Cain - fantastic. Gary Oldman - fantastic. Cillian Murphy - fantastic. Liam Neeson - fantastic.

Biggest movie fault - Katie Holmes as Rachel. No chemistry and kind of whiny.

Batman Begins is nothing short of excellent.

10.title: A great movie!!!!!
10.content: Like all the Batman movies, the character who plays Batman does a good job. But Christian Bale did an EXCELLENT job in this movie. He played his role perfectly to make it seem as realistic as possible. This Batman movie had the best story by far. This was probably the best Batman yet. The villains in this movie did a pretty good job and FINALLY weren't just villains that started by being thrown into a chemical bowl thing or getting some kind of hot liquid poured on their face. What makes Batman movies so good is that Batman isn't like superhuman or have superpowers. It makes it so much more realistic. I liked this movie better than the rest of the Batman movies also because there were many villains instead of just a couple. I really hope they make another sequel to this Batman, because they'll sure have my money!

10.title: A grounded and mature take on the traditional Batman mythos
10.content: I can still remember having the day off school to go and see this film when it was first released in cinemas when I was just eight years old with my dad. Assuming it was just another campy superhero flick he reluctantly took me to see it. After leaving the theater, he subsequently returned over the next few days to re-watch it multiple times. Looking back, this is affirmation that this movie is accessible to just about everyone, comic fan or not. This is mostly due to masterful directing, realistic dialogue, a brilliant story and some knock-out performances, namely Christian Bale, Liam Neeson and Cillian Murphy, who each perfectly embodied their characters. The tightly-woven, non-linear story helps make the protagonist, Bruce Wayne's, journey from disillusioned, billionaire playboy to crime fighting superhero far more engaging and enjoyable, as opposed to a regular, linear storyline. This strong story is aided by the dark, modern and gritty visuals of Christopher Nolan and the perfect delivery of lines by every member of the cast. Notably, Michael Caine served as an excellent comic relief, as well as a strong moral center for Bruce and was perfect in his role. While the latter half of the film began to feel a little redundant and too reliant on action effects instead of story, it still served as a decent conclusion to, in my opinion, one of the greatest films of all time.

10.title: Simple, Pure and 100% Batman
10.content: This may well be the movie that every Batman fan has ever wanted on the big screen. I myself never thought that any director could with success direct and portray Batman in such a convincing way that you start imagining Batman as a real living character, and this is of course achieved by the director because he uses simple things that everybody can understand and relate to and putting it in context of why Batman is the way he is. Christopher Nolan has done this masterfully and Christian Bale is perhaps the best actor ever to portray Batman. A very impressive movie on all levels and by this I mean the script, acting and directing.

10.title: Best Reboot Ever
10.content:
The last two Batman's left a bad taste in my mouth. I was pleased to know that Christopher Nolan was taking over. I knew he would steer the movie to a more darker tone. He did not disappoint.

I was impressed with cast, especially Christian Bale. He is Bruce Wayne and he did well as Batman. You couldn't cast someone better than him. He's going to be around Hollywood for a while after he stops playing Batman. I was also pleased with most of the other cast members especially Gary Oldman. He just slips into a role with ease.

It is nice to see a big budget movie that does not use much in the way of CGI. The people who choreographed the actions scenes did a great job.

One problem I did have with the movie was Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. Her performance was very bland and underwhelming.

Overall a great movie.

10.title: Great Movie.
10.content: Saw this last at the first 12:01am showing. Glad I did. Certainly worth seeing. Nice to finally see a darker Batman movie than the last few Batman movies that were clearly marketed towards the younger crowd. The cast for this movie was great, and I look forward to seeing the next Batman movie. Some people may say it moved a little slow at times throughout the beginning of the movie, but it needed to in order to establish the story again. Christian Bale was great, but it took a little bit to get used to his Batman voice. I really enjoyed the mood that they set throughout the movie, as things were not as bright as the other previous Batman movies. I can't say much more, as I don't want to spoil it for anyone who hasn't seen it yet, so I'll just say that it's certainly worth seeing.

10.title: Not just the best Batman
10.content:
This is not just the best Batman movie, but one of the best movies I have ever seen period. In a word...EXCELLENT! Just go see it. George Lucas could learn something about story telling and choosing excellent writers, actors and director.

The characters are well developed and well acted. You actually care about them. The story and atmosphere are real. You get sucked in from the beginning and stay until the very last frame. Christian Bale IS Batman and Michale Cane does a great job as Alfred. The biggest surprise is Gary Oldman as a good guy. He should do it more often. Can't wait for the next installment!!

10.title: It's him! Who? The Batman!
10.content:
"Batman Begins" is a movie about Bruce Wayne's early years and how he became the dark knight. There is an all-star cast which includes Christian Bale, Michael Cain, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, Gary Oldman, Cillian Murphy, and Morgan Freeman. As a young boy, Bruce Wayne watched in horror as his parents were gunned down right in front of his eyes. Then Bruce becomes obsessed with revenge, but his chance at revenge is taken away by fate. Bruce then flees to the east and seeks the counsel of dangerous but noble ninja cult leader Ra's Al-Ghul. Bruce then returns to the now decaying Gotham City, which is overrun by organized crime. Meanwhile, Wayne Industries is slowly slipping through his fingers. Bruce then sets his plan in motion to help Gotham City. With the rediscovery of the cave under his family's estate and a prototype armored suit, Bruce becomes Batman!

I liked this movie very much because it's not like your typical comic book movie. This movie shows that maybe, just maybe, this could happen in real life.

Christian Bale gives a great performance as Batman, not as good as Michael Keaton in the original "Batman" but very believable. The rest of the cast is amazing in their roles; Michael Cain is terrific as Alfred.

Overall I give it 3 out of 4 stars.

10.title: The Bat is back!
10.content:
Batman Begins is a reboot of the entire Batman film franchise. No longer would we have to suffer through another of Mr. Freeze's campy one liners. No longer would we have to suffer through the "nippled" bat suits again. From here on out, it's dark territory.

Let me just say if you're a Batman fan, then you're going to love this picture. Christopher Nolan has truly looked out for those who wanted a better adaptation of the titular character, and it shows throughout his movie. Batman is once again pictured as a dark character, a watchful guardian throughout the night. He doesn't hesitate at beating criminals to a pulp with his bare hands. In fact, he's pretty brutal here.

This has to be the most accurate depiction of Batman that I have ever seen, and if you're truly a fan of the comic books, you're in for a real treat.

10.title: The Best Batman? In a Word, Yes!
10.content:
Having just seen "Batman Begins" for my third time (the other two were during its theatrical run), I must say that the hype is true. It is the best overall effort yet in bringing Batman and the world he inhabits to the screen. Christopher Nolan brings shows us EVERYTHING we wanted in a film about Batman's origins.

Bruce Wayne's descent into the caped crusader is handled with care and grace. The script is based on several different Batman comics from over the years, which makes its story very well-rounded. It's a script that's emotional without being sappy and funny without being stupid. Also, it has one of the best casts ever assembled and each member shines in every line they deliver.

The design of Gotham City is amazing and the special effects are not over-reliant on CG images (which is a problem for big-budget movies these days) and are comprised of many different elements, including very realistic miniatures. To sum it up, the feel of the movie is dark, brooding, shrewd, and refreshingly pragmatic.

That's not to say the film has its share of blunders. The music is less than impressive. It sucks to think that a film this great has a musical theme comprising of TWO NOTES. Maybe some people see its effectiveness, but in my mind, it causes only disgruntlement. And to boot, "Batman Begins" had TWO great composers working on it. That's ONE note for each guy credited with the score! I give their effort a D. Another nit-picky problem I had with it is in it's rather fast-paced editing not only during action scenes, but even when there are only talking heads. It's just a little nerve-wracking.

But these are small problems when compared to the whole movie package. The fact that I'm complaining about such small details only exemplifies the film's success as a whole. What else is there to complain about?!? I would recommend that any self-respecting movie lover buy the deluxe DVD. You'll be making a great and worthy addition to any collection.

PS.....Being that the Tim Burton Batman movies were very influential and special to me as a kid, I personally LIKE them better than Nolan's film. But regardless of my personal preferences, I of course acknowledge "Begins" as a better display of Batman's universe. I'm just a sucker for those Burtonesque visuals set to Danny Elfman's amazing, beautiful music. And no, I don't shop at Hot Topic.

PPS....There's no point in even mentioning the horrible Batman Forever. Not even Jim Carrey and Tommy Lee Jones could save that one. And Batman and Robin is such a festering abomination that rationalizing its existence is a futile aspiration.

10.title: Batman begins review
10.content: This is one of the only movies I can rewatch and never get sick of! Great superhero film!

10.title: A perfect start to a trilogy
10.content: Batman Begins was the without a doubt the perfect start to a great trilogy. I absolutely love the cast choices for each character. I love the origin story for Bruce on his road to being Batman. The way we saw him grow from being Bruce Wayne to Batman was done beautifully. The way we saw him trained by Ras Al Ghoul was a great way to see him learn the skills needed to be Batman. Christian Bale playing Batman was done better than I have ever seen anyone else as Batman, Liam Neeson as Ras Al Ghoul was done beautifully, Michael Caine is the perfect choice for Alfred, Gary Oldman was fantastic as Gordon, and Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox is amazing. Personally, i don't think they need to do the origin story again, because this movie did it to the point that it doesn't need to be done again.

10.title: Loved It!
10.content:
Just few things to say...

I loved it! I loved it! I loved it! Best movie I've seen in two years! I have to admit, I had my fears. I'd seen sooo much of it the past few weeks, I figured it was just an over hyped machine. But, my fears were allated. Now I can't wait to see the next one.

After seeing it, you'll say, "Tim Burton who?" My cousin put it well. The Tim Burton movie was a revamp of the 60's campy TV show. This one is the comic book to big screen version. It captures the Dark Knight oh so well.

How would a crime fighter work in the realities of our world? This movie does a fine job of explaining away most of the holes.

10.title: Finally, Batman is back in business!
10.content:
I have to first admit that I avoided this movie. After experiencing the utter disappointment that was Batman Forever (adequate, but flawed) and Batman and Robin (just plain awful), despite the wonderful Christopher Nolan at the director's helm and gifted actor Christian Bale in the suit, the sentiment shared by many Batman fans that what would come out of this film would be more regret was shared heavily by myself. How could I be so wrong? Firstly, this movie is not a sequel or a prequel - Nolan has created a new Batman franchise which (arguably) betters Burton's. Gone are the campy villains, neon backgrounds and bat nipples. In their place are multi-layered, wonderfully acted villains, a dark, brooding Gotham so reminiscent of the early Batman comics, and a Batman actually able to kick butt and look convincing while doing it.

The movie is wonderfully scripted and plotted. The initial scenes which describe to the viewer Bruce Wayne's adult fascination with bats - and the reason for his lifelong quest for justice - are done in such a way that you actually don't question how a grown, normal man could fight crime in a bat suit. The rest of the movie becomes more complex as it goes along, while still retaining several moment of humor that don't seem too forced or too campy - though I'll leave it for you to discover for yourself.

The casting is brilliant. Christian Bale has already proved himself as a quality actor in such films as American Psycho and The Machinist, and he did not disappoint in Batman Begins. As the quissential comic book love interest, Katie Holmes as assistant District Attorney Rachel Dawes has little to do, though she does give a surprisingly spirited and engaging performance. Supporting actors Liam Neeson, Ken Wantanabe, Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine are all icing on a delicious cake.

The real find in this movie, however, has to be Cillian Murphy, who plays Dr. Jonathan Crane, aka The Scarecrow. His performance is mind-blowingly articulate and at the same time chilling from the first moment you lay eyes on him in a courthouse. As much as I hate to use clichés such as this, Murphy is truly a face to watch.

What else can I say? Nolan, Goyer ... thank you, from the bottom of this Batman fan's heart. 10/10.

10.title: Not just a Comic Super Hero Adventure
10.content:
Solid Cast + Great Music + Superb Pacing + Good Action +

Simply Put- One of the best Mainstream American Film 2005 has to offer up to 6/15. There are many contenders for various Awards and the only gripe that I could possibly think of is that Combat scenes were frequently filmed in high speed with a close up zoom. Fine for occasional effect but not for every fight scene.

Dialogue strikes a balance between serious and humorous like it was lifted from one of the Elseworlds DC universes.

Calibre of the Cast is not wasted on this project as all the roles have their moments and the film ultimately leaves the audience feeling as if they witnessed something special. Not just Special effects and Big Budget Gadgetry or formulaic Action Blather, but a genuine attempt to give a fresh look at the origins of a Super-Hero Icon. First Constantine and Now Batman Begins show that serious topics and themes can be used in Comic-Book Films. This succeeds more than most ultimately because of the air-tight pacing and great cast. Oh and a few Surprises along the way help too.!

10.title: "Batman Begins" Review
10.content:
Following the works of Tim Burton and Joel Schumacher, Christopher Nolan presents a new and improved Batman movie more heavily grounded in reality (or about as real as a comic-book hero film can be), and with a strong emphasis on in-depth storytelling and style.

Despite the emphasis on character development and drama, the film is entertaining. It might even be more entertaining than all the other films before it. Action is frequent and impressive. Some of the fights might be hard to see with the shaky cameramanship and fast editing, but the car chase, the stuntwork, the (few) special effects, and the finale are all very noteworthy. In between the major action scenes, the story moves with a fast and tight pacing. There's hardly a dull moment.

At its core though, this telling of "Batman" presents a very strong story, filled with deep characters, strong themes, and detailed nuances. The story itself is pretty solid, for as the mystery unravels it proves to be cleverly sublime and tight. What is most important is the character development though; Bruce Wayne's origins are explored in depth and with solid reasoning behind his ascension into a masked vigilante. Going hand-in-hand with this portrayal are strong themes about fear, morality, and ultimately the value of decisive action. And as the Batman character comes into a fully-realized being, a lot of interesting concepts are poured into it like hot iron filling an ingot; using fear as a weapon, the principles of ninjutsu, the power of symbols, to name a few. And on top of all that, the physical genesis of the character is explored more thoroughly than ever before; we finally see where he gets all his cool gadgets from, where his costume came from, how he gained the trust of key law enforcement officers, among other things. All of these concepts work together to make the story more believable, whereas in previous movies nothing was defined and everything about the character simply existed without any basis. The movie gets high marks as it is for utilizing previously unused opportunities. I'd give it even higher marks for its strong themes.

As a film, it is interesting. Photography is superb throughout, with plenty of unique imagery and camera angles. Editing is very rough, with some choppy action scenes, but most of the time it works to create a unique and frenetic style. Acting is excellent all around; Christian Bale shows both aggression and subtlety in his dual-natured role, Michael Caine makes for a wise and witty butler, Cillian Murphy and Liam Neeson are cool as the villains, and Gary Oldman is perfect as Jim Gordon. It's also pretty cool seeing Katie Holmes, Morgan Freeman, Rutger Hauer, and Ken Watanabe in the mix. Production value is very high, with loads of excellent sets, props, costumes, weapons, cars, gear, and everything else. The music score is epic! 5/5 (Entertainment: Very Good | Story: Perfect | Film: Very Good)

10.title: Great depiction of Batman
10.content: I watched this movie a lot when I was younger, with other movies like The Dark Knight, Star Wars, Spider-Man, etc. I hadn't watched this movie in a long time when I decided to re-watch the Dark Knight Trilogy. It's safe to see this is one of the best Batman movies. It's sequel is ofcourse way better, but people often forget this one.

10.title: Really awesome
10.content: One of the best super hero movie from legendary director. Major plus point is realistic approach or we can say characterization of Bruce . That realistic approach I liked the most and other plus is cinematography and CG they are very good. Overall a must watch movie. Perfect start for triology. Nolan you are unbelievable.

10.title: Batman for everyone!!
10.content:
*Spoilers*

Batman (1989) and Batman Returns (1992) were visually stunning but you could feel it's cartoonish vibe. While the characters (the good and the villains) were perfect in every aspect, the experience was all about fantasy. The action sequences in both movies were great but not as spectacular as in 2005's Batman. I know, the f/x were not that advanced but still. 1995's Batman was a great sequel to end the franchise. It had two quality villains, a spectacular scenario, great f/x but you could say that it was all about cash. The movie had potential. Batman & Robin...well, what can I say? it's not even better than Batman's worst comic. This is the best "Batman" movie of te saga, period.

BATMAN BEGINS delivers for everyone! It explains every single doubt for every Batman fan. The plot is as good as you can get in an action film by inserting the obligatory dramatic elements, a love story, and the basic subplot that deals with Bruce's internal demons. The way Christopher Nolans connects all the events is simply amazing. The man demonstrated with "Memento" that he could create a clever, fast-paced, visually stunning thriller-action movie. He did the same and I say better work with this movie. The plot is dark but effective, it doesn't deal with the expected cartoonish villains or something like that, it deals with believable villains (in the standards of comics) that could anytime beat easily The Joker or The Riddler. There were some "scary" moments in the movie. Not only visually but mentally. I mean, Dr. Crane's technique to create panic by wearing the mask and spreading some kind of poison is an impressive technique to create tension and fear. The same goes for the panic that Gotham City started feeling after the massive poison spread. Batman has scenes FOR EVERYONE.

ACTING. The acting in the movie is easily the best in the series. Christian Bale (of American Psycho fame) portrays Batman in a solid, violent, and cool way. Batman was never this impotent! Excellent dramatic performance. The best Batman no doubt about it. Michael Caine delivers a great, dramatic, and tender performance as Alfred. Also, congratulations to Morgan Freeman (as always), Gary Oldman (as always), and Liam Neeson for great, convincing performances. Cyllian Murphy and Katie Holmes deliver expectations. The rest of the cast including Ken Watanabe and Tom Wilkinson are solid.

DIRECTING. Christopher Nolan did a great job. He created the spectacular Batman movie everyone was waiting for since Tim Burton's Batman Returns. The innovative camera angles, the scenes to break (in the climatic train scene at the end, Nolan makes a take of a fully illuminated Gotham City with tense music) or increase tension (pair to pair scenes with explosions), the fight scenes, etc. are high quality, the best you can ask for in an action movie. Mr. Nolan deserves respect, a lot of it because he overpassed expectations in a way that only a few can.

F/X, SOUNDTRACK, ART DIRECTION, CINEMATOGRAPHY. The movie is brilliant to look at. It has an impressive shinning yet dark cinematography beautifully done. The soundtrack is perfect for the movie and the art direction is excellent, with great details. The F/X are just great, Batman is a movie that proves that CGI abuse is not the best to impress people.

As a hard core Horror movie lover, I can say I'm satisfied with this movie. The same should go for fans of comics, action, and films in general. BATMAN BEGINS is an impressive movie recommended for anyone that wants to have a great time with a movie that mixes drama and action in a perfect way.

10.title: Arguably the best Batman film ever
10.content: Batman Begins is an exciting and incredibly satisfying experience. The story was spot on and thrilling, the plot realistic and fulfilling. The special effect were both breathtaking and terrifying. The cast, as well, didn't fall one step short. Morgan Freeman and Michael Cane were deliciously funny and exquisitely cast. Liam Neeson and Gary Oldman alone were worth the price of admission, and Cillian Murphy as Dr. Crane was thrilling and disturbing. Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne AND as Batman gave a gorgeous and flawless performance: Keaton and Kilmer can eat their hearts out! A wonderful film for any Batman aficionado as well as those just looking for a great film. It's rare for a film to achieve this much perfection.

10.title: Damn!
10.content:
This movie rocked the house. I mean, it had everything a Batman fan could hope for. Action, good character development, a strong storyline, and hot babes to boot! Being somewhat of a comic enthusiast myself, I'm glad Christopher Nolan remained faithful to the comics in order to tell his vision of the Caped Crusader itself. When you watch this movie, you WILL believe that Christian Bale is Batman. He completely owns the role in every way. I also liked that all the actors played their roles seriously, and didn't act all cheesy and melodramatic, like some of the characters in the older Batman movies. Although I thought some of the action scenes were edited together a little sloppily, it actually emphasizes that Bruce uses deception and speed to overtake his enemies. Also, I liked the way all the characters had a role in the movie. Even Commissioner (or rather, Lieutenant) Gordon got to drive the Tumbler in the final action scene! All in all, a wonderful film.

Bottom Line: Go see this. Like now. Run to your nearest theater! Now!

10.title: Easily the best Batman movie ever
10.content:
I've just gotten back from a screening of *Batman Begins*, and I can tell you all quite honestly that I wasn't too keen on seeing it beforehand. I knew Christian Bale and Katie Holmes were in it; I knew that it contained the origins of Batman; I knew (sort of) that it was opening this week. Other than that -- I knew nothing. I had seen the other Batman flicks before... my least favorite being with Clooney and those anatomically correct suits (had to have the nipples) -- and none really grabbed my attention quite like this new one has.

The casting is brilliant, and Bale as our dark brooding bat is nothing short of excellence. Caine as Alfred -- had some excellent comedic timing (although, I kept having this nagging expectation that he'd turn into Powers Sr. again).

I'm sorry. I'm just so speechless -- it's the PERFECT summer blockbuster. Star Wars EIII's got Nothing on this one.

10.title: Batman Begins is one heck of a great film! Its cool with an excellent cast and a astounding score!
10.content:
It was on the 4th of July, 2005 I saw Batman Begins! It was an awesome experience to see the Dark Knight on the big screen once again! I have been anticipating this film and it did not disappoint. The movie is solid with an outstandingly large and famous cast, great acting, super storytelling and character development, excellent action and effects, a tremendous musical score, and great directing! There are many points in the film I want to talk about including the cast and characters, composers, and scenes. The commentary is below.Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne/Batman: Bale has a great performance. He is younger than Michael Keaton but he pulls off the charisma Wanye needs. He is nearly identical as Keaton when it comes to the putting on the suit. He has very good movement that makes you believe he is the Batman! His voice fits the character really well. I know that there are people who think that Keaton IS Batman. In My opinion Bale comes very close being number one. Michael Caine as Alfred: In My opinion Caine was the perfect choice to play the famous butler. Caine provides very good acting here. In fact its some the best I have ever seen him do!Liam Neeson as Henri Ducard: Arguably his greatest role and greatest performance Neeson is terrific in this film and literally steals the show! He is one of My favorite actors of all time and it was just awesome to see him as a big time villain! I love the way he looks. His goatee, hair style, clothing, fighting ability, everything! If you are a fan of his and loved how he performed in Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace then you WILL LOVE HIM HERE! Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes: I was very surprised by this actress. I have read many, many comments saying how weak, dull, and boring her performance is. Well I didn't see any of that! I thought that she was very good and not to mention looked the same. Her character IS A WOMAN and she is very convincing as A WOMAN! I like female characters like this! Holmes is a very fine actress and I hope to see her in many other great action films in the future! Gary Oldman as Lt. Jim Gordan: He is excellent as Gordan. A very likable character indeed. I like the way he is and looks. Another top notch performance by Oldman! Cillian Murphy as Dr. Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow: He is something else. Just by looking at him I thought that he was insane! The Scarecrow character is good and scary. Tom Wilkinson as Carmine 'The Roman' Falcone: One of the most talented actors performs greatly as the big time mobster. Wilkinson's British accent is gone and a very good Italian accent has taken its place for his role. I was really anxious to see how he would perform as someone of this stature in a comic book feature film and in My book he was great! Morgan Freeman: Freeman is a dandy charmer here! Great acting as always. Rutger Hauer as Earle: Hauer was very good. He's not his usual action hero self here as he is a business executive. Ken Watanabe as Ra's Al Ghul: Great performance here. He makes his character mysterious and fearful at the same time. He has an awesome sword fight and shows you why he's a master! Mark Boone Junior as Flass: A good performance by this big man! Linus Roache as Thomas Wayne: In a brief performance he is very good. Musical Score by Hans Zimmer & James Newton Howard: This is an extraordinary score. It fits so perfectly in it and it is completely different than the music that Danny Elfman and Elliot Goldenthal composed for the previous Batman entries. I love those scores but this one is excellent as well. Its just so dynamic and exciting! If there are more Batman films which I hope there will be I hope that they will be chosen to score again and again! Direction by Christopher Nolan: He really put it together here. The fight scenes and everything is just marvelous. I hope that he directs more Batman movies in the future because I like his direction. Fight Scenes: People are talking about how bad the fight scenes are. I liked 'em! They were very exciting and some of them were long too like the Wayne vs. Ducard scenes. I loved those! The street chase was really cool with all of the city lights and such. So there you have it! I loved the film. There many, many things I love about it. The things above like cast, music and the fight scenes are just a few. I like the fact that all of the cast members have a decent amount of time on screen. I saw Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith twice and I adore that movie and I just love this one! People, we have a very exciting movie year in 2005 and so far I am pleased and you should be too! I want more of the Batman movies because I love the people in this film and there are limitless possibilities that can happen in them! I would love to see the return of the Scarecrow! Bring fourth the Joker, Man-Bat, Killer Croc, The Huntress, Harley Quinn, the Spoiler, Cain, Egg Head, Mad Hatter, and the rest of the gang to the big screen!

Movie Nuttball's NOTE:

Before the movie started the trailers of War of the Worlds and The Island were shown and boy do they look great! Bring on more DC films like more Batman, Superman Returns, Wonder Woman, The Justice League of America, The Legion, The Green Arrow, Justice Society of America, The Death and the Return of Superman, I could go on! I want DC & Marvel to come out with a whole bunch of films including Crossovers! It'll be so awesome!

10.title: This is truly Bob Kane's vision
10.content: We've had various versions of the the caped crusader through out his illustrious history. Some were great, like Tim Burton's first Batman film. Some were laughable like the Adam West TV series. Some were just so awful we dare not speak of it (Bat-nipples? Why?!). I can finally say that someone got it right this time. Christopher Nolan and David Goyer brought us a Dark Knight that is so close to Bob Kane's vision that I'm sure he's smiling down to us from "up there". Christian Bale was perfectly cast in the lead role. He played the Bruce perfectly. He gave us a Bruce Wayne that we can actually care for which was not done well in the previous Bat-flicks. His portrayle of Batman was so intense and mean that it brought a tear to the eye of the most die hard bat-fans. The villains were villains, which was the big mistake in "Batman Forever" and "Batman and Robin": the villains were jokes. Ra's Al Ghul was such a cerebral villain and a "ying" to Batman's "yang". The Scarecrow was such a creepy, scary character that embodied how dark and scary Gotham has become. Cillian Murphy played the Scarecrow like a horror villain which is how it was meant to be; a twisted mind concealed in the form of a "respectable" doctor. Michael Cain for me was the biggest surprise. I never thought much of Alfred before. I always that he was a handy butler for Bruce Wayne. Michael Cain however changed my view of him. He played Alfred with such a warmth as a father figure and a friend. He was actually quite funny as well with his one-liners every now and then which helped lighten the mood in the darkest of situations. Gotham City was also stunning, being all dark and gloomy, and not a bright light circus act that the last two bat-films showed. I do not want to get into the plot in respect for those who have not seen the movie but I guarantee whoever watches this movie, they won't be disappointed. Many films in the comic book genre are predictable. I can proudly say that "Batman Begins" is not predictable at all. It's riveting, exciting, intense, and very very fun. This is definitely the joyride of the summer and I highly recommend it. I'm sure Bob Kane would too.

10.title: Outstanding
10.content:
The first time I saw Tim Burton's take on Batman, I was stunned. I fell in love with everything the movie had. I was anxious to see the sequel when it came out, and it certainly didn't disappoint. The dark, Gothic settings, fascinating characters, cool gadgets... they had it all.

When I heard about the third one being in the makes, I was dying to see it. I was pretty young back at the time, and watched the Batman Forever trailer over and over again. Granted, I was very, very disappointed to see Michael Keaton (and Burton) step down, but I was still hopeful for the movie. I hadn't heard much about Joel Schumacher or Val Kilmer at the time, but as I got over the shock of the new guys taking over the franchise, I went into the theater open minded... and came out utterly disappointed. I felt betrayed, like they'd turned one of my favorite movies into some sort of a joke. I lost all hope. I didn't see the following one (Batman & Robin) until early last year, and it was even worse.

When I heard about a fifth one -at this time they still hadn't revealed a director or the leading man- I wasn't interested at all. I saw the whole franchise as this old, limping dog, taking its last few breaths before disappearing for good. Then one day, I watched a little movie called "Memento". Still one of my favorite films, I decided to check this Christopher Nolan guy out. It turned out he was a fantastic director, very talented, but not really the comic-book-action kinda fellow. So when I found out he was going to make "the new Batman" I was quite puzzled. At the time, at least, I was sure it was bound to be better than the two previous movies.

I followed every single bit of news they had on the movie, and was mostly positively surprised. Christian Bale, an actor I've liked for a long time now, was going to be Batman. A sigh of relief, it was. When I learned about the rest of the cast, I was nearly knocked off my chair. Michael Caine as Alfred? What? Amazing.

I still remember refreshing the Apple.com trailer page repeatedly, waiting for the trailer. I was ready to pop after that. I HAD to see this film.

Well, I just watched it (LATE, I know, I know), and I have absolutely no doubt that this film saved the franchise. I thought it was impossible. The cast is superb. The story follows the comics almost religiously, and by god, it works. I was saying "wow" out loud every five minutes while watching this movie. It tells you everything you ever wanted to know about Bruce Wayne becoming Batman, yet has time to give you all the Bat-action you were missing out on for the last 13 years. Twists and turns, fantastic action, stunning acting and even a wonderful hint about the next film in the end.

This is THE Batman movie as far as I'm concerned. See it.

10/10
