It's advisable to Murphy's that he tone down his "pretty boy" looks by taking roles that embellish the super villain, bad guy genre, Why? Because Hollywood needs more good looking bad guys! Ask Johnny Depp he will concur! Murphy certainly has the talent to carry of these types of roles and I sense it's a conviction for him to avoid the trap on winning roles based entirely on one's looks and being overlooked for one's talent. We all wish the best of luck - however Hollywood has a way of revising one's conviction for the sacrifice of something else. Still, we anticipate that his career will rise like the sun and we continue to watch with great interest.

Batman Begins - a great film and a damn good use of my increasingly precious time. I am for one, exceedingly grateful that Christopher Nolan was at the helm! And we liked that he kept the hair cuts clean! One of the best films of the year.

9.title: Batman Begins- finally erasing the memory of George Clooney and Joel Schumacher!
9.content: Fantastic. Simply superb. This is the Batman movie Tim Burton should have done and what that destroyer of tradition Joel Schumacher didn't have the brains to do. Christopher Nolan and Dave Goyer couldn't have wrote a better origin story and re-ignited the franchise that Schumacher nearly killed in 1997. Basically, the previous 4 Batman movies do not exist. This is a not a sequel or a prequel to them, this is new start for Warner Bros as the superb script focuses on the origin story of Batman- how Bruce Wayne was traumatised by his parent's murder's and travelled the world learning various fighting skill's and studying the criminal mind in order to return to Gotham City to fight the injustice that is plaguing the city, and in doing so creates his alter ego Batman. The creation is of Batman by Wayne is very realistic in detail, such as him creating the Batsuit from a protective military outfit taken from the Research and Development Department of Wayne Enterprises rather than the usual 'How in the hell did he make that rubber suit?' nonsense. Christian Bale is superb as Wayne and is brilliant as a much darker Batman, who finds himself up against his mentor Ras Al Gul and the insane Scarecrow. The fantastic supporting cast (featuring greats like Michael Caine, Liam Neeson and Morgan Freeman) add so much depth to a film that isn't just about action sequences but about character development and excellent story telling. A smash hit at the box office, this is brilliant viewing.

9.title: Life in the old bat yet
9.content:
Well, where did they pull this corker from? with Batman and Robin forever scared in my memory I felt Spiderman and forthcoming Superman were the only hope left for the super hero's.

Was I wrong? - yes way out. Christian Dale was bred for it and when you have a supporting cast that includes Caine, Freeman and Oldman you are already half winning but then if you then add a little Neeson, and a bit of a back story then you have made a 'stayer'.

Very enjoyable and to be honest there are not many films in the last 5 years that have had my attention to watch them more than once - Batman Begins has surpassed this with honours.

I loved it, they scrapped everything and went back to the roots, brought back the dark to the story and the light to the characters.

This is a must see, even the car is brilliant, they even had a good story on how the car (the tumbler) came about.

The 'baddies are good (but not excellent) but they (hollywood) have finally learnt not to kill the best bad guys at the end of the film unlike the Joker and the Penguin.

Buy the film!!! you will not be disappointed.

9.title: It's not who you are underneath, it's what you do that defines you.
9.content:
We've seen so many Batman movies just to disappoint ourselves but this one's different. This one's more than a superhero movie. It's a hero movie. Batman, in this movie, is not just some guy in a fancy bat-suit beating the heck out of criminals. Batman is not fighting rogues on the streets of Gotham. Batman is fighting a battle within. And that's what makes the movie so special. Bale has portrayed Batman like no one could've ever. Nolan has made the character so intricately that it leaves an impression on your mind. Batman is more than a hero. More than a savior. More than a guardian. He's a symbol.

The movie has its flaws but they can be neglected. Liam Neeson is just awesome. Plays the proper mentor and villain at once. Katie Holmes is good. Michael Caine is just superb as ever. Gary Oldman & Murphy are as good as they can be. Morgan Freeman needs no judging.

I think this movie is way better than its sequel. Not saying that The Dark Knight is a bad movie. It's one of the greatest movies I've seen but this one's special. This movie's not bout Batman like The Dark Knight. It's bout Bruce Wayne.

9.title: The revival of the franchise
9.content:
After Batman and Robin, as well as Batman Forever it was clear that the Batman Franchise should either avoid movie adaptations or find a way to revive the quality of the original batman movie.

That is where Christopher Nolan comes in. Batman Begins goes where no other batman movie has gone so far and shows how Bruce Wayne acquired all of his gadgets and became the able-bodied fighter of the comics. I was sceptical about Christian Bale playing Batman, but I was delightfully surprised by his portrayal of Batman.

If you have seen Batman and Robin or Batman Forever, it is good to know that this adaptation is much darker, but at the same time the movie doesn't take itself too seriously. Michael Caine, isn't as good and Alfred as the one from Batman Forever, however he still plays the part well by being a mentor for Bruce Wayne and source of comic relief.

In less detail, the other performances are also of high-quality. Although, Katie Holmes's part is weakest in my opinion.

The action sequences could have been improved. However, the sequences were still impressive and there is more room for improvement and development in the sequel. A sequel, which I am already eager to see.

9.title: The Dark Knight Returns
9.content:
In 1966 Burt Ward and Adam West took to the screen in the cinematic adaptation of the cheesy Batman TV series. Twenty-three years later a twisted film geek named Tim Burton revived the mysterious superhero for modern audiences. His two films, Batman and Batman Returns, delivered a darkly comic vision of Bruce Wayne's alter ego. The first film was a massive success, both critically and financially. Batmania was in full swing, despite many casual moviegoers mumblings that the film was "too weird and bleak." Burton's vision didn't wane the slightest bit as he offered up an equally chilling sequel three years later. Batman Returns was successful, but failed to generate the hysteria that surrounded its predecessor. The powers-that-be must have felt the only way to revitalize the franchise was to water it down for mass consumption. This led to the appointment of Joel Schumacher as director for the third and fourth installments (Batman Forever and Batman & Robin). Fresh blood could not save these features from their ludicrous dialogue and cartoonish tone. Even the most die-hard fans were wishing for the Bat to be put to sleep. After all, if Hollywood wasn't going to tell these stories right, why tell them at all? Flash forward to the year 2005, which Batman enthusiasts will henceforth refer to as "Year One." Christopher Nolan, the gifted filmmaker responsible for the mind-bending Memento, has finally given this series the honest, respectable makeover it has sorely needed. Modeled after the Batman graphic novels penned by Sin City creator Frank Miller, Nolan's feature gets back to the crusader's roots. Christian Bale (American Psycho) assumes the role of Bruce Wayne this time around, and it's a brave choice that pays off nicely. The film itself focuses on the events that molded the young billionaire into the masked vigilante we all know and love. After failing to avenge his parent's death, Wayne disappears into the criminal underworld, eventually finding himself in a distant prison. Angry and sorrowful, he is under the tough tutelage of Henri Ducard (Liam Neeson). Ducard instructs Wayne in the ways of martial arts, while also helping him to confront his deepest fears. As Wayne nears the end of his training, he realizes that Ducard and his master, Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe), intend on destroying Gotham. They feel it is little more than a breeding ground for impoverished criminals, and while there is some truth in this, Wayne disagrees with their ideology and genocidal methods. He soon returns home after a seven-year hiatus, and begins creating the mythic figure we call Batman. It is as this point that the film finds it groove and will likely win over most of its observers. The first act of the film has all been backstory that is unfamiliar to most casual fans of the character. However, director Nolan was wise to stay true to his vision. By taking Wayne out of Gotham and briefly disorienting viewers, he has injected a much-needed jolt of reality to the story. We look on quizzically as exotic locales, ninja warriors, snow-capped mountains, and Asian mystics wash over us. Are we in the right theater? But those who remain patient through the first half of the film will be greatly rewarded. It took a lot of guts for Nolan and the studio to make this film. It is not the merchandiser's Batman, and it is most definitely not a children's movie. This should be evident by the stellar cast that surrounds the still relatively unknown Bale. Morgan Freeman, Michael Cain, Gary Oldman, and Katie Holmes are just a few of the talented actors who deliver wonderfully reserved performances in this truly unique picture. As last year's Harry Potter installment proved, great things can be done with popular material when entrusted to the right filmmaker. This movie isn't likely to smash box office records or send kids running screaming to toy stores, but it has done something remarkable just the same. It has taught an old bat some new tricks and given the rest of us a complex, believable superhero. That's more than just fine with me.

Rating: A-

9.title: A surprisingly good movie
9.content: Having got Batman Begins for Christmas, I was wary of its content considering the lame efforts after the first one. However, having watched it I found myself engrossed in it. It was a highly entertaining movie and possibly the best Batman yet. The DVD just contained the movie and the trailer which was something of a surprise but sometimes this is a good thing. Having watched several DVD's which show in dept backgrounds to scenes and the highly irritating stories of what a struggled it was to bring the movie to the screen, the lack of extra's was somewhat of a bonus! The movie itself is brilliant and for once the blurb on the front was justified.

9.title: Best Batman Ever
9.content: This movie makes the Tim Burton version seem as outdated as the 1960's t.v show. Batman has never been one of my favorite superheros (until now!) and after the last couple horrible sequels I wasn't feeling too pressed to catch this one. Boy was I surprised. Great acting all around and a awesome script by David Goyer who also did the great Blade movies. The biggest surprise to me was how well the female character was written and how good Kattie Holmes was in the role. Bale is also perfect in the role of Bruce Wayne and the costume, car and gadgets he uses were all designed really well. I really hope they can keep this tone and look in the sequel. And I hope they again use villains who haven't been used to death. This Batman would kick Spiderman's sulking butt. I see they're making a new Superman - it might make for a cool sequel to team them up.

9.title: Batman has begun
9.content:
I was excited for this film since it was first announced, the darker tone to the movie was more akin to the Burton films and with Nolan at the helm I knew I was in for a different take on the character.

The film is a classic origin story of any franchise but the main difference here is that Nolan manages to make what the character accomplishes believable and make the how and why Batman can do certain feats a possibility.

There are a couple of scenes which could frighten the younger children so I would advise parents to watch the film before hand, it is not the usual superhero movie most expect to see. The film is a lot darker than the Burton films, The character installs fear into the villains through various ways. Just a word of warning.

There is really too much to say on the film and for the most part they would be huge spoilers, my view is simple, this is a must watch movie even for the viewers who are not superhero fans.

9.title: Phenomenal
9.content: I couldn't rate this movie without at least writing something about it, especially after watching the four previous ones which I'm glad I did because it made me recognize how valuable this one is. Not like the others, this one is closer to the reality therefore doesn't feel unreal or cartoonish, which in my opinion makes us more connected with the story. In a nutshell, I'd say it's the most precise and realistic interpretation of the Batman I've seen to this day.

9.title: The best Batman movie ever
9.content: Definitely and undoubtedly the best Batman movie till date.It was not like the other Batman movies that had a certain amount of futuristics added to it,Christopher Nolan's direction added a dash of realism to the flick.The story was the same but the screenplay was totally different,from Bruce Wayne's childhood to his journey as the dark knight of Gotham the story started from the scratch and everything was different and quite realistic. Christian Bale portrays the Batman as no other actor has ever before,he exceeded our expectations both as the Batman and as the suave ,notorious playboy Bruce Wayne even better than Michael Keaton.Gary Oldman was perfect as police officer Gordon,the best part was the making of the costume ,Batman's Den and the acquiring of the famous Batmobile,his flying has a logical angle(which actually is gliding).His costume is the best among all the other Batman and his Batmobile too was the best(its origin was logical),It was intended to be a vehicle used during combats but was never put into production,until Bruce Wayne gets his hands on it. Also Michael Kaine and Morgan Freeman did judgment to their parts as Alfred and Mr.Fox respectively .This movie is a definite watch,for all movie buffs.

9.title: A Clinic On How To Do A Superhero Origin Story
9.content:
After the colossal flop that was "Batman and Robin", the entire Batman franchise went into a bit of a lull. Rumors of a "young Bruce Wayne becoming Batman" movie circulated for years, but nothing substantial was finalized. That is, of course, until up-and-coming director Christopher Nolan became attached to this project. What resulted was an absolute clinic on how to craft a superhero origin story.

For a very basic overview, this movie centers on young Bruce Wayne's (Christian Bale) transformation into the Dark Knight. After the death of his parents in Gotham City, Bruce travels the world and is ultimately initiated into the League of Shadows, a mysterious vigilante group headed by a mentor-type figure (Liam Neeson). This is an intriguing process that probes the very roots of civilized society and makes us question the notions of revenge, vengeance, and justice. Later, as the film transitions into more of a traditional comic book story, the piece's primary villain--The Scarecrow (Cillian Murphy)--of comic book fame serves to reinforce all those themes in Bruce's return to Gotham, this time as the winged avenger of iconic lore.

The hallmark of "Batman Begins" is how it doesn't simply use a single event--the death of Thomas and Martha Wayne--to turn Bruce Wayne into Batman. Sure, that is the inciting incident, but the "middle stuff" isn't glossed over. In fact, those years between young Bruce in an alley and Batman's entrance into Gotham are precisely what Nolan delves into here. His transition from essentially a spoiled rich kid to a symbol of hope/justice is expertly cataloged and very much makes sense from a practical, real-world perspective.

Lest one get too philosophical, though, this film contains more than its fair share of exciting chases and intense action, the staples of superhero films. Viewers are introduced the the Batcave, the Batsuit, and The Tumbler (proto-Batmobile), again all setup in very real-world, practical terms. All those elements are seamlessly weaved into the overall storyline.

The acting in this movie is pretty solid throughout as well. Christian Bale is a solid Batman and an even better Bruce Wayne, while Michael Caine (Alfred), Gary Oldman (Officer Gordon), Neeson, and Morgan Freeman (Lucious Fox) are spot-on as usual. Katie Holmes seems a bit mis-cast as a potential romantic interest for Bruce, but it works well enough to at least get by.

Overall, this film is nearly the perfect amalgamation of origin story, intense action, and relevant world-building. If you were intrigued by the Burton Batman films but fell away from the franchise after the Schumacher years, you need to re-discover this new incarnation as represented by Christopher Nolan.

9.title: Absolutely THE best Batman movie ever made...
9.content:
I really loved Batman Begins. It has the perfect blend of action, emotion and romance. The special effects are well done and subtle. The story was well written. You will like this movie. Each actor is totally believable in his/her role.

I was particularly happy with Christian Bale's performance as Batman/Bruce Wayne. He played his part wonderfully, bringing to the screen the perfect amount of mystery, bravery, & elegance. He was born for this role. The supporting cast was amazing, from Liam Neeson to Morgan Freeman. I was very impressed.

This is the best Batman movie by far. It has every element you need in a superhero film.

9.title: What Batman is all about
9.content:
May I start by saying that the contrast between 'Batman&Robin' and 'Batman Begins' could not be more obvious. The 4th movie was disastrous and killed off the franchise for years, this movie comes storming in under a brilliant and visionary director(Christopher Nolan) and has replaced any garish comic book slapstick with a more serious and gritty tone. Gone are the bright colours and campness, this film means business!

This time the black suit is filled by Christian Bale. He is an obvious choice for the caped crusader;hes good looking, well built and has a stern look that is used frequently to good effect. He adds a depth to the character that George Clooney didn't even touch, he shows us his dark side.....

The element of fear is pivotal throughout this movie .

This is the 5th instalment in the franchise and I would say the best. Yep, even better than the original Batman. Why? because it delves deep into Bruce Wayne's past: his parents death, his loving father, his pre Batman training at a snowy and mysterious mountain temple, his pre Batman attitude. The film itself is very slick: amazing special effects,pumped up action, stunning visuals and very interesting characters. Not to mention of host of new gadgets. I highly recommend this movie to anyone, young or old, as this movie truly en captures the spirit of Batman and tells you what he stands for.

9.title: Batman Begins
9.content: Not only that it is the best Batman film, but is probably the greatest superhero film ever. This tells the origin of how Bruce Wayne (Christian Bale) became the Dark Knight. The story is absolutely incredible. After the death of his parents, Bruce Wayne decides to leave Gotham City and travel through out the world to try to find a way of overcoming his fears (including bats). While he was in this Asian prison, he meets Ducard (Liam Neeson) who becomes Bruce's mentor. He was then later release and decides to find the League of Shadows, led by Ra's Al Ghul (Ken Watanabe). When he nearly finish his training, Bruce finds out that the League are attempting to destroy Gotham. He manages to escape, and returns to Gotham to become Batman. Directed by Christopher Nolan, he has a damn good job at doing it. With a brilliant supporting cast such as Michael Caine as Alfred, Gary Oldman as Lt. Gordon, Cilian Murphy as the Scarecrow and Morgan Freeman who plays the inventor of Batman's gadgets. The film also starring Katie Holmes as Batman's love interest and Tom Wilkinson as a hardcore gangster. The new Batmobile is unstoppable. But especially, Christian Bale is by far the best actor to play Batman. I can't wait for the sequels to come, and who will play the Joker and Two-Face.

9.title: Unconventional conventional blockbuster
9.content:
So much has been covered in all the reviews so far that I will keep this short and sweet.

Many art house movies aspire to Hollywood greatness; Batman Begins is a Hollywood blockbuster with art house aspirations. Turning the hero/villain action film formula on its head in this manner works exceptionally well here in the hands of Christopher Nolan & company, who have put together a film where no matter how packed the action, no matter how much Cee-Gee-Eye Candy crowds the frame, plot and character hold forth as the principal driving force from start to finish.

Christian Bale acquits himself admirably well here, and the many familiar faces in the supporting cast provide impressive depth and nuance working in an ensemble context. One standout is Cillian Murphy, who is either rivetingly creepy or creepily riveting depending on your point of view.

The cinematography is gorgeously noir and the sound design and score do a phenomenal job of setting the tone of the film (hey, how can you go wrong with BOTH Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard working in tandem on the compositions). There is as much ear candy as there is eye candy in this production, thanks to a crack team of foley atists and sound design pros.

Regardless of whether you're a die-hard Batfan or have simply been jaded too many times by Hollywood excesses typical of productions like these, you will find a lot to like in this movie.

9.title: Brilliant cast, excellent story, thrilling action
9.content:
Batman Begins is a masterpiece, miles better than the Michael Keaton Batman's (although they're not bad) the film obviously benefits hugely from Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman, Katie Holmes, Morgan Freeman, Liam Neeson and Cillian Murphy playing the main villain the "Scarecrow". Neeson's character is also a villain (better add a spoiler warning for that) but less so and he's more morally grey.

Action wise the film's impeccable, the plot is great but not perfect and the cinematography, special effects and music are all on point. I would highly recommend the trilogy.

9/10: Expertly crafted, not just a stupendous film but also very enjoyable.

9.title: Almost perfect
9.content: This movie is as close to perfect as it gets. Especially for a superhero movie. Where do I begin. Christian Bale. Wasn't sure about him. I was wrong. Even better than Michael Keaton at handling the dual role. I enjoyed watching him as Wayne as much as Batman. And as Batman, Bale proved outright to be the most physical of all Batman's portrayers. In one scene where he is shirtless, you see the physique and go "wow". Small detail, but Keaton and Clooney never bared their chests, and when Kilmer did it in "Forever" it made you want to laugh. In fact, if I remember correctly, my brother did laugh. But when Bale is in bed recuperating after a rough night and Alfred brings him some kind of health drink, you can see the muscle tone that Bale possesses. It's real and not CGI--most impressive. He drinks, then gets up and starts doing pushups on the bedroom floor. I was completely convinced that Bale is the right man for the job. Now Alfred. No doubt. Micheal Caine. Perfect. Luscious Fox. Morgan Freeman. Now the plot. "Batman Begins" pretty much covers it and Nolan does it beautifully. The origin story is the plot. The villains take up about 2 thirds and Cillian Murphy, Tom Wilkinson, Ken Wantanabe and Liam Neeson are completely awesome. Some of the best villains Batman has ever faced. And Lt. Gordon. Gary Oldman. I can't remember seeing him in a role I didn't like, even if I wasn't crazy about the movie.

9.title: Seven years later, still the best Batman film.
9.content:
Seven years later and after two exceptional films The Dark Knight(2008), and The Dark Knight Rises(2012) I still stand behind my belief that Batman Begins is quite simply the best superhero film of all time. It had it all-- a exceptional cast, a great story, and finally for once told the story of Bruce Wayne.

Everything from the action scenes, to the pacing, the dialogue, and sense of humor just made the film one of my favorites throughout the years, and Christian Bale's performance as Bruce Wayne/Batman finally had depth to such a complex character. Fans including myself, finally portrayed a realistic Bruce Wayne, a side you never seen in the previous film. Bruce is supposed to be a troubled soul, a playboy, and of course his alter-ego Batman.

It was satisfying to also see Michael Caine as Alfred who gave a great performance in the role, where during Burton/Schumacher series their wasn't much of a relationship between Bruce and his trusted butler. Their was a emotional connection that I felt was important and added character to Alfred and Bruce.

The rest of the cast was exceptional as Gary Oldman as James Gordon, who also developed a relationship with Batman, a relationship I felt important to the film series. Morgan Freeman as Lucius was a great addition because you have to wonder where he get's all these cool toys, and for once it is believable.

Liam Neeson was great as well, and his character fit so well into the plot. I couldn't imagine anybody else playing Henri Ducard as well as Neeson. The only thing lacking in my opinion was The Scarecrow played by Jonathon Crane who's hallucinogen played a vital role in the plot, as well as Katie Holmes character of Rachel Dawes left a bit of a sour taste in your mouth.

Regardless this movie had great action scenes, although some of the fight scenes are too fast, and the camera angles we're horrendous on some of those scenes. The Tumbler scene is still in my honest opinion the best action scene in all of the trilogy. Finally the Batman franchise was given a respectable movie-- darker, grittier, and more realistic. A believable world brought to life by Christopher Nolan.

9.2/10

9.title: A new side of the bat.
9.content:
This to me is the best batman movie up to date. It is going to leave you begging for more.

Batman Begins shows how Batman came to be, fighting the Crow, and ra's al ghul.

This takes away most of the humor, better costume, more about Batman's origins, and they take away the nibbles finally. The acting by Christian Bale is superb. Plus, the action is way better. The fighting includes Martial Arts which Batman is supposed to be an expert in. I didn't get to see this movie until it came out on DVD. How I wish I would have seen it in theaters. It's always better in the theaters. Enjoy.

9.title: A Dark and Gripping Origin
9.content:
"Batman Begins" is a masterclass in origin storytelling and a remarkable reboot of the Batman franchise. Christopher Nolan crafts a grounded and emotionally resonant narrative that delves deep into Bruce Wayne's journey from a grief-stricken boy to Gotham's Dark Knight. This film not only redefines the superhero genre but also elevates it to a level of sophisticated storytelling.

The standout aspect of "Batman Begins" is its focus on character development. Christian Bale delivers a stellar performance as Bruce Wayne/Batman, portraying his internal struggles, determination, and duality with remarkable nuance. The supporting cast is equally compelling, with Michael Caine as the wise and loyal Alfred, Gary Oldman as the earnest Jim Gordon, and Liam Neeson delivering a commanding performance as Ra's al Ghul. Cillian Murphy's chilling portrayal of Dr. Jonathan Crane/Scarecrow adds a layer of psychological tension.

The cinematography and production design create a dark, gritty atmosphere that perfectly complements Gotham's decaying state. Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard's score is a triumph, evoking both the heroism and the underlying darkness of Batman's journey.

Nolan's direction shines in the film's exploration of fear and justice, themes that resonate throughout the story. The action sequences, particularly the Batmobile chase and the climactic confrontation, are thrilling and well-executed. While the pacing occasionally falters in the first act, the film quickly finds its footing and delivers a captivating narrative that keeps the audience engaged.

"Batman Begins" succeeds not only as an origin story but also as a film that respects its audience's intelligence. It's a thoughtful, mature take on a beloved character that sets the stage for an exceptional trilogy. This is a must-watch for fans of Batman, superhero films, and anyone who appreciates compelling storytelling.

9.title: One of the best superhero origin movies
9.content: Great acting, a good villain and a good story what more could you want.

9.title: Christian Bale takes the crown as the best Batman ever....
9.content: I was unfortunate enough in not seeing this film in theaters and I regret it everyday. I own the single wide screen version of the film on DVD, but if you have a 1080p TV go for the blu-ray version. I honestly believed that Christian Bale was the wrong actor for the role and boy was i dead wrong. I must say he is the best Batman hands down. Now that would be a big statement coming from a huge fan of the comics. I base my decision on Bale's incredible skills of performing real moves of martial arts. for the first time i finally see batman actually use his elbows as well as his knees to take down some of his foes. It's funny to see in the 1989 Version how Michael Keaton could just do a back hand punch on somebody and knock him out instantly. I also find him to be a bad shooter as he literally aims at the joker with his arsenal on the bat wing and still misses. I believe Christian Bale is the real deal and now that the "Dark Knight" is out, it's official that no one else is capable of beating him as Batman. This movie makes you forget that there was ever a Batman film before it. I recommend this film for hardcore Batman fans and those who are just introduced to the franchise. I suggest getting the DVD since it's cheaper but if you're spoiled with a HDTV then get the blu ray.

9.title: Christopher Nolan + Batman = genius
9.content:
Admittedly, I watched this after watching The Dark Knight because I was just so excited to watch The Dark Knight after all the hype that's built up from the reviews, also their vastly different titles, I did not know they were from the same director or even connected with each other. I don't think I'm alone in saying it's inferior in comparison to its successor, but the writing and acting were already miles ahead of the previous Schumacher Batman franchise.

Batman Begins came out at just the right time, before the market became over commercialized with super hero comic book movies and the right amount of time for Batman fans to want more after the Schumacher movies ruined him for most people. I wasn't even allowed to watch the Nolan movies because my older siblings said they were too dark. But that kinda made me more excited to see them and I was thoroughly impressed after seeing Batman Begins and the Dark Knight

I feel like anyone can watch this film and enjoy it immensely.

Aside from the superb writing, amazing production design, engaging acting, and the single best live action Batman ever; this movie's action really isn't that good to watch. That's my only problem with this film. The action scenes are so choppy and disorienting that it's hard to know what's going on, it is forgivable, at least to me because Christopher Nolan didn't exactly have the experience of making action films, considering this is his first one.

Clearly, he's taken that criticism on the chin and took whatever coaching he needed and knocked it out of the park with the action in Inception and The Dark Knight.

Even with so many great things involved with Batman Begins, Christopher Nolan still is the star of this film and deserves the credit.

9.title: Great!
9.content:
After seeing the last three awful Batman movies I had to be coaxed to see this one. I was very glad that I went. This is not only by far the best Batman movie I have seen but the best comic adaptation film outside of the Spiderman movies! What always bothered me about Batman and my main sticking point with the Michael Keaton film was that he had all this elaborate equipment and this super high-tech batcave and it was never explained how he got it. Also, you wondered how nobody would be able to figure out who he was, especially the person who built the batmobile in that movie. Finally, we have a movie that explains everything and does it well.

Also, Batman doesn't appear till more than halfway through the movie and we don't really care. The character of Bruce Wayne is fascinating and the director did such a good job of telling the murder of Wayne's parents that it was difficult to watch the scene without crying yourself.

Liam Neeson is super in this film as a teacher to a troubled Bruce Wayne, schooling him in Ninjitsu and other fighting arts. Morgan Freeman is excellent as an employee of Wayne Enterprises who was pushed aside after the senior Wayne was murdered and who is in charge of a lot of R&D military equipment that he provides for Bruce. And of course Michael Caine makes a super Alfred! Then there is "Sargent" Gordon, who seems to be one of the few non-corrupt police officers that Batman immediately identifies as someone he can trust for help.

There are many memorable scenes in the film, especially where Bruce is making his first batarang and designing the Batman suit. The city looks a lot more realistic than any of the previous films (even though it doesn't look like the Gotham of the comics) as does the bat signal (it appears in the sky distorted, as it should).

I hope the director can do as well with a sequel and not be tempted to go off on the "camp" road that the other series of Batman films followed.

9.title: Finally a movie that does Batman Justice
9.content: When i first saw this movie; i have to admit i didn't think it held up to the Burton originals (Batman and Batman Returns). But after seeing it for a second time i realized how deep this movie really is. Batman Begins is all about the inner conflicts that occur within Bruce Wanye. This movie truly delivers on the the emotional trauma that young Bruce went through; and as the movie progresses it pulls you in deeper and deeper into what goes on in his head to make him become "The Batman." By becoming grittier and darker than its predecessors Christopher Nolan is able to finally do the comics justice and reboot this wonderful franchise. This movie might not be as supernatural in its approach nor is does it have any of the mainstream villains that we remember from the TV show but it does have intellect, heart, and most of all the atmosphere Gotham has always been waiting for.

Watch now!

9.title: In a way, it's the best of the trilogy
9.content:
I recently rewatched all 3 of the Nolan Batman movies, and it shocked me how good Batman Begins was because I hadn't seen it in so long. Something I realized while watching it was in more than one way, it is the best of the trilogy.

Firstly, Gotham is really well done Begins, much much better than DK and DKR. The city's atmosphere is very prominent and it feels like the city straight out of the comics. The only other Batman-verse movie I've ever seen whose Gotham is better or matches Begins, is the Joker (2019). This is an important aspect missing from the two sequels as in those movies Gotham just feels like New York and Pittsburg and lacks character. And make no mistake, Gotham is a character in and of itself, or at least it should be.

The 2nd way it's the best is it's not as grounded. DK and DKR both feel like they're very real and exist in our world. That's not necessarily a bad thing but it also takes away from the movies' atmosphere. Begins has more wacky elements to it like the device Batman uses to call all of the bats to escape the Asylum, and the visions people had when they were dosed with Scarecrow's drug and the layout and architecture of the city. Things like this make the movie more fun than the others.

All of this is not to say I don't love DK and DKR, I think DK is one of the greatest movies ever made and I think DKR is very under appreciated in the trilogy. But I almost wouldn't even categorize them as superhero movies, they're more crime thriller than anything. Begins definitely feels like a superhero movie to me, and in my opinion, it was way ahead of its time.

9.title: My favorite Batman movie to date
9.content: Out of all the Batman movies from the Nolan trilogy, Batman Begins is my favorite. There's just something about it that makes me love it so much. I love this depiction of Gotham; it feels so true to the original source material, especially the Narrows. Ra's al Ghul is such a great character too. I think Liam Neeson nails this character, it's just unfortunate we didn't get more screen time for this character. And the evil master plan was genius, and it brought some really cool cinematography. The action is great; not as good as the others, but it makes sense as it's an origin story for Batman. And the music is absolutely awesome. This is my favorite depiction of Batman to date, and I highly recommend everyone to watch the Nolan trilogy in chronological order.

9.title: This is what i call PERFECTION
9.content:
Christopher Nolan's reimagining of the Batman mythos in "Batman Begins" isn't just about the caped crusader's battles against Gotham's criminals. It's about the man behind the mask, Bruce Wayne, and his journey from a vengeful orphan to a symbol of hope and justice.

The film delves into Bruce's psyche, showing us the trauma that drives him to become Batman. His fear of bats, stemming from a childhood incident, becomes a powerful motif throughout the story, symbolizing his own journey to conquer fear and darkness.

Nolan's masterstroke lies in making Gotham City itself a character in the film, a corrupt and decaying metropolis in desperate need of a hero. The city's bleakness mirrors Bruce's own inner turmoil, highlighting the moral ambiguity of his mission.

The moral of "Batman Begins" is twofold: first, that true heroism isn't about superpowers or flashy gadgets, but about overcoming one's own fears and flaws to make a difference in the world. Bruce Wayne isn't just fighting crime; he's confronting his own demons and finding redemption in the process.

Secondly, the film explores the power of symbols and their ability to inspire hope and fear. Batman isn't just a man in a costume; he's a symbol of justice and defiance against corruption. Likewise, the villains in the film, from Scarecrow to Ra's al Ghul, use fear as a weapon to control others, highlighting the thin line between heroism and villainy.

In the end, "Batman Begins" is a triumph of storytelling, blending heart-pounding action with rich character development and thought-provoking themes. It's a film that challenges us to confront our own fears and embrace the hero within. A perfect 10 out of 10.

9.title: A fine return to form for the Batman franchise
9.content: A brilliant, a brilliant film, cast in lavishly dark tones, supported by an amazing cast and coherent storyline. Christian Bale rightfully inherits the Bat-mantle from the stellar Michael Keaton, and crafts a character that is layered yet far more interesting to watch than any of the latter incarnations. The scenery is amazing, and the cinematography is spot-on. Christopher Nolan's Gothic vision of Gotham is the best I've seen so far. The Scarecrow is a truly horrifying villain, and Ra's Al Ghul and Henri Ducard make very worthy foes additional foes. I left extremely satisfied by the amount of information they packed in. I would have enjoyed a little bit more of Gordon, but more can be done with him in future films. The last scene is a killer.

9.title: "Your anger gives you great power. But if you let it, it will destroy you. As it almost did me"
9.content:
The best phrase to describe Batman Begins would be a perfectly balanced classic'.

This is a phenomenal superhero movie, and one of the best films that I have had the pleasure of watching.

Batman Begins is a heavily character-driven story, but the beauty of it is that it manages to combine the perfect blend of action, drama, emotion, suspense, and beautifully crafted storytelling throughout the length of the feature.

The origin of Batman was the right place to give the franchise a unique breadth of life, most people know of Bruce Wayne who turned to vengeance after the death of his parents. But this is the first time we see a confused, but intelligent, Bruce which takes him into the depths of the criminal underworld.

In Batman Begins, Bruce Wayne is searching for his identity, he meets Henri Ducard while in a prison cell who informs him that they are fighting on the same side. Bruce then journeys onwards toward the league of shadows who are led by a man by the name of Ra's Al Ghul.

Once at the Himalayan temple of the League Of Shadows, Bruce undergoes a grueling training regime to transform his body and mind into something more than a man, a symbol that can inspire hope and will put fear against those who would use fear themselves.

In this story, you naturally forge an emotional bond with Bruce Wayne's transformation into Batman. You follow his struggles, and his actions against Gotham's criminal underbelly which is told with clever dialogue by Rachel Dawes, and then repeated back to her later in the film by Bruce Wayne thus revealing his identity 'It is not who I am underneath, but what I do that defines me

There is maybe only a handful of performers that speak with a commanding presence. One is Liam Nesson, and the other the Michael Caine. Every time one of them spoke they stole the scene. There is just an aura of white noise in the background so that you are silently alert, and you take notice of absolutely everything that they have to say.

When a film becomes iconic such as Batman Begins, it's not just the epic storytelling, but also it's a lot to do with the dialogue or phrases that leave you with a powerful, lasting impression.

Some of these imprint in your mind and stay with you forever such as a phrase from Bruce's father 'Why do we fall, Bruce? So we can learn to pick ourselves back up.

The discussion between Alfred and Bruce 'Why bats, Master Wayne? Bats frighten me. It's time my enemies share my dread.

And even Henri Ducard 'You must become more than just a man in the mind of your opponent'.

Batman Begins has a monumental ensemble cast, one that is almost unrivaled in today's cinema. Christian Bale as Batman, Michael Caine as Alfred, Katie Holmes as Rachael Dawes, Cillian Murphy as Dr. Crane/Scarecrow, Gary Oldman as inspector James Gordon, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Tom Wilkinson as Carmine Falcone, Rutger Hauer as Earle, Ken Watanabe as Ra's Al Ghul and Liam Neeson as Henri Ducard.

It's also worth noting that Director Christopher Nolan is extremely bold but adventurous. Many of the action sequences are done without CGI. He demands a certain level of realism which means everything you see represents our world in some way, and therefore he has a great sense of believability in his work.

Batman Begins is exactly how you should tell a story with cinema. It transports you into the world and gives you a little bit of everything with a vast variety of locations, props, and characters to keep you feeling engaged and interested.

Overall there was a wonderful collaboration in this picture. From the opening scenes in Iceland to the gritty Narrows, extensive cityscapes, and fine attention to every detail including the grueling fighting styles this is a film that will be remembered for the ages.

9/10.

9.title: The Definitive Superhero Origin Story
9.content:
Christopher Nolans "Dark Knight Trilogy" is one of the greatest trilogies of all time and it all started with this movie that breathed new life into what was considered to be a dead franchise and proved that Nolan was a talent to be reckoned with. The way this film handles its central character is just perfect, Nolan creates a wounded and damaged character that is just amazing to watch. Wayne in this movie is not the perfect billionaire playboy that other films have presented him as he's got some major issues and makes some questionable choices in this films flashbacks. His training with The League of Shadows was done just right you got just home Important it was for him to pass them but understandable why he doesn't stay with them. Christian Bale was fantastic in this movie he captured all versions of the character that was require and to date remains the best iteration of the character. Katie Holmes was fine here she did that was required of her and was a good support for Bruce, while far from a great performance not razzie worthy. Liam Neeson was great as Ra's Al Ghul he's not in the film much but was really good when he was their and really felt like he was another version of Bruce and made some good points. Michael Caine is absolutely perfect casting for Alfred he hits just the right note between funny and fear and is never dull for a single second. Before this film the character of Commissioner Gordon had never been done much justice in film but Gary Oldman gave such a good performance in this movie and was a really likable presence. The action sequences in this film were really good they felt very realistic and gritty especially the final the sequence on this train that was a really intense and well done action set piece. The fear toxin was a really good plot device, you got his dangerous this was a why it needed to be stopped. I do have but one flaw with this film and it's the way in handle the villains. Scarecrow was good for the most part but he was far the easily defeated. Ra's Al Ghul needed to be in this film more and the swing between Ken Watanabe and Liam Neeson wasn't done well and felt very forced and awkward.

This is an amazing film it got most of its characters right and went on to start the perfect superhero franchise.

93%/A

9.title: Simply Superb

By far the best "Batman" film yet and probably the biggest surprise of 2005. This one's not a comic book. It's dark, it's suspenseful and it's well-acted. Not saying that Jack Nicholson wasn't superb in "Batman", but Cillian Murphy (playing one of the villains) gives the old man a run for his money. 9.title: Batman Begins With a Vengeance
9.content: Back in the late 90's, early 00's, I was introduced to Tim Burton's 'Batman' and 'Batman Returns' and I immediately turned my back on the overly light, and crumbling Christopher Reeves 'Superman' series. Here was a story about a man who gives up his life to catch the bad guys who murder and steal, just like the one who killed his parents and goes out every night to protect the city and stop the bad guys, even if he has to spend the rest of his life doing it, and even to my five or six-year-old mind, to me that was fantastic. Whilst the pretty okay 'Batman Forever' and the utter failure of 'Batman & Robin' still leaves a very bad taste in my mouth, Christopher Nolan's 'Batman Begins' brings in a fresh new turn at the Dark Knight, and explores every nook and cranny of the origin story, even the ones that were not fully explained even in the comics. With a good, new, sharper and a more darker, stormier Knight, played by the brilliant Christian Bale, 'Batman Begins' proves to be the grittiest of them all, even without the overuse of special and visual effects, because they focused on something that the last two Batman's did not have, a dark, gripping and emotionally hooking story, and at 2hrs and 20mins, it tells that story with perfect pacing and shows no point of slowing down from the moment the logos hit, all the way until the Batman spreads his cloak and soars into the night's wind for the closing image. Christopher Nolan delivers a Batman for the new generation whilst giving the fans of the old generation the Batman that they deserve, desperately need, and the Batman that they have been crying out for, and that my friends is something to aspire to.

9.title: Masterful Filmmaking
9.content:
I've got to be honest right from the start. Batman Begins is an amazing film. From the acting to the cinematography to... everything, really. The film opens to show a young Bruce Wayne falling into a well and being scared by bats before being rescued by his father. Later, Bruce's parents are murdered, due to his fear of bats. The next thing we know, he is in a prison. A businessman by the name of Ducard shows up and offers him a deal. If he can make it to the top of a nearby mountain bearing a purple flower, he will be trained by the League of Shadows and given the means to "fight injustice". He makes it, goes back to Gotham to fight crime, and a legend is born.

This film is one of the darker superhero films in recent memory, and it pays off. Where other movies are cheesy or even downright ridiculous, this one is brutally honest. Bruce Wayne is a real man driven by real emotions. He is real, and those watching can feel him reflecting even the deepest parts of their souls. After his parents' deaths, he is driven by anger and more than anything else, he wants vengeance. But the more he fights evil, the more he begins to love those he is fighting for. In the end, he is Batman not out of hatred, but out of love.

If the film has a fault, it's that the pacing feels just a little off halfway through. Batman fights a variety of villains, and this leads to a slightly unbalanced feeling in a few parts. However, this does not last for long, and when the finale hits... It's most definitely a finale. The tone of the film is brilliant. Though it tends to be very dark, it is ultimately hopeful. Score two for realism. The acting is spot-on. Christian Bale absolutely nails the essence of Batman. Also, Cillian Murphy makes a fantastic Scarecrow. The music is simply incredible. Batman's theme, in particular, is an astounding work of art that, in a four-note motif, manages to capture all that Batman is.

All in all, I feel that this film, while not absolutely perfect, is an amazing accomplishment by Christopher Nolan that gives Batman fans the world over the movie they've been waiting for. I dare you to walk away from this movie and never utter the words "I'm Batman" in your lifetime. 4.5 out of 5 Tumblers from me.

9.title: The Batman franchise is Saved,
9.content:
Batman Begins is a fantastic movie with a very well developed storyline and a brilliant cast. Before this movie, fans started losing faith in Batman, after the disastrous Batman Forever with Val Kilmer, followed by another major disappointment, Batman & Robin, but Christopher Nolan saved this franchise, he made the universe much darker and more realistic, the villains are genuinely terrifying, even more so because they could actually be real, unlike villains such as Mr. Freeze or Poison Ivy. My only problem with this movie is that it struggles to find it's main villain, it focuses on Ra's Al Ghul at the beginning, then moves to the Scarecrow for a while, and then towards the end there's a lot of back and forth moving from one character to another, they are both great but I felt like the Scarecrow probably should have had less screen time as his story simply wasn't as important. It's makes a great decision by focusing on Batman and diving deep in to his origins, I didn't like how the Tim Burton films focused on the villains origins and barely showed how Bruce Wayne became the caped crusader, this film focuses on it immensely and that's really what we want to see. The start of a terrific trilogy that only improves, Batman Begins is a terrific movie that I would recommend to all fans of the franchise and to anyone looking for a good action or adventure film.

After a traumatic childhood and some intense training, Bruce Wayne is ready to fight crime on the dangerous streets of Gotham City as his alter ego, Batman.

9.title: Rethinking Comics on the Big Screen
9.content:
Tim Burton's successful films "Batman" and "Batman Returns", as well as their less notable sequels "Batman Forever" and "Batman and Robin" from Joel Schumacher set some tone for the narrative about probably the darkest widely known crime fighter in the DC universe. All the more vivid was the new reinterpretation of Batman under the leadership of Christopher Nolan. The director seems to have turned the world of comics upside down, demonstrating that fictional costumed heroes and villains can perfectly fit into the real human world.

"Batman: The Beginning" I have always somehow compared with the previous tetralogy. And Nolan's film, which originally existed in my understanding as a kind of prequel, was very different from these adaptations about the Gotham Knight. Nolan's world is a vibrant Gotham that existed in Bruce Wayne's youth, and then a metropolis mired in corruption and violence. Nolan perfectly demonstrates this change with light tones in flashback scenes, and also shows a dark and gloomy city at the time when an avenger in a bat mask appears in it.

We are shown the path of becoming the main character, who was well shown by Christian Bale. Before this, we had not seen a full-fledged origin in the cinema. Therefore, the origin of Batman turned out to be very important, both from the point of view of the plot and in general for understanding the complex character of Wayne on the screen as a whole.

The picture allows you to follow the formation of the hero through the demonstration of several significant figures from comics in this story at once. First of all, this is the butler of the Wayne couple, Alfred Pennyworth, who raised an orphan. Michael Caine is a great actor. All his roles are great, but the role of Alfred is special for me. He is a kind of father and senior companion for the main character, the kind of person who may be missed in his younger years by a seemingly grown-up guy. For paternal advice for a young man may well seem out of place, and an older authoritative friend who has been around all his life often does not happen in real life. And Alfred here acts as a kind of substitute for a parent and at the same time a wise adviser. Always witty and bright, but at the same time not oppressive and allowing Bruce to experience adult life himself.

Another important character is James Gordon, played by the equally iconic actor Gary Oldman. The transformation of the actor into a positive and strong hero turned out great. If earlier for me he personified the villains from the "Fifth Element" or "Leon", then here he is a completely different person. A guardian of the law, a loving family man, a just man. Oldman is a great actor and his role as Gordon here is also important in the formation of Bruce Wayne.

In the film, we are shown three villains from Batman comics at once. It was a bold move for its time, because, as a rule, the hero and the villain converge one on one. Nolan went further, showing the Scarecrow, Falcone, Ras al Ghul in the picture. Again, except for the saturation of the narrative and confrontations, I see such an introduction for Bruce Wayne to come to become Batman. After all, it was Carmine Falcone who opened the young man's eyes to what was happening in his hometown, forcing him to think about how Bruce could influence the situation, being the "prince of Gotham", a billionaire who simply lives his life aimlessly. The scarecrow becomes the personification of fear. Bruce decides that it is with the help of fear suggestion that he will fight criminals, thereby creating a kind of sword of Damocles - criminals will always be afraid to do something illegal, because Batman is somewhere, and he will definitely come for them. Well, Ras al Ghul, the man who taught Wayne, gave him knowledge about controlling himself and his fears. Batman takes something from everyone. And collectively becomes the one who will later be called a Legend.

Visual and audio rows are pleasing. The production is excellent, the battle scenes are beautiful, the music is beyond praise. Zimmer and Howard's soundtrack will definitely be remembered for their motives. The Oscar nomination for the best work of the operator is also an indicator of the quality of the project.

Christopher Nolan's work is definitely worth a look. This is the beginning of an excellent trilogy, a film with a lot of interesting ideas, visual and technical solutions, a film that sets a new fashion for superheroics.

9 out of 10.

9.title: Chris Nolan master piece.
9.content:
The first in a trilogy of near flawless comic book story telling for an intelligent adult audience, with depth, grit, excitement & cool, set to the dark world of Gotham & Bruce Wayne's tormented alter-ego.

I first saw Batman Begins upon its cinematic release in 2005, but didn't fully appreciate its brilliance until a revisit at home earlier this week. All the elements are there; Chris Nolan's skill at grown-up storytelling, a script (that whilst set in a world of the superhero), helps you buy into the main characters drive & fears, Christian Bales consummate portrayal of the dark knight & a veritable smörgåsbord of supporting cast cool in; Caine, Freeman, Hauer and Oldman.

Even if you're not a fan of the eponymous hero, there's enough here for the action, thriller or intelligent film goer to keep you hooked & coming back for more.

A good friend once told me he favoured Batman because he never loses, in this instance Nolan/ S. Goyer et al more than cement that legend.

Nine Stars.
