Most of the action sequences are less satisfying - too fast, too dark, too many cuts to fully follow who's doing what to whom. But the climactic battle is a marvel of big-budget, computer-generated mayhem. Overall, this film may be the best of the bunch; or maybe Ben Affleck's recent flop in "Daredevil" lowered the bar even further. Either way, the running time passed quickly, and the dangled sequel hook at the end looks tempting.

7.title: not bad
7.content:
I'm a bit mad at myself for not giving this movie a chance and going to see it at the movies. I'm sure it would look fantastic on the big screen.

The movie is detailed and it's attempt at complexity i'll accept. What i really liked was the humorous exchange between Michael Caine and Christian Bale. The special effects were interesting and at the end i almost felt more than a little bit of sympathy for Batman. Mind you, i already felt sorry for him because he probably got the least "powers" out of all the superheros. I'd be angry about that too.

The moral story is obvious. In the beginning scenes where he is trained by the "baddies" and when he refuses to kill the criminal we see that there is little difference in strength between bad and good, but instead that it is a choice to be bad or good. That even 'superheros' like Batman have to make that brave choice. There's the always told but true story of man as having the choice to be good or bad. As Batman says, he's in-between; the protector in that he can prevent us from choosing bad by not being seduced by it- by eradicating it first.

Gotham is reflective of our society today. Corrupt, immoral, unforgiving. The story of Batman within it, is what i liked about it. I've never really thought about the cartoon heroes at any deeper level than what they were: cartoon heroes. But corny as it may be, Batman Begins, allowed me to do so. For that reason, i give it a 7 1/2.

Christian Bale, i suppose is a good batman. Katie Holmes- the worst monotone speech i've ever heard when she gives the "Gotham as corrupt" commentary in the car ride with Bale- the one she ends with a slap in the face. Otherwise, she's fine. My favorite, was Michael Caine. It's the accent i tell you.

Not bad stuff! Moral of the story: even if a film looks like (insert word here) from the ads, give it a chance in the cinemas. You may regret it.

It is interesting to see Christian Bale's range of acting. I've seen him in an indie flick with Kate Beckinsale, Batman and recently The Machinist. While I am dying to give his lips a little restalyne injection, he is a solid actor who is interesting enough.

7.title: Holy Great Movie Batman!!
7.content:
Batman begins is story telling with pictures at its best. With an all-star cast (Bale, Oldman, Caine, Neeson and it girl Holmes) you can't lose. Rutger Hauer was a pleasant surprise. This is the best ensemble in the Batman movie lineup since Keaton / Nicholson and Kim Basinger ooh la-la.

Christian Bale always striving to give more than he's asked to his performance gives us his all once again. The first actor to wear the suit who didn't need all the padding to make himself seem physically up to the task. Bale is in mad shape which is such an essential oversight on the previous movies details. We know that the directors want us to feel Batman is a regular guy in a suit but come on! Mr. Mom had the eyebrows and dialog but he could have done a sit-up or two before shooting. Bruce Wayne's motives for becoming the caped crusader are clearly defined, his training period with Neeson are believable respectable and entertaining.

Gadget freaks will appreciate the details with regards to the BAT SUITs conception. There are so many films were you just want to get a good close look at some of the great contraptions but the directors give only fleeting glimpses to keep us interested. This movie very generously goes into the making of all the toys on the utility belt. BATMAN BEGINS's BatGeer are the best yet, and the BAT MOBILE is shown often in all its glory and is oh so cool.

I walked out of the theater at age 31 with my wife and just wanted to whisper in her ear "I'm BATMAN"

7.title: The start of a hero
7.content: Not bad a slow start to the film but does warm up after an hour with Gary Oldman as commissioner Gordon, and Michael Caine as Alfred an amazing combination. The start of one of the greatest superheroes ever with amazing fight scenes and featuring some of Batman's greatest villians such as the scarecrow an intense thrill ride from start to finish.

7.title: Good, but no cigar.
7.content:
It was an entertaining film but I thought it lacked a lot in some important departments. Before slating the weaker points, I must say I was impressed with C.Bale as Batman. I've seen his previous film, "The Machinist", and could not believe how he managed to fill the role of the caped crusader. Michael Caine was, as always, marvellous in a supporting role. A little too cockney for the role of Alfred, but that's just personal opinion. He really helped to hold this movie together along with Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox. Gary Oldman was wasted as Jim Gordon. Dear Mr.C. Nolan, Gary Oldman is best playing borderline psychopaths. A little bit like***Dr. Jonathan Crane***! Cillian Murphy, while pretty good in this role, just would not be able to hold a candle to G.Oldman !

The martial arts segments were not well choreographed. The camera work was too close to the participants in most of the fights and it looked messy. Mr.Nolan should have taken a look at some Bruce Lee films beforehand or perhaps the more recent "Ong-Bak".

The locations were not well thought out. Bruce Wayne's mansion was obviously shot somewhere in England(Marlborough House ?)when it was supposed to be on the outskirts of Gotham City. It didn't seem to fit with the story. Gotham City itself had no sense of size or structure. You see a couple of shots of the skyline but mostly it's all filmed in garbage strewn alley ways. The asylum was cool but not really used to full effect. It was the most menacing feature in the film.

Katie Holmes was dreadful. Not at all believable in her role as a District Attorney. She did not create the illusion of an intelligent, tough woman working in a corrupt city full of gangsters, thugs and other low-life's. Weird choice in an otherwise great cast list.

Much of the dialogue was po-faced rubbish. Especially the scenes between Christian Bale and Katie Holmes. Absolutely terrible.

Now, if Robert Rodriguez could be persuaded to do a "Sin City" on Batman, I think it would be getting closer to my ideal. Obviously without the language and gore, but the comic book feel of that was spot on.

7.title: Spoilers? Guano to Gold
7.content:
Okay, let me tell you. I've always preferred Spiderman to Batman. I don't know why. And when most of the first 45 minutes of this movie turned out to be dull stuff about Batman being a ninja and lots of boring blathering about Eastern philosophy complete with (poppy?) sniffing. C'mon. I don't care if it was in some mystical original version way back when (don't know) or not. I hope not. The execution of whatever idea they were trying to make was painfully bad. I came very close to turning it off (saw it on Cable...big screen TV, at least) with the phrase "guano" (as in "bat poop") coming to mind.

But then, once they got through that (except for another boring segment with the Kung-Fu/Jedimaster/wannabe badguy showing up again near the end), the rest of the movie was WAY COOL MAN. Grin. And may I say that I actually got spooked with the drug-induced vision of black-toothed Batman? I couldn't look at him straight on. Creeped me out! I think I need that delicious DA Dawes (in that silk blouse she wore braless at the end of the movie, please) to snuggle and comfort me. But I digress.

My point is that, especially after reading that the Batmobile is a real vehicle and that no special effects were used for it, this was the most palpably realistic version, complete with the brooding feeling that Bruce Wayne/Batman "ain't quite right" and could turn back to evil at any time, that grainy voice...It was all just very, very well done. It answers all of your questions about Batman, his genesis, his weapons, his vehicle, his motivations. All great stuff and very satisfying.

The first place in my superhero heart will always be Spidey (maybe it's because I prefer redheads and am still looking for my Mary Jane). But Batman gave him some serious competition in this movie. Be afraid, be very afraid. This guy can turn guano to gold.

7.title: it is a base of a masterpiece
7.content:
The movie started with Bruce at 8 years old exposed to his deepest fear, which is bats, then the sequence of movie continues with an enjoyable and interrelated scenes.

When Alfred ask Bruce, while he was preparing batman costume, "why bats ?", Bruce said "bats frighten me, it's time my enemies shared my dread". and these words indicate that Bruce face his deepest fear (bats) and now he is fearless.

it is a good movie, you should watch it before dark knight because there are some related scenes, which make Dark Knight more masterpiece than it is.

7.title: Batman begins for real this time
7.content:
I really enjoyed this film. I did not hold up high hopes for another 'Batman' film, and was really surprised.

I don't think this film should be viewed as part of the preexisting Batman franchise. In a way, it erases those films and starts all over again. Don't expect it to fit in with any prior films or the campy TV series.

This is a serious film, and is much more sophisticated than anything else with Batman in the title. There is a somewhat complex story, and it brings up serious issues to think about.

The movie starts off somewhat subdued as we learn the genesis of Batman. It flourishes into a full blown Hollywood action adventure, that maybe goes a bit over the top. Because of this, there is some lack of balance or coherency that bothered me a bit.

Still, this minor point can be overlooked as the film was thoroughly entertaining and engaging. Never a dull moment. The production values were top notch, as was the cast. Forget what you know about previous 'Batman' films and view this as a fresh start. Batman begins for real this time.

7.title: The Best Batman Movie
7.content:
Including the original, in which the Joker dominated the film, and Batman was relegated to a supporting role.

Batman Begins does what none of the other movies did; it gives us a living, breathing Bruce Wayne, the man who becomes Batman. It understands that the audience has to care about the person first before he does something bizarre like put on a silly costume, and still expect us to care about him.

In this film, Batman makes mistakes, almost gets himself fried through stupidity, and uses his brain to survive more than his gimmicks.

This is far from a perfect movie (I didn't find the Scarecrow villain particularly scary or intimidating; basically, if you wear a gas mask, he's harmless, and should have been no real threat to Batman). However, compared to the Batman travesties, particularly Batman Returns (Penguin riding a giant motorized rubber ducky), and Batman and Robin (every moment was incoherent and insulting), this deserves high marks, for simply making us even look at the character again half seriously.

The directing, the acting, and most importantly, the writing are all there. If you have written off the franchise because of the earlier films, check this one out, and watch it on the biggest plasma t.v. you can find. Visually, it is excellent, not a live-action cartoon. My only quibble is that it wraps up Bruce Wayne's war against his former allies, The League of Shadows, much too neatly and easily, particularly considering how unstoppable they have been before (and having them do rather stupid things with explosives that leads to their downfall). Other than that, it is an excellent picture that you can take seriously. That is, as seriously as you can take a character named "Batman".

7.title: Bale makes a good Batman, but he makes an even better Bruce Wayne
7.content:
Batman Begins is a great character story, and a great beginning to a new line of Batman features after the franchise had hit rock bottom with the awful Joel Schumacher disaster, Batman and Robin. The script is very tight, and creative while the characters three dimensional and uncharacteristically drawn out for a comic book adaptation. We learn a lot about Bruce Wayne and what drives the man into becoming the icon we all know and love. Christian Bale makes a good Batman, but he makes an even better Bruce Wayne in Batman Begins. It is an origin story after all and Bale delivers an excellent performance as do the supporting cast, bar one.

What I didn't like was Katie Holmes character - I thought she was definitely the weakest link of the story. The set design and look of the film didn't appeal to me at all either. After seeing Tim Burtons vision of Batman and having been a fan of the comics and character, there is no going back. I found the look to be too tamed and basic for Batman film which bothered me somewhat.

The story is what drives Batman Begins and thanks to a great script and character development it delivers - but I'd still rather watch Burton's original.

7.title: better than the other movies, but not as good as the cartoons
7.content: This show is probably the best out of all the batman movies ever made, but i found it somewhat lacking when i compared it to the animated series. The movie borders on the cheesy at times, with countless references to "your (wayne's) father" and what he would do in such and such situations. However, the arguments for justice from different views are strong, and each character talking about it, including the bad guys, do have a point and are right in certain ways-- which adds depth to the film. The cast is good, with solid performances that allow you to feel the anguish, bitterness or joy of each character, with Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, and Gary Oldman coming out the strongest in terms of portrayal of character. I personally thought that Cillian Murphy did a good job as the snide and cunning Dr Jonathan Crane cum Scarecrow. Overall, not a bad movie, but there is room for improvement.

7.title: The prequel to Tim Burton's Batman follows a young Bruce Wayne as he witnesses his parents' murder, joins a group of ninjas and dons the black cape to rid Gotham City of evil.
7.content: The original revealed Batman within minutes but in Begins it takes an entire hour for him to get all spruced up. However, that doesn't mean the first half isn't crammed full of action. After getting out of a Chinese prison, Bruce joins The League of Shadows in a bid to become strong and powerful enough to fight crime and save Gotham City. Michael Caine provides the film with most of its humour as Bruce's butler, Alfred. He is sarcastic, quick-witted and doesn't get nearly enough screen time. The same applies to Morgan Freeman's character, Lucius Fox, who works for Wayne Enterprises and helps out with Bruce's quest to kick the asses of evil mobsters (Tom Wilkinson with a very dodgy accent) and the scarecrow. Cillian Murphy is terrifying as the scarecrow with the mask on and off. It is during his scenes that I wonder why Batman Begins only received a 12A certificate. The hallucinations are truly scary and enough to give children nightmares for a week. Christian Bale kicks some serious ass as the caped crusader and the bat-mobile could give James Bond a run for his money. However, the biggest drawback is the Spider Man 2-style climactic ending which is nowhere near as good as the original. Batman Begins brings something new to the genre while still leaving more to be developed in future films. This is one for Batman fans everywhere.

7.title: Not bad
7.content:
The film is marvelous in vision. Gotham really pops as a real, grimy city. It's almost as if the writers wanted to see Batman in the real world where motivation is not cut and dried. In previous incarnations, emphasis was placed solely on Batman instead of Bruce Wayne. Here, Nolan rightfully explores this new Gotham through the eyes of Bruce. He, like us, is a newcomer to this rough grit.

Nolan really shines in terms of character which is brilliantly portrayed by the actors. It will be difficult to reassemble this cast for another film. Sadly, the action cuts are so fast that I really could not tell who threw what punch. Nolan is not an action-oriented director. I want to see Batman in full frame, stomping people flat.

Other worries were the tacked-on villain aspect. Was it really necessary to have the Scarecrow? Aside from appeasing those who read the comics, Scarecrow (brilliantly played by Murphy) did nothing in terms of structure. All of his screen time would be better invested in Ra's Al Ghul. This fellow is THE Moriarty of Batman. By the end, I had little interest in Ghul as an individual. He came across as iconic in that he was just a really smart bad guy. Batman is too good to simply beat up bad guys. This is the Cadillac of super heroes. A wealth of potential exists within the comics (Bride/Son of the Demon anyone?). Part of what makes Batman so appealing is the whole duality between him and the villain. How are they alike and where do they differ? More than one villain merely detracts from any connection I had with the characters as people, rather than icons.

I smell a sequel. STOP READING if you do not want to know A SERIOUS SPOILER....

I have serious fears as to how the sequel will deal with Joker. This is a character with such an amount of weight that he stands on equal ground with Batman (largely due to Jack Nicholson's stint). The rules of this new franchise must be followed. Gotham is a very scary place. I do not think that "the clown prince of crime" sort of Joker will be acceptable. Nor do I think that a likable Nicholson Joker will pass either. This Joker will have to be sickly perverted. I do not want to laugh with this Joker. He must be dark, nebulous, and sick.

Tremendous kudos to the cast and Nolan. I loved every set, costume, angle, etc. The cutting was too quick and the villains were shallow.

7.title: Nolan's underrated film
7.content:
I'll be honest, I didn't really like this movie when I first saw it because I was just a kid who cares about action over story.

In my teens, I decided to give Batman Begins another chance and I actually pretty much enjoyed it. This seems like a new origin story for our familiar hero, and I like how this film make it feel a bit modern and real. The cinematography is wonderfully shot, the story is a great new take to Batman, and although the action scenes seem cool the fight choregraph was hard to watch. Nolan has never been much of an action director but his does improve in later films.

This movie doesn't really get talk much because of Christopher Nolan's other phenomenal Batman movies and other films. Overall, it's a pretty good watch and a new "serious" take on the caped crusader.

7.title: City Freaks Origins: The Batman
7.content:
Bruce Wayne's parents are billionaires. One night, somebody kills them both in front of him. The killer does get caught soon enough. Life goes on. Bruce grows up and learns just how strong the crime world is in his city. He leaves and explores the surrounding world under the radar, he learns life is even less black and white than he thought, basically becomes a criminal himself and ends up in prison.

It turns out there is an ancient secret organization named "The League Of Shadows" going age after age destroying cities when they're so corrupt saving them is impossible. They get him out of prison and try to make him one of them. But once he learns they're about to go to his city to destroy it, he leaves them. Not without a conflict.

He returns home and creates an armored masked suit with wings that can, indeed, fly, and his goal is to physically fight and terrify criminals. So he does. And since he was born and spent quite a few years here, he won't really be alone on his secret mission.

Things don't go too bad but "The League Of Shadows" secretly arrives, and they have a way to drown the whole city in chaos and leave no survivors, destroy everything. They can do so thanks to a military device they have stolen from Bruce Wayne's corporation. Luckily, though, there are not many of these invaders, and The Bat Man takes them down using his scientific resources and allies.

When the secret organization meant to have been destroying huge corrupt cities throughout human history is on screen, there aren't many of them to see. One can assume they're just the tip of the iceberg but nothing seems to back that assumption up. The movie should have explored "The League Of Shadows" more. And one detail, in particular, would have amplified things in a major way.

Has Gotham City been their target for a while now? Or did Gotham City just become their target at this specific time and because of Bruce Wayne, a billionaire from that city, almost becoming one of them? If they have been planning this for a while and would have embarked on this mission with or without Bruce Wayne losing his way in life and ending up in their secret camp, then his whole interaction with them only makes him stronger and more experienced. But if him running away from home and ending up in their secret camp is what triggers them, then he is to blame for their attack.

Come to think it! Bruce Wayne becoming The Bat Man to fight crime and defend his city could have also functioned as a danger magnet. In other words, The Bat Man is here to do good by fighting the bad, but if he's responsible for a huge terrorist attack on the whole city, that makes things even more interesting. The way things are in the movie, The Bat Man is an outlaw, but he fights for the good. He's only bad on paper. But if he ends up being the reason for the worst crisis this city has ever gone through, the whole "life isn't just black and white" could have been even more serious.

7.title: Expected More...
7.content:
With all the hype, i expected so much more from this movie, i bought it on it's theatrical release, and didn't goto the cinema to watch it. But i was reasonably disappointed with it.

I expected a lot more action than we got, the main action isn't close combat fighting or anything, but big bad explosions with fire and clever cgi effects. Personally i think the original Batman, and Batman Returns are better! Cheesier but good. And Jack Nicolson in the first is awesome. But don't get me wrong this isn't a bad film, it's pleasant, but expected more from all the hype! Morgan Freeman is good in his little parts, and Michael Caine is amusing with some 1 liners, and also Christian Bale is no doubt the better Batman, he's quick, agile, and looks convincing! he puts everything into his parts. There is a story line to follow with this one, the movie mainly focuses on the Beginning of Batman, Like you'd expect with the Title, Begins. But needed more action to keep us bat lovers awake if you will, but still I'm curious to see the sequel, & if that brings us more Action! and Hopefully we get Catwoman, or Robin!

My opinion i rather the original!

7.title: One of the best origins
7.content: This is easily one of the best superhero origin stories and one of the best superhero movies in general. I actually prefer this to the year one comic origin, the fact they showcase some of batmans actual training and travels and give a tease on just how long and hard it was is really cool. The way all the pieces of this story fit together is also very well done and really makes a complete arc. Something not many people talk about with this movie, is that it doesn't play itself too seriously, characters will make jokes in a very realistic way that doesn't feel cheesy but instead natural and allows the movie to be much more enjoyable. All that being said I do have a couple issues with this film, my biggest is the action, the first action scene is really entertaining but after that I feel the movie relys way too much on jump cuts, causing very messy and confusing fight scenes where you can't really see what is happening. Like most origin stories, I did personally find that it did drag a little, considering the movie spends nearly half its runtime before he gets the suit it surprisingly doesn't drag as much as you'd think, but around the 40 minute mark I did find it dragging. Funnily enough though I'd actually say the Bruce Wayne side of this film is the most entertaining, Batman is amazing in this film don't get me wrong, but the bruce Wayne scenes actually might be more interesting. Another issue I have with this movie is scarecrow, I think he serves the plot perfectly but it does feel a little disappointing at just how underused he is. If I was to nitpick I also think Christian bales deep voice comes off a bit too goofy at times, this might just be from the memes but he deepens his voice so much at times that it almost feels like a parody, for the most part this isn't too distracting though, and I think a fair amount of the scenes that are, were meant to be comedic anyway. My final gripe with this film, is the ending fight does feel a little contradictive, it's not too big of a deal but I feel it was an incredibly weird choice for the film and it does slightly hurt the character arc and plot. Overall this is a great origin story that really understands exactly what Bruce Wayne is as a character, it has a fair amount of issues, but they all feel minor when the story is articulated so well.

7.title: batman begins here...
7.content: Batman begins: slowly but it does pick up. There is so much batman out there from the comics to the cartoons and from Burton to where we are now, Christopher Nolan (of memento fame). We are promised a much darker batman far removed from the silly campness of the last few films that have graced our screens and yes this is a darker film but not that dark. It still has the unfunny one-liners like the kind we used to get in old Arnie films from the eighties (Remember 'stick around') and it still has the sickly sweet love interest in the form of Katie 'am I only getting work because I'm seeing tom cruise' Holmes. Aside from her terrible performance and Christian bales need to suddenly put on a pantomime baddie voice every time he dons the bat costume, there is some good acting here. Michael Cane especially as Alfred the smart English butler and Morgan freeman as the weapons expert both take to the roles like ducks to water. Gary Oldman regardless of dodgy tash also adds to the ambiance. The enemies are also quite weak but lets wait until batman 2 with the joker to comment on them. But I have to say the cars the star. The new half tank, half all terrain vehicle that is the new bat mobile is brilliant and steals the show in some awesome jumps and chases that feature as some of the better set pieces in the film. Nolan is no action director and this shows slightly towards the end where as Rami in Spiderman 2 kept the action fast but clear, here it becomes muddled and sloppy. Don't get me wrong this is a far better film than say star wars (got my dig in) but not as stylish as Sin City. If you like super hero action films that you don't really have to think about and you can't wait for Spiderman or x-men 3 then this is the film for you.

7.title: I admit it was good.
7.content:
When I first saw it, I thought it was awful. Watched it again, and immediately changed my mind about how I felt towards it a second time. Maybe cause I kept hating how this movie had a long prologue to Batman. But since I'm only half batman fan I had different thought on how a Batman film should be presented.

To those who probably already knew as a fact, that this movie has no relation with the previous 4 Batman films. This in fact is an entirely new vision on the franchise after the huge criticisms on "Batman & Robin" 11 1/2 years ago. Course back then Warner Bros. tried to make the franchise suit-able towards the kid audience by lightening up the theme. Big mistake, and they learn their own lesson on that and made sure they wouldn't waist millions on another Batman film again.

So this time they're starting from scratch with a completely fresh new beginning that's suppose to give the franchise a better name in cinema. They succeeded with this being the best Batman film in a long time. I admit it's good for being a revision on the series. But I don't have the heart to call the greatest comic book movie in the world.

In this film it tells how Bruce Wayne became the Dark Knight and how he learned to do martial arts in which it becomes handy later on. He learns the meaning of moral justice as a way to bring down criminals as he tries to become someone in which everyone would look up to for hope. Hope in which to bring down the criminal master minds in Gothan City where gangs and mobs run the streets. Only someone like Batman can clean up the streets, only to face another criminal mind who's about to spread fear in the city.

If you are a fan of the series, then there's no problem in worrying about the out come of this film. Cause I'm sure all fans of the franchise will be more satisfied with over "Batman and Robin" or "Catwoman".

7.title: The Best Origin Story
7.content: Batman Begins is an epic and satisfying origin story for one of the most iconic superheroes while relying more on character development, story progression and philosophical themes to provide a rich canvas on which to write its epic action and comic book plot threads.

7.title: Batman- performed as a junior high school production.
7.content:
Casting issues: I just couldn't get over how Rachel and the Scarecrow/Dr. Crane both looked like they were twelve. I realize this is supposed to be Batman "the early years" but it was hard to take them seriously in their professions. (plus of course I'm not impressed by Katie's "acting" so that didn't help). And I love Michael Caine, but where's the old Alfred?? Christian Bale was OK, better than Michael Keaton's neurotic dweeb but not as good (IMO) as Val Kilmer.

It was an OK prequel, though certainly not deserving of being in IMDb's top 250. It did a fairly good job of sticking to the storyline and not contradicting earlier versions.

It had all the standard ingredients. It tried to bring in the deeper philosophical underpinnings of Batman's character. The usual flashbacks to his parents death. There was a simplistic "Nepal=enlightenment" sort of stereotype thing going on. There were ninjas (everyone loves ninjas right?) It also tried to make Batman more of a fighter than someone relying on toys/gadgets so we got some good fights scenes (more inspiration from the growing interest in Hong Kong action films). There was the generic childhood friend/love. The plot was basic destroy city stuff. There were the generic throw-away one-liners ("nice car"/"nice coat").

The mise-en-scene was pretty good, too much CG for my taste - but since when did Gotham resemble Chicago? I always thought it was a stand in for NYC? And why does Batman live in a mansion in the English countryside? These were kind of jarring moments that broke the spell of suspended disbelief for me.

Basically it was a crowd pleaser with nothing too original. You can figure out the plot miles ahead, but doesn't mean it's not an enjoyable ride to the end. I think I still prefer the more stylized Tim Burton movies though (exc. Keaton who's miscast) - but this was a worthy successor.

The part I probalby liked best was the Conservative (punishing people and/or profiting off crime) vs. Liberal (address the root cause of crime, understand things in context, try to help people)arguments that crop up periodically through the film. Particularly I felt they made a good distinction between justice and revenge and showing Wayne's having to choose between the two.

7.title: An intelligent block buster
7.content:
First of all an admission - I was never really a big lover of the Batman franchise. The movies reminded me somewhat of Sin City in that they looked good, but there wasn't much substance.

I was therefore pleasantly surprised by the new movie. Christian Bale always seemed like a good casting for Batman and so it proves. The first two thirds of the film really delves deep into the character of Bruce Wayne and how he becomes Batman. It is a rare thing to see a blockbuster paying attention to the script, but that is exactly what happens here. I don't think this is really suitable for young children or adrenalin junkies, but it's great fayre for those of us who like to become involved in a character.

The final third of the film is where the special effects kick in, but courtesy of the first part of the film you really do care what happens to the characters. Good movie.

7.title: A good start
7.content:
Going into Christopher Nolan's latest film "Batman Begins", I asserted that my favorite Batman film thus far was Tim Burton's original "Batman", featuring Michael Keaton and Jack Nicholson. After walking out of "Batman Begins", my opinion did not change, but I was left with a lot of hope for this franchise.

"Batman Begins" basically takes the story of Bruce Wayne (Bale) and starts from scratch; pretending that the other Batman films didn't exist (which, after seeing the third film, is probably a wise thing to convince yourself of). Taking cues from the original Bob Kane story, our new Batman still has some of the same background as the Burton/Schumacher offerings, (the essentials, like how Wayne's parents die, etc.) but we now have a truly dark knight. The guilt with which Wayne is wracked regarding his parents' death is so pervasive that he puts himself through grueling and potentially life-threatening events. While in an Asian prison, he meets Ducard (Neeson) who works for Ra's Al Ghul (Watanabe). Ducard convinces him to join their cult, which teaches him the way of the ninja, only their motives and honor are questionable. Returning to Gotham City, Wayne begins to seek his revenge on the mob boss who runs the city, and was behind the killing of his parents. While doing this, he discovers that there is another dangerous villain, Dr. Jonathan "Scarecrow" Crane, who drugs his patients and eventually, his enemies, with a hallucinogen that turns them psychotic. Helping Wayne are his trusty friend and butler Alfred (Caine) and Lucius Fox (Freeman), a former employee of his father who creates Wayne's weapons and gear. Since there inherently has to be a love interest, Wayne's childhood friend Rachel Dawes (Holmes) acts as both the object of his affection and a source of grounding.

It was unfortunate that I went into this film having read a lot of reviews, something I generally don't do, because pretty much every review I read or heard was a rave, and called it the best Batman film ever made, and even one of the greatest movies of all time, period. Therefore, I had high expectations going into this film, but came out of it feeling slightly under whelmed. I think I was expecting to do what I did after seeing "Kill Bill" on opening night, and was jumping around, I couldn't contain my delight over the film, whereas I walked out of this one and said, "It was a good movie, but I still liked the first Tim Burton film better." Perhaps it's bad taste or something on my part, but I really liked the art deco and Gothic setting of that film, but more importantly, I relished the character of The Joker. I have always been one to root for the villain (a recent example of my hero worship of the bad guy is my assertion that the coolest character in Robert Rodriguez's "Sin City" was Kevin, a guy who had maybe five minutes of screen time) and Ra's Al Ghul and particularly Scarecrow just didn't do it for me. Cillian Murphy is a great actor, and it was fun to see him chewing up scenery after having only witnessed him in "28 Days Later", but overall I was pretty disappointed in the villains of this film.

Having said that, I think that the character development of Bruce Wayne and his cohorts was definitely superb. By now, it's cliché to say that this was the vision that Bob Kane had of the character of Batman, but it really is appropriate to reassert this. I was a casual reader of the comic as a child and in my teens, so while I really like Burton's style, I can really appreciate Nolan's creation and Bale's depiction. Christian Bale is the best Batman we've had so far, hands-down (sorry Adam West). He brought believability to the tortured and conflicted Wayne, as well as a sense that this could be a real guy. There was nothing cartoonish about his performance; rather at times I was reminded of an earlier role of his, Patrick Bateman of "American Psycho" in his understated ness in certain situations. Rachel Dawes notwithstanding (sorry, Katie Holmes may be cute and all I guess, but she can't act her way out of a paper bag) Nolan creates an excellent supporting cast of characters that will serve the franchise well, including Gary Oldman as a not-yet Commissioner Jim Gordon. Caine and Freeman are both as good as they usually are, and it is great that they are lending their talents and some class to the series.

Understanding that one of the main themes of the film was to create groundwork for future endeavors, "Batman Begins" is a very good film. If you look at it from the perspective of a stand-alone film, it could be lacking some key elements (like the aforementioned villain thing). Then again, I could just be completely picky and I rely too much on certain things to make a film fantastic. I just know that if there were a bit more dynamism in our bad guys I probably would have given the film an additional point on the ratings scale. But in bottom-lining the film, it really is a good movie and it makes me look forward to the next installment, which means that the film did for me exactly what it probably intended. 7/10 --Shelly

7.title: You'll become something else entirely
7.content: After the childish disaster that was Joel Schumacher's Batman&Robin(1997), it seemed that Batman was dead and buried but in 2008 Director Christopher Nolan would revive the cape crusader not only exploring deeper into the origin of the character but bringing them into the real world perspective with Batman Begins. While The dark knight was the film that got people to take comic movies seriously again. Batman Begins served as the stepping stone. While in many ways The movie shows the possible steps it would take to be a superhero. The first half of the movie spends the whole first hour on how Bruce becomes the Batman, and in any way, it's handled well by talking about the deception of becoming one with shadows. In The fear of criminals and what you've done, I understand. The journey does real from the training to making the suit and weapons. So by the time he becomes Batman, it feels like a different movie has started. The cast all do a good job although some seem questionable. Christian Bale's evolution in the movie is good yet it seems off. Bruce Wayne, you buy the playboy persona enough yet he seems like somebody who's hiding something. He is not secretive and subtle Lucius Fox pretty much finds out immediately what he's doing. The movie is supposed to be taking more of a Year one approach to it where he's not as refined yet, but it never really changes that when it comes to the live-action depiction of Bales, not the smartest Batman. He looks cool and a lot of the scenes of them disappearing and posing are cool. Although the costume here is rather bulky. He does have an opposing status to him that is until he speaks his voice cannot be entirely put on Christian himself Nolan himself should've known better that I haven't had him do his voice was not a good idea. When you speak softly it's fine Brooding similar to Keaton it sounds ominous, but when you have the screaming and shouting his lines "swear to me!" It does make seem like he's trying to sound scary as impose to appear scary. Michael Caine as Alfred with words of wisdom at the same time guiding Bruce to uphold his family's name. Gary Oldman as Gordon again is very reminiscent of the year one. He's not corrupt like the others yet he wants to make a difference, but it Has to be Batman to make that push. Rachel overall isn't that interesting she's meant to serve as a reason for Bruce to care and help define him to not go down a dark path. Having Bruce act like an idiot in front of her doesn't make their relationship any more interesting. Villains are not executed as they probably could've been. Ras al Ghul which I have to admit honestly was an interesting approach with the league of shadows. Given that this is a villain waiting for the time was not one that a lot of general people knew about. It does seem like his plan is rather convoluted you can't get into the more mystic side of the character given the more realistic tone of the movie. The second is Cillian Murphy as the scarecrow. Who honestly Should've been the main villain of the movie. However, He has a couple of scenes it doesn't take advantage of the full potential of this character. Especially having Bruce trying to instill fear in the criminal of Gotham. You have a villain that is obsessively centered around fear would've been an interesting concept to use as well. The use of CG could've done a lot of creative nightmares visuals with this character. The actions are alright even though the Tumblr is unnecessary, does Batman need something this excessive for everyday crime-fighting. The chase through is still nice as well as the finale with the train but the biggest problem with the movie is the fight scenes. Everything's shoot so closes up and fast that you can barely it out. Batman begins while having problems with its flaws. It did help usher superheroes back into the limelight and managed to take a character and flesh them out. How he evolves into us from a man to a symbol serves as a good start to this trilogy.

7.title: Sadly, a disappointment
7.content: Don't you just hate it when you're watching a movie and you get to a point, maybe about halfway or two-thirds through, when you think to yourself, "Ah, f--- it, it's not going to get any better, is it?" So it was, alas, with Batman Begins. It's not a bad movie - far from it. If anything, the movie failed for me because it probably has too much ambition. The "Ah, f--- it" moment for me was the car chase, and herein lies the problem of any Batman movie. You have to have a Batmobile. And so you have to have a car chase. This is all well and good if you can produce a really good car chase, but apart from the neat idea of starting it on the rooftops, this one isn't much good. The other thing going through my mind at this point was something like, "Now, did that car really have to flip over like that?" Alfred the butler shared my displeasure, at least. Then of course there's the whole seeing-his-parents-being-murdered thing. I accept that a reasonable chunk of the audience won't know this already. But there comes a point where you have to say, "OK! We know! Now get on with it!" There are so many little flashbacks here it's like being bludgeoned with the complete works of Sigmund Freud. But I'm conflicted - there's plenty of good stuff here too (the prototype batsignal being my favorite). Problem is, there's too MUCH stuff. There's probably enough material here for about 4 or 5 hours worth of movie without adding any extra plotting. Rutger Hauer, Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine - these are actors who could easily carry very long scenes with actual character development, but we seem to be served the minimum possible to hold the complicated plot together. Actually the plot's not complicated, it just seems that way. I have a sneaking suspicion that Christopher Nolan (whose work until now I've loved) was trying, underneath the superhero hype, to make something reminiscent of the classic seventies New York crime movies, like French Connection or Serpico. Unfortunately, he has to spend too much time on explosions and exposition. So we're deprived of more Batman (why do the movies concentrate on Bruce Wayne? Read the title, guys), more Gordon, or more Scarecrow (acting honors ultimately go to Gary Oldman's understated cop and Cillian Murphy's inordinately creepy Crane). By the time we got to the monorail bit I had lost most of my interest, although Bale and Oldman saved it in the dying seconds. I suppose I should be grateful that a summer blockbuster should aim so high, but if you'd told me 6 months ago that Batman Begins would have been nowhere near as enjoyable as Star Wars 3, I'd have thought you were insane. Perhaps the sequel will be everything I want.

7.title: The origins of the legendary Batman, on how he became Batman, and why
7.content: I thought it was amazing. Unlike the other films, it goes right into depth on how he became Batman, and this film has more of a modernisation story line from the other ones, where it was quite imaginative. In the other films, they show only flashbacks on how Bruce's parents get killed. Also I thought Liam Neeson's performance was really very good. I loved all the dialogue, as it was kept entertaining and the action was amazing! I absolutely loved the music, it was really dramatic and exhilarating from start to finish, and it was very different from the other films, shown from a different angle. I also thought Christian Bale in it, and I loved all the scenes with Bruce and Rachel. They were so sad some of them!

7.title: It's okay
7.content:
Cillian Murphy is hot, but he didn't have enough screen time. I think the movie focused too heavily on Bruce's backstory rather than Scarecrow's motives. Idk, it felt too slow in the beginning but too rushed at the end.

However.

Cillian Murphy makes a great villain. It's absolutely criminal that he didn't get as much time on screen as FALCONE. Dude, Falcone wasn't even that important compared to Dr. Crane. Consider this a prejudice. Honestly, the villain that's actually doing the work should be mentioned more than some guy in Arkham that doesn't get mentioned after he gets detained.

To sum it up: Good movie, Scarecrow is hot, kinda wish Cillian Murphy had more screen time, Christian Bale's Batman voice is weird.

:)

7.title: the real batman
7.content: "im just a fan" We have never see the story of batman at this deep nolan give the story another face i never expect that the story of batman like this and at that way the movie was amazing he give you the fellings like you watch a drama movie but its a superhero movie.

7.title: The beginning of a great movie trilogy
7.content:
This is where it beginns. For me this the best comic book movie trilogy there is until today, which happens to also includes one of my all time favourite movies: "The Dark Knight". I am a huge Batman fan, I love reading Batman comics and I absolutely adore Christopher Nolan, so back then this was a must watch for me.

But first of all I must sadly say, that this is the weakest of the three movies out of this trilogy and even the weakest movie of Nolan and there is one simple reason for it. The treatment of Ras al Ghul, one of my favourite Batman antagonist, maybe even my second favourite next to the joker. All in all it is a good movie and it delivers a decent story to start this trilogy. We see the beginning of Bruce Wayne and what influences him in his core, his transformation into Batman, how he starts fighting for Gotham and how struggles in the beginning. There are definitly thrilling moments in this film, wenn get action and there are some twists in it. The directing, cinematography and the score are of course really good, like always in a Nolan movie. The Acting is on point and Bale is amazing, same as Caine.

So this is definitly a fun movie to watch, hell you should watch the entire trilogy.

But I myslelf can not get around the fact of how poorly they used and portrait Ras Al Ghul. This could have been an incredible movie, where we have two amazing fighters facing each other while there are mysterious plots playing out in the backround. I think there was so much missed potential and there where so many great things Nolan could have done with him in this movie, but instead he was just used like garbage in my opinion.

Still this is a great movie with big moments, that everybody should check out.

7.title: Not up to the other instalments quality [7.0/10]
7.content:
Going in from the other two movies excitement for me was high to watch Batman Begins, but ultimately I exited disappointed. Not too much to say because just so much of this movie can be described as just "passible". The score was kinda bland, the story was only moderately interesting. The characters were mixed.

The villains in this movie were really bad, which shocked me because Joker and Bane in the other movies were so outstanding. The motivations are self conflicting in the case of the LOS and for Crane he just barely has presence in the film.

Oh and that cinematography... just unforgivably bad. Like who thought this was a good idea? The whole final act is just a disgusting brown tint/lighting on each shot that makes each scene look so... bad. The fight choreography here is some of the worst I've ever seen with there being 4-6 shots per second at its worst.

I understand that my review makes it seem like I hate this film, I don't. I just don't "like" it per se. If you enjoyed Dark Knight, than you will still get a thrill out of this film, but it's not the same quality whatsoever if you ask me.

7.title: The beginning of the dark knight
7.content:
What a great day I had when I finally watched batman begins, I woke up around 8:00AM and was excited to watch this film. I heard great things about this movie, and it did not fail to disappoint. I love the look of this film, how it has that realistic take, and that is just the thing with some of Nolan's other films that i've seen (Dark knight and Inception). I know from the previous batman films that there is always a selected villain for the film, and they misused almost all of them especially in batman & Robin, but the did something right in this film, they didn't focus on the bad the whole time. The movie is called Batman begins, so it is suppose to be about batman and how he came to be. Ra's al gaul is a big villain from the comics i know, but what i loved was the scarecrow, because the whole theme of this movie is revolving around fear. "Face your fear, conquer your fear, become your fear". All this talk about fear, and for it to be an actual plot device is simply brilliant ( but in a way obvious if someone asked).

Something that bothers me is the way the fake Ra's al gaul looks, he has the white hairs on his chin like in the comic, and I thought when he died in the fight he'd just be revived again and fight batman in the end, I thought they were about to do it, but no, it turns out that Ra's al gaul is actually the guy who trained Bruce. It makes sense in a way, because the man who were suppose to believe is Ra's doesn't seem all that intimidating.

Back to the look, I love how the bat suit looks in this, and I like the tumbler. The bat-mobile was cool, but this was better. Looking back on the bat-mobile, it looks cheesy and I'm suppose to believe that it can do anything, but with the tumbler, I can believe it can drive through concrete, I can believe it can shoot missiles (they even call it out as a tank), I'm still a little puzzled on the jumping roof part, but it looks good.

Ending statement: I think this is a great way to revive the franchise, especially from thr wreckage Batman&Robin left, and I think that this would be a great movie for anyone to watch.

7.title: Well done Mr. Nolan!
7.content: I really liked this movie - gave it a 7. The only thing that kept me from giving it an 8 or 9 were the fight scenes. I found it hard to follow the action during those scenes, but I'm fully aware that Nolan designed it that way. I mean, I can just see someone saying "dude, these fights are taking place at night, in the dark, with a guy dressed entirely in black - of course it's gonna be hard to follow". I realized this, but when you look at The Matrix, it's easy to see that a fight in the dark where the actors are dressed in black can be done, and done well. I love everything about the movie except that. Also, I think Nolan isn't done with this genre - he's gonna keep getting better at this sort of thing. One of the things I think is so cool about Nolan is the fact that he brings so much to the table in terms of shooting style, depth, and dynamics. I have to keep reminding myself that this is the same guy that directed Memento - a fantastic film, but nothing like Batman Begins. I applaud Nolan for this movie, but I have to say that I'm really excited about his next project. No matter what the title or subject matter, I'll go see it!

7.title: Movie Review Profits
7.content: Play Batman Begins! It is fast and easy to view! A good way to spend your time. Be the best!

7.title: A good way to reboot a dead movie franchise!
7.content:
With the old batman movies, that were created by Tim Burton, long dead. A reboot came around the corner with this one, directed by one of the great British Directors, Christopher Nolan. This is probably one of the best superhero Origins movies out-there along-side the first Spider-man, it makes the character of Batman dark again, and did a good job with the story of the film.

The story is that Bruce Wayne (Played by Christian Bale), who's parents were shot and killed as a child, left Gotham for over 7 years since the beginning of his adulthood, he made it his way to the other side of the world, where he eventually met-up with Henri Ducard (Ra's Al Ghoul) (Played by Liam Neeson) to goes into the "League of Shadows", an martial arts Terrorist organization. After finishing his training, Wayne soon goes against the League and once he thought he wipe them out, he moved back to Gotham, to not just to continued his parents' successful wealth as Billionaires and Enterprises' owners, but to use his martial arts to go against the criminals of the city, as he blame all of them for killing his parents, as they were murdered by a Crook. He made his career of becoming the vigilante, Batman. As he getting into more of his crime-fighting, it turned-out that the League of Shadows are in Gotham City, alongside a associate, Scarecrow, hoping to bring it to an end, in which have to prevent it from happening.

The characters of this movie are great, Christopher Nolan is good as Bruce Wayne, with good emotions and powerful acting, but as Batman, some issues, most notably his growling voice, like okay I know Batman is supposed to be Batman, but this is unnecessary to hear. The costume is actually neat-looking so, most likely my favorite character. Good-old Liam Neeson played as this film who it turned-out to be Ra'Al Ghoul, the main villain of the film, he did a good job here playing such a fantastic villainous personality. The secondary Villain of the film, Scarecrow, I thought was awesome in this movie, especially when he first uses his fear Toxins to that Mob guy, it was quite horrifying, and they did an brilliant job. The only problem of the character so, is that he was quite somewhat of a minor Character, he had a few memorable scenes, like his encounters with Batman was enjoyable to watch, but it was all disappointing in the end with him joining with Ghoul's chaos in Gotham City, where he was only engaging for about 5 minutes and then was stopped not by Batman, but his love interest, Rachel. Both Alfred and Commissioner Golden was both well replaced by Michael Caine and Gary Oldman, both did well with who's there playing, especially with how they made Golden in this film, finally having him have a character in him, like seeing him in Action, showing Emotions, not at all a fat emotionless who can't even defend himself in any of the original films.

With this movie being quite powerful as its carried a realistic world, which I grew to like, with it being about Fear, and having a realistic serious issue like Terrorism as related to that topic, just genius. I like the whole martial arts theme of this film, it real nice tributed to movies that mainly centering around that sort-of topic. Despite this however, there are problems I have with this movie. Such as going back to the Growling voice of Bale's Batman and the showing of the Scarecrow's character of the film, as well others like the action scenes which are unenjoyable to watch as we can't even see what is going on. Overall, this movie ain't too bad despite these major problems I already. It was a good reboot to the series, and the start of one of my favorite Movie Series, the "Dark Knight Trilogy", I absolutely recommend it, if you haven't seen this one which is possible.

7.title: Batman's Saviour
7.content: After George Clooney stabbed Batman in the heart and watched him die, Christian Bale breathed life back into the suit and once more created the 'Dark Knight', something which hadn't been achieved since the glory days of Michael Keaton and Tim Burton. As is the seeming trend at the moment, 'Begins' is a prequel to the 1989 'Batman'. However, the keen observer may notice a few adjustments/errors in the storyline.The first being that 'Batman Begins' actually follows the comic book storyline regarding Bruce's parents. In the original story, Joe Chill murdered the Waynes, whilst Tim Burton changed this so that it was Jack Napier (who later on became The Joker) who shot them both, thus creating a relationship between Batman and The Joker. 'I made you you made me, how childish!'- The Joker Also, what's with Sergeant Gordon (who I am assuming later makes it to Commissioner)meeting Batman and being on his side? It was only at the very end of 'Batman' that he finally realised Batman was a crime fighter, not a criminal. At the end of the film, the next villain is introduced; 'He leaves a calling card', which was a joker from a pack of cards. Now then, all credit to the writers for trying to create a definite link to the 'next' movie, but at the beginning of 'Batman' The Joker is not a super villain, nor is he even The Joker. He is Jack Napier, a gang member working for a gangland boss, 'Grissom'. It is only when Grissom sets Jack up, Batman tries to save him but drops him in a vat of chemicals, and his plastic surgery goes horribly wrong (using the tools from 'Little shop of Horrors) that he finally snaps and takes over the mafia gang as the new super villain, The Joker. This last point persuaded me that it was meant as a definite prequel to the 1989 work of genius and therefore I am hoping that the errors were, for some reason, intentional. The thing that makes Batman the greatest superhero ever is the fact that he has no actual super powers and one great bit of story-writing is actually explaining where Batman gets 'those wonderful toys' which enable him to fight crime the way he does, without having been bitten by a spider or sent to Earth because his planet is about to explode. Having been designed for the US Army, the suit, car and weapons were far too expensive to mass-produce and so the entire operation was dropped. The suit was bullet/knife-proof Kevlar body armour, which Bruce personalised and turned into the Batsuit. Batman also never uses a gun, preferring such elements as hand-to-hand combat, 'Baterangs' and gas powered mobile zip-lines. Again, the film shows that all of these were created with the intention of being used in urban warfare, making them fit perfectly into Batman's arsenal. The new Batmobile is a fantastically fresh look at Batman's famous run-around. As one police officer states, 'It's a black...tank.'The Batmobile was actually MADE. The car did everything in real life that it does in the film. It drives, it jumps, it weighs two tons and it will be on Ebay within a week. Having said that, I still personally prefer the sleek stealthy Batmobile circa Michael Keaton, 1989-1992. For someone who has trained as a ninja in the art of stealth, a huge tank with lights everywhere that charges through the streets destroying everything in it's path is not the best mode of transport. But I suppose Mr Wayne had to make do with what he had. Finally, congratulations are in order for Christian Bale, the man wisely chosen by Christopher Nolan to play Batman. Despite the almost cheesy gruff voice, Bale brings a sense of foreboding, and rebuilds the Dark Knight after being left behind in the trail of camp destruction that was George Clooney. In all a great film, but still not beating the majesty that was 'Batman'.

7.title: Batman Begins slowly, but has very nice gadgets...
7.content:
The beginning of the movie was slow. Nobody wants a long, drawn-out childhood sequence (though that was borderline bearable), nor do they want to see Batman in prison wallowing in mediocrity. And what's with his girlfriend - if you can call her his girlfriend? She's boring to look at and listen to, completely miscast and extraneous to the main plot. And much of the fight scenes are cut too close to the action, a la Bourne Supremacy.

On the other hand, the special effects are very well done, especially the larger shots of Gotham City; Batman's gadgets are both cool and believable; and the Batmobile is indescribably awesome. The directing and plot aren't bad aside from the caveats listed above, Christian Bale and Liam Neeson deliver excellent performances, and the rest of the cast (with the exception of Katie Holmes) are adequate for their parts.

Bottom line, this is the best Batman movie yet, and is probably worth going to see in the movie theaters. Based on the plot and directing alone, I'd give it an average rating (5), but it gains a couple points for cool gadgets, special effects, and Batmobile. One can hope that sequels will be better paced now that we've gotten past the "History of Batman" material.

7.title: Backstory Batman
7.content:
I was disappointed in this. Too much backstory in Asia with Liam Nesson. An hour into the film, and I still hadn't seen Christian Bale in the batsuit .

Then there's that Batmobile. Didn't like it.

The baddies especially Tom Wilkinson character- baddie clichés. Dirty and sweaty types.

Main problem, not enough Batman this one.

The action is incredibly loud- hard to find a level for the volume at home. Good level for the dialogue is deafening for action.a reasonable level for the action and I can't hear dialogue so was turning the volume up and down constantly.

I didn't enjoy Alfred either. Bit of a smart Alec.

7.title: An enjoyably revived Batman in a new old traditional style
7.content:
Yes, this film is definitely an advance to the Schumacher's Batman films. One can enjoy the myth of Batman again, thanks to Nolan and Bale, though it was not a perfect film to me...

The good aspect: For the first time, a Batman film consequently shows Bruce Wayne's development into the black knight. This part is also the best of the film, Bale perfectly illustrates Bruce Wayne's fear as well as his lust for revenge.

In addition shows the film a comprehensible reason of the villain for destroying Gotham City. We get to know why the city shall be destroyed, the explanation isn't only "pure evil" as in the early Batman films. Good news is that Nolan has returned to the very dark optics of the original Batman comics. The scenes when Bruce Wayne is trained in the mountains and when he discovers the secret cave under his property are very stylish and brilliantly pictured.

Another advantage of the film compared to Schumacher's and Burton's films is that Nolan combines realism with comic style. Schumacher's as well as Burton's Batman films were lacking realism. Batman and the villains had some supernatural powers that were never explained, and the Batman's arms were a bit too exaggerated and strange.

But this time Batman is no supernatural hero, the will for revenge and justice pushes him on and his abilities are all acquired and trained and his weapons and the Batmobil are rejected military project from the armament production of the Wayne corporation.

But the despite all the realism, when Bruce Wayne slips his Batmann dress over for the first time and beats up the first villains the well-known and satisfying hero-movie and comic feeling comes back.

Christian Bale is definitely the best cast for Bruce Wayne up to now. He illustrates Bruce Wayne's dark side and his inner conflict as great as his role as the heir of millions.

Unfortunately the last quarter of the film loses the realism and the darkness that made it so great up to this point. The final action sequences get lost in familiar Hollywood stereotypes. It has huge crashes, massive explosions and the usual action film humor, everything that Nolan was able to abandon before. But the biggest disappointment to me was, that Nolan couldn't even do without the Hollywood-usual kiss at the end.

These facts regrettably bedim the previously excellent impression.

But nevertheless the bottom line is, that Christopher Nolan and his excellent cast have adequately brought the myth of Batman back to screen and have awoken the appetite for more tales from Gotham City.

7.title: Bats!
7.content:
Batman is the adult version of spiderman. While the friendly neighbourhood spiderman tries to keep his little neighbourhood in check, batman's goal is to menacingly fix his city: Gotham City.

Batman's backstory is a bit cheesy (though maybe original at the time). He is the son of a billionaire and his parents were killed when he was young. At first, he was consumed by revenge and fear but slowly turned from it because his girlfriend smacked him for that.

The movie was not bad. I just didn't like the fight scenes. Not sure why they decided to have the camera move like that, it was so erratic, I couldn't barely see anything but it rather hurt my eyes.

The last scene foreshadows the Joker. Let's see if that guy is a joke or not.

7.title: Logical, but less fun.
7.content: Batman is back at last! Joel "I suck" Shumacher has moved on and one of the best directors around today has moved in. Christopher Nolan. And a new Batman has come. Christian Bale. With these two new weapons, Batman re-emerges ready for anything! However, his reemergence is a little lackluster. Though everything is given more reason and explanation now, plus a little more dignity (no butt-grove close-up this time), fun and cohesion is left at the door. The villains master plan is very ingenious, apart from the gaping hole in it. If the machine makes water turn to vapour, what about all the people surrounding it? (We're 70% water you know) But lets not let that get in the way. If we did, no Boond movie would ever be tolerated. But what i found difficult to tolerate was the complete lack of theme. For me, any super hero movie HAS to have a theme to get you excited when the hero comes on screen to do away with crime. No theme present here! However those are all the negatives, which are far outweighed by the positives. The supporting cast is nothing short of brilliant. I was shocked to see Rutger Hauer. At all. Morgan Freeman seems to have the most fun out of anyone in his small but great role. Michael Caine steals every scene he's in as Alfred. Whilst Michael Gough was wise and caring, Caine is casual and great to laugh with. Gary Oldman, while most probably miscast, also has fun as Gordon. All in all, a great first, and hopefully not last, outing for Christian Bale as Batman.

7.title: A breath of fresh air
7.content:
When it first came out I assumed it was intended as a prequel to the already existing Batman film series started off by Tim Burton's Batman (1989) . Only with the release of the later films did it dawn on me that this was an entirely new and independent take on Batman.

The plot, as the title suggests, revolves on the origin of Batman, how Bruce Wayne learns to overcome his fears to fight evil. It is quite straight forward, but that's fine with an origin story. There is a twist at the end, but not a very good one. Definitely one of those 'Curse you sudden but inevitable betrayal!' moments.

The acting is amazing, with an all star cast including Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Liam Neeson, not much needs to be said here.

Nolan does a great job directing. He keeps you interested throughout Wayne's training up the point where he finally becomes Batman. He manages to weave a strong thematic element of overcoming your fears into it, from Waynes struggle with his fear of bats to the antagonist Scarecrow using peoples fears against them.

Considering the last two installments in the previous series, Batman Begins is a welcome breath of fresh air and does a fine job of reviving the franchise while adding a new spin to it. I am quite fond of Nolan's approach. Tim Burton's vision was of a more surreal Gotham, while Nolan goes for a very realistic 'crime drama' of sorts. For this reason it is impossible to compare this film to Tim Burton's. They are both very good films and I can only recommend you watch both and decide for yourself who's vision you like more.

7.title: This is a story of how Bruce Wayne becomes Batman by conquering the fear in his heart.
7.content:
I hadn't read the Batman comics before watching this movie.Also I have not seen any of the earlier Batman films.So my comments are entirely based upon the experience of this movie.

THis film has the greatest cast ever worked for a Batman movie.All the veterans do a great job.THe new Batman(Christian Bale) is very believable as Batman.Director Nolan does a good job as a writer also.The film has great action and drama sequences.The cinematography in darkness was wonderful.When I came out of the movie hall at midnight I felt like I was in the city of Gotham.

However the theme music should have been better.The overall music of the film is good but the theme music should have been something like Harry potter.YOU don't notice these things while watching the film.I think this is one of the best entertainers of this year and even if you don't like Batman or superhero movies , you will like this one.

7.title: Batman Begins to Amaze
7.content: Great portrayal of Batman's origins. Liam Neeson and Christian Bale steal the show with amazing quotes and facial expressions. Holmes character, Rachel fills the gap between Bruce Wayne and Batman quite well. Two thumbs up for a good take on a Batman movie many have seen.

7.title: Batman Begins
7.content: I imagine if I was rating this movie just after I watched it that it would be much higher, but now I can only think of it in relation to the latter two movies. This movie is great, but Christian Bale was always the weakest link in the series. The villains are what make the movies and, now that I think about it, what make the comics as well. Al Ghul is a good starting point for Batman but not as memorable as Joker or Bane. This was a great first entry but really only serves as an introduction to the stronger sequels.

7.title: May Be The Best Batman Movie Ever Made
7.content: While I think Tim Burton's Batman has a unique and distinct place in American filmmaking this movie does a great job of treating the genre with a serious and exciting face. Christopher Nolan's complex and multi-layered origin story is distinct from Burton's, but to some degree could never have happened where it not for Burton and Keaton. Christian Bale is superb as the conflicted and somewhat morose crimefighter. Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes, and Gary Oldman take a serious approach to their characters and to the subject matter. This one is exciting and visceral. More adult than any of its predecessors and much less comic book like in its execution. It worse very well. Although the second installment in this trilogy was hailed as the best I still am fondest of this one and had this not been executed so precisely the remaining two may never have happened.

7.title: "Batman Begins"
7.content: The best Batman ever because it is believable,the humanity,relationship,personal back-story are fully realized. I'm annoyed by Bale's Batman's voice but in time I will get used to it although he is the better choice as Batman and Wayne than Keaton,Clooney and Kilmer.Nolan executed a better job as well compared to Burton. My only problem with Nolan is his unease with the action scenes but the movie as a whole has emotional fluidity and resonates with the audience.The bat toys also inflames our imaginations. The shocking part and best treat of all is that this Batman is actually a nice dude, he is dark,sexy but vulnerable not some jerk portrayed in the comics and cartoons or the past films like the clone of James Bond. Christian Bale and Katie Holmes also connected on many levels even when their arc is underused. The scenes are sweet and sexually charged and Katie Holmes delivered it with spunk and a twist of sadness. I'm fired up with the sequel and I cant wait for the reunion of Christian Bale with Gary Oldman, Katie Holmes,Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine. Its OK too if they bring back Cillian Murphy so we have real closure what happened to Scarecrow. Batman Begins also boasts as the best group talent ever assembled.

7.title: Second to ...Batman!
7.content: I think after watching C.Bale in Batman Begins at a local cinema and now on DVD , that this is the best Batman since Michael Keaton did his best show in 1989. Christian Bale is a very strong contender to be Batman,he is the most muscular but Keaton still rules in my opinion. Where Bale is strong and young,Keaton was kind of distinct and mature,-like the Batamn we got to know in the Neil Adam's B/W-series from the 70's. Batman Begins is good ,but I think C.Bale's character is a little bit to boyish - especially when doing Bruce. Bruce and Batman should be a bit older - in appearance and behavior. The story is there - o'yes - and has suspense - but I don't know yet if I'm comfortable with Bruce's training and education sequence,meeting his mentor played by Liam Neeson.It 's a bit overdone in matters of martial arts and fighting . I like Bale in many ways :He is strong and he is tall ,displays a good physique - and he is capable in being a treat to both thieves and the mob,but does he bring Batman the true character the right moods,the mystery and thrill? Because both Batman and Bruce is originally somewhat on a distance from others - he should be to maintain the ability to surprise and to vanish when ever he wants - he needs some distance mentally to keep his mind clear like a detective,not mix to much with others ,only with Alfred. M.Caine is doing his job OK, but Alfred from 1989 was more like The Alfred I like. Batman Begins should have been made in B/W - and Bale could have cut his hair to a shorter black trim.But he is good.

7.title: Good.
7.content: Good start for the trilogy and a good origin story for Bruce and Batman.

7.title: Nolan shows his mastery while taking comic books movies in a new direction.
7.content:
Even though I hadn't watched this film in a long time, it still existed in my mind as a testament to the genius of Christopher Nolan. Revisiting this today is still pretty much the same, even though this film largely exists in the shadow of its sequel.

I only watched this film for the first time after 2008's Dark Knight was my favorite movie. Being 9 years old when this one came out, I wasn't exactly in the target demographic and I don't think it was a big enough cinematic experience for my family to go out and watch it. I don't remember exactly when I first watched this film but I know that I first learned of its existence when my younger brother told me our favorite Batman movie actually had a prequel. Saying this film's existence is clouded by the perception of its sequel is almost an understatement, especially in my case.

The only reason I ever watched this film was because I loved Dark Knight so much and I was one of those cringey kids in middle/high school that would randomly quote Joker lines. I was predestined to like Begins from the first instance of my watching and really I can quote almost as many lines from this film as I can from the other.

Watching it today, after who knows how long, I cannot help but notice the politics of this film. In that sense, 2012's The Dark Knight Rises also paints my perception of this film. As Nolan's characters have a certain opinion of the world colored by a Conservative lens.

The most notable example would obviously be Nolan's characteristic extreme example, Ra's al Ghul (notably not an Asian man). He depicts the world and humans as innately corrupt and that it is in our nature to always devolve into a society rife with crime and violence because of our evil nature. He believes that criminals prey on the fear of the rest of us and take advantage of it for their own selfish desires. He believes that in order to solve this evil you must be as ruthless as those evildoers.

Largely Bruce agrees with mister Ra's because he is a dumb rich kid who knows nothing about the world, hence he is prime real estate for right wing radicalization. But he finally realizes the lunacy of his mentor when he asks him to execute a murderer, and Bruce remembers what Rachel taught him.

Now for the most part, criminals in this world exist as a result of the desperate situations perpetuated by powerful people just like in real life. And Rachel largely advocates this idea, even directly telling Bruce this when he himself is lost and in a desperate situation. We see that the economic situation produces an underclass to be exploited and fight each other for survival. Just a very bleak depiction of late stage capitalism BUT the culprit in this movie are the corrupt crime lords and the government employees they employ. The crime lords swamp the city with drugs and do whatever they want because they are above the law (also it turns out the economic conditions are also caused by Ra's and the League of Shadows because it can't be the societal structure that is wrong). And for all her talk about justice and vengeance, Rachel doesn't even seem to care about fixing the world via helping the downtrodden and just wants to punish those she believes are causing all of the ill.

And I guess that brings me to the third villain of the film, a Psychiatrist who is obsessed with using people's fear for his own pleasure (I think that is his motivation). Dr. Jonathan Crane doesn't really play a huge role in the film, as he mostly just works to develop the toxin for the shady terrorists and help the crime lord keep his goons out of prison and in a psychiatric ward because I guess they haven't seen One Flew Over The Cuckoo's nest and think that is a lesser sentence. It seems everybody in this film believes that lawbreakers only lose when they get punished by being thrown in literal prison. Crane himself operates within the same system Rachel does but I guess for the opposite reason, mostly.

So really this is a film about a terrorist group (seemingly based in Asia somewhere and made up of mostly Asian men) trying to ruin our way of life. This is what a post-9/11 Batman movie looks like I guess, who else would Hollywood make him fight if not terrorism and terror itself.

Christopher Nolan making a movie about the moral white family Gotham and their struggles to stave off international terror really seems like an absurd idea, yet somehow it isn't. It speaks volumes to his talent that Nolan took a superhero and made him fight a concept and created a really intellectual film in the end. There is plenty here about justice, crime, morality, vigilantism, political idealism, legacy, etc.
